input:

There is no way I can write this review without giving Russell, the owner of Body Cycle, a shout out. Russell's passion for fitness and cycling is so evident, as is his desire for all of his clients to succeed. He is always dropping in to classes to check in/provide encouragement, and is open to ideas and recommendations from anyone. Russell always wears a smile on his face, even when he's kicking your butt in class!
Rewrite this for me:

One thing that sets Body Cycle apart is their convenient online scheduling system. It's a lifesaver for those who struggle to find time for workouts. No more waiting in long lines at the gym just to reserve a spot.

I have to give a special shout-out to Russell, the owner of Body Cycle. His passion for fitness and cycling shines through in everything he does. He genuinely cares about each client's success and is always checking in and providing encouragement. Russell is also open to feedback and suggestions from anyone. And let's not forget his contagious smile, even when he's pushing you to your limits in class.

input: Family diner. Had the buffet. Eclectic assortment: a large chicken leg, fried jalapeño, tamale, two rolled grape leaves, fresh melon. All good. Lots of Mexican choices there. Rewrite this for me: The interior of the place was adorable, and the owner graciously showed us around the upcoming patio/rooftop area, which would be perfect for enjoying beautiful days like today. I ordered the onion, gruyere, and tomato sandwich, and it had just the right amount of cheese, which I really appreciated. However, I felt like it needed something extra, perhaps some pepper jelly. It would be great if they could offer more menu options, such as salads with exciting cheeses. They had an extensive selection of beers and wines, and a few cocktails, but I'm looking forward to trying one of their draft wines next time.

input: Loved this tour! I grabbed a groupon and the price was great. It was the perfect way to explore New Orleans for someone who'd never been there before and didn't know a lot about the history of the city. Our tour guide had tons of interesting tidbits about the city, and I really enjoyed the experience. Highly recommended tour. I actually thought we were just going to tour through the cemetery, but she took us around the French Quarter for the first hour, and the cemetery for the second half of the tour. You'll meet up in front of a grocery store (seems strange at first, but it's not terribly hard to find, and it'll give you a chance to get some water), and you'll stop at a visitor center part way through the tour for a bathroom break if needed. This tour was one of my favorite parts of my trip!
Rewrite this for me: I absolutely loved this tour! I found a great deal on Groupon, making it an affordable option. Our tour guide shared fascinating tidbits about the city, making the experience truly enjoyable. I highly recommend this tour. Surprisingly, it wasn't just limited to the cemetery visit. In fact, for the first hour, we explored the French Quarter, which was a pleasant surprise. The cemetery visit was equally captivating during the second half of the tour. The meeting point in front of a grocery store may seem strange initially, but it's not difficult to locate, and it even provides an opportunity to grab some water. Additionally, there's a scheduled bathroom break at a visitor center midway through the tour if needed. All in all, this tour was one of the highlights of my trip.

input:
My experience with Shalimar was nothing but wonderful. 
I wanted to get my engagement ring sized and was told over the phone that it could probably be done within the day. 
When I brought it by, the team confirmed that the jeweler would be able to accommodate my same-day request and that it would be around $40 (simple band, decrease by three full sizes).
I checked my size one more time, confirmed, and left to let them do their thing.
When I came to pick up later that afternoon, the ring was too small. It's very important to note that Shalimar sized the ring perfectly, but that I made a mistake and should've gone up a half-size.
The Shalimar group were completely understanding and accommodating, even resizing my ring back up and getting it back to me within an hour at no charge! Even though it was my mistake!
The associates' attitudes in dealing with what was a pretty embarrassing situation instantly earned my satisfaction and loyalty as a customer. Very grateful for such a wonderful experience.
Rewrite this for me:
Shalimar exceeded my expectations with their exceptional service. Initially, I contacted them to inquire about resizing my engagement ring, and they informed me that it could likely be completed within the same day. After double-checking my ring size, I confirmed it and left it in their capable hands. However, when I returned later that afternoon to pick it up, I discovered that the ring was too small. It is crucial to emphasize that Shalimar had accurately sized the ring as per my specifications, but it was ultimately my own mistake in underestimating the necessary size increase by half a size.

Remarkably, the Shalimar staff were understanding and incredibly accommodating. They quickly resized my ring, increasing it back to the desired size, and returned it to me within an hour without charging any additional fees – despite the error being entirely my own. Their admirable attitude in handling this rather embarrassing situation instantly won my satisfaction and loyalty as a customer. I am genuinely grateful for the wonderful experience they provided me.

input:
The bun makes the Sonoran Dog. It's like a snuggie for the pup. A first, it seems ridiculous and almost like it's going to be too much, exactly like everyone's favorite blanket with sleeves. Too much softness, too much smush, too indulgent.  Wrong. It's warm, soft, chewy, fragrant, and it succeeds where other famed Sonoran Dogs fail. 

The hot dog itself is flavorful, but I would prefer that it or the bacon have a little more bite or snap to better hold their own against the dominant mustard and onions. 

I'm with the masses on the carne asada caramelo. Excellent tortilla, salty, melty cheese, and great carne. 

Super cheap and you can drive through.
Rewrite this for me:
The Sonoran Dog is made complete by its bun, acting as a cozy cover for the hot dog. At first glance, it may seem excessive, much like the beloved snuggie blanket with sleeves. However, the abundance of softness and indulgence is just right. The bun is warm, soft, chewy, and has a delightful aroma, making it stand out from other renowned Sonoran Dogs.

While the hot dog itself boasts flavorful taste, I personally feel that either the hot dog or the bacon could use a bit more texture and crunch to better complement the overpowering flavors of mustard and onions.

Like many others, I am a fan of the carne asada caramelo. Its tortilla is excellent, with a perfect balance of saltiness and melted cheese, paired with deliciously prepared carne.

Additionally, the affordability and convenience of a drive-through option make it even more appealing.

input: Great place for breakfast! I had the waffle, which was fluffy and perfect, and home fries which were nice and smashed and crunchy. Friendly waitstaff. Will definitely be back!

input: Upland is a brewery based out of Bloomington, Indiana that has become popular enough to open up a couple additional locations in central Indiana.  All of their beers are very good, and I am also a fan of their burgers and tenderloins.  Therefore, I was excited to try their pizza, but I don't think it ended up being on par with these other items.  My margherita pizza had a cracker-like crust and was pretty light overall.  The cheese was good, but none of the other toppings added much flavor.  There was no red sauce as is typical for a true margherita pizza.  My opinion is that Upland's pizza might serve as a nice appetizer for a group, but I'll be sticking with their burgers or tenderloins as my meal of choice on future visits.
Rewrite this for me: Upland, a brewery originating from Bloomington, Indiana, has gained enough popularity to expand with a few more locations across central Indiana. My margherita pizza had a thin, crispy crust, and although it was light, it didn't possess the same exemplary characteristics. The cheese was satisfactory, but the other toppings lacked flavor. Surprisingly, the pizza lacked the customary red sauce found on a traditional margherita pizza. In conclusion, Upland's pizza could serve well as an appetizer for a group, but for me, I will continue to indulge in their burgers or tenderloins as my preferred meal during future visits.

input:
I was really between 3 and 4 stars for this one. I LOVE the 96th street Naked Tchopstix so I was very excited to see this one which is closer to my house.
The vibe is totally different as this is geared more to take out although they do have a decent size dining area. You order at the counter and they deliver it.
My daughter and I tried the sushi bowl. You pick up a piece of paper and  select from a choice of proteins, vegetables, rice and toppings. I like the fact that it is on paper and you don't have to guess what things are or have to shout over the counter to tell the server what you want. The sushi bowl was good but not wonderful. The choices particularly of the vegetables seemed a little too limiting and I felt I had more rice than other food items. The sauces were tasty. My husband ordered the Maui roll which is my favorite roll at the 96th street location and this just was not up that standard. It was good but the quality and consistently was not as good as at 96th street. I would go back though and I think a lot of people would be happy with the sushi bowls. I do want to make a comment about the low reviews that people have given the place because of service. People - it is a sushi place - it isn't McDonalds- so it will be a bit slower. You are not going to order and get out of there in five minutes even though it is called express. As a healthy alternative to fast food in the area, it is worth the wait. Oh and try the bubble tea. I had the strawberry and it was quite yummy. Next time I am going to try the vanilla chai.
Rewrite this for me:
I was torn between giving this place 3 or 4 stars. I'm a huge fan of the 96th street Naked Tchopstix, so I was really excited to try this location, which is closer to my house.

The vibe is completely different here, mainly focused on takeout, although they do have a decent-sized dining area. You place your order at the counter and they bring it to you.

My daughter and I decided to try the sushi bowl. You grab a piece of paper and choose from a variety of proteins, vegetables, rice, and toppings. I really appreciate the fact that it's all written down, so there's no confusion or need to shout over the counter to the server. The sushi bowl was good, but not amazing. I found the choices of vegetables to be a bit limited and felt like there was more rice than other food items. However, the sauces were tasty. 

My husband ordered the Maui roll, which is my all-time favorite at the 96th street location, but unfortunately, it didn't quite live up to that standard here. It was good, but the quality and consistency were not as great as at the 96th street location. Despite this, I would still come back, especially for the sushi bowls. 

Now, I want to address the negative reviews that some people have left regarding the service. People, it's a sushi place, not McDonald's, so it may take a bit longer. You can't expect to order and be out of there in five minutes, even though it's called "express". However, as a healthier alternative to fast food in the area, I believe it's worth the wait. 

Oh, and definitely give their bubble tea a try. I had the strawberry flavor and it was absolutely delicious. Next time, I'll be trying the vanilla chai.

Plus, it's conveniently located right next to the Santa Barbara Wine Collective, sharing the same tables. We indulged in a delightful savory croissant and it was absolutely fantastic.

input: Nice relaxing place to get a massage! Same day appointments are easy to come by! I have never been disappointed with any therapist I have had at the Center!
Rewrite this for me: Looking for a pleasant and tranquil spot to enjoy a massage? Look no further! At the Center, securing a same-day appointment is a breeze, and I have consistently found every therapist I've seen there to be exceptional. Disappointment has never been in the equation for me!

input: We checked in around 2:30 pm.  Check-in was quick and easy with complimentary valet parking (always appreciated).  The Peppermill is huge and reminded us of the Caesars Palace in Las Vegas.  They have around eight restaurants on site offering almost any type of food you could want.  The casino area is huge, rivaling almost anything you could find in Las Vegas.  One thing we noticed is that many of the slot machines were noted as being penny machines, but when you actually started to play them you realized they had minimum bets of anywhere from 30 cents to $5.  Talk about false advertising!  We were in the Tuscany Tower on the 12th floor.  Our room had a nice view of the huge pool area.  Our room was large and featured free WiFi (likewise always appreciated), a huge bathroom area with large shower (with two shower heads), TV, a large jetted bathtub and a phone next to the commode.  There were dual sinks and lots of counter space.  Plenty of towels were supplied.  The roomy main area had a king bed with night stands, closet, TV, mini fridge, dresser with two drawers, a safe, table for computer or writing, complimentary bottles of water, and three nicely upholstered chairs and table.  The thermostat did a good job controlling the temperature and keeping it comfortable.  Staff were all courteous and helpful.  A very nice place and we enjoyed our stay.
Rewrite this for me:
We arrived at around 2:30 pm and the check-in process was quick and easy. We were pleased to find complimentary valet parking available, which is always a nice perk. The Peppermill is a massive hotel that reminded us of Caesars Palace in Las Vegas. On-site, they have an impressive selection of about eight restaurants offering a variety of cuisines. The casino area is also quite large, comparable to what you would find in Las Vegas.

However, one thing that caught our attention was the abundance of slot machines labeled as penny machines. Upon playing them, we discovered that they actually had minimum bets ranging from 30 cents to $5. This felt like false advertising.

In terms of our accommodations, we stayed in the Tuscany Tower on the 12th floor. Our room had a lovely view of the expansive pool area. It was spacious and featured convenient amenities such as free WiFi, a generously sized bathroom with a large shower equipped with two shower heads, a television, a large jetted bathtub, and a phone by the toilet. The bathroom also had dual sinks and ample counter space. We were provided with plenty of clean towels.

The main area of the room boasted a comfortable king-sized bed with nightstands, a closet, a TV, a mini fridge, a dresser with two drawers, a safe, a table for working on a computer or writing, complimentary bottles of water, and three tastefully upholstered chairs and a table. The temperature control system worked well to keep us comfortable.

The staff at the Peppermill were all courteous and helpful, adding to our pleasant experience. Overall, it was a very nice place to stay and we thoroughly enjoyed our time there.

input: My boyfriend and I tried this deli for the first time today. I had a turkey, avocado & bacon panini and he ha a buffalo chicken wrap. We will definitely be returning. The wait for food wasn't too long, which is always appreciated during lunch hour. There was SO much to choose from. They have salads, soup, macaroni, sandwiches and hot food. Rewrite this for me: Today, my partner and I decided to give this deli a shot. This was our first time trying it out, and we were both delighted with our choices. I opted for a mouthwatering turkey, avocado & bacon panini, while he savored a satisfying buffalo chicken wrap. We were both impressed with the prompt service, as waiting too long for our food during the busy lunch hour can be frustrating. Additionally, the extensive variety of options at this deli blew us away. From refreshing salads and soul-warming soups to delightful macaroni dishes and delectable sandwiches, there was something for every taste. I truly appreciate a deli that offers such a diverse array of choices! Without a doubt, we will be revisiting this place in the future.

input: Amazing biscuits and (fill in the blank). Great cocktails too. Highly recommended. A bit busy though.

input: Food was good- atmosphere/decor is like a fishing lodge- menu is someplace between outback & bonefish. Went on a Groupon & all 3 of our meals & calamari appetizer that we ordered were cooked perfectly- we will def be back.
Rewrite this for me: The food was delicious, with an atmosphere and decor reminiscent of a fishing lodge. The menu offered a delightful blend of flavors, falling somewhere between Outback and Bonefish. We decided to try this place out using a Groupon, and we were pleasantly surprised that all three of our meals, along with the calamari appetizer we ordered, were cooked to perfection. We were so impressed that we will definitely be returning in the future.

input:
Straight to the point, it's cheap, it tastes and feels cheap

The good: price, location, dessert (edible food items are: baked chicken, fried chicken, mashed potatoes, Salad bar lol, meat and cheese bar, ravioli, pizza) also our waitress was bomb af

The meh: behind counter meat slicing station, shrimp (not even deveined), Mexican station

The bad: breakfast -worst eggs ever, actually worst, eggs. Le Benedict can't even cut through ham or English muffin (tried on all 3 occasions), steak, shrimp again, hell breaded items can't even, don't even. Decor it's the 1970 nightmare you can imagine

Tried 3 times and failed
Rewrite this for me:
To put it bluntly, this place is cheap in every aspect - from the price to the taste and overall experience.

The good things about this place include its affordability, convenient location, and a variety of dessert options such as baked chicken, fried chicken, mashed potatoes, Salad bar, meat and cheese bar, ravioli, and pizza. Additionally, the service provided by our waitress was excellent.

On the other hand, there are some mediocre aspects to be aware of. The meat slicing station behind the counter, as well as the shrimp that isn't even deveined, fall into this category. The Mexican station also didn't meet expectations.

Unfortunately, there are some outright negative aspects that shouldn't be overlooked. The breakfast options, particularly the eggs, were the worst we have ever had. Even the classic Eggs Benedict failed to impress, as it couldn't even cut through the ham or English muffin on all three occasions we tried it. The quality of the steak and shrimp also left much to be desired. Furthermore, the decor of the place is like a nightmare from the 1970s.

Despite giving this place three chances, it consistently failed to meet our expectations.

input:
The only reason I didn't give this restaurant a 5 star rating, is because of one single pretentious waiter. As a 4 night guest at Hotel Palomar, the location of the restaurant is an obvious plus. The first night of my stay, I met a coworker in the restaurant for a cocktail. When we arrived, the host staff were busy and not available, so we just walked in. The restaurant was not too busy, so we just looked at a small table next to the bar and proceeded to take a seat. A waiter came by and I quickly asked if we could have a seat, before sitting down and told him we'd only be having cocktails. He stumbled on his reply, and in an irritated/in-convinced tone, told me "I guess it would be fine" and basically just kept walking mid sentence. My guest and I brushed it off, and started having a conversation while looking at the drink menu. To make a long story short, he was distant and we both got the "couldn't be bothered" vibe from him. When it came to the bill, we asked if it could be split due to company transaction policies, and you would have thought asked him for some inconceivable task. We basically spent the rest of our night and elevator ride to our room in shock of the rudeness we had just experienced. 

Although that situation left a bad taste in our mouth, and the night before we decided to avoid the restaurant, we decided to grab another cocktail and give this place one more try. After looking around and ensuring "last nights waiter" wasn't on shift, we walked over to the bar and started looking over the menu. Instantly, the bartender greeted us with pleasant small talk and made us feel 100% welcome. He asked about our day, recommended cocktails and was a completely genuine person. This guy (I think his name was Ben) is an absolute star! He gave us lessons on Whiskey, described how to make classic cocktails, and was 100% invested in our experience. This is exactly what a bartender at a 4/5 star establishment should be - actually he exceeds that. He was kind, funny, friendly and completely redeemed this restaurant/bar from our terrible experience the night before. 
I also ordered room service last night from this restaurant, and it was amazing. The bacon wrapped dates and chocolate cake are to die for! Great restaurant and amazing bartender(s). Too bad one bad egg could have spoiled this experience.
Rewrite this for me:
The only reason for my decision not to give a 5-star rating to this restaurant is due to one pretentious waiter. As a guest at Hotel Palomar for four nights, the restaurant's convenient location was a definite advantage. On the first night of my stay, I met a coworker at the restaurant for a cocktail. Upon arrival, the host staff were occupied and unavailable, so we took it upon ourselves to find a table. The restaurant was not overly busy, so we settled at a small table next to the bar. A waiter approached us, and I quickly inquired about seating before sitting down, informing him that we only intended to have cocktails. His response came across as hesitant and in an annoyed tone, he begrudgingly said, "I suppose it would be fine," and then walked away abruptly before completing his sentence. My guest and I brushed off the encounter and began a conversation while perusing the drink menu. To cut the long story short, the waiter remained distant, and we both sensed an indifference from him. When it was time to settle the bill, we requested separate checks due to company policies, and it seemed as if we had asked him to complete an unimaginable task. We spent the remainder of the night and the elevator ride to our room shocked by the rudeness we had just experienced.

Although this incident left a negative impression, we decided to give the restaurant another chance the following night, after choosing to avoid it the previous night. Ensuring that "last night's waiter" was not on duty, we proceeded to the bar and examined the menu. Immediately, the bartender greeted us warmly and engaged in pleasant small talk, making us feel completely welcome. He inquired about our day, recommended cocktails, and exuded genuine warmth. I believe his name was Ben, and he was an exceptional individual. He provided us with lessons on Whiskey, described the preparation of classic cocktails, and demonstrated a genuine investment in our experience. He exemplified precisely what a bartender at a 4/5-star establishment should be, exceeding expectations. He was kind, humorous, friendly, and ultimately redeemed the restaurant/bar from our previous terrible encounter. 

In addition, I ordered room service from this restaurant last night, and it was fantastic. The bacon wrapped dates and chocolate cake were absolutely delightful. The restaurant itself is excellent, and the bartender(s) are amazing. It is unfortunate that one unpleasant encounter could potentially tarnish the overall experience.

input: Stopped by after a Sunday morning walk in the park - great food, coffee customer service - love the vibe in here
Rewrite this for me: I swung by this place after a refreshing Sunday morning stroll in the park. The food was amazing, the coffee and customer service were top-notch. I absolutely adored the atmosphere and overall vibe of this place.

input: In a word... "OVERRATED!".  The food took forever to come out.  The burger was WAY overcooked (Especially when I ordered it Medium Rare) and the Seafood Jumbalaya was Decent.  Not worth the price.  There are better places to eat in the french quarter.  It was not horrible, but for everything that we had heard about this place, I would have expected much better.
Rewrite this for me: In one word... "Overrated!" The wait for our food was incredibly long. The burger was severely overcooked, especially considering I specifically asked for it to be medium rare. The Seafood Jumbalaya was passable, but not worth the hefty price. There are definitely superior dining options available in the French Quarter. While it wasn't terrible, considering the hype surrounding this place, I had anticipated a much higher standard.

input: Comfortable bed, good breakfast, fast internet, great location, and low price. Overall I was really impressed with this place. However, if you stay on the top floors you may be waiting up to 15 minutes for an elevator in the morning.

input: NEVER AGAIN. This is a so called restaurant that does nothing that a restaurant should other than prepare food, because the rest is done by the patron. Want water? Get up and go across the yard to get it. Want a drink, walk up a flight of stairs and pay cash. Want to sit in a dirty yard in dirty lawn chairs, enjoy yourself. The wait staff is mildy helpful in that they bring you your food after you go to the window and pay cash for it...kind of like New Orleans Hamburger and Seafood, but dirty and with live music (which is nice). It's a one in a lifetime experience for me...just once.
Rewrite this for me: I will never go back to this so-called restaurant. It fails to meet the basic expectations one would have from a restaurant, as everything else besides food preparation is left up to the customers. If you want water, good luck fetching it yourself from across the yard. Craving a drink? Prepare to climb a flight of stairs and pay in cash. And forget about enjoying a comfortable seating arrangement - dirty yard and lawn chairs await you. While the wait staff does bring your food after you've paid for it at the window, their assistance is mediocre at best. It reminds me of New Orleans Hamburger and Seafood, except dirtier and with live music (which is a nice touch). This place is an experience I have no desire to repeat - one visit was more than enough for me.

input:
If you want to pay for everything a la carte this is the place for you.  
Food wasn't terrible not impressive.
They brought a basket of chips and some tomato sauce which I asked politely for something spicier and some pico de gallo.  She brought them happily to me and the salsa was much better.  When asked what we would like to drink I asked for a coke and she brought out a bottle which I stated I wanted the fountain drink.  She said "oh that's only Pepsi".  Never mentioned that they only had bottle drinks for coke.  
We ordered our food which was reasonably priced, asked for sour cream and also to put cheese on the taco.  She let us know cheese was extra.  
It was $2.50 extra for another basket of chips.  
When I received the bill we paid more for the condiments then the actual food.  Side of sour cream 2.00, pico de gallo 2.50, salsa 2.00, chips 2.50, cheese 1.00 and the bottled coke that we didn't want 5.00.  
Just a suggestion...when you order anything make sure to ask if there is an extra charge.
Rewrite this for me: This is the perfect place for those who prefer paying for each item separately. The food was not terrible, but it didn't leave a strong impression either. We requested spicier seasoning and some pico de gallo, and the server happily brought them to us, greatly improving the salsa. However, when we asked for a coke, the server only had it available in bottles and failed to inform us of this beforehand. We proceeded to order our food, which had reasonable prices, and asked for sour cream and cheese on the taco. The server informed us that cheese was an additional charge. Surprisingly, another basket of chips cost an extra $2.50. To our dismay, when we received the bill, we noticed that we spent more on condiments than the actual food. The side of sour cream was priced at $2.00, pico de gallo at $2.50, salsa at $2.00, chips at $2.50, cheese at $1.00, and the unwanted bottled coke at $5.00. It's a suggestion for future reference to ask about any possible extra charges when placing an order.

input: The cafe was extremely cute. We came at 8am and they even had a jazz band playing at that time. I got the breakfast sandwich and it was delicious. I loved how they rolled the egg and put the bacon pieces inside. Great price for a filling breakfast!
Rewrite this for me: The cafe had an incredibly adorable ambiance. Our visit at 8am was accompanied by a delightful live jazz band performance. Opting for the breakfast sandwich, I was thoroughly impressed by its deliciousness. The way they rolled the egg and nestled the bacon pieces inside was particularly enjoyable. Moreover, the breakfast came at a fantastic price, providing a satisfying and filling start to the day.

input:
On a scale of one to things that are awesome, this place is the bomb. 

I was drawn in by the promise of the duckfat frenchfries. Took the boy for his birthday and put our name in, had a drink around the corner while we waited and were given seats at the bar after about 45 minutes. 

We were waited on by Keith, the bartender, who was congenial, knowledgeable about his whiskeys and an all-around cool guy. We started with 3 cape may salts (two for me, one for the boy) and tater tots, both of which made me happy.

For dinner, I got Kentucky Fried Quail (stellar, though the succotash was not as exciting as I wanted it to be) and the boy got the 24$ Fois Gras burger, which was incredible. Worth every penny. The duckfat fries were pretty yummy, but not even the best part of the meal. I could've done without the cheese sauce, but as it was on the side I wasn't deterred.

I look forward to coming back here, with everyone I know.
Rewrite this for me:
This place is absolutely amazing, ranking high on the scale of awesomeness. The main reason I was attracted to it was because of the famous duckfat french fries. I decided to take my son here for his birthday celebration. We put our name on the waiting list, then went to grab a drink nearby while we waited. Finally, after approximately 45 minutes, we were given seats at the bar.

Our bartender, Keith, was fantastic. He was friendly, knowledgeable about various whiskeys, and an all-around cool guy. To kick off our meal, we ordered 3 cape may salts (two for me and one for my son) and tater tots, both of which brought me immense joy.

For the main course, I opted for the Kentucky Fried Quail. It was absolutely outstanding, although I must admit that the succotash didn't live up to my expectations. On the other hand, my son went for the $24 Fois Gras burger, which was simply incredible. It was worth every single penny. The duckfat fries were quite delicious, although they weren't even the best part of the meal. The cheese sauce, although not necessary for me, was served on the side, so it didn't bother me.

I am eagerly anticipating my next visit to this place, and I can't wait to bring all my friends and family along.

input: We started with the artichoke dip, big mistake. It was cold and the chips were stale. Mentioned to our waitress, but nothing came of it.  We ordered a large pizza, thin crust which after adding toppings it was a bit pricey for pizza.  Pizza was ok, not great. Except for not being our advocate our server was good.  I have been here before for Cardinals game, it was better then. Will try another venue next time.
Rewrite this for me: Our experience began with the artichoke dip, which turned out to be a regrettable choice. The dip was served cold, and the accompanying chips were disappointingly stale. Despite mentioning this to our waitress, nothing was done to address the issue. Moving on, we decided to order a large pizza with a thin crust. However, once we added the toppings, the price seemed quite high for a simple pizza. The taste of the pizza was average, not particularly outstanding. We have to acknowledge that although our server did not stand up for us, they provided satisfactory service otherwise. Having previously visited this establishment for a Cardinals game and having had a better experience, we will seek out a different venue next time.

input: It was my fiance's birthday and he decided he wanted a good, laid back Thai restaurant for dinner. Yelp steered us in the Jasmine Rice direction, and it was definitely a good decision. We wanted the summer rolls, which were on the menu, but apparently will not be available until summer, so we settled on the pan-fried dumplings. The flavor was good, but I don't think we'd order them again. We got the green curry fried rice with duck and chicken pad thai. Both of those dishes were great, but the duck stole the show. That was some the of tastiest duck I've ever had. The pad thai was a bit sweet for us, so I think we'd try a different noodle dish when we return. But it was still very good, especially with some chili sauce mixed in. Our service was good, but other people had issues. One table was rushing to get to a show at the Kimmel Center and waited quite a while for their meal (and were going to be late). Another person who got take-out was missing one of their items (but the owner realized it and called him and walked the dish to his house, which was very nice). Overall, good quality Thai! We would definitely go back.
Rewrite this for me: For my fiance's birthday, we wanted to find a relaxed Thai restaurant to celebrate. After checking Yelp, we decided to give Jasmine Rice a try, and it turned out to be a great choice. Although we initially wanted summer rolls, they were not yet available, so we opted for the pan-fried dumplings instead. While the flavor was good, we probably wouldn't order them again. However, the green curry fried rice with duck and chicken pad thai were both delicious. The duck, in particular, stood out as one of the tastiest we've ever had. The pad thai, on the other hand, was a bit too sweet for our liking, so next time we visit, we'll explore other noodle dishes. Nevertheless, it was enjoyable, especially when paired with some chili sauce. Our service was satisfactory, although we noticed some issues with other customers. One table, in a hurry to reach a show at the Kimmel Center, waited quite a while for their meal and worried about being late. Additionally, someone who ordered take-out found that one item was missing. However, the owner promptly realized the mistake, called the customer, and personally delivered the missing dish to their home, which was a very kind gesture. All in all, Jasmine Rice offered good-quality Thai food, and we would definitely return in the future.

input: I absolutely love Courtney! She is hands down the best hairstylist I have ever had. Rewrite this for me: I have a deep admiration for Courtney! Without a doubt, she is the most exceptional hairstylist I have ever encountered. One aspect that sets her apart is her unmatched ability to discern the most flattering looks for me, taking into consideration my personal style preferences. With complete trust, I often enter the salon and simply ask her to work her magic, and without fail, I am consistently amazed by the results. input:

If you require an oil change, this establishment is acceptable; if a state inspection is what you need, they can handle it. input: Replaced 2 old 70s lennox with 2 new ones.  They did a great job and have been runnong for 3 years now.

input:
I love the Brewpub for their variety of dishes.  Nachos, pizza and sandwiches.  Variety of beers to choose from crafted right on sight.  

Every time we go, the service is slow.  I think it's just the pace of the restaurant.  It's never a quick beer and a bite of food.  Instead, enjoy the patio and friends, savor that time.  

Kid and dog friendly environment.  Also great for your vegetarian and vegan friends.  

My go to is a half order of the nachos or fish & chips.  

Tried their Pumpkin Seasonal Beer and it's on par with some of my favorite pumpkins.
Rewrite this for me:
I absolutely adore the Brewpub because of their extensive selection of delectable dishes including nachos, pizza, and sandwiches. Additionally, they boast a wide variety of freshly crafted beers, all made in-house. 

On the downside, the service tends to be quite slow every time we visit. However, I believe it's just the restaurant's relaxed pace. Instead of expecting a quick beer and a bite to eat, it's encouraged to take your time, enjoy the pleasant patio atmosphere, and bask in the company of friends.

Not only is the Brewpub an ideal spot for those with kids and dogs, but it also accommodates vegetarian and vegan preferences, making it a great choice for everyone. 

Personally, my ultimate favorites are the half order of nachos or the fish & chips. 

One remarkable offering that I recently tried is their Pumpkin Seasonal Beer, which managed to impress me as much as some of my all-time favorite pumpkin beers.

input: Farmhouse, rustic, chic.Helpful staff with great ideas to decorate your home. Prices reasonable. Store has items from Joanna Gaines ( Fixer Upper) and much more. Finally a good home store in SB with reasonable prices.

input: My brother came to visit and we wanted to pick up a six pack of good beers for a night in. Ended up staying and having a few while playing their Nintendo 64 (Super Smash Brothers, which the owner said was donated by fellow patrons). It's a great place with good food and genuinely nice people. Should be a staple in the Northeast.
Rewrite this for me: When my brother paid me a visit, we decided to grab a six pack of quality beers to enjoy during a cozy evening. However, we ended up staying longer than planned as we got engrossed in playing Super Smash Brothers on their Nintendo 64, which was generously donated by other customers. The place was fantastic, featuring delicious food and genuinely friendly individuals. I believe it should become a popular spot in the Northeast region.

input:
My go to menu is coconut soup and pad thai with protein. I tried same menu here. 
Actually really like their coconut soup. They used enough amount of coconut milk that soup was really creamy and wasn't over powering with herb. I am so used to Americanized thai cuisine that I prefer less herb on my dish except cilantro.
Pat thai was great too. Liked the amount of peanut they used, noodle was chewy and perfect and not too sweet. They gave me generous amount of chicken and white meat wasn't dry so I was very happy with my meal.
Rewrite this for me:
My preferred choice for a meal is a combination of coconut soup and pad thai with protein. I recently had the opportunity to try the same menu at this place, and I must say that I was truly impressed. The coconut soup had the perfect consistency and creaminess, thanks to the generous amount of coconut milk used. It was delightful to taste a soup that wasn't overwhelmed with herbs. Being accustomed to Americanized Thai cuisine, I generally prefer dishes with fewer herbs, except for cilantro. 

The pad thai was equally fantastic. The balance of peanuts was just right, and the noodles were cooked to a chewy perfection, without being overly sweet. The portion of chicken provided was generous, and the white meat was cooked perfectly, ensuring it remained moist and not dry. All in all, it was a satisfying meal that left me very content.

input: Excellent service! Great diner food and breakfast is served all day. Came here for lunch- they were busy but very friendly and hospitable. Easy to get to off the 295.
Rewrite this for me: The service provided at this place is outstanding! Their diner food and all-day breakfast options are exceptional. Even during a busy lunch hour, the staff remained friendly and hospitable. Moreover, it is conveniently located off the 295 highway, making it easily accessible.

input:
My go-to spot on a Saturday night! I was real bummed that lucys closed, but was pleasantly surprised by this bar just across the street!
Their food is better than expected. I always get wings and fries. (be careful of the wtf sauce though) Sometimes it takes a real long time to get the bartenders attention, but the place is usually packed. And if you're lucky the always sunny crew will pop in!
Rewrite this for me: This place has become my favorite Saturday night hangout! I was disappointed when lucys closed down, but luckily I discovered this bar right across the street. Surprisingly, the food here is even better than I anticipated. My usual order includes wings and fries, although I would advise being cautious with the wtf sauce. Occasionally, it can take a while to grab the attention of the bartenders due to the crowd, which is usually quite packed. If you're fortunate, you might even spot the always sunny crew stopping by!

input:
We were a bit weary about trying the Shellfish Company on the Wharf as more often than not, many places like these (see Cannery Row, Monterey) feast on a captive audience and provide sub-standard fare at high prices.

However, emboldened by the perennial good reviews on Yelp, we suppressed our initial observations and went ahead with the trying it out. The place is small, so definitely plan ahead. You will have to wait, so either you know, just do so, or perhaps try to visit outside of peak hours. Luckily, our wait was only about 20 minutes as the dinner rush was just leveling off.

The special was the local rock crab - $25 for 3 lbs of California Rock Crab, salad, and your choice of soup/chowder. After taking a look at a few trays of rock crab being served out, the wife and I both opted for it, as it looked awesome.  

The salad/chowder combo was great as you actually received hearty portions of each, so it was a good start. As much as I liked the chowder however, the Shrimp Bisque the wife ordered was amazing, so I would recommend that going forward. 

But enough of prattling on about side dishes: the rock crab tasted just as glorious as it looked. Juicy, buttery chunks of white crab meat await you, just a few cracks away. While the rock crab shells are pretty thick, once cracked, they splinter and separate easily, a good sign they are cooked to perfection. The rock crabs provided a great amount of meat for what I felt to be the least amount of work you're going to do for crab, King or otherwise. 

We were thoroughly satisfied with our meal and along with the special being an overall great value, devouring the Rock Crab at SBSC turned out to be one of the favorite meals on the trip. I think ordering crab here is a safe proposition indeed.
Rewrite this for me:
Initially, we were hesitant to try the Shellfish Company on the Wharf because places like these often take advantage of a captive audience and serve mediocre food at high prices, as we have experienced at other locations such as Cannery Row in Monterey.

However, after reading consistently positive reviews on Yelp, we decided to ignore our reservations and give it a shot. Keep in mind that the restaurant is small, so it's wise to plan ahead. Be prepared to wait, or try visiting during off-peak hours. Fortunately, we only had to wait about 20 minutes since the dinner rush was just starting to die down.

The special of the day was the local rock crab, priced at $25 for 3 lbs of California Rock Crab, accompanied by a salad and your choice of soup or chowder. After seeing several trays of rock crab being served, my wife and I both chose it because it looked fantastic.

The combination of salad and chowder was excellent, as we were served generous portions of each. Although I enjoyed the chowder, my wife's Shrimp Bisque was absolutely amazing, so I highly recommend it for future visits.

But enough about the side dishes; let's talk about the star of the show, the rock crab. It tasted just as glorious as it looked. The meat was juicy and buttery, waiting to be savored with just a few cracks. Despite the thick shells, the crab was cooked to perfection, easily separating with a crack, indicating that it was well-prepared. The rock crab provided a satisfying amount of meat with minimal effort compared to other types of crab.

We left the restaurant completely satisfied with our meal. Not only was the special a great value, but devouring the Rock Crab at SBSC turned out to be one of the highlights of our trip. Ordering crab here is definitely a safe bet.

input: I LOVE Weaver's Way and really disagree with some of the content in previous reviews. WW is not necessarily meant for convenience shopping. I am a single woman and I find that I have no trouble shopping at the co-op, during peak times or otherwise. I actually find the co-op to be a great place to shop if you live alone because I can get smaller quantities of items than if I shop at the corporate stores like Acme. I also enjoy the work hours - I've worked throughout the store, but most recently, I have been getting in my hours by participating in the membership committee. I wouldn't say that the community is necessarily made up of "tree huggers" and "earth children", though. The community is made up of a variety of similarly-minded folks from different backgrounds. I enjoy having a place to go to where I can obtain locally grown produce, a place that offers more natural, wholesome, and preservative-free foods than chain stores with prices way below that of Whole Foods. I enjoy interacting with other members and contributing to my local and global community. I don't find the membership fee or the work hours to be prohibitive being a single person vs. a family. I don't think that membership in a co-op is for everyone and, if you aren't single, it's definitely not a solo decision. If you're keen on being committed to the Weaver Way values, you couldn't find a better place to shop. If not, stick to the chain stores or just pay the 10% visitors' fee to pop in once in a while.
Rewrite this for me:
I am a big fan of Weaver's Way and strongly disagree with some of the opinions expressed in previous reviews. It is important to understand that Weaver's Way is not designed for convenience shopping. As a single woman, I find it incredibly easy to shop at the co-op, regardless of whether it's during peak times or not. In fact, I believe it is a fantastic place to shop for individuals living alone because I can purchase smaller quantities of items compared to corporate stores like Acme. 

Moreover, I genuinely enjoy the flexible work hours offered by Weaver's Way. While I have worked in various departments in the store, I am currently involved with the membership committee. It is worth noting that the community within Weaver's Way is not exclusively composed of "tree huggers" or "earth children." Instead, it consists of like-minded individuals from diverse backgrounds. 

What I appreciate most about Weaver's Way is the availability of locally grown produce and the wide range of natural, wholesome, and preservative-free foods -- something you won't easily find at chain stores with prices far higher than Weaver's Way. Additionally, I love the opportunity to interact with fellow members and contribute to both my local and global community.

As a single person, I do not consider the membership fee or the required work hours to be burdensome. However, I do recognize that membership in a co-op is not suitable for everyone, and if you are not single, it should be a decision made collectively as a family. If you are truly committed to the values upheld by Weaver's Way, I assure you there is no better place to shop. If not, it may be best to stick to chain stores or simply pay the 10% visitors' fee for occasional visits.

input:
After living in the STL area for way over 10 years now, I am both ashamed and remorseful to admit that I ate here for the FIRST time just a few weeks ago. I am ashamed because it's a St. Louis tradition and remorseful because I missed out on it for so..many...years! 

This place is amazing. What is not to love! It's a factory where you can get a tour (Friday-Sunday, noon-5pm on the hour), there's a shop, bar, and dining area. They also host many event with live music on the weekends. It's fun to just kind of wander and look around - don't worry, you'll get a chance because there will likely be a wait before you dine. The beer is, of course, amazing. The Hefeweizen is my personal favorite and a great start for anyone who is not a huge beer drinker (like myself). Additionally, the food is homegrown and damn good. I had the pizza (recommendation from my server) and it was really spectacular, though I'm admittedly a pizza connoisseur so I enjoy a good pizza pie more than most probably ;P My date had a bison burger which was also really good. 

More fun info: the service is great! I think they tend to hire more funky and alternative people (like tattoo parlor staff) which I support. The quality is what makes this place stand out along with the emphasis on local food and brewery. 

It is a little on the pricier side but for all the experience you get and the quality, it is worth it. I will go again and again and you probably should, too!
Rewrite this for me:
Having lived in the STL area for well over a decade now, I must confess that I recently dined at this place for the very first time, and it fills me with both shame and regret. I feel ashamed because it's a cherished St. Louis tradition, and remorseful because I missed out on it for so many years!

Let me tell you, this place is absolutely incredible. There's so much to love about it! It's not just a restaurant; it's a whole factory where you can take a tour (available on Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays from noon to 5pm on the hour). They also have a shop, a bar, and a dining area. On top of all that, they frequently host events with live music on weekends. It's a fantastic place to wander around and explore. Just be prepared for a wait before you get your meal.

And speaking of meals, the food and drink here are superb. The beer, in particular, is outstanding. As someone who isn't a huge beer drinker myself, I highly recommend starting with their Hefeweizen. It's my personal favorite and a great choice for those new to beer. The food is also locally sourced and incredibly delicious. My server recommended the pizza, and it was simply spectacular. Now, I consider myself a bit of a pizza connoisseur, so you can trust me when I say it was top-notch. My companion ordered the bison burger, which was also excellent.

On top of all the amazing food and drink, the service here is top-notch. They seem to hire individuals with a more alternative and funky vibe, much like a tattoo parlor staff, which is something I really appreciate. It's this unique combination of quality service, emphasis on local food and brewery, and funky atmosphere that sets this place apart.

Now, I'll admit that this place can be a bit on the expensive side, but when you consider the overall experience and the quality of everything they offer, it's well worth it. I plan on returning again and again, and I highly recommend that you do the same!

input:
I visited this restaurant 4 times during my 5 days stay. Crazy, right? Here are a list of reasons/pros:

- We were staying a nearby hotel.
- The restaurant opens 11 - 10:30 pretty much every day including new year's day so it fits into our schedule.
- If you are a party of two, chances are you get seated right away.
- $9 per dozen of oysters which is a really great deal by any standard!
- They have a seafood shop next door that sells boiled and fresh seafood to- go.
- Our server (same) is very friendly and recognized us every single time.

Now I want to talk about the reasons why I only give it 3 stars.

- We tried a bunch of stuff which are all pretty mediocre. Raw oysters are not cleaned well. So if your schedule is flexible, go to Superior Seafood during their happy hours for their 50 cents/oyster - better quality and cheaper. Turtle soup has a strange taste so I definitely prefer Felix's. A portion of my boiled shrimps are always mushy somhow, maybe boiled for too long?...
- The ambient is inviting but not comfortable so we basically just finished our food and go. 
- Clean the bathroom!!

Will probably visit again if we stay in the area next time or simply just pick up some seafood quickly.
Rewrite this for me:
I frequented this restaurant four times during my five-day stay. It may seem crazy, but let me provide you with a list of reasons why:

- Our nearby hotel made it convenient to dine there.
- The restaurant had consistent opening hours from 11 am to 10:30 pm, including holidays like New Year's Day, which perfectly fit our schedule.
- If you were a party of two, they would often seat you immediately.
- The price of $9 per dozen oysters was an excellent deal by any standards.
- Furthermore, they had a seafood shop next door where you could purchase boiled and fresh seafood to-go.
- The friendly server, who recognized us each time, consistently provided great service.

However, I must mention the reasons why I only rated this restaurant three stars:

- We tried various dishes, but unfortunately, they were all rather mediocre. The raw oysters weren't adequately cleaned. If you have a flexible schedule, I recommend going to Superior Seafood during their happy hours, where you can get higher quality oysters for only 50 cents each. Additionally, the turtle soup had a strange taste, and I personally prefer the version at Felix's. I also found that a portion of my boiled shrimp was consistently mushy, possibly due to overcooking.
- The atmosphere was inviting but not particularly comfortable, so we usually finished our meal and left.
- Lastly, the cleanliness of the bathroom left much to be desired.

Despite these drawbacks, I would still consider returning if I find myself in the area again or simply want to quickly grab some seafood to-go.

input:
Id you haven't been to the Smoothie King center since it was know as the New Orleans Arena, you are in for a nice surprise. The arena has had a face lift and, while the seats are the same,  everything else has been refreshed.

input:

The band members were dapper, engaging and insanely talented.  It's in a tiny hole in the wall space that only holds maybe 200 people? So it's very intimate and nice to see the smiles on the faces of the musicians as they share their craft with you. This is a must do while in NOLA!

It was heartwarming to witness the smiles on the musicians' faces as they shared their craft with such close proximity. If you find yourself in NOLA, this is an absolute must-do activity.

The tour itself was SO much fun! We were laughing and smiling and our tour guide was funny! We saw lots of alligators! From babies swimming in the water to full grown ones! We saw turtles and birds too! Our tour guide had a baby alligator we could hold that he's raising until it's a little bigger since it was a late hatch that would have died because of when it was born. The ride back was fun too because we went fast and the guide did some "tricks" with the boat! I highly recommend this tour!!!

input: We stayed at The Saint last year for a girl's trip. The lobby is lovely, they have a cool bar and restaurant that you can't help but to "ohh and ahh" over when you walk in.  All the things I'm accustomed too when I stay at a hotel anywhere...ambiance, a little sexy but not overkill! Everyone is so friendly, etc.  I'm thinking "oh shhhh this is going to be a great weekend!"  I checked in a few hours before my girl arrived because I had a ton of work i needed to do. So I set up my laptop ordered some room service and worked for about 4 hours straight. Left out to buy a bottle and get a mani/pedi.  My girl arrives...its about to be some trouble in NOLA... the two of us and no supervision...we pop out for dinner, come back in giggling as usual and we see it...a HUGH flying roach.  I'm freaked out.  I literally walk right out of the room down to the front desk.  I CANNOT!!!! They tell me they're sending a maintenance worker to handle it.  NOT GOOD ENOUGH! If there's one that's bold enough to show itself, he has other cohorts that prefer to live behind the scenes. They give us another room but tell me they can't do more until 8am.  No the room the move us too also has small spiders and other dead small bugs in the corners of the window. The TV doesn't work and one of the lamps doesn't have bulbs in it! COME ON!  At this point its about 3am and I know I'm not staying here past 8:15am. I dont want to sit my purse let alone my luggage in this hotel! I go online to my normal go to hotel, The W and book us there for the rest of the trip! 8am comes and goes no manager comes to our room. I go down and demand to see someone immediately.  This younger gentlemen comes out and apologizes.  I thank him for his apology and politely request ALL of my money back immediately.   He obliged and asked if  I would consider coming back after changes have been made! Bless his heart. NO dear!
Rewrite this for me:
Last year, my friends and I had a girls' trip where we stayed at The Saint. The hotel was impressive with a beautiful lobby, a cool bar, and a restaurant that left us in awe upon entry. It had all the qualities I typically look for in a hotel - great ambiance with a hint of sensuality but not overwhelming. The staff was friendly, creating a welcoming atmosphere, and I couldn't help but think that this weekend was going to be fantastic.

Since I had some work to do, I arrived a few hours before my friend and settled into the room. I set up my laptop, ordered room service, and focused on work for a solid four hours. Afterward, I stepped out to buy a bottle and treat myself to a mani/pedi. When my friend finally arrived, we were both excited and ready to have some fun in New Orleans. However, our joy quickly faded when we discovered a massive flying roach in the room. It completely freaked me out, and I immediately rushed down to the front desk, unwilling to stay in that room. 

The staff assured me they would send a maintenance worker to handle the situation, but I wasn't satisfied. If one roach had the audacity to make an appearance, surely there were others lurking unseen. They offered us another room, but warned that further assistance would only be available after 8 am. To my disappointment, the second room also had small spiders and dead bugs in the window corners. Additionally, the TV wasn't working, and one of the lamps lacked bulbs. It was simply unacceptable!

By this point, it was already 3 am, and I knew I couldn't stay in that hotel past 8:15 am. It was unimaginable for me to even think about placing my purse or luggage in such an environment. In response, I immediately went online and booked us a room at my usual go-to hotel, The W, for the remainder of our trip. When 8 am rolled around, we received no visit from the manager, so I went down to the front desk demanding to see someone right away.

Finally, a young gentleman came out and apologized for the inconvenience. While I appreciated his apology, all I wanted was a full refund. He agreed and asked if I would consider returning to the hotel after they made improvements. Bless his heart, but no, I had no intentions of returning.

Strike three - I had grilled yellowtail which was basically execrable - could not even finish it (overcooked and an inferior-frozen piece of fish - unacceptable for SB).

input:
Milktooth is the place to go if you want a good breakfast cocktail and a twist on traditional brunch. At first glance of the menu, you may think you've never heard of any of these foods for breakfast, and you may be right. I guarantee no matter what you order, you're going to enjoy it. 

Milktooth is one of the most popular brunch places in Indy, which means you will typically have a wait. Trust me, it's worth the usual 30 minute wait (on weekends). To make it go by a little faster, they've got a walk up bar for their coffee drinks and pastries. Snack on one of those to give you a preview of the amazing meal you're about to have.

Their menu changes from time to time but they have a few things that stay one the menu but change ingredients. I love all of their variations on a Dutch pancake, and their raclette grilled cheese is to die for.  If you're making this a boozy breakfast, don't pass up on the michelada. And sit outside if it's warm enough!
Rewrite this for me:
If you're looking for a fantastic breakfast cocktail and a unique take on traditional brunch, Milktooth is the place to be. The menu may offer unfamiliar breakfast options at first glance, but rest assured, every dish is guaranteed to be a delight. 

Being one of the most popular brunch spots in Indy, Milktooth tends to have a wait time. However, trust me when I say that the usual 30-minute wait (on weekends) is well worth it. To help pass the time, they offer a convenient walk-up bar where you can grab a coffee drink or pastry to snack on, giving you a taste of the incredible meal that awaits you.

While their menu does change periodically, Milktooth has some staple items that remain but with varying ingredients. Personally, I adore their different versions of Dutch pancakes, and their raclette grilled cheese is absolutely amazing. If you're looking for a boozy breakfast experience, be sure not to miss out on their fantastic michelada. And if the weather permits, opt to sit outside for a delightful al fresco dining experience.

input:
Oh Chickie's and Pete's, you are the perfect place to watch some sports and indulge. 

No doubt this is not the best food I've ever had but, if you can get a seat, grab some beer with mussels red and crab fries, there's no way not to thoroughly enjoy this place during a game or any time you're down by the stadiums. 

My favs are the crab fries, mussels red (white is overloaded with garlic that I can't always take it), the spicy pull and peel shrimp, steamers, and if the mood is right the blue crabs (it's a lot of work but tasty). This place also makes getting down and dirty with your food easy. There are sinks all over so you can rinse the mess off your hands once you're done....good touch.

To sum it up, Chickie's and Pete's is a Philadelphia institution and always a good time. I strongly suggest going at least once to enjoy the experience. 

Please note: Make sure to remember two things before coming during major sporting events. 1. You'll never get a table and 2. You'll deal with a ton of drunk people. I've absolutely been one of these people before and we can get annoying unless you're in the right frame of mind. :)
Rewrite this for me:
Chickie's and Pete's is the ultimate spot to catch a sports game and indulge in some delicious eats. While it may not be the absolute best food I've ever tasted, there's no denying the immense pleasure that comes from grabbing a seat, sipping on a beer, and devouring their mouthwatering mussels red and irresistible crab fries. Whether you're cheering on your team or simply hanging out by the stadiums, this place guarantees a fantastic experience.

As for my personal favorites, I can't get enough of their delectable crab fries, along with the flavorful mussels red (although the white can sometimes overwhelm with garlic). The spicy pull and peel shrimp, steamers, and, if you're up for it, the blue crabs are all worth trying too, despite the effort required to crack them open. And let's not forget the convenience factor - Chickie's and Pete's provides sinks throughout the establishment, making it easy to clean up after getting your hands dirty. A thoughtful touch, indeed.

In a nutshell, Chickie's and Pete's is a beloved institution in the heart of Philadelphia, guaranteeing a good time whenever you visit. I highly recommend experiencing it at least once. However, it's important to keep two things in mind if you're planning to go during major sporting events: firstly, securing a table will be nearly impossible, and secondly, you'll have to navigate through a crowd of rather intoxicated individuals. I must admit, I've been one of these rowdy folks before, and unless you're in the right mindset, it can be a bit bothersome. But, hey, that's all part of the lively atmosphere!

input:
I'm giving this joint 4 stars because they have earned it, but they are definitely 5 star material, if they work out a few kinks. Granted, they just opened, so some of the errors I've experienced (I work in the area, so I've been there several times) will probably get worked out and they are more than willing to make corrections and accommodations when they mess up. 

But over all, the food is REALLY good. Unlike my fellow Yelp-ers, I would say that ther pizza is not their strong suit - its kinds greasy and not sure if they use 100% mozzarella - tastes like its cut with something cheaper. However, so far I've had:  

The Quaker (Chicken version) - Delicious. They make their chicken steaks with the chunky chicken, which I like much more than the shredded version. They could season the chicken more, but the cheese was melted perfectly and the veggies were fresh. 

The fries - crisp and flavorful. I didn't even need ketchup, and I always eat ketchup on my fries

The onion rings - a little greasy, but very tasty and crisp. The onions stayed in the breading and didn't slide out when you bit them (which I hate). 

Spanakopita - mine was a little over cooked, but the flavors were really good

Baklava - VERY GOOD! 

Signature Salad - The veggies they use are very fresh which will make or break a salad. Their balsamic is great too!

The (turkey) Greek Burger - one of the best turkey burgers I've ever had! The patty was moist and flavorful all on its own, but then they top it with what must be homemade tzatziki. I could eat a bowl of that stuff! My burger had romaine instead of the advertised arugula, but it was very fresh, so I didn't mind as much. I also asked for feta, which I didn't get, but that sauce made me forget all about it. 

Overall, this place is great! Provided they don't stray from the high quality standard they are setting, I will keep going back.
Rewrite this for me:
I'm awarding this establishment 4 stars because they have proven themselves, but they definitely have the potential to be a 5-star restaurant if they address a few issues. It's important to note that they just recently opened, so it's likely that they will iron out the errors I encountered (as I work in the area and have visited multiple times). When they make mistakes, they are more than willing to make amends and accommodate their customers.

Overall, the food is incredibly good. Unlike other reviewers on Yelp, I would say that their pizza is not their strong point - it's a bit greasy and it's unclear if they use 100% mozzarella as it seems to be mixed with a cheaper alternative. However, I have enjoyed the following dishes so far:

- The Quaker (Chicken version): It's delicious. They use chunky chicken in their chicken steaks, which I prefer over the shredded version. The chicken could be seasoned a bit more, but the cheese is melted perfectly and the veggies are fresh.
- The fries: They are crispy and full of flavor. They are so good that I didn't even need ketchup, and I usually always have ketchup with my fries.
- The onion rings: They are a tad greasy, but very tasty and crispy. The onions stay inside the breading and don't slide out when you take a bite, which I appreciate.
- Spanakopita: Mine was slightly overcooked, but the flavors were excellent.
- Baklava: It is exceptionally good!
- Signature Salad: The veggies they use are incredibly fresh, which is crucial for a satisfying salad. Their balsamic dressing is also great!
- The Greek Burger (made with turkey): It's one of the best turkey burgers I've ever had! The patty is moist and flavorful on its own, and it's topped with what must be homemade tzatziki. I could eat a bowl of that sauce! My burger had romaine instead of the advertised arugula, but it was very fresh, so I didn't mind as much. I also requested feta, which I didn't receive, but the sauce made me forget about it entirely.

Overall, this place is excellent! As long as they maintain their high-quality standards, I will continue to be a loyal customer.

input: Eat here at least 2 times a week. Servers are always friendly and the food is amazing. I never leave disappointed & always leave with a full stomach
Rewrite this for me: You should definitely dine at this place a minimum of two times per week. The servers consistently provide friendly service, and the food is absolutely remarkable. I have never experienced dissatisfaction when leaving, and I always depart feeling satisfied and satiated.

input:
A truly delightful find! This is the transformed Carrow's Restaurant on Plumb and Kietzke that was saved by the wrecking ball by its beautiful redwood beams and fascia. The food was fantastic. My wife had the tri-tip salad -- greens on one side of the plate with a balsamic vinagrette balanced by four good-sized slices of medium-rare tri-tip and potato "croutons" --
little heavenly bits of crunchy potatoes. I had the tri/tip/chicken combo, selecting the fresh corn salad and potato salad as my two sides. It was so good that we ordered dessert as well (not something I do regularly). The offering was lemon meringue, mudd pie, apple pie, and ice cream. We shared the first -- again delicious, with real, perfectly set and browned meringue. The prices were very reasonable for the quality of food and the experience. We've already recommended to family and friends locally, and expect to return soon. Well done!
Rewrite this for me: What a delightful discovery! Carrow's Restaurant on Plumb and Kietzke has been beautifully preserved, thanks to its stunning redwood beams and fascia. The food was absolutely amazing. My wife opted for the tri-tip salad, which featured a bed of greens alongside four generous slices of perfectly cooked medium-rare tri-tip and potato "croutons" that were simply heavenly with their crunchy texture. As for me, I went for the tri-tip/chicken combo and chose fresh corn salad and potato salad as my sides. The flavors were so incredible that we couldn't resist ordering dessert (which is not something I normally do). The dessert options included lemon meringue, mud pie, apple pie, and ice cream. We decided to share the lemon meringue, and it was absolutely delicious, with a perfectly set and browned meringue that tasted divine. The prices were very reasonable considering the high quality of the food and the overall experience. We have already recommended this place to our family and friends in the area, and we are definitely planning to return soon. Well done!

input:

Rewrite this for me: Although Rebecca wasn't present during my birth as a doula, she served as a nanny to our firstborn daughter. input: Recently had my car tinted by Orange Tint and Tune and had fantastic service.  They offer a car pick up service if you live within 4 miles of their shop which is extremely convenient.  Carlos was my technician and went over all the tint options with me and even adjusted the grade of the tint after I expressed the look that I was trying to achieve. input: Stayed here three nights on business.  The property is located very close to the airport but you really don't hear it.  The rooms are standard TownePlace Suite rooms with a refrigerator, stove, etc..  The area in which the hotel is located is quiet with a combination of other hotels and office buildings.  It's about a 20 minute drive to the downtown or university area.  About 5-10 minutes from Pima Air Museum.  There are not too many restaurants close by but there are some fast food options and a sandwich place called Baggins that was really good and within walking distance.  The staff of the hotel was really friendly and helpful.  The breakfast is standard continental with a couple of hot options. They also have a reception on weekday evenings.  My only complaint is that the food and drink go quickly so get there early.  You could use this as a dinner if you wanted.  I got there about 45 minutes after it started and although there was food left there were very few soft drinks left (no diet).  They could improve by keeping the area stocked throughout the period.  Anyway, the rooms are nice, beds are comfortable and area is safe.
Rewrite this for me: I stayed at this property for three nights while on a business trip. Despite its close proximity to the airport, the noise was surprisingly minimal. The rooms are typical TownePlace Suite rooms with all the necessary amenities such as a refrigerator and stove. The hotel is situated in a quiet area, surrounded by other hotels and office buildings. The downtown and university area is about a 20-minute drive away, while the Pima Air Museum is only 5-10 minutes away. While there aren't many restaurants nearby, there are fast food options and a great sandwich place called Baggins within walking distance. The hotel staff were friendly and helpful throughout my stay. The breakfast offered is your standard continental selection, with a few hot options available. Additionally, the hotel hosts a weekday evening reception, which can be used as a dinner option. However, be sure to arrive early as the food and drinks tend to run out quickly. During my visit, I arrived 45 minutes after it started and found that there was still food left, but very few soft drinks (no diet options). Improvements could be made by keeping the area stocked throughout the duration of the reception. Overall, the rooms are comfortable, the beds are cozy, and the area feels safe.

input:
We got diverted to Tampa and decided to make the drive to Orlando but first we needed somewhere to eat. Wanting to avoid chain restaurants, yelp steered us towards this little local gem!

The ladies had the 7 oz. Tampa strip and the gents both had a 14 oz. ribeye. They grill their steaks over oak and citrus Wood and the smoky flavor is to die for! We are big fans of our smoker back home and cook our steaks this way as well, it's rare to find steak cooked over woodsmoke in most places and this was worth the side trip!  Sides were veggies and sweet potatoes. The wines on offer were so reasonably priced- most under $20 a bottle but a decent selection. They just don't mark them up 5x like most places! 

Our waitress Lisa also made great recommendations and her service was welcoming, friendly, and excellent. We are so glad we went local instead of to a chain. Bookmarking this place for a return trip next time I am in Tampa for sure!
Rewrite this for me:
After being diverted to Tampa, we decided to drive to Orlando. However, we needed to find a place to eat first, and we wanted to avoid chain restaurants. Following Yelp's recommendation, we ended up in this charming local spot!

The ladies in our group chose the 7 oz. Tampa strip steak, while the gentlemen went for the 14 oz. ribeye. These steaks were grilled over oak and citrus wood, resulting in a mouthwatering smoky flavor. We, too, are fans of cooking steaks over woodsmoke at home, so finding a place that served them this way was a rare treat! The sides we opted for were vegetables and sweet potatoes. The best part? The wine selection was reasonably priced, with most bottles priced under $20, and there was a decent variety to choose from. Unlike many other places, they didn't mark up the prices by 5 times!

Our waitress, Lisa, provided fantastic recommendations and delivered exceptional service with a warm and friendly attitude. Choosing to support a local establishment instead of a chain was definitely the right decision. I'll be sure to remember this place for my next visit to Tampa and bookmark it for future trips!

input:

input: Came here after my husband bought home their lemon pepper wings. They have plenty of flavors. input:
Back to Tom Jones and time to update my review. I didn't see that odd ATM type machine that only lets you withdraw money to apply to your check. It's no longer there-used to be next to restrooms. There is still a payphone back there which I love. There are now ATM's at front entrance.
  The blue ribbon is now $3.79, but still a bargain since it includes everything: pancakes, 2 eggs, toast, sausage, bacon,juice & coffee. I ate here with my kids. My daughter's choice. Says she "loves Tom Jones". Our meals included blue ribbons, french toast, chicken, club sandwich & baked potato . Everyone gets what they like. 
   I don't smell stale smoke and would not call it dirty.  I like the "loud" orange booths. I feel like I went back in time with these and the payphone. Service is always fast and I always seem to get a different waitress. Don't know where they find these young ladies but they're good. I've seen different managers there and they are all quick and on top of things-which makes a good manager.
   Since it's my daughter's fave I'm bumping it up from 4 to 5 stars.

Time to update my review on Tom Jones. Unfortunately, I didn't find that peculiar ATM machine which only allowed withdrawals to be applied to your check. However, they now have ATMs at the front entrance.

The price for the blue ribbon has increased to $3.79, but it remains a great deal as it includes pancakes, 2 eggs, toast, sausage, bacon, juice, and coffee. During this visit, I dined with my kids, and it was my daughter's choice because she absolutely adores Tom Jones. Our orders consisted of blue ribbons, french toast, chicken, club sandwich, and baked potato. Everyone was satisfied with their choices.

I didn't notice any stale smoke smell, and I wouldn't describe the place as dirty. I particularly like the vibrant orange booths, which give off a nostalgic feel along with the presence of the payphone. The service is consistently fast, and I always seem to have a different waitress. I don't know where they find these young ladies, but they are competent. I've observed different managers during my visits, and they all demonstrate efficiency, which is indicative of good management.

Since it's my daughter's favorite place, I am increasing my rating from 4 to 5 stars.
