input:
I've been wanting to try Trust Me BBQ for over a year now.  I stopped in there about 3 months ago and waited in line for 10 minutes with no service and left.  After reading reviews, I figured I'd give it a chance again just to see what all the fuss is about.  The food was 50/50 but the service was horrible so I'll likely never return.  The gentleman behind the counter didn't speak, smile or engage with us at all, I felt like I was at a vending machine.  Once we finally ordered, he didn't even listen to the order and put the wrong sides in our meals, we had to correct him while he was serving.  All in all, I will just stick with Down to the Bone BBQ

Pros:  BBQ Sauce is delicious, macaroni salad was different and interesting, "pulled" pork was moist.

Cons:  Chicken was more dry than a sheet of paper, inedible even with the BBQ Sauce.  Mac & Cheese was served from a pan that has probably been on the steam table for 2-3 days.  Collard Greens were very mildly flavored.
Rewrite this for me:
I have been eager to give Trust Me BBQ a try for over a year now. However, my first visit about 3 months ago left me dissatisfied. Despite waiting in line for 10 minutes, I received no service and decided to leave. After reading some reviews, I decided to give it another shot just to see what all the fuss was about. Unfortunately, the experience was a mixed bag. While the food was decent, the service was absolutely terrible, which is why I doubt I will be returning. The person behind the counter seemed uninterested and showed no signs of engagement or friendliness. It almost felt like I was interacting with a vending machine. After finally placing our order, he didn't even pay attention and ended up putting the wrong sides in our meals. We had to correct him while he was serving us. Overall, I think I'll just stick with Down to the Bone BBQ.

Pros: The BBQ sauce was delicious, the macaroni salad had a unique and interesting flavor, and the "pulled" pork was moist.

Cons: The chicken was incredibly dry and practically inedible, even when paired with the BBQ sauce. The mac & cheese seemed like it had been sitting in a pan on the steam table for several days. Lastly, the collard greens had a very mild flavor.

input: Was in town for a week and came by this little hole in the wall.  The pa nang chicken was excellent.  I ordered one star spicy and it came quick.  Will definitely return.

input: Cinco de mayo means margaritas and sangria and all things fried... this great place does a nice job with combining flavors of several different ethnicities and backgrounds and develops recipes that are unique.  Although not touted as a "Mexican" destination they know how to rock the rock salt and pour that tequila.  They also just opened a wine bar a couple doors down for overflow and specialty bottles. Rewrite this for me: Cinco de Mayo represents a celebration filled with delightful margaritas, sangria, and delectably fried treats. This exceptional establishment excels in blending flavors from various cultures and backgrounds, resulting in one-of-a-kind recipes. Additionally, they've recently opened a wine bar nearby to accommodate overflow customers and offer an impressive selection of specialty bottles. Give a high five to their on the rocks margaritas and their homemade white or red sangria – the experience is well worth the journey!

input:
This small little donut bakery is located in one of Hermitage's oldest shopping centers! 

I can imagine baking donuts is a hard job, let alone running the business...it's one of those jobs that starts in the wee hours of the morning so that the donuts are freshly made daily!

Yeu, the owner, serves not only your common popular donuts, but he also serves donuts with bacon on top, apple fritters, pigs in a blanket, breakfast pastries, and  kolaches....in addition to these yummy treats...he makes doughssants....they are what seems to be a scandalous marriage of a donut and a croissant...!!!!!!!! Need I say more? Yeah...you heard me. A doughssant! Worth the trip just to eat one of these! 

Prices are considerably cheap! The doughssants are only $1.99 each! The regular donuts are about $.60 each! 

These sweet donuts are my favorite treats to buy for my kid's school teachers...and they love them! 

Coffee also served here!
Rewrite this for me:
Located in one of Hermitage's oldest shopping centers, this cozy little bakery specializes in crafting delectable donuts. The demanding task of baking these treats begins in the early hours so that they can proudly offer freshly made donuts each day.

Yeu, the dedicated owner, goes beyond the usual range of popular donut flavors. Alongside classics, he offers unique creations like bacon-topped donuts, apple fritters, pigs in a blanket, breakfast pastries, and kolaches. However, the real star of the show is his innovative creation, the doughssant. This delightful concoction tastefully combines a donut and a croissant, creating a truly indulgent treat that you simply must experience for yourself!

Not only does this bakery offer irresistible treats, but they also do so at incredibly affordable prices. The decadent doughssants are a steal at just $1.99 each, while their regular donuts are a mere $0.60 each.

I personally find these sweet donuts to be the perfect gift for my children's school teachers, and it seems they share my sentiment as they thoroughly enjoy them. Additionally, you can also enjoy a cup of coffee to complement your donut experience at this establishment.

input:
Went here based on the high ratings and raves from people.  The entire experience was underwhelming from start to finish.  Their website which is fairly useless if you want to figure out the menu before going, you have to pick your location choice out of 3 locations and then drill down to the bottom to see the weak descriptions of their menu offering, no explanations and no price, just this

    Roast Beef
    Roast Beef Combo
    Roast Pork
    Roast Pork Combo
    Baked Ham
    Baked Ham Combo
    Roast Turkey
    Roast Turkey Combo
    Broccoli Rabe
    Broccoli Rabe Combo


No explanation of whats in a combo (its just where they add cheese by the way)

The table placecard (instead of menu) had a more detailed description than the website.  

When I walked in, its more bar than restaurant, no big deal, but there were tables.  Since I couldnt decide and the sandwiches werent too expensive at $6.85, I got the roast beef and roast port combos.

I got my two sandwiches fast enough, but the roast beef was cold and the roast pork was hot.  Not sure how a cook (for lack of a better word) could serve 2 things at the same time with such a temperature differential, one was obviously sitting for awhile.  I asked the waitress to reheat the roast beef while I finished the roast pork, and supposedly it was reheated, since it was warmer, but it was still cold-ish compared to my roast pork I had just finished.  The waitress did offer to replace it when she inquired, but I was in a hurry and didnt really care for a hot version of this sandwich.

The sandwiches were very skimpy on meat, but they "made up for it" by adding too much gravy to make it overly messy and the bread was disintegrating.  The menu place card mentions the "wet meat" option where you get less gravy, I strongly recommend you get it that style, especially if the gravy overpower the meat and structural integrity of the sandwich.
Rewrite this for me:
I decided to visit this place based on the high ratings and positive reviews from people. However, my experience was disappointing from beginning to end. Their website was not helpful at all if you wanted to check the menu before going. You had to select one out of three locations and scroll all the way down to find weak descriptions of their menu items, with no explanations or prices listed. The only information provided was a simple list of items like Roast Beef, Roast Beef Combo, Roast Pork, etc. There was no clarification on what a combo included, which I later found out meant they added cheese.

Interestingly, the table placecard had more detailed descriptions than the website. When I arrived, I noticed that the place seemed more like a bar than a restaurant, which wasn't a big issue since they had tables available. Since I couldn't make up my mind and the sandwiches were reasonably priced at $6.85, I decided to order the roast beef and roast pork combos.

The sandwiches were brought to me quite quickly, but disappointingly, the roast beef was cold while the roast pork was hot. It was perplexing how the cook could serve two items at such different temperatures, indicating that one had been sitting for a while. I asked the waitress to reheat the roast beef while I finished the roast pork. Although it was warmer after supposedly being reheated, it was still colder compared to the roast pork I had just finished. The waitress did offer to replace it when she inquired, but as I was in a hurry, I declined and didn't really want a hot version of the sandwich.

Moreover, both sandwiches were lacking in meat, but they compensated for it by adding excessive gravy, making the sandwiches overly messy. Additionally, the bread was falling apart due to the abundance of gravy. Interestingly, the menu place card mentioned a "wet meat" option where you could get less gravy. I highly recommend choosing that style, especially since the gravy overpowered the meat and compromised the structural integrity of the sandwich.

input: Picked up takeout from Village Whiskey (so I can't review the actual restaurant). The Whiskey Burger is pricy ($26) but is amazing if you're ok with a greasier burger. Super tender, the bacon is awesome and it's pretty big. If you can get past the price then highly recommend it. The Duck Fat fries are also rich and delicious.
Rewrite this for me: I ordered takeout from Village Whiskey, so I cannot provide a review of the restaurant itself. However, I must mention that the Whiskey Burger, despite being a bit expensive at $26, is truly remarkable if you don't mind a burger with extra grease. It is incredibly tender, with fantastic bacon and a substantial size. If you can overlook the price, I highly recommend giving it a try. Additionally, the Duck Fat fries are indulgent and flavorsome.

input: Blew $80 on food for the family was worth it food was hot and orange chicken best I've tasted in a awhile..now it will be the place we get Asian food!!
Rewrite this for me: I spent $80 on food for the family, but it was definitely worth it. The food was piping hot, and the orange chicken was the best I've tasted in a long time. We have now found our go-to place for Asian cuisine!

input:

I was searching for a laundry mat that would be safe, clean and not full of questionable people.  I was so happy to find this facility. input:

I will say the garlic bread they bring out before the meal was AH-MAZING! I could have probably eaten my weight in just the bread. 

Overall - I probably wouldn't eat there again myself. But it could have been an off night. There is just too much competition in the food world around St Louis!
Rewrite this for me:
Last night, we hurriedly went for a dinner late in the night. The prices were undeniably steep. Both couples agreed to share a plate, which visibly annoyed our server. While the food was decent, it certainly didn't justify the high cost.

However, I must admit that the garlic bread they served before the meal was absolutely incredible! I could have easily devoured a whole loaf by myself.

All in all, I personally wouldn't choose to dine there again. Perhaps it was just an off night, but given the abundance of competition in the St. Louis food scene, there are plenty of other options to explore.

input:

I will be going back to the Haven. Might go for, say lunch on a Tuesday, so it's less busy.
Rewrite this for me:
I decided to grab a burger while watching the Seahawks/Saints game today, and as expected, the place was extremely crowded. But it was justified because the Haven burger that I ordered was absolutely amazing.

Since I was seated right by the entrance, I didn't have the chance to venture further than six feet into the restaurant. input:

input: I had the Chicken Marsala recommended by our waiter. The chicken was very thin, tough, and dry. The pasta was under cooked and stuck together. There was absolutely no flavor. My friend ordered the lasagne and did not like it all. There was only a thin layer of pasta and no flavor. My other friend was still eating her dinner and they cleared her plate when she went to the restroom, after she told the waiter she was not finished. They did bring her a new meal in a doggie bag. The positives are a Great atmosphere and live music. I enjoyed dancing with my husband. However, very expensive for awful food.
Rewrite this for me:
Our waiter recommended the Chicken Marsala, but unfortunately, it turned out to be a disappointment. The chicken was incredibly thin, tough, and dry, while the pasta was undercooked and clumped together. It lacked any sort of flavor. Similarly, my friend ordered the lasagna, but found it equally unsatisfying. The dish only had a thin layer of pasta and lacked any flavor as well.

To make matters worse, while my other friend was still enjoying her meal, the waitstaff prematurely cleared her plate while she was in the restroom, despite her informing the waiter that she was not finished. On a positive note, the atmosphere at the restaurant was great, with the added bonus of live music. I did, however, enjoy dancing with my husband. However, considering the subpar quality of the food, the high prices were simply not justifiable.

input: This place is a gem.Attractive space, great location near Broad Street line, plenty on street parking. BYOB. I've been twice and enjoyed every dish. Highlights were the chaats, beef short ribs, lamb vindaloo, beet salad, breads/pickles, and chai. We got the chocolate cake for the table to share each time and everyone loved it. Can get takeout beer at the corner bar. We'll be back.
Rewrite this for me: This location is truly a gem. It has an appealing interior, a convenient location near the Broad Street line, and ample on-street parking. It's also a BYOB establishment. I have personally dined here twice and have thoroughly enjoyed every dish on both occasions. The standout items for me were the mouth-watering chaats, delectable beef short ribs, flavorful lamb vindaloo, refreshing beet salad, delightful breads and pickles, and comforting chai. Additionally, we ordered the chocolate cake to share with the table each time and it received rave reviews from everyone. If you're in the mood for takeout beer, there's a corner bar nearby where you can grab some. Needless to say, we will definitely be returning.

input: This is my favorite restaurant!  I always order their ceviche, which is delicious.  The atmosphere is fun, and the service is great.  Alex was our server, and he was friendly, attentive and thoughtful.

input: Love this store!  Who doesn't!  The salad bar is fresh and they have all types of ethnic food to try.  N-JOY

input: I love this place.  The food is great and the space and staff are very pleasant.  Highly recommended for vegetarians and non-vegetarians alike.

input: Took a while to get actual service but once we did I was happy. The gumbo was awesome and loved the chicken & waffles. Friendly staff and right on Bourbon St for good people watching!

input:
As airport grab-and-go restaurants are, Earl does a decent job with a variety of sandwich options including turkey, tuna and even a Hawaiian. But today I could smell the roast beef and so I got that one. Yum. Good portion of sliced beef that was beyond medium cooked with cheddar cheese and a yummy horseradish sauce. Nope, don't get lettuce or tomatoes on it. It's perfect the way it is.

And since it's right between the security station and the top of the D gates (right near the Delta SkyClub!), it's easy to get and eat at the gate or on board.
Rewrite this for me:
Earl, an airport grab-and-go restaurant, offers a decent selection of sandwiches including turkey, tuna, and even Hawaiian. However, the aroma of the roast beef caught my attention today, so I decided to go with that option. It was absolutely delicious—a generous portion of medium-cooked sliced beef complemented by melted cheddar cheese and a delectable horseradish sauce. I opted not to add lettuce or tomatoes because it was already perfect the way it was.

Additionally, its convenient location between the security station and the top of the D gates (close to the Delta SkyClub!) allows for easy accessibility and the option to enjoy the sandwich at the gate or during the flight.

input: WOW!  What a fantastic place!  Food A+, Service A+++  We started with an appetizer of cheese curds served with a red pepper jelly.  LOVED IT!  I ordered the fish tacos and the wife ordered a beer brat for dinner.  We both thoroughly enjoyed what we ordered!  The portions were huge and priced just right for the portion size.  Our server was on it!  Very attentive and was very knowledgeable about the menu and made us feel very welcomed.  The manager stopped by and asked how everything was.  I let him know that I am pretty sure I have found a cool new place to hang out, have a beer and watch football. I will be back!

The manager informed us about their fantastic deals on game days and also mentioned their delicious brunch options available on weekends. As we were leaving, everyone bid us farewell and kindly reminded us to pick up a root beer candy on our way out. I am definitely coming back to this place!

input:

.

input:
Too big, too expensive and too far from Downtown.  

I was here for a conference, which seemed like an awesome idea. It wasn't.  I'm in Direct Sales and (like most people at this conference) don't have tons of extra money to spend on mediocre meals when I'm traveling.  $10 for a slice of generic pizza, small side salad and a soda for lunch.   I understand it's a hotel but there weren't any options close by.  Just getting your car from valet was a hassle and took a lot of time.  Being such a big property, it made getting to restaurants off the property really time intensive.  Since you're so far out of Nashville (out near the airport), the good little holes you find when you're in a city are pretty nonexistent.  

The property itself was great.  The hotel is HUGE but really pretty.  I enjoyed walking around but was really happy when I found what I didn't know existed...a shortcut between my room and the Convention Center.  It took my 10-15 minute walk down to about 3 minutes!  BONUS!  Like I said, this place is ginormous.  

Room: Our room was great.  I shared a wonderful suite in the Garden Conservatory with 2 other girls.  We were under a group rate and my friend was quoted $200/night, which is awesome for the space we had.  We had a large room (probably used as a hospitality suite for groups) for socializing.  It had a great bar area set-up and a nice big fridge and lots of drawer space.  Our bedroom was separated by doors that could be locked from either side (like an adjoining room), so it looked like the hospitality suite could be reserved without reserving the room.  It was different than what I was expecting, but whatevs.  It was fine.  So, I wasn't there at check-in.  The girl who reserved the room checked in a couple days earlier than my friend and I.  So, Sunday comes, and the bill was waiting for us when we woke up.  Our friend was charged $1200 for one room (I'm guessing the suite) and $1400 for the other room.  YEP.  She reserved what she thought was a 2 room suite for $200.  The bedroom door was closed when she got there and she asked them to open it up. It was all arranged by the bellman.  She was never told that the bedroom wasn't included....kind of necessary if you're staying over for 6 nights, dontcha think???  So, she's being charged $2600 for what was supposed to be $1200.  Last I heard, the Gaylord's legal department was investigating what she was told, what she wasn't told and if they should charge her the entire amount.  

Checkout:  A FREAKING NIGHTMARE.  Between the money situation, which was not resolved as of late this week, and the 45 minute wait for a cart (in a hotel that holds thousands of people, you'd think they'd be plentiful and they aren't) and a 25 minute wait for the car, my friend and I decided to sweat it out and schlep our goods to the door where our car would be delivered to us.  It was not a short walk and we had a TON of stuff, which meant multiple trips.  UGH.

I'm sure I'll be back for another conference (I am pretty sure my company has booked this for at least one more year....) but I'm not going to be happy about it.  I might even consider driving down, staying in a hotel somewhere downtown and driving out to the Conference stuff.
Rewrite this for me:
The hotel was too big, too expensive, and too far from Downtown. It was not a good experience for me as a Direct Sales representative who didn't have extra money to spend on meals during travel. The prices for basic meals were exorbitant, with a slice of generic pizza, small side salad, and a soda costing $10. Despite being a hotel, there weren't any nearby dining options. The process of getting my car from valet was also time-consuming and inconvenient due to the hotel's large size. Being located far from Nashville limited the availability of good local restaurants. 

However, the hotel property itself was impressive, with its grandeur and aesthetics. I enjoyed exploring, and thankfully, I stumbled upon a shortcut that significantly reduced the walking time between my room and the Convention Center. This made my 10-15 minute walk a quick 3 minutes, which was a pleasant surprise considering the enormous size of the hotel.

Regarding our room, it was fantastic. I shared a spacious suite in the Garden Conservatory with two other individuals. We managed to secure a group rate, with my friend being quoted $200 per night, a great deal considering the size of the suite. The suite included a large room suitable for socializing, complete with a well-equipped bar area, a sizable fridge, and ample drawer space. Our bedroom was separated by lockable doors, similar to adjoining rooms, which was different from my expectations but still acceptable. However, I was not present during check-in, and my friend who made the reservation a few days prior was surprised to find an unexpectedly high bill upon waking up on Sunday. She was charged $1200 for one room and $1400 for the other, totaling $2600. She had reserved what she believed to be a two-room suite for $200, but the bedroom was closed off when she arrived. The bellman had arranged everything without informing her that the bedroom was not included. This lack of communication was crucial, especially for a six-night stay. The hotel's legal department was investigating the situation and determining whether she should be billed the full amount.

The checkout process was a nightmare. The money issue remained unresolved, and we had to wait 45 minutes for a cart despite the hotel's capacity to accommodate thousands of guests. Similarly, the wait for our car took 25 minutes. Frustrated, my friend and I decided to carry our belongings to the door where our car would be delivered, which was a long and arduous journey due to the distance and the amount of stuff we had to transport.

I anticipate having to attend another conference at this hotel, as my company has likely booked it for at least another year. However, I am not looking forward to it and may consider staying in a downtown hotel and commuting to the conference instead.

input:
This was my first time dining at Ava and I enjoyed most of it. We ordered the Ricotta cheese & toasted bread and although the flavor was excellent, I thought the bread to cheese ratio was off quite a bit. The ricotta came in a tiny ramekin typically reserved for flavored butters, so I expected more for an appetizer. 

The two pizzas split among a couple of people were the sausage and the potato with rosemary. They were both tasty but I think they forgot the Rosemary on ours. Still yummy, tho! Another entree was the grouper w/Israeli couscous. Scrumptious!

Dessert was a must and the zeppoles, or sugared donuts, were amazing. The cherry tart a little less so, but one person at our table loved it, so maybe it was just not my cup of tea. The cherries were a sort of candied cherry-interesting, but sweet with a very dense crust. Again, just not my personal fave. 

I will definitely return to try other menu items that looked great-like the pastas made in-house daily...that's next!!
Rewrite this for me:
I had my first dining experience at Ava and overall, it was enjoyable. We started with the Ricotta cheese & toasted bread, which had excellent flavor. However, I felt that the ratio of bread to cheese was a bit off. The portion of ricotta came in a small ramekin usually reserved for flavored butters, so I expected more for an appetizer.

Among the pizzas we ordered, the sausage and potato with rosemary were both tasty. Although, it seemed like they forgot the rosemary on ours. Nevertheless, they were still delicious! The grouper with Israeli couscous was also scrumptious as an entree.

Of course, we couldn't skip dessert. The zeppoles, or sugared donuts, were absolutely amazing. However, the cherry tart was a little less impressive for me. Although, one person at our table loved it, so it might just be a matter of personal preference. The cherries in the tart were candied and had an interesting flavor, but the crust was very dense. It just wasn't my favorite.

I'm definitely planning to return to Ava and explore the other enticing menu items, like the daily homemade pastas. That's next on my list!

input: 1st time eating here. Very clean, nice folks and very good sushi.  Would and will go back. Service was spot on, sushi was very fresh and reasonably priced .
Rewrite this for me: This was my first time trying this place out, and I was pleasantly surprised. The establishment was extremely clean, the staff were friendly, and the sushi was top-notch. I would definitely go back again in the future. The service was excellent, the sushi tasted incredibly fresh, and the prices were also reasonable.

input: This place is just the best. If you really have to ask why it's all in the name itself. If u don't like chicken then don't come here bc their birds are fly! Don't forget to try their fried corn on the cobs. It's dank!
Rewrite this for me: This place is truly wonderful. The reason for its excellence is apparent in the name itself. If you are not a fan of chicken, it's best to avoid this place because their poultry is exceptional! input: REALLY below average food.  Akin to waffle house.  I wanted this to be good based on the reviews but not so.  The pancakes tasted like a frozen processed version, "homemade" maple syrup was watery/sugary with fake flavoring.  Trees make authentic syrup, not people.  The hash browns were greasy and fairly tasteless. The bacon overcooked, hard and chewy.  Obviously had been sitting awhile. Overall, very uninspired food.  Unfortunately, this is one of those places that is living on an outdated "must go" reputation.  There are much better offerings in Nashville.
Rewrite this for me: The food quality was significantly below average, comparable to a Waffle House. Despite the positive reviews, it did not live up to expectations. The pancakes tasted like a processed, frozen version, while the "homemade" maple syrup was thin, overly sweet, and lacked genuine flavor. Authentic syrup comes from trees, not from people. The hash browns were oily and lacked any distinct taste. The bacon was overcooked, tough, and chewy, indicating it had been sitting out for a while. Overall, the food lacked creativity and enthusiasm. Unfortunately, this restaurant seems to rely on an outdated reputation as a "must-go" place, but there are far superior dining options available in Nashville.

input: Excellent.  Went there for lunch (the budget option).  Prix fixe menu was tempting.  Wife had the prime rib po'boy with the soup of the day (tomato fennel).  Both were excellent (the po'boy being an upscale interpretation, with gruyere and a really good horseradish sauce).  I had the seafood jamabalaya and seafood gumbo, also excellent (probably the best I've had).
Rewrite this for me: It was an excellent dining experience when we went there for lunch, opting for the budget-friendly option. The prix fixe menu was quite enticing. My wife chose the prime rib po'boy accompanied by the soup of the day, which happened to be tomato fennel. Both dishes were superb, with the po'boy offering a sophisticated twist, featuring gruyere cheese and a delectable horseradish sauce. As for me, I indulged in the seafood jamabalaya and seafood gumbo, both of which were outstanding - possibly the best I've ever had.

input:

input: My husband and I are not "spring chickens", but we love to Par-Tee. The server immediately welcomed us and asked about our drink preferences.  He was very knowledgeable and helpful. He was incredibly knowledgeable and helpful. The variety of beers available was impressive, and the selection of spirits was exquisite. Even though the menu for bar food was limited, the quality was superb. Initially, I was hesitant to try the pork belly due to its unattractive name. However, when my husband ordered it and convinced me to taste it, I became a fan. I highly recommend trying their pork belly sliders! Hopefully, they will continue adding more delectable tapas to their menu. These individuals definitely have their act together and are remarkably engaging. We definitely plan on returning frequently.

input:

Not worth $12 on its own.

Rewrite this for me: The restaurant is average or slightly above average despite the hype it receives. It is on the expensive side, as evidenced by the fact that for $10 or $12, one would expect to receive fries with their burger, instead of a large portion meant for sharing priced at $8. The only reason I visited was to try their bison burger. Our order consisted of one beer, one iced tea, one regular burger, one bison burger, and a shared large fry, totaling around $37. This seems rather unreasonable. The restaurant tries too hard to be unique or interesting, but it ultimately ruins the dining experience. The bison burger was disappointing with unnecessary slaw and BBQ sauce that did not align with the promised Carolina bison burger. It is not worth the $12 price tag on its own. I have already been there and done that, and see no reason to return. Moving on to the next option.

input:
Before I share the main issue, I want to share the reason I give any stars is because of our awesome server, LaToya. She was thoughtful and engaging! 

The black bean burger was dry. Sweet potato fries were good. 

Today while at lunch with a group of colleagues the most disturbing thing happened. I noticed the manager in a green sweater lingering around the entrance and then two cop cars with lights flashing pulled up and 3 officers rushed in walked to the table next to us that the manager was pointing to and one of the officer's proceeded to pull out their handcuffs and tell the guy delivering food to put food down at the table and hands behind his back. They escorted him near the front door and had him sit down for a moment before taking him outside in freeZing cold with no jacket where he stood for a few minutes while cops came in and out of restaurant. 

This entire thing was poorly handled, disturbing and unsettling not only to the customers but the other staff. They should have had the cops walk back away from where customers were and deal with it there. Then all the managers disappeared not available to talk to any of the customers let alone apologize or acknowledge people being unsettled. 

No one needs to know why the arrest happened but there needed to be more care for customers and staff in how it was handled. 

Not ok!!!
Rewrite this for me:
I would like to begin by expressing my appreciation for our exceptional server, LaToya, who truly made our dining experience enjoyable. However, I must address a rather disconcerting incident that occurred during our lunch today with my colleagues.

While we were seated, my attention was drawn to the presence of the manager, who was wearing a green sweater and seemed to be lingering near the entrance. Suddenly, two police cars arrived with their lights flashing, and three officers urgently entered the restaurant. They headed directly towards the table adjacent to ours, which the manager had pointed out. To my dismay, one of the officers proceeded to handcuff the person who was delivering food to that table, instructing him to place the food down and place his hands behind his back.

Subsequently, the suspect was escorted to a nearby area close to the front door and was made to sit for a brief period. It was chilling to witness him standing outside, exposed to the freezing temperatures without a jacket, while various police personnel frequently entered and exited the premises.

The entire incident was handled in an extremely poor manner, displaying a lack of consideration and deeply unsettling both the customers and the other members of the restaurant staff. It would have been more appropriate for the authorities to deal with the situation away from the public eye. Furthermore, it was disappointing that none of the managers were available to address any concerns from the customers or even offer an apology for the disturbance caused.

While the specifics of the arrest are not crucial to disclose, it is important to stress the need for better care and attention towards the well-being of both the customers and the staff in handling such situations. This kind of handling is completely unacceptable and left all of us feeling shaken and uneasy.

input: Love this little shop so much for so many reasons. First off, whenever I'm on my way to Sweet Divas, I can smell the spices wafting from this little, inviting shop. Their knowledgeable staff is available and more than happy to assist you in finding the right spice you are looking for all your cooking needs. Over the years I've purchased many items from here and I can attest that they do last a long time (about a year, year and a half, including some stuff I use often!). I see all kind of specialty salts for example (onion salt, celery salt) as well as sugars and powders (lavender vanilla sugar, vanilla bean powder). Their products even seem to taste fresher (I can taste a difference between their cinnamon and nutmeg and what I can get at a dollar store, for example). The prices aren't too bad and they last long. My three bottles pictured cost about $19, but that will last a good year, so its worth it to me.

input:

Verdict - Gator gumbo, end of story.

input:
My mother, aunt and myself went on this walking tour of Ybor with stops for good food.  What a nice time!  Our guide,  Raymond was very knowledgeable and friendly.  
It was about 3 hrs long,  we passed that 3 hr mark because we were sidetracked a few times and chit chatted quite a bit, lol. 
We learned great details and background about the early days of tampa, the culture, people and ybor in general,  very informative! Along the way we stopped for food tastings . Everything was great,  especially the stone soup company Cuban sandwich!  I would recommend everyone to go on this tour,  visiting or lived here for years this is a fun adventure.  And for the step counters we chalked up over 5000 steps ! It will help offset all the wonderful calories you take in on the tour haha
Rewrite this for me: I had a wonderful time going on a walking tour of Ybor with my mother and aunt. The tour included stops for delicious food, making the experience even more enjoyable. Our guide, Raymond, was friendly and incredibly knowledgeable. Although the tour was supposed to last about 3 hours, we ended up going over that time because we got sidetracked and spent quite a bit of time chatting. It was worth it though, as we learned a lot of interesting details about the early days of Tampa, the culture, the people, and Ybor itself. The tour also included food tastings along the way, and everything we tried was fantastic. The Cuban sandwich from the Stone Soup Company was particularly amazing. I highly recommend this tour to everyone, whether you are visiting or have lived here for years. It's a fun adventure that also helps you get some exercise - we ended up walking over 5000 steps! This definitely helps offset the wonderful calories you consume during the tour, haha.

input: Went here with a friend after having an incredible experience at Laurel and was hoping for more of the same at a slightly less bulgy pricepoint, and oh my, is it worth it... First thing to hit the table (or bar in this case) was a three dollar beef fat biscuit that was the best thing ive eaten in this city all year. We went on to eat many more things which i will try to name now... Stars were Foie with Apricot Miso, Pork Cheeks with some insanely good vegetables, trout pumpernickel soldiers and one of the best cocktails ive had in a damn long time, the ouroboros.   The are playing around with cold smoking things in there and on their BAR MENU!   Honestly, place is just terrific and i meant to write this review sooner but hey... better late than never.  Now that i think of it, im getting hungry... maybe ill head to East Passyunk for some of the best this city has to offer!

After being impressed by my experience at Laurel, I decided to visit ITV with a friend, hoping for a similar, but more affordable, dining experience. And let me tell you, it was definitely worth it. The staff is not only attentive but aesthetically pleasing as well (I want to paint a complete picture for you). 

The first delightful surprise that arrived at our table (or rather, the bar) was a three-dollar beef fat biscuit, which happened to be the best thing I've tasted in the city all year. I couldn't resist expressing my satisfaction to Chef Nick Elmi, who, just like at Laurel, made an appearance in the dining room. 

We proceeded to try several other dishes that I'll attempt to name... The standout stars were the Foie with Apricot Miso, Pork Cheeks accompanied by incredibly flavorful vegetables, and delicate trout pumpernickel soldiers. Additionally, I wish the store had a larger, brighter, and cleaner space. The cramped aisles, dust accumulation, and flickering yellow lights don't create the same trendy and inviting atmosphere as other beauty stores. If I were to offer one piece of advice to management, it would be to focus on improving the store's appearance. Other than that, I am generally satisfied with my experiences at Sally's.

input:
Let me preface by saying that I have been getting my hair cut by a guy in Austin for seven years, even though I've lived in other cities for half that time. He is that good. The couple of times that I've strayed, I have been severely disappointed in the outcome. But I wasn't planning a trip back to Austin for a while and badly needed a cut, so I decided to bite the bullet.

My friend walks in a few weeks ago with *srsly* the cutest short hair cut. And so I ask her who and where, and she says Rodney Mitchell. I figured that this place would be too expensive, but she corrected my thinking on the matter. So I called to make an appointment with her guy (whose name I sadly cannot remember at the moment) and Rodney answered the phone. Turns out the guy my friend had seen didn't do morning appointments and all my afternoons were filled, so Rodney said "look, I'm the owner, I can absolutely vouch for Allison who has several openings in the next few days." So I thought, alright, he's the owner so he knows his stuff--I'll do it.

Allison absolutely did not disappoint. First off, she's a total sweetheart, but not super chatty (I appreciate stylists who can be content to both hold and not hold a convo while working) so there was no pressure there. I came in with my laptop and several photos I'd found that approximated what I wanted in a haircut, as I couldn't find exactly the right one. We talked about it a bit, discussed front and back length, bangs, etc. and she said alright and went to it. What she gave me was the cutest damn shaggy bob that I never thought possible. I seriously can't wait to go back.

One of the other awesome things about RMS is that they give you a discount for your first visit and I believe they have some kind of discount for students and teachers. They also will give you *another* discount when you refer people. So I got my friend a discount, and then referred a friend, so I'll get another discount when I go back for my next cut. All good things when you're trying your best to be a frugal  grad student.

input:
So much to like about this place--the beautiful Mercer Building location, the spaciousness, the lovely, friendly baristas. But there are a couple of important cons for me. Biggest being, the music is constant and too loud, ruining everything you go to a coffee shop to do: read, work, reflect, or enjoy a good conversation. When I asked for it to be turned down, they told me they can't--it just plays at one level all the time, and the speakers  are everywhere so you can't get away from it. It sucks.

Secondly, if you're a tea drinker, you're out of luck. They don't serve the tea in pots, but huge, sloppy individual filters--it makes your beverage totally ungainly, hard to drink and is really off putting.

Pros: gluten free goodies and yummy Italian sodas. I'd love to spend more time here, but the music usually drives me out after 10 minutes.
Rewrite this for me:
There are many aspects to appreciate about this place, such as its beautiful location in the Mercer Building, the spacious atmosphere, and the presence of friendly baristas. However, there are a couple of significant drawbacks that I find important to mention. The main concern for me is the constant and excessively loud music, which disrupts activities one typically engages in at a coffee shop, such as reading, working, reflecting, or having a pleasant conversation. Despite my request, they informed me that they are unable to adjust the volume as it remains at a consistent level throughout the day, and the speakers are positioned in a way that escaping the sound is nearly impossible. This is quite frustrating.

Additionally, if you prefer tea over coffee, you might be disappointed here. Rather than serving tea in pots, they provide oversized and messy individual filters, which make the drinking experience awkward, difficult, and unappealing.

On the positive side, they do offer gluten-free treats and delicious Italian sodas. It would be delightful to spend more time at this place, but unfortunately, the incessant music usually forces me to leave after a mere ten minutes.

input:
Spice n Grill has the best Indian food in St. Louis. We had the beef nihari, palak paneer, and naan. The palak and beef were perfectly spiced, adequately spicy, and crave-worthy. I've never had a nihari dish before and I will be sure to try it again. 

The restaurant doesn't have great seating  in the store, so I will take food to go next time. The owner served us and he was very nice, but I don't think people eat in the restaurant very often. 

I was so excited to see that the previous owners of 'Indian Food' have opened a new restaurant and I would recommend it if you're in the mood for delicious take-out.
Rewrite this for me:
If you're looking for the best Indian food in St. Louis, Spice n Grill is the place to go. We tried their beef nihari, palak paneer, and naan, and they were absolutely phenomenal. The spices in the palak and beef were on point, providing just the right amount of heat to make them truly addictive. I had never tasted nihari before, but it was a delightful surprise and I plan on indulging in it again.

While the seating arrangement inside the restaurant could use some improvement, it doesn't deter from the amazing food. On my next visit, I'll opt for take-out to enjoy their delicious cuisine in the comfort of my own home. The owner, who personally served us, was incredibly friendly and welcoming. However, it seems that most people prefer taking their food to go rather than dining in.

I was thrilled to discover that the previous owners of the popular 'Indian Food' establishment have opened this new venture. If you're in the mood for mouthwatering take-out, I highly recommend giving Spice n Grill a visit.

input:
I've come from Cali where boba is very common there. However I was thinking this place would have had the same feel. After being told this place branched off from California, I was disappointed. 

I'm more of a natural person. I enjoy real flavor, real fruits, and of course the perfect boba. I notice that some flavors were used by real fruits but others were just powder which I could definitely taste the different. Especially the taro flavor, being one of my favorites. 

But, if you're not too concern about natural vs powder flavor then this place could be good for you. They ask what level you would like you sweetness and any additional add-ons you would like. I always get boba but sometimes the grass jelly is pretty good too! I'd recommend you try. 

This is also a good place to catch up, talk, play board, card games and even do homework. I know it's always busy with students from the U of A and being told from them it's a nice area to just hang out, that's a pretty good sign. 

Maybe I'm just too picky, but I think it could be better. 

"See it, taste it, Yelp it"
Rewrite this for me:
I come from California, where boba is very popular. I had hoped that this place would have a similar vibe since it originated from California, but to my disappointment, it didn't.

I prefer natural flavors made from real fruits, including the perfect boba. I noticed that some flavors here used real fruits, while others were artificial powders, which I could definitely taste the difference in. Especially with the taro flavor, which happens to be one of my favorites.

However, if you're not too concerned about natural versus artificial flavors, then this place might be good for you. They give you the option to choose the sweetness level and you can add additional toppings. I always get boba, but they also have pretty good grass jelly that you should try.

This place is also great for hanging out with friends, catching up, playing board or card games, or even doing homework. It's always busy with students from the University of Arizona, and hearing from them that it's a nice area to just relax is a good sign.

Maybe I'm just too particular, but I believe there is room for improvement.

"See it, taste it, Yelp it."

input: This is an updated review. I've been ordering from silver mine's at the same location for the last 4-5 years and they have only gotten progressively worse. Don't ask for anything to be added to your soup or chili; they'll charge you for the additions but will not include them in the order. They'll also most likely to include the free side such as the bread. It literally takes at least an hour to get your food delivered, maybe they should call Jimmy Johns and ask the what their secret is. This business is in major trouble with all of the other options available. The service is worse than if you had a bunch of kindergarteners running the business, at least they would be nice. You guys are right next to Eller Business School, why don't you ask them how you can improve??? Currently, this place is an embarrassment to their industry, and a waste of space on University Blvd. NEVER ORDERING FROM THIS PLACE AGAIN.
Rewrite this for me: This review is an updated version of my experience with Silver Mine's. I have been ordering from their location for the past 4-5 years, but unfortunately, their service has only deteriorated over time. It is frustrating that they charge for additions to your soup or chili, but fail to actually include them in your order. Additionally, the free side, like bread, is often missing as well. The delivery time is incredibly slow, taking at least an hour, whereas other establishments like Jimmy Johns seem to have a quicker delivery process. Given the numerous alternatives available, this business is clearly facing significant challenges. The service provided by Silver Mine's is even worse than if it were run by a group of kindergarteners who would at least be polite. Considering you are situated right next to Eller Business School, why not seek their advice on how to improve? Presently, this establishment is a disgrace to the industry and a pointless presence on University Blvd. I will never order from this place again.

input:
Bought my beautiful new bike from this shop a few weeks ago then promptly crashed it (curse you, trolley tracks!). I brought it back to the shop this afternoon to see if there was any way they could try to fix the front basket, which was pretty mangled, and to give the bike a once-over to make sure it was safe to ride. I was expecting to have to leave the bike with them for a few days, but the whole process took less than a half hour. Not only did they fix the basket (not perfect, but pretty damn close), but they also fixed the gear shifter that was a little out of whack... FOR FREE.  I couldn't believe it. 

I also want to note that everyone in the shop- from the owners, to the sales people on the floor, to the mechanics, to the dog that greets you at the door- is so friendly and welcoming. I am so happy I found them.
Rewrite this for me:
A few weeks ago, I purchased a beautiful new bike from this shop. Unfortunately, I promptly crashed it due to trolley tracks. Today, I visited the shop to inquire if they could fix the significantly damaged front basket and ensure the bike was safe to ride. I anticipated leaving the bike with them for several days, but to my surprise, the entire process took less than thirty minutes. Not only did they repair the basket (not flawlessly, but remarkably close), but they also fixed the slightly misaligned gear shifter at absolutely no cost. I was astounded.

Furthermore, I must mention that the entire staff of the shop, from the owners and salespeople to the mechanics and even the friendly dog who greets you at the entrance, exudes a welcoming and amiable disposition. Discovering this shop has truly brought me immense joy.

input: I love going in there just to look around. The prices are a bit high, but the store is like a Disneyland for adults. I LOVE IT!
Rewrite this for me: I thoroughly enjoy visiting that place merely for the purpose of browsing. Although the prices are slightly on the expensive side, the store exhibits an atmosphere similar to that of an amusement park designed exclusively for grown-ups. I am absolutely enamored with it!

input:
Underrated burger alert!!

Randomly came into Pag's during a stroll around Doylestown. The menu wasn't super appealing, actually, so I just went with a cheeseburger. Legitimately, one of the best cheeseburgers I've had in a while! Tasted like a quality Big Mac! Patty wasn't too thick, bun didn't overshadow the burger and whatever sauce they used - YUM.

We were in the wine bar section - ambiance is really nice; def not very kid friendly (we had our son with us.) but staff was friendly and accommodating.

We will totally be back next time we are in the mood for a good burger!
Rewrite this for me:
Attention burger lovers! Prepare for an underrated gem that will blow your taste buds away! While aimlessly exploring Doylestown, I stumbled upon Pag's and decided to give their menu a chance. Honestly, it didn't scream deliciousness, but I went ahead and ordered a cheeseburger anyway. Boy, am I glad I did! This cheeseburger ranks among the best I've had in a long time. It truly reminded me of a top-notch Big Mac with its flavorful patty, perfectly balanced bun-to-burger ratio, and the mouthwatering sauce that was slathered on. 

Although we were seated in the wine bar area, which had a delightful ambiance, I must note that this place might not be the most suitable for families with young children (we had our son in tow). Nevertheless, the staff was friendly and accommodating, making our visit pleasant. Rest assured, when the craving for a fantastic burger strikes again, Pag's will be our go-to spot.

input: Absolutely wonderful food & service! Go there for lunch/dinner with my boyfriend at least once every two weeks. Prices are very much reasonable. Weekends get pretty packed so may have to wait a little bit but that's never an issue for us. Always get the Indian Pancake & the Hainanese Chicken or Curry Chicken. Other dishes are delicious as well. Never get tired of it!
Rewrite this for me: The food and service at this place are absolutely amazing! My boyfriend and I make it a point to visit for lunch or dinner at least once every two weeks. The prices are very reasonable, making it even more enjoyable. Although the weekends can get quite busy and we might have to wait a bit, it has never been an issue for us. Our go-to dishes are the Indian Pancake and the Hainanese Chicken or Curry Chicken, but honestly, all the other options are delicious too. We never seem to get tired of this place!

input: Pretty slow service and the waitresses aren't very kind. I guess I was expecting something different at a diner with high ratings but I understand it's in the middle of a tourist area. However, service should be a priority. Something that really bothered me was how much trash was left on the floor of the outside deck- it all has the potential to blow right into the ocean. NOT OKAY. I had to stand up several times to grab straw wrappers and napkins before they blew into the water. If you're going to have a waterfront/beach front business, be responsible about it. It would be a very easy fix-just a screen on the bottom of the fence. The food was good but I won't be back.
Rewrite this for me: The service at the diner was disappointingly slow and the waitresses were not very friendly. Despite its high ratings, I had hoped for a better experience. I understand that being located in a tourist area may affect the quality of service, but it should still be a priority. Additionally, I was troubled by the amount of trash on the outside deck, as it posed a risk of blowing into the ocean. This is not acceptable. I had to constantly stand up and retrieve straw wrappers and napkins before they ended up in the water. If you choose to operate a business near the waterfront or beach, it is crucial to take responsibility and address such issues. An easy solution would be to install a screen at the bottom of the fence. Although the food was enjoyable, I will not be returning.

input:
I recently had the pre fixe meal for $22 and I enjoyed the combination of tastes on my plate. The chicken was moist my veggies were tasty but a little too greasy....overall is was a great meal. 

I also use them for take out/delivery. I have always enjoyed the way the package their food, in plastic containers that I use over and over again until they look too worn out and I recycle them. I hate take out places that use so much boxes and cups and card board - it's extremely eco-unfriendly. 

The food here is never spectacular but is a good standby you will always come away enjoying. The prices seem a little steep but the restaurant atmosphere is contemporary, the service has always been splendid and the food is dependable.
Rewrite this for me:
I recently had the pre fixe meal at a cost of $22, and I  thoroughly enjoyed the harmonious blend of flavors on my plate. The chicken was moist, and the vegetables were delectable, although slightly oily. Overall, it was a delightful dining experience.

Moreover, I frequently opt for their take out or delivery services. The way they package their food in reusable plastic containers has always impressed me. I continue to reuse them until they become worn out, at which point I recycle them. I strongly dislike establishments that excessively use disposable boxes, cups, and cardboard, as it is highly detrimental to the environment.

While the cuisine here may not be exceptionally remarkable, it serves as a reliable go-to option. Although the prices may seem slightly steep, the modern restaurant ambiance, impeccable service, and dependable food are worth it.

input: It's no different than any other Chinese place. Same menu, etc. this place does have some good lunch specials though, and the food is always ready when I go to pick it up.
Rewrite this for me: This restaurant is just like any other Chinese eatery - it offers the same menu and everything. However, I must admit that they do have some fantastic lunch specials, and I always appreciate how promptly they have my food prepared for pick-up.

input: Finally got to eat here last night. Eclectic foodie menu. I had their onion tart as an app and Kerry had the veal meatballs with sauce on polenta, very delicious. The red gravy tasted like my own. We both ordered the special of citrus short ribs with fat noodles and brussel sprouts, peas. couldn't finish we will be back to try other interesting items. Small crowded but great friendly atmosphere
Rewrite this for me: Last night, I finally had the chance to dine at this place. Their menu offers a diverse range of dishes for food enthusiasts. To start, I opted for their onion tart, while Kerry enjoyed the veal meatballs with sauce on polenta - both were incredibly delicious. The red sauce reminded me of my homemade recipe. For the main course, we both ordered their special citrus short ribs served with fat noodles and a side of brussels sprouts and peas. The portion was generous, and although we couldn't finish it all, we left satisfied and with the intention of returning to try other intriguing dishes. Despite the small and crowded space, the atmosphere was warm and inviting, with friendly staff adding to the enjoyment of our evening.

input: Last night we tried to get into the oldest Italian Restaurant in South Philly. Thankfully, they couldn't fit us in, so our son said lets try Angelina's  so we walked around the corner and into a small Italian Restaurant.  Immediatly we felt at home.  Angelina is cooking in the front of the resaurant and her husband is servicing. There were 3 of us and we started off with Eggplant and roasted pepper appetizer.  One bite and we were hooked.  We ordered the Veal Osso Bocca, Carbonara and lasagna.  Everything was absolutly DELISH!!  Can't wait to go back!!!
Rewrite this for me: Yesterday evening, our attempt to secure a spot at South Philly's oldest Italian restaurant proved fruitless, much to our relief. Our son suggested we explore Angelina's instead. Following his advice, we ventured around the corner and stumbled upon a cozy Italian eatery. Instantly, it felt like our second home. As we entered, Angelina herself could be seen preparing meals in the front area, while her husband attended to the customers. With three of us in tow, we began our dining experience with a delectable Eggplant and roasted pepper appetizer. Just one taste and we were immediately captivated. Subsequently, we indulged in Veal Osso Bocca, Carbonara, and lasagna. Every dish was absolutely divine! We are eagerly anticipating our next visit to Angelina's.

input: great food, great view. Try the lobster mac and cheese
Rewrite this for me: Experience exceptional culinary delights accompanied by breathtaking scenery. Indulge in our delicious lobster mac and cheese sensation.

input: Super tasty and enormous portions. Some unique flavors too. Not much else to say but an amazing ice cream store that others should try to emulate.
Rewrite this for me: With its exceptionally delicious and incredibly generous portions, this ice cream store sets itself apart. Daring to introduce distinct and one-of-a-kind flavors, there's not much more to add other than that it's an extraordinary place that others should aspire to replicate.

input: The food is average. Drink specials are great but the place is rarely crowded. Last time I was there it was a Friday night at 10 pm. There were maybe 3 other parties at the bar. About 5 minutes after ordering our first drink, they announced it was last call...at 10:15 PM on a Friday night! Needless to say we left for a different bar in the area and have removed it from our options of places to go past 6 pm for drinks.
Rewrite this for me: The food is mediocre, although they do offer fantastic drink specials. However, the place is hardly ever packed. I remember the last time I went there was on a Friday night at 10 pm. Surprisingly, there were only three other groups at the bar. To our disappointment, just five minutes after placing our first drink order, they declared it was last call... on a Friday night, no less, at 10:15 pm! Needless to say, we promptly decided to head to another bar nearby, and we have since crossed it off our list of places to grab drinks past 6 pm.

input: A good place to order from when its late and you have the muchies... for whatever reason ;-)
Rewrite this for me: If you're feeling hungry late at night and craving something delicious, there's a fantastic spot to order from, no matter the reason for your munchies!

input:
You think Value City, you think cheap value, right? Wrong! 

Think Rothman prices with Ashley Furniture pieces. Not a Broyhill in sight. 

Negatives:
- Entertainment centers and TV stand selection is small, and over priced selection.
-Their "Clearance" section is laughable and not much of a sale. No one is going to pay $299 for a nicked up coffee table that was originally $350. Go lower. 
- Sectionals by themselves average around $1,000 by brands I've never heard of. 
- The staff hangs out like a clique chatting in the middle of the store rather than helping customers. 
-Dining sets are nothing special and overpriced as well. I've seen the same selection everywhere else at a lower price. 
-5% military discount? Ooooh you're going to knock $20 off my sofa! 

Only Positive:
-They have a few modern pieces. 

Overall:

I think they're high for low quality-mediocre furniture. Shop around town. Or if you do find something you must have here, wait for a holiday sale.
Rewrite this for me:
When you think of Value City, you may assume it offers cheap value, right? Well, that perception is incorrect!

Instead, picture Rothman prices combined with the quality of Ashley Furniture pieces. You won't find any Broyhill products here.

However, there are a few negatives to consider. Their selection of entertainment centers and TV stands is small, and the prices are quite high. Additionally, the "Clearance" section is far from impressive and doesn't offer much of a sale. Who would be willing to pay $299 for a coffee table with nicks and scratches, especially when it was originally priced at $350? They should definitely lower their prices.

Furthermore, their sectionals, which are from unfamiliar brands, come with an average price tag of $1,000. This seems excessive. Additionally, the staff tends to gather and chat amongst themselves in the middle of the store, rather than assisting customers. It gives off a clique-like impression.

Moreover, their dining sets are nothing special and also overpriced. You can find the same selection elsewhere at a lower price. And their 5% military discount? It equates to a mere $20 off a sofa. Not very enticing.

On a positive note, they do have a few modern pieces available.

Overall, I feel that Value City offers mediocre, low-quality furniture at high prices. It's advisable to shop around in different stores in town. However, if you do find something you truly love here, it's worth waiting for a holiday sale.

input: I really like Franzone's. The owner is typically around, super friendly, and seems to really care about the product. While I'm not a big fan of sweet sauce, they also do a decent cheesesteak, fries, etc. Honestly, they may have been closer to a 4 if not that it's always just a really pleasant experience going in, which boosts their rating for me.
Rewrite this for me: Franzone's is one of my favorite places to go because of the owner's welcoming presence and genuine passion for their product. Even though I'm not particularly fond of sweet sauce, their cheesesteaks, fries, and other items are still enjoyable. If it weren't for the consistently positive experience I have every time I go there, I might rate them slightly lower, but the overall pleasant atmosphere really elevates their rating in my eyes.

input:
Finally had the chance to stop by Bab Cafe...what took us so long!  Both of us being Asian food fanatics, we are so happy to have Bab Cafe part of our ever expanding culinary experience here in Reno.

With the guidance of the very friendly and knowledgeable staff, we quickly got a hang of what to order, though there will be many more choices on our future visits.  Liking things a little spicy, we both ordered the Jeyuk Top-Bab (spicy pork).  What incredible flavor!  There is nothing that compares to this place in Reno.  The sauce bar gives you the opportunity to mix things up and the included miso soup is a definite bonus.  Great value for such a fresh, enjoyable meal.  Convenient downtown location to take away, dine in or have it delivered via UberEats.
Rewrite this for me:
After hearing so much about Bab Cafe, we finally made our way there and we can't believe it took us so long! As huge fans of Asian cuisine, we were thrilled to add Bab Cafe to our growing list of culinary experiences here in Reno.

The staff at Bab Cafe were incredibly friendly and knowledgeable, making it easy for us to navigate the menu. Although we know there are still plenty of dishes to try, we both decided to go for the Jeyuk Top-Bab (spicy pork) since we love a bit of spice. Let us tell you, the flavors were out of this world! Reno truly has nothing else like it. Another highlight was the sauce bar, which allowed us to customize our meal even more. Plus, the fact that they included miso soup was a wonderful bonus.

Considering the quality and enjoyment we got from our meal, the price point was great. Bab Cafe's downtown location makes it convenient for takeout, dining in, or even getting it delivered through UberEats. We can't wait to go back and explore more of their menu!

input: First meal in New Orleans. I had the $15 lunch special, a seafood stew (with oyster meat, crab claws, shrimp, and redfish) that came with a surprisingly thoughtful salad. Yeah, it's weird: I'm not even a fan of seafood and, to be honest, I wasn't even really that hungry. Still, before I knew what I was doing I had wolfed down the entire thing. The spice, consistency, tenderness of the meat -- all was precisely just right. Well worth your while.
Rewrite this for me: For my inaugural meal in New Orleans, I indulged in the $15 lunch special which consisted of a delectable seafood stew adorned with succulent oyster meat, crab claws, shrimp, and redfish, accompanied by a surprisingly well-composed salad. It may sound peculiar, considering my nonchalant attitude towards seafood and lack of appetite at the time, but to my own surprise, I devoured the entire dish without hesitation. The perfect balance of spice, texture, and tenderness in the meat made it an absolute delight, truly a culinary experience that should not be missed.

input: Totally worth the wait despite the heat!  I had the Vegan grits with a biscuit on the side. OMG!  So good. My 3 sisters each enjoyed their choices as well. Caution, the bloody Mary's are spicy!  The service was excellent. Really considering the wait was 45 mins, the line moved fast and then there was no long wait for our food. They have their process perfected!  Thanks Biscuit Love for a Delish breakfast!!!
Rewrite this for me: Despite the intense heat, the wait was completely worthwhile! I opted for the Vegan grits with a side of biscuit and boy, oh boy, it was fantastic! Each of my three sisters thoroughly enjoyed their own choices as well. A word of caution though, the bloody Mary's here pack quite a spicy punch! Nevertheless, the service was outstanding. Surprisingly, despite a 45-minute wait, the line moved swiftly and our food arrived without any prolonged delay. Biscuit Love certainly has their system down to a science! Thank you Biscuit Love for providing us with a delicious breakfast!

input:
Ichicoro Ane gets lots of things right and the best part about it is the combination of the ambiance with the food choices and whiskey selection. I'm very happy with this location and the servers I have encountered so far have been helpful and pleasant.

The katsu is great and I highly recommend it to people looking for a more filling dish on the menu. The bao buns were also good for a lighter fish. I haven't had anything I really regretted trying, but definitely ask your server about the portion sizes of each dish since they vary across the menu.

The cocktail selection is excellent. I even had a special Japanese Old Fashioned last time which was a little expensive, but well worth it for some quality Japanese whiskey. 

I'm looking forward to exploring the menu little by little. The best way to experience this is in a group setting so you can try more things and it really reminds me of Izakayas or Japanese pubs I visited in Japan and Korea.
Rewrite this for me:
Ichicoro Ane excels in many aspects, and what stands out the most is the perfect combination of the atmosphere, the food selection, and the array of whiskeys available. I am thoroughly pleased with this establishment, and the servers I have encountered so far have been both helpful and pleasant.

The katsu is outstanding and I highly recommend it to those seeking a more satisfying option from the menu. The bao buns, on the other hand, are a fantastic choice for a lighter meal. I have yet to try something that I genuinely regret, but it's wise to inquire with your server about portion sizes as they do vary throughout the menu.

The array of cocktails is top-notch. During my last visit, I indulged in a special Japanese Old Fashioned, which was slightly pricey but absolutely worth it for the high-quality Japanese whiskey it offered.

I eagerly look forward to gradually exploring the menu further. It is best enjoyed in the company of a group, allowing for the opportunity to sample a greater variety of dishes. This experience truly reminds me of the Izakayas and Japanese pubs I frequented in Japan and Korea.

input: Love this bakery!! Great breakfast sandwiches, coffee, and donuts! My friend and I love coming on weekend mornings

input: There is a great selection of whiskey/bourbon to suit anyone's taste. We had burgers with the fried egg on it and it was soo good and probably one of the best burgers I've ever had. input:
Although there are countless little Mexican places below Washington Avenue, I never get sick of them and always look forward to trying the new kid on the block. This time it was El Sabor Poblano on Federal, which could not look less special if it tried.

I liked that there were 3 fish tacos on the menu.  I picked the fried and battered version, though the tortilla chip covered fish could have been awesome. I was instantly impressed when I opened one of my three and found that El Sabor puts an entire filet of fish in each taco! The flakey meat had no fishy taste. These tacos came with the more American toppings of lettuce and, tomato, and cheese. I bet I could have gotten cilantro and onion if I asked. The sole staff member in the place seemed happy to accommodate us- well, we were the only ones dining in.

Another taco filling option that comes with more traditional toppings is the super crispy chorizo, only $8 for 3. There was no detectable gristle here, something I have often come across at this little places.

As unassuming as it looks, this particular South Philly Mexican place is worth stopping by.

input:
You would think from the size of the place it would be good for groups, but in my experience with 9 people on Saturday at 11am it was about a very hungry, tiring wait to get a seat. 

We tried to make reservations, but they do not take them. And I think we were too small to be put in the side meeting room. So hangry we stood, hoping for just the right table to leave.

The manager was nice enough to offer to fill cups of coffee for us while we waited. But I thought it was odd that they just didn't refill the pot for everyone who was waiting. 

Now for the food...They have these 1/2 and 1/2 combos. Which I love! I got a turkey Reuben and salad. I asked for lots of sauerkraut, and they charged $0.50 for it.. Which is no biggie but I'd expect a lot of kraut. Sadly there was not a lot of it.. But it was still a delicious sandwhich.  :) My friend got the sunrise chile rellenos. If I come back with a smaller party, that is what I would get.
Rewrite this for me:

As a result, we impatiently stood, hoping to secure a suitable table.

I specifically requested ample sauerkraut, but unfortunately, they charged an extra $0.50 for it. input: Terrace Lounge appears to want to have a great cocktail venue, but they fall short.  One bartender didn't even know there was a new cocktail menu.  The cocktail was weak and watery, and the liquors they have here and throughout Peppermill are the most unfortunate corporate types.  The service is also very spotty.  It confounded me how four bartenders could not seem to handle about 45 customers.  They didn't have any bar areas, so they all floated around the circle, but then they'd stop, often just short of me and go to the waitress stations to fill their orders.  You can't really build up any rapport with four bartenders floating around trying to serve everyone.  I also hated the people there.  Sorry, but many were your run-of-the-mill casino gamblers.  Why don't you just sit at a machine and play?  You didn't come here for the drinks or to smooze with the bartenders, so seriously, go sit at a machine.  One just sat next to me and lite up a cancer stick and the smoke just blew in my face.  Look, if I walk into a bar and sit next to someone, it's their turf.  They can smoke, fart, vomit on themselves, if I don't like it I can leave.  But if I'm there, it's my turf.  Don't come sit next to me and smoke, fart, or vomit all over yourself.  Or at least be frickin thoughtful and if you see your smoke wafting in my face, put your cancer stick and tray on the other side of the bar so it wafts in your face.  Oh, you don't like smoke in your face???  Me neither moron.  Your life revovles around throwing away your pension money in a mindless electronic game of cards and killing yourself with carcinogens and toxins, well go kill yourself in private, seriously.  You don't see me walking up to a bar and slitting my wrists and burning my money.  It's gross.  I probably just realized this, but I really enjoy Cin Cin not only because they have the best cocktails in town, but they have no machines at the bar.  Peppermill, if you want to create a cool cocktail bar, ditch the machines, train your staff, or hire bartenders with better service skills, and buy some independent liquors.
Rewrite this for me: Terrace Lounge falls short of being a great cocktail venue. One of the bartenders was unaware of the new cocktail menu, resulting in weak and watery drinks. The liquors available, both at Terrace Lounge and throughout Peppermill, were disappointing corporate options. The service was inconsistent, struggling to handle a moderate crowd of 45 customers. The lack of designated bar areas led to bartenders floating around the circle, frequently bypassing customers to fulfill orders at the waitress stations. This made it difficult to establish any rapport with the bartenders. Additionally, I disliked the clientele, as many were typical casino gamblers. It seemed more fitting for them to sit at slot machines rather than occupying the space meant for enjoying drinks and interacting with bartenders. One individual even sat next to me and began smoking, allowing the smoke to blow in my direction. While I understand that people have the right to smoke in a bar, it is necessary for smokers to be considerate and take precautions not to inconvenience others. If someone notices their smoke drifting towards someone else, they should position themselves and their tray on the opposite end of the bar. It is common sense to not enjoy having smoke blown in one's face. If your pastime primarily consists of mindlessly gambling away your pension while exposing yourself to harmful substances, it would be best to do so in private. Just as you don't see me engaging in self-harmful behaviors at the bar, please extend the same courtesy. It is distasteful. On a positive note, I have recently come to appreciate Cin Cin, not only for their superior cocktails but also because they do not have slot machines at their bar. If Peppermill desires to establish a genuinely impressive cocktail bar, they should eliminate the machines, train their staff or hire bartenders with better customer service skill sets, and invest in a more diverse selection of independent liquors.
