input:
Thank you for a lovely morning!  I was in NJ early and decided to stop in for a delicious diner breakfast.  I got a taylor ham, egg, and cheese and a short stack of blueberry pancakes (I simply couldn't decide between sweet or savory, plus leftovers are never a bad thing).  

The egg sandwich was fantastic.  I was nervous when they said they didn't have kaiser rolls so I went with a hamburger roll.  It was an excellent decision.  The roll was excellent - not just an average cheap hamburger roll.  They layered the cheese on the sandwich, which to me is a must for a true egg sandwich.  It was served with home fries, which were sauteed with large slices of peppers and onions.  I'm not the biggest breakfast potatoes fan, but these were great and I appreciated that they didn't clearly just scoop some food from a huge pile of pre-cooked home fries.

The pancakes were great and fluffy.  My one gripe was their use of smuckers pre-packaged syrup.  I realize that if they put syrup in a container, it probably wouldn't be real maple syrup, but I sort of wish I didn't know that they were giving me sub-par syrup.

The server was friendly and very attentive.  The coffee refills were constant, and the coffee was actually good (so many diners fail at coffee).  Bonus points for the server agreeing not to judge my decision to get two breakfasts.

All around, I loved this place and hope to go back soon.  Long live the Jersey diners!
Rewrite this for me:
I want to express my gratitude for the wonderful morning I had! I happened to be in NJ early and thought it would be nice to have a delightful diner breakfast. After some contemplation, I finally settled on a taylor ham, egg, and cheese sandwich along with a short stack of blueberry pancakes (choosing between sweet and savory was proving to be quite difficult, and having leftovers is always a good idea).

Let me start by saying that the egg sandwich was absolutely amazing. Initially, I was a bit worried when they informed me that they didn't have kaiser rolls, but I decided to go with a hamburger roll instead. And boy, was it a fantastic decision! The roll itself was exceptional, far surpassing your average cheap hamburger roll. They were generous with the cheese, which, in my opinion, is an absolute necessity for a truly delicious egg sandwich. The meal also included home fries, cooked with large slices of peppers and onions. Personally, I'm not the biggest fan of breakfast potatoes, but I have to admit, these were fantastic. I appreciated the fact that they didn't just scoop some pre-cooked home fries from a pile of food.

Moving on to the pancakes, they were fluffy and delightful. However, I do have one small complaint regarding the use of pre-packaged syrup from Smuckers. I understand that if they were to serve syrup from a container, it probably wouldn't be genuine maple syrup, but I kind of wish I didn't know that they were providing me with sub-par syrup.

The server was friendly and attentive, always making sure my coffee cup was never empty. Speaking of coffee, it was actually quite good (unlike many other diners where coffee tends to disappoint). I must give them bonus points for not judging my decision to indulge in two breakfasts.

In summary, I absolutely loved this place and can't wait to go back again soon. Long live the Jersey diners!

input:
The new Han Dynasty took over the spot where the old Mid-Atlantic restaurant (with the unchanging menu) was. I like the Han Dynasty here a lot more than the one in Olde City even if I give both 4*. Maybe I'm biased, because I love the service here. They've always been very nice, and came over to check in with me and just make some small conversation when they heard I had a peanut allergy (even though they had no peanuts in any of the dishes I ordered; I think it was Han's sister?). I've been to this Han Dynasty more times in a month than the number of times I've been to the other.

Note though, that the different branches have different specialties. I heard the dan dan mian in Olde City is the best, but the one in UC isn't so good (I wouldn't know since it has peanuts). Overall, I think it;s okay food wise, still not spicy enough as with the other branch. But I like the layout and atmosphere a lot more.

Next, if you go during lunch, you can ask for lunch portions, that are smaller than the dinner portions, and half the menu price! So it's a great lunch place too, alone, or in a group of 2 or 3.

The staff has always been very kind and attentive, going above and beyond by checking in with me and engaging in small talk when they discovered I had a peanut allergy (even though none of the dishes I ordered contained peanuts; I think it was Han's sister who did it?). input:

input: This is a small hole in the wall in the African section of Woodland Avenue.  Though it might not look like much, there is some good food coming out of its kitchen representing Senegal and West Africa.  I enjoyed the national dish of Senegal - Thiboudienne - although note that here they do a version without the usual tomato sauce.  I also took home a Jollof Rice which is often called the mother dish of Jambalaya.  There are a few hightop tables inside for dining or you can order the food to-go.  Either way, service is friendly.
Rewrite this for me: Located in the African section of Woodland Avenue, this unassuming eatery may appear small, but it is a hidden gem serving up delectable Senegalese and West African cuisine. Despite its modest appearance, the kitchen churns out delicious meals that showcase the flavors of the region. One dish that particularly stood out to me was the Thiboudienne, the national dish of Senegal, which they offer without the customary tomato sauce. Additionally, I couldn't resist taking home a portion of their Jollof Rice, known as the "mother dish" of Jambalaya. Whether you choose to dine at one of their hightop tables inside or opt for a to-go order, you can count on friendly service.

All in all,  the place is a must visit if you are up for trying something new.

input: Husband and I made a mistake and came here on a Lenten Friday. The wait was forever. But since we were already there, might as well suck it up and see what's it all about. We ordered the blackened alligator and oysters for appetizers, the alligator came out within 15 minutes, and it was alright. A bit too greasy. Then another 15 minutes later, our raw oysters came out, I wanted mine char grilled but the waitress didn't mention they don't have char grilled oysters and still took my order, so I thought I was waiting for mine to be cooked the entire time. When she brought out the two half-dozen raw oyster trays, that's when she told me they only have raw oysters there. SMH. I have sensitive stomach so I only had 3 then gave the rest to my husband. Regardless, the oysters were really fresh. We waited for at least another 20 minutes later for our entrees to come out. At this point, I was really hungry and had hoped we were at home eating ramen noodles instead. My husband had the roast beef po-boy, and I had the tuna and shrimp kabob. My husband told me his roast beef was really salty and while ironically, my kabob was very bland. The kabob came with exactly 3 pieces of cubed tuna, 2 medium size shrimp with plenty of bell peppers and onions in between, and baby shrimp creole with rice. For the ok price, I shouldn't complain too much about this place. Didn't try their seafood boil, but it looked like that would have been a better choice.
Rewrite this for me: My husband and I made a mistake by coming here on a Lenten Friday, resulting in a long wait. The alligator was served to us in just 15 minutes, but it was a bit too greasy for our liking. After another 15 minutes, our raw oysters arrived. I had requested mine to be char grilled, but unfortunately, the waitress failed to inform me that they don't serve char grilled oysters. Consequently, I had been waiting for them to be cooked the entire time. When the waitress brought out the two half-dozen trays of raw oysters, she finally informed me of their unavailability. Disappointed, I could only consume three due to my sensitive stomach, and gave the rest to my husband. Despite the mix-up, the oysters were undeniably fresh. We then waited for at least another 20 minutes for our entrees to be brought out. At this point, hunger had taken over and I couldn't help but wish we were at home eating ramen noodles instead. My husband had ordered the roast beef po-boy, which he found to be excessively salty. Ironically, my tuna and shrimp kabob was disappointingly bland. The kabob consisted of three cubes of tuna, two medium-sized shrimp, plenty of bell peppers and onions, and a side of baby shrimp creole with rice. Considering the price, I suppose I shouldn't complain too much about this place. We didn't get to try their seafood boil, but it appeared to be a more promising choice.

input:
im going to have to give this place one star for its horrible customer service:

i called in to ask about the 50% off for tulane students they were advertising, the woman assured me if i came with an id it would be half off and made an appointment for me, only once i got there did they tell me it's only on certain days, "it says it right on the sign," i was perturbed by the inconvenience and said so you're not going to honor it even though you just made an appointment with me and told me it would be 50% off, they said no flat out at first even though the error was blatantly on their side, after my nagging, she eventually called john jay himself and he told the woman that he would not honor what i was told even though i had been inconvenienced by someone in HIS staff because it might cause a 'domino effect,' i said how will there be a domino effect unless you continue to give people incorrect information, there will be no other 'dominoes' as long as you remember what day it is from now on... they began to treat me somewhat patronizingly as i explained that usually businesses make concessions when they are the one at fault, that the customer is supposed to always be right, yadda yadda yadda, i left pretty upset and with ~45 minutes of my life having been wasted - empty handed but for a lame excuse from someone who owns at least 3 businesses over 10 dollars...

i have not received a haircut from them so if you're one of those people who ONLY cares about the product and you think you'll get a good cut go right on ahead, but if you're like me (principled) and you don't like handing profits to people who care nothing about their customers this is a good place to skip next time you need a cut
Rewrite this for me:
I am extremely disappointed with the customer service at this place. I called to inquire about the advertised 50% off for Tulane students. The woman on the phone assured me that if I showed my ID, I would receive the discount and even made an appointment for me. However, when I arrived, they informed me that the discount only applied on certain days and pointed to a sign that apparently stated this information. I was frustrated by the inconvenience and expressed my dissatisfaction. I questioned why they would make an appointment with me and promise the discount, only to retract it later. At first, they flatly refused to honor their mistake, even though it was clearly their fault. After persistently arguing my case, the woman reluctantly called the owner, John Jay, who also refused to honor the discount and justified it by claiming it would have a negative "domino effect." I argued that there would be no such effect if they simply provided accurate information in the future. They began treating me condescendingly as I explained that businesses usually make concessions when they are at fault and that the customer is supposed to be right. I left the establishment feeling upset, having wasted around 45 minutes of my time and having received nothing other than a weak excuse from someone who owns multiple businesses, all over $10.

I cannot comment on the quality of their haircuts as I haven't received one from them. If you are solely concerned with the end product and believe you will receive a good haircut, feel free to go ahead. However, if you share my principles and dislike supporting businesses that disregard their customers, I recommend avoiding this place the next time you need a haircut.

input: Awesome food, great place to split a bunch of delicious spicy, ultra flavorful dishes with a large group. It's the Chinese restaurant a lot of people know about for good reason - I haven't had a single bad dish here, and it's always a crowd-pleaser.
Rewrite this for me: This Chinese restaurant is known by many for all the right reasons - it offers delectable, spicy and incredibly flavorsome dishes that are perfect for sharing with a big group. The food here is truly awesome, and I have yet to come across a single dish that disappoints. It never fails to impress and satisfy everyone.

input:
My friend and I visited Tampa for a concert, and about ten minutes away from the Atlanta airport he realized that he had purchased tickets for the wrong day. We had already made hotel reservations and bought the concert tickets, so he just had to pay same-day price for airfare: all in all about $800 more. "It was totally worth it," he later told me, "Because I got to have the best sandwich of my entire life."

All because we randomly picked the Bricks of Ybor from Yelp. I can't vouch for the peanut butter or meatless menu, but the meat sandwiches that we bought were absolutely phenomenal. I had the pulled pork, which was flavored with ponzu and served on Hawaiian sweet bread. It was one of the best meals I've had in a long time. We spent a few hours hanging out and drinking, during which time Brian, the owner, came out and talked to us, comped us a drink, let us try new appetizers he was developing (all for free) and generally made us feel really welcome. 

I kept my eyes open to the kind of crowd that came in and out of the restaurant. It seemed to draw everything from hipsters to geriatrics and strait-laced families with young kids. I think it speaks to both the diversity of the menu and the pleasant environment. We went back for drinks before and after the concert. It got very crowded but we still received excellent food, drinks and service. I give this restaurant my strongest recommendation, and it's the first place I'm going when I next visit Tampa.
Rewrite this for me:
During a trip to Tampa for a concert, my friend and I encountered a major hiccup just ten minutes away from Atlanta airport. It turned out that he had mistakenly bought tickets for the wrong day. Despite already having hotel reservations and concert tickets, he had no choice but to pay a steep same-day price for airfare, amounting to an extra $800. Surprisingly, he later admitted that the whole ordeal was worth it because he discovered the greatest sandwich of his life.

This fortunate turn of events was the result of our random selection from Yelp: the Bricks of Ybor. I cannot vouch for their peanut butter or meatless menu, but their meat sandwiches were undeniably outstanding. Personally, I indulged in their pulled pork, which was expertly flavored with ponzu and served on delectable Hawaiian sweet bread. It truly was one of the most memorable meals I've had in a long time. 

We spent a few hours at the restaurant, savoring our food and enjoying some drinks. To our delight, Brian, the owner, personally came out to chat with us, even comping us a drink and treating us to his newest appetizers for free. His kind gestures and warm hospitality made us feel incredibly welcome.

Throughout our time there, I observed the diverse range of customers that frequented the establishment. It seemed to attract everyone, from hipsters to elderly individuals and families with young children. This diversity speaks volumes about both the menu variety and the inviting atmosphere. We even returned for drinks before and after the concert, despite the growing crowds. Thankfully, the quality of the food, drinks, and service remained exceptional.

I enthusiastically recommend this restaurant and I can confidently say that it will be my first stop the next time I visit Tampa.

input: So worth the wait! The crepes are amazing! I also loved the grits, which is rare. Tried my hubby's pancakes....awesome!
Rewrite this for me: The wait was absolutely worth it! The crepes are absolutely incredible! Surprisingly, I even enjoyed the grits, which is not something I usually do. I also had a taste of my husband's pancakes and they were absolutely awesome!

input: My sister-in-law and I visited this restaurant on 8/28/15 mid afternoon.  We were seated after requested 3 times that the hostess speak a little louder because we couldn't even hear her with the background music.  We were seated in a booth with a never ending Larry King vitamin commercial on the TV - really?  Our waitress introduced herself and a new trainee and then we never saw her again.  Two other wait staff seemed to be sharing our table, but no idea who was responsible for our table.  We got our drinks and ordered, but food took forever considering there was not more than 15-20 filled tables in the entire restaurant.  Burgers were not bad - I ordered the blue cheese burger and it would have been better with less blue cheese, way too much!  Fries and onion sticks were very good.  But no one came to see if we were satisfied, needing anything, etc and took two requests and waiting to get a carry out box.  There was a family seated across the aisle from us when we arrived and we assumed they had finished their meal and were "hanging out".  Only after we received our food did we understand they had already ordered and still did not have their food!  I doubt I will return to this restaurant in the future.
Rewrite this for me:
On 8/28/15, my sister-in-law and I decided to dine at this restaurant during the afternoon. Unfortunately, we faced several issues right from the start. Firstly, we had to ask the hostess three times to speak up because the background music made it difficult to hear her. Once we were finally seated, we were in a booth with a never-ending Larry King vitamin commercial on the TV, which was quite unexpected. Our waitress introduced herself along with a trainee, but then seemed to disappear for the rest of our visit. It was confusing because two other wait staff members seemed to be taking care of our table, but we had no way of knowing who was actually responsible for us.

Despite these initial obstacles, we managed to get our drinks and place our orders. However, the food took an incredibly long time to arrive, considering the fact that the restaurant was not even half-full. Eventually, our burgers arrived, and while they were decent, my blue cheese burger had an excessive amount of blue cheese, which overwhelmed the flavors. On a positive note, the fries and onion sticks were quite enjoyable.

Unfortunately, throughout our entire meal, no one checked in to see if we were satisfied or if we needed anything. It took two requests and a considerable amount of waiting just to receive a carry out box. To add to the disappointment, there was a family seated across the aisle from us when we arrived. We initially assumed they had finished their meal and were simply staying to hang out. However, we later realized that they had ordered their food before us and were still waiting for it to be served.

Given the numerous issues and lack of attentive service, I highly doubt I will be returning to this restaurant in the future.

input:
In short, the food was decently good, but completely overpriced.  The guacamole and my Mojito were probably the highlight of the meal. I had the peach pork medallions, which were nicely cooked, but lacked flavor. I tried the corn cakes with Barbacoa and that was pretty good.  

The atmosphere was inviting with a hip feel if that's what you're looking for.  What was really annoying was the parking situation. For a place with price points such as these and limited parking spaces, a valet service should be provided either at a cost or complimentary.  Don't even try and park in the back of the building, it's tight and dangerous even getting there and back.  I ended up parking three blocks away and broke a sweat walking in the dead of summer to the front entrance.
Rewrite this for me:
To put it briefly, the food was fairly enjoyable, but it was severely overpriced. The guacamole and my Mojito were definitely the highlights of my meal. The peach pork medallions were cooked well, but they lacked flavor. On the other hand, the corn cakes with Barbacoa were quite tasty.

The atmosphere was welcoming and had a trendy vibe, if that's what you're after. However, the parking situation was extremely frustrating. Considering the high prices and limited parking spaces, it would have been appreciated if they offered a valet service, either at a fee or as a complimentary service. Attempting to park at the back of the building was a tight and hazardous ordeal, so I ended up parking three blocks away. It was an unpleasant experience walking in the scorching summer heat just to reach the front entrance.

input: Had dinner Saturday night for the first time at rusty pelican. Called ahead and made a reservation and requested a table next to the window overlooking the water. Hostess went to seat us away from the window, when we questioned her she huffed off and left us staying in the middle of the dining room!! She did return and sat us by the window. The rest of the evening was great, drinks, food and wait staff was excellent. Liz was our server and went above and beyond. Still have to say the hostess was very disappointing!
Rewrite this for me: On Saturday night, I had dinner at the Rusty Pelican for the very first time. I had made a reservation in advance and specifically requested a table by the window, offering a beautiful view of the water. However, upon arrival, the hostess tried to seat us away from the window. Confused by this, we questioned her choice, but she seemed irritated and walked away, leaving us standing in the middle of the dining room. Thankfully, she eventually came back and seated us by the window as we had requested. Despite the disappointing start, the rest of the evening turned out to be fantastic. The drinks, food, and wait staff were all excellent. Our server, Liz, went above and beyond to ensure we had a great experience. However, I must admit that the behavior of the hostess was quite disheartening.

input:
This was a tough one!   On the merits of the wine, fairly average... I understand that the winery has more than one lable and other label is their premium wines.  I look forward to when that is available (I went two weeks ago so maybe it already is)     Location..   what's not to like?  On the pier!  A wonderful outdoor patio,  couldn't have a nicer setting to enjoy your tasting....   The staff were super, super nice,  I would give them an A+!  

So why only three stars?  It is because of the wine club!  Very expensive for the quality of the wines and stingy as HELL with the benefits to the members..   Most wine clubs will give you a free tasting every time you come in (after all, we are your best customers... we are the ones who buy your wine time and time again).  Some wineries will give their members a complimentary glass in leau of a tasting (Carr).   Most wineries allow you to bring guests which is how you get new wine club members.   This system works folks!  The way this wine club works is that you are given a very limited number of passes per quarter, five as I recall.   If I come with my wife once a month we wouldn't even be covered... let alone if we bring a guest!   

So go to this winery if you want to enjoy a tasting in one of the most beautiful settings on earth.   But avoid the wine club!  For that you can pretty much go to any of the other wine tasting rooms on the Urban wine trail.
Rewrite this for me:
This was quite challenging! In terms of the wine itself, it was fairly average. I learned that the winery has multiple labels, with their premium wines being the standout. I'm looking forward to trying those when they become available (I visited two weeks ago, so they might already be).

The location is absolutely fantastic, situated on the pier! The outdoor patio provides a wonderful setting to enjoy your tasting. The staff were incredibly friendly and helpful, I would give them an A+!

So, why only three stars? It's because of the wine club. The cost is exorbitant for the quality of the wines, and the benefits for members are extremely lacking. Most wine clubs offer a free tasting each time you visit, recognizing that their loyal customers are the ones repeatedly purchasing their wines. Some wineries even provide a complimentary glass instead of a tasting (like Carr). Additionally, many wineries allow members to bring guests, which helps promote the wine club. This type of system works well! However, this particular wine club offers a very limited number of passes per quarter, if I remember correctly, around five. If my wife and I were to visit once a month, we wouldn't even have enough passes, let alone if we wanted to bring a guest.

So, if you want to enjoy a tasting in one of the most breathtaking settings imaginable, I suggest visiting this winery. Just be sure to avoid their wine club. Instead, you can easily find other wine tasting rooms along the Urban wine trail that provide better options.

input:
I got a cheap haircut in NY for next to nothing and what do you know. it looks like some crazy chimp chewed up my hair and spat  it back on my raw scalp.

Since I'm going for job interviews, I needed to look better and went to Domenick's. The guys were great, Robert cut my hair and did a clean job. Bill came out to $35. I'd give it a 4, but it was a little pricy for my taste, but I look human again. Don't know what you guys in Philly normally pay for a haircut.
Rewrite this for me:
I recently got a budget-friendly haircut in NY and to my surprise, it turned out to be quite disastrous. It appears as if someone wildly disfigured my hair and left it scattered on my exposed scalp.

Considering my upcoming job interviews, it was crucial for me to improve my appearance, so I decided to visit Domenick's. The staff there, especially Robert who styled my hair, did a commendable job, leaving me looking presentable once again. The total cost came up to $35, which I found slightly expensive in comparison to my personal preference. However, it was worth it as I regained my human-like appearance. I'm unsure about the average haircut prices in Philly, so I'm curious to know what you guys usually pay.

input: Very unhappy, you lost a valued customer. We had a problem where Monro Muffler underfilled our engine by 3 quarts of oil and caused damage to the engine. Monro's insurance company said they would pay for damages if we brought to the dealer, we were frequent customers of Bergeys so we brought it here. They discovered the timing chain needed to be replaced, a chain that lasts the life of the car unless you don't change the oil or have low oil pressure the tensioner can lock and stretch the chain. Joe the service associate that took the car in specifically said I told the insurance company as little as possible and told them he couldn't tell if it was from the oil and there was no way to tell. And on top of that, was extremely rude and unprofessional to my wife bringing her to tears the way he spoke to her. My wife and I just bought a house in the area, only 26 years old and you lost a life long customer. Over the past year we spent about $7000 in repairs here, and Joe went out of his way to be unhelpful and leave us in a terrible spot. I brought it to another mechanic who was able to help us prove more it was from the oil and do what Joe told us and the insurance company they could not do. So on top of losing a service customer, I'm on the market for a new car and can tell you for sure where I will not be getting it.
Rewrite this for me:
I am extremely dissatisfied as I express my disappointment in losing a valued customer. Our unfavorable experience occurred when Monro Muffler negligently underfilled our engine with 3 quarts of oil, leading to severe damage. Despite Monro's insurance company offering to cover the damages, we chose to bring our vehicle to Bergeys, as we have been loyal customers of theirs for some time.

Upon inspection by the professionals at Bergeys, it was discovered that the timing chain needed replacement. This chain is supposed to last the lifetime of the car unless oil changes are neglected or if there is low oil pressure, which can cause the tensioner to lock and stretch the chain. Interestingly, Joe, the service associate who received our car, intentionally withheld information from the insurance company and falsely claimed that it was impossible to determine if the damage was related to the oil issue. Furthermore, Joe's behavior towards my wife was extremely rude and unprofessional, resulting in her being upset and distraught.

To provide context, my wife and I recently purchased a house in this area, and despite our young age of just 26, we have been loyal customers who have spent approximately $7000 on repairs here over the past year. Joe, however, went out of his way to be uncooperative, leaving us in a distressing situation. We eventually decided to seek assistance from another mechanic who was able to provide evidence supporting the fact that the damage was indeed caused by the oil issue, contrary to what Joe claimed couldn't be done. As a result, not only have you lost a loyal customer for your service department, but I can confidently assure you that I will not be purchasing my next car from your establishment.

input:
Beautiful clean shop with knock your socks off Everything ...
Homemade breakfast tarts and chicken pot pies .
All sweets looked well beyond beautiful and delish.
I felt some of the items were a tad pricey considering the sizes being on a smaller size. But I know premium quality costs more .. 
It's a great place for locals and worth a trip if traveling from center city etc .
I found counter staff to be most friendly and engaging 
Will be back and certainly will recommend
Rewrite this for me: The shop is absolutely stunning and impeccably clean. Everything they offer is amazing, especially their homemade breakfast tarts and chicken pot pies. The sweets are not only visually appealing but also incredibly delicious. Although some of the prices are a bit steep considering the portions are on the smaller side, I understand that premium quality comes at a higher cost. It's a fantastic spot for locals and definitely worth a visit for those traveling from center city and beyond. The staff at the counter are friendly and attentive, making the overall experience enjoyable. I will definitely return and highly recommend it to others.

input: Definitely get in line before 8:30am. We waited about 30 minutes. Pancakes were fine. My friends got the raspberry pancakes, the sweet potato pancakes and the san antonio. I got the sugar and spice pancakes. All were well and fine, a bit dry. I don't understand the hype, but if the line isn't too long it's not bad for normal breakfast food. If the line is longer I would highly recommend skipping this place and heading down the street to Fido - insanely good coffee and great breakfast food.
Rewrite this for me: Make sure to join the queue before 8:30am for sure. Our wait time was approximately 30 minutes. The pancakes were acceptable. Among my friends, they tried the raspberry pancakes, sweet potato pancakes, and san antonio pancakes. As for me, I opted for the sugar and spice pancakes. All of them were decent but slightly lacking in moisture. I fail to comprehend the excessive praise, but if the queue isn't too lengthy, it's alright for a regular breakfast. However, if the line is long, I would highly advise you to skip this place and head towards Fido just down the street. They serve unbelievably good coffee and offer exceptional breakfast options.

input: They have the WORST service advisors! Used to be good before Kelly and her team left. Unfortunately, it's convenient to work if I need oil change before I can make it to another Honda dealer.
Rewrite this for me: The service advisors at this particular place are absolutely terrible! They used to be excellent until Kelly and her team departed. Regrettably, it is convenient for me to go there whenever I require an oil change before being able to reach another Honda dealership.

input:
The best soon-dubu in the city!  This place is tucked away and once you walk in, it's like you've stepped into a Korean home.  Very welcoming, warm and inviting.

It's very vegetarian friendly!  The soft tofu is stewed and put into the dol sot pots which each and every stew feels like it's custom made for you. 

You can select from beef, seafood or mixed meats (seafood & beef), mushroom, and just plain.  They can adjust the spice as needed too.  I always get the extra hot with the hot temperature, can't beat it.  The rice also comes in a dol-sot which is great if you leave it in for a while, it burns the rice into a nice crispy shell.  DROOL.

Just thinking about this place makes my mouth salivate!  

If you're not into tofu, they also offer korean bbq meats (cooked in the back), with other soup/stew items.

Love this place!!!
Rewrite this for me:
This city is home to the absolute best soon-dubu you'll find! Tucked away, it truly gives off a cozy and authentic Korean home vibe the moment you step inside. The atmosphere is incredibly welcoming, warm, and inviting.

For all the vegetarians out there, this place is perfect! The soft tofu is stewed and served in dol sot pots, making each and every stew feel like it's personally customized just for you.

You have a variety of options to choose from, including beef, seafood, mixed meats (seafood & beef), mushroom, and plain. They are also able to adjust the level of spiciness to your liking. Personally, I always go for extra hot with the high temperature, as nothing beats that combination. Plus, the rice is served in a dol-sot as well, which means if you leave it in for a while, it forms a deliciously crispy shell. Just thinking about it makes my mouth water!

In addition to their amazing soon-dubu, they also offer Korean BBQ meats (cooked in the back) and other soup and stew options.

This place is an absolute love of mine!

input:
As motels go this one is very nice for the rate. Clean, comfortable and well-managed. You get what you pay for so the breakfast buffet is just OK. The pool is too small to swim laps (disappointing). The lobby area is spacious and comportable. 

If you are looking for a moderately priced place to sleep that is clean and comforable this will suit you just fine.
Rewrite this for me: If you're searching for an affordable place to stay that is both clean and comfortable, this motel is a great choice. It is well-managed and offers a pleasant experience for its rate. However, keep in mind that the breakfast buffet is just average. Additionally, the pool is not suitable for lap swimming, which may be disappointing. On the bright side, the lobby area is ample and cozy. Overall, this motel is a suitable option for those seeking a reasonably priced and pleasant place to sleep.

input:

input:
From the second you walk in the door, you're greeted by the adorable woman at the counter. It seems if you come in here more than once a week, she'll know you're name but I haven't been so lucky since my visits are a bit more sporadic.

My most recent discovery are the vegetarian breakfast sandwiches, which are served all day! I particularly enjoy veg. sausage w/ havarti on an everything bagel. I could actually go for one right about now... I've also had the veggie club sandwich and my other half has enjoyed the chicken cheesesteak hoagie and the chicken salad on a croissant. Everything always taste fresh, they are priced really well  (I think my favorite bagel sandwich I mentioned is $2.09-2.99- cheaper than wawa!). The people at the deli are super helpful, offering menus if you can't read the one on the wall and will make great suggestions and accommodations to your needs and want.

Don't forget to grab a really great snack too while you're there- they have amazing chocolate bars, an incredible drink case, tons of chip varieties and those addictive hi-chew candies in every flavor.

I know i'll be back here, who doesn't like fast / delicious / attentive service?
Rewrite this for me:
As soon as you step inside, the charming lady at the counter warmly greets you. It appears that if you visit this place frequently, she remembers your name, but unfortunately, my visits are a bit more irregular, so I haven't been as fortunate.

Recently, I discovered the vegetarian breakfast sandwiches, which are available all day! My personal favorite is the veggie sausage with havarti on an everything bagel. I could really go for one right now... I've also tried the veggie club sandwich, while my partner enjoyed the chicken cheesesteak hoagie and the chicken salad on a croissant. The freshness of everything always stands out, and the prices are quite reasonable (even cheaper than wawa, I believe!). The deli staff is incredibly helpful, providing menus if you can't read the ones on the wall, and they offer great suggestions and accomodations to suit your preferences.

While you're there, don't forget to grab a fantastic snack. They have a wide variety of amazing chocolate bars, an impressive selection of beverages, countless chip options, and addictively delicious hi-chew candies in every flavor.

I know I'll definitely be returning to this place. After all, who doesn't appreciate fast, delicious, and attentive service?

input: We stopped in for brunch and we weren't expecting the food to be so delicious.  The 3 meat hash was amazing, as was the turkey sandwich and bagel/salmon.  The employees were very friendly and accommodating.  A little pricey, but well worth.  We will visit again if in the area.
Rewrite this for me: We unexpectedly dropped in for brunch and were pleasantly surprised by the incredibly delicious food. The 3 meat hash surpassed our expectations, along with the mouthwatering turkey sandwich and bagel with salmon. The staff was exceptionally friendly and accommodating. Although slightly expensive, it undoubtedly justified the cost. If we find ourselves in the area again, we will definitely be returning.

input: Nice little bar located at the very far end of Terminal E and Tampa International. The airport recently added several new restaurants with a "local vibe" and this is one of them. There isn't a ton of seating but it also isn't close to the TSA area so it's a bit hidden. Hey have TVs if you wanna catch a game while you wait for your flight. Food is very reasonably price for the portion size. Appetizers run from $5-$10 and majority of sandwiches are $12. I didn't order any food but it looked amazing! Drinks are tasty and Prices are not terrible. Think 22oz Jai Alai for $8.50. You cannot take alcoholic beverages into the terminal (Columbia does this I think). I had a Manhattan for $11 and it was very tasty. Staff is attentive and friendly. I know my new spot when I'm waiting on a Delta flight!
Rewrite this for me:
Located at the furthest end of Terminal E in Tampa International Airport, you'll find a delightful little bar with a local ambiance. Recently, the airport has introduced a selection of new restaurants with a similar vibe, and this gem is one of them. Although the seating capacity is not extensive, it's discreetly tucked away from the TSA area. If you're in the mood to catch a game, they provide TVs for your entertainment while you wait for your flight.

The pricing at this bar is incredibly reasonable considering the portion size. Appetizers range from $5 to $10, while the majority of their sandwiches are priced at $12. Although I didn't have an opportunity to try their food, it certainly looked incredible! When it comes to drinks, they offer a flavorful selection at decent prices. For instance, you can enjoy a 22oz Jai Alai for just $8.50. However, it's worth mentioning that alcoholic beverages cannot be brought into the terminal, similar to Columbia's policy.

During my visit, I indulged in a delicious Manhattan cocktail, which only set me back $11. The staff at this bar is attentive and friendly, providing exceptional service. Now, whenever I find myself waiting for a Delta flight, I know exactly where to go. This bar has become my new go-to spot at Tampa International Airport.

input: The depot burger is so delicious along with the shishito peppers! Perfect food, perfect atmosphere, perfect drinks!
Rewrite this for me: The Depot Burger and Shishito Peppers are incredibly tasty! The food is perfection, the atmosphere is fantastic, and the drinks are top-notch!

input: Quality of this store has gone downhill over the past few years. In the past,  I was able to easily choose from a wide selection of food at reasonable prices any time of day. I have noticed recently that the produce is not as fresh, but more expensive,  and the prices of the organic foods are more expensive than Whole Foods. This morning I debated on going to Wegmans or going to this store. I only had to get a few items so I decided on this Giant since it was closer. Big mistake. I have seen on average at least 3 or 4 people shopping around 5 a.m. In the past but today just me. They had all of the store roped off where it was impossible to get to certain aisles and very difficult to get to the register. In my frustration I went under a rope to get soup.  I was then berated by a number of people who were supposed to be cleaning the floors but some were just standing around doing nothing. I couldn't even walk out of the closest door because that was blocked off. If they needed to clean the floor they should have closed the store for a few hours. It would have taken less time at Wegmans which is where I will shop for now on.

This morning, I had to choose between going to Wegmans or this store. Since I only needed a few items and it was closer, I opted for this Giant. Unfortunately, it turned out to be a big mistake. Previously, I would see around 3 or 4 people shopping around 5 a.m., but today I was the only one. The entire store was cordoned off, making it impossible to access certain aisles and challenging to reach the register. In my frustration, I had to go under a rope just to get soup. To make matters worse, the individuals who were supposed to be cleaning the floors were berating me, even though some of them were simply standing around doing nothing. input:
--------DINNER REVIEW----------

I rarely write reviews, but this honestly was one of the worst group dining experiences I've ever had. It was objectively a horrible experience, even without comparing it to the hype it receives, and ruined what was supposed to be a nice birthday dinner celebration. 

We had a group of 8 that had a reservation made well in advance. Short wait, but not too bad. Keep in mind, it seemed like a normal Friday night, but weren't super busy or at-capacity.

It was a birthday dinner, so I told the hostesses that it was her birthday, and asked if they could bring out something for her at the end of the meal, which was acknowledged. Pretty standard stuff, whether at a Applebee's or the French Laundry. We were sat at a booth right next to the Maitre D' stand, and next to all the wait staff's home base, so pretty much no excuse for not getting any attention. 

After getting us waters, it took them a LONG time to even come by and acknowledge us. After ordering wine, it took them another good 15-20 minutes to even bring us our wine, and no one even checked in on us! (hint: if you're running a restaurant, wine is your profit center and doesn't take any work other than taking a bottle off a shelf and opening it. bring it out ASAP...). 

After ordering food, it was more of the same...a long wait for food to start coming out and no one checking in on us AT ALL. We drank the bottles we ordered and had to get up and flag someone down to get another wine order. A couple of us even got up during the meal to remind them to bring out something for birthday girl at the end of the meal. 

Once our meal was done and taken away, we were given dessert menus and the server disappeared for 10-15 minutes... AGAIN. After coming back, he asked what dessert we wanted, so we ordered some coffees... and waited... and waited. Eventually we got up and asked him what was going on and if they were going to bring anything out like we asked multiple times. 

They finally brought out a couple of cookies with a candle...

In summary, the food was pretty hit or miss, pretty mediocre for this price point. Whipped feta, like other reviews have said, was amazing, and the Braised Lamb was really good. But the Sirloin was chewy and bland and the Grilled Caesar tasted like a soggy, luke-warm, wilted mess (two orders were left untouched by a group of 8). Atmosphere was nice and trendy. But the service, which is a huge reason to spend your hard-earned $ at a restaurant, was absolutely horrendous. 

I really love going to cool, popular restaurants and having a great time, and I hate writing such a negative review, but I had to share my experience, especially for a restaurant that is getting an awful lot of (undeserved) hype.

input:
See's candies is California base bakery reach Florida. I know about this candies when my wife living in California. Their chocolate is very soft and tasty. 

In Tampa, the International Plaza Mall has this temporary store from Thanksgiving to Easter. They located very close to H&M clothing store. You can have samples before you buy it. I got the lollipop candies. I also bought one assorted chocolate candies. They are very good. The store clerk was kind enough to let us try their assorted chocolate other their typical sample candies.

input:
Second stop for Center City Restaurant Week:  R2L, dinner for $35 each. 

On the 37th floor of Two Liberty Place is a very fancy-cool restaurant/lounge where you can get a bird's eye view of the city! Group of us went to dinner here together after a day of meetings. Didn't get one of the tables facing the windows, but still had great views of the sunset and city by night. Again, multiple choices for the three courses, but I chose to start with the crisp peas/ham/garlic risotto [balls]. Main course was the Butcher's Filet (braised short rib + Steuben bean chili, potato/farm veg slaw and basil), which was quite heavy since there was also meat in the chili as well. The dazzling dessert to finish it off was the milk chocolate + hazelnut pudding served with salted caramel and coffee to melt the chocolate, and candied almonds on the side. A bottle of wine for the table as well. Food was great, waiter was awesome (making sure to warn me that the risotto came in ball form rather than a bowl, for instance), very classy experience.
Rewrite this for me:
We made our second stop for Center City Restaurant Week at R2L, where we enjoyed a delicious dinner for only $35 each. Located on the 37th floor of Two Liberty Place, this restaurant/lounge offers breathtaking views of the city. Despite not getting a table by the window, we still had a fantastic view of the sunset and the city lights at night.

R2L provided us with a variety of options for each of the three courses. As for me, I started with the delightful crisp peas, ham, and garlic risotto balls. For the main course, I opted for the Butcher's Filet, which consisted of braised short rib, Steuben bean chili, potato and farm vegetable slaw, and basil. The dish was quite hearty due to the addition of meat in the chili. To top off the meal, I indulged in the scrumptious milk chocolate and hazelnut pudding served with salted caramel, coffee to melt the chocolate, and candied almonds on the side. We also enjoyed a bottle of wine at our table.

The food at R2L was excellent and our waiter provided exceptional service. He made sure to inform me that the risotto would be served in ball form rather than a bowl, showcasing the attention to detail this classy establishment offers. Overall, it was a truly classy and memorable dining experience.

input:
I moved from Chicago to Philadelphia over a year ago.  Everybody here raves about the restaurants, but I have yet to find many that deserve five stars, or even four.  This is the best restaurant I have eaten in in Philadelphia.  

Tahini and bread  arrived at the table, and I thought, hum, plain but I'm hungry.  They must put crack in that Tahini.  I wanted to lap it out of the bowl like an uncouth dog.  The bread is excellent too.

I love a menu with many organic meat choices.  How often can you order an organic beef shishkabob?  It was superb.  The meat done perfectly, the onions nearly caramelized but not quite so they still had some substantive crunch.  The purslane salad tasted like I was eating a plant in the middle of a garden.  It is not often that I dream about a salad but I do dream about this one

My husband had a chicken dish with black eyed peas and green peas and fantastic rice.  I won't begin to describe the flavoring; it is beyond my culinary vocabulary.  We asked what spices they use, and in addition to traditional zatar, they use their own blend of spices.  I don't even need to know what is in it just so long as we can keep coming back and ordering it again and again.

I was so full but ate dessert none the less, which I usually don't do.  But when a diner is this good, I had a feeling the desserts would be too and I just needed to find out.  Pistachio creme brulee.  It could have come out over the top, but no indeed.  It was pure pistachio heaven in s super light yet rich custard.  Heaven. Heaven.

Our service was superb.  The squeezed us into a last minute Friday night reservation with the caveat that we would need to get through our dinner in an hour and 15 minutes in order to accommodate a reservation made prior to us.  Given the time constraints they never made us feel rushed and timed the meal perfectly.  Then my husband left to go to the restroom, the waiter picked up his napkin and refolded it nicely on the table.  Do I care about the napkin placement in the middle of a meal?  Not really, but it is a sign that the waitstaff is incredibly attentive and extremely well trained.  

My eating out plan for Philly might just be to skip eating most everywhere most of the time so I can frequent this expensive, though appropriately priced restaurant.  Kudos to the chef.
Rewrite this for me:
After moving to Philadelphia over a year ago from Chicago, I must admit that I haven't been impressed with many of the restaurants here. However, I recently discovered a gem that stands out from the rest.

When the tahini and bread were served on our table, I initially thought they were plain. However, my hunger got the best of me, and I couldn't resist. Surprisingly, the tahini was absolutely addictive. I wanted to savor every bit of it and found myself wishing I could lick the bowl like an uncivilized dog. The bread was also exceptional.

One thing I love about this restaurant is their extensive selection of organic meat options. How often do you come across a place where you can order an organic beef shishkabob? The dish was superbly executed, with the meat cooked to perfection and the onions caramelized just enough to retain their satisfying crunch. The purslane salad tasted as if I were eating fresh garden greens, and it's not often that I dream about a salad, but this one certainly left a lasting impression.

My husband opted for a chicken dish accompanied by black-eyed peas, green peas, and flavorful rice. It's difficult to put into words the complexity of the flavors. We asked about the spices used, and besides the traditional za'atar, they incorporate their own blend that is simply exceptional. I don't even need to know the exact ingredients; all I care about is being able to come back and enjoy it again and again.

Despite feeling full, I couldn't resist trying their desserts, which is not something I typically do. I had a hunch that the desserts here would be just as impressive as the rest of the meal. And boy, was I right. The pistachio creme brulee was a sublime creation. It struck the perfect balance, offering a heavenly pistachio flavor within a light yet rich custard. True bliss.

The service at this restaurant was top-notch. Despite squeezing us in for a last-minute Friday night reservation, they kindly informed us that we would need to finish our meal within an hour and 15 minutes to accommodate a prior reservation. However, they managed to flawlessly time our meal without making us feel rushed. In fact, I was touched when my husband went to the restroom, and our waiter kindly refolded his napkin on the table. It may not seem like a big deal, but it demonstrated the incredible attentiveness and exceptional training of the waitstaff.

After experiencing this culinary delight, I may just make it a plan to skip dining out elsewhere in Philly so that I can frequent this slightly pricey, yet absolutely worth it restaurant. Kudos to the talented chef who has truly created something special here.

My sister was visiting for the weekend, so I wanted to show her a solid night on the town that lasted till the wee hours of the morning. We started on Frenchmen, but for whatever reason it was dead. 
Deciding to adventure Uptown we proceeded on a respectable bar crawl, including Delachaise, Columns, and St. Joes, however, at 3 AM the usual Uptown culprits start to raise their heads. A summary of the following dialogue:

Friends "Let's go to FMs" 
Me: "No, too much broken glass"
Friends: "Let's go to Snake and Jake's"
Me: "Eh...."
Friends: "Brothers 3?"
Me: "I'm afraid I'll hit my head on the ceiling"
Friends: "The Saint!!"

input:
I stopped by Bell Meade during a recent visit to Nashville. The best way for me to describe my experience is to say that the next time I go to Nashville I will go out of my way to make sure I return to Bell Meade.

On my travels, I tend to stop from time to time to see if I can find specific bourbons that may be out locally. At this time of year, I did not expect any great finds because many of the items for which I look have their annual release later in the year so it's a surprise to find any of them on the shelf. For example, Elmer T Lee is a favorite of mine so it was one that I asked about.

Despite the fact that I walked away without Elmer T, I still had a great time. I enjoyed a few tastes at the tasting bar and even better I had a great conversation with Max. He is one of the reasons I will return.

I did walk out with a bottle of Tennessee whiskey cream that is not sold locally and there was a bottle on the shelf that I have not seen locally that I need to investigate. As I said I will return and a five star rating from me should say at all.
Rewrite this for me:
During my recent visit to Nashville, I made a stop at Bell Meade. To put it simply, my experience was so amazing that I am determined to make a return trip specifically to revisit Bell Meade.

Whenever I travel, I like to take the opportunity to search for specific bourbons that might not be readily available locally. Given the time of year, I didn't expect to stumble upon any remarkable discoveries, as many of the sought-after releases occur later in the year. It's always a pleasant surprise to find them on the shelves. One bourbon that I particularly love, Elmer T Lee, was on my list, but unfortunately, I left empty-handed in that regard.

However, despite not finding Elmer T, I had an absolutely fantastic time at Bell Meade. I indulged in a few tastings at their fabulous bar, and to top it off, I engaged in a delightful conversation with Max. His pleasant demeanor and excellent service are among the key reasons why I intend to return.

Although Elmer T was a miss, I did manage to acquire a bottle of Tennessee whiskey cream, which is not commonly sold in my local area. Additionally, I noticed a unique bottle on the shelf that I've never come across before, so I'm quite curious and will make it a point to investigate it next time. All in all, my intention to return to Bell Meade is best expressed by giving it a five-star rating.

input:
I love trying fresh seafood on piers, wharfs and seaside markets. Most of the time, it is a disappointing experience but this place is not. The food is legitimately fresh and prepared well. The gorgeous view is just a cherry on top of nature's beautiful sundae. I have been here before but ordered the "wrong" thing (cioppino). That wasn't very good when I had it a couple of years ago here. 

We came for a late lunch/early dinner on a Monday. Even at 4pm,  there was a wait! We waited about 25 minutes and got a table outdoor. While it wasn't ideal that we sat right in the sun with no shelter other than our sunscreen and sunglasses, the view was worth it. 

We got the local crab special which was a steamed 3-lb. crab served with a salad and soup for $26. I thought this was quite the steal because the crab was huge, delicious and meaty. The garden salad was fresh as simple as it was. The lobster bisque we got was pretty good. (The other options were Caesar salad and clam chowder). They topped off the crab with a couple of onion rings and cups of cocktail sauce and drawn butter. Yum!

We also got the fried platter of shrimp, oysters, calamari and scallops for $12.95. It came with cole slaw, onion rings, tartar sauce and cocktail sauce. As greasy of a meal as this made, it was one of the better fried platters I've had anywhere. The seafood was just really fresh including the sometimes-feared fried oyster. :)

The ice in our iced teas melted away in the sun. Our waitress was so cool and brought us lots of extra ice and an extra iced tea in case we needed it (we did because it was hot out!). She was just friendly and good at her job - five stars for her!

By the time we left at about 6, there were so many people waiting. Make sure you sign up for a seat on the clipboard right when you get there. The restaurant is the last one at the very end of the pier. Parking on the pier is free for 90 minutes but it looks like a drive that will upset tires. I parked in the large lot south of the pier and walked 15 minutes up and onto the pier. It was free on a Monday late afternoon.

I parked in the large lot south of the pier and walked approximately 15 minutes to reach the pier. On a Monday late afternoon, the parking was free in that lot.

input:

 Here is something I am not sure of, I have only lived here a few months now, is it customary to charge for each soda every time you get a refill here? input:
I stayed at the Orange St location from Friday to Monday.

Arrival: I already read plenty of reviews about no signs marking the location therefore, I looked for Starbucks. I parked in a spot in front of the multi business complex. I went inside to find a guard at a desk that said we have been contracted to hand guests their keys and room number and nothing more. He advised me there was a phone that was on the wall that I could make a call to someone if I needed to. He also stated that the very few parking spots in front were free* only on the weekend.

The Room: This wasn't a room, this was an apartment and I absolutely loved it. It was very spacious and had everything I sought* after for that weekend, such as: fully stocked kitchen, a desk, lots of space, king bed, huge table, nice living room, lots of closets. My only complaint is that I could not open any windows for fresh air...they are nailed/screwed shut. There was also a small welcome bag w cookies and water and papers letting you know where all the food delivery locations and numbers.
There wasn't maid service knocking loudly or trying to barge in early in the morning. This place is more of a long term setting and I'm sure the maids come around during the week Monday-Friday if you desire. I was only here for 3 days and I was fine with that. I went shopping at Shoprite and filled my fridge with water and breakfast to cook.

Overall: This place is awesome, I had a huge living room to entertain my guests when they visited, and a nice desk to study my Anatomy notes. I forgot to mention how quiet** this place is. I loved it. I felt as if no one was there except me. Very quiet* which worked for me on Sunday bc I had lots of studying to do and two TV's to watch The Walking Dead on. Lol!  I would most definitely stay here again. Very spacious and updated. Loved it!
Rewrite this for me:
I booked a stay at the Orange St location from Friday to Monday. When I arrived, I had already read reviews mentioning the lack of signs marking the location, so I looked for the nearby Starbucks. I parked in front of the multi-business complex and entered the building. Inside, I found a guard at a desk who informed me that they were responsible for handing out keys and room numbers but couldn't provide any additional assistance. He pointed out a wall phone that I could use if needed. He also mentioned that the few parking spots in front were only free on the weekend.

Upon entering my room, I was pleasantly surprised to find that it was actually an apartment. It was incredibly spacious and had everything I needed for the weekend, including a fully stocked kitchen, a desk, plenty of space, a king-sized bed, a large table, a comfortable living room, and ample storage space in the closets. The only downside was that the windows were permanently sealed shut, so I couldn't open them for fresh air. However, there was a small welcome bag with cookies, water, and papers listing various food delivery options and their contact information.

I appreciated that there wasn't any disruptive maid service knocking loudly or attempting to enter my room early in the morning. This place seemed more suitable for long-term stays, and I believe the maids only came around during the weekdays from Monday to Friday if requested. Since my stay was only for three days, this arrangement worked fine for me. I went shopping at Shoprite and stocked up my fridge with water and breakfast items to cook.

Overall, I had a fantastic experience at this place. The large living room provided a great space for entertaining guests, while the desk was perfect for studying my Anatomy notes. I also want to mention how incredibly quiet the location was. I absolutely loved the tranquility of the place; it felt like I was the only one there. This quiet atmosphere was especially beneficial on Sunday when I had a lot of studying to do and two TVs to watch The Walking Dead on. I would definitely choose to stay here again. The accommodations were spacious and modern, and I really enjoyed my time here.

input: I had the worst experience of my life and it's not over yet.  I made a mistake in purchasing a vehicle that is out of my budget on a Friday afternoon.  By Sunday after review of my budget I realized I was unable to afford the car.  I called the salesman and tried to explain my situation at 11:30am.  He stated he would speak with his manager and call me back.  At 3:30 after no return call, I called him again, no answer. I left a voicemail and still no call at closing time.  Monday morning I arrived at the dealership as they were opening.  I asked Stephen, the salesman what they determined.  He instructed me to have a seat and he would talk to his management team.  One hour + later, I was called into a cubicle and told my loan had been funded and the title had been changed.  Therefore, I would have to sell the car back to the dealership as a used car.  I would lose a lot of money in doing this.  This morning, Bill head of finance advised that the bank had questions about funding the loan.  I received a call from the bank stating the loan had NOT been funded and they would be unable to okay the loan.  I have left numerous messages with the dealership and have yet to receive a callback.  I contacted an attorney and per his review I again called the dealership and asked for a time to return the vehicle and take back my trade.  Still no response!  These people will lie to your face, avoid this dealership!!
Rewrite this for me:
I had an extremely negative experience that is still ongoing. On a Friday afternoon, I made a mistake by purchasing a vehicle that was beyond my budget. After reviewing my budget on Sunday, I realized that I couldn't afford the car. At 11:30 am, I called the salesman to explain my situation. He said he would consult with his manager and call me back. However, by 3:30 pm, I hadn't received a return call, so I called him again, but he didn't answer. I left a voicemail, but still received no response by closing time.

The following Monday morning, as soon as the dealership opened, I went there and asked Stephen, the salesman, for an update. He asked me to wait and said he would discuss the matter with his management team. I waited for over an hour until I was finally called into a cubicle. There, they informed me that my loan had already been funded and the title had been changed. As a result, if I wanted to return the car, I would have to sell it back to the dealership as a used car, which would mean a significant financial loss for me.

To make matters worse, this morning Bill, the head of finance, informed me that the bank had raised concerns about funding the loan. I immediately received a call from the bank saying that the loan had not been funded, and they were unable to approve it. I've left numerous messages with the dealership, but they have yet to return my calls. Frustrated and seeking legal advice, I contacted an attorney. Following their advice, I once again called the dealership and requested a time to return the vehicle and take back my trade. However, I still haven't received a response.

In summary, this dealership lacks integrity and they are willing to lie to your face. My suggestion would be to avoid doing business with them at all costs.

input:
I have been a patron of Desi Village in West Philly for years.  After moving the suburbs, we saw the KOP Desi Village and finally tried it.  We were skeptical having also tried Mood Cafe (owned by the W.Philly folks), and it wasn't as good. But the KOP location is actually very comparable to the West Philly location.  

There is no ambiance or atmosphere here.  The strip mall where it's located is pretty depressing.  Desi Village may be the only active store in it.  And its decor is tired and old.  It is a big space and it appears they do a big lunch buffet but I'm curious if it's ever full.  So don't go for the ambiance.

But the food is good.  We ordered some Keema Naan, Samosas, Saag Paneer, and Lamb Biryani.  All of it was really good.  Perfectly seasoned, not too oily, and appropriately spicy.  I have a nut allergy and made them aware of that and they did not screw it up (most Indian restaurants do).  So we'll definitely be back.  It would be great if they moved into nicer digs but the food is what is most important.
Rewrite this for me:
I have been a loyal customer of Desi Village in West Philly for many years. Recently, after relocating to the suburbs, my family and I decided to give the KOP Desi Village a try. Admittedly, we were hesitant, considering our underwhelming experience at Mood Cafe (owned by the same people from West Philly). However, we were pleasantly surprised to find that the KOP location is actually quite comparable to its West Philly counterpart.

Unfortunately, the ambiance and atmosphere leave much to be desired. The strip mall where the restaurant is situated is rather gloomy, with Desi Village being the only active store around. To make matters worse, the decor inside the restaurant feels outdated. It's a spacious place, and while they seem to offer an extensive lunch buffet, we were unsure if it ever gets full. So, don't expect a charming setting when you visit.

Nevertheless, the food is where Desi Village shines. We ordered Keema Naan, Samosas, Saag Paneer, and Lamb Biryani, all of which impressed us. The dishes were perfectly seasoned, not overly greasy, and had just the right amount of spice. As someone with a nut allergy, I made sure to inform the staff, and to my relief, they took it seriously and didn't make any mistakes (unlike most Indian restaurants). Because of this, we will definitely be returning. It would be wonderful if they relocated to a nicer space, but ultimately, it's the delicious food that truly matters.

input:
What an AMAZING occurrence that we ended up here after another barbecue place ran out of food!

So yeah, we started out at another spot and they were out of food when we got there. Super bummed and still in the mood for barbecue, we started wandering around Mid City and my trusty Yelp app guided me to this place. We were greeted by the super nice woman working the counter and she explained the whole process.

I decided to get the one-meat plate with "wet" pulled pork, grits and potato salad, I also got a medium mac and cheese, because I can. My boyfriend got the two-meat plate with brisket and pulled chicken with potato salad and fries. The food blew us both away! It was delicious from beginning to end. The pulled pork was perfect and had the perfect amount of sauce without being drenched. I could tell that if I hadn't ordered it wet it still would have been able to stand on it's own. The mac and cheese was incredible, and after the pork, was my favorite part of the meal. The stone ground grits had a different type of flavor (almost smoky) that I enjoyed and the potato salad was served cold and had that nice crunch that I like in potato salad,

We both agreed that the food was excellent, and a good deal to boot, and that we would both make the trip back out to Earhart, just to have more of this delicious food. The owner himself was bringing the food out to folks and he was really friendly and made sure that we were happy with everything. I like when the owners take the time to make sure that everything is okay. The atmosphere is casual and comfortable and the entire process was a breeze. I will definitely return to LA Smokehouse and I'll be adding it to my "BBQ Favorites" list for future reference.

Feeling disheartened but still craving barbecue, we decided to explore Mid City and thankfully, my trusty Yelp app led us to this gem. The woman at the counter warmly welcomed us and walked us through the ordering process.

I opted for a one-meat plate with "wet" pulled pork, accompanied by delectable sides of grits and potato salad. And just because I could, I indulged in a medium portion of mac and cheese. Meanwhile, my boyfriend went for the two-meat plate featuring brisket and pulled chicken, served with potato salad and fries. Let me tell you, the food exceeded our wildest expectations! Each bite was a mouthwatering delight. The pulled pork was perfection, generously sauced but not overwhelming. Even without the "wet" option, it would have stood on its own. The mac and cheese was absolutely incredible and quickly became my favorite part of the meal after devouring the pork. The stone ground grits had a distinct and enjoyable smoky flavor, and the potato salad had a refreshing crunch that I adore.

We both couldn't help but rave about the food, which not only impressed us but was also reasonably priced. It was agreed upon that we would gladly make the journey back to Earhart solely to relish in more of this scrumptious fare. The owner himself personally delivered our meals to our table, exuding friendliness and ensuring our satisfaction. I appreciate when owners take the time to ensure everything is up to par. The atmosphere was laid-back and cozy, making the entire experience a breeze. Without a doubt, I will be returning to LA Smokehouse and adding it to my list of beloved barbecue spots for future reference.

input:
After today's lunch, Iris has moved to the top of my New Orleans favorites lists--no small feat in a city where restaurants are numerous and culinary competition is fierce. Iris excels in every area: food, drinks, service, atmosphere, location, music and overall graciousness. I made the reservation for 10-15 people, not knowing exactly how many in my party would show up. Iris pulled out all the stops to make sure everyone had comfortable seating and even prepared an overflow table for us. At no time did we feel jostled or rushed, which is a common fine dining concern. 

The layout of the restaurant allowed diners to move freely to and from the table and to exchange seats as needed. The music selection was fun and unique, ranging from the Magnetic Fields to Johnny Cash. It was also quiet enough to be enjoyed while allowing conversation to flow unimpeded. Our waiter had excellent timing and anticipated our every need. 

Though they don't have a full drink menu for lunch (I hear they have an amazing mixologist for the dinner hour) they do offer a selection of martinis and wines. One of the guests has accounts with several high-end bars in the Quarter, and the drink list passed his muster. Our table settled for Chardonnays, Perseco and chilled shots of Chartreuse, though I hear they have several types of absinthe as well. 

Our group began with slices of warm, heavenly bread that Iris bakes in house. We continued with an assortment of salads--I had the Hollygrove arugula with warm goat cheese, niçoise olives and balsamic vinaigrette. It was fresh perfection. A few of us opted for the mussels, which I heard were delicious. For my main course, I had a wonderful drum with onions prepared in a tangy soy reduction, which was an elegant complement for the fish. I also heard rave reviews about the gnocci and chicken. 

All the entrees were creatively arranged and selected, and at no point did I feel overwhelmed or that any fuss or pretense had gone into the food. I also appreciated that the portions were European-sized (it always makes me laugh when other Americans list too-small portion size as a complaint even when the food is well-prepared!). Iris prepares a lot of their basic ingredients in-house, and I appreciate that the kitchen makes a point of incorporating gulf fish and produce purchased from local, farmer-friendly markets. 

We settled on the prix fixe menu, which was $20 a person for appetizer, main course and the dessert of the day (the best strawberry sorbet I have had yet). With the added drinks and tip it came out to under $35 a person, which is an excellent price for such a delicious white-linen lunch. No matter the size of my group, I will definitely be returning!

For my main course, I indulged in a beautifully prepared drum with tangy soy reduction and caramelized onions, enhancing the fish's delicate flavors. input:
Great atmosphere and decor. Super friendly staff seat you right away. I stopped once for lunch and one time for dinner. They have some lunch specials one of which was Pad Thai. I order with chicken as the protein but they have the typical options for this .  The portion was good for lunch and had good flavor.

For dinner I ordered the chicken satay to start and the Panang Curry with chicken for main course. I was very disappointed in the satay being that you only get two small skewers. The flavor and peanut dipping sauce were very good but they give a few more skewers.  The Panang was good and you get a good size portion of rice.

On a side note, I was disappointed they do not have Pad See Ew. Still some other options on the menu I will return to try.

The staff and manager really know customer service.  Look forward to returning soon!
Rewrite this for me:
The atmosphere and decor at this place are fantastic. The staff is incredibly friendly and seated me right away. I visited for lunch and dinner on separate occasions. They offer some great lunch specials, one of which was the Pad Thai. I chose to have it with chicken, but they have the usual options available. The portion size was perfect for lunch and the flavors were really good.

For dinner, I started with the chicken satay and had the Panang Curry with chicken as my main course. I was a bit disappointed with the satay because they only serve two small skewers. However, the flavor and peanut dipping sauce were delicious, and I just wished they would have given a few more skewers. On the other hand, the Panang Curry was really good and the portion of rice that came with it was satisfying.

I was a bit let down by the fact that they don't have Pad See Ew on their menu. Nevertheless, there are still plenty of other options that I'm excited to try next time I visit.

The staff and manager truly understand the meaning of excellent customer service. I can't wait to come back again soon!

input: I went to the pearl for my birthday and every detail of the experience was awesome!  The food, the wine and the service were all impeccable!  We didn't realize the time and were chatting away after closing time and the staff never made us feel rushed.

input: I work at the Frist and I don't eat at the cafe much, since I like to leave the building and go home for lunch. Add an extra egg for extra protein punch (as if all the meat wasn't enough already) and oil and vinegar dressing and i'm doing ok. A lot of museum visitors and local employees come for the cheap prices and quick bites. Beware of Senior Mondays (every 3rd Monday of the month) and weekends at lunchtime- it's usually busiest at 1130-noon.

input:
The food at Ghini's is just delicious. Everything for French breakfast imaginable, and more. I highly recommend the eggs provencale, not something you can get anywhere else. Two eggs basted with a sliced hot house tomato, thyme, garlic and herbs de provance. Get the baguette toast and add the great hashbrowns for a mere dollar.
My personal favorite are all the crepes, both sweet and savory. Especially recommend the spinach and swiss.

input: This was such a unique spot, from the graffiti style art on the walls to the delicious food options and special hummus flavors. Good prices, great portion size. I had the greek steak pita with guac hummus. Will definitely be back!

input:
I really like Prep & Pastry - we have been twice in the last two months on a Sunday.  The best trick I learned is to put your name on the waitlist BEFORE YOU ARRIVE.  As long as you are within 5 miles of the restaurant, you can be added.  It is a great service.

I have tried a number of things for brunch and all have been excellent - even their sweets. I think my favorite is the breakfast sandwich.  I am not a big drinker, so I usually order the ice team and it really is better than almost anything else I have tried. 

Staff is really, really nice.  I highly recommend a visit if you are in town.
