The most valuable tip I discovered is to add your name to the waitlist prior to arriving. It's a nifty service that allows you to join the waitlist as long as you are within a 5-mile radius of the restaurant.

Their brunch offerings are absolutely delectable, and I have tried a variety of dishes, including their mouthwatering sweets. Among them all, my personal favorite has to be their breakfast sandwich. Even though I'm not much of a drinker, I always opt for their iced tea, which never fails to impress me with its exceptional taste.

Furthermore, the staff at Prep & Pastry is incredibly friendly and accommodating. I wholeheartedly recommend paying them a visit if you happen to be in town.

input:
Another great annual festival Edmonton has to offer.

The Fringe is over two weekends and the joining week full of performances. There's a variety of venues and plays to watch, street performers and musicians. There's a schedule online to find show times, buy tickets and learn more about the artists. 

Half of 104th closes down to add space for a variety of food vendors and artisan vendors (art, jewelry, clothing, etc.).

Good tip: there's a gourmet mini donut truck off behind the farmers market a bit tucked away. Amazing!

It's nice to take an hour or two before or after a show to walk around and casually stumble on other street performances. Or even go without seeing a play just to snack and shop at the vendors.

The location is absolutely fabulous.
Rewrite this for me:
Edmonton's annual festival, known as the Fringe, is a must-attend event. Spanning two weekends and a joining week filled with captivating performances, this festival offers a diverse range of both venues and plays to enjoy, showcasing the talents of street performers and musicians alike. Show times, ticket purchasing, and artist information can be easily found on their online schedule.

Taking place on half of 104th street, the festival closes down this bustling area in order to accommodate a plethora of food vendors and a variety of artisan vendors selling everything from art to jewelry and clothing.

For a hidden culinary gem, make sure to visit the gourmet mini donut truck located just a little behind the farmers market. The experience is simply amazing!

While attending a show, it is delightful to take some time beforehand or afterward to stroll around and serendipitously come across other captivating street performances. One can even attend the festival without watching a play, simply enjoying the delightful snacks and shopping opportunities offered by the vendors.

Lastly, the chosen location for this festival is truly remarkable.

input:
Wow have things changed at this location. I used to come here on a regular basis with a friend. I haven't been back in over a year and so couldn't wait to have lunch today. I was surprised at the deterioration in customer service...,.our server didn't smile, was unwilling to give a recommendation and didn't offer us a tea to go. When I used to come, every server was friendly, gave suggestions and always offered a tea to go. 

The food was okay and probably would have been better if we had been treated better.  I noticed there was tape on the benches where the leather/vinyl is wearing out; this looks tacky.

This used to be my favorite lunch spot; this is no longer the case. I will not be back.

Our server lacked a smile, refused to provide any recommendations, and did not even offer us a tea to go. Once upon a time, this place held the title of my favorite lunch spot, but those days are long gone. Regrettably, I have no intention of returning.

input:

Darin and Sierra have such attention to detail and quality that Darin even stopped by one of the wineries to meet us and to ensure that everything was as expected. Our driver was also extremely knowledgeable about the area and had many good suggestions throughout the day.

We couldn't have picked a better choice for a winery, brewery day tour and wedding day transportation than Jump on the School Bus! I highly recommend them to everyone!

input:
A great spot to take out-of-town guests. I take all my Chicago friends here and they fall in love. The burgers are incredible and the boozy shakes are like no other. The first time I had horchata shake I honestly had dreams about it for like a week. It's also super centrally located, a quick walk from Wash Ave and other downtown attractions. Great vibe, although I always prefer to get a table upstairs than sit at the community tables on the ground floor.

The burger selection is really, really great. You can pretty much get whatever your heart desires. I've had mac n cheese patties on my burger, you can get a bison burger, turkey burger, literally anything. I have tried a ton and have never been let down by the flavor combinations. The waiters are always super honest, in a good way. If you ask them what's better, X or Y, they're not going to jerk you around and say they're equally good. They'll give you their honest opinion. LOVE that. 

Another unique aspect about Bailey's Range is that they have a burger showdown (can't remember their technical term for it) where last week's featured burger goes up against a new burger recipe. It's a cool call-out that you don't see at a lot of other restaurants. 

The only reason I gave it a 4/5 star instead of 5/5 is because I've had a couple of instances (out of MANY visits, so it's really not alarming or anything) where I requested my burger medium or medium-rare and it turned out a little well done. I still ate it, but it wasn't really what I expected.
Rewrite this for me:
Bailey's Range is an excellent choice for entertaining out-of-town guests. I always bring my friends from Chicago here and they absolutely love it. The burgers are absolutely amazing and the boozy shakes are unmatched. I'll never forget the first time I had their horchata shake, it was so fantastic that I couldn't stop thinking about it for a whole week. Additionally, its central location makes it easily accessible, just a short walk from Wash Ave and other attractions in downtown.

The burger selection at Bailey's Range is truly impressive. Whatever your heart desires, they have it. I've had burgers with mac n cheese patties, bison burgers, and even turkey burgers, and they have all been outstanding. The flavor combinations are so delicious that I've never been disappointed. What sets this place apart is the honest and genuine service from the waitstaff. When I ask for their opinion on which burger is better, they don't beat around the bush, they give me their truthful thoughts. I really appreciate that.

Another noteworthy aspect of Bailey's Range is their burger showdown. Each week, a different burger recipe competes against the previous week's featured burger. It's a unique and exciting concept that you don't often see in other restaurants.

The only reason I didn't give it a perfect rating of 5/5 stars is because on a couple of occasions (out of many visits), my burger was cooked more well-done than I had requested. Although it was still enjoyable, it didn't match my expectations.

input:

However, it's worth noting that they don't have air conditioning. Although they do have ceiling fans, they aren't exactly effective during the monsoon season. But despite this, the food is definitely worth the journey!

input:
Super lunch option
Watch out for the yoga mats
You won't miss the meat

Lunch has been very strange for me since HipCity opened. Because here's the thing: I am a meat eater. I mean like my last meal on earth would be a burger. Or, just maybe, the fajita wrap. Because it's that good.

Haven't had everything on the menu yet, but everything I have had has been great. The buffalo bella and crispy hipcity ranch are amazing sandwich alternatives, especially paired with the green lemonade. The groothie is also delicious, and can stand on its own to get you through an afternoon if you only want to spend a few bucks.

Okay suffice it to say that the food is great. The staff is also very friendly, and when they get busy someone will come out along the line and take orders so congestion doesn't get too bad at the register itself.

My only issue with HipCity is that it is at times nearly impossible to figure out where to stand when you're waiting to order or waiting for your food. People kind of convene everywhere and it can get awkward when there's a line out the door. In such a small space it's hard to rectify, but if I see a line out the door I tend to walk on by not because it's a long wait (they're really efficient), it's just difficult to navigate the interior.

People seem to gather everywhere, causing some awkward moments when there's a line out the door. input:

input:
Rosemary's Grill is my favorite resaurant.  My wife and I take my Mother in law to Rosemary's Grill often for many reasons.  Their menu is extensive.  You can get Classic American food in many categories prepared fresh and delicious with great care and attention to detail that is lacking in common chain restaurants.  You can also get traditional Turkish cuisine that is the very best kebab that I ever had.  Rosemary's is a family owned business and they treat you like you are part of that family.  We are making Rosemary's our Saturday night place.  last weekend my wife and I took my. Mother in law to Rosemary's Grill for dinner.  It was even better that the time before.  I tried the Mixed grill kebab platter.  Lamb, Chicken, Adana, and gyro kebab meats, so tender and expertly spiced and grilled, along with a shepherds salad, grilled half tomatoes, rice, and of course flat bread.  The Adana kebab was particularly tender, juicy, and tasty.  I had never had Adana kebab before and will be ordering it again.  I shared a taste with my Mother in law and she loved it too!  mom in law had crab cakes and she enjoyed them very much.  My wife had the French onion soup, which she raves about and always orders.  She also had the roast turkey, mashed potatoes, cranberry sauce, and corn.  She loved everything on that platter.  She commented that the gravy was especially good.  The portion sizes are huge and we love to have the left overs again at home.  I have honestly not been to a restaurant in the area that has such good quality in all there entrees, sides, salad bar, and drinks, and you have to try the rice pudding.  We have eaten a few times here for breakfast, lunch, and dinner and it continues to be our very favorite place.  The waitstaff and owners make you feel right at home and are warm, welcoming, and friendly.  I can not say enough good things.  

Sent from my iPad

input:

input:
I regularly go to student salons for hair cuts and styling. 

I have long, fine, mostly straight Asian hair, and have had mixed results from the Aveda Institute -- to be expected considering I had a different stylist in every case.

Just know that if you haven't had a student stylist before, don't expect perfection. Do expect the cut to take an inordinately long time compared to a seasoned professional -- most of my cuts/styles have taken around 2 hours. The basic cut price includes massaging wash, cut, and blowdry style, plus the stylists do take the time to check in with their teachers and make sure the cut is going the way you want it to. Another plus: all of the stylists I've had at the Aveda Institute have been professional and committed to their service, which isn't always the case at other schools. And the prices are right.

input:
I would NOT recommend this place to anyone. Their biggest mistake is not having a customer service department. They rely on their sales team to provide customer service meaning every time you call in to try and get something done, you get put into a voicemail because the sales guy is out selling - which should be their only job. This left me on numerous occassions incredibly frustrated that I could not get an answer. I even left the manager a voicemail (big surprise I couldn't get them to answer) and they never had the decency to call me back - Just made my sales person call me back.

I purchased my car last July and was promised numerous things would be done to the car before I purchased it. One of which being the tint on the rear window would be removed as the view out of the back was blurry. Somehow, that passed thru inspection and when I came to sign the papers, I noticed that it was still on the back windshield. I was told that they would have it removed by the time we were done the paperwork. Also, I was told that the price was going to be higher than the original agreement because the sales manager did the math wrong the previous day when we ran numbers. I told him that wasn't my fault and I would only pay the agreed upon amount and he spoke with the manager and got it sorted out. 

After sitting in the office for 2.5 hours, they finally told me that they were unable to even start taking off the tint and I would have to bring the car back. I dropped it off that Friday and let them keep it for the weekend. My sales guy called me on Saturday night to tell me that they never got to finish it and I would have to bring it back again and leave it. I live 45 minutes from the dealership so this isn't something I can easily do. I insisted on them giving me a loaner car for whatever day they would do this as I was sure this wouldn't be a one day process from my previous experience. 2.5 weeks later they were able to provide me with said car and I dropped off my vehicle. When I went to pick up my "finished car" there was still tint left on the bottom of the windshield. 

After all of that I knew I would never bring my car back for service there if that's the kind of service they provide. Now with all the rain we've been having, my trunk is leaking and when I called to check with the service department to see if it would be covered under warranty, I got the same run around with the service department who just said "I don't know" - OK well give me someone who will be able to tell me. Once they forwarded me to the correct person, I again got "I don't know". We need you to bring it in and look at it then submit to our warranty company to see if it gets accepted. No thanks after my previous experience of bringing my car in there to get "serviced". 

Invest in a customer service department to handle complaints in a professional and timely matter. This should not in any way be left upon the sales department to do. My sales guy did the best he could and I appreciated the help he gave me, but no one else would help me throughout the entire process. Not a good look on managements part.
Rewrite this for me:
I strongly advise against recommending this place to anyone due to their lack of a customer service department. Instead, they rely on their sales team to handle customer inquiries, resulting in frustrating experiences of being placed on voicemail. I even left a voicemail for the manager but never received a call back, only a return call from my sales person.

Last July, when I purchased my car, I was promised various things would be taken care of before the purchase. One of these was the removal of the blurry tint on the rear window. However, during the paperwork signing, I noticed that the tint was still present. They assured me it would be removed in due time. Additionally, they informed me that the price would be higher than initially agreed upon because of a math error made by the sales manager the previous day. I voiced my disagreement, insisting on paying only the agreed-upon amount, and after some discussion with the manager, the issue was resolved.

After spending 2.5 hours at the dealership, they informed me that they were unable to start removing the tint. They requested that I bring the car back for this purpose. I dropped off the car on a Friday and allowed them to keep it for the weekend. However, on Saturday night, my sales person informed me that they hadn't finished the job and requested me to bring it back again and leave it with them. Unfortunately, this was inconvenient for me as I live 45 minutes away from the dealership. I demanded a loaner car for the duration of the tint removal, as I anticipated it would not be a one-day process based on past experiences. Finally, 2.5 weeks later, they provided me with a loaner car, and I dropped off my vehicle. When I picked up my car after the supposed completion of the job, I noticed that there was still tint residue on the bottom of the windshield.

After all of this, I decided I would never bring my car back to this dealership for servicing due to the poor service they provided. Now, with the ongoing heavy rain, my trunk is leaking. When I called the service department to inquire about warranty coverage, I encountered the same unhelpful response, with the service department employees saying, "I don't know." I requested to speak with someone who could provide me with answers, and although they eventually forwarded me to the appropriate person, I received the same unsatisfactory reply of "I don't know." They insisted that I bring in the car for inspection and submit it to the warranty company to check if it would be covered. Given my prior experience with their service, I declined their offer and decided not to bring my car in for service.

It is essential for the establishment to invest in a dedicated customer service department to handle complaints professionally and promptly. It should not be the responsibility of the sales department to handle such matters. While my sales person did their best to assist me, no one else provided any support throughout the entire process. This reflects poorly on the management.

input: I love this restaurant. The owners are the nicest family. The food is delicious!!. My favorite is bacon pizza. I love that there is a play room for my kids to play while we wait for our food.

input:
Harry's blue bell is a nice spot. We stopped a few days ago for a quick dinner. It's tucked in the corner of a shopping center and it's very easy to miss. It was packed and seemed like the place to be for locals. The inside is nice but small, only a few tables in the entire place. The service was just okay. 

The beer selection is very good as are the prices on the beer. The food menu was a bit limited with you're basic bar food. The wife went with the bbq pulled pork and I went with the chicken and honey mustard wrap. The bbq pork was good, the bun was nicely toasted but the sauce was overly sweet for our liking. The wrap was fresh and good but nothing spectacular. The fries were hot and crispy. The kale slaw was fantastic but a very small portion.

Overall it was a decent meal. I wouldn't go out of my way to go back. If I were in the area I'd stop though. Solid 3 stars.
Rewrite this for me:
Harry's blue bell is a pleasant spot that we visited a few days ago for a quick dinner. It's tucked away in the corner of a shopping center, making it easy to miss. Despite its hidden location, it was bustling with locals and seemed to be a popular place to be. The interior is nice, albeit small, with only a few tables available. The service was satisfactory, nothing outstanding.

The highlight of Harry's blue bell is undeniably its impressive beer selection, accompanied by reasonable prices. However, the food menu was somewhat limited and consisted mainly of standard bar fare. My wife opted for the bbq pulled pork, which was satisfying overall, though we found the sauce to be excessively sweet for our taste. I went for the chicken and honey mustard wrap, which was fresh and enjoyable, though it didn't leave a lasting impression. On the bright side, the fries were hot and crisp, and the kale slaw was fantastic, despite the portion being quite small.

In conclusion, our experience at Harry's blue bell was decent. While it may not be worth going out of our way to return, we would definitely stop by if we happened to be in the area. It earns a solid three-star rating.

input:

input: Great atmosphere, service was very friendly and prices were very reasonable however I found the food a bit bland, not bad just bland. My husband and I were starving after a long drive to Philly and this filled the spot but it wasn't overly enjoyable and we most likely won't be back.

input:
Freedom toast = check, freedom fries = check, awesome breakfast food = check.

The is a greek owned pancake house (hence the over doing it on naming the food) and is a great alternative to your larger chain pancake houses such as Robert Evans, IHopity hop, and Mr. Dennys. 

We eat here every new years day, typically around 2 pm when we drag ourselves out of a drunken slumber to brave the bitter cold. They never have a problem seating our group of about 12-15 and are pleasant and quick service. 

The energetic owner likes to roam around making sure everything is going well. In my opinion, the food is also better than the chains. The secret ingredient is love.
Rewrite this for me:
We've got freedom toast, check. We've got freedom fries, check. And of course, we've got awesome breakfast food, check.

This pancake house is proudly Greek-owned, which explains their enthusiasm for giving food some quirky names. It's a delightful alternative to the bigger chain pancake houses like Robert Evans, IHopity hop, and Mr. Dennys.

On every New Year's Day, around 2 pm, we stumble out of bed, still feeling the effects of the previous night's festivities, and brave the freezing temperatures to come here. Despite our large group of 12-15 people, they never have any trouble seating us and provide us with pleasant and efficient service.

The spirited owner can often be found making the rounds, ensuring that everything is running smoothly. In my opinion, the food here surpasses that of the chain restaurants. There's a secret ingredient in every dish, and that ingredient is love.

input:

I have been here several time. My previous experience is better. During the month of Ramadan, they serve the buffet that are plenty of choices and attractive. I would said try them during this time. The buffet of Ramadan usually start at 8:30. Go early because is a lot of customers.

input:
This review is mainly chicken talk as Cuenelli's Peruvian Style Rotisserie Chicken brings to the table. Pollo a la brasa.... Rotisserie chicken.... Whatever you wanna call it.... I call it a technique done here with love and pride. Lets be clear, you will find no comparison coming from your grocer deli section or at the checkout isle.

Why do I think this chicken have some TLC put into it? On biting down of this chicken you can note seasoning flavors down to the bone. This is an inclination that prior to even getting into the rotisserie oven, these birds spend some time in some form of marinating process. Building flavor, the chicken also has a seasoning rub all over the skin.

Lets go to this rotisserie oven. Another unique element is this oven has a charcoal or grill like component. This gives the chicken a smoky element in the flavor build. As these birds turn in this oven, they keep moist from the natural drippings dropping from bird to bird as they rotate through this oven. In turn, this a reason why some people may note some pieces the skin end up dry and crispy and others get moist or soggy skin on their chicken In the end, you end up with this tender, smoky, well seasoned, fall off the bone goodness. Wait.... how can they add more flavor? Cuenelli's serves it with two dipping sauces, a chimichurri  which gives a herbaceous and slightly spicy flavor, and an aioli which has a garlicky - lemony element.

Round out this meal with some solid sides. Must haves for me would be the cilantro rice. Another herbaceous addition that works well with this meal. I got to use the word herbaceous a few times in this review, it has reflects such great imagery for food talk:) Must have beans with rice no? I pick the spicy pinto beans over the black beans at this establishment but lets be clear these beans are pretty spicy. I also love the maduros here. These sweet plantatains are cooked to perfection where the outsides has this caramelization from the natural sugar of the sweet plantain, leaving you with this toffee-like, stick to your tooth exterior and soft and sweet interior. 

Wash all down with Inca cola or a bottle of chicha limena.  Inca cola is almost like a cola champagne or a cream soda type of drink. Chicha Limena I say is Christmas in a bottle. This juice has a floral base blended with cinnamon and cloves.

Though Cuenelli's Peruvian Style Rotisserie Chicken have many other notable Latin dishes, the one thing that comes to mind to me is this chicken made with love. This chicken gives new meaning to all who thought they knew what rotisserie chicken is. I say, go to Cuenelli's and taste again for the very first time.
Rewrite this for me:
Cuenelli's Peruvian Style Rotisserie Chicken is a chicken lover's dream. From the moment you take a bite, you can taste the delicious flavors that have been infused into the meat. Unlike the rotisserie chicken you find at the grocery store, Cuenelli's chicken is marinated beforehand, making every bite bursting with seasoning. The chicken is then cooked in a special rotisserie oven that adds a smoky touch to the flavor. As the birds rotate in the oven, the natural drippings keep them moist, resulting in tender and flavorful meat.

But the flavor doesn't stop there. Cuenelli's serves their chicken with two incredible dipping sauces - a chimichurri with a hint of spice, and an aioli with a garlic-lemon kick. These sauces complement the chicken perfectly and enhance the overall experience.

To complete the meal, there are fantastic sides to choose from. The cilantro rice adds an herbaceous twist that pairs well with the chicken. And of course, you can't forget the beans - spicy pinto beans that pack a punch. And if you're in the mood for something sweet, the maduros are a must-try. These caramelized sweet plantains have a toffee-like exterior and a soft, sweet interior that will leave you wanting more.

To wash it all down, Cuenelli's offers refreshing drink options. Inca cola, with its unique cola champagne flavor, is a great choice. Or, for a taste of Christmas, try the Chicha Limena - a floral juice blended with cinnamon and cloves.

While Cuenelli's has a variety of other Latin dishes to offer, their Peruvian Style Rotisserie Chicken is truly something special. It's clear that this chicken is made with love, surpassing any preconceived notions of what rotisserie chicken should be. So, head over to Cuenelli's and experience rotisserie chicken like never before.

input: fuck yes. meat, bourbon libations, and a salad (to round things out aka make myself feel better about ingesting the aforementioned two items.) i took myself on an early birthday date with myself and was not disappointed (neither in the food nor the company). i had a medium rare plain burger to see if it was worth all the fuss...no cheese, bacon, dressing, etc to disguise the quality of the meat. (of course, no bread either since i'm gluten free.) the burger was great - perfectly cooked and seasoned... though, i felt like a bit of a freak sitting at the bar eating my burger with a knife and a fork. i'd like to come back to try a fancypants burger since the extras look pretty tasty.  the salad was so-so; it was no frills with the perfect amount of dressing. the bartender-cum-waiter was super attentive but not cloyingly so. he made delicious sazeracs to accompany my repast.
Rewrite this for me: Absolutely! I indulged in some delectable meat, paired with bourbon libations and a salad to balance things out and ease my guilt over the indulgence. I treated myself to an early birthday date and was thoroughly satisfied, both with the food and my own company. I opted for a simple medium rare burger without any additional toppings or bread, just to truly appreciate the quality of the meat. It did not disappoint, perfectly cooked and seasoned. Admittedly, I felt a bit peculiar dining at the bar while using a knife and fork to enjoy my burger. However, I am eager to return and try one of their more extravagant burgers, as the extras seemed irresistibly flavorful. The salad was decent, uncomplicated, and paired well with just the right amount of dressing. The bartender, also doubling as the waiter, was attentive without being overly obtrusive. He skillfully whipped up sazeracs to accompany my delightful meal.

input: Here's an update for my further Comcast experience. Our bill was increased to 250.00 a month. We called and removed some luxery items which brought our bill to 225.00 a month. Called 4 time a to see how we could get our bill lowered, as we have been a loyal customer for 14 years. "Nothing we can do" was all I heard. We decided to no longer be raped by this company and set up service with Verizon. Called Comcast to cancel once we got hooked up with Verizon. All of a sudden, they can do better and reduce my bill to 140.00 a month....which I would have been extremely happy with. Unfortunately, it should have been offered the four previous times I called.  I have Verizon now and have been quite happy with the installation, customer service, and overall product.  I wish Comcast would go under because they don't care about quality customer service. They could offer me a years free of service, yet I wouldn't take it on principle. Screw you Comcast!
Rewrite this for me:
I would like to provide an update on my recent experience with Comcast. Our monthly bill was increased to $250.00, prompting us to call and remove some luxury items in order to bring it down to $225.00. Despite being loyal customers for 14 years, every time we called four times to inquire about reducing our bill, we were told that there was nothing they could do.

Frustrated with this lack of assistance, we made the decision to switch to Verizon for our services and called Comcast to cancel our subscription once we were set up with Verizon. Surprisingly, Comcast suddenly offered to reduce our bill to $140.00 a month, a price we would have been extremely happy with. However, it should have been offered during any of the four previous calls we made.

Now that we have switched to Verizon, we are pleased with the installation, customer service, and overall product they provide. It is disappointing that Comcast doesn't prioritize quality customer service. Even if they were to offer me a year of free service, I wouldn't accept it out of principle. Comcast, you've let us down.

input:

input:

Now, though, the food is disgusting. 90% of their buffet offerings are WAY too salty. The pulled turkey was tough, the fish tasted like licking a bottle of meat tenderizer, and the vegetables cooked to a putty-like state. The only thing vaguely edible was the corn pudding and mashed potatoes. The desserts are ok, almost store-bought quality. 

The service at least was good. Our waitress refilled our drinks promptly and removed plates often. The only good I saw all night.

A vast majority of their buffet offerings are excessively salty, rendering them practically inedible. The pulled turkey was extremely tough, the fish tasted as if it had been marinated in a bottle of meat tenderizer, and the vegetables were cooked to a mushy consistency. Fortunately, the silver lining lies in the service. Our waitress promptly refilled our beverages and frequently cleared our plates. That was the sole positive aspect I witnessed throughout the entire evening.

input:
The long and the short of it: A romantic little BYOB in Newtown Square that hits the mark in several areas. Big portions at decent prices. You won't leave hungry!

And now for a full review:

I have been to this Fellini's Cafe and the one in Bryn Mawr several times and each time I've visited there have been some memorable moments...and there have been speed bumps that keep this place from reaching its full potential.

On my latest visit this past Friday night, I made reservations for 730. My beautiful wife and I arrived right at 730. Although there were two vacant tables available, it took them at least 10 minutes or so to seat us. And when they did, they broke up a table for 6 instead of putting us at the 2 seater. Odd.

Being out and away from the kids for a few hours, we wanted at least a little bit of privacy, instead of sitting next to (pretty much connected to) a table of four. We asked the manager if we could be moved to the 2 seater...he said fine. Another 5-10 minutes (too long!) later a member of the wait staff came and, without any indication as to his intentions, whisked up our bottle of wine and silverware and ran off to the other table. Not a problem, but some eye contact and a simple 'follow me please' with even a hint of a smile would have been lovely. We shrugged and just rolled with it.

The interior is quaint, and the lighting is dim. It's a nice place for a romantic meal. But it is LOUD. So loud I would say this place is kid friendly despite being in such close quarters with your neighbors. Not sure if we'd ever try taking our four kids there (actually I'm certain we won't) but one or two can be done without much trouble.

Our waitress was extremely polite and offered the energy and enthusiasm that our other friend lacked.

For dinner, we ordered a caesar salad to share and for our main courses my wife opted for her usual tagliatelli with mushroom cream sauce and i had what i always have, the tortellini pasticiatti.

Complimentary with the meal were two pieces of bruschetta (very nice) and a small loaf of crusty Italian bread, which is served with butter packets (which perhaps only I find strange for an Italian restaurant?). 

Overall the food was delicious, except for a few somewhat minor hiccups: 

1. The caesar salad was served on a warm plate. The salad was excellent and would have been legendary had it been served on a chilled (or at least not warm!) plate.

2. I am pretty sure they used frozen peas in the tortellini dish, which is fine with me as long as you make sure the peas are thawed before you serve it! Only a few peas were not quite thawed, but it marred what was otherwise a perfectly crafted masterpiece of a dish.

When we paid, the manager allowed us to use an expired gift card. That was a very nice gesture and one that required no push from us to induce.

All in all, I'll keep visiting Fellini because it's relatively inexpensive and they do most everything well.
Rewrite this for me:
Fellini's Cafe in Newtown Square is a charming and romantic BYOB spot that excels in many aspects. The portions are generous and reasonably priced, ensuring you won't leave hungry.

During my most recent visit on a Friday night, I had a mix of memorable moments and minor setbacks that prevent Fellini's from reaching its full potential.

Despite making reservations for 7:30 pm, my wife and I had to wait around 10 minutes to be seated, even though there were available tables. Furthermore, they seated us at a larger table instead of a smaller one, which took away some privacy. However, after requesting to be moved, we were eventually accommodated.

The interior of the restaurant is quaint with dim lighting, creating a perfect ambiance for a romantic dinner. However, it can get quite noisy, making it somewhat kid-friendly. Personally, I wouldn't bring my four kids here, but it could work for couples with one or two children.

Our waitress was polite and attentive, making up for the lackluster service from another staff member.

For our meal, we shared a caesar salad and ordered our usual favorites, the tagliatelli with mushroom cream sauce and the tortellini pasticiatti.

The complimentary bruschetta and crusty Italian bread were delicious additions to our meal. However, serving butter packets in an Italian restaurant seemed slightly odd to me.

Overall, the food at Fellini's Cafe was delicious, but with a couple of minor hiccups. The caesar salad would have been perfect if it hadn't been served on a warm plate, and there were a few partially thawed peas in the tortellini dish. Despite these issues, the dishes were still enjoyable.

The manager made a nice gesture by allowing us to use an expired gift card when paying, showing their willingness to go the extra mile.

All things considered, I will continue visiting Fellini's Cafe because it offers good value for money and most aspects are well executed.

input:
Pretty bummed I didn't try out the Catbird Seat, because this place was totes underwhelming. When you enter, there is a large, awkward entrance and you have to go upstairs to be seated. It was probably only half full, but since it was strange weather, we decided to sit indoors. I'll just say again, walking up towards the hostess as she watches you approach just feels....weird. 

Our server was nice, and we joked with him about the silly flower in a very knock-over-able vase. We got two drinks--julep and one of their other ones with gin, both of which were utterly average to bad. 

The crowd was sort of stuffy. The bread was blah. The food was pretty forgettable. The tenderloin was good because it was a good cut of meat. The Amish chicken was pretty average, with a not so flavorful and slightly MSG-y twang jus. Their signature grits was underwhelming as well. 

All in all, stuffy and so overpriced. Bummed out!
Rewrite this for me:
I was really disappointed that I didn't give the Catbird Seat a try, because it turned out to be quite underwhelming. As you enter, you are greeted by a large and awkward entrance, and you have to go upstairs to find your seat. Despite the place being only half full, we chose to sit indoors due to the peculiar weather. I must say, approaching the hostess as she watches you can feel quite uncomfortable.

Fortunately, our server was pleasant, and we shared a laugh with him about the ridiculous flower in a vase that seemed like it could tip over any moment. However, the two drinks we ordered, the julep and one with gin, were nothing special and quite average or even bad in taste.

The crowd seemed a bit uptight, the bread turned out to be unremarkable, and the food itself was rather forgettable. The only redeeming quality was the tenderloin, which was decent thanks to its high-quality cut of meat. As for the Amish chicken, it was average at best, with a slightly MSG-like twang in its not-so-flavorful jus. Even their signature grits were underwhelming.

Overall, the place had a stuffy atmosphere and was incredibly overpriced. I left feeling quite disappointed.

input:
This review is LONG overdue!  I visited Stitch-It in June 2013

In brief: Stitch it did an EXCELLENT job on my dress and I was extremely pleased.  I needed it done in a rush and they were able to accommodate me.  Given the tight turnaround, and the work that needed to be done, I didn't mind paying a premium.  The service and results far exceeded my expectations.

Complete Experience: I was attending a convention in Nashville, TN and had ordered an evening gown online a week before (admitted procrastinator tendencies).  The gown was a navy blue Tadashi Shoji evening gown with sequins and an intricately designed lace and sheer layered bodice. The gown was a tad bit too long and there was a bulge in the back. The dress arrived a few days before I was scheduled to fly out to Nashville and I knew I wouldn't have time to get it tailored before leaving.  I found a few Nashville area tailor shops on Yelp, read the reviews and decided I might try Stitch-It.  I also saw a few cleaners that advertised they performed tailoring services, but they (quite frankly) didn't give me the warm and fuzzies.  

Stitch-It was about a 30 minute drive from the Gaylord Hotel where I was staying, so before taking a taxi that far, I decided to check with the hotel to see if they had an in-house tailor.  When I took the dress to the Gaylord tailor/seamstress (who was the nicest lady ever), she looked at the gown and said "I can hem the bottom....I'd have to do it by hand.  The top part though....I won't touch that with a 10ft. pole!"  I laughed, but appreciated her honesty in not being able to handle the work that I needed done.  

I contacted Stitch-It and sent pictures of the dress via text message to a nice young man who's name I can't remember (I think it was Cameron...I could be wrong).  They assured me that they should be able to accommodate me, so I hopped a cab and visited Stitch-It.  When I arrived I was greeted by courteous and professional staff.  I was shown to the dressing room and changed into my gown.  My personal tailor was Maggie O'Neill and she was AWESOME!  After the fitting and pinning, I left the gown and picked it up in two days.  It fit perfectly and was well worth the fee.  If I lived in Nashville, I would DEFINITELY use Stitch-It on a regular basis.
Rewrite this for me:

In short, Stitch-It did an incredible job altering my dress and I couldn't have been happier. I was in a rush to get it done and they were able to accommodate me without any issues. Given the tight timeframe and the amount of work that needed to be done, I didn't mind paying a little extra. The service and the end result surpassed all my expectations.

Here's the full story: I was attending a convention in Nashville, TN and had ordered an evening gown online just a week before (yes, I'm guilty of procrastination). The gown was a beautiful navy blue Tadashi Shoji with sequins and a meticulously designed lace and sheer layered bodice. Unfortunately, it was a little too long for me and had a bulge in the back. The dress arrived only a few days before my trip, so there was no time to get it tailored beforehand.

I did some research on Yelp and came across a few tailor shops in Nashville. Among them, Stitch-It seemed like a good choice based on their reviews. I also found some cleaners that offered tailoring services, but they didn't give me the best vibes.

Stitch-It was around 30 minutes away from the hotel I was staying at, the Gaylord Hotel. I thought it would be worth checking with the hotel first if they had an in-house tailor. I contacted Stitch-It and sent them pictures of the dress via text message to a helpful young man, whose name I unfortunately can't recall (maybe Cameron?). If I lived in Nashville, I would definitely make Stitch-It my go-to tailor. Their service was superb and I highly recommend them to anyone in need of alterations.

If you're looking for a great brunch place in New Orleans, definitely come here!

My boyfriend and I had brunch here on Sunday, and we loved it! We both started with the Brandy Milk Punch, which was divine.  If you are of age, order this drink!  It is an alcoholic milkshake, and I could literally go here just to drink that because it is so good.  

They bring out fresh bread and butter, and then my boyfriend and I ordered the trio of appetizers.  The trio is quite small, but it includes a duck springroll, fried chicken livers and a fried oyster.  The duck springroll came with a wonderful tangy sauce, which I greatly enjoyed.  My boyfriend enjoyed the fried chicken livers and the fried oyster, but those are not two of my favorite things.

For my entree, I ordered the shrimp and grits.  Oh my goodness... so good! The shrimp are bacon-wrapped, and the grits are true Southern grits.  I will definitely order this dish again when I get the chance to return.  My boyfriend ordered the fish of the day, which was blackened Mahi Mahi, and he loved it.  

Definitely go to Mr. B's!

As my turn came up, I approached the cart tenuously, for I did not want to blow it by asking too many questions. He immediately recognized me as a new customer and told me all about the fresh ingredients he uses.

There was enough food for 2 people.
Well worth the wait!

input: Another five-star dining review!  Fresco serves-up wonderful fresh and tasty pizza.  We tried this store as a change in our usual fare when we visit Tucson during the gem shows. input:
We went to this restaurant after running in the Philadelphia marathon.  We had a large group (12) with us including kids (ages 10-14), parents and grandparents. The food was very good for the parents but everything was on the spicy side which was not so great for the kids and grandparents.  The lighting was very dim which was an issue for the grandparents reading the menu.  

The Veggie wings were great as were the cactus and sweet potato burritos.   The guacamole was very good although the spicy chips were a little too much.

They offer pitchers of margaritas which was great for our large group.
Rewrite this for me:
After participating in the Philadelphia marathon, our group of 12, including children aged 10-14, parents, and grandparents, decided to visit this restaurant. It appeared to be well-maintained and either recently renovated or adorned with new decorations. The service provided was exceptional and friendly. Although the food satisfied the parents' tastes, it leaned towards the spicier side, which was not particularly enjoyable for the kids and grandparents. The dim lighting posed a problem for the grandparents, making it difficult for them to read the menu.

Nevertheless, we found the Veggie wings, cactus, and sweet potato burritos to be excellent choices. The guacamole also impressed us, although the spicy chips were a bit overwhelming.

What made our experience even better was the fact that they offered pitchers of margaritas, which perfectly catered to our large group.

input:
First of all, I think this might be my first Yelp review about "fast food." It's not a genre I ever eat unless I'm forced to on a road trip.  However, I am from Buffalo, NY, and am a chicken-finger connoisseur, so I decided to give this place a chance.  Additionally, it was on a road trip of sorts.  We had been at the beach all day and were halfway back home to central Tampa.

The service is amazing!  I have never seen fast-food workers who take so much pride in their jobs.  These people were drinking the Zaxby's cool-aid!  They seemed more like Disney employees than fast-food workers.  Both a female counter gal and a male (possible the manager/franchisee) went out of their way to make sure we liked everything.  

The food was a solid 4 stars, but my review overall is rounded up for the above mentioned points.  We had the chicken finger sandwiches on Texas toast.  While the chicken fingers themselves were super juicy and moist, the Texas toast was too greasy to eat them on.  I love sauce and enjoyed the variety.  We tried the Zax, hot honey mustard, insane hot and ranch.  What is missing from the sauce variety, for me, is a spicy bbq and blue cheese.  Serving ranch with hot sauce is an insult to the folks in Buffalo that created the cuisine.  Aside from the bread and sauce small issues, I really enjoyed our meal.  Additionally, it was so cheap!!  $12 and change for 2 meals with drinks.  

I am a fan!  This place doesn't quite hit all the marks of Buffalo-Inspired food, but it does a pretty good job of putting a southern twist on chicken fingers!
Rewrite this for me:
To begin with, I believe this might be my inaugural Yelp review for "fast food." It's not a type of cuisine I typically indulge in unless circumstances oblige me to during a road trip. Nonetheless, being a chicken-finger enthusiast hailing from Buffalo, NY, I decided to give this establishment a try. Furthermore, it happened to be during a road trip of sorts, as my companions and I had spent the day at the beach and were now midway on our journey back to central Tampa.

The service provided was absolutely outstanding! I have never encountered fast-food employees who displayed such immense pride in their work. These individuals were completely absorbed in the ethos of Zaxby's! Their dedication to customer satisfaction made them appear more akin to Disney staff rather than fast-food workers. Both a female cashier and a male (possibly the manager/franchisee) went out of their way to ensure that we were pleased with our experience.

Now, when it comes to the food, I would give it a solid 4 stars, but my overall review is rounded up due to the aforementioned exceptional service. We opted for the chicken finger sandwiches on Texas toast. While the chicken fingers themselves were incredibly juicy and tender, the Texas toast was overly greasy to be eaten alongside them. I, personally, am a sauce aficionado and thoroughly enjoyed the variety offered. We sampled the Zax, hot honey mustard, insane hot, and ranch sauces. However, I feel that the sauce assortment lacks a spicy BBQ and blue cheese option. Serving ranch with hot sauce is a slight to the creators of Buffalo cuisine. Apart from the minor issues with the bread and sauces, our meal was genuinely enjoyable. Furthermore, it was incredibly affordable! For two meals with beverages, we only paid around $12.

To summarize, I am now a fervent admirer of this establishment! While it may not completely capture the essence of Buffalo-inspired cuisine, it does an admirable job of infusing a southern twist into chicken fingers.

input: I can't say enough great things about the baked goodies that come out of this kitchen.  I have YET to have anything that is 'subpar'.  Everything comes out with full flavor and with the right texture! Then the delicate and decorative detailing--just phenomenal.  You can tell that TIME and LOVE goes into each piece of goodness!!  I love all of the signature flavors.  I am a 'classic' cupcake person- and absolutely love her signature cream cheese frosting.  Talk about melt in your mouth! If you are looking for any sort of cake, cupcake, pie, cookie, or ALL THE ABOVE...do yourself a favor and treat yourself and loved ones to Sugar Coated! (no pun intended!) =)
Rewrite this for me: I cannot express enough how amazing the baked goods from this kitchen are. Every single item I've had so far has been exceptional, with no room for mediocrity. The flavors are all rich and delightful, while the texture is just right. The attention to detail in the delicate and decorative designs is simply phenomenal. It is evident that each piece of goodness is crafted with time and love. Personally, I am a fan of the classic cupcakes, and the signature cream cheese frosting is absolutely heavenly and melts in your mouth. Whether you are in the mood for cake, cupcakes, pie, cookies, or a combination of all, I highly recommend treating yourself and your loved ones to Sugar Coated. Trust me, it's worth it!

input:
It is unfortunate that with such a unique location and such a brand and product offering this specific store offers such lousy service. The wait is endless, no one is available to help and at Christmas time getting a gift wrap is act of God that requires endless wait. I bought gifts and knew that the wait for wrapping would be long SO I even left my items at the store to be gift wrapped at their leisure. They were not even moved from the counter where I bought them when I returned almost two hours later ready for pick up. This was a gift that needed to be given and The staff COMPLETELY "dropped the ball" on my time constraints! 

I love their stuff, but today was my last shopping experience at this location: couldn't get a gift wrapped after being assured that it could be done in a timely fashion???  I'll  cancel my card, do everything online and try not to go there if I can. It's really a shame!
Rewrite this for me:
Unfortunately, despite having such a unique location and an impressive brand and product offering, the service in this particular store is extremely disappointing. The waiting time is unbearable, assistance is nonexistent, and even getting a gift wrapped during Christmas feels like an impossible task. In anticipation of the long wait, I left my purchased items at the store to be gift wrapped at their convenience, only to find out that they hadn't even been moved from the counter when I returned almost two hours later. This was a time-sensitive gift that needed to be given, and the staff completely failed to meet my expectations. 

Although I have a great affinity for their products, today's shopping experience at this location has left a sour taste in my mouth. Despite being assured that timely gift wrapping was possible, it simply wasn't delivered. Therefore, I have decided that this will be my last shopping trip to this store. I will cancel my card, opt for online shopping, and avoid going there if I can. It's truly unfortunate that it has come to this.

input: They have a couple of really nice ladies, that go out of their way to help you. But there's one that will rip your head off if you're not careful. It won't take ya long to figure this out on your own though.  Jus' sayin'......
Rewrite this for me: They have a few incredibly pleasant ladies who willingly go above and beyond to assist you, except for one individual who may respond aggressively if you're not cautious. However, it won't require much time for you to realize this by yourself. Just thought I'd mention it.

input: Hendricks is a must try in St.Louis. The meats,sauces,and sides are better than most barbecue places.Onion rings are huge and the coleslaw is tasty and finely shredded. Service is good and very friendly. Takes awhile to get the meal,but it gives you time to check out the unique decor.
Rewrite this for me: When in St. Louis, you simply cannot pass up the opportunity to give Hendricks a go. This barbecue joint surpasses most others with its exceptional meats, delectable sauces, and delectable side dishes. The onion rings are impressively sizable, and their coleslaw is both flavorful and expertly shredded. The service is commendable, as the staff is both efficient and incredibly amiable. Although it may take a little longer to receive your meal, this affords you the chance to appreciate the establishment's distinctive decor.

input: Found there to be a good variety of food for a late night dinner with young kids. Wish we had one this good near us in upper PA. Person that rang us in was friendly and helpful. Two things  made our experience top notch. First was out waiter Eric, who was friendly, observant, went out of his way to get odd requests, and quick to getting back to us.  Eric is the type of waiter you would find a quality sit down restaurant.  The other were the 2 people at the grill house station. When I asked to have shrimp not basted due to a pepper allergy that offered to get different tings to remove them from the grill. I appreciated their thoughtfulness.
Rewrite this for me: We discovered a great variety of food available for a late night dinner with our young children. It's a shame we don't have a similar place like this near us in upper PA. The person who served us was friendly and helpful. Two aspects truly stood out and made our experience exceptional. Firstly, our waiter Eric was amazing. He was warm, attentive, and went above and beyond to fulfill our unusual requests. Not to mention, he was incredibly prompt in taking care of our needs. Eric is the kind of waiter you would expect to find in a high-quality sit-down restaurant. Secondly, the two individuals at the grill house station impressed us greatly. When I informed them about my allergy to peppers and requested for the shrimp to be prepared without any basting, they kindly offered alternative options to ensure the allergens were removed from the grill. Their thoughtfulness was highly appreciated.

input: i was looking forward to a new coffee spot, but this won't be it for me.  they dont have a menu first off, and im not a coffee connoisseur, so i was a little thrown off.  i kept it simple, asked for an iced tea, but they did give me hot tea w/a cup of ice.  v. artsy crowd here, great for people watching, but not for studying.  its a little loud, my headphones were not enough to block out the noise, so i was stuck listening to watever they chose, which wasn't my preference.  the servers were all really nice, and they kept cleaning the tables quite often.  all in all it wasnt a bad experience, but not one to keep me coming back either...
Rewrite this for me: I was excited about trying out a new coffee place, but unfortunately, it didn't live up to my expectations. Firstly, they didn't have a menu, which was a bit off-putting for someone like me who isn't a coffee expert. I decided to keep it simple and asked for an iced tea, but instead, they gave me hot tea with a cup of ice. The atmosphere was very artsy, attracting an interesting crowd for people-watching, but not conducive to studying. It was quite noisy, and even my headphones couldn't drown out the noise, so I had to endure their music choices, which weren't what I preferred. On the positive side, the servers were all friendly, and they kept the tables clean. Overall, it wasn't a terrible experience, but it's not a place I'll be returning to.

input: lit!!!!! just wanna give a shoutout to my g, kyle. he was such a chill waiter and deserves a raise or somethin. he recommended me the honey hot sauce and it was some of the best hot sauce i had eaten in ages. kyle from milk and honey changed my life and i will forever owe him. also the biscuits brought me to heaven. i didn't even order one i just stole from my friends but they were just that. good. so yeah def come here and ask about kyle. tell him i miss him and that i hope we get reunited soon.
Rewrite this for me: I wanted to take a moment to give a huge shoutout to my incredible friend, Kyle. He was absolutely amazing as our waiter and truly deserves recognition for his exceptional service. Not only did he recommend the honey hot sauce, which turned out to be the most delicious hot sauce I had tasted in years, but he also single-handedly changed my entire culinary experience at Milk and Honey. I will forever be grateful to Kyle for that. Another highlight of my visit were the heavenly biscuits. I couldn't resist stealing a bite from my friends, and let me tell you, they were outstanding. If you ever visit, make sure to ask about Kyle. Let him know that I miss him dearly and that I hope we have the chance to reunite soon. This place is an absolute gem, thanks to people like Kyle.

input:
Went here before a show we were seeing in the University City area.  It is just across the street from 30th Street Station, and just down the street from Drexel University.  We we able to get street parking about 2 blocks down the street, so that is always a plus.  

Service was sufficient for dinner.  We tried the mac and cheese appetizer that had just the right amount of breadcrumbs on it.  It was served hot, but with average taste.  We also tried the cheeseteak egg rolls - decent, but not a lot of meat in them.  Some of the bites I had of the egg roll were merely the fried dough without getting to any of the cheese and meat.   They were served with ketchup and a special mustard that had some horseradish in it for a bit of a kick!  I must say, it is a neat thing for a Philadelphia Pub to have on a menu.  

For our main entrees, we both had the chicken pot pie.  The vegetables were plentiful, and the chicken was all white meat, though there was not that much of it.  The crust was somewhat flaky, but there was a section of my pot pie crust that didn't seem like it was cooked all the way through.  

Dessert portion sizes were huge!  We had the bread pudding which was average in taste, and served with a scoop of vanilla ice cream.  The brownie was served ala mode with vanilla ice cream as well.  The brownie was definitely dry and lacking in taste, though I consider myself to be a brownie snob, so maybe I'm being overly picky.
Rewrite this for me:
We visited this place before attending a show in the University City area. It's conveniently located across the street from 30th Street Station and near Drexel University. Luckily, we managed to find street parking about 2 blocks down, which was a bonus.

The service for dinner was satisfactory. We decided to try the mac and cheese appetizer, which had just the right amount of breadcrumbs. It was served hot, but the taste was average. We also ordered the cheesesteak egg rolls, which were decent but lacked a significant amount of meat. Some bites of the egg roll only consisted of fried dough without any cheese or meat. They were accompanied by ketchup and a special mustard that had a hint of horseradish for a bit of a kick. It was interesting to see a Philadelphia Pub include these items on their menu.

For our main entrees, we both chose the chicken pot pie. The dish had plenty of vegetables and the chicken was entirely white meat, though there wasn't a substantial amount of it. The crust was somewhat flaky, but I noticed that a section of my pot pie crust didn't seem fully cooked.

The dessert portions were huge! We tried the bread pudding, which had an average taste and was served with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. The brownie was also served with vanilla ice cream and was unfortunately dry and lacking in flavor. However, I must admit that I am quite a discerning brownie connoisseur, so my criticism may be overly picky.

input: Went for a bachelorette party on a Saturday night in April. Definitely try to arrive on the earlier side! We got there at 8 and there was no line (by the time we left at around 11 there was a line down the street). The cover band is awesome. There were at least 10 other bachelorette groups there and a few 50th birthday parties too. Their signature cocktails are great but overpriced in my opinion. I would go back though for another bachelorette party or birthday. Probably wouldn't try if it was any regular night out. Gets very crowded.
Rewrite this for me: I attended a bachelorette party on a Saturday night in April and it is highly recommended to arrive early. When we arrived at 8, there was no waiting line (although by the time we left around 11, there was a line extending down the street). The live band was absolutely fantastic. Notably, there were numerous other bachelorette groups, as well as a few 50th birthday parties. While their signature cocktails were delicious, I felt they were somewhat overpriced. Nevertheless, I would definitely consider going back for another bachelorette party or birthday celebration. However, I would probably not choose this venue for a regular night out due to its tendency to become excessively crowded.

input: Hands down best fall off the bone BBQ I've ever had.Excellent pulled pork everything had that great smoky flavor.Very creamy mac and cheese.Service was fast and friendly. Dessert was equally as good walnut brownie and ice cream delight.Such a great find.
Rewrite this for me: Without a doubt, the BBQ here is the absolute best I've ever had. The pulled pork is exceptional, with a fantastic smoky flavor. The mac and cheese is unbelievably creamy. The service is quick and friendly. For dessert, the walnut brownie with ice cream is just as amazing. This place is truly a hidden gem.

input: It's a good thing I've had a few weeks to cool off from my experience at Copabanana before writing this review or it might not have been pretty. Anyhow, I came during university city restaurant week and will never return. We sat outside and there were kids playing football right near the tables and being loud. We moved to the other side of the restaurant (still outside) and the kids made there way over to us and continued playing. We couldnt get away. We went to a table inside. Food was terrible. Steak was fatty and overcooked and mashed potatoes werent fresh. The waitress was about the only thing good about this place. She agreed on the steak and took it back. Came back with chicken as I asked for and it was like biting into rubber bands. All in all it was a disaster and I'll never return. 1 star for the waitress.
Rewrite this for me: Luckily, I had some time to calm down after my experience at Copabanana before writing this review, otherwise it might have been quite unpleasant. I decided to visit during university city restaurant week, but I regret that decision now and I won't be coming back. We chose to sit outside, but unfortunately there were kids playing football near our tables and being very loud. To escape the noise, we relocated to the other side of the restaurant, still outside, but the kids somehow managed to find us and continued playing nearby. There was no way to get away from them. Eventually, we gave up and moved to a table inside. However, the food was a major disappointment. The steak was full of fat and overcooked, and the mashed potatoes were far from fresh. The only positive aspect of the whole experience was our waitress, who acknowledged the flaws with the steak and took it back. However, when she returned, she brought chicken instead, which was incredibly tough and resembled biting into rubber bands. Overall, it was a complete disaster and I have no intentions of ever returning. I can only give one star for the waitress.

input: Best shrimp and grits in NOLA! Delicious fresh juices too. This is my fiance's second time here in two years and he still thinks it's the best he's tried.
Rewrite this for me: Looking for the finest shrimp and grits in New Orleans? Look no further! Indulge in a delectable plate of our exquisite shrimp and grits, accompanied by our refreshing assortment of fresh juices. Even after his second visit in just two years, my fiance still maintains that our shrimp and grits are unparalleled in taste and quality.

input: Finally! A good tapas place in Nashville. Friendly staff, nice open kitchen, delicious food. I can't wait to go back and try more.
Rewrite this for me: I am thrilled to have found an excellent tapas spot in Nashville! The staff is incredibly friendly, the open kitchen adds a nice touch, and the food is absolutely delicious. I'm already counting down the days until I can return and explore more of their amazing options.

input: Super delish!! No frills! Just great sea food, sour dough bread was great! And I loved the 80s music playing!!
Rewrite this for me: Absolutely delicious! Simple and fantastic seafood, the sourdough bread was fantastic! The 80s music playing added to the overall enjoyment!

input: Dr. Curtis Dechant has an excellent chair-side manner, and he establishes a good rapport with his patients. The office is very comfortable, and the latest high-tech equipment makes eye appointments much easier to bear. I also appreciate their selection of eyeglass frames and the friendly staff.
Rewrite this for me: Dr. Curtis Dechant possesses an outstanding ability to make patients feel at ease, fostering a strong connection with them. The office boasts a remarkably cozy environment, while the incorporation of cutting-edge technology in eye examinations significantly alleviates any discomfort. Furthermore, I am particularly pleased with the wide variety of eyeglass frames available and the amicable staff.

input: Very cute place and good food. Pear cider beer was really good the service was really good and great ambiance and the price was very reasonable
Rewrite this for me: The place was incredibly adorable, with delicious food to match. The pear cider beer was exceptional and the service provided was top-notch. The ambiance was delightful, and all of these fantastic experiences came at a very reasonable price.

input:
I really enjoy this little restaurant full of goodness. Primarily a dessert place, Seasons also serves up some wonderful food dishes which are largely modernized updates on traditional classics. 

I always enjoy the shaved ice when I come here. The kind Seasons offers is a different type of dessert that I haven't seen anywhere else. The variety of boba tea that they have is also very 
good. Among my favorite shaved ice are the hula and the koko loco. If you want half and half flavors of shaved ice in your cup there is an additional $1.50 charge for a large size. There are pre-designed concoctions or you could create your own configurations of toppings and flavors. The pre designed concoctions are a better deal.

Seasons is situated on the end of a strip mall (across from a large shopping plaza with Regal Cinemas and Marshalls) with plenty of parking. The store itself is clean, bright, and modern and is kid-friendly as there are high hairs available for use. 

The service has always been friendly, fast, and efficient. Seasons employs an order at the counter, take number, and food is borough out to you when ready model. 

I can't comment on the food exactly but my boyfriend loves the quail and our friends enjoy the chicken wings which Boon touts as "the best food item" there. The quail is small and very flavorful and the wings are a good size and seasoned with five spice which was enjoyed by all. 

I look forward to many more visits with friends at this location. Check Seasons out and enjoy!
Rewrite this for me:
I really love this charming little restaurant that offers a delightful mix of desserts and tasty food dishes. While it specializes in desserts, Seasons also presents modern twists on traditional favorites.

Whenever I visit, I always indulge in the shaved ice, which is a unique dessert unlike anything I've encountered elsewhere. The selection of boba tea at Seasons is also excellent. Among my personal favorites are the hula and the koko loco shaved ice options. If you desire a combination of flavors in your shaved ice cup, opting for a large size incurs an additional $1.50 charge. You have the choice of selecting from pre-designed concoctions or creating your own custom toppings and flavors. The pre-designed options offer greater value.

Situated at the end of a strip mall, Seasons provides ample parking and is conveniently located across from a large shopping plaza featuring Regal Cinemas and Marshalls. The restaurant itself is clean, bright, and modern, making it a great place for families as it offers high chairs for children.

The service at Seasons has consistently been friendly, speedy, and efficient. The ordering process involves placing your order at the counter, receiving a number, and then having the food brought to your table when ready.

Although I have not personally tried all the food items, my boyfriend highly recommends the quail, and our friends thoroughly enjoy the chicken wings, which Boon, the owner, proudly describes as the best item on the menu. The quail is small but bursting with flavor, and the wings are nicely sized and seasoned with a delicious five-spice blend that everyone enjoyed.

I eagerly anticipate many more enjoyable visits with friends at this location. I encourage you to check out Seasons and savor the experience!

input: Overpriced for what you get. I think this is a cute spot to meet up with a friend, but that's about it. I prefer my own homemade coffee to be honest. Adorable concept, just could use some improvement to products offered and prices.
Rewrite this for me: The place is not worth the high prices considering what you receive. It's a nice place to catch up with a friend, but that's pretty much it. To be honest, I prefer the coffee I make at home. The concept is really cute, but they should work on enhancing their product offerings and adjusting the prices.

input: This place was absolutely awesome. 75 cent oysters. After 2 dozen I moved to the excellent cheesy grits. Great place to eat. Even better during happy hour.
Rewrite this for me: I had an incredible experience at this place. The oysters were priced at just 75 cents each, and I couldn't resist devouring two dozen of them. After that, I indulged in the amazing cheesy grits they offered. It truly is a fantastic place to dine, especially during their happy hour.

input: Love it!! I go to this place whenever I am in town and have NEVER been disappointed. The food is organic, fresh and delicious. I love that they buy from local farmers and fishermen. They also grow a lot of their own veggies! You can't get much fresher than that. There's lots of variety so I haven't even come close to trying everything. My favorite breakfast item is Carly's breakfast. Avocado on sourdough toast with a fried egg and sweet potatoes. Sooo good! Highly recommend this place!
Rewrite this for me: I absolutely adore this place! Whenever I am in town, I make sure to visit and I have never once been let down. The food here is not only organic, but also incredibly fresh and scrumptious. I am particularly fond of the fact that they source their ingredients from local farmers and fishermen. Additionally, they take pride in growing many of their own vegetables, ensuring an unparalleled level of freshness. The menu offers a wide range of options, making it impossible for me to even come close to trying everything. However, if I had to pick a favorite breakfast item, it would be Carly's breakfast. It consists of avocado on sourdough toast, topped with a fried egg and accompanied by sweet potatoes. I must say, it is absolutely delightful! Without hesitation, I highly recommend this place to everyone!

input: The burgers were very good very flavorful. I had the El Mariachi. As with what other reviewers have said the portion is not big. But I believe it makes up in flavor. I also have salted caramel ice cream it was very good homemade style. I do recommend the rooster sauce.
Rewrite this for me: The burgers at this place were incredibly delicious and packed with flavor. I personally tried the El Mariachi burger and, like many other reviewers, found the portions to be on the smaller side. However, the outstanding taste more than makes up for it. As for dessert, I indulged in the salted caramel ice cream, which was superbly prepared and reminiscent of homemade goodness. I highly recommend trying the rooster sauce as well.

input: Just had a late dinner there on a Sunday night and was really surprised at how good the sushi was and how low my ticket was. I had a plate full of sushi and it cost me $13.00. The staff seems to be having a good time too. Very friendly place. I really enjoyed it and will be back soon!
Rewrite this for me: I recently had a delightful experience dining at a restaurant on a Sunday evening. I was pleasantly surprised by the excellent quality of the sushi served and the remarkably affordable price of my meal. For just $13.00, I enjoyed a generous plate filled with delectable sushi. Moreover, the staff appeared to be genuinely enjoying themselves, creating a friendly and welcoming atmosphere. I thoroughly enjoyed my experience and am already looking forward to my next visit.

input:
I had to write an order after coming here a couple of times because this place is just terrible. I tried their hoagies and they are so greasy i got nauseous after eating them... Then yesterday i accidently ordered from here instead of angelinos and i got the buffalo chicken sandwhich and it was just covered in blu cheese and greasy sauce it was so Disgusting.  All their food is terribly greasy and over seasoned its too much.. Back off on it a little and use freasher ingredients it will be much better!

Ill also add that their desserts suck, taste bland and a waste of money. Their sodas are usually expired and flat. I hate everything about this place!
Rewrite this for me: After visiting this establishment multiple times, I was compelled to leave a negative review due to the unsatisfactory experience. The hoagies I tried were exceptionally greasy, to the point where I felt nauseous after consuming them. Furthermore, on a recent occasion, I mistakenly ordered the buffalo chicken sandwich instead of my usual choice from Angelinos. To my dismay, the sandwich was drenched in an excessive amount of blue cheese and greasy sauce, resulting in a disgustingly unappetizing meal. It seems that all of their food suffers from being overly greasy and heavily seasoned, an imbalance that is simply too overwhelming. Perhaps using fresher ingredients and toning down the seasoning would greatly improve the overall quality. I must also mention that their desserts lack flavor and are not worth the expense. Additionally, their sodas are usually expired and disappointingly flat. Overall, I am thoroughly dissatisfied with every aspect of this establishment.

input: Paid for non-smoking room but there was a smell and ashtrays in the room. Since all we were doing was sleeping there we didn't say anything. Shower was crazy slow to drain. Pillows were so lumpy that I woke up with a migraine. Room was clean and staff was nice. Free wifi but wouldn't connect.
Rewrite this for me: Despite paying for a non-smoking room, we were disappointed to find a noticeable smell and ashtrays in the room. Since our stay only involved sleeping, we chose not to complain. Additionally, the shower had an incredibly slow drainage system, causing inconvenience. The pillows provided were uncomfortably lumpy, resulting in waking up with a migraine. On the positive side, the room was clean and the staff was friendly. Although free wifi was available, we unfortunately couldn't establish a connection.

input: Maybe caught the staff on a bad day, but the people in the pharmacy were not friendly. Was told my prescription be ready in 15, when i showed up 20 minutes later they said it would be ready in a half hour. If your in a hurry dont bother filling up your prescription here. Might as well go next door to Walmart!
Rewrite this for me: It's possible that I caught the staff on a rough day, but the individuals working at the pharmacy were not particularly friendly. I was initially informed that my prescription would be ready in 15 minutes; however, when I arrived 20 minutes later, they informed me that it would actually take half an hour. If you're in a rush, it's advisable to avoid getting your prescription filled here. It would be more convenient to go to Walmart next door instead.

input:
I loves me some seitan, and that's why I keep going to El Camino. The seitan wings & seitan nachos are so good! Unfortunately, the service is not. It can be extremely slow. On one occasion it took them so long to get my seitan nachos out to me that they had to give them to me on the house. All of my friends were done eating and ready to leave and I was JUST getting my food! 

As for the rest of the food at El Camino, the only other thing I've tried would be the fried pickles. I have to say, I was not impressed. I love both pickles and fried things but these were not good. The coating was too grainy and I just didn't like the taste. 

The seitan is so good that it keeps me coming back. And the margaritas are pretty good too.
Rewrite this for me:
I really enjoy the seitan dishes at El Camino, which is why I continue to frequent the restaurant. Their seitan wings and seitan nachos are absolutely delicious! However, the service at El Camino leaves much to be desired. It tends to be incredibly slow, and on one occasion, it took an exorbitant amount of time for them to bring out my seitan nachos. To make up for the wait, they ended up giving them to me for free. It was quite frustrating as all of my friends had already finished their meals and were ready to leave by the time I received my food.

Regarding the other menu items at El Camino, the only other thing I've tried are the fried pickles. To be honest, they didn't impress me. I generally love both pickles and fried foods, but these particular pickles were disappointing. The coating had a grainy texture and the overall taste didn't suit my preferences.

Nevertheless, the exceptional quality of the seitan keeps me coming back to El Camino. Additionally, I must mention that their margaritas are pretty good too.
