input:
After a long hiatus from reviewing I have awaken from my 6 mouth yelp hibernation and my tummies a grumbles with an insatiable hunger for the cacophonous symphony of flavor that is Indian food. Like an all too familiar pattern, I go back to Mohammad Butt, my main man for marsala.
But whats this? 
There are whispers that he no longer cooks for "Best Taste of Asia," that he is gone, never to return; some sort of falling out.

No.
No, it can't be! 
I need to score - one .. final .. hit..

Life ceases to have meaning, existential murmurings dog the mind. Who am I?
Why am I here?
What is Cheeze Wiz?
Its done, over, a round falls into the chamber and just as I prepare to end it all and pull the trigger- steps in ZAIKA.

Zaika - meaning the art of taste -  stays to to its name. This is a place where the Paneer (cheese) is made fresh in house, resulting in a cheese that's silky in texture. Especially when in contrast to the prepackaged rubbery bone-white LEGO blocks most small Indo-Pak places purchase from Indian Grocers in attempts to reduce prep-times. While at Zaika such shortcuts are not taken,  the Chef takes the extra steps needed to ensure a dish comes together as a whole. For example, the Chicken Makhani uses Smokey Tandoori Chicken, which I have never seen done before but it certainly aids the chicken to cut though the rich buttery tomato sauce and elevates the dish as a whole. Even entrées like Dall Fray or  Palak Paneer  have so much flavor that they will leave you not missing animal protein in the least should you choose to go the vegetarian route. 

Zaika 's appetizers, like the Veggie Samosa and Aloo Tikki, (spiced potato patties) are generally large, peppery and well spiced - the latter of which remind me of something my own mother would make. Though I must warn others to avoid the items that occasionally pop-up as specials like the potato stuffed chili peppers, unless they have a iron stomach or are a gluten for punishment. These peppers are spicy, not deveined or even seeded. Further, I find the fish pakora to be far too fishy.
 
I've become rather taken by Zaikia. Even the simply things such as the naan are good there. Just right in elasticity, the bread does not have too much give and yet isn't too soft. It's nothing elaborate, just properly risen with a light texture and  no egg or yeast flavor. The only complaint being that it lacked that signature faint sweetness naan has. But hey, I use it mostly for mopping up the other good stuff on the plate anyway and the sweetness gets lost in the mix, so I don't mind at all.

The menu has nearly 120 different items, all numbered to order by, making take-out phone orders convenient and should eliminate any fears anyone should have of a language barrier problem. Furthermore, it has short descriptions of each dish - something all ethnic places like this should have.
Though some items like Lassie (a frothy yogurt drink) do not appear on the menu, that too is offered - both a salty and sweet mango verities. 
The head chef speaks English quite well and should be easy to deal with should you want to inquire more or want to setup large orders.

I have already noticed parties negotiating catering for Ramadan as I anxiously awaited my own order.

The bottom line here is this, Mohammad Butt has expanded on the menu he once created for "Best taste of Asia," and taken an all HALAL meat approach. 

Only good things can come of this, only good things.

P.S.
ZAIKA is right behind Nifty Fifties on Grant Ave., so you are all set for dessert should you want a milkshake. 
However, I would suggest getting the Ras Malai if available. These riccotta cheese dumplings flouting in soaked in sweetened, thickened milk are delicately flavored with cardamom, a very some amount of rose water and then garnished with pistachios. They are ungodly good.
Rewrite this for me:
After a lengthy break from reviewing, I have finally emerged from my six-month Yelp hiatus. My craving for the delectable cacophony of Indian flavors has awakened, and I find myself returning to my go-to spot for marsala: Mohammad Butt at "Best Taste of Asia."

However, I am met with shocking news. Rumors circulate that Mohammad is no longer cooking at "Best Taste of Asia." It seems there has been some kind of falling out, and he will never return.

No, this can't be true! I need one last taste, one final experience.

Existential questions plague my mind as life loses its meaning. Who am I? Why am I here? What is Cheeze Wiz? As despair sets in, I reach a breaking point. Just as I am about to give up and end it all, Zaika comes to my rescue.

True to its name, Zaika, which means "the art of taste," lives up to its reputation. Here, they make fresh Paneer (cheese) in-house, resulting in a silky texture that surpasses the rubbery, prepackaged blocks commonly found in small Indo-Pak establishments. Zaika does not take shortcuts; the chef goes the extra mile to ensure every dish is executed perfectly. For instance, their Chicken Makhani incorporates Smokey Tandoori Chicken, a unique twist that cuts through the rich, buttery tomato sauce and enhances the dish as a whole. Even vegetarian options like Dall Fray and Palak Paneer are bursting with so much flavor that you won't miss meat at all.

Zaika's appetizers, such as the Veggie Samosa and Aloo Tikki (spiced potato patties), are generously sized, peppery, and well-spiced. The Aloo Tikki reminds me of my mother's cooking. However, I must advise against trying the occasional specials like the potato stuffed chili peppers unless you have an iron stomach or enjoy punishment. These peppers are incredibly spicy, with intact veins and seeds. Furthermore, the fish pakora is too strongly fishy in taste.

I have developed a fondness for Zaika. Even their simple naan bread is excellent. It strikes the right balance between elasticity and softness, perfectly risen with no detectable egg or yeast flavor. The only minor complaint is that it lacks the slight sweetness that naan usually has. Regardless, I mainly use it to soak up the other delightful flavors on my plate, so the sweetness is not a big concern.

With nearly 120 different items on the menu, all conveniently numbered for phone orders, Zaika makes take-out a breeze and eliminates any language barrier concerns. Each dish comes with a short description, a thoughtful touch that all ethnic restaurants should implement. Although some items like Lassie (a frothy yogurt drink) may not appear on the menu, they are offered, including both salty and sweet mango varieties. The head chef speaks English fluently and is easy to communicate with, whether you have inquiries or need assistance with large orders.

While eagerly awaiting my own order, I have already observed other customers arranging catering for Ramadan festivities at Zaika.

In conclusion, Mohammad Butt has expanded his menu from the days of "Best Taste of Asia" and now focuses exclusively on HALAL meat. This can only lead to good things, only good things.

P.S. Zaika is conveniently located right behind Nifty Fifties on Grant Ave., so you can satisfy your dessert cravings with a milkshake afterward. However, if available, I highly recommend trying the Ras Malai. These ricotta cheese dumplings soaked in sweetened, thickened milk are delicately flavored with cardamom and a hint of rose water, then garnished with pistachios. They are unbelievably delicious.

input:
My boyfriend and I both decided to try Jesse's for the first time after we'd both grown up in the Brandon area and neither of us had ever been, and really hadn't heard much about the restaurant. 

We dined on a Saturday night and even though the parking lot and restaurant was packed, we were sat right away at a 2-top next to a window facing SR-60. 

Our server, Nikki, greeted us in a reasonable amount of time. We ordered our beverages and she brought them shortly after that. Something I did not like was there was not a drink menu on the table, but Nikki was able to tell us what beers were on draft and non-alcoholic drinks. She took our appetizer and entree order all at once. 

We ordered crab stuffed mushrooms and a French onion soup to share. These items came out together. The crab stuffed mushroom was basically a giant thing of crab stuffing on a TINY mushroom, which was almost laughable, but had a good flavor nonetheless. The French onion soup had a great flavor and wasn't scalding hot, which was super nice to eat right away. 

After our appetizer came out and we finished it, our Caesar salads came out as well as a loaf of bread and some butter. This was also really great pacing of our meal! Nikki never let empty plates sit on our table, was very attentive, and always made sure we had drinks in front of us. The Caesar salads were good. I gave the bread two chances... once dipped in the French onion soup and once just with butter on it... the bread could have definitely been better - it just didn't have a good flavor to it. 

I ordered the 6 oz filet and he ordered the 16 oz Delmonico - both cooked medium rare. The steaks are served with sautéed mushrooms, your choice of side, and a salad or soup of the day, which isn't mentioned anywhere on the menu. I got broccoli as my side and my boyfriend got a sweet potato with all the fixings. I saw three tables sat after us receive their entrees before us - I don't know if it was a kitchen issue or something else, but we were sat at least five minutes before each of those tables - I tried to make sense of the delay, but it honestly wasn't a big deal to me. Our steaks came out on hot metal plates that were inserted into a cooler outer shell. My filet was nice and thick and cooked perfectly and the broccoli was steamed very tenderly, but there were not enough sautéed mushrooms on the plate, in my opinion. If I had known it would have been like five mushrooms with the steak, I totally would have gotten them as a side. My boyfriend's steak was cooked perfectly as well, but being on the hot metal dish led the steak to cook more at the table, which he wasn't particularly pleased with. He enjoyed his sweet potato with butter, but it didn't come out with cinnamon on it like he requested. 

Anyway, I am sure we will return! Our server, Nikki, was fabulous. She was extremely attentive, had a great attitude, and was knowledgeable!

input:

APPETIZERS:
I ordered the BBQ Oysters and..wow.. fucking wow...1st of all the oysters not in their shells. Instead they placed in a soup cup filled with  "BBQ sauce" that tasted like cheap Ketchup and Chef Boyarde! Disgusting! The oysters themselves were gooey.

Instead, they were placed in a soup cup filled with a so-called "BBQ sauce" that tasted like cheap Ketchup mixed with Chef Boyardee. It was truly disgusting to say the least. On top of that, the oysters themselves were unpleasantly gooey.

As for the garlic bread, it was absolutely dreadful. The flavor resembled that of stale frozen garlic bread. Adding insult to injury, when the appetizers arrived, they were cold and it seemed as though they had been microwaved and left out. It was definitely not appetizing.

In addition, I also ordered the Chicken wings, which turned out to be undercooked, cold, and accompanied by a distasteful sauce.

To make matters worse, the other members of our group ordered entrees and they all voiced their dissatisfaction, stating, "This is awful!"

Despite these flaws, it is important to note that the service was exceptional. The servers were all very kind, polite, and attentive. The restaurant itself was clean and had nice tables, creating a pleasant ambiance.

input:
Ick.  That sums up my experience at Dinardo's in one "word."  Dinardo's gave me that "Ick" vibe the minute I set my foot in the door. THough we were greeted by a very friendly hostess, the place looked like a run down diner on the interior--and it wasn't very clean or charming.  This would have been fine because a lot of times the "run down" places have the best "authentic food," but this was not the case at Dinardo's.  At Dinardo's you do not get what you pay for as the prices are rather high and the food quality is rather low.    Our server hated his life and made snarky, mean comments throughout our time there which, though entertaining, was kind of unwelcome and unpleasant.  My friend had the mussels which were puny and in an unimpressive sauce--unimpressive being the general adjective I would use to describe any given dish my party ordered.  I had a soup which was extremely salty and bland beyond that and the broiled flounder and "seafood imperial" dishes were OK at best. 

I'd say if you're looking for good seafood you'd be better off at any BYOB; little fish, audrey claire, ANYWHERE but Dinardo's.  I don't understand how this place is still in business, to be honest.
Rewrite this for me:
My experience at Dinardo's can be summed up in one word: Ick. The moment I stepped foot into the restaurant, I was hit with an undesirable vibe. While the hostess was friendly, the interior looked like a rundown diner and lacked cleanliness and charm. Normally, I wouldn't mind the run-down atmosphere if it meant delicious and authentic food, but unfortunately, that was not the case at Dinardo's.

The prices were high, yet the quality of the food was disappointingly low. To make matters worse, our server seemed to despise his job and constantly made snarky and mean comments throughout our entire dining experience. Although somewhat entertaining, these remarks were unwelcome and unpleasant. One of my friends ordered the mussels, which turned out to be small and served in an unimpressive sauce. Overall, every dish we ordered was unimpressive and lacking flavor.

If you're craving good seafood, I highly recommend visiting a BYOB like Little Fish or Audrey Claire. Anywhere but Dinardo's, really. To be honest, I'm surprised this place is still in business.

input:
Don't judge a book by it's cover.  Looked like a any similar bar food type chain like Friday's, Bennigan's, or Ruby Tuesdays... JB Dawson's is far better.
Awesome experience from the second we stepped in, hostess greeted us with a smile and time to table waiting expectation.  We were promptly seated, and tended to right away with a smile and good attitude by a server, Nancy, who helped us with a beverage and app order.  

For our app we shared the twisted shrimp as it was Twisted Tuesday.  Nancy told us this dish far surpassed Bone Fish's Bang Bang Shrimp, to our surprise, it clearly did.  Our beverage and app shortly followed. 

Shortly there after another server stopped by, Kyle, who was our designated server.  Boy, smile, great greeting, great attitude, engaging.  We talked a bit, figured our way through the menu and placed our order.

For our dishes, my wife selected the Four Cheese Mac & Cheese side -- Sharp Cheddar, Pepperjack, Mozzarella & Reggiano dusted with bread crumbs with cornbread as she had large lunch.  Very good.  Unexpected, light, not overly creamy, not burnt, just right.  And the corn bread with maple butter..... ahhhhhh that was really nice.

 I ordered the fish tacos-- 3 Flour tortillas, seasoned tilapia, chimichurri sauce, mango cilantro salsa & a lime cream drizzle.  Passed on starch sides and had their asparagus that was cooked to perfection.  To my surprise the they were filling, nice size portion (see photo)  not a two bite app.  Very moist and super fresh fish.

Great first experience all around expect one key aspect.  Their so called craft beer menu was really limited and did not contain a variety of types; focused more on IPAs.  Limited thinking for the bar manager I must say.  Kyle our waiter also bar-tends.  We got to talking and he offered with no questions to swap out my beer for another option --- Stoudts Scarlet, which is a reddish beer.  For my beer palette it was better then the others limited options had a nice taste at the swallow then waned off.   Kyle informed us that they buy for all 4 restaurants and try to find a middling that works across the 4 guest demographics.  Not a great decision honestly.  There are so many great craft brewers in the Bucks County region and even Bristol area that should be showed cased and tested through.  For me a bad or poor beer selection stunts the overall experience.

We'll be back but I may need to sneak in my own beer selections from my craft collection.
Rewrite this for me:
Do not judge a book by its cover. JB Dawson's may look like any other generic bar food chain such as Friday's, Bennigan's, or Ruby Tuesdays, but it is actually far superior.

From the moment we walked in, our experience was amazing. The hostess greeted us warmly and gave us an accurate wait time for our table. We were seated promptly and our server, Nancy, came over with a smile and a great attitude to take our drink and appetizer order.

We decided to try the twisted shrimp, as it was Twisted Tuesday. To our surprise, Nancy informed us that it far surpassed Bone Fish's Bang Bang Shrimp, and she was right. When our drinks and appetizer arrived shortly after, we were impressed.

Shortly after that, our designated server, Kyle, came by. He had a big smile and greeted us warmly. He was engaging and helped us navigate the menu and place our order.

My wife ordered the Four Cheese Mac & Cheese as a side, which was made with Sharp Cheddar, Pepperjack, Mozzarella, and Reggiano, and dusted with bread crumbs. It also came with cornbread. It was unexpectedly light, not overly creamy, and had the perfect texture. The cornbread with maple butter was a delightful addition.

I opted for the fish tacos, which consisted of three flour tortillas filled with seasoned tilapia, chimichurri sauce, mango cilantro salsa, and a lime cream drizzle. Instead of a starch side, I had their perfectly cooked asparagus. The fish tacos were surprisingly filling and the fish was incredibly fresh and moist.

Overall, it was a great first experience, except for one key aspect. Their craft beer menu was disappointingly limited and focused mainly on IPAs. This was a letdown as I believe the bar manager could have been more creative with their selection. However, Kyle, our waiter who also bartends, offered to swap my beer for another option without hesitation. He recommended Stoudts Scarlet, a reddish beer, and it turned out to be much better than the other limited options. It had a nice taste that lingered after each sip. Kyle explained that they buy beer for all four restaurants and try to cater to a wide range of guest preferences, but I believe this decision lacks innovation. There are so many amazing craft breweries in the Bucks County region, as well as the Bristol area, that should be showcased and tested. In my opinion, a poor beer selection hinders the overall dining experience.

Despite this, we will definitely be back, although I might have to bring my own craft beer from my collection.

input:
Stopped here for lunch on the way to drop some people off at the airport. It's a bit unexpected and a tiny bit off the beaten path on a residential street just behind a business district.

I chose the vegetarian plate and a Greek salad. The salad was the absolute best I've ever had. The cheese was absolutely fresh, the vegetables were fresh and chopped just for the salad, and the dressing and seasoning was perfect. The salad was quite large on its own and could easily make a light lunch by itself.

The vegetarian plate came along with their fresh pita-like bread that is baked fresh every morning, seasoned, pan fried vegetables, rice, and a tzatziki-like sauce drizzled on top. The flavors were astounding, and despite a lack of desire to stuff myself silly, I did anyway. Plenty of food for lunch and very reasonably priced.
Rewrite this for me:
We made a stop here for lunch while en route to drop off some people at the airport. It was a pleasant surprise to find this hidden gem tucked away on a residential street, just a little off the main path behind a business district.

For my meal, I decided to go with the vegetarian plate and a Greek salad. Let me tell you, the salad was hands down the best I have ever tasted. The cheese was ridiculously fresh, the veggies were perfectly crisp, and they were all cut specifically for the salad. The dressing and seasoning were spot-on, adding to the amazing flavors. The portion size of the salad alone was quite generous and could easily pass as a satisfying light lunch on its own.

Now onto the vegetarian plate - it came accompanied by their freshly baked, pita-like bread which is made every morning. Alongside the bread were pan-fried vegetables done to perfection, a serving of rice, and a drizzle of a delicious tzatziki-like sauce on top. The combination of flavors in this dish was simply mind-blowing. Even though I didn't intend to stuff myself silly, I couldn't resist devouring every last bite. The portion of food provided for lunch was abundant, and the pricing was very reasonable.

input:
Awefull!!!! 
If I could give zero or negative stars I would!
I've never wrote a review before, but I am going out of my way to say that I had the absolute worst dining experience at the Sake House!! 
And esp families, stay clear! 
So first off, I decided to take my 15 month old son out on a sushi date. We arrive at the Sake House at 4pm. There is only one other table and they were closing out. We sit down, and I immediately ask for a simple ice water with lemon. Waiter comes back 20 minutes later (no water). I order a simple roll for my son, to get him started  and a cold Sake. I said I will wait to order mine to get him settled. Another 30 min later, still no water, no food. Waiter comes back with hot Sake, instead of cold. 20 minutes later, the roll for my son (not how I asked) finally some cold Sake, then I have to request water, and then only one cup for my son, no lemon. When I see 2 going on a third table had come in and ordered, and a "to go" order is being placed, all with food and water, I became perturbed. The waiter never came back to see what I wanted. Never came back to check on the order. Finally after  nearly 2 hours of waiting and trying to deal with my antsy son, who waited so long to be served, and seeing one chef trying to make everyone's order I decided it was time to go. Finally after waiting another 5/10 minutes I had to walk up and ask for my check , which was only a $6 drink. Which I reluctantly paid. After being in the hospitality industry for years, I know what to expect, and I know what to forgive. I also know that English being a second language must be tough...BUT since he was able to wait in other tables i know that wasn't the issue. After 2 hours of waiting, and dealing with a fussy/hungry toddler as a single mother I feel like the least they could have done is offer a free drink, to say "we understand we couldn't accommodate you, but we tried." It's principal above all else. ...I just waisted 2 hours! And had to leave and take my baby somewhere else. Time is money! And I waisted 2 hours here! 
Time that is rare and I had to plan being a busy mother.
I should have listened to the other reviews about the shitty service here. 
Don't waste your time or money!!!
Stay away! Any other place is better than here!

CURED was not only high end, but it was classic. Like The Hamptons type of classic but with a comfortable low key brunch with girlfriends mimosa type of vibe. I think it would be amazing for a bridal party with so many photo opportunities. I felt comfortable with their prices, competitive to anywhere else I've gone in Nashville worth mentioning. 

I didn't know where to park so I parked on the side in a random parking lot. Looks like there's a lot of up and coming businesses beside them under construction. So I'm assuming once those are complete, parking will be pretty straight forward? 

When my Mom & Sister come into town next I'm going to take them here & go to Local Honey for lunch since it's so close. 

Can't wait to go back. Welcome to the neighborhood!
Rewrite this for me:
I'm absolutely in love with this salon! The style is absolutely impeccable. The color scheme and decor they've chosen make it feel like you're flipping through the pages of a Restoration Hardware magazine...in the heart of France...surrounded by beautiful heirloom antiques. I didn't know what to expect when I arrived, but I was pleasantly surprised by their luxurious nail options, including brands like Chanel, that I never knew I needed in my life until I stepped foot in here.

The service was incredibly prompt, and I especially enjoyed the extended massage. And the best part? The tools she used were all brand new and sterilized. I watched her open up fresh packages, which made me feel confident about the cleanliness and safety of the salon. I don't know if all nail salons have stylish gold tips on their nail trimmer tools, but now I want them for my personal collection.

For my toes, I chose a lovely gray shade, and for my nails, I went with OPI Funny Bunny gel. So far, I'm completely loving both shades!

It's so refreshing to see a high-end nail salon finally arrive in Nashville. I've been to others in town that claim to be upscale, but they end up feeling like a trendy club on the Vegas strip, with loud music and excessive glitter, just waiting for a Justin Bieber song to come on. CURED, on the other hand, is not only high-end but also exudes a timeless elegance. It reminds me of the classic charm you'd find in The Hamptons, but with a relaxed, comfortable vibe perfect for a brunch with girlfriends, sipping mimosas. I can imagine it being a fantastic spot for a bridal party, offering numerous photo opportunities. And their prices are quite reasonable, comparable to other high-quality nail salons in Nashville.

I wasn't sure where to park, so I ended up parking on the side in a random parking lot. It seems like there are many up-and-coming businesses being constructed nearby. I assume once those are completed, parking will be much more straightforward.

When my mom and sister visit next, I'm definitely taking them here, and we'll grab lunch at Local Honey since it's conveniently close.

I can't wait to return. Welcome to the neighborhood!

input: This has fast become one of my favorite New Orleans gems! Enter over at the bridge on Peters near Elysian Fields or a little way up on Piety, either way, if you like breezes and city views, your efforts will be rewarded. The path stretches about a 1.25 miles from close to Elysian Fields over to the area near the old Navy installation. Along the way are various art installations, a dog park, and a wonderful walk along the mighty Mississippi River. If you time it just right, you might catch one of the spectacular sunsets. A beautiful way to end any day in NOLA!
Rewrite this for me: This has quickly become one of my favorite hidden treasures in New Orleans! You can enter from the bridge on Peters near Elysian Fields or a bit further up on Piety. The pathway extends for approximately 1.25 miles, starting near Elysian Fields and leading towards the old Navy installation area. Throughout your journey, you'll come across various captivating art installations, a dog park, and a delightful stroll along the majestic Mississippi River. If you time it just perfectly, you might even witness one of the most awe-inspiring sunsets. It's a truly enchanting way to conclude any day spent in the wonderful city of NOLA!

input:
4-5 stars, this is just after one visit so far, worth a try if you're a thai fan. I liked the food, but you always have to have the first visit to see "how they do things" and figure out what your preferences will need to be.

I did use their living social deal so I brought my dad in when he came in from out of town to try it out with me. I like the set up, the quaint house is cute (and well, quaint), but I can see how it wouldn't be ideal it if was jam packed. I imagine you could potentially do family style for some of the pub height tabletops. I did call ahead to make sure that I didn't need to print out the coupon and it could be used from my ipod and to make sure they were open, as the website said to just double check.

We started with shrimp spring rolls, probably the best I've had, the ingredients seemed fresher, and crispier. No shredded lettuce here. Simple and loosely wrapped, but you could taste the individual components. The peanut sauce was tasty too, though they don't have sirracha (spelling?) to add to it, just dried pepper flakes. 

We then got the tom yum (gai?) with shrimp. I know it is hot (because of the name, duh), I usually prefer it a little less spicy (I am white), though I still got a good sour flavor (for instance at Thai chili it's too hot for me, I don't taste any sour). I usually get my tom yum without meat or seafood because I feel the meat gets dried out, but the server assured me the shrimp wouldn't be overcooked, and they weren't. I think they are making sure to use fresh ingredients, but I do prefer straw mushrooms (I think they are usually canned) over the button mushrooms they used. Next time I am probably going to try out a veggie version (i love the soup with the cabbage, and broccoli). The owner did tell me they are trying to be authentic and so maybe button mushrooms and less veggies is more authentic?

We then got shrimp pad thai and chicken pad keo mao (drunken noodle) minus the red pepper. Both were tasty, the portions were probably a little less than other places in Reno (not sure if just lunch sized portion now that I think about it).

Like Ernie said, the pad thai noodles were a little soft, overdone, and its not the 'orange-y' sauce like other pad thai's, but there was still flavor there. The shrimp were also tasty in this dish. The drunken noodles was done exactly how I like them, lots of baby corns and the noodles covered in the sauce and of course spicy. 

My dad and I talked outside for a while and the husband did come out and talk with me about the food, and asked if I was happy (we were outside a while). I hope the living social deals bring in some business, and I do plan on coming back, it is just hard because I don't live in the area. I also asked about the cooking classes (they are a steal at $65), and on facebook it said they are looking to improve and give some focus to that side of the business. The owner did say that they use just a regular kitchen so no woks or anything like that (meaning what they teach us can actually be done at home), I wonder if that is why the pad thai noodles are that way? Regardless, they seem to pride themselves on authentic and quality food and service.

I did include pictures. Oh I did try a thai iced tea for the first time too, pretty tasty, reminded me of chai tea. 

I didn't get to see the bill closely, but it was $24 and some change after the living social deal (takes $20 off), I didn't think that was too bad for 2 for lunch (the total cost), with an appetizer and soup and a drink.
Rewrite this for me:
I would give this place a rating of 4-5 stars. Although this review is based on just one visit, I believe it's worth a try if you enjoy Thai food. The food was delicious, but like with any new place, the first visit is important to understand their style and your own preferences.

I used a Living Social deal to bring my dad along when he visited from out of town. The restaurant is set up in a quaint house, which adds to its charm, but it might not be ideal if it gets too crowded. However, I think some of the pub height tabletops could accommodate family-style dining. I made sure to call ahead and confirm that I didn't need to print out the coupon and that they were open since the website advised double-checking.

We started with the shrimp spring rolls, which were probably the best I've had. The ingredients tasted fresher and crunchier, and they didn't overload them with shredded lettuce. They were simply and loosely wrapped, allowing the individual flavors to shine. Although they didn't have Sriracha sauce, the peanut sauce was tasty, and they provided dried pepper flakes instead.

Next, we ordered the tom yum soup with shrimp. As expected, it was hot (as indicated by the name), and while I usually prefer it slightly less spicy, I still enjoyed the tangy flavor. Unlike at Thai Chili, where it's too spicy for me to notice any sourness, this tom yum had a good balance. Usually, I skip the meat or seafood in tom yum soup because I find them dry, but the server assured me that the shrimp wouldn't be overcooked, and they weren't. However, I do prefer straw mushrooms (usually canned) over the button mushrooms they used. Next time, I might try the vegetarian version with cabbage and broccoli, which I love. The owner mentioned that they strive for authenticity, so perhaps using button mushrooms and fewer vegetables is considered more authentic?

For our main dishes, we had shrimp pad thai and chicken pad keo mao (drunken noodle) without red pepper. Both dishes were flavorful, although the portions were slightly smaller compared to other places in Reno. As Ernie mentioned, the pad thai noodles were a bit soft and overcooked, and it didn't have the usual orange-colored sauce, but it still had a good taste. The shrimp in this dish were also delicious. The drunken noodles, however, were exactly how I like them—lots of baby corn and noodles coated in sauce, with a satisfying spiciness.

My dad and I stayed outside to chat, and the husband eventually came out and asked if we were happy with the food (we had been outside for a while). I hope their Living Social deals attract more customers, and I do plan on returning, even though it's difficult as I don't live nearby. I also inquired about their cooking classes, which are quite reasonably priced at $65. Their Facebook page mentioned a focus on improving and expanding that side of the business. The owner mentioned that they use a regular kitchen, which allows us to replicate their dishes at home. I wonder if that's the reason behind the texture of the pad thai noodles. Regardless, they take pride in offering authentic and high-quality food and service.

I included some pictures with my review. Oh, and I also tried a Thai iced tea for the first time, and it was quite tasty, reminding me of chai tea.

I didn't examine the bill closely, but with the Living Social deal (which took $20 off), the total came to $24 and some change. Considering we had an appetizer, soup, main dishes, and a drink for both of us, I thought it was a reasonable price for lunch.

input:

They've got lululemon, Jacob, Danier, Gap, Club Monaco, American Eagle, and a variety of other shops that work for me, and it's never so busy you have to brush past people in the halls. 

I sometimes just go for the food -they've got New York Fries, Orange Julius, Poppin' pop corn, Booster Juice, Extreme Pita, Bad Ass Jack's and other choices. 

The food court has a ton of seating. It's never completely full. There's a Zellers and a dollar store and a Sears. I just wish they had a Bay and a movie theatre to round it out a bit. Otherwise, Kingsway is as good a mall as I need.

Plus, it's never too congested, so there's no need to squeeze past people in the hallways.

Sometimes, I visit Kingsway solely for the food options available - they have enticing choices like New York Fries, Orange Julius, Poppin' popcorn, Booster Juice, Extreme Pita, Bad Ass Jack's, and more. The food court provides ample seating, and it's rarely completely occupied. While I do wish they had a Bay and a movie theatre to complement the mall, overall, Kingsway serves my shopping needs satisfactorily.

input:

Sorry to say this curry was not great, the sauce was very heavy on the salt and tomato and the goat was tough as an old boot, the naan bread was below mediocre. Only nice thing was the rice.  Very Very dissapointed

input:
Yes, it's a little pricey, but it was darned near worth it. 
It certainly didn't seem a priority to get us our menus, but once they did, the service was pretty on point. The bread was good. I ordered a chopped salad and a crab cake, and the hub got a crab cake sandwich with fries. We had water to drink, no appetizers-walked out for $45 with tip. The food came quickly.  My food was great-and I'm no salad eater. The crab cake was quality, fries were good. 
Another drawback is that we had to sit in the bar area bc it was after 9. The table was the size of a chair, 3 plates were too much.

P.S. i used my bank card, and noticed that I was charged significantly more than I agreed to, so I called the restaurant. The manager said it's a banking glitch, and should correct itself before the money comes out of my account... It better.
Rewrite this for me:
Although it was a bit expensive, I must say it was almost worth the price. Initially, they seemed to have no urgency in giving us our menus, but once we finally got them, the service was quite impressive. The bread was tasty. I decided to go for a chopped salad and a crab cake, while my partner opted for a crab cake sandwich with fries. We only had water to drink and skipped appetizers, and the bill, including the tip, came out to $45. The food arrived promptly, and to my surprise, my salad was amazing, even though I'm not usually a fan. The crab cake was top-notch and the fries were delicious. 
One downside was that we had to sit in the bar area because it was past 9 PM, and the table was so small that it could only accommodate three plates. 
By the way, I paid with my bank card and later realized that I was charged much more than what was agreed upon, so I contacted the restaurant. The manager apologized and informed me that it was a banking error, assuring that it would be resolved before the transaction is finalized. I surely hope it does.

input:

I'm going to be honest. This was literally the worst sushi Ive ever had.  It was warm... WARM! (and NO! it wasn't tempura).

I also paid $3 for a side salad which was literally iceberg lettuce. 

Nope... no spring mix...no romaine...no iceberg with slivers of carrots or even purple cabbage... LITERALLY just iceberg. I was puzzled and then angry and then i had to smirk and whisper, "well played my friend... well played".

I will never be back..

Check and Mate.
Rewrite this for me:
I have to admit, I have high standards when it comes to sushi.

To be completely honest, the sushi I had today was absolutely terrible. It was actually warm, can you believe that? And no, it wasn't even tempura.

On top of that disappointment, I also paid $3 for a side salad, which turned out to be nothing more than plain iceberg lettuce.

There was no variety with spring mix or romaine lettuce, not even a touch of carrots or purple cabbage. Just plain old iceberg. I was confused at first, then frustrated, and eventually I couldn't help but smirk and whisper, "Well played, my friend, well played."

Needless to say, I will never visit that place again.

It's checkmate for them.

input: My partner and I split the vegetarian platter and left stuffed! Delicious food, very kind and attentive staff.  Will help you make decisions on ordering and certainly won't take advantage of you. Will definitely be back.
Rewrite this for me: My partner and I shared the vegetarian platter and left feeling completely satisfied! The food was incredibly delicious, and the staff was exceptionally friendly and attentive. They provided helpful suggestions for ordering and never tried to take advantage of us. We'll definitely return in the future.

input: I have never stayed at a hotel so ghetto. Sure the atmosphere is great and very classy looking. However the staff is the opposite. Rewrite this for me: I've never encountered such a run-down hotel before. Although the ambiance appears to be elegant and classy, the staff completely fails to measure up. input: I've been to this place in numerous occasions and I have never been disappointed! My friend and I are traveling to Puerto Rico and my mother in law wanted Tamales! Rewrite this for me: I have visited this place multiple times, and it has never failed to impress me! input:
Wish I had read the reviews before we stopped for dinner.  When we arrived there were only two other tables of patrons and a handful of people at the bar. Rewrite this for me:

Although our food order was taken promptly, it took a disappointing 50 minutes for it to finally reach our table. input:
i enjoyed the experience eating here and will definitely go back.

first of all, there are vegetarian options on the menu. we started with the veggie spring rolls which were hot, crisp, and delicious. my husband had the duck and rice vermicelli soup which we both agreed was great in a yummy, savory broth. i had the beef pho which i didn't care for because the meat was a bit grisly and i'm not a fan of tripe. i've not eaten a lot of pho and wasn't sure what to order, though. they offer several different beef cuts and i should have picked a different one. next time. also, the regular serving size was way more than enough. i don't think either of us could have come close to finishing the largest bowls.

the restaurant was clean and quiet with a sparse, yet very 80s decor. the server was quick and attentive.
Rewrite this for me:
I had a wonderful dining experience here and will definitely visit again. One thing I appreciate is that they have vegetarian options on their menu. To start, we ordered the veggie spring rolls which were perfectly hot, crisp, and absolutely delicious. My husband tried the duck and rice vermicelli soup, and we both agreed that it was fantastic with its flavorful and savory broth. On the other hand, I had the beef pho, but unfortunately, I didn't enjoy it as much because the meat was a bit tough and I'm not a fan of tripe. However, since I'm not very experienced with pho and wasn't sure what to order, I should have chosen a different cut of beef. But that's something I'll keep in mind for next time. Additionally, the regular serving size was incredibly generous; both of us couldn't even come close to finishing the largest bowls.

The restaurant itself was clean and had a quiet atmosphere, adorned with an interesting sparse 80s decor. Our server was quick and attentive, providing great service throughout our meal.

input:
3.5 stars.

Chickie's and Pete's is a friendly sports bar, particularly for women, and it has lots of seating for Sunday games. I appreciate the sound booth in the sky, as it means that (admittedly bad) music is played during the commercials, along with special themes for Eagles fans. And, the place seems to be smoke free.

But, I am not impressed by the famous crab fries, which are crinkled, lightly fried, and seasoned with garlic, chili pepper, and salt. Something about the congealed cheese sauce detracts from the entire experience, and I also prefer my fries to be piping hot. However, there are towers of beer available (complete with taps), which is pleasantly tacky. 

With loads of space, booming sound, cute servers, and rowdy fans, Chickie's and Pete's is a perfect place to catch a game.
Rewrite this for me:
Chickie's and Pete's, with its 3.5-star rating, is a welcoming sports bar that particularly caters to women. It offers ample seating for Sunday games and features a sound booth in the sky, providing a unique experience with music during commercials and special themes for Eagles fans. Additionally, it is worth noting that the establishment is smoke-free.

While there are many positive aspects, I must admit that I was not overly impressed with the famous crab fries. Though they are crinkled and lightly fried, seasoned with garlic, chili pepper, and salt, the presence of congealed cheese sauce detracts from the overall enjoyment. Furthermore, I personally prefer my fries to be served piping hot. On the bright side, the availability of towered beer, complete with taps, adds a delightfully tacky touch.

Overall, with its spacious layout, booming sound, attractive servers, and enthusiastic fans, Chickie's and Pete's proves to be an ideal destination for catching a game.

input: Pancake Pantry is an institution in Nashville. A place to see country stars and have a great breakfast. Pancakes are good. It's a thing to do in Nashville. Plan to stand in line and enjoy the conversation.
Rewrite this for me: Pancake Pantry is a renowned establishment in Nashville, an integral part of the city's culture. It serves as a gathering spot for both country stars and breakfast enthusiasts alike. The pancakes offered are undeniably delicious, making Pancake Pantry a must-visit destination in Nashville. Be prepared for a potential wait in line, but don't worry, as it provides an opportunity to engage in pleasant conversations.

input: I have been a loyal customer at Magasin Cafe for years, it's what made me fall in love with Vietnamese food. Since Magasin Cafe has closerd for renovations I came to Magasin Kitcheb to curb my weekly pho cravings. The food and service were good- even the chopped was seasoned better than the other location. Rewrite this for me: For years, I have remained a steadfast patron of Magasin Cafe, being deeply enamored with Vietnamese cuisine. However, since Magasin Cafe has temporarily shut down for renovations, I resorted to visiting Magasin Kitchen to satisfy my weekly pho cravings. input: I love this place...stop whenever I can; either at this location or the Philadelphia one. I could eat the cumin style lamb every day of the week. But honestly, all of their food is good. I'm definitely a fan of their rabbit appetizer. People can argue about how authentically Sichuan it is...whatever. The only place I've actually had Sichuan food taste exactly like they serve in Sichuan Province was when I went to Chengdu. This place is well worth eating at.
Rewrite this for me: I have a strong admiration for this place and make it a point to visit whenever I can, be it this particular location or the one in Philadelphia. The cumin style lamb they serve here is so incredible that I wouldn't mind devouring it every single day of the week. However, I must admit that all of their food is undeniably delicious. Personally, I am especially fond of their rabbit appetizer. Some may debate its authenticity in terms of being truly Sichuan, but honestly, it doesn't matter to me. The only other place where I experienced Sichuan cuisine that tasted exactly like what they serve in Sichuan Province was during my trip to Chengdu. Hence, I believe this place is truly worth indulging in.

input:
A quasi political rant and a store review all wrapped in one, so enjoy. 

Ever since Target hit the scene I really have to ask, "Who even goes to Kmart anymore?" I asked this to myself out loud the other day as I had to get my meds filled due to a sinus infection. No one looked at me odd, as there seemed to be several people talking to themselves. I now go here because of the stolid contractual war between Express Scripts and Walgreens. Thanks you two....idiots.....qausi-political rant over.

This store is harshly bright, rather dingy, and the selections, especially in the electronic section, are on the cheaper end.  On top of that, I've found the mainstream DVD and Blu-Ray movies are overpriced.  I laughed at the men's area, especially the young man's department, as they had a tv with music videos playing. I laughed because it just seemed a lame attempt to be cool and creating a shopping experience that you will find at a department store like Macy's or Dillard's. This is hard to create when everything is whitewashed. You will feel like you are in that August Burns Red's "Whitewashed."  The best WTF moment is discovering the opportunity to purchase Joe Boxer male thongs. Who knew that Kmart cared about male panty line?

One great tip is you can find patio furniture cheap during the off season and clearance days. I bought a great patio table for under $50. So, keep that in mind.

The extra star is for the pharmacy, as they filled my prescription out efficiently and with the greatest of ease. The hours are little later than Target.  No problems there and credit when credit is due!

The later 80s quote, "K-Mart sucks", remains as true as ever and who knows, you may even bump into someone who still dresses from that Tom Cruise era who cares about male panty line. One never knows?
Rewrite this for me:
Let me start off by saying, ever since Target came into the picture, it's hard to fathom why anyone even sets foot in Kmart anymore. I found myself pondering this question aloud when I had to pick up my medication for a sinus infection. Surprisingly, no one batted an eye, probably because there were several people talking to themselves. The reason I now frequent Kmart is due to the never-ending standoff between Express Scripts and Walgreens. Thanks a lot, you two...idiots. So that concludes my quasi-political rant.

Now, let's move on to this store itself. First of all, it's excessively bright and feels rather grimy. The selection, especially in the electronics section, is mediocre at best. And don't get me started on the outrageously high prices for mainstream DVDs and Blu-Ray movies. The men's section provided me with some comic relief, particularly with the young man's department showcasing a television blaring music videos. It just seemed like a feeble attempt to appear hip and create a shopping experience similar to Macy's or Dillard's. But honestly, everything feels so sterile and lackluster. You might even feel like you're stuck in August Burns Red's "Whitewashed" music video. And to top it all off, imagine my surprise when I stumbled upon the option to purchase Joe Boxer male thongs. Who would have thought Kmart cared about male panty lines?

Now, here's a helpful tip. If you're looking for affordable patio furniture, Kmart is the place to go during the off-season and clearance days. I managed to snag a fantastic patio table for less than $50. So keep that in mind if you're in need of outdoor furniture.

I will give an extra star solely for the pharmacy. They swiftly filled my prescription with utmost efficiency. Their operating hours are also more convenient than Target's. Credit where credit is due!

It's safe to say that the sentiment from the late 80s, "K-Mart sucks," still holds true to this day. Who knows, you might even run into someone who still dresses like they're straight out of the Tom Cruise era and genuinely cares about male panty lines. Anything is possible at Kmart, right?

input: The Tuck Special. So good I would drive all the way back out to Nashville from TX just to have it again. I can see how this place gets crowded, but if you have patience and look up the menu ahead of time, it should be manageable.
Rewrite this for me: The Tuck Special is undeniably irresistible. It's so delicious that I would willingly make the long drive back from Texas to Nashville just to savor it once more. This unique creation boasts an intriguing blend of ingredients – mouthwatering brisket, perfectly cooked eggs, and delectable pimento cheese. When these elements come together, they form an extraordinary flavor combination. Although my husband wasn't particularly fond of the BBQ sauce readily available on the table, the meat itself was quite satisfying. It's easy to understand why this place tends to get crowded, but with a little patience and a glance at the menu beforehand, the experience should be perfectly manageable.

input: The restaurant smelled like a toilet.  I couldn't stand it.  My daughter and I got the meals to go and the guy put them in the same box.  She doesn't eat fish and that is what I got. input:

input: This is a must get when you come to Reno is Yellow Subs. Ask for the sprouts on your sub and you won't regret it. It is way better then  anywhere I've ever been. input: Tina I believe was our waitress.. I'm not sure if I want to give 3 or 4 stars. Its just that the initial wait was kinda long. But it was my first time eating the food and I thought it was pretty good. I liked my side salad too!

input: Love!! Our new favorite local spot. We've gone a few times since they opened and it's always a good ambiance, and great food. The drinks are great, the salsa is super yummy, and the salads are very much entree sized. Bring your friends, sit outside, grab a margarita and enjoy!

input:
Despite it's great reviews by other Yelpers, I was not that blown away by Nippon Tei. 

My roommate and I were craving sushi and were recommended to come here by Yelp and a friend so we decided to give it a shot. 

First off, they get bonus points for serving FREE edemame as an appetizer. I usually pay $4 to $5 for it at other sushi restaurants. The mango sake drink I have was alright, but not worth the price I paid for it. 

On to the main event...SUSHI! We had the philly roll, tempura roll, tuna roll, and california roll. They were all yummy, but I would have to say I have had better. Actually, out of the hand-full of sushi restaurants I have tried, this was the worst sushi I have tried, but I cannot say the sushi was bad by any means. Don't get me wrong, it was still tasty. 

The other big thing was that the rolls were actually falling apart. I have never had this happen. Therefore, I can say that the presentation and the ability to get the sushi from the plate to my mouth without falling apart did make me unhappy. 

I am willing to come back to Nippon Tei, but I have to say I already have my other favorites. The prices were average compared to other sushi bars, so that won't really help them out either when it comes to bringing me back. We will see!
Rewrite this for me:
Despite the positive reviews from other Yelpers, Nippon Tei didn't quite live up to my expectations. My roommate and I were in the mood for sushi and decided to give it a try based on recommendations from Yelp and a friend.

To their credit, they provided complimentary edamame as an appetizer, which was a nice touch considering it's usually an additional cost at other sushi restaurants. The mango sake drink I ordered was decent, but I felt it was overpriced.

Now onto the main attraction... SUSHI! We tried the Philly roll, tempura roll, tuna roll, and California roll. While they were all tasty, I must admit I've had better. Compared to the handful of sushi restaurants I've been to, this was actually the least impressive. However, I wouldn't consider the sushi bad in any way, it just didn't blow me away.

Another issue was that the rolls were falling apart, which was something I had never experienced before. This definitely affected the overall presentation and made it challenging to enjoy the sushi without it falling apart.

I might consider revisiting Nippon Tei, but I already have other favorite sushi places that I prefer. The prices were average, so that alone won't be enough to entice me back. We'll see!

input: Went to see Star Wars Rogue One yesterday in 3D.  Buying the tickets was a breeze, and the atmosphere was inviting.  Found the comfortable seats with no problem and ordered right away before the movie began.  I ordered pretzel sticks - food was hot, prompt & delicious.  I was excited for the movie to begin.  Once the advertisements were done and the movie started, that's when I noticed something wasn't right.  The entire screen was so dark that I was not able to make out the faces of the actors on the screen.  I kept lifting up the 3D glasses to see if it made a difference - nope.  The two people seated next to me were noticing the same and complaining.  I thought that maybe this is how the movie was filmed?  Then it got worse.  Even with the 3D glasses on, the shadows in the background on the screen were double and there was no discerning most actors' faces at all.  I got up and went to the lobby and asked for the manager.  The gentleman wore a blue shirt, middle age with a beard, said that this was the 3D experience, it was a "closed-system" and there was nothing he could do.  I simply asked him to come with me into the theater to see with his own eyes how dark it was.  He would not and did not.  I suspect this wasn't the first time he's heard this from a customer.  I've seen normal movies at this location before, but this was my first, and last experience with their 3D in room #1.
Rewrite this for me: Yesterday, I went to watch Star Wars Rogue One in 3D and the ticket purchasing process was easy. The overall atmosphere of the theater was inviting, and I easily found comfortable seats. Before the movie started, I swiftly placed an order for some pretzel sticks, which turned out to be delicious and arrived promptly. I was eagerly anticipating the start of the movie, but unfortunately, my excitement soon waned. As soon as the advertisements ended and the movie began, it became apparent that something was amiss. The screen was exceptionally dark, to the extent that I couldn't discern the actors' faces. Despite repeatedly lifting my 3D glasses, the situation didn't improve. The people seated beside me were experiencing the same issue and expressing their dissatisfaction. I wondered if this was intentional, perhaps a stylistic choice made during filming. However, the situation worsened when even with the 3D glasses on, the background shadows appeared doubled, making it impossible to recognize most actors' faces. Frustrated, I decided to go to the lobby and speak to the manager. The manager, a middle-aged gentleman with a beard and wearing a blue shirt, explained that this was part of the "closed-system" 3D experience and that there was nothing he could do to rectify the situation. I requested for him to accompany me into the theater to witness the darkness firsthand, but he declined my invitation. This led me to believe that he had encountered similar complaints in the past. While I have watched regular movies at this theater in the past without any issues, this incident has left me with no desire to repeat the 3D experience in room #1.

input: Overpriced for average food served warm (not hot) by servers who had trouble saying the names of the dishes and seemed in a rush to give us our bill when the place was more than half empty (on a Saturday night). When one of the servers came over to check on the $23 pork chop (which was not listed in the menu - $18 price was), my spouse commented there was a lot of fat....she seemed baffled by his comment, then walked away! The "ropa vieja" dish was good, but overpriced for being served in moderate portion. The menu prices did not reflect the ambiance (random plastic container boxes placed on a nearby table nor the sagging knitted item hanging over our table - it looks like there should've been a lamp in it).
Rewrite this for me: The food at this restaurant is average and served warm, not hot. The servers had trouble pronouncing the names of the dishes and seemed in a hurry to bring us the bill, even though the restaurant was mostly empty on a Saturday night. We were surprised to find that the $23 pork chop was not listed on the menu, which only showed an $18 price. When my spouse commented on the amount of fat in the pork chop, the server seemed confused and walked away. The "ropa vieja" dish was tasty, but the portion was small considering the high price. The prices on the menu did not match the overall ambiance of the restaurant, with random plastic containers on a nearby table and a sagging knitted item hanging over our table where a lamp should have been.

input: Should have listened to other reviews--we were kind of disappointed.  The layout of the restaurant is interesting in that it's made to look sort of like the inside of a chicken coop (made for people).  However, the food was overpriced and underwhelming.  We ate from the Sunday brunch menu--only decent value on the menu is the chicken strips and fries.  My wife ordered the seasonal salad, which was comically small and was way short on the actual lettuce (and not cheap either).  Chicken was good, but nothing better than Raising Canes in my opinion.  Service and food seemed on the slow side, especially with the small crowd.
Rewrite this for me: Had we heeded the other reviews, our disappointment could have been avoided. The restaurant's unique layout resembling a chicken coop for humans is intriguing. Nevertheless, the food was both expensive and underwhelming. Opting for the Sunday brunch menu, the only worthwhile option was the chicken strips and fries in terms of value. My wife decided on the seasonal salad, which was laughably minuscule and lacked an adequate amount of lettuce, despite its high price. The chicken was satisfactory but failed to surpass the quality offered at Raising Canes, in my personal opinion. The service and food seemed rather slow, particularly considering the small number of customers.

input: Wow. I am not a vegetarian, nor am I a health-food nut (except for my random "diet" binges) but this place is awesome. input:

input: Perfect place for a date night. The sweet potato nachos and the "breakfast" we're to die for! Really everything we tried was delicious...I can't wait to go back again.

input: We had dinner at Convivio right after it opened and we will definitely go back. Rewrite this for me: After attending Convivio for dinner shortly after its opening, we were thoroughly impressed and will undoubtedly return. In particular, I indulged in the tortelloni pansotti, which I can confidently say was the most exquisite pasta I've ever tasted. Undoubtedly, we will become regular patrons of Convivio.

input: After driving pass all the seafood restaurants around Clearwater Beach, I knew wanted seafood right there and then. I wasn't familiar with the area and did not do any yelping before hand, so was pretty hesitant to just blindly pick a restaurant.  Finally, after a long day at the beach, we made a quick walk across the street to all the restaurants and thats when we stumbled into Crabby Bill's. We ordered the $25 bucket of steamed seafood. It was decent, not necessarily the best fresh seafood. This was just a quick snack that I shared with one other person to keep us going before our big dinner at Bern's Steak House that we had reservation for a couple hours later.
Rewrite this for me: As I drove past numerous seafood restaurants near Clearwater Beach, my craving for seafood grew stronger. Being unfamiliar with the area and not having researched any reviews beforehand, I was hesitant to randomly choose a restaurant. However, after a tiring day at the beach, we decided to take a short stroll across the street to where all the restaurants were located, leading us to discover Crabby Bill's. Opting for their $25 bucket of steamed seafood, we found it to be decent but not necessarily the freshest. It served as a quick snack to keep us satiated before our planned dinner reservation at Bern's Steak House a few hours later, where we expected a more substantial meal.

input:
Just finished a State Street Kitchen, Grilled Chicken, Spinach, Swiss and Honey Mustard Sub.  To kick it up a notch I stuffed in Jalapeno Chips for a spicy crunch. 
It was great on an afternoon when autumn is starting to assert itself with bluster.  

This excellent local establishment continues to turn out first rate creative dishes thanks to the ever-present Micha, and her friendly staff.  It has become my most constant breakfast companion, and often my lunch date, as well.  

If you have not been in for a taste of home cooking with a Korean flare, you don't know what you are missing. 

Find a way to get there.  Sit down and become part of the family.
Rewrite this for me:
I just had a mouthwatering State Street Kitchen sandwich filled with grilled chicken, spinach, Swiss cheese, and honey mustard. And to add a little extra kick, I threw in some jalapeno chips for a spicy crunch. It was the perfect meal for a blustery autumn afternoon.

This amazing local restaurant, thanks to the ever-present Micha and her friendly staff, consistently delivers delicious and innovative dishes. It has become my go-to spot for breakfast and often my choice for lunch as well.

If you haven't tried their unique Korean-inspired home cooking, you're truly missing out. Make it a priority to visit this place and immerse yourself in their welcoming family atmosphere.

input: awesome place.  good food. nice people.  rotating specials.  all home made.  what else do you want?  Chicken salad is a great pickup to make sandwiches at home.
Rewrite this for me: The place is absolutely amazing, with delectable food and friendly individuals. They offer enticing rotating specials, all of which are homemade. What more could you ask for? If you're looking for a fantastic option to whip up sandwiches at home, their chicken salad is the perfect choice.

input: I'm rating this based on the service and not the food. I am a sales administrator at a hotel. Typically, many places offer a hospitality discount because we do refer guests different places. Front desk told me I should try this place as they give a decent discount. I called to place my order and wasn't really able to say what I liked b/c the girl who answered would cut me off to finish my statement.(she wasn't in the best mood) We get to the end of the order and she asks me am I a guest or an employee. I told her an employee. She asked my title. I told her. She gives me a total and I asked her about the discount. She says it's only for front desk. I'm shocked that this is a departmental thing 1 and 2 I'm thinking to myself, "I'm in sales. I get groups of people here. They ALWAYS asked for recommendations." I said well should I hang up and have front desk place my order? She huffed and puffed and then said "well i'll give it to you this time but please dont abuse it." I was so shocked at how rude she was. So when I finally got my food, I tipped the driver and gave him their menus back and said we will no longer be doing business with you guys. She didnt know SALES is in charge of who the front desk can recommend. Her name was Neisha.The food was good though.
Rewrite this for me: I am evaluating my experience based on the service provided rather than the quality of the food. In my role as a sales administrator at a hotel, it is common for various establishments to offer us hospitality discounts because we often refer guests to different places. The front desk recommended a particular restaurant to me, mentioning that they offer a decent discount. When I called to place my order, the person who answered interrupted me abruptly and did not seem to be in a pleasant mood. Consequently, I had difficulty conveying my preferences. Towards the end of the order, the person asked whether I was a guest or an employee, to which I responded that I was an employee. Subsequently, they inquired about my job title. After providing them with the necessary information, I asked about the discount. Surprisingly, I was informed that the discount was only applicable to front desk staff. I was taken aback by this department-specific policy and also pondered the fact that as a sales administrator, I frequently bring groups of people to the hotel, and they often request recommendations for places to dine. I asked if I should hang up and have the front desk place my order instead. The person seemed annoyed, hesitated, and then reluctantly agreed to give me the discount, but cautioned me not to abuse it. I was shocked by the rudeness displayed throughout the conversation. Once my food arrived, I tipped the driver, returned their menus, and informed them that we would no longer be patronizing their establishment. It seemed that the person I spoke with, Neisha, was unaware that the sales department has the authority to determine the recommendations provided by the front desk. Despite the unfavorable encounter, I must admit that the food itself was enjoyable.

input: Always the sweetest ladies! Appointments never take forever and barely any wait time!
Rewrite this for me: The ladies here are always incredibly sweet! Appointments are quick, and there's hardly any waiting time!

input: We won't be back. We got the Brussel sprouts and they tasted like pure salt. Our server sent them back and we got another batch and they tasted exactly the same. My husband got the burger and it was okay but the fries that came with it tasted like pure salt also. Maybe the cook working this night was just a little heavy handed on the salt, I don't know. I got the flank steak and it was okay. I wouldn't rave about it or ever get it again. Our cocktails were good and the atmosphere was nice, but we were really disappointed with the food :(
Rewrite this for me: We won't return because our experience was disappointing. The Brussels sprouts were extremely salty, even after sending them back for a new batch. The burger my husband ordered was alright, but the accompanying fries were also overly salty. Maybe the cook on duty that night was too generous with the salt, I'm not sure. As for my flank steak, it was just okay, nothing I would praise or order again. On a positive note, our cocktails were tasty and the ambience was pleasant. However, overall, we were let down by the quality of the food :(

input: I love going to Phillies games sooo much and this stadium definitely adds to the experience. I was never a big baseball fan until about a couple of years ago, when my bf introduced me to the wonder that is the Phils- instant love. Sure,my first Phils game was the 10, 000 loss but whatever. The places has a open feeling, and never feels clausterphobic. The only time i've felt that I had bad seats was when we sat right under neath the scoreboard, and I had to keep on looking up.  I like how you can wander about and watch the game from the lower levels, and that despite it's a sold out game, it never feels cramped or you're really aching to get around the stadium. They have a lot of great food (lots of variety) and the facilities are always clean- both are numerous, so I'm never waiting in line.  I am missing baseball season and I cannot wait until April! Go Phillies!
Rewrite this for me: I absolutely adore going to Phillies games and this stadium definitely enhances the entire experience. I never used to be a huge baseball fan until a couple of years ago when my boyfriend introduced me to the incredible world of the Phils. It was love at first sight. Even though my first Phils game happened to be the 10,000th loss, it didn't deter my enthusiasm. This place has an inviting atmosphere that never feels suffocating. The only time I felt like I had less than ideal seats was when we were positioned directly beneath the scoreboard, forcing me to constantly look up. However, I enjoy the ability to wander around and catch glimpses of the game from the lower levels. Even during a sold-out game, the stadium doesn't feel overly crowded, and I never find myself desperately trying to navigate through the masses. The array of delicious food options (with plenty of variety) and the clean facilities contribute greatly to the overall experience - and the numerous options prevent any long wait times. I'm already counting down the days until baseball season returns in April. Go Phillies!

input: My boyfriend and I decided to stop by for lunch yesterday, and I am so glad we did. I ordered a side of beans, chips and salsa, and guacamole. He ordered two steak tacos and a side of rice. The beans are hands down my favorite I've had from a mexican restaurant.  My only complaint is that, unfortunately you do not get a very big portion. The salsa is so fresh tasting and delicious-very cilantro forward, and the chips were nice, thick and crunchy without being oily at all. Take note though, chips and salsa are not included with your purchase and must be bought separately. Now let me get to the best part-the made to order, chunky guacamole. The hardy chips would definitely withstand this heavy duty guac, but I opted instead for tortillas as my vessel to stuff it with along with my beans and salsa. The hot sauces were anything but, though admittedly my tolerance to spices may be higher than the average persons. While I had a great eating experience, my boyfriend did not. He said the meat was of low quality and quite flavorless. He did say he would give it another shot though!
Rewrite this for me: Yesterday, my boyfriend and I made a spontaneous decision to have lunch at a restaurant. I'm really pleased that we went because the food turned out to be amazing. To satisfy my appetite, I ordered a side of beans, along with chips and salsa, and some guacamole. On the other hand, my boyfriend went for two steak tacos and a side of rice. Without a doubt, the beans blew me away and became the best I've ever tasted at a Mexican restaurant. However, my only complaint is that the portion size is disappointingly small. Moving on to the salsa, it had a refreshing and delicious taste with a prominent cilantro flavor, and the chips were perfect - thick, crunchy, and not greasy at all. It's worth noting that chips and salsa aren't included in the meal and must be purchased separately. Now, let's get to the highlight - the made-to-order, chunky guacamole. The hearty chips could definitely handle the robust guacamole, but I decided to use tortillas instead to stuff them with beans and salsa. As a spice lover, I didn't find the hot sauces to be particularly spicy, but that might be because I have a higher tolerance than most people. While I thoroughly enjoyed my meal, my boyfriend had a different experience. He found the meat to be of poor quality and lacking in flavor. However, he expressed willingness to give the place another chance in the future.

input: I love this place. It's been in La Cumbre Plaza for I don't know how long now. If you are looking for a good sandwich look no further. All of the ingredients taste fresh, and their bread rolls are amazing. They are nice and soft, not with that cut the roof of your mouth crust. Being born and raise in Santa Barbara, actually just down the street, I have been coming here for some years now. I've tried probably over half of their sandwiches and all have been good, so good it's hard to pick a favorite.  In addition, I cannot forget to mention their awesome soda selection, so awesome I cannot hesitate to try something different with every visit. You won't find anything super fancy or exotic, like a roasted duck pastrami sandwich here, but if you're a local or just passing through and feel like having a great sandwich with good fresh ingredients swing by Plaza Deli and grab a bite.
Rewrite this for me:
I absolutely adore this place. It has been a popular fixture in La Cumbre Plaza for as long as I can remember. If you're on the hunt for a delicious sandwich, look no further. The ingredients they use are incredibly fresh and their bread rolls are simply divine. They have the perfect texture - soft and delightful, without that crust that can cut the roof of your mouth. 

Being a proud Santa Barbara native, I have been coming to this place for quite a few years now. I'm proud to say that I've sampled more than half of their sandwich menu, and each one has been consistently fantastic. They're all so good that it's nearly impossible to choose a favorite. 

And let's not forget about their amazing soda selection. It's so impressive that I can't resist trying something different every time I visit. While they may not have any super fancy or exotic options, like a roasted duck pastrami sandwich, if you're a local or just passing through and you're in the mood for a top-notch sandwich made with fresh ingredients, I highly recommend swinging by Plaza Deli and satisfying your cravings.

input: I think this Nordstrom's shoe department is better than other locations.  There was a lot of variety and they carry some higher end lines here.  The sales professionals were very good.  A gentleman named Erwin helped me locate two pairs of shoes throughout the Nordstrom's network AND price matched them to Bloomingdale's clearance sale price.  And no charge for shipping and handling.  Nordstrom's has won my loyalty due to the very high level of customer service!
Rewrite this for me: In my opinion, the Nordstrom's shoe department at this location surpasses others. They offer a wide assortment of options, including some luxurious brands.
