input: A small aquarium that is interesting mainly for kids.  They have a shark feeding show and stingrays that you can pet and buy food to feed.  It is not the first place i would go in Tarpon Springa, but it is ok, small children seem to like it.
Rewrite this for me: The small aquarium in Tarpon Springs is primarily designed to captivate kids, offering a range of fascinating attractions. One of its highlights is the shark feeding show, which never fails to thrill the young visitors. Additionally, there are also friendly stingrays available for children to pet, and they even have the option to buy food to feed these marvelous creatures. Although it may not be at the top of my list when visiting Tarpon Springs, I must admit that it is an acceptable place, especially for families with small children who seem to thoroughly enjoy their time there.

input: Nothing extraordinary, but if you want some simple Chinese takeout, this is the best place around. The food seems less greasy than you sometimes find and the people are super nice.
Rewrite this for me: This place may not offer anything extraordinary, but if you're in the mood for some easy Chinese takeout, it is definitely the top choice. The food here appears to be less greasy compared to what you may usually encounter, and the staff are exceptionally friendly.

input: Quaint place with great ambience, food and service. I had the Shrimp Po Boy. It was delicious. The fries and cole slaw were perfect side dishes. This was my first visit. Definitely not my last.
Rewrite this for me: I recently discovered a charming spot with a delightful atmosphere, exceptional cuisine, and impeccable service. On my inaugural visit, I indulged in the mouthwatering Shrimp Po Boy, which left me thoroughly satisfied. Accompanied by the perfect pairing of fries and cole slaw, the meal was a delectable experience. Needless to say, this initial encounter has ensured that it won't be my last.

input: Broussard's was pretty good when I went there a few weeks ago. I had a Groupon that was about to expire so I took my parents out to dinner.  I knew going in that Broussards is a very old skool New Orleans restaurant, and it is very nice when you walk in to see the old tile on the walls in the foyer of the building. The courtyard is beautiful and I just had to turn into a tourist and take a picture in front of the fountain with my mom. We were seated and very promptly greeted by the drink guy.  He brought us our water and told us about the extensive wine list, but they were of course out of the Pinot Grigio that I ordered.  He successfully suggested a Chardonnay for me instead and I was happy. The head waiter came out and explained with great detail the specials for the night, but I went for menu regulars, the maytag blue cheese salad and the pecan crusted drum. I wanted more salad, it was so good, I ate it up so fast. The drum was excellent too. It had this soy butter sauce on it that was so good and topped with crawfish. I was definitely happy with my meal and glad I had the experience. What makes me knock off two stars is that though the foyer's vintage appeal is nice and the courtyard is beautiful, I feel like the dining room needs an upgrade.  The chandeliers on the walls in the main dining room are very reminiscent of the hallways of my grandmother's assisted living home. I think its just one of those places I am glad to say I've been to, but I don't think I will choose to go there again.
Rewrite this for me: Broussard's proved to be a satisfactory dining experience during my visit a few weeks ago. With an expiring Groupon in hand, I decided to treat my parents to a meal there. Familiar with its reputation as a classic New Orleans restaurant, I was pleased to discover the charming vintage tile on the foyer walls upon arrival. The courtyard was especially remarkable, prompting me to embrace my tourist side and snap a photo with my mom by the fountain. Once seated, we were promptly attended to by the drink server who provided us with water and offered an extensive selection of wines, albeit lacking the Pinot Grigio I initially requested. However, his recommendation of a Chardonnay proved to be a satisfactory alternative. The head waiter then came out and elaborately explained the evening specials. However, I opted for the menu regulars, starting with the absolutely delightful Maytag blue cheese salad and following it with the pecan crusted drum. The salad was so scrumptious that I devoured it with lightning speed, while the drum impressed me with its soy butter sauce and decadent crawfish topping. Overall, I was thoroughly satisfied with my meal and pleased with the overall experience. However, my only complaint lies in the need for an upgrade in the main dining room. The chandeliers on the walls reminded me too much of the corridors in my grandmother's assisted living home, which detracted from the overall ambiance. While I am glad to have checked Broussard's off my list, it is unlikely that I will choose to dine there again, resulting in a deduction of two stars.

input:
Service is excellent. Atmosphere is great. The raw bar was fantastic. Those were the best Alaskan crab legs I've had. Well worth splurging for them. 

My friends were drawn in by the awesome looking burger they had, and indeed the burgers were all they hoped for. It came with a generous portion of crispy fries. But if you want anything else besides the $17 burgers, expect to spend over $30 for your entree. While the ambience feels and looks casual, it is fine dining.

Unfortunately, the waiter did sell the shrimp and grits with the additional crab as "heaven in his mouth", but that it was not. I've had better shrimp and grits in Atlanta, and there is no reasonable way you should be paying $30 for shrimp and GRITS. Without the crab, it was still over $20.

But everything else was great. Drinks were delicious. Everything came out pretty quickly. Oh, when we mentioned we were visiting from out of town, the waiter was nice enough to give us a complimentary appetizer of the cool pizza to start. It was great but the name is hard to say or remember. And the rabbit and chicken liver pate was super worth since it comes in a huge mason jar.

I recommend sticking to the drinks, appetizers, and burgers and you'll be a pretty happy camper.
Rewrite this for me:
The service provided at this restaurant is exceptional, and the overall atmosphere is fantastic. The raw bar offers a truly enjoyable experience, particularly when it comes to the Alaskan crab legs, which are undeniably the best I've ever had. They are definitely worth indulging in, even though they may be a splurge.

My friends were enticed by the visually appealing burgers on the menu, and they were not disappointed. In fact, the burgers exceeded their expectations. Each serving also comes with a generous portion of crispy fries. However, if you desire something other than the $17 burgers, be prepared to spend more than $30 for your main course. Despite the casual ambiance, the dining experience here could easily be classified as fine dining.

Unfortunately, the waiter oversold the shrimp and grits, claiming they were heavenly. However, they did not live up to the hype. I have had better shrimp and grits in Atlanta, and it is unreasonable to charge $30 for a dish that primarily consists of grits. Even without the addition of crab, the price still exceeded $20.

However, apart from that disappointment, everything else about the restaurant is wonderful. The drinks are delicious, and the service is prompt. We were pleasantly surprised when we mentioned that we were visiting from out of town, as the waiter kindly offered us a complimentary appetizer, which happened to be a delicious pizza that was a challenge to pronounce or remember. Additionally, the rabbit and chicken liver pate in the large mason jar is highly recommended.

Therefore, I suggest focusing on enjoying the drinks, appetizers, and burgers, as they guarantee a satisfying dining experience.

input: I love Doan's. It's the kind of place you have a "usual" and every time you have it, it's just as good as the last time. They staff is friendly and speedy so if you don't have a long lunch it's a great place to go.
Rewrite this for me: I have a great fondness for Doan's. It's the type of establishment where you establish a regular order, and every time you indulge in it, the experience is consistently excellent. The staff, known for being amicable and efficient, makes it an ideal spot to frequent when time for lunch is limited.

input: This amazing brick oven pizza joint gets better every time I go. The last I time I went I got a Rotolo and a prosciutto pizza. The Rotolo is dough wrapped around mortadella and ricotta cheese and topped with pistachios and oil. It is so good. I order it every time. It's about the size of a bun and cost $5. The pizza was amazing. The prosciutto was incredibly tasty. The dough is divine. The service is always great and the beer selection is good. Definitely one of the best pizza places in Philly.
Rewrite this for me: Every visit to this incredible brick oven pizza establishment surpasses the last. During my most recent trip, I indulged in the delightful combination of a Rotolo and a prosciutto pizza. The Rotolo boasts a mouthwatering blend of mortadella, ricotta cheese, and a sprinkle of pistachios and oil, all meticulously enveloped in a delectable dough - a true masterpiece that captivates my taste buds. Without fail, I find myself ordering this delightful creation each time, with its bun-sized portion priced at a mere $5. The pizza itself was a revelation, with the prosciutto offering an exceptionally flavorful and savory experience. The divine dough that forms the foundation of their pizzas is truly unparalleled. The service in this establishment is consistently exceptional, complemented by a commendable selection of beers. Undoubtedly, this gem stands as one of the premier pizza destinations in the dynamic city of Philadelphia.

input:
Amazing pizza. AMAZING! After my first bite, I felt like that Oprah Winfrey meme, where her head is thrown back, her mouth is agape and her arms are open wide, and she's screaming, "You get a car!" Except it's not Oprah, it's me. And I don't get a car -- I get a pizza. But I felt that excited.  

This is basically the pizza I have been looking for since moving to the Indianapolis area. It's a whole lot of nothing: It's not cut into square pieces. It's not crispy and thin. It's not redolent of oregano. It's thick and chewy, cheesy, greasy, wonderful -- it tastes the way pizza is supposed to taste! I have found my new pizza home.
Rewrite this for me:
The pizza was absolutely incredible. I mean, it was mind-blowing! As soon as I took my first bite, I experienced a sheer moment of bliss. It was like that famous Oprah Winfrey meme, you know the one where she throws her head back, opens her mouth wide, and stretches her arms out while screaming, "You get a car!" Well, imagine that, except it's me in that moment, not Oprah, and instead of a car, I'm celebrating over a pizza. But trust me, I was just as thrilled.

I've been on the hunt for this kind of pizza ever since I moved to the Indianapolis area. It's simply incomparable. This pizza is in a league of its own. It's not like those square-cut pieces you typically find. It definitely doesn't have that crispy, thin crust that many people prefer. And forget about that familiar scent of oregano lingering in the air. No, this pizza is different. It's thick, chewy, and loaded with cheese. There's a bit of greasiness to it, but in the most wonderful way possible. It's everything I believe pizza should taste like.

Finally, after a long search, I have found my new go-to pizza place. This is where I belong.

input: Waited 27 minutes for three teas (no one else was in the store when we came in and ordered). NO tea is worth that long of a wait, especially in Chinatown.
Rewrite this for me: We waited for a total of 27 minutes to receive three teas, despite there being no other customers in the store at the time of our arrival and order. It's difficult to justify such a lengthy wait for a tea, especially in Chinatown.

input:

input:
We came here for an early mothers day celebration as we were on the quest to find a nail salon that could accommodate 4 pedicures at the same time. They were very friendly and even though they didn't have 4 pedicurists on the schedule that day they added one to accommodate us. That was really nice of them as they could have easily told us no. 

The place itself is decorated very modern and offers a very clean, minimalist atmosphere. Upon walking in we were immediately greeted and after we checked in with the front desk we were asked what we wanted to drink. They had complimentary mimosas, wine and champagne, the perfect way to begin to unwind. Once we picked out our polish colors we were well on our way to getting our pedicures. Everyone was so nice and made us feel comfortable and welcomed. My polish never chipped the whole time I had it on. I will definitely be back. 

The only downside is that its street parking only, which isn't something that they can control. They told us most of their business comes from people who work in the CBD so parking probably isn't an issue for their regular customers. Aside from parking being an issue I would definitely go to Buff again.
Rewrite this for me:
We came here to celebrate an early Mother's Day and were in search of a nail salon that could accommodate four pedicures simultaneously. Despite not having scheduled four pedicurists that day, the staff went out of their way to accommodate us, which was incredibly kind of them.

The salon itself has a modern decor and offers a clean and minimalist atmosphere. As soon as we walked in, we received a warm greeting, and after checking in at the front desk, we were offered a selection of complimentary beverages including mimosas, wine, and champagne, which was the perfect way to relax. Once we chose our polish colors, we began our pedicures. The staff was extremely friendly, making us feel comfortable and welcomed throughout the experience. I was impressed that my polish didn't chip at all during the time I had it on. I will definitely be returning.

The only downside is that the salon only has street parking, which is out of their control. They mentioned that most of their regular customers work in the CBD, so parking is not usually an issue for them. Despite the parking inconvenience, I would certainly visit Buff again.

input: Great spot for pho! Broth is very good. I ordered No. 51 (small) and it was filling. Would definitely come back again when I'm in Philly.
Rewrite this for me: This place is excellent for pho! The broth is superb. I went for No. 51 (small) and it was surprisingly satisfying. I would absolutely revisit this spot whenever I'm in Philadelphia.

input:
I love the concept of this place. One half of it a café that serves different types of coffees and teas, and breakfast type items, and the other world where it serves bar type apps, salads, and sandwiches,  Can't forget that they also serve a wide variety of beers that they serve on tap, bottled, or in can.

I absolutely adore the concept of this place. It is divided into two sections - one half serves amazing coffees, teas, and breakfast items like a café, while the other half offers bar-style appetizers, salads, and sandwiches. And let's not forget their extensive selection of beers available on tap, in bottles, or cans.

The atmosphere here is incredibly casual, making it the perfect spot to spend hours hanging out with friends. It brings back memories of those carefree college days when time seemed to stand still, especially on relaxing Sundays.

What's even better is that you can bring your furry, four-legged friend along too. They are more than welcome here!

input: My husband reserved a Corolla-sized car over the internet ten days ahead of time. When we arrived at Avis Rent A Car at the Reno airport I asked if the rental could be upgraded to a Camry-size vehicle. They offered us two different kinds of cars and finally we got the Camry we wanted. The man was very professional and in the end told us the rental would be $800.00 for five days. I felt the price was very high, however we had gone through most of the paperwork. I had already selected to get the $25.00 a day insurance which came to $150.00 with tax. We were very happy with the car and had no problems with it. During our vacation I decided to talk to an Avis representative when we dropped the car off. I asked her if a weekly rate would be less expensive. She said it would be $15.00 more. She said the upgrade cost an extra $20.00 a day. I will not rent from Avis any more. Next time I will go to Hertz or Dollar and make the reservation over the phone. Looking back, i would not have gotten the extra insurance. My personal insurance covers everything.
Rewrite this for me: Ten days before our trip, my husband made a reservation for a car the size of a Corolla through an online platform. When we arrived at Avis Rent A Car at Reno airport, I inquired about upgrading our rental to a larger vehicle resembling a Camry. Avis provided us with two options, and ultimately we were able to secure the Camry we desired. The attendant was very professional and informed us that the rental would cost $800.00 for a five-day period. While I found the price to be exorbitant, we had already completed most of the necessary paperwork. Moreover, I had already opted for the $25.00 per day insurance, amounting to $150.00 with taxes. Despite the steep price, the car itself met our expectations and performed well throughout our vacation. Nevertheless, upon returning the car, I decided to discuss our rental with an Avis representative. I inquired if a weekly rate would have been more cost-effective, to which she replied that it would actually be an additional $15.00. She also mentioned that the upgrade itself incurred a daily fee of $20.00. Dissatisfied with the overall experience, I have decided not to rent from Avis in the future. Instead, I plan to make my reservation over the phone with Hertz or Dollar. Reflecting on the situation, I realize that getting the extra insurance was unnecessary since my existing personal insurance provides comprehensive coverage.

input: Great customer service! Love my new car! Highly recommend to anyone who's trying to buy a new used car in good shape! Talk to Andy if you want some good help!
Rewrite this for me: I had an amazing customer service experience! Absolutely thrilled with my new car! I would highly recommend this place to anyone looking for a well-maintained used car. Andy is the person you should speak to if you need excellent assistance!

input: After moving to the area, Jungle Prada Tavern was one of the first places a friend took me.  The bartender made a great recommendation based on a beer I told her I liked and I loved it!  Now for the food- I LOVE seafood, so I am leary of ordering from places that don't do it justice, but alas, they impressed me thoroughly with all the seafood options I chose!!  The scallops prosciutto app, del mar pizza with crab and scallops, and crab stuffed portabella app (comes with a crab and lobster bisque- YUM) are all delicious!!  I also love the roasted portabella app- for a vegetarian option, it is delicious and was recomended by someone who isn't. I've actually gone back several times since then just to eat (obviously, I also drank ;) and took my sister when she was in town visiting (and is a seafood fanatic).  So all in all, give this place a chance!!  You will not be disappointed with the options!
Rewrite this for me: When I moved to the area, my friend introduced me to Jungle Prada Tavern as one of the first places to check out. The bartender there had an excellent recommendation based on my preferred beer, and I absolutely loved it! As a seafood lover, I'm always skeptical about ordering from places that don't do it justice, but Jungle Prada Tavern thoroughly impressed me with their delicious seafood options. From the scallops prosciutto appetizer to the del mar pizza topped with crab and scallops, and the crab stuffed portabella appetizer that comes with a delectable crab and lobster bisque, everything was simply mouthwatering! They even have a roasted portabella appetizer that's incredibly tasty, and it was actually recommended by someone who isn't a vegetarian. Since that first visit, I have returned numerous times just to indulge in their amazing food (and of course, drinks). I even took my seafood fanatic sister when she was in town visiting, and she was blown away as well. Overall, I highly recommend giving this place a chance - you won't be disappointed with the variety of options they offer!

input: This is one of my favorite bead stores in Nashville, walls and walls of seed beads and glass strands!
Rewrite this for me: I absolutely love this bead store in Nashville! They have an incredible selection of seed beads and glass strands, with walls adorned with them everywhere. It's definitely one of my favorites.

input: Went here for dinner on opening day and was SO HAPPY I DID!! Great atmosphere, lovely staff, and food on fleek!! Green tea (PHO PHREE) was so satisfying, summer rolls and spicy peanut sauce were DELISH, and pho was PHONOMENAL! Definitely making this one of my regular hot spotz as I eat my way through Fairmount!
Rewrite this for me: I went to this restaurant for dinner on its opening day and I was extremely happy that I did! The atmosphere was fantastic, the staff was lovely, and the food was absolutely divine! The green tea (complimentary with the pho) was incredibly satisfying. The summer rolls and spicy peanut sauce were delicious, and the pho itself was phenomenal. Without a doubt, this restaurant is now on my list of regular hot spots as I explore the culinary offerings of Fairmount.

input:
Don't let the outside fool ya or even the initial impression when you walk in because they food here is really good! When ya walk in this place it's like stepping back into the 1950's.  It's kinda awesome.  Definitely a small-town, homey feel that serves good ole family cookin'.  They had a iceskates up on the wall and a Christmas tree in the corner.  How precious.   
Don't come here expecting the best food in the whole wide world.  It is great for grandma's greasy cooking.  I've only eaten breakfast here but it's been amazing everytime.  I got pancakes and they are so fluffy and light and awesome (esp if you add a little butter).  The bacon was nice, thick, large slices; slightly overcooked maybe but super good cuz I love bacon! :)
The prices are reasonable and the service is great.  This is a great place for a quick delicious home cooked breakfast!
Rewrite this for me:
Do not be deceived by the exterior or your first impression when you enter, as the food here is truly excellent! Upon entering this establishment, you will feel as though you have stepped back in time to the 1950s, which is quite delightful. It offers a charming small-town ambiance, providing authentic family-style cooking. Adorned with ice skates on the wall and a Christmas tree in the corner, it exudes a charming atmosphere.

However, do not come here with the expectation of the finest cuisine in the world. It is perfect for indulging in grandma's comfort food. I have only had breakfast here, but it has consistently been amazing. The pancakes are incredibly fluffy, light, and delicious, especially when accompanied with a touch of butter. The bacon is thick, generously-sized slices, albeit slightly overcooked, but still delectable for bacon lovers like myself.

The prices are reasonable, and the service is excellent. If you are seeking a quick, tasty, home-cooked breakfast, this is the ideal place to visit.

input: Tried this place out after many suggestions from friends.  We went in one night about an hour or so before closing just to find that they were only serving a partial menu - we're not talking that late, it was like, 9:30 on a weekend.  There was no mention of going down to a bar menu on the website so I was a bit annoyed by that.  Something about 'surprise disappointments that could be totally avoided' really bother me.  So, the dish I had picked out online wasn't available and I ordered a burger instead.  The server seemed to have a very hard time understanding my burger and suggested that modifications couldn't be made?  I told him I'm sure removing a single topping wouldn't cause the kitchen staff any issues...  The rest of the meal we were generally ignored and the service wasn't great.  I found the food to be overpriced for the quality.  Unless there is a special reason to attend, I don't think we'll be going back.
Rewrite this for me:
After receiving multiple recommendations from friends, we decided to give this place a try. However, our experience was a bit disappointing. We arrived around 9:30 on a weekend, which we didn't think was too late, but to our surprise, they were only serving a limited menu. This information was not mentioned on their website, and it left us feeling frustrated. It's really bothersome to encounter avoidable disappointments like this.

Furthermore, the dish I had initially chosen from their online menu wasn't available, so I settled for a burger instead. Unfortunately, the server had difficulty understanding my request for a modified burger. I politely explained that removing a single topping shouldn't pose any issues for the kitchen staff, but it seemed to be a challenge for them to accommodate my request. Throughout the rest of our meal, we received minimal attention from the servers and the overall service was subpar.

To make matters worse, we found the prices of the food to be excessively high for the quality provided. Unless there is a special occasion prompting us to return, I doubt we will be visiting this place again.

input:
Second visit even better than the first!!  Loved the butternut squash and goat cheese Rangoons, and the delightfully filling mushroom yakisoba. Amazing flavor, and a smoky , meaty feel though it is meatless. Then came the coconut curry ramen. Heaven in a bowl. 
My only complaint is when you have to wait for seating there is no way to hang by the bar without constantly feeling you are in The servers' way as they breeze by with deliciousness in bowls and plates. So worth the wait before heading to the theater. Plus, food comes out very quickly so we made the curtain, just barely, but with really happy tummies.
Rewrite this for me:
The second visit was even more enjoyable than the first! The butternut squash and goat cheese Rangoons were amazing, along with the incredibly satisfying mushroom yakisoba. It had a delicious flavor and a smoky, meaty texture despite being meatless. And then there was the coconut curry ramen, which was heavenly. 
The only downside was that when we had to wait for a table, there was no place to hang out by the bar without feeling like we were in the servers' way as they passed by with delicious bowls and plates. Despite that, the wait was totally worth it before heading to the theater. The food came out quite quickly, allowing us to make it to the show just in time, but with fully satisfied stomachs.

input: I cannot comment on the food as I had only a couple beers. I did have the white IPA and a red ale which were good but not blow me away. I might be spoiled having 2 friends who brew professionally but the beers were good, not outstanding. The location is kind of far from other stuff which normally wouldn't bother me but everything around is seriously industrial and scenery does make a better place. They do discount the beer $1 when a train comes by and maybe that's the best they can make of a meh location. Probably give it more like a 3.5 stars. It does say something that there was a loyal following at 4pm on a Sunday.
Rewrite this for me: Unfortunately, I am unable to comment on the food since I only consumed a couple of beers. Specifically, I tried the white IPA and a red ale which were decent but not exceptionally remarkable. Perhaps, I have been spoiled by having two friends who brew beer professionally, which may have influenced my opinion. While the beers were satisfactory, they did not exceed expectations. The establishment is situated quite a distance away from other locations, which normally wouldn't concern me. However, the surrounding area is predominantly industrial, lacking in scenic beauty. Despite this drawback, they do offer a $1 discount on their beer whenever a train passes by. This might be the best they can do considering the less than desirable location. Taking everything into consideration, I would probably rate it around 3.5 stars. It is worth noting that the fact that there was a loyal following even at 4pm on a Sunday speaks volumes about the place.

input:
I first found out about this adorable little salon here on yelp while looking for a place to get a manicure downtown/ CBD.  I visited on 3/8/13 and got their "Mini Manicure"- it's only $15!  I chose an OPI polish and the nail technician did a GREAT job!  So great in fact, that today on Monday, 3/18/13- I did not have ONE CHIP!  This is amazing for polish!  My nails looked fabulous!  The technician was friendly, as were the other stylists.  I'm not sure if it was the manager or the owner that was working the front desk- but she came over as well and was super friendly and welcoming.  The salon looks amazing, trendy, and peaceful.  It has a great vibe.

I was so happy with my first appointment- that I went back today, and left disappointed.  I went to the same nail techinician- and we talked as she worked on my nails.  The person working the front desk (seemed like an owner/ manager- although different from my first visit) was SO  nice, welcoming, and talkative.  This time though I needed a gel manicure, in french- as I am in a wedding this weekend.  I explained that I was in the wedding, assuming the technician would know that this more special than just an everyday manicure  The technician stated after she started my nails, that she did not have the proper brush that she needed in order to do the manicure.  So like most places- they paint the white, and then go back later with a brush to create the crisp, perfect line.  Since she did not have the brush to do that- she used a q- tip.  So obviously the lines are not perfect or even.  Along with the lines being uneven- some are thicker than others, and the edges go up, instead of down.  My nails are not at all filed and shaped pretty either.  For $40 (+ a tip)- I really expect them to look right.  I went during my lunch hour, and it was supposed to be 30 minute appointment, but the appointment took a little bit over an hour.  I understand that french takes a little extra time- but this seemed like quite a bit extra.  I was late for work, and had to hurry out of there when she was finished and did not want to be even more late to work to stay there to make a complaint.  I wish I would have- but I also felt bad because the technician was trying so hard- but they are just not up to par.

I'm conflicted, but I don't know that I'll return.  I loved it to so much the first time, I even sent friends over there.  But after this time- I am not happy with the product.  I wish it wasn't gel- because I can't even take the polish off myself.  So I'm forced to have nails that I am unhappy with, or go to somewhere else and pay to have this taken off, and then pay to have them re done- all before a 6am flight on Wednesday morning, and it's Monday afternoon....
Rewrite this for me:
I discovered this lovely salon here on Yelp when I was searching for a manicure place downtown/CBD. I visited them on 3/8/13 for their "Mini Manicure" which is only $15! I chose an OPI polish and the nail technician did an amazing job. Believe it or not, my nails didn't have a single chip until today, Monday, 3/18/13. That's remarkable for nail polish! My nails looked absolutely fabulous. The technician was very friendly, as were the other stylists. Either the manager or owner, who was working the front desk, was also incredibly warm and welcoming. The salon itself has a trendy and peaceful vibe that I loved.

Due to my fantastic first appointment, I decided to go back today but unfortunately, it left me disappointed. I went to the same nail technician and we had a conversation while she worked on my nails. The person who seemed like the owner or manager, but a different one from my first visit, was extremely nice, welcoming, and talkative. This time, I needed a French gel manicure as I am in a wedding this weekend. I assumed that the technician would understand that this is a more special occasion than a regular manicure. However, after she started on my nails, she informed me that she didn't have the proper brush necessary for the manicure. So, like most places, they usually paint the white and then use a brush later to create the clean, perfect line. Since she didn't have the necessary brush, she used a q-tip instead. As a result, the lines are not even or perfect. Some lines are thicker than others, and the edges go upwards instead of downwards. My nails were also not filed and shaped nicely. For the price of $40 (plus a tip), I expect a better outcome. I went for my appointment during my lunch hour, and it was supposed to take 30 minutes, but it ended up taking slightly over an hour. Although I understand that French manicures take a bit more time, this seemed excessive. I ended up being late for work and had to rush out of there once she finished, without wanting to be even more tardy by staying to make a complaint. I regret not speaking up, but I also felt guilty because the technician seemed to be trying her best. However, the quality of the service just isn't up to par.

I'm torn, but I don't think I will be returning. I loved it so much the first time that I even recommended it to my friends. However, after this experience, I am dissatisfied with the outcome. I wish it wasn't a gel manicure because I can't even remove the polish myself. I'm now left with nails I'm unhappy with, or I'll have to go somewhere else to have it taken off and then pay to get them redone. All of this needs to happen before my 6am flight on Wednesday morning, and it's only Monday afternoon.

input:
A bit off the beaten path for most tourists, as it is in the Marigny, but worth the trip. Sure, the place is not perfect, but there are ultra-expensive restaurants in the FQ that are also not perfect. Look, cheap food, especially food this good, gives "wiggle" room for imperfections.

Breakfast served all day is a bonus. Sometimes you just got to have a lox omelet (under $10) late in the day. The restaurant boasts vegetarian and *gasp* vegan dishes, but someone needs to tell them that cheese doesn't fit into either of those categories. That aside, the french fry poboy, and the mac 'n cheese sandwiches are amazing. So is the Saturday Blue Plate of BBQ Chicken legs. 

Every entree is under $10, well except for the Friday Blue Plate, but why quibble? And who can argue with $5 Bloody Mary's, especially ones that are this good?
Rewrite this for me:
Slightly off the usual tourist path in the Marigny, but definitely worth the visit. Sure, the place isn't flawless, but hey, even some of the overpriced restaurants in the FQ have their flaws. The great thing about affordable food, especially when it's as delicious as this, is that it allows for a little imperfection.

The added bonus of breakfast being served all day is fantastic. Sometimes you just crave a lox omelet (for under $10) even when the day is almost over. The restaurant offers vegetarian and *gasp* vegan options, although someone should inform them that cheese doesn't fit into either of those categories. Nonetheless, their french fry poboy and mac 'n cheese sandwiches are absolutely amazing. The Saturday Blue Plate BBQ Chicken legs are equally impressive.

With every entree priced below $10, except for the Friday Blue Plate, why get caught up in minor details? And who can argue with $5 Bloody Mary's, especially when they're this good?

input: Awesome sangria.  Rotating craft beers. Pizza and calzones keep me coming back
Rewrite this for me: I keep coming back for the amazing sangria, the ever-changing selection of craft beers, and the irresistible pizzas and calzones.

input: First off, it is a bar through and through. The alcohol selection is good and the drinks well mixed. It is also a casino bar, so you'll be paying higher than average prices. There is a small food menu, but the selection isn't that great. To add insult to injury the food made me ill. The reviews about service aren't exaggerations. We, too, practically had to tackle our server to order food and drinks many of times. Not my preferred place to go when there are so many better options in Reno.
Rewrite this for me: To start, this establishment is unmistakably a bar with a great variety of alcoholic beverages that are skillfully prepared. However, as it is also a casino bar, the prices are higher than the average. Although there is a limited selection on the food menu, it fails to impress. Regrettably, I personally suffered from illness after consuming their food. The criticisms regarding the service have proven to be accurate, as we too encountered difficulties in ordering food and drinks, often having to make great efforts to get the attention of our server. Given the abundance of superior options available in Reno, this is not my preferred destination to visit.

input: Rude and unprofessional staff. I called today to find out if they had availability over the Thanksgiving holiday and the staff was short and basically said no then hung up the phone. I will take my business elsewhere.
Rewrite this for me: The staff was impolite and displayed unprofessional behavior. When I called today to inquire about availability during the Thanksgiving holiday, their response was brief and dismissive, followed by abruptly ending the call. As a result of this negative experience, I have decided to find another place to conduct my business.

input: Went there due to having a gc, and was suprised at the great food!  Had the sauteed stirfry over spinach, and my gf had the abundant pile of nachos.  They have a pretty decent selection of other delectables, and the day time bartender was very pleasant.  I would recommend to someone who wants a friendly atmosphere with decent food in a sports bar setting.  They actually do have sports playing on the tvs.
Rewrite this for me: I visited the place because I had a gift card and was pleasantly surprised by the amazing food! I ordered the sauteed stir fry over spinach, while my girlfriend enjoyed a generous portion of nachos. The menu offered a good variety of appetizing options, and our experience was enhanced by the friendly daytime bartender. Overall, I would recommend this place to anyone looking for a welcoming atmosphere, decent food, and a sports bar setting. They even have TVs playing sports games.

input: Horrible experience, pizza was soggy and cold when I received it, took 2 hours until I actually received my order as well. Absolutely no communication on my order, even after calling twice. Once I finally received the pizza I called to get my money back, which was communicated that I would not be charged, soon to find out that I was charged the very next day. I highly recommend never ordering from here, service was horrible and they were extremely rude. I won't be ordering from here again and either should you.
Rewrite this for me: My experience was incredibly disappointing. The pizza I received was both soggy and cold, and it took an excessively long time of 2 hours before it actually arrived. Moreover, there was a complete lack of communication regarding my order, despite my two phone calls inquiring about it. When I finally received the pizza, I promptly called to request a refund as I was assured I would not be charged. Unfortunately, the very next day, I discovered that I had indeed been charged. The service I encountered was abysmal, coupled with the extremely rude behavior of the staff. I strongly urge others to refrain from ordering from this establishment. I, for one, will not be ordering from here again, and neither should you.

input:
Incredible service and incredible food! The black bean ravioli is succulent! The bone-in steak was flavorful and amazingly juicy and delicious. And the best of all, service was perfect. From the friendly hostess to the waiter to the chef who personally came over to make sure we enjoyed our food, everyone really made us feel at home. 

As an added bonus, the ambiance is beautiful. Decor, lighting, and fireplace makes the place very homely. 

Highly recommended. I went as a group of four and had an excellent time.
Rewrite this for me:
The service and food were absolutely amazing! The black bean ravioli was incredibly delicious and flavorful. The bone-in steak was juicy, flavorful, and downright delicious. But what truly stood out was the impeccable service. Everyone, from the friendly hostess to the attentive waiter and the chef who personally checked on our satisfaction, made us feel welcomed and at home. 

Furthermore, the ambiance of the restaurant was stunning. The beautiful decor, perfect lighting, and cozy fireplace created a warm and inviting atmosphere. 

I highly recommend this place. I visited with a group of four and we had an outstanding time.

input:
I've been driving by this location for several weeks anticipating their opening.  With the established Legends Sports Bar directly across the street I thought this place must have something very special to feel they can compete.

They took over the building that was prevriously used by the Ruby River Steakhouse.  The owners apparently opted not to change a thing about the indoor seating.  Gone are all the cowboy boots, up are various team jerseys. It looks like somebody went to Pro Image at the mall to decorate the place.  Nothing appears to be autographed or evoke a sense of authenticity.

Video games are available for the kids, so bring your quarters.  No dart boards, shuffleboard, air hockey or pool tables.  This is pretty much a dine and drink only establishment.

More TV's in the place than I could count (I figure at least 20), all tuned to ESPN or ESPN2.  No clue at this time if they are choosing to use Direct TV, Dish, or Cable One for their service.  However, they already have made one of the biggest mistakes I think most wannabe sports bars make; they broadcast music rather than sound from a live sporting event.  With live sporting events available almost everyday from 12pm - 12am, you would think they would want to try to emphasize that rather than muzak (tuned to a country station; still feels like the Ruby River).

A word of advice here, if you want people to stay and eat and drink, you gotta give them something on which to focus their attention.  The sounds of the game will get their attention.  They came to a sports bar to think about sports, not Conway Twitty.

Typically, when I see the word pub in a restaurant name, I think it is just beer and wine, but it looks like Timeout has a full bar with several specialty drinks.  With a designated driver, it may be fun to experiment.

The food is typical sports bar fare; salads, burgers, pasta.  Most items will cost $9 - $11, with entrees running more.  A few twists on their offerings will ensure that I stop in to try something different, but unless the atmosphere improves, I think I will always leave a little disappointed. 

Those staying at the nearby motel may like the proximity, but I think they might find the walk across the street to Legends worth the extra steps.

Happy Hour 2pm - 6pm Monday -  Friday; Late Happy Hour 10pm - close Monday - Thursday.  Happy Hour all day Sunday.
Rewrite this for me:
For several weeks, I've been driving past this location eagerly waiting for its opening. Seeing the popular Legends Sports Bar just across the street, I couldn't help but wonder what makes this new place think it can compete.

They have taken over the building that used to house the Ruby River Steakhouse. Interestingly, it seems like they haven't made any changes to the indoor seating. The cowboy boots that adorned the walls have been replaced with various team jerseys, giving the place a decoration style reminiscent of Pro Image at the mall. However, there are no autographed items or anything that gives off an authentic vibe.

While they do have video games for the kids, there are no dart boards, shuffleboard, air hockey, or pool tables. This establishment seems to focus solely on dining and drinking.

The number of TV's in this place is mind-boggling (I estimate at least 20), all tuned to ESPN or ESPN2. It's still unclear whether they use Direct TV, Dish, or Cable One for their service. However, they have already made one big mistake that many wannabe sports bars make; they play music instead of broadcasting the sound from live sporting events. With live sports happening almost every day from noon to midnight, you would think they would want to emphasize that rather than playing generic music (which is still country, like the Ruby River).

Here's a piece of advice: if you want people to stay, eat, and drink, you need to give them something to focus on. The sounds of the game will grab their attention. They came to a sports bar to immerse themselves in sports, not listen to Conway Twitty.

When I see the word "pub" in a restaurant's name, I usually assume it only serves beer and wine. However, Timeout seems to have a full bar with several specialty drinks. It might be fun to try some of these drinks with a designated driver.

The food here is what you would expect from a typical sports bar: salads, burgers, and pasta. Most items are priced between $9 and $11, with entrees costing more. They do have a few unique twists on their offerings that make it worth stopping by to try something different. However, unless the atmosphere improves, I always leave feeling a little let down.

Those staying at the nearby motel might appreciate the convenience of this place, but I believe they would find it more worthwhile to take the extra steps and go to Legends across the street.

They have happy hour from 2pm to 6pm, Monday to Friday, and a late happy hour from 10pm to closing time, Monday to Thursday. On Sundays, happy hour lasts the entire day.

input: If you like onion rings order them here. Some of the best I have ever have. I also had a Reuben which was very good also.
Rewrite this for me: If you enjoy onion rings, you should definitely order them at this place. They have some of the best I have ever tasted. I also tried their Reuben sandwich, which was equally delicious.

input: The cutest and definitely the friendliest coffee shop in Boise! The coffee is great but the staff is even better. Love this place!
Rewrite this for me: This coffee shop in Boise is hands down the cutest and most welcoming! Not only is the coffee fantastic, but the staff goes above and beyond. Absolutely adore this place!

input:
Hubby and I were eager to try this establishment due to a rave review from some close friends. We decided for our date night we would give it a try on Saturday. We pulled up about 8pm and the open sign was turned off. We thought maybe the light was burnt out or someone just forgot to plug it in. So we proceeded to the door. There were people inside and the sign said open till 11pm, so we walked inside. It was like walking into the Twlight Zone, everyone stopped and stared at us. The woman behind the bar came over and told us they were closed. HUH! Ok.... so we left. It was very akward and unpleasant. If they were closed then the door should of been locked or a sign on the door stating private party or something. 
Not sure if we will attempt to try to dine there again.
Rewrite this for me: My husband and I were excited to visit this establishment based on a glowing recommendation from some close friends. Determined to make it our date night, we planned to try it out on Saturday. Arriving at around 8pm, we noticed that the open sign was turned off. Initially, we thought it could be a simple case of a burnt-out light or someone forgetting to plug it in. Undeterred, we proceeded towards the door. Inside, we saw people and the sign clearly indicated that they were open until 11pm, so we entered. However, as soon as we stepped in, it felt like we had entered the Twilight Zone, with everyone stopping and staring at us. The bartender approached and informed us that they were actually closed. We were taken aback by the sudden change in plans. It would have been more appropriate for them to either lock the door or put up a sign indicating a private event. The entire experience felt awkward and unpleasant. We are now uncertain whether we should give it another chance in the future.

input: Awesome food! It was so fresh and delicious. The papaya salad was delicious! Try the curry..simply spicy and beautiful. The service was great too! They have take out!!!
Rewrite this for me: The food here is absolutely amazing! Not only was it incredibly fresh, but also incredibly delicious. The papaya salad was absolutely delightful, and I highly recommend trying the curry as well - it's a perfect balance of spice and flavors. The service was exceptional too, and an added bonus - they offer take-out!

input: I have new dental insurance and had to find a dentist in network and came across Music City Dental. Dr. Spurlin and her staff are great! They are very gentle and make sure the patient is comfortable at all times. I had to get a filling and am terrified of shots. I didn't even feel when Dr. Spurlin gave me my shot. I was offered a pillow, blanket and choice of watching a movie or listening to music. I had a pleasant experience and am definitely a permanent patient!
Rewrite this for me: After getting new dental insurance, I had the task of finding a dentist within my coverage network. That's when I stumbled upon Music City Dental, and I couldn't be happier. Dr. Spurlin and her team are truly amazing! They go above and beyond to ensure their patients' comfort and well-being throughout the entire process. Even though I was nervous about getting a filling, Dr. Spurlin made sure I didn't feel a thing when she administered the shot. To make my experience even better, they offered me a pillow, blanket, and the choice between watching a movie or listening to music. It was such a pleasant visit that I am now a loyal, long-term patient of Music City Dental.

input:
The beef noodles was a bit too salty and the fried rice was a bit oily. But overall they are good. We liked the shrimp spring rolls a lot. It is one of the best we have tried. 

The place could have earned higher points. But I have to give it a three stars because of the chaotic seating arrangement. The owner gave tables to people behind us despite we reminded the him and the staff. Perhaps that is what you get when you go to a teeny tiny Chinese restaurant during a long weekend.
Rewrite this for me:
The beef noodles were overly salty and the fried rice was quite greasy. However, overall, they were still enjoyable. The shrimp spring rolls were exceptional and easily one of the best we have ever tasted. 

The establishment could have obtained a higher rating, but unfortunately, due to the disorganized seating arrangement, I am giving it three stars. Despite our repeated reminders to the owner and staff, they still gave tables to customers behind us. It seems that this is the result of dining at a small Chinese restaurant during a busy holiday weekend.

input:
Great community vibe... i've run into friends and struck up conversation with new ones each time i've been in.  Its nice to have new hang within walking distance of my house.  I've stuck to the classic burger and love it... everything from the buns to the ketchup is made in-house and has unique taste. The bar had pretty much whatever i wanted... last night the bartenders made some homespun watermelon concoction.

To touch on some other reviews... i understand everyone has a different experience, but to say the place is 'too hipster' seems like someones still jaded from feeling left out in high school...  and personally attacking the owner is tasteless and has no place in a review.  We should be glad we don't all have someone looking over our shoulder attacking our motives. I like what Burger Up is trying to do and i like that they hired a bunch of folks representative of our Nashville community... if you need a non-musician wait staff who dresses just like you and takes you to prom, you're probably in the wrong town.
Rewrite this for me:
The atmosphere in the community is fantastic. Every time I've been there, I've had the opportunity to run into my friends and strike up conversations with new acquaintances. It's great to have a hangout spot within walking distance of my house. I always stick to their classic burger, which I absolutely love. Everything from the buns to the house-made ketchup has a unique and delicious taste. The bar caters to all my preferences, and the bartenders even whipped up a homemade watermelon concoction for me last night.

Regarding other reviews, I understand that everyone's experience can be different. However, labeling the place as 'too hipster' seems like it's coming from someone who still feels bitter from their high school days. Additionally, personally attacking the owner is uncalled for and inappropriate in a review. We should appreciate that we don't have someone constantly scrutinizing and attacking our own motivations. I appreciate what Burger Up is striving to achieve and their choice of hiring diverse individuals representative of our Nashville community. If you're looking for a wait staff that doesn't include musicians and dresses exactly like you, then perhaps you're in the wrong town.

input: I am not an indian food type of person but this place lives up to the hype. When you go, just let Hassan make something for you, don't try and overwhelm yourself with the different options. Make sure to get a chaat and a lassi as the two really complement one another.
Rewrite this for me: Although I typically don't enjoy Indian cuisine, I have to admit that this place definitely lives up to its reputation. Instead of getting overwhelmed by the numerous options, I highly recommend letting Hassan surprise you with his choices. input:
Excellent food, good service, great location. 

My wife had shrimp and grits, I had the barbecued shrimp -- both were outstanding. The appetizers were good. The bread pudding was a tad dry in the city that is supposed to be the mother lode of bread pudding. 

Mr. B came close to snagging the fifth star but the service could have been more attentive and the place is freezing - - in July in New Orleans. Wear long sleeves or bring a jacket.
Rewrite this for me: The food at this establishment is top-notch, with excellent flavors and a wide range of options. The service is generally good, although there is room for improvement in terms of attentiveness. The location is ideal, offering a great atmosphere. However, it is worth noting that the bread pudding, despite being in a city known for it, was slightly dry. Additionally, the temperature inside the restaurant was quite chilly, especially considering it was July in New Orleans. It is advisable to come prepared with long sleeves or a jacket. Overall, while almost deserving of a perfect rating, there are a few areas that could be improved upon.

input:

input: Quite possibly the perfect business model to fail if it wasn't for a sequestered clientel?  We visit New Orleans often, and it is an activity of ours to bet on how many beers or ingredients they are out of.  Bartenders rude and swearing. It's almost comical, we sit and listen to patrons asking for draft beers and mixed drinks and getting responses "can't do that". Rewrite this for me: If it weren't for a loyal clientele, this business model would undoubtedly be destined for failure. It's truly disheartening to witness such a wasted opportunity.

input: We had a mixed experience at Mr. B's.  We started at the bar for drinks and a starter due to table wait. Bar was nice for a busy night. Our table was ready early so the bar staff transferred our starter to the table and things went down hill quickly. Starters were delivered and then we were ignored for over 45 minutes. No drinks, water etc. Finally a waiter in another section took out order. We ordered BBQ shrimp (best thing on our table), rabbit and wood plank grilled fish. Fish was a very small piece and not worth the $$$. Rabbit was good! Hit and miss service ruined the experience.
Rewrite this for me: Our experience at Mr. B's was a mixed one. We initially started at the bar for drinks and a starter due to having to wait for a table. The bar was quite pleasant considering how busy the night was. Surprisingly, our table was ready earlier than expected, so the bar staff kindly transferred our starter to our table. However, things quickly went downhill from there. After our starters were delivered, we were completely ignored for over 45 minutes. We were not offered any drinks or even water. Eventually, a waiter from a different section noticed our plight and took our order. We tried the BBQ shrimp, which was the highlight of our meal, but unfortunately, the wood plank grilled fish was disappointingly small and not worth the price. On the other hand, the rabbit dish was delicious. Inconsistent service really dampened our overall experience.

input:
This place is so cute. The interior is adorable and casual. There's some small booths and chairs and tables for hanging out and enjoying your food/drinks. It's all so clean, too, which is a huge plus.
There's a little section with baked goods, some Asian and some more American. They have mostly Vietnamese food, but I also saw some other types of food (e.g bulgogi).
I came in with two friends and the woman who helped us was really personable and friendly. We ordered banh mi and boba tea, and sat down waiting for our food to be brought to us. The banh mi was really yummy, especially the bread. I had boba milk tea, which was as good as any milk tea I've had before. 
They have a drink card which you can get stamped to receive a free tenth drink. Definitely an incentive to return. Also, their hours are awesome, which is a huge plus.
Rewrite this for me:
This place is absolutely adorable. The interior has a charming and relaxed atmosphere, with small booths and a variety of chairs and tables where you can enjoy your food and drinks. The cleanliness of the place is also worth mentioning, as it adds to the overall appeal.

I noticed a cute corner dedicated to baked goods, featuring both Asian and American options. While they mainly serve Vietnamese cuisine, I was pleasantly surprised to see other types of food, such as bulgogi, on the menu.

When I visited with two friends, we were greeted by a very friendly and personable woman who took our orders. We opted for the banh mi and boba tea, and sat down while waiting for our food to be served. The banh mi was incredibly delicious, especially the bread. As for the boba milk tea, it matched the quality of any milk tea I've tasted before.

One thing that caught my attention was their drink card, which you can get stamped each time you make a purchase. After collecting nine stamps, you can enjoy a free drink, which is definitely a great incentive to return. Additionally, their convenient hours of operation add another positive aspect to the experience.

input: This is the best Italian food I've ever had. Very small elegant restaurant, entrees were really good and very tasty cheesecake. To top it off, the entire staff was super friendly. Highly recommended for date night.

input:
This is my favourite place to get fish tacos! It's all I ever order, along with the occasional queso or beans which are also delicious. My friend was visiting from out of town and he ordered the beef taco and chicken fajitas and thought they were pretty average. However, he agreed that the fish tacos were amazing. Rewrite this for me: My preferred spot to indulge in fish tacos happens to be this place! Every time I visit, I can't resist ordering my all-time favorite, along with occasionally trying their delightful queso or beans. Recently, my out-of-town friend came along and decided to try the beef taco and chicken fajitas, but found them to be average. However, we both agreed that the fish tacos were absolutely incredible. input: Replaced a dive watch battery in less than 5 minutes for a very reasonable fee.  Prompt, friendly service.  Plenty of staff.  Convenient location.
Rewrite this for me: In just under 5 minutes, the battery of my dive watch was efficiently replaced at a very fair cost. The service provided was not only prompt and friendly but also had an abundance of staff members available. Moreover, the location was conveniently situated.

input:
Stopped here last week while in the area from Burbank. Had read about it on Trip Advisor. It is in a great location, quiet, peaceful and cool under the shade of the big old trees. For its location and it being noon on a Thursday we were surprised to find there was literally only one table open when we walked in. Food is served pretty quick though so it didn't seem anyone was really waiting. 
Based on reviews we had read, my hubby had the tri-tip sandwich. I ordered the buffalo burger. I have to say that was one of the best burgers I have ever had in my life. As usual, we traded tastes of our orders. My hubby was so jealous of my buffalo burger and I heard about it several more times throughout the day, that he should've got the burger. The tri-tip was quite dry, and it was literally just the meat on bread, big bread.  The horseradish sauce (served on the side) was very tasty though.
For the tri-tip, I give a 3, hubby gives a 4. We both give the buffalo burger a definite 5++.

Either way, worth checking out if you want something with a unique atmosphere and that is away from town but not a long drive. Very peaceful.
Rewrite this for me:
I stopped by here last week while in the Burbank area. I had heard about it on Trip Advisor and was intrigued. The location is fantastic, surrounded by big old trees that provide a peaceful and cool ambiance. Despite it being noon on a Thursday, I was surprised to find only one table available when we arrived. However, the food was served quickly, so it didn't seem like there was much of a wait.

Based on the reviews we had read, my husband went for the tri-tip sandwich while I decided to try the buffalo burger. I must say, the buffalo burger was hands down one of the best burgers I have ever had. We swapped bites of our meals, and my husband couldn't help but feel jealous of my delicious choice. He even mentioned it several times throughout the day, admitting he should have gone for the burger. On the other hand, the tri-tip sandwich was quite dry and lacked any substantial toppings. It was basically just a piece of meat on a large piece of bread. The horseradish sauce served on the side, however, was incredibly tasty.

Overall, I would rate the tri-tip sandwich a 3, while my husband would give it a 4. As for the buffalo burger, it unquestionably deserves a perfect score of 5++ from both of us.

Regardless, I highly recommend checking this place out if you're looking for a unique atmosphere away from the busy town, but still within a short driving distance. It offers a peaceful and tranquil setting that is definitely worth experiencing.

input:
I have frequented the Mad Mex, University City location for years.  I was pleased to see this new location which is closer to my home and I don't have to deal with the obnoxious students.  I have been here for Happy Hour and just for dinner at another time.  It has been busy both times and it seems that the staff need to be trained a little more in chaos and crowd management.  The best deals are during Happy Hour - the $3, $5 & $7 Margarita's.  I also believe wings are 1/2 off.  My friends seemed to enjoy their orders of Burritos, Gaucamole and enchiladas.  

The food is average and for the price of drinks - it would be a great place to hang if the service improves.

While the food itself is average, the drinks are reasonably priced. If the service improves, it would be the perfect spot to hang out.

input:
I brought my boyfriend here on a Saturday for a tour and beer sampling since Yuengling is one of his favorite beers. We never knew it was so close!

Be sure to look on their website for tour times before going and read the FAQ's. 
- First note: There were many people wearing flip flops on our tours vs. the insisted closed toe shoe policy, but that could be because of the next note.
- Second note: There is no production/brewing on Saturdays so the brewery is quiet and empty.

We looked around the main waiting/lobby area and gift shop waiting for our 12p tour to begin.  We had quite a large group, which had to split into two smaller ones. The tour lasted about 40 minutes, starting with a ten minute video of the history of Yuengling and the rise to present day. Next, the guide takes you out to the brewery, and into the kettle room, around through the lab, the bottle line, and the holding tanks. The tour was informative and hands on. Our guide was informative and knew quite a lot about the history and brewing process. She did a great job!

Once done, you loop back into the lobby where the tasting room is and it's drinks galore. The BEST PART? FREE. Tips are encouraged! ;)
We tried the Premium Lager, Lager, and Black and Tan. Sadly they were out of the Lord Chesterfield this day and the Premium Light is not available here in FL.

Overall, a great tour and I will be revisitng with my parents when they are in town!
Rewrite this for me:
On a Saturday, I decided to treat my boyfriend to a tour and beer sampling at Yuengling, as it happens to be one of his favorite beer brands. Much to our surprise, we discovered that this brewery is actually located quite close to us!

Before heading over, make sure to check their website for tour times and read through the FAQs. I just wanted to note that during our visit, we noticed that despite the closed-toe shoe policy, many people were wearing flip flops on the tour, but that may be due to the next observation.

Keep in mind that there is no production or brewing happening on Saturdays, so the brewery tends to be quiet and empty.

Upon arrival, we explored the main waiting area, lobby, and gift shop while waiting for our 12p tour to start. Since we had a large group, we were split into two smaller groups. The tour duration was approximately 40 minutes, which began with a ten-minute video about the history of Yuengling and its journey to the present day. Following that, our guide led us through various sections of the brewery, including the kettle room, lab, bottle line, and holding tanks. The tour was quite informative and interactive. Our guide was knowledgeable and shared fascinating details about the brewing process and the brewery's rich history. She did a fantastic job!

After the tour, we returned to the lobby, where the tasting room was located. This was definitely the highlight of the experience! And the best part? The samples were completely free, although it's encouraged to leave a tip. We had the opportunity to try the Premium Lager, Lager, and Black and Tan. Unfortunately, they were out of the Lord Chesterfield that day, and the Premium Light beer is not available in Florida.

Overall, it was an excellent tour, and I'm already planning to revisit with my parents when they come to town!

input:
Really disappointed. I've been to the Marathon at 18/Spruce and had excellent service, drinks and food. Thought that would transfer to this location - not at all.

To sum it up, our server was extremely energetic, but not in a good way. More like a frantic energy. I was there to enjoy a few drinks and dinner with a friend who was visiting (AKA looking to spend money AKA you will get a larger tip if you let us stay longer) and we were rushed out. Server brought boxes for food we were still eating, without asking if we wanted them. A few minutes later he physically put the food in the boxes at the tableside while mumbling something like "I don't like food sitting on the table." .....we didn't even want to take it home. Next, when we said we were having another friend join for another round or two of drinks he told us we couldn't stay at the booth we were at and we needed to go to the bar. What? I point blank asked him if he was kicking us out of the booth and he said "yes!" energetically. There was no one waiting for tables and there were numerous open tables/booths around the restaurant. I felt extremely uncomfortable and wanted to leave immediately. Our friend joined after all this happened, and when the server came over to ask if they wanted a drink, he seemed surprised when we told him we were just going to leave. YOU LITERALLY just told us we couldn't sit at this table any longer!! We then left.

I worked in restaurants for a long time and I'm pretty easy to please when it comes to restaurant service. I was not pleased at all during this visit.

On another note, the food was not that great.

input: We arrived for lunch at 12p on a Friday - wasn't busy at all. It took FOREVER to get anything. input: Walked by this place and decided to check it out. Great beer and burger place, made even better knowing many things were organic. You can order from the menu, or create your own burger. Additionally, they featured a rotating assortment of beers and special offerings. The ambiance was pleasant, complemented by the amiable and accommodating staff. Should you desire a side of fries alongside your burger, please be aware that it is not included in the burger order and must be requested separately. Fear not, for they also offer appetizing sandwiches and salads for patrons seeking an alternative to the traditional burger experience. Furthermore, vegetarians need not fret, as this establishment proudly provides vegetarian-friendly options as well.

 service not so great sat at the bar did not really care for a bartender tried it again second time bartender was really rude I would never go back there  or Recommend it to anyone

input:
I visited Jake's for the first time after learning that the small diner I used to go to in Delaware as a kid had become a franchise. I was so excited to experience the delicious burgers and fries that I craved as a kid.

I walked into the establishment and was frankly unimpressed by the ambiance. The restaurant was moderately clean and very open. The menu actually reminded my of a Five Guys. You get to choose your own toppings (all free) to put on 1, 2, or 3 patties.

I ordered the regular cheeseburger with a ton of toppings and a regular size french fry to share with my boyfriend. The burgers were delicious. The bread was soft and tasty and the burgers were succulent and juicy. The fries were disappointing. McDonalds fries taste better and usually aren't even as cold as Jake's were.

Man oh man, Jake's. I'll go back for the burgers, maybe, but I definitely will stick to the original location for a better experience.
Rewrite this for me:
After learning that the small diner I used to frequent in Delaware as a child had expanded into a franchise called Jake's, I decided to pay them a visit. I was eagerly anticipating the opportunity to relish in the mouthwatering burgers and fries that I had always yearned for during my childhood.

As I stepped foot into the establishment, I couldn't help but feel underwhelmed by the overall ambiance. The restaurant appeared moderately clean and had a spacious layout. Interestingly enough, the menu reminded me of the offerings at Five Guys, as it allowed customers to freely select their desired toppings to be piled onto one, two, or three succulent patties.

Opting for a regular cheeseburger with an abundance of toppings, I also ordered a regular-sized french fry to share with my boyfriend. The burgers proved to be nothing short of delightful. The bread was soft and flavorful, perfectly complementing the juicy and mouthwatering patties. However, the fries left much to be desired. In comparison to the tastiness of McDonald's fries, Jake's fell short and were disappointingly cold.

Although I may consider returning to Jake's for their delicious burgers, I firmly believe that the original location holds a superior experience overall.

input: This place was cute and was in a great location!  It is one block up from the beach and wharf, two blocks over from State Street.  Parking was convenient, and our room was a King overlooking the courtyard and spa on the ground floor.  If there were people in the spa, they could be heard, but the noise didn't bother since the spa closed at 9pm.  The room was clean with a nice couch to lounge on, a refrigerator, a nice fireplace, ample closet and counter space, and a nice bathroom.  The wine and cheese at 5 was a nice touch as well.  Although this place didn't have a lot of extras, it was a pleasant stay, friendly and helpful staff, a good price, perfect location, and suited our needs just fine for a place in Santa Barbara.  My only complaint was that the room got a little stuffy, but was fine once we opened the windows and used the ceiling fan to air it out.  Would consider staying here again.
Rewrite this for me: The location of this place was fantastic, just one block away from the beach and wharf, and two blocks over from State Street. It was also really cute. Even though we could hear people in the spa, it wasn't a bother since it closed at 9pm. The room itself was clean and had a comfortable couch, a refrigerator, a lovely fireplace, plenty of closet and counter space, and a nice bathroom. The wine and cheese at 5pm was a nice added touch. The only downside was that the room could get a bit stuffy, but opening the windows and using the ceiling fan resolved that issue. We would definitely consider staying here again.

input:
I've been to Mirna's about four times over the past few years and never been disappointed. The portions are HUGE, especially for the modest price tag. Do yourself a favor and get a pasta dish, I can assure you that you'll be glad you did. I've had fish there too, which wasn't bad by any means, but the pasta plates are definitely their specialty. A couple of the times I've been there they treated us to free hummus and pita, which is always a plus. BYOB!

Only knock on the place is that it's pretty small, so make sure to call ahead to reserve a table or check for a wait.
Rewrite this for me: I have visited Mirna's approximately four times in the past few years, and every visit has been nothing short of satisfying. The portion sizes are exceptionally generous, especially considering the reasonable prices. If you want to treat yourself, I highly recommend trying their pasta dishes - you won't regret it. While their fish option isn't bad, it's clear that their expertise lies in creating delectable pasta plates. On a couple of occasions, they even surprised us with complimentary servings of hummus and pita, which was a delightful bonus. It's worth noting that Mirna's is a small establishment, so it's advisable to call ahead and reserve a table or inquire about potential waiting times. Additionally, don't forget that you can bring your own beverages.

input: While I generally support independent restaurants over chain places,I still don't buy into the overpriced center city Phila hype. The bus help was a bit out of sync with the waiter,as they were asking us if we were done with our plates just as the waiter was telling us the desserts,and as the Philly standard the bathroom was a bit small to accomodate the size of the place.
Rewrite this for me: Although I generally prefer independent restaurants to chain establishments, I am not convinced by the inflated prices often associated with downtown Philadelphia. Surprisingly, this particular place was more spacious compared to the cramped eateries we typically choose to celebrate my mother-in-law's birthday in South Philly. However, the prices were shockingly high and not in line with what we saw on the online menu. input:

I was extremely impressed with this place, especially the menu which was absolutely amazing. We decided to order the fruit bruschetta, and oh boy, it was such an awesome and unique idea. We also tried the Popeye skillet and the Roadhouse sandwich, both of which were delicious. The food here is fantastic, and they offer some really creative options. 

However, there are a couple of areas that could use improvement. Firstly, it was absolutely freezing inside the restaurant. It was even so cold that every woman present had to wear a sweater in the middle of July. Additionally, the ambiance was lacking a bit. It wouldn't take much effort to fix this issue with some decent background music and better lighting. The overhead office lighting felt dull, but on the bright side, they did have large windows which added a positive touch. 

In terms of customer service, it was good but not outstanding. It felt a bit disconnected, although I will take into consideration that it was a holiday weekend. Despite these minor drawbacks, I still think this place is a keeper. I will definitely be coming back!
