input:
I don't know how I lucked out with having this taqueria in our neighborhood, but this is the best Mexican food you'll get in New Orleans.

We discovered Taqueria Guerrero after finding that burrito joint down the street was packed, had a line wrapping around the buidling (you know which one!).

After finding street parking near the mattress store, we plopped down and ordered the 3-taco plate (al pastor, mmmm) with beans and rice on the side and a burrito (barbocoa). I am a creature of habit and order the same tacos, but the bf has ventured out to get other dishes such as the fajita plate or the really spicy shrimp (camarones del diablo?). All very tasty.

The rest is history. It's embarrassing how often I suggest this place when we want to go out/get take out.
Rewrite this for me:
I can't believe how lucky we are to have Taqueria Guerrero in our neighborhood. Hands down, it's the best Mexican food you'll find in New Orleans.

We stumbled upon this gem after realizing that the popular burrito joint down the street was overflowing with customers (you know the one!). After finding a spot to park near the mattress store, we settled in and decided to go for the 3-taco plate (the al pastor is heavenly) with a side of beans and rice, along with a burrito (barbacoa). I usually stick to my tried and true tacos, but my boyfriend likes to explore and has ventured into other dishes like the fajita plate or the incredibly spicy shrimp (camarones del diablo?). They've all been incredibly delicious.

Since then, there's no denying that Taqueria Guerrero has become our go-to spot for dining out or grabbing takeout. I can't help but suggest it every time we're looking for somewhere to eat. It's a bit embarrassing, really.

input:
Came here with a group of 15 people on a Tuesday night. We had reserved a space in advance. 
While the food was good, what was lacking was good service and cleanliness. We sat down at our table and it was sticky, and there was a dirty and also sticky fork still on it...so the assumption was that the table simply hadn't been wiped down all the way. Yuck. 
We ordered and the food took a fair amount of time, understandable because of such a large party. Problem was, when the food came out, no server knew what we'd individually ordered, so it became a huge mix up with people eating others' food. 
I ordered the pork belly tacos which had a great caramelization on the outside and tender inside. I also ordered the spicy beef pho, which was perfectly balanced with flavor after adding the accompanying bean sprouts and limes. 
The wait for the check and processing payment was long and arduous, a problem again because we had a Lyft driver waiting outside for us. 
All in all, go for the food, not for the service.
Rewrite this for me:
I arrived at the restaurant with a group of 15 people on a Tuesday night. We had made a reservation in advance. While the food was enjoyable, we were disappointed by the lack of good service and cleanliness. When we sat down, our table was sticky and there was a dirty fork left on it, indicating it had not been properly wiped down. It was quite unpleasant. 
We placed our orders and had to wait a considerable amount of time, which was understandable given the size of our party. However, when the food arrived, the servers seemed confused about who ordered what, resulting in a mix-up and people eating the wrong dishes. 
I personally ordered the pork belly tacos, which had a delightful caramelization on the outside and a tender interior. I also tried the spicy beef pho, which was well-balanced in flavor, especially after adding the provided bean sprouts and limes. 
The process of receiving the check and paying took a long time, causing inconvenience since we had a Lyft driver waiting for us outside. 
Overall, I would recommend visiting this restaurant for the food itself, but not for the service.

input: Unfortunately, I'm NOT happy after coming to this salon yet again. I got a message from the owner saying he'd like to have me come in to receive a FREE service because they previously ruined my hair. So, I thought since he's the owner my hair would turn out good but I was wrong. I'm really unhappy with this whole experience. I showed him multiple photos on google of what I wanted done to my hair which was a lot of blonde. I told him I do not want any ORANGE in my hair as I wanted a "white blonde". He said you won't have any orange in your hair. I have a message from him the OWNER saying I would receive a FREE service if I deleted my previous review. He should of NEVER offered a free service if it wasn't really free! So, I said how much because I thought I was getting my hair done for free. He said since your hair is long and thick you'll have to pay for the hair color and "medicine" but he won't charge me for his time. I said ok how much he said $80. He said it would cost me $180 if he didn't give me a discount which is very pricey. He put a lot of highlights on my hair and worked quickly as he seemed to want to rush on my hair which I do not like. My hair is important to me, I don't want my hair to fall out. He said this medicine he's gonna put on my hair is $50 for a treatment and that I needed it because of the blonde going on my hair which I know any coloring is damaging and blonde is very damaging but he said he charges everyone who gets hair color for this so called medicine which they mix into the color you dye your hair. You can purchase the entire set online (3 bottles) for $75 which is supposed to give you like 15 applications so he's definitely charging a lot of money! He only put No.1 on my hair and not No.2 or No.3. He also had a lady (the receptionist) wash out my hair? Ok, even though she was nice why would he have her do that when she said she knows nothing about hair because I asked if she's styling my hair and she said she doesn't do hair and I wouldn't want her to do my hair. As I was waiting there was a lady next to me, she got her hair cut and a perm. She was done but she wasn't happy, she told the lady she didn't like the hair cut and she had her style it more and trim off a little more but the lady still wasn't happy. The girl told the client when she washes her hair it will be better.. um how? I know she left very unhappy! Also the lady behind me was getting her hair cut and when he (the owner) was done cutting her hair she looked in the mirror and wanted it different and styled different so that made me have to wait longer but 2 clients were not happy and also myself. That's not a good look TJ nail and spa! I had a towel on my head and waited about 30 mins just to get my hair blow dried because he was cutting another clients hair. I seen orange roots, I was mad!!! He finally came over and I said I don't like the orange color on my roots, can you put a toner on my hair and he said it's not orange it's the lighting. The lighting?! It wasn't the lighting! He proceeds to blow dry hair and then starts straighten it without asking me if I wanted it straightened or curled, you are supposed to pick how you want your hair styled. At that point I knew my hair wasn't what I wanted and it wasn't gonna be fixed even if I wanted it too. I just sat there in the hair, mad and yet again very disappointed! I looked in the mirror and seen my hair damaged and brittle, orange and brassy and not even close to what I wanted. There goes my money down the drain, yet again. I will not be back to get my hair ruined and he made me delete my previous review which was also 0-1 stars before I left his salon but I had to write this one, this is real, this is honest, beware of getting your hair completely ruined and nothing close to what you want! Like I said I showed the OWNER multiple photos and I stated I did NOT want any orange on my hair but I did have orange on my hair, I didn't get what I wanted like he said, he said he doesn't mess up, he's been doing hair for years. As a salon owner I think he should take the time to really do what the client wants and achieve what the client wants done to their hair, if the workersowner would do that then there shouldn't be any bad reviews but there is so that shows you they do not care, not even the owner cares. They just want to rush and get done to get paid, they don't care if the customer is happy or not. There are more bad reviews from people going to this salon and having horrible experiences but he is bribing people to delete their bad reviews because he told me the bad reviews is hurting his business which is why people do reviews, to let people know this place is awesome or this place is horrible, beware, stay away. I do reviews to let people know the good, the bad and the ugly. I do reviews anywhere and I'm always 100% honest. So, if bad reviews hurt his business that is all on him and his employees not me or anyone else.
Rewrite this for me:
Regrettably, I am still dissatisfied with my experience at this salon. Despite receiving a message from the owner offering a free service to rectify a previous hair mishap, I had high hopes that my hair would turn out well under his care. However, I was mistaken. This entire experience has left me feeling extremely unhappy.

During my consultation with the owner, I showed him numerous pictures from Google of the blonde hair color I desired. I made it clear that I did not want any hints of orange; my goal was to achieve a "white blonde" look. He assured me that there would be no orange in my hair. Additionally, the owner promised me a free service in exchange for deleting my previous negative review. It turns out this "free" service was not truly free. When I inquired about the cost, he informed me that I would have to pay for the hair color and a hair treatment, but he would not charge for his time. He quoted me $80, which is still quite steep considering I thought I would be getting the service for free. He mentioned that without the discount, the total would have been $180, an exorbitant price.

As the owner worked on my hair, I noticed that he applied a significant number of highlights and appeared to rush through the process, which was not to my liking. My hair is important to me, and I don't want it to suffer any damage. He claimed that the hair treatment he applied, costing $50, was necessary due to the damaging effects of blonde coloring. However, I know that any coloring process is harmful to the hair, and blonde coloring especially so. Despite this, he insisted that everyone who receives hair color must pay for this so-called "medicine" to be mixed into the dye. Interestingly, the entire three-bottle set of this product can be purchased online for $75, offering around 15 applications. It is clear that he is charging a significant amount for this treatment. Furthermore, he only applied No.1 of the product and skipped No.2 and No.3. Additionally, to my surprise, the owner had the receptionist wash out my hair. While the receptionist was friendly, I found it odd that she had no knowledge of hair care, which she confirmed when I asked if she would also be styling my hair. It was clear to me that I did not want her touching my hair in any way.

During my wait, I observed two other clients expressing dissatisfaction with their haircuts. One individual had her hair cut and permed, yet she was unhappy with the outcome. She requested further styling and trimming, but even after these adjustments, she remained dissatisfied. The receptionist informed her that the hair would look better after washing, which seemed unlikely. It was evident that she left the salon feeling very unhappy. Similarly, the individual seated next to me had her hair cut, but upon seeing the final result in the mirror, she requested a different style and further styling. This led to me waiting even longer, as two clients, in addition to myself, were not pleased with their hair outcomes. This does not reflect well on TJ Nail and Spa.

After waiting with a towel on my head for approximately 30 minutes, I finally received a blow dry since the owner was occupied cutting another client's hair. To my dismay, I noticed orange roots. I was furious! When the owner finally approached me, I expressed my dissatisfaction with the orange color and requested a toner be applied. However, he dismissed my concerns, attributing the color to the lighting. It was clear to me that the lighting was not at fault. He proceeded to blow dry my hair without asking if I preferred it straightened or curled, which goes against the standard practice of allowing the client to choose their desired hairstyle. At that moment, I knew that my hair would not turn out as I had hoped, and there was no chance of it being fixed, even if I desired it.

I sat in the salon chair, frustrated and deeply disappointed. When I looked in the mirror, I saw damaged, brittle, orange, and brassy hair that was nowhere near what I had envisioned. It felt like a waste of my money yet again. I have no intention of returning to this salon to have my hair ruined once more. The owner coerced me into deleting my previous review, which had already given the salon a low rating of 0-1 star. However, I felt compelled to share this honest account of my experience. I want to warn others about the possibility of having their hair completely botched and ending up with a result far from what they desired. As I mentioned earlier, I showed the owner multiple photos and explicitly stated that I did not want any orange in my hair, yet I ended up with orange anyway. He had assured me that he never makes mistakes and has years of experience in the industry. As a salon owner, it is crucial that he takes the time to understand and fulfill his clients' desires for their hair. If all the employees, including the owner, were attentive to achieving customer satisfaction, there would be no reason for such negative reviews. However, it is clear that they do not care; not even the owner demonstrates concern. It appears that their main focus is rushing to complete services in order to get paid, without considering whether the customer is content or not. Numerous other negative reviews from dissatisfied customers further emphasize the poor quality of this salon. The owner is attempting to bribe individuals into removing their negative reviews because he claims that such reviews harm his business. However, it is important to remember that people write reviews to inform others about their experiences, both positive and negative. Therefore, if his business suffers as a result, it is solely due to him and his staff, not myself or others who share their genuine opinions through reviews.

input:
I am so glad we had our wedding here!!! I cannot say enough what a pleasure it was to work with Breanna, the venue manager and Eli, the food and beverage director. Our wedding here was a destination wedding, so we were very concerned about making sure all of our family and friends that travelled a long way to get to our wedding had a good time. Being a couple straight out of grad school, we were also very concerned with keeping the cost manageable. Everything worked out on all accounts! 

We first picked the venue for two reasons: the price was right and the venue is GORGEOUS. The pricing was very straightforward, which we really appreciated, and when looking at other options in the Santa Barbara area, the Riviera mansion was pretty comparable with other venues which are not all inclusive (ones where you have to find your own caterer, rent linens, etc etc). Planning a wedding without a coordinator and from across the country, it was also definitely worth it for us to go with a venue that minimized the amount of details we would have to think about.

The looks and layout of the place are what sold us though. With people coming from the east coast and middle of the country, we wanted something that would really showcase Santa Barbara's cool architecture and vibe. The mansion is exactly that.  The layout is also pretty perfect for a multigenerational wedding. We were able to enjoy the California weather for our ceremony and cocktail hour outside, then go inside for dinner, avoiding the cooler night air. Later, we could turn up the party in the bar/dance floor area, while the older folks talked and relaxed on the couches in the living room. It really has something for everyone.

What I didn't realize when we picked it was how absolutely awesome all the staff would be to work with. When we did our walkthrough a couple of days before the wedding, Breanna and Eli paid attention to every detail and made sure we were taken care of, as they did the day of the wedding too. Eli was incredibly attentive and easy to work with! The attention to bartending at the Riviera Mansion deserves a paragraph of its own. Five stars all around. It was absolutely a joy to have our wedding here.

input:
Yeah, I know what you're thinking. One Wawa store is pretty much the same as another, so why even bother writing a review? But I think we have a winner here.

When this Wawa store opened for business, gas prices at gas stations all along Concord Pike fell by 30 cents per gallon just to compete with them. Sure, this Wawa store could've followed the general pricing in the area and lowered prices just a few cents, keeping the bulk of the profit. But no, they'll have none of that. I love a store that is on the side of my wallet!

Secondly, I love the automatic start/stop digital air pump. So far, I've only seen that at BJ's Wholesale and Sheetz. It's a snap to use and I get the exact tire pressure every time.

As for service, they seem nice and relatively efficient. The internal layout of the store is the new style that I first saw in Newark. Having separate non-cigarette cashier lines may speed things up in peak periods, although I've never been there during the day, so I wouldn't know.

input:
For a seafood restaurant at the edge of pear expectations should be set high. My wife and I have come here 3 times now and ordered different plates off the menu each time. This last time we ordered cioppino, clam chowder, and a crab salad sandwich;
*Good - clam chowder (excellent flavor and consistency) would order again.
*Not great - cioppino (lacked flavor & a variety of sea food/lack there of) would not order again
*Pass - crab salad sandwich (lacked flavor, mayo was overpowering, crab flavor was almost non-existent, side of onion rings too greasy) - would not order again 
The overall experience is okay, better if seated outside right on the pear overlooking the ocean, inside is very small. Service is good but be prepared to wait a bit to be seated. 
Is it worth a visit? Yes, but be selective of what you order as the menu tends to be a hit and miss.
Rewrite this for me:
Expectations should be set high for a seafood restaurant located at the edge of the pear. My wife and I have dined here on three separate occasions, trying different dishes each time. During our most recent visit, we ordered cioppino, clam chowder, and a crab salad sandwich.

The clam chowder was good, with excellent flavor and consistency. I would definitely order it again. However, the cioppino was disappointing as it lacked flavor and variety in terms of seafood. I would not order it again. The crab salad sandwich was a pass for us, as it lacked flavor, had an overpowering mayo taste, and the crab flavor was almost non-existent. Additionally, the side of onion rings that came with it were overly greasy. We would not order this dish again.

Overall, our experience at the restaurant was okay. It is better if you can secure a seat outside, right on the pear with a view of the ocean. The inside is quite small. The service we received was good, but be prepared to wait a bit to be seated.

Is it worth visiting? Yes, but it is important to be selective with your order as the menu tends to be hit or miss.

input: Chef Kevin Sbraga knows fried chicken. My first exposure to his succulent birds was the hot chicken at The Fat Ham. Lo and behold, his lavender honey fried chicken tops its spicy cousin. The chicken is brined in buttermilk, dredged in seasoned flour and sits for ten minutes. It's then coated with a second round of flour and dropped into the fryer. The chicken (breast, wing, thigh, drumstick) is drizzled with lavender honey and sprinkled with salt and ground pink peppercorns. It comes with a buttermilk biscuit, whipped honey-thyme butter, and red bliss potato salad. It is some of the best fried chicken I've eaten in a long time. Crunchy, crispy coating on the outside with a juicy, moist inside. The sweet honey glaze is truly outstanding and finger lickin' good. The biscuit is awesome. I would definitely order this dish again and again. I got the salty but delicious fried smelts with chili pepper aioli as an appetizer. My friend Chris W got the filet mignon and butter poached king crab surf and turf. For dessert, I had a slice of salted pecan pie and he had the ice cream sundae. Every dish at Juniper Commons was top-notch. Chef Sbraga does it again!
Rewrite this for me: Chef Kevin Sbraga is a master of fried chicken. My first taste of his delectable poultry was at The Fat Ham, where the hot chicken impressed me. However, his lavender honey fried chicken surpasses even its spicy counterpart. The chicken undergoes a brining process in buttermilk, followed by dredging in seasoned flour and a ten-minute resting period. It is then coated with another layer of flour and fried to perfection. The chicken includes breast, wing, thigh, and drumstick, which are then drizzled with lavender honey and sprinkled with salt and ground pink peppercorns. Accompanied by a buttermilk biscuit, whipped honey-thyme butter, and red bliss potato salad, this dish is truly one of the best fried chicken offerings I've had in a long time. The exterior is wonderfully crunchy and crispy, while the inside remains juicy and moist. The honey glaze adds a delightful sweetness that is finger-lickin' good. The biscuit is also exceptional, leaving me eager to order this dish repeatedly. As an appetizer, I opted for the salty yet delicious fried smelts with chili pepper aioli. Meanwhile, my friend Chris W chose the filet mignon and butter-poached king crab surf and turf. For dessert, I savored a slice of salted pecan pie, while my friend indulged in the ice cream sundae. Every dish at Juniper Commons was outstanding, showcasing Chef Sbraga's excellence once again!

input:
I really wanted to like Casselli's, but it wasn't in the cards. Maybe I just caught them on a bad night, but I didn't really enjoy much about my visit. The waiter was very unpleasant - was banging down the plates and glasses on the table when he delivered them. Maybe he was having a bad day, but I still would have expected better. 

We had mixed experiences with the food. Mine and our friends' was OK, but my wife's baked ravioli would have been more use to a hockey team for use as pucks. They were really overdone - woefully overdone. 

The worst part was that our table was next to the opera singer guy. He was singing extremely loudly and it was nigh impossible to maintain a conversation - especially coupled with how close we were to the table next to us and their attempts to speak over Opera Guy.

Part of me wants to give them another chance (since I hate writing bad reviews) and the other part is annoyed over the waiter's attitude. I probably will not go back. There are so many good Italian restaurants worth visiting that the opportunity cost of returning to Casselli's seems too high.

On the upside, they have somewhat convenient parking in the lot behind the restaurant (near the Shawmont School).

Note: cash-only.

The food was a mixed bag. Our friends and I found our meals to be alright, but my wife's baked ravioli was incredibly overcooked - to the point of being useless as hockey pucks. It was a disappointing experience.

The most frustrating part was that our table was situated next to a very loud opera singer. It made it nearly impossible to hold a conversation, especially with the additional noise from the neighboring table attempting to talk over the opera music.

Despite my inclination to give them another chance (as I'm not one to write negative reviews), I find myself bothered by the waiter's attitude. As a result, I don't think I'll be returning. There are plenty of other great Italian restaurants worth trying, and revisiting Casselli's doesn't seem worth the opportunity cost.

On a positive note, they do offer relatively convenient parking in the lot behind the restaurant, near the Shawmont School.

Important to note: Casselli's only accepts cash as a form of payment.

input:
Amazing food!! and  the whole experience is great there every time. I suggest going there with a  group of about 6 people so it doesn't totally break the bank but if you've got the money then who cares! Have fun!

First you enter in and select the wine you would like. The staff is helpful and knowledgeable about their stock. (And if for some reason at the end you didn't  finish your bottle they will cork it back up for you to take.) Then select your cheese platter. Lots of yummy stinky cheese to select  from and prosciutto. I wish they had more cured meats but it's all yummy anyway. You pay for the wine and cheese there. Which in a large group one or two people can take care of this  part. 

Then going to get a seat can be difficult but just be patient. There's outdoor seating that's very nice and always a live band playing. Inside upstairs is nice as well. Once you're all set with your wine and group it's time to order. Go to the window and play your order. Definite things you must get.... the bacon wrapped dates stuffed with chorizo and the goat cheese and mushroom dish....AMAZING! Although everything I've ever had here is great. 

Then just wait for your cheese platter, food and enjoy!
Rewrite this for me:
The food at this place is absolutely incredible! Every time I go, the entire experience is fantastic. I recommend going with around 6 people to keep the cost reasonable, but if you don't mind splurging, go for it! Have a great time!

When you first arrive, choose the wine you want from a great selection. The staff is really helpful and knowledgeable about their wines. And if you don't finish your bottle, they'll cork it for you to take home. Next, select your cheese platter. They have a variety of delicious, aromatic cheeses to choose from, as well as prosciutto. I do wish they had more cured meats, but everything is tasty regardless. You pay for the wine and cheese at this stage, and in a larger group, one or two people can handle the payment.

Finding a table can be a little challenging, but be patient. They have lovely outdoor seating with live music always playing. The upstairs area indoors is also nice. Once you're settled with your wine and group, it's time to order. Head to the counter and place your order. There are a few must-try dishes, like the bacon wrapped dates stuffed with chorizo and the goat cheese and mushroom dish. Both are absolutely amazing! Although, honestly, everything I've ever had here is delicious.

Then, just sit back, relax, and wait for your cheese platter and food to arrive. Enjoy!

input:
I find it hugely ironic that WF is trying to reposition itself as a 'value' food store right now when others (i.e. Trader Joe's up the street) have been doing that for years.  For value, go elsewhere.  For pretty food, lovely store displays and a feeling of smugness, check out Whole Foods.

Despite my snark, I have to admit that it's nice to see an enormous, clean and well stocked yuppie market in Reno finally.  Now that this town has been rated by National Geographic as a top outdoors place to live in, it needs the retail to support that (and I don't mean another REI).  For myself, I'm too cheap to look seriously at this place for my regular shopping needs, but for lunch and the odd stopover, it's awesome.   Beautiful produce, drool inducing cheese selections and a bakery that would break my budget if I bought everything that struck my fancy.

Plus it's proximity to the freeway (for those of us who do our shopping based on distance from the 395 or 80) makes it an ideal stop to/from the airport.
Rewrite this for me:
I find it incredibly ironic that Whole Foods is currently trying to position itself as a 'value' food store, considering that other stores like Trader Joe's have been doing that for years. If you're looking for value, you're better off going elsewhere. However, if you're interested in aesthetically pleasing food, attractive store displays, and a sense of smugness, then Whole Foods is worth checking out.

Despite my sarcastic tone, I have to admit that it's nice to finally have a large, clean, and well-stocked upscale market like Whole Foods in Reno. With National Geographic rating this town as a top destination for outdoor activities, it's important to have retail options that cater to that demographic (and I don't mean another REI). Personally, I find Whole Foods a bit too expensive for my regular shopping needs, but it's a great place to go for a lunch or a quick stopover. They have beautiful produce, an impressive variety of delicious cheeses, and a bakery that could easily break my budget if I indulged in everything that caught my eye.

Additionally, its convenient location near the freeway (which is important for those of us who base our shopping decisions on proximity to the 395 or 80) makes it an ideal place to stop by on our way to or from the airport.

input:
Monthly lunch with my fellow colleagues the other day and the person assigned to get lunch ordered from Fresh and had it delivered. 

My selection was the Chopped Italian salad. The salad consists of mixed greens, salami, smoked turkey, tomato, garbanzo beans and parmesan cheese served with the house vinaigrette. The salad was lacking for me. I think such a salad would be so much better with a few more Italian-esque ingredients in it, perhaps a little more anitpasto like. I know, it's not advertised as antipasto but c'mon....this salad was boring.  Throw in a couple of olives, some artichoke hearts, some sliced pepperoncinis. Maybe my tastebuds were having an off day but the salami wasn't very flavorful either. Charge a couple dollars more for a more inventive salad. Please!

I do want to give them another chance since so many reviews on here are glowing. Maybe I need to stick with a panini or something but I really do love salads for summer lunches.
Rewrite this for me: During our monthly lunch gathering with colleagues, one of them was tasked with ordering our food from Fresh and having it delivered. On this occasion, I decided to go for the Chopped Italian salad. The salad included mixed greens, salami, smoked turkey, tomato, garbanzo beans, and parmesan cheese, served with the house vinaigrette. Unfortunately, I found the salad to be lacking in flavor. Personally, I believe that adding a few more traditional Italian ingredients, like olives, artichoke hearts, and sliced pepperoncinis, would greatly enhance its taste. Additionally, the salami itself didn't have much flavor to offer. I believe that charging a slightly higher price for a more inventive and satisfying salad would be worth it. Despite my disappointment with the salad, I am willing to give them another chance, considering the positive reviews I have come across. Perhaps next time, I should opt for one of their paninis instead, although I generally enjoy having salads for lunch during the summer season.

input:
Great pizza!  The owner Pete is usually there and he's a great guy.  They have lots of fantastic pizzas, but my favorites are the California (white pizza with pieces of breaded chicken cutlet, bacon, and tomatos, and ranch dressing instead of red sauce), Meatlovers (5 meats, but the sausage is the kind that does not have fennel in it, so more points for that), Veggie pizza (they saute the veggies first before they go on the pizza, and instead of using green peppers, they use sweet peppers).  

Unfortunately, the shop was damaged by a fire in the next door laundry mat and they've been closed for a few weeks, but I can't wait for their doors to open again soon. I miss the lunch special, 2 slices and a self serve soda for $3.99.   Best local pizza you'll find in the Hatboro area.

The pizza at this place is amazing! Pete, the owner, is always around and he's a really nice guy. They offer a wide variety of delicious pizzas, but my personal favorites are the California (a white pizza with breaded chicken cutlet, bacon, tomatoes, and ranch dressing instead of red sauce), the Meatlovers (with five different types of meat, and the sausage doesn't contain fennel which is a bonus), and the Veggie pizza (where they sauté the veggies before putting them on the pizza, and they use sweet peppers instead of green peppers).

Unfortunately, there was a fire at the laundromat next door which caused damage to the shop, so they have been closed for a few weeks. However, I am eagerly waiting for them to reopen soon. I really miss their lunch special, which includes two slices of pizza and a self-serve soda for only $3.99. This is hands down the best pizza you can find in the Hatboro area.

input: Buffalo chicken cheese dip is amazing.  Friendly wait staff and prices are reasonable.

input:

input:
If you are going for the food, I would give it 5 stars, but since this is a brewhouse, I only gave it 3. 

I ordered the light flight since we went for lunch and I wasn't looking for a heavy meal. The beer was OK at best. It was bland, a little strange in after taste and uninspired. Light beers dont have to equal tasteless. My boyfriend had a "hoppy beer with citrus undertones". He could taste neither the hops or the citrus  (disclaimer - we are from VT and are used to very hoppy beers!)  

Now the food - that was great. We went at lunch time and was able to get a soup and salad for 8.95. We both had the same thing - Chicken Bruchetta salad and French Onion Soup. The portion was fantastic for a lunch size and the soup really flavorful! 

For a lunch downtown it was great, but I would go for the brews...
Rewrite this for me:
I would give it a 5-star rating if it was solely based on the food quality. However, since this establishment is primarily a brewhouse, I can only give it 3 stars. 

During our lunch visit, I opted for the light flight as I wasn't in the mood for a heavy meal. Sadly, the beer was mediocre at best. It lacked flavor, had a peculiar aftertaste, and overall felt uninspired. Light beers shouldn't have to be tasteless. On the other hand, my boyfriend tried a "hoppy beer with citrus undertones," but couldn't taste either the hops or the citrus. (Disclaimer: We come from Vermont and are accustomed to very hoppy beers!)

However, the food was a different story. We arrived at lunchtime and took advantage of the soup and salad combo for $8.95. We both ordered the Chicken Bruchetta salad and the French Onion Soup - both were exceptional. The lunch-sized portions were generous, and the soup had a delightful burst of flavors.

Overall, this brewhouse is a great spot for a downtown lunch, but I wouldn't specifically recommend it for the brews.

input:

The head chef was nominated for a James Beard Award and it shows in his flavorful and diverse menu choices! The restaurant has both an outdoor and indoor setting with double doors that allow access to both, with a bar around the corner. 

I personally have tried every taco on the menu as well as the appetizers! Each taco uses fresh local ingredients with an option for vegetarians and meat eaters like myself. My two favorites are the mushroom taco and the short rib taco, both have unique and fantastic flavors. But I would recommend trying them all, you will not be disappointed! Overall a great place for lunch or dinner! I will definitely be going back soon!

input: I attended the #welldoneTBO tweet-up at Anthony's Coal Fired Pizza last week and had a great time. The folks at Anthony's were amazing with the customer service. input:
Define the worst Mediterranean food I have ever had.  The hummus appeared to have a good texture, that is the little bit I could see under the ocean of olive oil.  The pita bread was burned- not just over toasted, but black on the majority of the wedges.  I went home and was sick the rest of the evening from the amount of oil it had in it. 

The manager was probably the worst of the experience. He told my gf he would "upgrade her hummus for no charge, because normally it's $1.00" but said it as if he was doing us this huge favor.  He then continued to yell at us from across the restaurant after we sat down  (instead of coming up to our table and actually having a conversation) and says, "please let me know how your food is because that's the only way I can know if we are doing a good job or not is when customers tell me."  But we agreed that the vibe he gave off would not be that of open mindedness and gratitude if we were to say anything about his plate of olive oil, er I mean hummus.  There is also a sign that advertises the "cleanest bathroom in town".... Ehhhh ok, good to know for our next road trip.

input:
This hotel was fantastic. I was in town for a week, working at my company's PA office in Wayne. Great location and easy to get in and out. Hotel staff was very friendly. Room was immaculately cleaned and very spacious for just one person. Kitchenette was fully stocked with dishes, silverware, utensils, a small dishwasher and a full size fridge. Windows surrounding the king size bed were great- lots of natural light. I liked that opting out of housekeeping got me a $5 credit at the restaurant. 

The pool is small but no one was there the two times I went to use the hot tub. The bar has a decent drink selection, although I was bummed they were out of mint and couldn't make a mojito (which was on the drink menu). Burger was okay. Dessert was mediocre (but free with my $5 credit, so nbd). Omelet station was a nice touch in the AM. Coffee frequently had coffee grounds in it/was very weak, but the breakfast spread overall was nice.

Speaking of which, the pool was on the smaller side, but I never had any issues using the hot tub as it was always empty when I visited. The bar had a decent selection of drinks, although I was slightly disappointed to learn that they were out of mint and couldn't make my desired mojito from their drink menu. The burger I tried at the restaurant was okay, but the dessert left something to be desired. Luckily, the dessert was complimentary with my $5 credit, so it wasn't a big deal. The omelet station during breakfast was a nice touch and added a special touch to my mornings.

However, there were a few minor downsides. The coffee often had coffee grounds in it and was on the weak side. Thankfully, the breakfast spread overall was enjoyable and made up for it.

input:

input:
On my first day in New Orleans, I walked to Fair Grinds for a caffeine boost. It was a beautiful afternoon, and a handful of people were scattered around the shop and the outdoor seating area, working on laptops and visiting with friends. 

I ordered a small cold brew with vanilla, easy on the ice. I added a hunk of gluten free zucchini bread (the bread butt; the best part!) to my order and paid with a credit card. They have a fancy touchscreen register that lets you add tip to your card purchase. 

I topped off my drink with whole milk -- which in itself was a real treat. It's so rare to see whole milk at the mixing station! 

Before leaving, I asked what else they had in the way of a GF offering, and the young man behind the counter said "just the zucchini bread." That's a real bummer; the zucchini bread is great but I'd love to have more than one option. 

My drink was smooth and had a perfect flavor. I was happy with my choices. 

If I lived in the neighborhood, I'd be here all the time. I like the hipstery feeling of this place, and everything I've ordered has been delightful.
Rewrite this for me:
During my first day in New Orleans, I strolled over to Fair Grinds seeking a caffeine boost. The weather was splendid, and both the shop and its outdoor seating area were adorned with a few individuals engrossed in work or engaged in conversations with friends.

I decided to order a small cold brew with a touch of vanilla, with the ice kept to a minimum. Alongside my drink, I indulged in a slice of gluten-free zucchini bread (a personal favorite, especially the end piece!). Opting to pay by credit card, I utilized their sophisticated touchscreen register, which conveniently allowed me to include a tip on my purchase.

To enhance my beverage, I complemented it with whole milk – a rare find at the self-serve station! It truly made my experience all the more delightful. Before leaving, I inquired about any other gluten-free options available, only to be informed that they solely had the zucchini bread. While disheartening, as the zucchini bread was fantastic, it would have been splendid to have more than one choice.

The drink itself was flawlessly smooth and possessed an impeccable flavor. I was genuinely content with my selections. If I resided in this neighborhood, this place would undoubtedly become my go-to spot. Its trendy ambiance and consistently enjoyable fare have left a lasting impression on me.

input: This place is so lovely! I went for a sweet and was amazed at the variety. The gooey butter cookies were awesome and the German chocolate cupcake simply amazing!
Rewrite this for me: I couldn't help but be captivated by the enchanting atmosphere of this place! I decided to indulge my sweet tooth and was absolutely blown away by the extensive assortment available. The scrumptious gooey butter cookies were beyond incredible, and the German chocolate cupcake was nothing short of awe-inspiring!

input:
Decent frozen yogurt with a lot of options for toppings. They have about 8 different froyo flavors to chose from. Lots of possible combinations. However, it can get expensive pretty quickly when you weigh the cup. 

There's not a lot of seating inside. Staff is friendly but not very active. I do want to try their bubble tea, but j wasn't very impressed.
Rewrite this for me:
They offer a good variety of frozen yogurt flavors along with numerous topping options. You can choose from around 8 different flavors and create plenty of delicious combinations. Although, it's important to note that the cost can add up rapidly when you weigh the cup.

The seating area inside is limited, and while the staff is friendly, they aren't very proactive. Additionally, I had the opportunity to try their bubble tea, but it didn't leave a strong impression on me.

input:
I loved this place!  We drove down from Tahoe just to eat here!  The 90 miles round trip was worth it!  The food was that good!  The Chicken Basil was the best!  And they have good Boba Tea!

Don't believe the nay-sayer about this place.  The food was pretty authentic Taiwanese.  Try it and see for yourself!
Rewrite this for me: I absolutely adored this place! We made a special trip all the way from Tahoe just to dine here. The 90-mile journey was definitely worth it because the food was simply outstanding! The Chicken Basil dish, in particular, stood out as the absolute best. Moreover, they also have a delightful selection of Boba Tea. So, don't pay any attention to those negative reviews. The food here is genuinely Taiwanese and I strongly urge you to experience it firsthand!

input:
Cru is such a cute quaint wine bar! In the front is a wine store and in the back ins the wine bar. The wine bar area is small but had a very modern atmosphere.

I started off with the Vina Vino wine flight and my friends ordered The Bold and the Beautiful. Both came on a cute wood/chalkboard board with the wine written in chalk. All the wines were very tasty but the Vespucci  Primitivo and the Il Fauno di Arcanum were my favorite.

We then ordered the fig jam and prosciutto, bleu cheese, arugula flatbread. A little heavy on the blue cheese for my liking but overall was really good. We also ordered the Farmers Platter. You can choose anything from 1-7 items and build your plate from a variety of cheese and meats. We selected the Brillat-Savarin, Cypress Grove "Purple Haze", Blue Brie, Spressata and the Italian Speck. The farmers plate also came with jam, mustard,  caramelized nuts and crostini. The Farmers plate by far was my favorite!

Overall I really liked CRU. Its cute, quaint and cozy. Can't wait to come back!!
Rewrite this for me:
CRU is an adorable and charming wine bar with a unique setup - a wine store in the front and a cozy wine bar area in the back. Despite its small size, the wine bar exudes a modern atmosphere.

To start off our evening, I chose the Vina Vino wine flight while my friends opted for The Bold and the Beautiful. Both were presented on a charming wood/chalkboard board with the names of the wines written in chalk. All the wines proved to be delicious, but my personal favorites were the Vespucci Primitivo and the Il Fauno di Arcanum.

Next, we ordered the fig jam and prosciutto, bleu cheese, arugula flatbread. I found the blue cheese to be slightly overpowering, but overall it was delectable. We also indulged in the Farmers Platter, allowing us to select up to seven items and create our own plate from an assortment of cheeses and meats. We chose the Brillat-Savarin, Cypress Grove "Purple Haze", Blue Brie, Spressata, and the Italian Speck. The Farmers Platter also included a delightful assortment of jam, mustard, caramelized nuts, and crostini. Undoubtedly, the Farmers Platter was the highlight of our culinary experience.

In conclusion, I thoroughly enjoyed my visit to CRU. Its cute, quaint, and cozy ambiance left a lasting impression, and I am eagerly looking forward to returning in the future.

input: Great spot I've been coming here for years. Top 3 steaks in the city! Nothing has changed even after the name change. Try a chicken cheesesteak for something different
Rewrite this for me: This place is absolutely fantastic! I've been a loyal customer for years. It serves the top 3 steaks in the entire city, hands down! input:
Pina's is easily one of the mroe underated places to eat in Roxborough. They have great stromboli (which are HUGE) and thier sicilian pie is the best I have every had. Sandwiches and pizza are just ok. 

I stopped ina two occassions for a sit down dinner and came away very stisfied and full. Ordered the chicken park with was a huge chickem covered in cheese and sauce. Excellent.
Rewrite this for me:
Pina's in Roxborough is a highly overlooked dining spot that deserves more recognition. Their stromboli is absolutely fantastic, and it's worth mentioning that they are generously sized. On two separate occasions, I decided to dine in at Pina's, and both times I left feeling completely satisfied and with a full belly. I tried their chicken parm, which was a substantial portion of chicken smothered in cheese and sauce, and it was truly excellent.

input: It may be a bit pricey, but it's good food in the cafe and a good selection in the grocery. I love their vegan sandwich and tofu melt and they always have a great selection of vegan sweets.

input:

My friends ordered the Gator burger and the deer burger. I personally ordered the buffalo wings, which was very good. We left super happy! Btw they're drinks are very good too!
Rewrite this for me:
These individuals are absolutely incredible! The top-notch burger joint in New Orleans without a doubt. Their service was exceptional, ensuring our meals arrived promptly and with fresh ingredients. As soon as we arrived from Atlanta, this was our first destination, and we will certainly return before our departure.

input:
Went here with my boyfriend and we loved it!
Old school feeling, with 3 floors!!

We have been here twice, and each time was great!
The food was amazing, I got the veal since it had been recommended to me, as well as the clams casino, mussles, pasta with oil and garlic, and the home-made garlic bread. Staff was nice and helpful!

MUST EAT!!!
Rewrite this for me:

This place is a definite must-visit for anyone looking for an amazing culinary experience!

input:
First impression:

Home Wine Kitchen's "No Menu Monday" is a must-try for anyone interested in the St. Louis fine dining scene or good food more generally.  We came prepared with reservations, but the restaurant actually began quieting out while our delicious meal was ramping up; the tables offer more elbow room than the photographs online belie.  As the name of the evening suggests, no menu is in play here; you'll let your friendly server know if you have any food allergies or particular preferences, and before long watch your customized meal unfold.  That's a three-course meal, $30, plus $12 for three half-glass wine pairings.

As starters, we were served lamb meatballs -- likely the favorite of the night -- and goat cheese-stuffed poblano peppers.  The peppers had a good bit of spice offset by the chalkiness of the goat cheese, making an excellent pairing for my Soave (white wine).  The mains were a corvina fish delicately cooked in wax paper and a swordfish steak served over asparagus with homegrown tomatoes and "love sauce."  The corvina came out on the rarer side, perhaps a little too complex for this Midwesterner's palate, but the hearty swordfish was some of the best seafood I've tasted in Missouri.  Dessert comprised a champagne gelatin and a chocolate tart, both of which were topped by fluffy homemade whipped cream and quickly eaten.

The staff at Home Wine Kitchen made our visit pleasant, acting casual yet professional during our meal.  The restaurant patrons seemed to be largely industry types that oohed and aahed about the cuisine (perhaps a trifle self-importantly, but this Yelper is no saint himself).  I was surprised to note that other diners were served the same courses as we were (albeit in different configurations), when I was under the assumption there would be a little more variation; however, I can only imagine the challenge such an endeavor would pose to the talented kitchen.  The interior, lighting, and volume here were all very good.

By the end of the evening, we realized that putting yourself in the hands of the chef is not for the faint of heart, as evidenced by one conversation near us during the meal that all but stopped when a beautiful whole fish was served to the table.  Leaving the restaurant, I was glad that I had tried No Menu Monday, but did wonder what the meal would have been like had I ordered off the menu.  I guess that calls for a return visit, don't you?
Rewrite this for me:
The "No Menu Monday" at Home Wine Kitchen is a must-try for those interested in St. Louis fine dining or simply good food. Despite coming with reservations, the restaurant became quieter as we enjoyed our delicious meal; the tables were more spacious than they appeared in the online photos. As the name suggests, there is no set menu for this evening; instead, you inform your friendly server of any allergies or preferences, and soon enough, a personalized meal is presented. The price for this three-course meal is $30, with the option to add three half-glass wine pairings for an additional $12.

For starters, we were served delicious lamb meatballs, which were likely the highlight of the night, and goat cheese-stuffed poblano peppers. The peppers had a nice kick of spice, complemented by the texture of the goat cheese, making them a perfect pairing with my Soave (white wine). The main courses consisted of a delicately cooked corvina fish wrapped in wax paper and a swordfish steak served with asparagus, homegrown tomatoes, and a sauce called "love sauce." The corvina was slightly undercooked for my Midwestern taste, but the robust swordfish was some of the best seafood I've had in Missouri. Dessert consisted of a champagne gelatin and a chocolate tart, both topped with fluffy, homemade whipped cream and devoured quickly.

The staff at Home Wine Kitchen provided a pleasant dining experience, striking a balance between casual and professional. The majority of the other diners seemed to be individuals within the industry who were enthusiastic about the cuisine, albeit sometimes a bit self-importantly—although I must admit, I am no exception as a Yelper. I was surprised to see that other diners were also served the same courses (albeit presented differently), as I expected more variation. However, I understand the challenge this would pose to the talented kitchen. The interior, lighting, and noise level were all excellent.

By the end of the evening, we realized that entrusting the chef with our meal choices requires a certain level of bravery—illustrated by a nearby conversation that abruptly ceased when a beautifully presented whole fish was brought to their table. Leaving the restaurant, I was grateful for trying No Menu Monday but couldn't help but wonder how the experience would have differed if we had ordered from a menu. Perhaps a return visit is in order.

input:
Went here with a few friends as the place to have our reunion dinner. We hadn't seen eachother since elementary school and got reacquainted through Facebook so this was a pretty special dinner. 

The restaurant is very swanky and the prices show this. I do think the food was worth the price although all of my party thought it was very expensive. I ordered the lobster bake which was delicious. It was not fantastic and there wasn't alot of seafood but it was adequate for me. I also ordered a Neopolitan Old Fashion which was made perfectly. 

My friends ordered the fritters, carpaccio, crab cake and fries. Plus 2 shots of tequila, a lemonade and 2 more old fashions. Bill was $170 which is not bad but some of my friends weren't expected it. 

And I must say something about our waiter. Unfortunately, I didn't remember his name but he was fantastic! Very attentive, nice and even bought out a dessert because it was also one of my friend's bday. He was just real cool. 

5 stars for service
3 stars for food
4 stars for ambience 
2 stars for price.  

But I was satisfied.
Rewrite this for me:
I visited this restaurant with a small group of friends to celebrate our reunion dinner. It had been years since we saw each other, but thanks to reconnecting on Facebook, this dinner held a special significance for us.

The restaurant had an upscale atmosphere, and the prices reflected it. Although my friends found it quite expensive, I believed the quality of the food justified the cost. Personally, I opted for the lobster bake, which turned out to be delicious. It wasn't extraordinary and lacked a significant amount of seafood, but it was satisfactory for me. Additionally, I ordered a Neopolitan Old Fashioned cocktail, which was expertly prepared.

Among my friends, various dishes were ordered, such as fritters, carpaccio, crab cake, and fries, accompanied by two shots of tequila, a lemonade, and two more Old Fashioned cocktails. The bill amounted to $170, which some of my friends found unexpectedly high.

I must take a moment to praise our waiter, whose name unfortunately slipped my mind. He provided exceptional service, being attentive, friendly, and even surprising us with a dessert for one of our friend's birthdays. He was truly fantastic.

Considering the overall experience, I would give the service a five-star rating, the food a three-star rating, the ambience a four-star rating, and the price a two-star rating.

However, despite the price, I left the restaurant feeling satisfied.

input: My first trip to Susanna Foo was at 6 months old when the restaurant was still a hole-in-the-wall takeout joint owned by Susanna's parents. My parents have been taking my brother and I ever since. I have many fond memories of Susanna fashioning dolls for us out of the linen napkins and preparing Chicken with Cashew Nuts when we refused to eat anything else. The food has always been reliable, but now that I am an adult, I find it lacking excitement. The service is always impeccable and I have never been disappointed by the overall decor or ambience. I'd like to see Susanna improve upon some of her traditional recipes by either adding new flavors or perhaps returning to her Chinese roots with a more ethnic menu. I'm hoping there will be a revitalization and that I will come to love Susanna Foo as much as I did as a child.
Rewrite this for me: My initial visit to Susanna Foo took place when I was merely 6 months old. Back then, the restaurant was a small takeout establishment operated by Susanna's parents. Since that time, my parents have been regularly taking my brother and me there. I have cherished memories of Susanna creating dolls for us using linen napkins and preparing Chicken with Cashew Nuts when we adamantly refused any other dish. The food has always been dependable, but as an adult, I find it lacking in excitement. Nevertheless, the service remains impeccable, and I have never been disappointed by the overall decor or atmosphere. It is my desire to witness Susanna enhance some of her traditional recipes by incorporating new flavors or perhaps revisiting her Chinese heritage with a more ethnically diverse menu. I am eagerly anticipating a revitalization, in the hopes that I will once again develop a profound love for Susanna Foo as I did during my childhood.

input: I am from California and was looking for something besides the hotel dining room to have dinner at.  I usually use the Yellow Pages to find restaurants and judge them by the size of their ads.  Spiro's jumped out at me, not because of the size of their advertisement (small) but Greek food just sounded good to me tonight.  I wasn't disappointed at all.  The Greek lemon soup was excellent and I liked the Moussaka, although the waiter suggested the Sea Bass.  All in all, the dinner was terrific and if I am back in this area, I will head to Spiro's again.  Thanks Neil for the wonderful service!
Rewrite this for me: I come from California and was in search of an alternative to the hotel dining room for my dinner. Typically, I rely on the Yellow Pages to discover nearby restaurants, basing my judgment on the extent of their advertisements. While flipping through, Spiro's caught my attention, not due to the size of their advertisement (which was small), but because the idea of Greek cuisine appealed to me tonight. To my delight, I was not let down. The Greek lemon soup surpassed my expectations, and even though I initially chose the Moussaka, the waiter recommended the Sea Bass. Overall, the dinner was exceptional, and if I find myself in this area again, I will undoubtedly return to Spiro's. Many thanks to Neil for the outstanding service!

input: I'm a Barbecue judge and this ain't barbecue.  Not in Texas, not in the southeast.  Not in KC.  An earlier reviewer nailed it perfectly.  The brisket is fatty pot roast.  No evidence of smoke.  Mushy texture like long braised  meat.  My sandwich was 75 percent fat.  Big meatless chunks of fat.  Either the owner doesn't care or he's left the place in the hands of employees who don't know any better. Sorry.  But you can do much better elsewhere.
Rewrite this for me: As a Barbecue judge, this does not meet the definition of barbecue. It would not be deemed as such in Texas, the southeast, or Kansas City. The previous reviewer accurately described it. The brisket resembles fatty pot roast, lacking any hint of smoke flavor. The texture is overcooked, resembling long braised meat. Sadly, my sandwich consisted of 75 percent fat, with substantial chunks of meatless fat. It seems that either the owner does not prioritize quality or they have entrusted the place to employees who lack knowledge in barbecue. Apologies, but you would be better off dining elsewhere with higher standards.

input:
Our second favorite place to watch a sunset. It's way north of Tampa, so a bit of a drive. We love to join everyone to clap when the sun goes down...a wonderful way to end the day. 

The music is lively, as are the patrons. Don't expect to swim in the water, it's a rocky beach, not much sand. Have been taking our boys since they were babies...are fifteen now. The food and drinks don't make an impression either way, it's the view and atmosphere that draws you in. 

Never disappoints.
Rewrite this for me:
Our second most cherished spot to witness a picturesque sunset lies a significant distance north of Tampa, requiring a bit of a journey. We thoroughly enjoy joining the crowd in applauding as the sun bids farewell, creating an exquisite conclusion to the day. 

The ambiance is filled with lively music and vibrant individuals. However, it's important to note that swimming is not feasible as the beach consists predominantly of rocks, with minimal sand. We have been bringing our boys to this location since they were infants, and now they have reached the age of fifteen. The culinary offerings and beverages may not leave a lasting impression, but it is the alluring view and captivating atmosphere that truly captivate you.

Rest assured, it never ceases to amaze.

input:
Obviously they are doing something right since they have been around since 1958. Great soft serve and scooped ice cream cones, boats, floats and sundaes.
Prices great too.  Enjoy!
Rewrite this for me: With their establishment dating back to 1958, it's evident that they are clearly excelling in their operations. They provide fantastic soft serve and scooped ice cream cones, as well as a delightful range of boats, floats, and sundaes. Moreover, their prices are also incredibly reasonable. So go ahead and indulge - you're in for a treat!

input: I decided to stop by since I was in the area and craving some authentic Mexican cuisine. I was literally by myself (late lunchtime on a tues) and really excited to try the pazole!! It was delicious ( granted my first and only time) I believe it's pork and has hominy, lettuce, radishes,onions and they give you a small container of dried oregano. Not the biggest fan of the lettuce cause it's gets all wilted but add some hot sauce and it's a meal in itself!!! I got also got the taco lunch special (2 pork tacos and rice) and that was good. Besides the amazing service from the sweet lady, the salsa was way sweet! Wasn't the biggest fan but everything is def fresh! And the pineapple water is a must. I don't like pineapples but I read reviews and just had to try it and thank u guys! Great reviews :) I'm excited to come back to try the burritos esp since I come out here for Costco shopping (soooo close by!) pretty dangerous when I find good food cause then I get cravings :/ enjoy this gem and eat up!!!
Rewrite this for me:
I decided to make a detour and visit this place because I was in the vicinity and had a strong desire for some authentic Mexican food. I was dining alone, on a Tuesday afternoon, and I was really looking forward to trying their pazole! It turned out to be delicious, although it was my first and only time having it. From what I gather, it's made with pork, hominy, lettuce, radishes, onions, and they provide a small container of dried oregano. The lettuce wasn't my favorite because it tends to wilt, but when you add some hot sauce, it becomes a satisfying meal on its own! 

In addition to the pazole, I also ordered the taco lunch special, which included two pork tacos and rice. It was quite good. Apart from the outstanding service provided by the lovely lady, I found the salsa to be too sweet for my taste. However, everything else was undoubtedly fresh! I must insist that you try the pineapple water, even if you're not a fan of pineapples. I read some reviews and decided to give it a chance, and I'm so glad I did! The positive reviews were accurate. 

I can't wait to return and try their burritos, especially since I frequently come to this area for shopping at Costco, which happens to be conveniently close by. It can be dangerous for me to find such good food because it tends to create cravings. Nonetheless, I hope you treasure this hidden gem and enjoy your meal to the fullest!

input:
by 3 stars, i really mean 3.5-

white brick walls, cool rustic furniture, seasoned, attractive employees. and the lighting is lovely.. nay, PERFECT. probably good for a blind date.  and service is good and timely.

but 3.5 could've been 4 if it wasn't so expensive for what i'm getting. and if the kitchen was more accommodating.

the first time i ever ate there, (around when it first opened), i ordered ravioli and received 3 or 5 pieces for $11-13.  another time i visited, i tried substituting a salad for fries with my burger. and my server said, "no, sorry, the kitchen won't do that." 

are you $^%ER@# kidding me??? it wasn't a super modification. it's not as if i asked for a burger with only one bun, no tomato, half piece of lettuce, two onion rings, and love. it wasn't like i wanted to substitute lobster for fries!!! needless to say, this is the first time i've been unable to substitute. i'm usually really easy to please, but this is the first time i've ever felt difficult. at least in my head. is this in my head?

unforgivable.
Rewrite this for me:
I mean 3.5 (almost 4) stars.

The establishment has visually appealing white brick walls, cool rustic furniture, and a staff that is seasoned and attractive. The lighting is not just good, but perfect. It would be an ideal place for a blind date, as the service is commendable and prompt.

However, the rating could have been a solid 4 if it weren't for the expensive prices in relation to the overall experience. Additionally, the kitchen's lack of flexibility is a drawback.

During my first visit when the place had just opened, I ordered ravioli and was served a disappointingly small portion of 3 or 5 pieces for $11-13. On another occasion, I wanted to substitute fries for a salad with my burger, but my server informed me that it was not possible due to the kitchen's restrictions.

Are you seriously kidding me? It was not an extreme request. I didn't ask for a completely customized burger with various modifications. I didn't even request to substitute fries with lobster! Needless to say, this is the first time I've encountered such an issue regarding substitutions. Usually, I am very easy to please, but this experience made me feel difficult for the first time. Is it just me? Or is this a valid concern?

This unforgivable inflexibility tarnishes the overall experience.

input: I would eat here again, but mostly because it is an interesting destination in a town with a lot of bad restaurants. Great decor, noisy atmosphere, and funky vibe. Servers seem hip, but we were rushed through an inattentive service. (One of those dinners where you better ask for the check when you can because you don't know when you will see the waiter again). Note to Gluten Free folks, this place is not completely safe or knowledgeable and the GF buns were awful. The house catsup, which is apparently a thing here, is not GF. Note to anyone with a car: parking sucks.
Rewrite this for me: I would consider returning to this restaurant, primarily because it stands out in a town filled with subpar dining options. The interior decor is impressive, although the atmosphere can be quite noisy and the overall vibe is unique. The servers appear trendy, but our dining experience felt rushed and the service lacked attentiveness. It was one of those meals where it's wise to request the bill as soon as possible, as you may not see your waiter again for quite some time. It's important to note that this establishment may not be entirely safe or knowledgeable for individuals following a gluten-free diet, and the gluten-free buns were disappointingly unpleasant. Additionally, their house catsup, which seems to be a specialty here, is not gluten-free. If you happen to be driving, please be aware that parking is quite challenging.

input: Good drinks and food. Had the pulled pork and fried chicken po boy. Mac and cheese was amazing. Very reasonable for the price. Great draft list as well. Serves food till1am.
Rewrite this for me: The drinks and food at this place are excellent. I tried the pulled pork and fried chicken po boy, both of which were delicious. The mac and cheese was particularly impressive. input: If you like to wait while several tables are open,  terrible service, a dirty restaurant, and very mediocre food that is overpriced for breakfast then you'll love this place! Don't bother wasting your time on this dilapidated dump.

input:
So, I went back to El Arado on Monday with a group of six people. The staff seemed shocked about our 6 pm arrival, and "sanitized" a large table for us quickly. Yes, the table smelled like dirty sanitized rags, ugh, but, once you got buzzed on...I mean beyond, the smell, your waiter will appear and take your drink orders. 

We got beers and margaritas. The margarita drinker in the group declared that it "was good."  The prices for drinks weren't that bad.  ($2.95 for Mexican beers). 

We all ordered our food, which was brought out at a good time, fresh, and hot. Everyone snarfed - it was good and tasty and all our needs were met attentively by the quiet waiter. 

All of us were let satisfied, and our specific requests (i.e. "no beans" "light on the cheese") were met by the kitchen staff with no problems. We left with full bellies then went to the Red Garter for a mind-numbing strip club experience. 

What a way to wrap up a review..

El Arado has gotten a bad wrap - but, the staff is decent, the food wasn't too shabby and the drink prices are cheap. A good place to start out for affordable and filling eats before a night out in Fountain Square (or to strip clubs).
Rewrite this for me:
On Monday, I revisited El Arado accompanied by a group of six individuals. The staff appeared taken aback by our arrival at 6 pm, but swiftly provided us with a sanitized table. Unfortunately, the table emitted an unpleasant odor reminiscent of dirty sanitized rags. However, once we overlooked the pungent scent, our waiter promptly took our drink orders.

We opted for beers and margaritas, and one member of our party commended the margarita, stating that it was enjoyable. The prices for the drinks were reasonably fair, with Mexican beers being priced at $2.95 each.

When our food was served, it arrived promptly, fresh, and piping hot. Everyone eagerly devoured their meals as they were delicious and met our requirements splendidly. The attentive waiter catered to all our needs silently.

Each of us left the restaurant satisfied, as the kitchen staff easily accommodated specific requests such as omitting beans or reducing the amount of cheese. With contented bellies, we proceeded to the Red Garter for an adventurous evening at a strip club.

To conclude the review, El Arado has been unjustly labeled negatively. The staff is decent, the food is delectable, and the prices for drinks are affordable. It serves as an ideal establishment for an economical and satisfying meal before embarking on an evening in Fountain Square or exploring strip clubs.

input: The Loew's hotel is very clean and looks very nice. The service is amazing. My family and I wanted to stay for a whole month. The breakfast there is fantastic! My son said it looked like it was the future. That's how nice it was! The rooms were nice size and the parking is convenient. That's why I give the Loew's hotel 5 stars.
Rewrite this for me: The Loew's hotel is exceptionally clean and boasts an impressive appearance. The service provided is truly remarkable. We were so satisfied with our stay that my family and I wished to extend it for an entire month. Additionally, the breakfast served at the hotel is absolutely fantastic! My son even remarked that it seemed futuristic due to its remarkable quality. The rooms are spacious and the parking facilities are conveniently located. For these reasons, I wholeheartedly bestow a 5-star rating upon the Loew's hotel.

input:
Yayyy for honeygrow ! I honestly can 't believe it took me so long to try this place. It's awesome ! It is in the same complex as my gym and I always said I would give it a shot but didn't seem to make it over there. 

Well this past Tuesday it happened and I have a new spot to grab a healthy meal. input: This is hands down my favorite brewery in The world!! My husband is from STL and every time we go back to visit his family we visit the brewery! Rewrite this for me: Without a doubt, this is my absolute favorite brewery in the entire world! Whenever we go back to STL to see my husband's family, we always make a point to visit this brewery. input:
We arrived a few minutes early for a 7pm reservation. When we asked for our table, both hostesses looking at their paper, then said they'd have to go check and would be back. 5 minutes later, they returned and did not acknowledge us. Meanwhile, another large party arrived without a reservation and were told it would be a 40 minute wait. We then heard one hostess say to the other that she didn't want to seat them soon because the kitchen was backed up and people were waiting 40 minutes for their appetizers. So unprofessional.
We walked up again, after they continued to ignore us, and asked about our table. They weren't apologetic when they told us that the girl we spoke to earlier that day was new and never recorded our reservation. They continued to tell us that it would be at least a 20 minute wait before they could put our table together. We got a smug "I'm sorry, but she was new" and they brushed us off.
I really understand that sometimes things just don't go the way they were supposed to and that people make mistakes. However, a little customer service would have gone a long way. Offer us some water, or a seat at the bar or say that you're doing everything you can to get us in as soon as possible. They basically blew us off and blamed it on the new girl. 
Needless to say we left and I will not be returning.
Rewrite this for me:
We arrived a few minutes early for our 7pm reservation, but when we approached the hostesses, they were both focused on their papers. After requesting our table, they informed us that they needed to check and would return. Unfortunately, they came back after 5 minutes without acknowledging us. Meanwhile, a large party without a reservation arrived and were informed of a 40 minute wait. We overheard one of the hostesses mentioning that they were hesitant to seat them soon due to a backed-up kitchen and customers waiting 40 minutes for their appetizers. This lack of professionalism was disheartening.

Since they continued to ignore us, we approached them once again to inquire about our table. Their response lacked any apology as they explained that the girl we spoke to earlier, who was new, had failed to record our reservation. They further informed us that it would be at least a 20 minute wait before they could arrange our table. Their nonchalant "I'm sorry, but she was new" attitude left us feeling dismissed.

While I understand that mistakes happen and things don't always go as planned, a little bit of customer service could have made a significant difference. Offering us water, a seat at the bar, or reassurances that they were doing their best to accommodate us would have been appreciated. Instead, they simply brushed us off and shifted the blame onto the new employee.

Needless to say, we decided to leave and I have no intention of returning in the future.

input:

input: Oh my goodness if you ever want to start on a health "trip" this is the place to start. Rewrite this for me: If you're looking to embark on a journey towards better health, look no further than this amazing place. input: I love this shoppe. I have been here a few times, but I have been coming more regularly. The staff is AWESOME and the atmosphere GREAT. THey have healthy tasty treats which is nice and a host of croissants and other tasty treats. They also have food for lunch and breakfast. I havent had anything here that wasnt fantabulous.

input: Great Cranberry Orange Muffin and Caffe Latte on a Saturday morning. Great ambience and fast service.

input: My favorite place to eat sushi and the nicest people I know that work there! It'll always be my first choice and they have a great menu! It's always more than just good when you eat from there!

input: This might be my favorite coffee shop in the city. The food is unbelievable. Anything I have ordered has been fresh, delicious and so enjoyable. The place has a cool edgy vibe and lots of comfy seating and some great seats outside when the weather is nice. Definitely worth checking out especially if you want a some food as well.
Rewrite this for me: This coffee shop is possibly the best one in the city according to my preference. The food they offer is unbelievably good. input: I absolutely love this place and think is easily the best burrito shop in town. Great salsas, relaxed atmosphere, excellent service and price,  Most importantly the burritos are delicious. The chicken and chorizo combo is  my personal favorite but the smoked brisket is great as well. The medium burrito is plenty unless you are training for an eating event.  Family owned, not a chain and it shows in the attention to flavor. Highest recommendation if you are interested in good, healthy food (unless you eat yourself into oblivion) at a reasonable price.
Rewrite this for me: This place is absolutely amazing! In my opinion, it's hands down the top burrito shop in town. The salsas are fantastic, the atmosphere is laid-back, the service is excellent, and the prices are reasonable. But what truly sets this place apart are the mouthwatering burritos. I personally can't get enough of the chicken and chorizo combo, although the smoked brisket is also incredibly tasty. Unless you're gearing up for an eating competition, the medium-sized burrito should be more than enough to satisfy your hunger. One of the things I truly appreciate about this place is that it's family-owned, not a generic chain, and that really shines through in the flavor and quality. If you're looking for delicious and nutritious food (unless you go overboard on the portions), this is definitely the place to go. I highly recommend it!

input:

input:

input: Great store if you like 50's-Midcentury modern! The prices are a little high compared to my favorite stores in STL, but this store is one of a kind thats for sure!

input: STAY AWAY! I am a gold member, so I stay at Hamptons frequently. I have stayed here before, and it seems to be under constant construction. My room was dirty. input: The best fried rice ever! Also the best Pho I had while in Nashville. I'm from Seattle so I'm a little spoiled in that department. If you're looking for a good place to try it for the first time or just looking for a good Vietnamese restaurant, GO!

input: As far as I know, this is the best video rental store in existence.  The staff is knowledgeable and friendly, but the selection really sets it apart.  Suppose you want to rent the newest release and a VHS of the best hockey fights of the 1970s...They would probably have both available at a very low cost.  I only wish that there was a place like Casa Video in Chicago.
