I've been a regular patron of Jonny's, a dive bar, for years. It's known for its excellent daily happy hour and laid-back atmosphere. Despite its unassuming appearance, the food at Jonny's is always top-notch. If you believe that a dive like this can't offer great options, you're mistaken, my friend. They make their dough from scratch, and their naked wings are irresistible.

One of my go-to dishes is their Jon's salad with grilled chicken, a true classic. And let's not forget about their pizza. It's definitely a staple for me, especially when they have half-price pizza on certain days.

In addition to the great food, Jonny's offers a variety of games such as trivia and bingo. The best part? They're all free to play, and you can win amazing prizes like gift certificates and even one-cent pitchers of beer. Now that's a deal you can't pass up.

It's important to note that Jonny's is a smoking bar, so keep that in mind if it's a concern for you. During busy times, the smoke can become quite bothersome. Additionally, the bar tends to get crowded on game days or nights.

Overall, Jonny's is the perfect spot to enjoy a few budget-friendly beers with friends and indulge in a half-price pizza. Trust me, you won't be disappointed.

input:

The wait staff is always nice and the owner is often around to talk to.  Free dum dum lolly pops at the counter as you walk out and news papers to read if you are eating alone or want to check in on the Phillies.
Food- always good. Great pancakes that are fluffy and crispy on the edges.  Kansas City  is a great breakfast too- for the most part great.

Overall, it's a pleasant experience that is definitely worth a try.

I had the catfish smothered in poblano sauce and melted cheese.  They told me it was farm catfish but it tasted like the catfish I used to catch out of a lake near my house as a little kid.  Farm fish never tastes this real.

My wife had chile relleno - fresh peppers, not surprising this time of year but definite kudos to the chef.

The late-stage adolescents with us enjoyed their enhiladas and chimichangas too.

Meanwhile, my wife savored the chile relleno dish, showcasing the use of fresh peppers - a delightful surprise, particularly during this season. Kudos to the talented chef!

Our companions, a group of teenagers, thoroughly enjoyed their enchiladas and chimichangas as well.

My problem, though, was with the service. We placed our order for the carrot cake with a nice young teenager, and then waited. And waited. I could see the carrot cake just sitting in the pretty covered cake stand, and I felt really tempted to just slice it myself. After a bit (felt like 10 minutes, although I'm sure it was more like 5 or 6), another employee came and sliced the carrot cake, setting the slice on the back counter with the ticket. And then we waited. And waited some more. After about another 5 to 10 minutes, I flagged the teenager down and asked if he could box up the cake for us. He seemed confused, and it took an awkward minute-long exchange for him to understand we hadn't yet received our order. He did apologize for the wait, which I do appreciate, boxed up the cake, and then we were on our way.

I should clarify that we did not go into the shop at a busy time. It was a relatively cool day and not many people were out. While there were maybe 2 to 3 tables seated, we were the only ones at the counter ordering. And while I'm sure the wait staff who repeatedly walked by our lonely piece of carrot cake sitting on the back counter had many important tasks...I just wanted to eat my $10 cake.

Four stars for the cake. Two stars for the service.

input:
The gym part of City Fitness is better than most, good equipment, clean, variety, it's a nice gym. I find the rates reasonable and have been a member since they opened and will continue to be a member. So, for the rating I give the gym at CF a 3.5 star, I give MBSC a 1.5 star for an overall 2.5 star rating.

MBSC review: I thought I would kick it up a notch so joined the MBSC thrive program at CF on South Street and tried it for three months. Trainers really aren't "personal" trainers. They have a set program that they put people through and you have very little to say about what you like/don't like. The trainers work with several people in a session so depending on how many people are in a session you could be waiting for the trainer to get back to you or waiting for the person in front of you to finish. One of the things that frustrated me is they want you to push through the routine they have come up for you in the hour's time. The sessions are hard with ropes, sleds, balls, bands, cables, weights and the most uncomfortable stationary bike I've ever had to sit on (and they make you end every session on the thing). No two sessions are alike - so if you like variety then great, if you like consistency or at least enough repetition to get the moves and form down then not so great. I seldom found a session to be fun or enjoyable, rather I often felt like I was a contestant on the Biggest Loser. They also play hip-hop all day long and you either like it or you don't. The environment and training is designed (in my opinion) to appeal to 20-30yo demographic.

If you really want to push yourself beyond your limits and don't care how you get there then you might really enjoy the MBSC program. If you want a professional personal trainer to spend quality time with you in achieving your goals and if you want a training program that you actually learn what muscle groups you are working and not just to be pushed through a routine then you probably won't like MBSC. Definitely do a introductory program because the usual 30 day notice from the contract date applies if you cancel and it's $200+/mo program.
Rewrite this for me:
City Fitness's gym is undoubtedly outstanding, boasting top-notch equipment, pristine cleanliness, and a wide range of options. It truly is a pleasant place to exercise. As a member since its inception, I find their rates to be quite reasonable and will continue to be a loyal member. Consequently, I rate the gym at City Fitness a solid 3.5 stars. In contrast, MBSC receives a lackluster 1.5-star rating, resulting in an overall rating of 2.5 stars.

Regarding MBSC, I decided to challenge myself and enrolled in their thrive program located at CF on South Street. Unfortunately, the trainers fail to provide the personalized experience one would expect from personal trainers. They adhere to a rigid program, leaving very little room for client input. Moreover, since they handle multiple individuals in each session, there could be considerable waiting time for assistance. The insistence on pushing through the prescribed routine in the hour-long sessions became increasingly frustrating. These sessions incorporate challenging exercises with ropes, sleds, balls, bands, cables, weights, and an extremely uncomfortable stationary bike that concludes every session. While the variety in each session could be appealing to some, it posed difficulties for those seeking consistency or adequate repetition to grasp proper form. Regrettably, very few sessions were enjoyable; instead, they often resembled something out of "The Biggest Loser." Additionally, the constant playing of hip-hop music may either be a preference or a deterrent. Ultimately, the environment and training at MBSC seem tailored to a younger demographic, specifically those aged 20-30.

If your goal is to push your limits without concern for the means used, the MBSC program may truly suit you. However, if you desire a professional personal trainer who devotes quality time to help you achieve your objectives, and a training program that educates you about the specific muscle groups involved rather than merely rushing through a routine, MBSC is unlikely to meet your expectations. I strongly recommend trying their introductory program before committing, as cancelling after the contract date necessitates a 30-day notice and the program costs over $200 per month.

input:
Four stars for price. 
I drive truck, so I've eaten bbq all over America. This place is better than most, but it's certainly not 4 star worthy. I'd say the food is more like 2.5 star. 
The cheeseburger was quite large and the meat was tasty. (Be advised: if you don't stop them they'll automatically put that disgusting invention called mayonnaise on it.) I got it plain so I can't comment on their lettuce/tomato game. 
The pork bbq sammich was soggy on the bottom. Moist is good, but this was just plain wet. The meat itself was bland but not bad. 
The bbq sauce is pretty good but not great. 
The Mac & Cheese tasted ok but the noodles were way overcooked. It'd be much better if it were baked and had a little crustiness to it. 

If I lived local I'm sure I'd come here occasionally.
Rewrite this for me:
I would rate this place with four stars for its pricing. As a truck driver who has tried BBQ all across America, I can say that this place is better than most, although it falls short of deserving a four-star rating. In my opinion, the food here is more like a two-and-a-half-star quality.

The cheeseburger was impressively large and the meat had a delicious taste. However, be cautious as they tend to automatically add a distasteful condiment called mayonnaise unless specified otherwise. I ordered mine plain, so I cannot comment on the quality of their lettuce and tomato combination.

On the other hand, the pork BBQ sandwich was disappointingly soggy at the bottom. While moistness is usually appreciated, this was simply too wet. The meat itself lacked flavor but was overall decent.

The BBQ sauce provided was fairly good, although not exceptional. As for the Mac & Cheese, it had an okay taste but the noodles were drastically overcooked. It would greatly benefit from being baked and acquiring a slight crustiness.

If I resided in the vicinity, I would surely visit this place occasionally.

input:
So we've been wanting to try the sushiritos since they opened up a location closer to us and we finally tried it last Friday. 

I got the slammin' salmon and my wife got the crunch. I'd say they both definitely had fresh ingredients, and definitely tasted fresh, but I think the balance of flavors wasn't quite right for the slammin' salmon. Way too heavy on the sauce, completely overpowering the crisp fresh veggies and salmon. 

We tried the Japanese fried chicken. Sauce is a little sweet and sour. And the chicken was a little dry. 

We also tried their green tea and lemonade, which were pretty good, but you don't come to a place like this because their green tea and lemonade are their best things on the menu. 

Overall, you pay a high premium for a gimmicky meal. With this location being essentially at a revolving door of new customers on the corner of Penn's campus, I think they have the potential to do well. But I don't think I'll be coming back. We'll take our $34 elsewhere.

I opted for the slammin' salmon sushirito while my wife went for the crunch. While both had fresh and flavorful ingredients, the slammin' salmon lacked balance. The excessive amount of sauce overwhelmed the crisp vegetables and salmon, leaving an overpowering taste.

We also tried the Japanese fried chicken, which had a slightly sweet and sour sauce. Unfortunately, the chicken itself was a bit dry, not living up to our expectations.

In terms of drinks, we sampled their green tea and lemonade, which were enjoyable. However, it's important to note that we didn't visit this place solely for the drinks.

Overall, we found that the high price tag for this novelty meal didn't quite match the quality. Given its location near Penn's campus with a constant influx of new customers, this restaurant has the potential to thrive. However, personally, we won't be returning. We'd rather spend our $34 elsewhere.

input: Beautifully sweet ending to a sweet trip to NOLA with the girls. We stumbled upon this after a delicous savory lunch nearby at Cochon (review to follow). Cupcake was good, mocha filling best part. Rasberry truffle was my fav, love the dark chocolate so it's not cloyingly sweet. The coffee was a wonderful chaser, not overly burnt, smoky, or acidic... I usually have coffee with milk n sugar, forgot this time, but I didn't even need it!  Seating was nice, with a few cafe tables inside. Enough for our 6-girl troop. We treated ourselves to a delightful selection of cupcakes and truffles. The chocolate cupcake with mocha filling was a definite standout, with the mocha filling stealing the show. Among the truffles, the raspberry flavor stood out as my favorite. The dark chocolate ensured that it wasn't overwhelmingly sweet, which I loved. To complement our treats, we enjoyed a perfectly brewed cup of coffee. It had just the right balance and wasn't overly burnt, smoky, or acidic. Surprisingly, I didn't even miss adding milk and sugar.

The seating at Sweet Confections was cozy, offering a few cafe tables inside. It was just enough to accommodate our group of six girls. The service was also excellent, with the staff being helpful in suggesting flavors and providing clear labeling. I would give this place a solid 4 out of 5 stars, only because having one more staff member could have made the experience even more pleasant.

input:
This hotel is a gem in the heart of Philadelphia.

It's a cozy, quaint, and charming property. The rooms are spacious, modern and gorgeous. 
The decor is chic and attractive: big wooden desk, hardwood floors, couches and throw pillows: Looks more like a friend's apartment than a hotel. 

Free breakfast is always a plus for those of us with limited time. It's not a hot breakfast (I've had so many mass-produced bad ones, so I'm not complaining) but greek yogurt, a huge croissant, an orange and some cranberry juice hits the spot! They leave it at your door though, instead of ringing your bell to wake you. So if you ask for it to be delivered at 7 a.m., check outside your door; by 7:01 it WILL be there. 

Coffee, a variety of teas, cold and hot water, as well as ice and a bowl of assorted fruit are available 24/7 in the lobby. There are doorbells for each room, and the hotel can only be accessed after hours if you have a key card. Floors are acessible with a keycard as well, for extra protection. The staff is very polite: one of the few places in Philly where someone will actually say "good morning" to you (No, seriously. I lived there for 5 years, so trust me on that). They're also extremely helpful. When I checked in the night before, the gentleman at the reservation desk called to make sure I had a cab waiting for me at 8:15 the next morning so that I could make my speaking engagement on time. While I was getting my clothes ready, my iron was making more wrinkles than it was taking out, so I asked them for a new one and within 30 seconds, I had a brand new model with all the bells and whistles.

I've read a few reviews talking about the noise level of this place. My room was closest to the reception desk and I never heard a peep. There were people out and about, but I didn't hear a thing. And I'm a very light sleeper...

A few things to note:
Its location on a tight, one way street can cause a little difficulty if you're traveling solo, but if you have one person to unload the car while someone else parks, you should be fine. The parking garage they use is about half a block from the hotel, but you have to drive in a big rectangle to get there. 

There's a stand-up shower instead of the traditional bathtub/shower combo. It fits one comfortably enough... provided that you're not too far from average height and build. (My boyfriend is 6'2 with a football player build and he made out okay.)

Don't expect much of a view. The view from our room was of the side of another building. But that's what the city is for... go out there and see something!

Overall, this was an excellent trip and a great find. I highly recommend this hotel to anyone.
Rewrite this for me:
Nestled in the heart of Philadelphia, this hotel is a true hidden gem. With its cozy and charming atmosphere, it offers a delightful and comfortable stay. The rooms are not only spacious but also adorned with modern and stunning furnishings. The chic and attractive decor, featuring a large wooden desk, hardwood floors, couches, and throw pillows, gives it more of a homely apartment feel rather than a traditional hotel.

One of the standout features of this hotel is the complimentary breakfast, which is especially valuable for those with limited time. Although it's not a hot breakfast, the offering of Greek yogurt, a generous croissant, an orange, and cranberry juice is simply perfect. To top it off, they conveniently deliver it to your door at the specified time, ensuring you never miss out.

24/7, the lobby provides unlimited access to coffee, a variety of teas, cold and hot water, as well as ice and an array of fresh fruits. The security measures are also commendable, requiring a key card to enter both the hotel and individual floors. The staff members are not only polite but also genuinely friendly, a rarity in Philly, as they greet you with a warm "good morning." Their helpfulness knows no bounds, exemplified by the reservation desk's effort to arrange a cab for my early morning speaking engagement and the swift replacement of my faulty iron.

Despite reading reviews about potential noise disturbances, my experience proved otherwise. Even though my room was located near the reception desk, I never heard a sound, allowing for a restful night's sleep.

A few details to keep in mind include the hotel's location on a narrow, one-way street, which can pose challenges if traveling alone. However, with a second person to help unload the car while someone parks, this inconvenience is easily managed. Additionally, instead of the typical bathtub/shower combination, the rooms feature stand-up showers. While it comfortably accommodates most individuals, those significantly taller or broader may find it slightly cramped.

Although the view from our room was not particularly remarkable, the beauty of the city lies just outside the hotel's doors, beckoning guests to explore and discover its wonders.

All in all, this hotel exceeded expectations, making our trip truly outstanding. I wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone seeking an unforgettable stay in Philadelphia.

input:
One of my most favorite Indian restaurants. Nothing fancy but absolutely delicious meals.

Never an issue being seated promptly. A casual dining experience awaits. Service is pleasant. Ambience a bit blahh but still enjoyable.

Now onto the real reason to come here... the FOOD:
Naan is soft. Garlic is tasty but I usually like the original best.  Regardless of your entree of choice, you really cannot go wrong. And although it does not appeal to my level of spiciness preferred (I like it HOT HOT HOT), it has great flavor and is great for the average spicey food eater. My recommendations are the Masala or Vindaloo (Chicken, Shrimp, Lamb... option is yours). Room for dessert? Order the Rice Pudding  and Gulab Jaman, mix together and enjoy the creamy sugary treat.
Rewrite this for me:

Seating is never a problem here, as you can always find a spot without any issues. The dining experience is casual and laid-back. The service is pleasant, although the ambience may not be anything special, it is still enjoyable.

But let's get to the real highlight of this place... the food. The naan bread is soft and delicious. While the garlic naan is tasty, I personally prefer the original flavor. No matter what entree you choose, you won't be disappointed. Even though it might not be as spicy as I like it (I prefer it extremely hot), it still has amazing flavor and is perfect for those who enjoy moderately spicy food. My top recommendations are the Masala or Vindaloo, whether you prefer chicken, shrimp, or lamb, the choice is yours.

If you have room for dessert, I highly recommend ordering the Rice Pudding and Gulab Jaman. Mix them together for a delightful and creamy sugary treat.

To the other reviewers, 
I would like to address the fact that we are here to review the stadium itself, not solely focus on personal fandom or past achievements of a team.

There is a lack of vendors available, making it inconvenient for fans to enjoy the game without having to constantly get up to purchase snacks like pretzels or soda. They tend to be heavily intoxicated and may invade personal space or purposely spill things on others, without regard for basic respect, even towards women. 

Overall, this stadium disappoints in several aspects, including the food selection, limited vendors, subpar TVs, and the behavior of certain Philly fans. It is advisable to strike this stadium off your list, unless you are specifically seeking a venue known for easy home runs, as it caters to hitters. As if that isn't enough, the store also boasts a fantastic selection of music, complementing the store's ambiance beautifully. And to top it all off, they even offer you a glass of wine while you browse! It doesn't get any better than this. 

I can't wait to revisit Tampa and see you both again soon! :)

input: Good menu, solid ingredients, but these folks are not sandwich artists.  I had a Turkey and Brie Wrap one day and the Spinach Florentine Wrap the next.  Both "wraps" could have more fittingly been called "crumples" because that's how they were assembled.  While watching the sandwich line I kept thinking, "Thank god they're not trying to fold burritos!"  Everyone in the sandwich line either looked befuddled by anything other than a plain bagel or like they were supposed to be somewhere else ten minutes ago.  Also, can we please hang a few signs like "order here", "pick-up here," "pay-here" to direct traffic instead of the east coast "If you don already know, then leave!" attitude?
Rewrite this for me: Although the menu is good and the ingredients are of good quality, the staff lacks the skills of a sandwich artist. I had a Turkey and Brie Wrap one day and the Spinach Florentine Wrap the next, but both wraps were poorly assembled, resembling crumples rather than carefully crafted wraps. Observing the sandwich line, I couldn't help but feel relieved that they weren't attempting to fold burritos. The individuals working in the sandwich line seemed either confused by anything beyond a plain bagel or as if they were supposed to be elsewhere ten minutes ago. Additionally, it would be beneficial to have clear signs such as "order here," "pick-up here," and "pay here" to direct customers, instead of adopting the unfriendly attitude of "If you don't already know, then leave!" commonly seen on the east coast.

input:
This place is absolutely amazing. A cute little bakery and the employees are super attentive. I walked in and was bouncing around from one dessert to another deciding if I should make a purchase. The employee offered me a sample of the banana puddings - definitely try some! And you know how sometimes when they give you so small of a sample to taste, you can't really make a proper judgment because there isn't enough to judge from? Not the case here!

I got the salted caramel banana, the strawberry banana pudding and the upside pineapple cake.

Thoughts: OMG!! I never crave banana pudding and never really thought anything of the dessert. But man after this, I wanted to go home and make my own banana pudding (Although I highly doubt that I could make it half as good)! Their desserts are crafted perfect - three/four layers depending on what you get. The bottom layer the the pudding, second layer is the nilla wafers or they might even use some sort of pound cake(whatever it was - it was AMAZING), third layer, the strawberry and then the top layer is pudding with a nice whipped creme and topping. The creme has so much flavor and the texture is so smooth. Everything just comes together so nicely! 

The upside pineapple cake was BOMB. the cake wasn't too fluffy but was dense to the perfect amount to Taste like what it's suppose to. The pineapple flavor isn't overwhelming but just right. My only problem was that the pineapple bottom got a little too carameliZed with brown sugar and was a bit hard to chew.

Definitely go to this place! I was so sad that there was no option to leave them a tip. (They use an iPad to ring you up). The service/help was so great and I would have left a tip but I had no cash. Any ways, highly recommend this place for desserts!!
Rewrite this for me:
This place is absolutely incredible! It's a charming little bakery with incredibly attentive employees. As soon as I walked in, I was overwhelmed by all the delicious dessert options and couldn't decide what to get. Thankfully, one of the employees offered me a sample of their banana puddings, and let me tell you, they were absolutely worth trying! Unlike other places where the samples are too small to properly judge, these samples were generous and allowed me to fully appreciate the flavors.

I ended up getting the salted caramel banana, strawberry banana pudding, and upside pineapple cake. Oh my goodness, they were all amazing! I usually don't crave banana pudding and never thought much of it, but after trying theirs, I wanted to go home and attempt to recreate it (although I doubt mine would be anywhere near as good as theirs!). Their desserts are crafted to perfection, with three or four layers depending on the option you choose. The bottom layer is the pudding, followed by nilla wafers (or maybe some sort of pound cake, whatever it was, it was incredible), then the strawberry layer, and finally topped with pudding and a delicious whipped cream topping. The cream has so much flavor and the texture is incredibly smooth. Everything just comes together beautifully!

The upside pineapple cake was fantastic as well. The cake had the perfect density, not too fluffy but just right, and the pineapple flavor was spot on. My only tiny issue was that the pineapple on the bottom was a little overly caramelized with brown sugar and was slightly tough to chew.

I highly recommend visiting this place for desserts! I was disappointed that there wasn't an option to leave a tip since they use an iPad for transactions. The service was exceptional, and I would have gladly left a tip if I had cash. Regardless, this place is definitely worth a visit if you're in the mood for some incredible desserts!

input: I visited the new Paoli location. BIG selection of tasty donuts. It's about time--the cardboard impostors found at Dunkin are so lame compared to these beauties. Salted Caramel, Bacon Maple, Lemon--now you're talking my language. Breakfast sandwiches, muffins, and bagels, oh my.
Rewrite this for me: I recently paid a visit to the new Paoli location and was pleasantly surprised by the extensive and delectable array of donuts they offered. Finally, we have a worthy alternative to the lackluster imitations found at Dunkin. Their Salted Caramel, Bacon Maple, and Lemon flavors truly speak my culinary language. Not only that, they also serve a diverse range of breakfast sandwiches, muffins, and bagels. It was quite an impressive experience!

input: So our most recent visit earlier this month was very disappointing, however we received an email from the company's guest service, followed by a call from the Hermitage O'Charley's manager Chris who was very professional and apologetic about our experience and asked that we give his location another try on them. So I convinced my husband to do so. Here's how this 2nd chance went:: Absolutely wonderful. Chris asked that we let him know when we wanted to give the restaurant a second chance, but we decided not to. We didn't want any special attention. We wanted real unreviewed service.  We were seated in the bar because it was a very  busy night, regardless of that the server was very attentive and had a great personality. Our food came out in a timely manner, well prepared and delicious. We have since then been back several times and service continues to remain great.
Rewrite this for me: Our recent visit earlier this month was quite disappointing. However, the company's guest service team reached out to us via email, followed by a call from the manager of Hermitage O'Charley's, Chris. He was extremely professional and apologetic about our experience, urging us to give his location another chance, so we decided to do so. It turned out to be an amazing decision. Chris had asked us to inform him when we were ready to return to the restaurant, but we chose not to. We wanted an unbiased experience without any special treatment. Since then, we have revisited multiple times and the service has consistently remained excellent.

input: In love with my haircut! Very reasonable prices as well. This is my second time here. The first time the cut and style were amazing but the color was a little off from what I wanted but it still looked good. I will definitely continue to be a returning customer.
Rewrite this for me: I am absolutely thrilled with my new haircut! The prices are very affordable too. It's actually my second visit to this place. The first time, the haircut and style were absolutely incredible. However, the color was slightly different from what I had envisioned, but it still turned out great. Without a doubt, I will continue to come back here as a satisfied customer.

input: So much care is given to healthy, delicious food (ex. Japanese squash rather than white potatoes in curry). Thay have nice touches like a welcome snack and straw wrappers twisted in a rose. The sauces are amazing, menu has so many options, they accomodate special dietary needs easily since everything is made from scratch; even the desserts have that extra touch using both white and black sticky rice. This is our go-to for Thai from now on!
Rewrite this for me: We really appreciate the attention given to creating wholesome and delectable meals at this place. For instance, instead of using regular white potatoes in their curry, they opt for the more nutritious Japanese squash. They also add lovely little touches like a delightful welcome snack and creatively twisted straw wrappers shaped like roses. Moreover, their extensive menu offers a wide range of options, making it easy for them to cater to special dietary requirements as everything is prepared from scratch. Even their desserts go above and beyond by incorporating both white and black sticky rice, adding that extra special element. This place has definitely become our new favorite Thai restaurant!

input:
Great grocery store in the Mid-city neighborhood. It had great deli, soup, hot bar, and salad bar options. It was like a waaaay less expensive Whole Foods. On the weekends they had crawfish or lobster boils by the lbs. This would be my go to store if I lived here for sure. Big plus it's LOCAL!!!

* Fried Chicken was BOMBlicious!!!!
Rewrite this for me: There is an amazing grocery store located in the Mid-city neighborhood that offers a wide range of options. Their deli, soup, hot bar, and salad bar choices are exceptional, reminiscent of a more affordable version of Whole Foods. On weekends, they even have delightful crawfish or lobster boils available by the pound. If I were a resident here, this would definitely be my preferred shopping destination. A major bonus is that it is locally owned and operated. Oh, and their Fried Chicken is absolutely phenomenal!

input: I made my Yelp account for the soul purpose of reviewing this place; I think that very much speaks to how I enjoyed the experience. It's exactly what you would expect from a local cafe/coffee shop and then some. The food and coffee were great and the atmosphere was very friendly and casual. The architecture of the dining room was very cool as well - it had a very Victorian feel, which I personally love. The service was a bit slow, but the barista was the only person working behind the counter and she was also very personable, so for that we can forgive her. When I go to a coffee shop I usually go to stay and relax, often reading or sketching. It is the perfect place for that, with both indoor and outdoor tables, a booth, and a counter. I also appreciated the dog-friendly policy but that's definitely a personal preference and isn't right for everyone. The location is also great, being situated in the French quarter. My only complaint is that I could only visit once on my trip to New Orleans.
Rewrite this for me: I created my Yelp account specifically to review this place, which indicates how much I enjoyed the experience. This local cafe/coffee shop exceeded my expectations. The food and coffee were excellent, and the atmosphere was inviting and laid-back. The dining room had a charming Victorian vibe, which I personally adore. The service was a bit slow, but considering there was only one barista handling everything, her friendly and personable nature made up for it. When I visit coffee shops, I usually like to stay and relax, whether it's reading or sketching. This place is perfect for that, offering indoor and outdoor seating, as well as booths and a counter. I also appreciated their dog-friendly policy, although I understand that's not for everyone. The location within the French quarter is fantastic. My only complaint is that I could only visit once during my trip to New Orleans.

input: High pressure tea sales!  Good teas but outrageously expensive.  Try Republic of Tea or even good old Twinings.
Rewrite this for me: Looking for high-quality teas? We have an extensive collection of exceptional teas, although they may come at a higher price. Consider exploring Republic of Tea or the timeless classic, Twinings, for a satisfying tea experience that fits your taste and budget.

input:
oh Millers, how i wanted to like you.  You are close to my house, have ample parking, and large spacious tables.  you even have a fireplace in the back for a little ambiance. 

friends and i tried to come here 2 or 3 times for a quick/inexpensive* bite to eat and every time there was a 30-60 minute wait. we thought this must mean they are really good.  perhaps it just means that people in Springfield are willing to settle for a less than average dining experience.  *side note- this place is not inexpensive. 

hubby and i ordered apps- he got zinger boneless wings, and i got the guacamole. portion size was ENORMOUS on the guac - it could have served 8 people, seriously.  flavor was meh. apparently the wingz were good.  hard to tell what hubby enjoyed more, the wingz or the scantily dressed hostesses. 

our server was great, attentive and pleasant.  When something went wrong she did her best to fix it. That was much appreciated.   Side salad came out wilted and gross. management offered to take it off the check, would have rather had a decent salad in the first place but i digress.  Dinner was not very flavorful - at all - and portion sizes were okay. i got the quesadilla appetizer (which was plenty for an entree) but it was very sloppily put together and had no seasoning at all.  I have had food that is presented better and tastes better at fast food restaurants, where i am happy to pay $5 for a meal.  

At the end of the meal, i badly wanted dessert but didnt want to risk another poorly flavored dish.  Not to mention, all the dishes were like lunch tray plastic, and i felt that a $50-60 dinner for two was at least worth a nicer presentation. who knows, it may have even made up for the bland flavors. 

perhaps i was let down by the fact that there always seemed to be a wait and i had over hyped it in my head.  Never have i wanted to send back everything i ordered at a restaurant before this night.  i will never be back.  my husband says he will order the wings, but takeout only. no more dining in at this place.
Rewrite this for me:
Oh Millers, I really wanted to like you. Your location is convenient, there's plenty of parking, and your tables are spacious. You even have a cozy fireplace in the back for some added ambiance.

My friends and I tried to dine here a couple of times for a quick and affordable meal, but each time we faced a 30-60 minute wait. We initially thought it meant you must be really good, but perhaps it just means people in Springfield settle for below-average dining experiences. On a side note, this place is not as inexpensive as we thought.

My husband and I ordered some appetizers - he got the zinger boneless wings and I went for the guacamole. The portion size of the guacamole was enormous, it could have easily fed eight people. Unfortunately, the flavor was mediocre. Apparently, the wings were good. It's hard to say what my husband enjoyed more, the wings or the hostesses dressed in revealing attire.

Our server was wonderful, attentive, and pleasant. Whenever something went wrong, she did her best to fix it, which we appreciated. However, the side salad that came out was wilted and unappetizing. The management offered to remove it from our bill, but we would have preferred a decent salad to begin with. As for dinner, it lacked flavor entirely, and the portion sizes were just okay. I ordered the quesadilla appetizer, which was more than enough for an entree, but it was carelessly assembled and completely lacking in seasoning. I've had better-tasting and better-presented food at fast food restaurants for only $5.

By the end of the meal, I was really craving dessert, but I didn't want to risk disappointment with another poorly flavored dish. Additionally, all the plates and utensils seemed cheap, like something you'd find on a school lunch tray. Considering we paid $50-60 for our dinner as a couple, I expected a nicer presentation to justify the bland flavors.

Maybe I was let down because of the persistent wait times and the high expectations I had built up in my mind. Until that night, I had never wanted to send back every item I ordered at a restaurant. I won't be returning, but my husband plans to order the wings for takeout only. No more dining in at that place for us.
