input:
I am sort of a simple man, so I had never been to a liquor bar before. I have been to The Libertine twice and had a good experience both times. They use fresh ingredients all the way down to the crushed ice, which they crush with a mallet right at the bar. 

The biggest problem I ran into was figuring out which restroom was the men's. You have to look at the hair on the dimly lit pictures that indicate which is which, all the faces look the same.
Rewrite this for me:
As someone who considers myself quite uncomplicated, I had never visited a liquor bar before. However, I have had the pleasure of going to The Libertine on two occasions and both times were delightful experiences. They take pride in using fresh ingredients, even going so far as to crush the ice right in front of you at the bar.

The only challenge I faced was determining which restroom was designated for men. In the dimly lit area, I had to rely on the hair depicted in the faintly illuminated pictures to distinguish between the two, as all the faces appeared identical.

input: Came with the family based on a recommendation and was not disappointed.  I consider myself to be a bit of a Pizza connoisseur and this was right up there.  The staff was friendly and the food came out quick.  Solid experience across the board.  I would come back and recommend it to others.
Rewrite this for me: My family and I came to this place based on a recommendation and we were not let down. Being someone who prides themselves as a Pizza enthusiast, this place lived up to my expectations. The staff was welcoming and the food was served promptly. Overall, it was a delightful experience. I would definitely return and recommend it to others.

input: We tried these at the Collingswood Art Festival this weekend. they are a bit pricey, but worth it. The flavor is perfect. they aren't greasy. I will be seeking them out. Once you try them... you will want to have them again. they are a light cheddar curd, battered and friend. You don't taste grease or batter. the flavor of the cheese is delicious, and so stringy and melty. The sauces are a delicate compliment to the curd. Well worth the splurge.
Rewrite this for me: We sampled these delectable treats at the Collingswood Art Festival over the weekend. Although they may be on the pricier side, they are absolutely worth it. The flavor is simply exquisite, and what's even better is that they are not greasy at all. In fact, you won't even notice any trace of grease or batter. These light cheddar curds, coated in a delightful batter and fried to perfection, are irresistible. Once you give them a try, you'll find yourself craving them time and time again. The cheese has a delicious taste and its texture is both stringy and melty. The sauces accompanying the curds provide a delicate and complementary touch. Splurging on these treats is definitely a worthwhile experience.

input:
Yats rocks. You walk in and they've got 4-6 cauldrons full of your choices...which are written in sidewalk chalk on a blackboard. There's always something vegetarian, and a plate full of any of it costs five fitty. Add a buck and you can get a split plate of 2 delectable cajun creations with rice. But the best part is the ridiculously awesome garlic bread...which you can get a bowl of for like a buck.

Not only is the food awesome, but the owner (Joe Vuskovich) is a local celebrity. He's a famed restaurateur from New Orleans that sells his secret spice to restaurants everywhere. Everybody in town knows him (despite the fact that there are two other locations) and he's highly supportive of local bands and kids that most older people stay away from.
Rewrite this for me:
Yats is amazing. Upon entering, you'll find 4-6 cauldrons brimming with an array of choices, all beautifully displayed on a blackboard with sidewalk chalk. They always have a vegetarian option available, and a generous portion of any dish costs just five dollars and fifty cents. For an extra dollar, you can even enjoy a split plate of two delectable Cajun creations served with rice. But the absolute highlight is their unbelievably delicious garlic bread, which you can enjoy in a bowl for just a dollar.

Not only is the food exceptional, but the owner, Joe Vuskovich, is a local icon. Hailing from New Orleans, he is renowned as a successful restaurateur who has shared his secret spices with restaurants far and wide. Despite having two other locations, he is a well-known figure in town, respected by everyone. Joe is also incredibly supportive of local bands and embraces the younger crowd that some older folks tend to shy away from.

input:
Today after our Ethiopian food fiasco (see Selam review), we literally RAN into Pi after waiting hours to be served at the prior restaurant. We must have looked like a pack of hungry wolves so we told the hostess what had just happened. She seated us right away and sent us two orders of garlic bread (which we later found out were comped!). 

We ordered two pizzas and scarfed it all down. Pi has been consistently good on every visit I have made since I've moved to STL. Service is always excellent. Both the deep dish and thin crust are amazing every time.
Rewrite this for me:
After our disastrous Ethiopian food experience, which you can read about in our Selam review, we coincidentally stumbled upon Pi while desperately waiting for service at the previous restaurant. I suppose we must have appeared famished, like a pack of ravenous wolves, so we decided to recount our unfortunate ordeal to the hostess. Surprisingly, she promptly seated us and even treated us to two complimentary orders of garlic bread, a delightful surprise we discovered later.

Without hesitation, we ordered two pizzas and devoured them with gusto. Pi has consistently impressed me every time I have visited since relocating to STL. The service is consistently outstanding, and both their deep dish and thin crust pizzas never fail to amaze.

input: I went here to get my wisdom teeth out and they did a great job. The only complaint I have is that I never see the same dentist. I've been going here for 5 years.
Rewrite this for me: I came to this place to have my wisdom teeth extracted and they performed an excellent job. The only issue I have is the lack of consistency with the dentists; I've been coming here for five years and never see the same one.

input:
After hearing about this place from a fellow Yelp Elite, my SO and I decided to try this place! We were warned of possible waiting times so came here on a Saturday around 10:45, and a line was already forming! 

For apps, we ordered the takoyaki and fried octopus. The takoyaki are delicious-an order comes with 5 balls that were perfectly cooked and topped with sauces. Takoyaki are little circular doughs with squid in the middle, topped with sauces and squid flakes (?). I definitely recommend this app. As for the fried octopus, it was just fried without sauces on top and came with mayo on the side, but it didn't come with enough mayo to dip the octopus in.

For ramen, I got the red spicy tonkotsu ramen and my SO got the black garlic tonkotsu ramen. For both ramen, the thin noodles were mushy/overcooked and just didn't quite fit with the ramen. That was the flaw with the dishes, and it tasted like the noodles were overcooked in a pot of flour-y water so it wasn't as clean (which explains the mushy feeling). They should use more bouncy noodles for this.

Now let's talk about the broth. The broth is flavorful, but the red chili broth was a bit too spicy for me and covered up the depth of the broth. I prefer the black garlic tonkotsu broth for that reason.

Overall, delicious food and pricing is reasonable. The decor is very nice as well, but screaming kids that were running around didn't make our meal pleasant.
Rewrite this for me:
Upon receiving a recommendation from a fellow Yelp Elite, my significant other and I decided to give this place a try! We were informed about potential wait times, so we arrived on a Saturday around 10:45, only to find a line already forming!

For appetizers, we opted for the takoyaki and fried octopus. The takoyaki was absolutely delightful - a serving comprised of 5 perfectly cooked balls topped with delectable sauces. These little circular doughs filled with squid and garnished with sauces and squid flakes are a definite must-try. As for the fried octopus, it was simply fried without any toppings and served with a side of mayo. However, the portion of mayo provided was insufficient for dipping the octopus.

Moving on to the ramen, I ordered the red spicy tonkotsu ramen, while my significant other went for the black garlic tonkotsu ramen. Unfortunately, the thin noodles in both bowls were overcooked and mushy, which didn't quite complement the ramen well. This was the main flaw in the dishes, as it felt as though the noodles had been overcooked in starchy water, resulting in a less clean taste. A better choice would be to use more springy noodles.

Now, onto the broth. The broth itself was flavorful, but the spiciness of the red chili broth overshadowed the complexity of the broth. Personally, I preferred the black garlic tonkotsu broth for that reason.

Overall, the food was delicious and reasonably priced. The decor of the place was also quite appealing, although the presence of loud, unruly children running around made our dining experience less pleasant.

input: Hands down best breakfast in Philly!  I've only been here for four months, but I have tried nearly every "Best of" spot in town.  I'm a breakfast fanatic so I get little over critical.  However, this small cafe has managed to create incredible flavor while keeping their dishes fresh and simplistic.  While the actual space is "cozy," this menu could easily keep a place as big as Parc overflowing with patrons.
Rewrite this for me: Without a doubt, the top breakfast spot in Philadelphia! Although I've only been in town for four months, I've explored nearly every restaurant that claims to have the best breakfast. Being a breakfast aficionado, I tend to be overly critical, but this charming little cafe has impressed me with their delicious flavors and simple yet fresh dishes. Despite its cozy size, the menu here could easily rival that of a larger establishment like Parc and attract a steady stream of customers.

input: If I could give this place 6 stars I would. Don't let the looks deceive you, great diner food. Biscuits and gravy were incredible. Portions were more than I could eat.
Rewrite this for me: If I had the option to rate this place with 6 stars, I definitely would. Despite its appearance, the diner serves exceptional food. The biscuits and gravy were absolutely fantastic, and the portions were so generous that I couldn't finish everything.

input:
This place is hip.  Perhaps too hip for many over 35 but if you can tolerate the boisterous and extremely casually attired youth--I haven't worn a suit in 20 years either but even 20 year olds should have something besides skinny jeans and T-shirts with borderline obscene slogans in their closets--the food is worth it and the staff copes well.   

I had a 6:00 reservation (obtained the day before) but the sky seemed threatening a downpour so I came early to avoid it and was seated 20 minutes or so before the appointed time.  I often don't even make reservations and have no trouble getting seated at popular places by being there when they open or, for those open all day, coming before the popular dinner hour, but that didn't work the day before at Lüke.  Even at 4:30 the place was packed so I did make one for the following day.

My meal started with the crispy Brussel Sprouts.  Even if you hate Brussels sprouts (I like them), don't be afraid to try this dish--if no one told you you might not know what you were eating.  They are in some sort of sweet/sour sauce/dressing and fried both slightly blackened and crispy as advertised . . . tossed with almond slices, small bits of jalapeño and sprinkled with shavings of cheese on top.

Then I had pork schnitzel and "pommes frites" (that's shoestring fries to the Galliphobes).  It came with whitish gravy in a pitcher, I suppose to make it "Southern".  The gravy was good but I skipped eating it, doing that the usual way with a squeeze of lemon.  It was excellent and the fries were fine too.

I finished with some excellent decaf and a glass of Kahlua--I had had iced tea with the meal so some alcohol was not an excess.

A lady who was some sort of hostess dropped by my table while I was eating to make sure everything was OK and when told I needed ketchup (for the fries), went and got me some (in a dainty little single-serve Heinz bottle).  My waiter also checked several times but didn't hover.

I am giving it 4 stars.  The 5th star is withheld because of the crowded dining room and noise level . . . nothing to do with the food which I greatly enjoyed.
Rewrite this for me:
This place is trendy, maybe even too trendy for people over 35, but if you can handle the loud and casually dressed young crowd - I haven't worn a suit in 20 years either, but even 20-year-olds should have more variety in their closets than just skinny jeans and T-shirts with borderline inappropriate slogans - the food is worth it and the staff handles things well.

I had made a 6:00 reservation (made the day before), but the weather looked like it was about to pour, so I arrived early to avoid it. I was seated about 20 minutes before my reservation time. Usually, I don't bother with reservations and I'm able to get a table at popular places by being there when they open, or if they're open all day, coming in before the dinner rush. However, that tactic didn't work at Lüke the day before. Even at 4:30, the place was packed, so I made a reservation for the following day.

I started my meal with the crispy Brussels sprouts. Even if you dislike Brussels sprouts (I happen to like them), don't hesitate to try this dish - if no one told you, you might not even realize what you're eating. They're cooked in a slightly sweet and sour sauce/dressing and fried to a crispy, slightly charred perfection as advertised. They're tossed with almond slices, small bits of jalapeño, and sprinkled with cheese shavings on top.

Next, I had the pork schnitzel with "pommes frites" (just thin shoestring fries for those who aren't fans of French terminology). The dish came with a white gravy on the side, presumably to give it a Southern touch. The gravy was good, but I preferred to skip it and instead squeeze some lemon over the schnitzel, which was excellent. The fries were also tasty.

To end the meal, I had a great cup of decaf coffee and a glass of Kahlua. Since I had iced tea with my meal, I didn't feel like having alcohol in excess.

During my meal, a lady who seemed to be a hostess stopped by my table to check if everything was alright. When I mentioned that I needed ketchup for my fries, she promptly brought me a dainty single-serve Heinz bottle. My waiter also checked on me multiple times but didn't hover.

I'm giving this place 4 stars. I'm withholding the 5th star because the dining room was crowded and the noise level was high, but that has nothing to do with the quality of the food, which I greatly enjoyed.

input: Beers were amazing! I got the porter, the double IPA and the table gutt and they were all fantastic. Food was also killer if you like Russian cuisine. They had a special when I went with a sausage and sauerkraut which was tasty. I also got the pickled everything appetizer, great choice. This place rules.
Rewrite this for me: The beers at this place were absolutely incredible! I tried the porter, the double IPA, and the table gutt, and they were all absolutely fantastic. If you happen to enjoy Russian cuisine, you'll be pleased to know that the food here is also outstanding. During my visit, they had a special featuring a delicious sausage and sauerkraut, which I highly recommend. Additionally, I couldn't resist ordering the pickled everything appetizer, and it turned out to be an excellent choice. In sum, this place is absolutely amazing.

input: There are a ton of good sushi places in Reno and I have tried them all, but it always seems like Rickshaw has the freshest fish. I'm not a big fan of rolls and sauces, and opt mainly for Nigiri or sashimi. You can get some dressed up roll anywhere, hell you can buy them in the store, but if you are a true fan of sushi, just fish is where its at and Rickshaw has some of the freshest in town.
Rewrite this for me: I have had the opportunity to explore numerous sushi establishments in Reno, and among them all, Rickshaw consistently stands out with its exceptionally fresh fish. Personally, I am not particularly fond of rolls adorned with various sauces; instead, I tend to lean towards enjoying the simplicity of Nigiri or sashimi. Any place can provide you with fancy, elaborately crafted rolls, even those readily available in stores. However, for true sushi aficionados like myself, the emphasis lies in the quality of the fish itself, and in this aspect, Rickshaw truly excels by offering some of the freshest options in town.

input: This was my 1st visit here.  Overall, not that impressed!  To start with parking was really bad!  There are good choices of beer on draft.  The food was ok.  We split a few appetizers.  The fried olives were very tasty & different!  The rest of the appetizers were ok: the blue cheese chips, calamari, & meat/cheese platter.  I would try this place again, but overall not thrilled!
Rewrite this for me: This was my first time here, and honestly, I wasn't really impressed. The parking situation was terrible right from the start. On a positive note, they do offer a decent selection of draft beers. As for the food, it was just okay. We decided to share a few appetizers, and I must say, the fried olives were quite tasty and unique. However, the rest of the appetizers, including the blue cheese chips, calamari, and meat/cheese platter, were just average. Perhaps I would consider giving this place another chance, but all in all, I wasn't thrilled with my experience.

input: Really not sure what the hype was when it opened. It's fine, the ambiance was nice, but the menu is limited and food is nothing to write home about. They are in a nice location so at least if you decide to wait, then you have things to see...
Rewrite this for me: I'm honestly not quite sure what the fuss was about when this place first opened. It's decent, the atmosphere is pleasant, but the menu is quite restricted and the food doesn't really leave an impression. However, they do have a great location, so if you end up waiting, at least you'll have some interesting sights to enjoy.

input:
This place was amazing! I only tried their ice cream I really wanted to try the hot chocolate but didn't get a chance :(. Well the ice cream was great! The first night I came here I got a brownie sundae all for myself, brownie on the bottom and three scoops of ice cream topped with whipped cream and nuts. I finished it all happily! I chose pumpkin cake flavor which was delicious and smooth. I also got pralines and cream that was better than other praline ice creams. The Tennessee fudge was vanilla with fudge swirled it was good not too special. 

The next time I came I got nutter butter ice cream that was really good had cookie pieces in it! I got the hot fudge topping over it and that was a great combination. 

The service was great the workers were really nice and patient with me haha indecisive! They would joke around with me and let me sample all I wanted. Also no judgement for eating all the brownie sundae alone :) lol
Rewrite this for me:
I had an amazing experience at this place! Although I only tried their ice cream and didn't get a chance to try their hot chocolate, I was not disappointed. On my first visit, I treated myself to a brownie sundae that consisted of a brownie at the bottom, three scoops of ice cream, whipped cream, and nuts. It was absolutely delicious, and I happily finished it all. I opted for the pumpkin cake flavor, which was delightful and had a smooth texture. The pralines and cream flavor exceeded my expectations compared to other praline ice creams. The Tennessee fudge flavor, however, was good but nothing out of the ordinary as it was simply vanilla with fudge swirls.

On my next visit, I tried the nutter butter ice cream, which was really good and had cookie pieces in it. I topped it off with hot fudge, and it was a fantastic combination.

The service at this place was excellent. The staff members were incredibly friendly and patient with me, even though I couldn't make up my mind easily. They would joke around with me and allowed me to sample as much ice cream as I wanted. I also appreciated that they didn't judge me for devouring the entire brownie sundae by myself. It was a fun and enjoyable experience overall.

input:
My dad and I were here for lunch and after reading some of the reviews, I was excited to check out this restaurant located where an O'Henry's once stood.

The place was fairly empty at 1 on a Friday and we were lead upstairs. Honestly, there's not much going on up there and it was a bit warm, but we decided to stick it out. Everything on the menu looked great and I decided to get the Catfish Acadian, which is catfish topped with crawfish and sauce with a side of vegetables. My dad got the pork chop.

My dish was great! I have no idea what was in the sauce but it was delicious and it was a perfect pairing with the fish. The vegetables were also really good; they were nicely cooked and fresh. My dad wasn't overly blown away by his pork chop, so if you find yourself here you might want to stick to the seafood.

Bria was our waitress and she was wonderful! She was attentive, kept the fresh iced tea coming and she was extremely personable. She was probably the highlight of the visit.

I'm not sure if I would go back. The food was good, but the atmosphere left something to be desired and I feel like I can get good catfish at plenty of places without going out of my way. I might go back at dinner, when the weather is cooler, and sit on the balcony outside as Harry suggested.
Rewrite this for me:
My father and I decided to have lunch here after hearing about it in some reviews. The restaurant is located at the site of the former O'Henry's, which piqued my interest.

When we arrived at 1 o'clock on a Friday, the place was quite empty. We were guided to the upstairs area, which didn't have much happening and felt a bit warm. However, we chose to stay anyway. The menu had an array of enticing options and I opted for the Catfish Acadian – a catfish dish topped with crawfish and a delectable sauce, served with vegetables. My dad went for the pork chop.

I thoroughly enjoyed my dish! The sauce, although I couldn't discern its ingredients, was absolutely delicious and paired perfectly with the catfish. The vegetables were also fresh and cooked to perfection. However, my dad was not particularly impressed with his pork chop, so if you visit this place, seafood might be the better choice.

Our waitress, Bria, was wonderful! She was attentive, constantly refilling our iced tea, and had a delightful personality. She truly stood out during our visit.

As for returning, I'm still uncertain. While the food was good, the ambiance was lacking, and I believe there are plenty of other places where I can find tasty catfish without going out of my way. Perhaps I might consider returning for dinner, when the outside weather is cooler, and sit on the balcony as recommended by Harry.

input:
Well, well.... Where do I start with this place? First time experience, went in with my partner.

Walking in at about 7:30 on a Friday night (st paddys day weekend even)  and the  place had about 4 customers. That should have been my first clue as to what our experience was going to be like.

We seated ourselves and the waitress, an older gal maybe mid to late 40's who had greasy stringy unwashed hair and rotting teeth came up and took our drink order. My girlfriend got a Dr. Pepper and I got a water. She brought out Coke instead of DP. No biggie. We let it go, assuming it was an honest mistake. After about 10 minutes she returns and we order a 12 piece "jumbo" wing basket ($11.99), a 6 piece($7.99), and a beer batter sampler($11.99). 20 minutes pass and finally here comes our appetizer. The waitress throws the basket of appetizers on the table  and says "here's your food." Very flat with a big attitude and walks off. The beer battered mushrooms were doughy and undercooked. We had a single half full ranch cup to share between us for the big platter and she avoided our table when she saw we needed more.
***let me note that this waitress is giving the customers at the 3 tables surrounding us WAY better customer service. Even brought their food out in a timely manner with no attitude whatsoever.
I decide to let the mushrooms slide for the moment. I used to work in a restaurant and I understand that mistakes happen, however this far into the experience I'm being mighty generous since it's a first time experience.
We finish our appetizer and we wait and wait and wait and finally she comes by and takes the platter returning 10 minutes later with our wings. She makes no inquiry about the broken open, clearly undercooked, mushrooms still sitting on the platter.
I got the 12 piece with a single half full ranch. Again. Food on the table, doesn't ask if we need anything else which is something she is doing for other customers. at this point we have been here for about 40 minutes.

I got half regular and half thai flavor. The wings were NOT jumbo. They were puny. The flavor was good for the thai, and the waitress even stopped by to check up on us, though I wouldn't consider walking by quickly and saying in your flat attitude tone "youguysdoingalright?okaycool." Really all that helpful since she came and went so fast it took me a second to understand her. I had to reiterate for my girlfriend.  When I started on the regular I bit into my drumstick and had to fish a feather out of my mouth. DISGUSTING. It was that point that the entire experience was completely and thoroughly unacceptable.  The wings were soggy because they batter them or something on top of all that.  At first I had no plans other than to pay for the meal and leave the waitress 2 pennies and be on my merry way. But when the waitress came and asked if we needed a box I said no with 6 wings still on my plate, OBVIOUS SOMETHING WAS WRONG, again. She was going to take my stuff and make no inquiry to right the situation. I asked for the manager. Took a minute but finally the manager came over (mind you it is still pretty dead, what are these people doing I wonder?) I explained the food issues but blew off bringing up our treatment by the waitress. Normally I give the benefit of the doubt on this one but it was blatantly obvious that we were being treated differently with a different attitude than other patrons because we are a same-sex couple. Like our table had a contagious disease that prevented us from getting food in a timely manner, and getting drink and condiment refills too, regardless of the *empty* cups on the edge of the table. It wasn't like we were off in the distance. She had to walk by our table every time to communicate with the surrounding tables.

Anyways. The manager experience wasn't the greatest, but I wasn't going to pay for that meal after the feather thing, and she comped everything. BUT only after slightly arguing with us about the undercooked mushrooms, which by the way come frozen which  makes the fact that they weren't cooked all the way acceptable I guess? Don't know. Don't care. I WILL NOT BE GOING BACK!!!

2 stars because they did comp the meal, the waitress got lucky. If I would have had to pay for anything she wouldn't have gotten a tip due to the attitude but we left her $4 anyway since we didn't have to pay for the meal.  THAT IS THE ONLY REASON.
1 star though for the overall experience. Same-sex couples, steer clear. You aren't welcome there and it's obvious.
Rewrite this for me:
Where do I even begin with this place? My partner and I decided to give it a try for the first time. We walked in on a Friday night around 7:30, during St. Patrick's Day weekend, and there were only about 4 other customers. That should have been a sign of what was to come.

We found a seat ourselves and were approached by our waitress, an older woman in her late 40s with greasy, unwashed hair and rotting teeth. She took our drink order, but instead of bringing my girlfriend a Dr. Pepper, she brought her a Coke. We brushed it off as an honest mistake and placed our food order after waiting for about 10 minutes. We ordered a 12-piece "jumbo" wing basket, a 6-piece wing basket, and a beer batter sampler.

After waiting for 20 minutes, our appetizers finally arrived. The waitress simply threw the basket onto our table without any enthusiasm and said, "here's your food" with a rude attitude before walking off. The beer-battered mushrooms were undercooked and doughy. To make matters worse, we had only one partially filled ranch cup to share between us for the entire platter, and she ignored us when we tried to get her attention for more.

What bothered us the most was that the waitress was providing exceptional service to the customers at the other tables surrounding us. Their food was served promptly and without any attitude whatsoever. Despite this, we decided to let the undercooked mushrooms slide for the moment, assuming that mistakes happen in restaurants.

We finished our appetizer and waited and waited for our wings. Finally, the waitress came by and took away our platter, only to return 10 minutes later with our wings. She didn't even bother asking about the undercooked mushrooms still sitting on the platter. I received my 12-piece wing basket with only one partially filled ranch cup again. At this point, we had been waiting for about 40 minutes.

The wings were disappointingly small and not what I would consider "jumbo." The Thai flavor was decent, and the waitress briefly checked on us, albeit in a rushed and unhelpful manner. However, when I bit into one of the regular wings, I found a feather in my mouth, which was absolutely disgusting. This incident made the entire experience completely unacceptable. Additionally, the wings were soggy, possibly due to the way they were battered.

Initially, I had planned to pay for the meal and leave the waitress a minimal tip of 2 pennies. But when she offered to box up my remaining wings without even acknowledging that something was wrong, I asked for the manager. After a short wait, the manager finally came over. I explained the issues with the food but chose not to mention our treatment by the waitress. It was painfully obvious that we were being treated differently because we are a same-sex couple. It felt as though our table had some contagious disease that prevented us from receiving timely service, refills, or even basic attention, despite our empty cups on the table. The manager's response wasn't great, but she eventually comped our entire meal.

I won't be going back to this place. They get 2 stars only because they comped the meal, and the waitress got lucky by receiving a $4 tip from us. If we had to pay for anything, she wouldn't have received a tip due to her attitude. Overall, I give them 1 star because of the terrible experience. I advise same-sex couples to steer clear because it's clear that they aren't welcome there.

input: Why don't we have a Target?  I thought K-Mart was going out of business.  Well not this one, this miserable son of a bitch refuses to die.  They had the audacity to try to update it.  It reminds me of Jack Palance its old, tired, and smells funny, but it ain't going know where.    I wish a shiny new Target would come along and stab this relic of a store through the heart with its superior retail sword.  I have experienced on no less than 5 occasions of a product being labeled as on sale only to be charged full price at the counter.  Then I have to stop the line to back to the aisle and grab the sign to show it to the cashier.  Once I bought a beach chair here, well my wife saw the dopeness of said chair and wanted to copy me.  I return to the store the next day (happened to be 80 degrees and sunny) and those SOB's raised the price of the chair $10.  I was pissed yo.
Rewrite this for me:
Why don't we have a Target store? I remember hearing that K-Mart was closing down, but this particular branch seems determined to stay alive. They even had the nerve to try updating it, but it's still old, worn-out, and has a strange smell that never seems to go away. I wish a brand new Target would come along and put this outdated store out of its misery with its superior retail offerings. 

To make matters worse, I've had at least five instances where a product was labeled as being on sale, but I was charged the full price at the checkout counter. I had to interrupt the line and go back to the aisle to grab the sign as proof for the cashier. 

Another time, I bought a beach chair here, and the next day (which happened to be a hot and sunny day), those frustrating individuals increased the price of the chair by $10. I was extremely angry about it.

input:
Don't let the outside fool you-this place is much cuter and nicer inside than you would expect! 

Food is good and reasonably  priced. We ordered papaya salad, triple flavor duck, and king tofu soup. Papaya salad is always refreshing, but this place overdoes it on the fish sauce. Anything triple flavor is always a safe but delicious choice. I would say their king soup, with choice of protein, is a winner. 

And also, BYO!
Rewrite this for me: Despite its unassuming exterior, this establishment surprises with its charming and inviting interior. The food offered here is of excellent quality and comes at a reasonable price. Our order consisted of papaya salad, triple flavor duck, and king tofu soup. The papaya salad provided a refreshing experience, although it was a bit heavy on the fish sauce. Opting for anything labeled as "triple flavor" is always a safe and delightful choice. The standout dish, however, was the king soup, which allows you to choose your preferred protein. Additionally, it's worth noting that this place allows you to bring your own beverages.

input:
I feel so comfortable with the Mazzoni Center.  I, and many others, am incredibly lucky and grateful that these services exist.  Going through all sorts of life challenges can be painful and frightening when you know you're assumed to be a certain way.  Here, there are no assumptions.  They know who they're working with, and they are sensitive without the need to pry for information.  If you're in need of gynecology and you're not a woman, for example, they know exactly how to handle your needs while prioritizing respect for your identity.

My biggest concern is the physical space in which the Mazzoni Center clinic exists.  I feel sort of exposed in the waiting room.  I hope that they someday have the funds to upgrade to a larger, more private space.

If you visit during youth drop-in hours rather than making an appointment, you will probably wait a very long time to see someone.  This is completely understandable, in my opinion.  They'll advise you regarding what time you should show up if you call.

Occasionally, I've noticed lapses in communication; I have been kept waiting in the exam room before with no one around and no idea how much longer I would have to wait.  This is not a common issue, and I find that, overall, I receive more attentive service here than at any other clinic I've visited.

Be aware that the doctor you want to speak with may not always be available over the phone.  Don't be afraid to leave messages with reception.  You'll always receive quick assistance.
Rewrite this for me:
I have a strong sense of comfort when it comes to the Mazzoni Center. It's a fortunate and grateful feeling shared by myself and many others, knowing that these crucial services exist. Going through various challenges in life can be painful and scary, especially when you feel like people make assumptions about you. However, at the Mazzoni Center, there are no assumptions. They truly understand the individuals they work with and approach every situation with sensitivity while respecting your identity.

One aspect that concerns me is the physical space of the Mazzoni Center clinic. When I'm in the waiting room, I can't help but feel a bit exposed. I hope that in the future, they are able to secure the funds necessary to upgrade to a larger, more private space.

If you choose to visit during youth drop-in hours instead of making an appointment, it's important to note that there may be a significant wait time before you can see someone. Personally, I find this understandable. If you call ahead, they will advise you on when to arrive.

On occasion, I have experienced lapses in communication where I have been left waiting in the exam room without any staff around and unsure of how much longer I would have to wait. Although this doesn't happen often, overall, I feel that the service I receive at the Mazzoni Center is more attentive compared to other clinics I've been to.

Keep in mind that the specific doctor you wish to speak with may not always be available for a phone conversation. Don't hesitate to leave a message with reception, as they are always quick to provide assistance.

input:
If I could give half a star I would, I'm from Tx, and anyone that thinks this is BBQ, I am willing to apologize to you for being led to believe that this is what BBQ is like.
I ordered the sample platter, horrific, the chicken looked and tasted like frozen pressed meat, the ribs.... All cartilage, the sausage, bland.... The sauce.... Walmart basic sauce with cups of sugar thrown in.... Extremely overpriced for ummm.... A child's plate (what it seemed like). I would never recommend this place to anyone.
Rewrite this for me: If I had the option, I would give this place half a star. As a Texan, I feel genuinely sorry if you believe this is what BBQ is supposed to be. I ordered their sample platter and it was a horrible experience. The chicken seemed artificial and tasted like frozen processed meat. The ribs were nothing but cartilage, and the sausage was dull and flavorless. As for the sauce, it tasted like a generic Walmart sauce with an excessive amount of sugar added to it. The prices were ridiculously high for what seemed like a portion fit for a child. I cannot, in good conscience, recommend this place to anyone.

input:
Really great place for wine!

Came here with my dining group, there was about 20 of us on a Friday, for their Happy Hour. Excellent wine happy hour where all glasses are $5 or you can take $5 off any bottle of wine, which is a great deal if you're sharing with a few people...great way to try a few bottles.

The food was also great! Cheese plates are the way to go here! Excellent selections! Several of my foodie friends ordered sandwiches, which looked & smelled amazing! They all raved about them!

The ambiance is very warm and inviting! They do a great job decorating, especially around the holidays! My favorite space is the enclosed patio area, adjacent to the main dining area. Super warm and romantic on those cold winter evenings! 

The service is great as well!
Rewrite this for me:
This place is truly amazing for wine! I went with a large group on a Friday for their Happy Hour, and it was fantastic. Their wine happy hour offers all glasses for $5, or you can get a $5 discount on any bottle of wine. It's a great deal if you're with a few people and want to try different varieties.

The food here is also exceptional! The cheese plates are a must-try, with an incredible selection. Many of my foodie friends ordered sandwiches, and they were both visually and aromatically delightful. They couldn't stop raving about them!

The ambiance of this place is warm and inviting. The decoration, especially during the holidays, is top-notch. My personal favorite is the enclosed patio area, which is right next to the main dining space. It's incredibly cozy and romantic, perfect for those chilly winter nights.

Lastly, the service is top-notch. The staff is friendly and attentive, making sure you have a great experience from start to finish.

input: Rude staff. Can't even get a salad order right. Overpriced by the slice. When we sat down to wait for our food I thought wow this is taking a long time given the fact we were the only people in there. I guess it should stay that way. Don't waste your money.
Rewrite this for me: The staff is extremely rude and incapable of accurately fulfilling a simple salad order. Moreover, the prices for individual slices are unreasonably high. As we patiently waited for our food, it became apparent that the service was unusually slow, despite the fact that we were the only customers present. Perhaps it's best if this establishment remains empty. Save your money and avoid this place altogether.

input: Really good, really authentic! This is some of the BEST Mexican cuisine I've tasted since my nana cooked for me; I'm from California so I would know. The enchiladas w/mole are awesome and the carne asada tacos remind me of Rosarito Beach, yummy!
Rewrite this for me: Absolutely fantastic, incredibly genuine! This Mexican cuisine is truly remarkable, reminding me of the outstanding dishes my nana used to prepare for me. As a Californian, I have great knowledge in this area. The enchiladas with mole sauce are exceptional, and the carne asada tacos transport me back to the delightful flavors of Rosarito Beach. Simply scrumptious!

input:
You need a Cinnamon Roll from the bake house.  You probably need two; life would have just a little less happiness and light without their Cinnamon Rolls.
The coffee and salads are also excellent, a lovely Saturday morning breakfast treat.
Rewrite this for me: The bake house offers irresistible Cinnamon Rolls that you must have. One is simply not enough; their absence would diminish a sprinkle of joy and brightness from your life. Additionally, their delectable coffee and salads make for a delightful Saturday morning breakfast indulgence.

input: I had the carrot cake.... Very disappointed tasted like licorice and baking soda cooking powder. It's too bad because everything looks so delicious :( also didn't like the chocolate chips in it either.
Rewrite this for me: I tried the carrot cake, but to my disappointment, it tasted strongly of licorice and baking soda. It's unfortunate since everything else seemed so appetizing. Additionally, I wasn't a fan of the chocolate chips added to it either.

input: You can't beat the prices for the unlimited food, but I've had better. The sushi is delicious, the salad was subpar and the crab Rangoon was probably the worst I've had. I've been twice and would definitely go again.
Rewrite this for me: The prices for the unlimited food are unbeatable, although I've had more satisfying experiences elsewhere. The sushi is delightful, however, the salad leaves something to be desired and the crab Rangoon is arguably the worst I've ever tasted. Despite the mixed review, I have visited the place twice and would certainly consider going again.

input: Best chicken you could ever hope for in bourbon st. The chicken is good. The sauce is good. Everything is goof
Rewrite this for me: You won't find a better chicken experience on Bourbon St. The chicken is absolutely delicious, the sauce is fantastic, and overall, everything is excellent.

input:
Reviewing the food.
Hard to justify $16 for a burger and fries BUT wowow this burger was so delicious. I'm not sure if I was just starving but ordered the Lama burger and the patty size is quality. They also have random ingredients thrown in that you probably haven't seen before like gruyere stuffed in a pepper on your burger. Fries came out nice and crisp vs. soggy and the bun on that burger was great. You order inside by the Nook and then can sit around. They have tons of craft beer to choose from and I could see this place getting packed on the weekends.
Rewrite this for me: It's quite a challenge to justify paying $16 for a burger and fries; however, I must say, this burger exceeded my expectations. Maybe it was because I was really hungry, but the Lama burger's patty size was truly satisfying. What sets it apart are the unexpected and unique ingredients, such as gruyere stuffed in a pepper on top of the burger. The fries were cooked to perfection - crispy instead of soggy - and the bun was top-notch. To place your order, you go inside the Nook and then find a seat. The restaurant also offers an impressive selection of craft beers, which I can imagine draws a crowd on the weekends.

input: Stopped in for breakfast on 12/2/17 I used to like it here for breakfast.  Service was slow coffee was not hot, grits were only warm and twenty minute wait for cinnamon biscuit after breakfast was brought to table then ten minutes to pay at counter to get out of the place there are better places to get breakfast in the area.  Should have went with my first choice instead of here.
Rewrite this for me: I dropped by for breakfast on December 2nd, 2017, expecting to enjoy a satisfying meal like I used to. However, I was disappointed with the slow service, cold coffee, lukewarm grits, and a lengthy wait of twenty minutes for a cinnamon biscuit after my breakfast was served. To make matters worse, it took an additional ten minutes to pay at the counter and leave the establishment. All in all, there are definitely better breakfast options available in the area, and I regret not choosing my initial preference instead of coming here.

input: simply the best! everything from here is good! I come from a very Italian family and whenever there is a family event, there is always Termini brothers dessert trays! Their cannolis are amazing! Highly recommend.
Rewrite this for me: Termini Brothers desserts are absolutely top-notch! Every item on their menu is fantastic. Being brought up in a proud Italian family, we always make sure to have Termini Brothers dessert trays at our family gatherings. Their cannolis are truly out of this world. I cannot recommend them enough.

input: It's a nice place. Really nice! Great service and awesome restaurants in the hotel. Clean rooms
Rewrite this for me: The place is absolutely delightful! Incredibly nice! The service is exceptional, and the hotel boasts an array of fantastic restaurants. The rooms are impeccably clean.

input:
After our recent trip to New Orleans, I came back to Reno appreciating this place even more than before! 
The shrimp po boy is my favorite thing on the menu! And their corn bread is amazing as well!
Rewrite this for me: Upon returning from our recent adventure in New Orleans, I discovered an increased appreciation for Reno! The shrimp po boy, undoubtedly, has become my ultimate favorite delicacy on their menu. Additionally, their corn bread was simply superb!

input: People in this place are generally friendly, but do not make the mistake of going to Katie.  She went through my hair like a bulldozer-- slapped colour on it in less than 5 minutes and cut it in even less time.  I think she was in a rush to get out of there (it was late in the day), but then she shouldn't have agreed to take me on.  The whole thing cost me close to $200, and I was shaken up by the experience.
Rewrite this for me: The majority of individuals in this location are usually amiable, but it is important to avoid going to Katie. She handled my hair as though she was operating a bulldozer - hastily applying color in under 5 minutes and completing the cut even faster. It appeared that she was in a hurry to leave the establishment (it was late in the day), but she should not have agreed to assist me. The entire ordeal ended up costing me nearly $200, and it left me feeling unsettled.

input: Favorite place in Nashville for breakfast!! This is a must go to spot!! Near Vandy and always busy...park in the back lot and be sure to get the parking ticket from the machine so you won't be charged...its free parking for a specified amount of time. My favorite is banana pancakes...think banana bread only in a pancake!! Perfection!!!! I don't leave Nashville until I go here to eat my pancakes!
Rewrite this for me: You absolutely have to check out my top breakfast spot in Nashville! It's conveniently located near Vanderbilt University and is always bustling with activity. Remember to park in the back lot, and don't forget to grab a parking ticket from the machine to enjoy free parking for a specific duration. Now, let me tell you about their incredible banana pancakes. Picture the delectable flavors of banana bread, but in pancake form. It's truly a match made in heaven! Trust me, I never leave Nashville without indulging in these mouthwatering pancakes.

input:
Yes, there are vegan options in University City, you just have to know where to look for them. MexiCali has a number of great options.

Many options here can be made vegan by holding the cheese. I absolutely adore the marinated tofu burrito. The tofu has a wonderfully chewy texture, and along with the black beans, the meal packs a protein-filled punch that will leave you full well past dinner-time, should you choose to finish it.  The sweet potato and plantain burrito is purportedly dairy-free, and it's another delicious, filling vegan option. The veggie tacos come with a spicier version of the sweet potato, the marinated tofu and some cabbage on doubled corn tortillas. The tacos are not as filling as the burritos, but they're a delicious lighter option. Finally, a fourth option for vegans: the guacamole burrito. They homemade guac is to-die-for delicious. 

I end up at MexiCali about once a week. I've been going since they were just a lunch truck 8 years back. There's often a line at the restaurant, but this place has been around for years and they have a great system to get you your burrito in a very timely manner.
Rewrite this for me:
Yes, vegan options are available in University City if you know where to find them. MexiCali is a recommended spot with several delicious choices.

Many dishes can be made vegan by simply omitting the cheese. Personally, I highly recommend their marinated tofu burrito. The tofu has a satisfyingly chewy texture and, combined with black beans, it provides a protein-packed meal that will keep you full long after dinner. If you're looking for something filling and dairy-free, the sweet potato and plantain burrito is another fantastic vegan option. For those who prefer a spicier twist, the veggie tacos offer a combination of sweet potato, marinated tofu, and cabbage on double corn tortillas. Although not as substantial as the burritos, these tacos are a delectable lighter alternative. Lastly, if you're a fan of guacamole, their guacamole burrito is a must-try. Their homemade guac is incredibly delicious.

I find myself at MexiCali almost every week and have been a loyal customer since they were just a lunch truck 8 years ago. Despite occasional lines, this place has been around for years and has developed an efficient system to ensure you receive your burrito promptly.

input:
Great breakfast fare and all. Eggs provençale was pretty good; all kinds of herbs and seasonings, but cooked inconsistently. Tomato on the side was awesome.

Omelets were executed well, and the pastries were pretty impressive.

But the coffee was horrendously bad. And without good coffee, what's the point of breakfast?

And I still can't trust restaurants that have misspellings on their menus. Even if the misspelling is from another language.
Rewrite this for me:
The breakfast options were quite satisfying, especially the flavorful Eggs provençale with its assortment of herbs and seasonings, although they were cooked unevenly. The accompanying tomato was delicious.

The omelets were skillfully prepared and the pastries were quite remarkable.

Unfortunately, the coffee was extremely unpleasant. After all, what's the purpose of having breakfast without a good cup of coffee?

Furthermore, I find it difficult to place trust in restaurants that have misspelled words on their menus, even if the misspelling is in another language.

input: Another Yelper hit it -- this is a noisy, crowded restaurant with big screen TVs.  I wouldn't call it a sports bar.  Nothing wrong with the place.  Cool location, good beer selection.  The food - delicious, but eliminates itself as a "sports bar". My sons and I wanted to catch some pub grub and the hockey game.  Got the game.  The grub-- eclectic.  Do go here if you want a busy, bustling, energetic, tasty, flavorful, thumping music-beat experience.  Don't go here if you want  a burger, a beer and a hockey game amidst sports conversation.
Rewrite this for me: This place, as another Yelper mentioned, is a lively and crowded restaurant with large TVs, but it doesn't quite fit the description of a sports bar. However, there's nothing wrong with it. The restaurant has a great location and offers a good variety of beers. The food is absolutely delicious, but it doesn't align with the typical sports bar menu. My sons and I were looking to enjoy some casual pub food while watching a hockey game, and while we did get to watch the game, the food options were more diverse. If you're in the mood for a vibrant and energetic atmosphere with fantastic flavors and music, this is the place to be. However, if you're specifically craving a burger, a beer, and sports conversation while watching a hockey game, this might not be the best spot for you.

input: Fabulous, quick, stress free windshield repair. .. didnt cost a penny out of pocket. I would definitely use this company again and would recommend to anybody!!
Rewrite this for me: The windshield repair provided by this company was absolutely fantastic - it was fast, hassle-free, and didn't require any out-of-pocket expenses. input: I was so excited about this meal, I came home to review it immediately. The service was outstanding and the food I'd say was some of the best in New Orleans. Even the freshly made bread was piping hot and delicious. We started with the oysters good enough, which were four fried oysters with bearnaise sauce and Benton's bacon- a must get. Then we both got scallops and swine with a butternut squash purée and balsamic vinegar. All of the entrees sounded phenomenal, but we both couldn't resist getting that dish. The best part I have to say was the dessert. We got cafe au lait panna cotta with mini glazed donuts, which reminded us of beignets at cafe du monde. Finally, I sampled their house made 'cellos, including ginger and limecellos, and they were unique and delicious. An amazing experience!
Rewrite this for me: I couldn't contain my excitement when I returned home after having this meal - it compelled me to write a review immediately. The service was exceptional, and I dare say that the food was among the finest in all of New Orleans. The freshly baked bread, served steaming hot, was simply delightful. To begin, we indulged in the "oysters good enough" - four delectable fried oysters accompanied by rich bearnaise sauce and Benton's bacon. It goes without saying that this dish is an absolute must-try. For our main courses, we both opted for the scallops and swine, accompanied by a luscious butternut squash purée and balsamic vinegar. While all the entrees on the menu were enticing, this particular dish was irresistible to both of us. The highlight of the meal, without a doubt, was the dessert. We savored the cafe au lait panna cotta paired with bite-sized glazed donuts that instantly brought to mind the iconic beignets at cafe du monde. Lastly, I had the pleasure of sampling their house-made 'cellos, including the ginger and limecellos, which offered a unique and delicious twist. Overall, this was a truly remarkable dining experience!

input:
Absolutely amazing!!! My girlfriend and I went on a Wednesday night for Restaurant week and didn't know what to expect but we were overly satisfied. We ordered blood orange margaritas and they were strong and delicious. For our appetizers we had meatballs and let me tell you they weren't your average meatballs. They were veal and beef meatballs that melted in your mouth. Our other appetizer was some sort of grilled cheese that was amazing as well. For our entree we had the fishermen stew that was full of flavor and well balanced. Initially I did not think I was going to like it but it was to die for. Every element of the stew had it's own flavor and it was properly cooked. My girlfriend ordered the steak that came with cauliflower puree and a vegetable medley that was delicious as well. This was the first time we had ever ordered our steak to be medium-well and ever since we've been hooked. The steak was so juicy, tender and seasoned so eloquently and the puree was seasoned beautifully as well. 
The service there was amazing!! I forget the waitors name but he was great with the menu. He helped us order and came back frequently to check on us. 
Overall I think BARRA is amazing. It's not expensive and it is very intimate.  If you are looking for good food and great service at a reasonable price, BARRA is the place to go!!!!
Rewrite this for me: Wow, what an incredible experience! My girlfriend and I decided to try out BARRA for Restaurant Week on a Wednesday night, not knowing what to expect. However, we were completely blown away and left extremely satisfied. To start, we ordered their blood orange margaritas, which were both strong and delicious. As for our appetizers, the meatballs were absolutely exceptional - made with a delightful combination of veal and beef that practically melted in our mouths. We also tried a grilled cheese dish, which was equally amazing. Moving on to our main course, we opted for the fishermen stew, which turned out to be bursting with flavor and perfectly balanced. Although I wasn't initially convinced that I would enjoy it, I quickly fell in love with every distinct flavor that came together in the stew. My girlfriend chose the steak, accompanied by cauliflower puree and a vegetable medley that were equally delicious. This was our first time ordering a steak cooked medium-well, and it was a revelation; the steak was incredibly juicy, tender, and seasoned just right. The puree was also beautifully seasoned. The service we received was exceptional as well. Though we cannot recall our waiter's name, he was incredibly knowledgeable about the menu and provided excellent guidance in choosing our dishes. He also checked in on us frequently throughout the evening. In summary, BARRA exceeded our expectations in every way. The prices are reasonable, and the atmosphere is intimate. If you're in search of great food and outstanding service at a fair price, BARRA should be at the top of your list!

input:
We went here hoping for a good breakfast,  and we weren't disappointed.  We went on Valentine's Day, not because we wanted to, but because we had to.  In doing so,  we knew the wait would be long, which it was (an hour and a half), though i hear there's always a wait. 

The place is buzzing with servers and busboys. The tables around the edges of the room are a bit close to one another,  so seating is tight.  The service was though, considering how busy it was.  I ordered the famed cornmeal pancakes with a side of hash browns and a fried egg.  My girlfriend ordered the banana pancakes with a side of bacon.  Everything was amazing.  The pancakes were hearty but fluffy... The side of bacon only comes with three pieces which is disappointing,  but it was cooked to her liking.  The cornmeal pancakes had just the right amount of everything... Bacon,  peppers... Salsa, sour cream,  syrup... Yes,  all of that.  If you're looking for good coffee,  this is not the place, which was surprising. 

The only question is do you go with the homemade syrup or the maple.... Or both
Rewrite this for me:
We arrived at this place with hopes of enjoying a satisfying breakfast, and we were not let down. Despite going on Valentine's Day out of necessity rather than desire, we were aware that the wait would be lengthy, and it lived up to our expectations, lasting an hour and a half. However, I hear that there is always a wait here.

The establishment was bustling with servers and busboys. The tables along the room's edges were positioned quite close together, resulting in limited seating. Nonetheless, considering how busy it was, the service was commendable. I opted for the renowned cornmeal pancakes accompanied by a serving of hash browns and a fried egg. Meanwhile, my girlfriend chose the banana pancakes paired with a side of bacon. Every dish we ordered was exceptional. The pancakes were substantial yet fluffy. On the other hand, the bacon serving was a bit disappointing as it only consisted of three pieces, but it was cooked to my girlfriend's preference. The cornmeal pancakes, on the other hand, were perfectly balanced with bacon, peppers, salsa, sour cream, and syrup. Yes, all of those were incorporated into the dish. Surprisingly, if you are seeking good coffee, this place does not meet that criteria.

Now, the only predicament is deciding between the homemade syrup, maple syrup, or perhaps both.

input: My husband son and I went in for dinner last Friday night. Upon entering we were greeted by a friendly hostess. As we stood there waiting for her to grab the menus I couldn't help but to notice a strong dirty mop water stench. Thankfully when we left the entry way it didn't carry into the dining room. The remodel is impressive looking. We were sat at a booth. Looking over the menu I was surprised at how limited it was. As long as you make what you offer well no biggie. I ordered the mushroom swiss burger and a beer. My husband ordered the "knuckle sandwich", ( tri-tip sandwich served French dip style). My son ordered the chicken strips and we all got French fries as our side. Jesse, our server was nice enough but in the loud dining room you couldn't hear a word he said. I was more annoyed that he didn't take the initiative to speak up than about the noise. The beer came out, although tasty it wasn't cold enough at all. The food came out within a reasonable amount of time. My husband's "Knuckle Sandwich" was delicious! That is what the two stars are for. My burger was shockingly small and probably the blandest burger I have ever eaten. My son's chicken strips tasted like they floured them...and that was it... also, no hint of seasoning. The fries are your run of the mill freezer to fryer. I hope they step it up and are successful.
Rewrite this for me: Last Friday night, my husband, son, and I decided to have dinner together. When we entered the restaurant, a friendly hostess greeted us. However, as we stood there waiting for her to bring us menus, I couldn't help but notice a strong stench of dirty mop water. Fortunately, once we moved away from the entryway, the unpleasant odor didn't follow us into the dining room. The restaurant had an impressive remodel, and we were seated at a booth. As I glanced over the menu, I was surprised by its limited options. Nevertheless, I figured as long as they made their offerings well, it wouldn't be a big issue. I ordered a mushroom Swiss burger and a beer, while my husband opted for the "knuckle sandwich" (a French dip-style tri-tip sandwich), and my son chose the chicken strips. We all decided to have French fries as our side. Our server, Jesse, was polite, but it was challenging to hear him in the loud dining room. I found it more frustrating that he didn't take the initiative to speak louder, rather than being bothered by the noise itself. Although the beer I received was tasty, it unfortunately wasn't cold enough. Thankfully, the food arrived within a reasonable amount of time. My husband's "Knuckle Sandwich" was absolutely delicious, earning the restaurant two stars in my book. On the other hand, I was disappointed to find that my burger was surprisingly small and lacked flavor. Furthermore, my son's chicken strips tasted as if they only had flour coating them, lacking any seasoning whatsoever. As for the fries, they were just your average frozen-to-fried variety. Overall, I genuinely hope that the restaurant steps up their game and achieves success in the future.

input: I had a delicious breakfast at Tuttini a few months ago.  I went back for lunch recently and was excited by their sandwich offerings, however, I was not served.  It was 1:45 PM, and their sign states that they serve lunch until 2:30 PM.  I waited in line for 7 or 8 minutes before a woman came out to tell me that the kitchen was closing.  Closing over 30 minutes early!  She said she might be able to make something to go.  So, if you can make something to go, doesn't that mean the kitchen is not yet closed?  Besides, I wanted to have a few minutes to relax in the cozy restaurant and enjoy my sandwich, not gulf it down on the street, so I left.  I got a sandwich at North Star Coffee around the corner and gave them my $10 instead.
Rewrite this for me:
A few months ago, I had a delightful breakfast at Tuttini. Recently, I decided to give their lunch menu a try and was excited about the variety of sandwiches they offered. Unfortunately, my experience turned out to be disappointing. Despite their sign stating that they serve lunch until 2:30 PM, I arrived at 1:45 PM only to find that I was not served.

I patiently waited in line for approximately 7 or 8 minutes, hoping to order my desired sandwich, when suddenly a woman appeared and informed me that the kitchen was closing. I was taken aback as it was still well within their stated lunch hours. She mentioned the possibility of making something to go, but I couldn't help but question if the kitchen was truly closed if they could still prepare meals for takeout.

On top of that, my intention was to enjoy a peaceful and relaxed meal in their cozy restaurant, savoring my sandwich. However, if I had to hurriedly devour it on the street, it wouldn't fulfill that desire. Therefore, I made the decision to leave.

Instead, I opted to go to North Star Coffee, which happened to be around the corner. I purchased a sandwich from there, choosing to support them with my $10 instead.

input:
I've only eaten here twice and my experience has been great overall. The first time I went, they had just opened. There were some kinks but not anything I would complain about. After all, our group had 8 people so it was understandable. Second time was probably a month later and I noticed they figured out some of the kinks. Their servers are nice and I genuinely felt like they wanted to make my experience great. I know this because every time I made a request the waiter would literally run to get it. I've never seen a server so dedicated, kudos! Honestly most of the stars I'm giving them is because of their genuine service. Added bonus, they were playing Star Trek, hunger games, and iron man. Nice movie selections haha.

The seafood was ok. It's not their fault; it's Tucson so you know you really can't get fresh seafood. That's why I took off a star. They have 1 type of sauce with mild, medium, hot spiciness. It's similar to angry crab's "trifecta" or boiling crab's, "the whole shabang" but with an Asian twist. It was good in my opinion.

Lastly, if anyone has ever gone to angry crab, hot n juicy, boiling crab, should know that the price range is similar. Heck, if anyone has ever bought raw seafood at the store should know that it is on the expensive side. Expensive? Yes. Overpriced? No. I have been to many seafood places similar to this and it's a decent price for what you get. My advice for the Dungeness crab, since it did happen to me at other places and I saw a review on it here, is to share it or get their other selections that they can measure out. The dungeness crab is a full crab so finding a 1 lb dungeness crab is not common. 

Would recommend and go again.
Rewrite this for me:
I have dined at this restaurant on two occasions, and overall, it has been an excellent experience. During my first visit, they had just opened, so there were a few minor issues, but nothing that I would complain about. Considering our large group of 8 people, it was understandable. However, by my second visit, which was about a month later, it was evident that they had resolved some of those initial hiccups. The servers were friendly, and it genuinely felt like they wanted to make our dining experience exceptional. I was particularly impressed by their dedication as the waiter would literally run to fulfill any request I made. Their exceptional service is the primary reason why I am giving them most of the stars in my rating. Additionally, it was a nice surprise to see that they were playing Star Trek, Hunger Games, and Iron Man movies, offering a pleasant atmosphere.

As for the seafood, it was decent, but I don't blame the restaurant for it. Being located in Tucson, fresh seafood is hard to come by, so I deducted a star for that. They offer one type of sauce with three levels of spiciness: mild, medium, and hot. It has a unique Asian twist, similar to Angry Crab's "Trifecta" or Boiling Crab's "The Whole Shabang," and I personally found it delicious.

Lastly, in terms of pricing, it is comparable to similar seafood establishments such as Angry Crab, Hot N Juicy, and Boiling Crab. It may seem expensive, but considering the cost of raw seafood at stores, it is reasonable. In my experience, this restaurant offers a decent price for the quality and quantity of food you receive. If you plan on ordering the Dungeness crab, it is important to note that it is a whole crab and not commonly available in 1 lb portions. Therefore, I recommend sharing it or opting for their other measured selections.

I would definitely recommend this restaurant and would gladly visit again.

input: Food was well prepared and fresh. I had the oso bucco ravioli.
