Rewrite this for me: The food was prepared well and fresh. I ordered the oso bucco ravioli, which were clearly homemade but lacked sufficient filling, resulting in less flavor than expected. The service was great, but the noisy atmosphere made it difficult for the wait staff to hear us unless we raised our voices. It's a good place overall, but the small size and overcrowded tables make it not recommended for a date night. Considering the abundance of excellent dining options in the neighborhood, the only reason I would consider returning is because it allows bringing your own bottle. However, I am confident that I could find a comparable or even better dining experience elsewhere with less noise, more space, and tastier dishes.

input:
I moved to Philadelphia from the midwest as a wide eyed 19 year old full of wonder. Yuengling lager was the first beer I've ever truly enjoyed and remains in my top five favorites of all time. Smooth, sweet, cheap, it's like me in a bottle. I love that the bottlecaps can be rusty, I like that the taste varies per batch, I even like its relatively low alcohol content. 

The tour was pretty great, the British tour woman was funny in a non canned way. She took a shine to my grandpa and was constantly begging him to sell her his hat (signed, sports, I haven't a clue). I was amazed at how close they let you get to the active equipment, I could've spit in the mash and no one would've been the wiser. The whole facility reminded me of St. Pete Catholic High, 50's cinderblock with a residue of toil clinging to the walls. 

The tasting, that's what you came for right? Fantastic. They were out of Lord Chesterfield, but who drinks that? I "tasted" the shit out of the lager, probably 6 times. It makes sense, the bar is next to the gift shop and I went a bit insane in there. 

The fact that Dick Yuengling made it a point to hire back the laid off workers after the last closure bumps it up a star. This is a family business, one that deserves support as Inbev has encroached upon everything else.
Rewrite this for me:
I relocated to Philadelphia from the Midwest as a wide-eyed 19-year-old, full of curiosity and excitement. Yuengling lager quickly became my favorite beer, holding a cherished spot in my top five all-time favorites. Its smoothness, sweetness, and affordability make it akin to a bottled reflection of myself. I find charm in the rustic bottlecaps, the varying taste from batch to batch, and even its relatively low alcohol content.

The brewery tour was quite enjoyable, with the British tour guide exhibiting a genuine sense of humor. She took a liking to my grandpa and persistently tried to persuade him into selling her his signed sports hat, which I knew nothing about. What truly fascinated me was the close proximity allowed to the active equipment; I could have casually spit into the mash without anyone noticing. The entire facility reminded me of St. Pete Catholic High, constructed with 50's cinderblock walls that held a residual essence of hard work and dedication.

Of course, the highlight was the tasting. It was absolutely fantastic. Unfortunately, Lord Chesterfield was unavailable, but who drinks that anyway? I enthusiastically indulged in the lager, probably sampling it six times over. It's understandable since the tasting area is conveniently located next to the gift shop, where I may have gone a bit wild.

One factor that truly elevated my admiration for Yuengling is Dick Yuengling's dedication to rehire laid-off workers after the previous closure. This family-owned business deserves support as larger conglomerates like Inbev continue to encroach upon the industry.

input:
Came here with some friends during Mardi Gras. Even though it was a busy weekend and lots of people everywhere a lot of places aren't over crowded. The bartenders were just awful. The service was lacking and the pizza sucked. 

PROS:
-They had Port-O-Potty (2) put back which made it easier for a bathroom break
-Outdoor seating area
-Near the parade route (convenient) 

CONS:
-Bartenders don't take drink orders properly: they skip people, ignore you at the bar when you walk up (it wasn't that busy), lots of standing around
-Bartenders didn't know what microbrew meant or IPA beers (no joke)
Rewrite this for me:
Came here with a group of friends during Mardi Gras. Despite it being a hectic weekend with a multitude of people everywhere, we discovered that many places were surprisingly not overcrowded. However, the bartenders at this particular establishment were extremely disappointing. The service was severely lacking, and the quality of the pizza was subpar.

On the positive side, there were a few noteworthy aspects:
1. They had two conveniently placed Port-O-Potties, which made it much more convenient for bathroom breaks.
2. The establishment offered an outdoor seating area, allowing patrons to enjoy their drinks and food in an al fresco setting.
3. Additionally, it was conveniently located near the parade route, making it easily accessible for those wanting to catch the festivities.

Unfortunately, there were several drawbacks to our experience:
1. The bartenders consistently failed to take drink orders properly. They would skip people, ignore customers who approached the bar (even when it wasn't overly busy), and seemed to spend a lot of time just standing around.
2. To make matters worse, the bartenders displayed a lack of knowledge regarding microbrews and IPA beers. This may sound unbelievable, but it truly was the case.

input: Really nice place to get a pedicure! People are very friendly and it is a relaxing environment. Definitely recommend if you are looking for a clean place to get your toes done!
Rewrite this for me: This place is truly wonderful for getting a pedicure! The staff is extremely friendly, and the atmosphere is so relaxing. I highly recommend this place if you're searching for a hygienic and enjoyable experience for your toes!

input: Nice new burger spot downtown! They are apart of the harry & izzys chain. The burgers are pretty good. You do have to order a side separately which kinda sticks but seems to be a trend these days. They take reservations so that's always a plus. If you are looking for additional options besides a burger might not be your best spot to go. I'd like to see them do a lunch special during the week for those that go during the work day. I think it would help with costs and getting a bigger lunch crowd. Overall great experience and service. Check them out!
Rewrite this for me: There's a great new burger place in downtown! It's part of the Harry & Izzy's chain and the burgers are really tasty. The only downside is that you have to order sides separately, which seems to be a common trend nowadays. On the bright side, they do take reservations, which is a bonus. If you're looking for more than just burgers, this might not be the ideal spot for you. It would be nice if they offered a lunch special during the week for those who come during their workday. It could help reduce costs and attract a larger lunch crowd. Overall, the experience and service were great. You should definitely give them a try!

input: Salad was good.  Pizza is not good!  Boring, tasteless and just unsatisfying.  Very disappointed.  Also on a chilly night it is a cold interior.  This was my third try there.  Won't go back
Rewrite this for me: The salad was enjoyable, but unfortunately, the pizza was far from satisfying. It lacked flavor, was bland and overall disappointing. To make matters worse, the restaurant had a cold interior on a chilly night. This was my third attempt at dining there, but I won't be returning.

input: Not impressed at all. Sandwich bar was closed so I ordered a burrito. It was reheated in the microwave, cost 8 bucks, and nasty. Some sort of cream of chicken and old cheese on top. I'm amazed they can sell this and call it food. Could have had better at taco bell.
Rewrite this for me: I was absolutely underwhelmed. The sandwich bar had unfortunately closed, leaving me with no choice but to go for a burrito. To my disappointment, it was microwaved and tasted unpleasant, especially considering its steep price of 8 dollars. It was topped with some peculiar combination of cream of chicken and aged cheese. Frankly, I find it astonishing that this can be labeled as food and still be sold. I could have easily found something more satisfying at Taco Bell.

input:
I have visited the brewpub several times now, and I'm finally ready to write up a review.  I really like the decor here.  It's old-school brewpub with lots of games for children.  The beer is pretty good.  I wish they would do some more adventurous offerings, but I can still get a good beer here.  
The food can be a mixed bag.  I had a small pizza that was a gooey mess (mushrooms and hearty toppings need a thick crust for stability).  I love all the scotch egg offerings (you can get it on a pizza or burger here), but they are so salty.  The burgers are good. The desserts are great (please get the frangipane).  It's also great to get the ploughman's plate and a beer, and just relax for a bit.
Rewrite this for me:
After numerous visits to the brewpub, I am finally prepared to pen my review. The ambience here truly appeals to me, as it exudes a classic brewpub vibe and is equipped with an array of games to entertain children. The beer generally satisfies my palate, although I do long for more daring options. Nevertheless, I am still able to enjoy a good brew in this establishment.

When it comes to the culinary offerings, it's a bit of a mixed bag. The small-sized pizza I ordered turned out to be a gooey mess, perhaps due to the need for a thicker crust to support the hearty toppings, especially mushrooms. On the other hand, I particularly adore the various iterations of scotch eggs available (be it on a pizza or a burger), despite their tendency to be overly salty. The burgers, thankfully, do not disappoint. Lastly, the desserts are a highlight (I implore you to try the frangipane). Furthermore, it's a delight to indulge in the ploughman's plate alongside a beer, allowing for a truly relaxing experience.

input:
I think if I could, I would give Zen Yai a 3.5 stars, but alas, c'est la vie. 

The prices for their curry are excellent, at less than $12. Zen Yai is a tiny place, which is both good and bad. Good if you don't have to wait, because it is nice and cozy, but bad if enough people eat here on a given evening -- because you may just have to wait a while.

I like the decor a lot, and the use of colors. The tables and plates are full of refreshingly bright colors. 

The service was fine, and the food was at our table in no time.

My Pineapple curry was excellent! And the rice is served in the shape of a pyramid, which is fun. 

All that being said, my girlfriend had a less than pleasurable experience. She is a seasoned green curry lover, and was disappointed with their green curry offering.
Rewrite this for me:
Unfortunately, if given the choice, I would rate Zen Yai at 3.5 stars. The prices for their curry dishes are very reasonable, being under $12. However, Zen Yai is a small establishment with both advantages and disadvantages. It's great when there's no wait because the atmosphere is cozy, but it can be frustrating when it gets crowded and you find yourself waiting for quite some time.

On a positive note, I really admire the decor and their use of vibrant colors. The tables and plates are adorned with refreshing and lively hues.

The service we received was satisfactory, and our food arrived promptly.

Personally, I thoroughly enjoyed my Pineapple curry! Additionally, I found it amusing that the rice was shaped like a pyramid.

However, my girlfriend did not have a pleasant experience. As a green curry enthusiast, she was disappointed with their rendition of the dish.

input:
Having stayed here several times, it is my favorite hotel. The staff is excellent. Really exceptional. Everyone from housekeeping to front desk staff to valets.

Rooms are clean, heating and AC are quiet, beds are very comfortable and they make it feel special.

Special K is awesome. I cannot say enough about how wonderful and helpful he has been over all of our visits. One of the best reasons to visit this hotel. Did I mention the exceptional staff?

Turn-down service is Sucre chocolates on your pillow. Sweets for the sweet dreams.

The bathroom wasn't as slippery this time. 

This was the first time we used the valet service and it worked great. No more than a 10 minute wait for the car. You can text them from your phone and they text back with how long it will take.

They also hosted a Gold Status reception. We made a brief appearance on our way to a Mardi Gras ball.

Our only glitch was a mini-bar charge on our bill. We didn't consume any of their food or drink and they happily removed it from the bill.

We will be back. Note to hotel: please put Louis back in the elevator.
Rewrite this for me:
After multiple stays, this hotel has become my absolute favorite. The staff, without a doubt, is phenomenal - truly exceptional. From the housekeeping team to the front desk staff to the valets, they all go above and beyond.

The rooms are consistently clean, the heating and AC systems are whisper-quiet, and the beds are incredibly comfortable. They really know how to create a special atmosphere.

I have to give a special shout-out to Special K - he is absolutely amazing and has been incredibly helpful during all of our visits. He alone is a compelling reason to choose this hotel. And let me reiterate, the staff as a whole is just exceptional.

The turn-down service includes Sucre chocolates on the pillow, making for sweet dreams.

I noticed that the bathroom wasn't as slippery this time, which is a definite improvement.

This was our first time utilizing the valet service, and it worked like a charm. We waited no longer than 10 minutes for our car, and it was convenient being able to text them from our phone and receive updates on when it would arrive.

Additionally, we were delighted to attend a Gold Status reception hosted by the hotel. We made a quick appearance before heading off to a Mardi Gras ball.

The only minor hiccup we encountered was a mini-bar charge on our bill. However, the staff happily removed it once we informed them that we hadn't consumed any of the items. Their willingness to rectify the situation was greatly appreciated.

Without a doubt, we will be returning to this hotel. And a small request to the hotel: please bring back Louis in the elevator.

input: Great rolls and sake. We sat in the bamboo room, which definitely added to the experience, if you are able and agile.
Rewrite this for me: The rolls and sake were absolutely delightful. Our seating in the bamboo room truly enhanced the whole experience, especially for those who are capable and nimble.

input: First, I love that they offer food delivery! Second, THAT is a gyro! I got one delivered with fries, and actually I didn't need the fries! The gyro was so big I had to save half.  Both the fries and the gyro were very tasty. The tzaziki was spot on and the meat tender. I'll be back!
Rewrite this for me: I absolutely adore the fact that they provide food delivery services! Additionally, let me tell you, their gyro is phenomenal! I had it delivered along with a side of fries, although I must confess that the fries were unnecessary. The gyro itself was incredibly generous in size, prompting me to save half of it for later. Both the fries and the gyro were incredibly flavorful. The tzaziki sauce was impeccable and the meat was delightfully tender. Without a doubt, I will definitely be returning for more!

input: I stopped in to order take out and get a drink while I waited since it was happy hour. I am usually a beer drinker but I decided to step out of my comfort zone and ordered the dragonberry iced tea which was refreshing but not obnoxiously cocktail-ly, very pleasant. I had lemongrass chicken and crab rangoon, the lemon grass chicken and rice was fantastic. I do wish the crab rangoon had a little more filling but the dipping sauce was great. I've been here a few times and I have never been disappointed in the food or the service.
Rewrite this for me:
I decided to make a pit stop to place a takeout order and grab a drink while waiting, taking advantage of the happy hour offer. Typically, I stick to beer, but this time I decided to step out of my comfort zone and try the dragonberry iced tea. It turned out to be refreshingly enjoyable without being too overpoweringly cocktail-like. 
For my food order, I went with lemongrass chicken and crab rangoon. The lemongrass chicken paired perfectly with rice and was absolutely fantastic. However, I would have preferred a tad more filling in the crab rangoon, although the dipping sauce provided a great taste. Having been to this place multiple times, I have never been let down by either the food or the service.

input: Consistent quality and service.  Love the #1 Deluxe.  Props to Amanda for excellent customer service, above and beyond!
Rewrite this for me: We take pride in providing unwavering quality and service. Our #1 Deluxe item is truly appreciated. Huge shoutout to Amanda for going the extra mile and delivering exceptional customer service!

input:
*note* I wrote a similar review on tripadvisor.
I really wanted to like this hotel- it was charming and in a great location, with cute, unique rooms. It was just my style. Unfortunately, some blood-sucking insects ruined that.
Yup- bed bugs. We found them the morning we were leaving, because they normally come out very early in the morning (we were up at 530). Bleck! The management let us stay as long as necessary to take care of the issue (ie throwing away a bunch of our stuff and bagging the rest in ziplocks to be boiled) but it didn't change the fact that it was gross and a huge inconvenience. I threw away about $300 worth of clothing, shoes and luggage and I'm still worried that we brought the creatures back to our house with us. 
I would never stay here again, and I would urge you to think twice about it. Without seeing every carpet and mattress in the place replaced, there's no way I'd trust that the bugs were gone.
Rewrite this for me:
I had high hopes for this hotel as it had a charming ambiance and was conveniently located. The rooms were cute and had a unique touch, which appealed to my taste. However, my experience was quickly tainted by the presence of blood-sucking insects, namely bed bugs.

To my dismay, we discovered them on the morning of our departure, as they tend to be most active during the early hours (we were up at 5:30 AM). It was quite revolting! The management allowed us to extend our stay to deal with the issue, which involved discarding several belongings and sealing the remaining items in ziplock bags to be sanitized. Nonetheless, the whole ordeal was both disgusting and highly inconvenient. I had to part ways with approximately $300 worth of clothing, shoes, and luggage, and I still worry that we may have unknowingly brought these pests back to our home.

Given my experience, I would never consider staying at this hotel again, and I strongly advise you to think twice before booking here. Unless every carpet and mattress in the establishment are replaced, I simply cannot trust that the infestation has been fully eradicated.

input: Still running on EST, we arrived @8:30 on a Saturday to find no wait to be seated OR helped, ordering up the sweet potato pancakes with cinnamon cream syrup (good topped with excellent) with some borderline awful hash browns (really, people??). Can't say I'd return even without a wait, though; would prefer to just buy a jar of the syrup and apply it at home. Ended up at $24.43 pre-tip; no paper towels in the restroom and the day had barely started, so that was probably a dogshow.
Rewrite this for me: We arrived at 8:30 on a Saturday, still following EST, and were pleasantly surprised to find no wait for seating or assistance. We decided to order the sweet potato pancakes with cinnamon cream syrup, which tasted great topped with excellent ingredients. However, we were disappointed by the quality of the hash browns, which were borderline awful. Even if there had been no wait, I don't think I would choose to return to this place. It would be more preferable to buy a jar of the syrup and enjoy it at home. The bill came to $24.43 before tipping. Additionally, the restroom was lacking paper towels, which was quite unimpressive considering the day had just begun. It felt like a chaotic situation.

input:
There never seems to be a crowd at this Marsh store...getting in and out is always easy.  I agree with the other reviewer on the state of red baskets...ick.  Fix please!

I like that they opened up aisles so you don't have to walk all the way to one end to go to the next (prob happened a long time ago but I just noticed today).  And always seems like they are one cashier short here.

Very good selection of products (as always) from Marsh.
Rewrite this for me:
The Marsh store is consistently uncrowded, making it convenient to come and go without any hassle. I echo the sentiments of another reviewer regarding the condition of the red baskets; they could definitely use some improvement. 

On a positive note, I appreciate that the store has rearranged the aisles, eliminating the need to walk to one end in order to get to the next section (although this change may have occurred quite some time ago, I only noticed it today). However, it seems like they are always understaffed, as there is typically one cashier too few. 

Nevertheless, Marsh continues to offer an excellent variety of products, as expected.

input: Creative food and good. We get coffee or tea while we wait to be seated and even that is a cut above.  We love their Bloody Marys too.  Always interesting and an adventure.
Rewrite this for me: The food at this place is incredibly creative and delicious. While we wait to be seated, we can enjoy a cup of coffee or tea that surpasses our expectations. Their Bloody Marys are also worth mentioning, as they never fail to amaze us. Every dining experience here is full of excitement and new discoveries.

input: Wonderful atmosphere, great selection of beers.  We ordered the Asian chicken salads and the Cajun pasta and both were excellent. We will return again.
Rewrite this for me: The atmosphere was fantastic and they had an impressive range of beers. Our choice of Asian chicken salads and Cajun pasta was simply outstanding. We look forward to coming back in the future.

input: Love this place introduced almost 25 years ago when I enrolled at the UD and have loved ever since. For longest time it was basically just a Delaware treat but so happy it is so many more places now. Just want to know when you are coming to the Huntsville AL area. Sorry this review is not about this specific location but if it is half as good as others I have been to it will be great!!! This location has plenty of seating was real clean and playing good tunes as I waited. About only negative is it doesn't have Herrs chips like the Delaware locations but that is not really a problem.
Rewrite this for me: I fell in love with this place nearly 25 years ago when I started attending the UD, and my affection for it has only grown since then. Initially, it was just a hidden gem in Delaware, but I am ecstatic that it has spread to numerous other locations. I am eagerly awaiting its arrival in the Huntsville, AL area. Apologies for not reviewing this specific location, but if it is even half as fantastic as the others I have visited, I know it will be exceptional! The seating here is abundant, the cleanliness is impressive, and the music playing in the background while I waited was enjoyable. The only minor downside is that they do not carry Herrs chips like the Delaware locations, although that is hardly a significant issue.

input: At first I thought the prices here were pretty decent, but then I realized that they charge for every add on- chips/salsa, rice and beans, etc. I would be fine with this if the food was exceptional, but it is subpar. Both times I've been here, my side order of rice has been hard and dry, and burritos sad and limp. Additionally, the waitress we've had the two times going there had a horrible attitude. The only thing that saves this place is the guac, and the strong margaritas. Their strategy must be to get people drunk enough to not care about what they're eating and the rude service.
Rewrite this for me: Initially, I believed the prices at this establishment were reasonable, but it soon became apparent that they add charges for every little extra - be it chips and salsa, rice and beans, or anything else. I wouldn't mind this if the food was extraordinary, but unfortunately, it falls short. On both occasions I've visited, the rice on the side was dry and hard, and the burritos lacked flavor and were disappointingly lackluster. Moreover, the waitress we've had on both visits displayed a terrible attitude. The only redeeming qualities of this place are their delicious guacamole and strong margaritas. It seems their strategy is to intoxicate customers enough that they overlook the mediocre food and the impolite service.

input: My boyfriend and I have lived in trolley square for about three months now and tend to stick to the same restaurants.  We went out the other night planning on El Diablo and decided to try this cute little Italian restaurant. We are so glad we did! First off, the waiter was awesome, so friendly and on top of it.  He told us the history of the restaurant and gave us some good suggestions. The food was some of the best Italian food I have had in a long time. You can tell everything is made fresh.  The bread was delicious and a new recipe the owner received from his brother who lives in Sicily. We started off with the prosciutto wrapped Shrimp with a yummy sauce. I ordered the Penne Alla Vodka and my boyfriend ordered the traditional spaghetti and meatballs. The sauce in both dishes was excellent! The portions were a decent size with plenty of leftovers for my lunch the next day.  Finally, the cannoli was the best I have ever had! My boyfriend has been to Italy and said it was just as awesome as the ones he tasted there. I would highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a delicious Italian meal for a good price.  The special he night we went was order two entrees and get any appetizer for free! Check this place out!
Rewrite this for me: After residing in trolley square for approximately three months, my boyfriend and I have become creatures of habit when it comes to dining out. However, the other night we decided to break our routine and give a charming little Italian restaurant a try instead of going to our usual spot, El Diablo. It turned out to be a delightful choice! To begin, our waiter was incredibly friendly and attentive. He took the time to share the restaurant's history and provided us with some valuable recommendations. The food itself was some of the finest Italian cuisine I had enjoyed in quite some time. Every dish gave off the impression of being freshly made. The bread, in particular, was absolutely delicious and showcased a new recipe passed down from the owner's brother, who resides in Sicily. To start our meal, we indulged in the mouthwatering prosciutto-wrapped shrimp accompanied by a delectable sauce. With regards to our main courses, I opted for the Penne Alla Vodka while my boyfriend chose the classic spaghetti and meatballs. The sauce in both dishes was exceptional! The portion sizes were generous, leaving us with plenty of leftovers for my lunch the following day. Lastly, the cannoli surpassed any I had ever tasted before! Even my boyfriend, who has been to Italy, claimed they were just as fantastic as the ones he savored there. I confidently recommend this restaurant to anyone in search of a delicious Italian meal at a reasonable price. On the night of our visit, they were offering a special deal: order two entrees and receive any appetizer for free! Make sure to pay this place a visit, you won't regret it!

input: 3.5 stars because they don't serve alcohol (and I was in dire need of a drink after a veryyyy long week). Get the margherita pie - it is delicious and fresh. Also ordered the Greek salad for an appetizer which was filled with yummy veggies. Yum.
Rewrite this for me: I rate this place 3.5 stars primarily because they don't serve alcohol, and I really needed a drink after an incredibly long week. However, I highly recommend trying their margherita pie as it is exceptionally delicious and made with fresh ingredients. As an appetizer, I also ordered the Greek salad which was packed with tasty and wholesome vegetables. It was quite satisfying.

input: I love Mr. Wizard's because they offer frozen yogurt which is a  lot healthier than frozen custard. I like that they offer some pre-select combinations or you can create your own. The only part that sucks is that there is only outside seating so if it's cold outside, plan to eat in your car.
Rewrite this for me: I am a big fan of Mr. Wizard's because they provide a healthier alternative with their frozen yogurt compared to frozen custard. What I appreciate is the flexibility they offer, allowing you to choose from their pre-select combinations or create your own. The only downside is the absence of indoor seating, meaning that during chilly weather, you'll need to plan on enjoying your meal in your car.

input:
Not sure the significance behind the name and logo of the restaurant.  Unless it was three guys putting their money together to form this business 
The food was great/ staff friendly/ huge menu from breakfast /lunch/dinner to dessert.   Open 24 hours will definitely be back next time in town
Rewrite this for me: I'm not entirely aware of the meaning behind the restaurant's name and logo, unless it represents three individuals pooling their resources to establish this venture. The food was delightful, and the staff was amiable. The menu offered an extensive range of options, from breakfast and lunch to dinner and dessert. Additionally, the restaurant operates around the clock, which makes it a definite choice for my next visit to town.

input: I went to Spasso the other night with some friends. All four of us were SO pleased with our experience and our meals! We each had something different. I had the special for the evening, which was seafood (jumbo shrimp and jumbo lump crab) over pappardelle with tomato and asparagus. it was to die for, and my leftovers the next day were just as tasty :) service was amazing and wine was perfect. I live on state street and can't wait to visit again very soon!!
Rewrite this for me: Last night, my friends and I visited Spasso and we were absolutely thrilled with our experience and meals! Each of us ordered something different, and I opted for the evening's special - a delectable dish consisting of seafood (jumbo shrimp and jumbo lump crab) served over pappardelle with tomato and asparagus. It was absolutely divine, and even the leftovers the next day were equally delicious. The service was outstanding, and the wine selection was spot on. Being a resident of State Street, I am eagerly looking forward to my next visit!

input: Returned to get a fill and pedicure a week after getting a gel polish change, once I discovered the cost would be over $85 I canceled the pedicure and only wanted a fill. Originally the owner was very nice and attentive but when she sensed I refused to pay their ridiculous price, she turned her attention completely off of me and showed absolutely no regard. She no longer cared for my business and she had no problem showing it. She even reassigned the nail tech to someone else bc I refused to be over charged for service. I asked why the original nail tech was no longer doing my fill, I got no answer. I looked over and saw the owner catering to customers that had just walked in. I sensed flaky business so I ultimately walked out without being serviced. Horrible customer service from the owner. I understand they use quality products but not everyone is looking to spend hundreds of dollars in a nail salon regardless of how "high end" it's self proclaimed to be!
Rewrite this for me: After returning for a fill and pedicure a week following my gel polish change, I was informed that the cost would exceed $85. Deciding it was too expensive, I chose to cancel the pedicure and only proceed with the fill. Initially, the owner of the salon was polite and attentive, but once she realized I refused to pay their exorbitant price, she began neglecting me and showed no concern whatsoever. It became evident that she no longer valued my business and she made that clear. To make matters worse, she even assigned a different nail technician to someone else solely because I refused to be overcharged. When I inquired about the change, I received no response. Instead, I observed the owner giving special attention to newly arrived customers. This lack of reliability and poor treatment made me question the integrity of their business, prompting me to leave without receiving any services. The owner's customer service was truly terrible. While I appreciate the use of quality products, not everyone wishes to spend excessively at a nail salon, regardless of its self-proclaimed "high-end" status.

input:
Ice cream wasn't the best, and definitely not for the price. But it was there when I was passing through Belmawr, and it hit the spot when I needed to satisfy my sweet tooth! 

The service was friendly, albeit a little slow. And the place has a cute, quaint charm about it with the decor. If I lived in the area I'd probably return, but I wouldn't make any special trips to go back here.
Rewrite this for me: Although the ice cream was not exceptional, especially considering its price, it conveniently caught my attention while I was in Belmawr and satisfied my craving for sweetness. The service was pleasant, albeit somewhat sluggish, and the establishment exuded a delightful and charming atmosphere through its decor. If I happened to reside in the vicinity, I might consider returning, but I wouldn't specifically plan a trip just to revisit this place.

input: Best auto body shop in Philadelphia in my opinion. My Honda Fit had accumulated all sorts of nicks, dents, scratches, and even some really ugly lime deposit stains on the hood of my car. I took it to Devlin's to get touched up, and what I got back was a car that looked like it just rolled off the assembly line. Honestly, if I told you my car was 3 years old and had gone through a few scrape-ups, I don't think you'd be able to tell. Ed Devlin is a miracle worker, and he does his magic at a super affordable price... I was shocked at how inexpensive the bill came out to be.
Rewrite this for me: In my opinion, I believe Devlin's is the finest auto body shop in Philadelphia. My Honda Fit had accumulated numerous nicks, dents, scratches, and unsightly lime deposit stains on its hood. Seeking a solution, I brought it to Devlin's and was astonished by the result. When I received my car back, it looked as if it had just rolled off the factory floor. Despite being three years old and having experienced a few scrape-ups, you would struggle to notice any imperfections. Ed Devlin truly works miracles and offers his services at a surprisingly affordable price. I was genuinely taken aback by the unexpectedly reasonable bill.

input:
Even though theres nothing ostensibly stand-out about 45, I spend quite a bit of time here. This is definitely a "Cheers" bar, where everybody knows your name. If you can make out their face through the haze of cigarette smoke, that is. Personally, the smoke doesn't bother me, though i have plenty of friends who refuse to go here for that reason. 

I just love the laid back, dive-y vibe. On game days, theres always a spread of food to help yourself to, which is such a nice tradition that you rarely see in bars now. During baseball season, well, I hope you're a Red Sox fan. If not, keep your allegiances quiet, lol. And theres often a food truck parked out front. Yum! A great pre or post show stop if you're seeing music at Tipitinas, which is just down the street.
Rewrite this for me:
Even though 45 doesn't have any obvious exceptional qualities, I find myself spending a significant amount of time here. It's like a "Cheers" bar where everyone knows your name, if you can see their faces through the thick cigarette smoke, that is. Personally, I don't mind the smoke, but I have friends who refuse to come here because of it.

What I really enjoy about this place is its relaxed and dive-like vibe. On game days, they always have a spread of food for everyone to enjoy, which is a rare and pleasant tradition in bars nowadays. And during baseball season, it's all about the Red Sox, so if you're not a fan, it's best to keep your allegiances low key, haha. Additionally, there's often a food truck parked outside, serving delicious treats. It's a perfect spot to grab a bite before or after a live music show at Tipitinas, which is conveniently just down the street.

input: Please note: the coffee is excellent! However, you have to ask for cream and sugar. I find this pretentious and intimidating. It's coffee. I want it how I want it. It shouldn't be such a big deal.
Rewrite this for me: Just a heads up: the coffee here is amazing! However, they don't automatically include cream and sugar. Personally, I find this a bit pompous and overwhelming. After all, it's just coffee. I believe you should be able to have it exactly how you prefer it without any fuss.

input:
Is it okay to say this is my favorite brunch spot even though all I've ever had here is their grits? I would definitely try one of their other courses and I'm pretty sure they're amazing, but it is so hard to not get my favorite thing off their menu! Their portion is so huge, i usually share it with another person (if I'm not being greedy)! You can literally top anything onto your dish and they vary from .50 cents to 1.00 dollar.  I love to add on avocados, red bell peppers, bacon, cheddar, and mushrooms! Their grits are incredible, it is not grainy nor watery. It's just perfect. I can go on and on. but I'm pretty sure you get the point! 

Eventually, i will try their other dishes, but for now, it's all about their grits.
Rewrite this for me: Is it acceptable to claim this as my favorite brunch spot even though I've only ever tried their grits? I do plan on exploring the rest of their menu, as I'm certain it's just as exceptional. However, I can't resist ordering my favorite dish every time due to its generous portion size. I usually end up sharing it with someone else, unless I'm feeling a bit indulgent! The best part is that you can customize your dish with a variety of toppings, ranging from 50 cents to 1 dollar. Personally, I love adding avocados, red bell peppers, bacon, cheddar, and mushrooms. Their grits are simply outstanding - perfectly cooked without any graininess or wateriness. I could go on and on about them, but I think you get the idea! Eventually, I do plan on trying their other offerings, but for now, it's all about those amazing grits.

input:
Great staff.  Nothing is ever disappointing - chili cheese etoufee is the BOMB.  It's a 4 instead of 5 stars because it's CASH ONLY.  But I love that you can also sit outside on nice evening.  

Don't forget the garlic sauce!
Rewrite this for me: The staff is fantastic and consistently delivers an excellent experience. The chili cheese etouffee is absolutely amazing. The only reason it's not a perfect five-star rating is because they only accept cash. However, it's wonderful that they offer outdoor seating for enjoyable evenings. And make sure to try their incredible garlic sauce!

input: Nice view from outside tables. It has typical beach food and typical beach service, but nice place to grab a drink with a view.
Rewrite this for me: The outside tables offer a pleasant view, while the establishment serves typical beach cuisine and provides typical beach service. However, it is an enjoyable spot to unwind with a refreshing drink, all while enjoying the picturesque scenery.

input: Is there any way that I can give a sixth or even seventh star to this place? Perhaps I'll contact the Yelp! corporate offices in San Francisco to inquire about expanding the star system using Lou and All About Hair as the Exhibit A. I've been on a three year odyssey, which has included some of the worst haircuts and barbers this side of, well, anything, to find a place like All About Hair. It is simply fantastic. I was here early on a Friday morning and aside from doing an incredible to the follicles that rest atop my head, Lou provided fantastic conversation and an environment that was more than inviting. I haven't written a Yelp! review in a very long time, but after my experience at All About Hair, I felt compelled to fire off a five star review about this gem of a place. Needless to say, I've found my barber of choice and they've made a long-term customer out of me.
Rewrite this for me: Can I give this place a sixth or even seventh star? Maybe I should contact the Yelp corporate offices in San Francisco to suggest expanding the star rating system, using Lou and All About Hair as a prime example. I've been on a three-year journey, encountering the worst haircuts and barbers you can imagine, until I stumbled upon All About Hair. It's absolutely amazing. I visited on a Friday morning and besides giving my hair an incredible makeover, Lou also engaged in fantastic conversation and created a welcoming atmosphere. I haven't written a Yelp review in ages, but after my experience at All About Hair, I couldn't resist giving it a glowing five-star review. Needless to say, I've finally found my go-to barber and I'll definitely be a loyal customer from now on.

input:
Updating previous trip- I still would take my kids there but the derma bond sucked. Poor buddy has a scar. Yea, yea...it's in a bad spot. And he's not quite two (read: squirmy.)

 :-/

It's disappointing because I don't think it's unreasonable to expect a better outcome.

input: This hotel has wonderful views of the airport, and it has the only revolving rooftop restaurant.  It's connected to the airport that has several restaurants and shops.  From the revolving rooftop restaurant, I could see the runways, and the control tower.
Rewrite this for me: This hotel boasts spectacular airport views, offering the exclusive experience of a revolving rooftop restaurant. It is conveniently situated adjacent to the airport, featuring a variety of restaurants and shops. While dining at the revolving rooftop restaurant, guests can enjoy breathtaking sights of the runways and the control tower.

input: Love this place! The turkey, beans, and biscuits are amazing. Have had better pecan pie but that won't stop me from coming back :)
Rewrite this for me: I absolutely adore this place! The turkey, beans, and biscuits are absolutely incredible. While I have tasted better pecan pie elsewhere, it certainly won't deter me from returning here :)

input: Large menu. Clean restaurant and restroom. Friendly staff. They were fairly busy in the middle of the day when we visited. This was my first time here and all we had was a sandwich so I can't give them 5 stars yet but for a family style restaurant and bar we enjoyed our meal. They had a decent draft beer selection and also serve wine and mixed drinks. There are crayons on every table and instead of a single place mat they put a large sheet of white paper on the tables for the kids to draw on.
Rewrite this for me: The restaurant offers a diverse menu with a wide variety of options. The establishment maintains a clean atmosphere, including the restaurant and restroom areas. The staff members are welcoming and hospitable. During our visit in the middle of the day, they seemed reasonably busy. As it was my first time visiting, I can only provide a preliminary rating based on the sandwich we had, but considering it is a family-oriented restaurant and bar, we thoroughly enjoyed our meal. Their assortment of draft beers is commendable, and they also serve wine and mixed drinks. Each table is equipped with crayons, and instead of a basic place mat, they provide a large sheet of white paper for children to draw on.

input:
Delicious crab cocktail and my husband loved his steamers. 

Only down fall is it is really humid in the restaurant itself. A fan would be nice.
Rewrite this for me: The crab cocktail was absolutely delicious, and my husband thoroughly enjoyed his steamers. The only drawback was the excessive humidity inside the restaurant, making a fan a much-welcomed addition.

input: Freddy's has the best fast-food style burgers I've ever had. Great toppings choices and fresh meat. Their fries are delicious with their "fry" sauce. Their custard is just as good as their food. It's rich and creamy, and did I mention how delicious it is.
Rewrite this for me: Freddy's boasts the most exceptional fast-food style burgers I have ever tasted. Offering an array of delectable toppings and using top-notch, freshly prepared meat, their burgers are truly unrivaled. Additionally, their fries are simply delightful, especially when paired with their savory "fry" sauce. As for their custard, it is paramount in quality and taste, with a rich and creamy texture that is difficult to match. It's important to note just how incredibly delicious their custard truly is.

input: This place had fantastic donuts! They were very well priced and so soft. We tried the blueberry cake donut and apple fritter. We will definitely be going back.
Rewrite this for me: The donuts at this place were absolutely amazing! Not only were they reasonably priced, but they were also incredibly soft. We indulged in the delectable blueberry cake donut and savored the delightful apple fritter. Without a doubt, we plan on returning for more in the future.

input:
I really had a wonderful experience at the Nashville location, and we found out that New Orleans had one now and should go to it. Last night we got there kinda late around 10pm. Sat there for 10min and not one person greeted us. Went to the bar to see about service and she informed that the kitchen was behind on completing orders. 
I had to apologize to my friends that we may not get any food after driving three hours down to enjoy the weekend. We did end up leaving the restaurant after 25 min wait for no service or an apology. 

I have to say this not what I expected from a big known place for adults to have fun along with kids also. Please do something about this. I hope this is not a reflection of how others could become.
Rewrite this for me:
I had a fantastic experience at the Nashville location and was excited to hear that there was now one in New Orleans. However, my recent visit to the New Orleans location left much to be desired. We arrived fairly late at around 10pm and waited for about 10 minutes without anyone acknowledging us. Frustrated, we decided to check with the bar for some assistance. The bartender informed us that the kitchen was behind on orders.

I had to apologize to my friends who had driven three hours to join me for the weekend, as it seemed unlikely that we would be getting any food. After waiting for 25 minutes without receiving any service or an apology, we decided to leave the restaurant.

This experience was far from what I had anticipated from a renowned establishment that caters to both adults and children. I urge you to address this issue promptly. I sincerely hope that this incident does not reflect the quality of service others may encounter.

input:
Allegro's is great. The pizza is really cheap, and lightning fast. My favorite was the sicilian, followed by the, uh, meaty kind, followed in a close third by anything stuffed (sometimes the centers were cold). They also sell beer, but I can't comment much on that because when I lived in Philadelphia I was under 21.
The only downside is the service (occasionally rude) and the constant crazies that hang out there talking to themselves.
Rewrite this for me:
Allegro's is an excellent place with amazing qualities. Their pizza is not only extremely affordable but also prepared at an astonishing speed. Personally, I adored the Sicilian style most, closely followed by the meaty variety, and ranking in a close third were any of their delicious stuffed pizzas (although, on occasions, the centers were not adequately heated). Additionally, they offer beer for sale, although I am unable to provide much insight on that aspect as I resided in Philadelphia during a time when I was underage.

However, the service can sometimes be a downside, with occasional rudeness from the staff. Another factor to consider is the presence of eccentric individuals who frequent the establishment, often engaging in conversations with themselves.

input:
This place treats you right from the moment you walk through the doors. I stay here every time I come to Reno, and the service seems to be getting better and better every time I return. On my last visit I stayed for free for 3 out of the 4 nights, and on top of that they gave me $120.00 of free play. The Peppermill is rated the casino with the loosest slots in casino. The rooms were clean,  the bathroom smelled great, and there weren't any bed bugs in our bed. The casino reminds me of old casino, when they relied on millions of lights bulbs, neon signs, and the smell of argon in the air. Happy hour everyday from 4-6 , you get mini apps and 3 dollar martinis at the fireside lounge. Also the Fish bar is awesome to go and relax, since they have a 40 foot aquarium that wraps around two of the walls. They have some excellent restaurants in the casino, that you don't even have to leave to satisfy any food craving you might have. The staff is extremely friendly and that is the top reason I keep coming back to this casino in Reno.
The only thing about this place is that the lights in the casino can really discombobulate you! Just remember that they key sleeve they give you has a map, so keep that in your pocket !
Rewrite this for me:
From the moment you step inside, this place provides exceptional treatment. Every time I visit Reno, I choose to stay here and each time the service surpasses my expectations. During my last visit, I even enjoyed a complimentary stay for three out of the four nights, along with $120.00 worth of free play. The Peppermill is renowned for having the loosest slot machines in the casino. The rooms are spotless, exuding a pleasant aroma, and I am relieved to report that we found no bed bugs in our bed. The casino itself evokes the nostalgic ambiance of old casinos with its multitude of light bulbs, neon signs, and the unmistakable scent of argon in the air. Between 4-6 pm, they offer a delightful happy hour at the fireside lounge, complete with tantalizing mini apps and $3 martinis. Moreover, the Fish bar provides a serene atmosphere, boasting a mesmerizing 40-foot aquarium that wraps around two walls. In terms of dining options, the casino offers a variety of excellent restaurants, ensuring you never have to leave to satisfy your cravings. Above all, the staff stands out for their incredible friendliness, which compels me to return to this casino in Reno time and time again.
The only drawback of this place is that the casino lights can be disorienting. However, fear not, as they provide a key sleeve with a helpful map that you can conveniently keep in your pocket!

input: Two very good experiences.  Excellent burger and very good pulled pork.  Wife loved her egg white and goat cheese omlette.  Solid beer list and a good spicy bloody Mary.  Also had great service and an ecclectic play list.
Rewrite this for me: We had two amazing experiences recently. We enjoyed an excellent burger and the pulled pork was also very good. My wife absolutely loved her egg white and goat cheese omelette. The restaurant had a wide selection of beers and their spicy bloody Mary was really good. Moreover, the service was great and they had an eclectic playlist that added to the overall experience.

input:
One of their guests went on a rampage and started punching random people, knocking one to the ground.  I told the bartender to call security, then I restrained the assailant as efficiently as humanly possible, causing no injuries, no striking, basically a bear hug, until security finally arrived.  Instead of a thank you I was told to go to my room or I would be trespassing--- fine, Did they look at the video and figure it out? Make it right later?  No.  I was treated poorly, and when I called days later, I got no response.  Spoke with Art in Security, and no call back. 

Not  the way to treat someone who helped you out. 

I will not be going back to Peppermill.
Rewrite this for me: One of their visitors went ballistic and began assaulting innocent bystanders, ultimately causing one person to fall to the ground. I promptly instructed the bartender to contact security, and then proceeded to efficiently immobilize the attacker with a harmless bear hug, ensuring no harm was done. Despite my efforts, instead of receiving gratitude, I was instructed to return to my room or face trespassing charges. Well, did they bother reviewing the footage to set things right later? Apparently not. I received poor treatment and, to make matters worse, my attempts at reaching out days later went unanswered. I even spoke with Art from Security, but still no response. It's disheartening to be treated this way after lending a helping hand. Needless to say, I won't be revisiting Peppermill.

input:
IF YOU ARE ON A STUDENT BUDGET, READ ON:

This is a 5 mile wide/long convention center. It has up to 2,000 guestrooms.  The conference I went to had 6,000 attendants. Of course I booked late and I didn't want to spend $200+/night on these hotel rooms! Otherwise this place is ginormous. The service (shuttle), lunch/drinks were really well done.  This place is immaculate; I do not know how many workers they staff.  

The food of course is overpriced (I had lunch/dinner at Wasabi. My bento box was $25.  Overpriced right?)  I also had lunch at the pizza place Paisano (forgot the name).   

If you decide to stay at the hotels across the street from the convention center (it is only 1 mile away - across from the McGovick Pwky).  They have Cracker Barrel, Apple Bees, Chillis?, McDonalds there.  The hotel I stayed in (being on a student budget) was crappy but I can't complain for $55/night.  It was Days Inn. It was walkable to shuttle pick up stop at Marriott Hotel (walk ~0.3 miles).  

They have Finleys pub, FUSE (night/club), STAX burger, Jack Daniels and more restaurants inside this convention center.  

I posted some photos.
Rewrite this for me:
Attention all students on a limited budget, please continue reading:

This convention center is absolutely massive, spanning a staggering 5 miles in both width and length. With a capacity for up to 2,000 guestrooms, it can accommodate a significant number of people. The conference I attended had a staggering 6,000 attendees. However, since I made my booking late, I was reluctant to spend over $200 per night on hotel rooms. Nevertheless, this place is truly enormous, and the service, including the shuttle and the food and drinks during lunch breaks, was top-notch. The convention center is impeccably maintained, although I can only guess at the number of staff members working there.

Unfortunately, the food at the convention center is quite expensive. For instance, I had lunch and dinner at Wasabi, where a simple bento box cost me a hefty $25. It's definitely overpriced! I also grabbed a bite at the pizza place Paisano, although I can't recall its exact name.

If you decide to stay across the street from the convention center, you'll find yourself just a mile away, opposite the McGovick Parkway. There, you'll discover familiar dining options such as Cracker Barrel, Applebee's, Chili's, and even McDonald's. Due to my student budget, I settled for a less-than-ideal hotel, Days Inn, which cost me only $55 per night. It was within walking distance of the Marriott Hotel, where the shuttle pick-up point was located, at a distance of approximately 0.3 miles.

Inside the convention center, you'll find a variety of restaurants to choose from, including Finleys pub, FUSE nightclub, STAX burger, Jack Daniels, and many more. I've even shared some photos for you to see.

input: I took an 8 year old and a 14 year old for the lunch special pizza.  We have done this on several occasions, and the kids love that they each get their own personal pizza, made the way they like.   They both ordered their pizza with 2 items and wanted BBQ sauce as the base instead of tomato sauce.  (this is the only way they enjoy pizza).   I was told that they could only get tomato sauce, not BBQ sauce.   I explained that we have gotten it this way several times before.   We were told that they don't offer it this way any more.   I see that some of the pizzas offer BBQ sauce and pointed it out, but again was told that it couldn't be made this way for them.   I asked if I could pay additional to have it made with BBQ sauce, but once again told it was not possible.   Sadly, we left the restaurant and chose a different nearby restaurant for lunch.  I'm sorry to say I won't be able to take the kids here anymore.
Rewrite this for me: I took two children, aged 8 and 14, to the lunch special at a pizza place. This has become a regular occurrence because the kids love having their own personal pizzas, customized to their liking. They both requested pizzas with two toppings and BBQ sauce as the base instead of tomato sauce, as this is the only way they truly enjoy pizza. However, we were informed that they could only have tomato sauce and not BBQ sauce. I mentioned that we have received BBQ sauce on their pizzas before, but we were told that it is no longer offered. I even pointed out that some of the pizzas on the menu feature BBQ sauce, but unfortunately, they still couldn't accommodate our request. I inquired about paying extra to have the pizzas made with BBQ sauce, but once again, we were denied. Disappointed, we left the restaurant and opted for a different nearby establishment for lunch. I'm regretful to say that I won't be able to bring the kids to this restaurant anymore.

input: Super cute place! Employees are very nice! Cookie dough is delicious! This is a must & we are glad we found it (lost while in town).
Rewrite this for me: This place is absolutely adorable! The staff members are incredibly friendly, and their cookie dough is absolutely delicious! We highly recommend visiting here, especially if you happen to be in town and searching for a hidden gem. We're so grateful to have stumbled upon it!

input:
Tacos.....
The chips and salsa were pretty lame.....and the tacos were ok.....nothing special.....
Rewrite this for me: The chips and salsa served were rather lackluster, while the tacos were alright, without anything particularly outstanding.

input: Excited to have this place in Reno! Delicious matcha and ube flavors! Like authentic. Friendly staff, looking to get better but what they have as a base is solid. Soft serve, cake and the sauces aren't overly sweet.  Hoping they add more flavors!
Rewrite this for me: I'm thrilled to have discovered this place in Reno! They offer incredibly tasty matcha and ube flavors that truly capture the authentic taste. The staff is friendly and although there's always room for improvement, they have a solid foundation. Their soft serve, cake, and sauces are perfectly balanced and not overly sweet. I can't wait for them to introduce more flavors!

input: Delicious. So happy I Yelped for a restaurant closer to home and stumbled upon this. It's small and pleasant inside with some decent hip hop setting the mood. The menu is small, but packed a punch. We ordered the Duck Fries, which were heaven. Fries smothered in smoked gouda,  shredded duck, and scallions. For 8 bucks came a pretty large bowl that I couldn't stop picking at. I ordered one of the specials, the scallop and foie gras  tacos...wow...so good (then I read the origin of foie gras and hated myself, but aside that...). The person I was with ordered the pork roll burger, which I tried of course. It was incredibly juicy and cooked perfect. I will definitely come back here. Definitely.
Rewrite this for me: This place is absolutely delicious! I'm so glad I used Yelp to find a restaurant closer to my home and stumbled upon this gem. The atmosphere inside is cozy and inviting, with some great hip hop music playing in the background. Although the menu is small, each dish really packs a punch. We decided to try the Duck Fries, and they were like heaven in a bowl. These fries were generously covered in smoked gouda, shredded duck, and scallions. For only 8 bucks, we received a pretty large portion that I couldn't resist picking at. As for my main course, I went with one of the specials, which was the scallop and foie gras tacos. Oh my goodness, they were so incredibly delicious (although I did feel a bit guilty after reading about the origin of foie gras). The person I was dining with ordered the pork roll burger, and of course I had to try a bite. It was incredibly juicy and perfectly cooked. I am already looking forward to coming back to this restaurant again soon. No doubt about it, I will definitely be returning.

input: Went to Three Muses our first night in New Orleans. The plates are tapas style, small and meant for sharing. Between the four of us we got the blue cheese stuffed dates, the crawfish egg rolls, steak and cake, lamb sliders, feta fries and fish tacos. Everything was really good,i could have done without the tacos, but the lamb sliders and the steak and cake were AMAZING. The goat cheese paired with the lamb was to die for. And the crab cake was the best I have ever had.
Rewrite this for me: On our first night in New Orleans, we visited Three Muses. The menu consisted of tapas style dishes, small portions intended for sharing. Our group of four indulged in an assortment of delectable plates, including the blue cheese stuffed dates, crawfish egg rolls, steak and cake, lamb sliders, feta fries, and fish tacos. Overall, the food was remarkable, although personally, I could have done without the tacos. Undoubtedly, the lamb sliders and steak and cake stole the show with their astounding flavors. The combination of goat cheese with the lamb was simply divine, while the crab cake surpassed all others I've ever tasted.

input: Great ambiance!  Loved the trendy and modern decor.  The presentation of the dishes was also great.  The food was just okay though.  The potatoes weren't cooked and the pancakes were a bit on the greasy side.  Would def. go back again and give it another try...french toast and omelette looked good!  I would also like to try their lunch. Service was excellent.
Rewrite this for me: The ambiance was fantastic! I absolutely adored the stylish and contemporary decor. Additionally, the presentation of the dishes was impressive. However, the food itself was only mediocre. The potatoes were undercooked and the pancakes were excessively greasy. Despite this, I would definitely consider returning for another visit. The french toast and omelette appeared enticing, and I am curious to experience their lunch menu as well. The service provided was exceptional.

input: This place is awesome the food is dynamite . Super friendly service. And the. Coup de grace was the flan made in house fresh and believe me I've tried flan everywhere, there's is exceptional. The price was right on point. My only suggestion to make this place go into the stratosphere is if they had a liquor license.
Rewrite this for me: This place is incredible, with exceptional food that is simply dynamite. The service provided is super friendly and first-rate. What truly impressed me was their in-house made flan, which was incredibly fresh and truly exceptional. I've tried flan at various places, but theirs was outstanding. Moreover, the price was just right. The only way this place could reach even higher heights would be if they obtained a liquor license.

input: Had breakfast with the family after a quick stopover. Great food and service (thanks Jonathan!), definaelty a good find that was busy but had no wait on a Saturday.
Rewrite this for me: I enjoyed a family breakfast after a brief stopover. The food and service were excellent (special thanks to Jonathan!). It was a fantastic discovery, bustling with customers yet no wait time on a Saturday.

input: During the parents' visit,  dad wanted some southern food. We tried Willie Maes, but the line was long and they weren't crazy about the area.  So we waited a bit and went down to The Praline Connection. Dad was in heaven. He's been talking about the food since we left. Dad got the taste of soul platter pictured below. He said the fried chicken was the best he's had and he had not tasted red beans and rice like that since he was a kid and my granny used to make em. Mom got the meatloaf with cabbage and lima beans. I got the ribs with potato salad and mac and cheese. My ribs were good but hard to cut the meat off the bone. I could've ate em with my hands but I didn't want a BBQ face. The potato salad was good but my mac & cheese was a little bland. The cornbread was great.  I'm going back next time for the fried chicken!
Rewrite this for me: During our parents' visit, my dad had a craving for some southern cuisine. We decided to try Willie Maes, but unfortunately, the line was quite long and the area didn't appeal to them. So, we patiently waited for a while and ended up going to The Praline Connection instead. It turned out to be a hit with dad, as he was in culinary paradise. Ever since we left, he hasn't stopped raving about the delicious food. Dad had the soul platter featured in the picture below and absolutely loved it. According to him, the fried chicken was the best he had ever tasted, and it brought back childhood memories of my granny's flavorful red beans and rice. Mom opted for the meatloaf served with cabbage and lima beans, while I went for the ribs accompanied by potato salad and mac and cheese. Though the ribs were tasty, they proved to be a bit challenging to eat due to the difficulty in separating the meat from the bone. I contemplated using my hands, but I didn't want to end up with a barbecue-smeared face. The potato salad was enjoyable, but the mac and cheese lacked flavor. However, the highlight of the meal was undoubtedly the delectable cornbread. I can't wait to visit The Praline Connection again, especially for the mouthwatering fried chicken!

input:
Buddy Brew is a very trendy coffee shop based in Tampa. Their coffee is flavorful and their presentation is nice. I really liked the fact that their lattes and cappuccinos have beautiful latte art on top. The store has a beautiful modern design that reminds me of coffee shops in New York. 

This particular location is in Hyde Park Village. The benefit is that parking is free. The down side is that seating is limited. The store is also extremely cold, so it is uncomfortable to sit and socialize for very long. You may be better off getting your coffee to go and walking around Hyde Park Village instead.
Rewrite this for me:
Located in Tampa, Buddy Brew is an incredibly trendy coffee shop that offers a remarkable coffee experience. Their flavorsome coffee is complemented by an aesthetically pleasing presentation. One aspect that particularly stood out to me was the beautiful latte art adorning their lattes and cappuccinos. Furthermore, the modern design of the store evokes a reminiscent feel of coffee shops in New York.

Conveniently situated in Hyde Park Village, this particular Buddy Brew location offers the advantage of free parking. However, it is important to note that seating is limited, presenting a slight drawback. Additionally, the store tends to be excessively cold, making extended periods of socializing uncomfortable. In such instances, it might be more suitable to grab your coffee to go and take a stroll through the charming streets of Hyde Park Village.

input:
A really nice place to get your hair did with as much of an edge as you want.  

In the East Loop, across from the Pageant, might be one of the most underrated salons in the city.  I first went into this place as a walk-in, and keep on going back.  Yes, I'm a guy, and since my hair is pretty coarse, grows weird, and I want a bit of style to it, I go to hair salons.  At V Vegaz I've never been dissatisfied with my cut. 

When you walk in you realize how spacious the place is, with a bit of a slightly modern, slightly baroque interior design.  There's a nice vibe there too amongst the employees, and you can see that the stylists are happy with the work situation.  Of course, happy stylists, to me, mean better haircuts.

I go to Callie, since that first walk-in, and keep on going back.  Yes, she's real friendly, which is a nice touch, but she's also a great stylist.  I'm a bit wishy washy when I look for a cut, usually changing what I want most of the time.  Callie's sensitive to that, and really understands how my hair grows and where it's going to move.   I think the biggest compliment to her is that, as I'm a once a month haircut kinda guy, my brother and sister told me they really my hair a full month after I had it cut with Callie.  So that's really a testament to her skills.

I've not gotten color there, but it is a full service salon, and not just a turn and burn place.  

I highly recommend this place.
Rewrite this for me:
Located in the East Loop, just across from the Pageant, there is a hidden gem of a salon that doesn't receive the recognition it deserves. I stumbled upon this place as a walk-in and have been a loyal customer ever since. Despite being a guy with coarse and unruly hair, I believe in the power of a good haircut and V Vegaz never disappoints.

Upon entering, you'll notice the spaciousness of the salon, adorned with a tastefully modern yet slightly baroque interior design. The atmosphere is pleasant, and you can tell that the stylists genuinely enjoy working there. And let me tell you, happy stylists result in better haircuts.

My go-to stylist is Callie. From that initial walk-in, I immediately formed a connection with her friendly demeanor. But it's not just her personality that keeps me coming back - she is a phenomenal stylist. I tend to change my mind quite often when it comes to my desired haircut, but Callie is always understanding and possesses a deep understanding of how my hair grows and moves. The ultimate compliment I can give her is that my brother and sister genuinely loved my haircut a month after I had it done by Callie - a true testament to her skills.

While I haven't personally tried their coloring services, it's worth mentioning that V Vegaz is a full-service salon, not just a quick in-and-out establishment.

In conclusion, I wholeheartedly recommend this salon. It truly is a haven for those seeking an edgy or unique hair transformation.

input:

input:
Late one Saturday night, some friends and I made the mistake of trying to get drinks at Plough and the Stars and left very quickly. We were walking around trying to find somewhere else to go, noticed this unmarked bar and decided to check it out. We were so excited to see that there were so many great beers on tap, and there was a decent crowd there so we stuck around. It was a fun night! And after a few weeks of wondering where we had gone, we were able to find the Irish Pol on Yelp :D

I went back for happy hour recently and it wasn't exactly as I had remembered. It was pretty dark and dingy looking inside,  and the few people there were much much older. It just had a weird vibe. The beer was still great of course. The happy hour special was $3 drafts, but most of the beers I wanted weren't included. I won't be back for happy hour, but I would definitely stop in on a Saturday night!
Rewrite this for me:

That's when we stumbled upon an unmarked bar and decided to give it a try. We were thrilled to see an impressive selection of beers on tap and a decent crowd, so we decided to stay and had a great time. After searching for weeks, we finally found the Irish Pol on Yelp, relieving our curiosity.

However, my recent visit for happy hour didn't quite live up to my expectations. The interior was dimly lit and didn't look very inviting. Moreover, the crowd consisted mostly of older people, giving off a strange atmosphere. Despite these drawbacks, the beer was still fantastic. The happy hour special offered $3 drafts, but disappointingly, most of the beers I wanted were not included. As a result, I won't be returning for happy hour, but I would definitely consider stopping by on a lively Saturday night!

input: Hands down the best spaghetti & meatballs I've ever had. The atmosphere here is so nice and cozy. It has just won out as my favorite Italian restaurant.
Rewrite this for me: Without a doubt, the spaghetti & meatballs I've just savored are unparalleled. The ambiance at this place is incredibly inviting and snug. It has unquestionably secured its position as my preferred Italian eatery.

input: We arrived at Happy Hour, 50 cent oysters and half price drinks, so we had both, the ordered the beet salad (divine), mussels, and flammenkuchen (an appetizer I used for my entree),  All were excellent.  I first had flammenkuchen (or tarte flambe) in Strasbourg at a street fair, this was far and above that experience, with caramelized onions resting atop the cheese and hunks of bacon strewn around.  So good!

input: Have eaten at this place 3 times. Every time was a good experience for me and the kids. No smoke No noise and good food good service. input: Great pizza! The place is beautiful and the atmosphere is truly inviting. The service is very nice and fast.

input: Great dinner started with a wonderful fresh Caesar salad and bread followed by delicious cheese ravioli with pesto cream sauce. The pesto sauce was perfect, not overpowering the delicate pasta. I also enjoyed the Dunham cabernet. Delicious. Welcome to downtown, Richard's.
Rewrite this for me: Welcome to downtown, Richard's. Our dining experience began with a delightful and refreshing Caesar salad, complemented by freshly baked bread. To further enhance the meal, I relished a glass of Dunham cabernet, adding to the overall enjoyment of the evening. Exquisite flavors await you at Richard's.

input:
Had a great breakfast here last weekend before we headed out. You order at the front and they will bring the food out. I had the French toast (fruit on the side)  with an a la carte fried egg on the side. They dropped my egg when they got to the table but promptly brought out another one. I also had a vanilla latte which was yummy....no extra sweeteners needed. 

We sat outside on the patio which was just lovely. Even if you sat inside, like other restaurants in the French quarter, every door and windows are open, so fresh breezes flow throughout. Really nice experience.
Rewrite this for me:
Last weekend, we had an amazing breakfast at this place before setting off. You place your order at the front counter and the staff will bring your food to your table. Additionally, I indulged in a delicious vanilla latte that didn't require any extra sweeteners.

We chose to sit outside on the delightful patio. Even if you decide to dine indoors, similar to other eateries in the French quarter, every door and window remains open, allowing refreshing breezes to circulate. It was truly a pleasant experience.

input:

The food was good, but not great. I had quiche and my guest had a croque madame. The crust of the quiche wasn't done and the bread on the croque wasn't that great. Otherwise these two dishes would have been perfect. The fruit was fresh and the coffee was great!

I will definitely return.
Rewrite this for me:
Arriving early for church, we decided to grab a swift meal. The ambiance of the place was truly welcoming, with every member of the staff ensuring to acknowledge our presence!

The taste of the food was satisfactory, yet not exceptional. I opted for a quiche while my companion chose a croque madame. Unfortunately, the quiche crust had not been cooked thoroughly, and the bread in the croque was not as impressive. Nevertheless, had these minor issues been resolved, both dishes would have been impeccable. On the bright side, the fruit was delightfully fresh, and the coffee was superb!

Without a doubt, I intend to revisit this place in the future.

input:

We started with the Crabby Dip which the whole family enjoyed but feel it was a little overpriced at $14.  For the main course I enjoyed a Salty Burger while she had the macadamia crusted grouper, both were excellent choices!  Service was spot on making this a five star experience for us!
Rewrite this for me:
