input:
Stayed here for a bachelorette party. This place got the job done. Unfortunately, all the hotels in Santa Barbara are pretty freaking pricey. A lot of the other hotels started at $400+ /night.  This ain't Vegas where you can get something pretty cushy for $250. This seemed like a decent option on the lower end. Our rooms were about $250 a night. A lot of the other hotels in the area were already booked for the weekend or required more than one night to book. 

Pros: 
-decently priced
-clean and cozy rooms
-charming exterior and grounds
-relatively comfortable beds
-bath and body works shampoo, body wash etc
-free water bottles and fruit waiting for you in the room

Cons:
-dated decor 
-toilet issues: The hook inside kept coming undone. I guess we decided not to get maintenance because we temporarily fixed it, but it kept coming undone so it wouldn't really flush. We were checking out that day, so we decided just to deal with it. 
- door was difficult to open without using a certain technique
-no hair dryer, so bring your own
-no complimentary breakfast
-a bit noisy in the morning, but I slept fine. I guess the window in the bathroom was open or something for some ventilation.

Overall, I still don't think I would've chosen to stay anywhere else in Santa Barbara, so BW Pepper Tree Inn was still a good choice based on the location of the bachelorette and price range.
Rewrite this for me:
We stayed at BW Pepper Tree Inn for a bachelorette party and it served its purpose. Unfortunately, all the hotels in Santa Barbara are quite expensive. Most of them started at $400+ per night, unlike Vegas where you can find something nice for $250. Considering this, the inn seemed like a decent and more affordable option. Our rooms cost around $250 per night. However, many other hotels in the area were already fully booked for the weekend or required a minimum stay of more than one night.

Pros:
- The price was reasonable.
- The rooms were clean and cozy.
- The exterior and grounds were charming.
- The beds were relatively comfortable.
- Bath and Body Works toiletries (shampoo, body wash, etc.) were provided.
- Complimentary water bottles and fruit were waiting in the room.

Cons:
- The decor was outdated.
- There were some issues with the toilet, as the hook inside kept coming undone, affecting its flushing ability. We decided not to call maintenance since we were checking out that day and managed to temporarily fix it ourselves.
- The door was difficult to open without using a specific technique.
- No hair dryer was provided, so you need to bring your own.
- There was no complimentary breakfast.
- Some morning noise could be heard, but it didn't disturb my sleep. It seemed to be coming from the bathroom window, which was possibly left open for ventilation.

Overall, despite the drawbacks, I wouldn't have chosen to stay anywhere else in Santa Barbara. BW Pepper Tree Inn was still a good choice for the bachelorette party due to its location and affordable price range.

input: In my book you can never go wrong having a good old-fashioned meal a Johnny Rockets. I had their recent promo which was a barbecued pulled pork burger. Rewrite this for me: You can always count on having a satisfying classic meal at Johnny Rockets, as stated in my book. input: I always am in favor of local businesses.  They have a big selection here and you get free popcorn.  Why go to the big boys and have to pay for popcorn when you can get it here for free?

input:
I still love this place just as much as I ever did, and here's why:

1) Super friendly and knowledgeable staff 
2) Roomy, with lots of outlets and enough space to accommodate mid-sized groups (like the recent Yelp Office Hours)
3) Delicious tea, of course!

I've always loved their "Awake" Fizz Tea, but I've also broadened my horizons to include Pearl Tea (aka bubble tea). The taro flavor rocked my socks off. It did take a little getting used to though, as I had a mini anxiety attack every time I took a sip. Because I got it warm, it was in a paper cup and I never knew when a pearl was making its way into my mouth. As a result, I spent half my drink wondering "is there one in my straw?" It's totally worth the suspense, though.

The only thing that still troubles me is the music. It's just...not right. In fact, sometimes it's pretty distracting. It's easily avoided, however; just bring headphones and your own musical selection and all is well.
Rewrite this for me:
I still have an immense love for this place, just like before, and here's why:

2) The place is spacious, with plenty of power outlets and enough room to accommodate medium-sized groups, like during the recent Yelp Office Hours.
3) Needless to say, the tea is absolutely delicious!

The only thing that still bothers me is the music. It just doesn't feel right. In fact, it can be quite distracting at times. Fortunately, there's an easy solution: bring your own headphones and enjoy your own choice of music. That way, everything will be perfect.

input: Yah Man was yah man! Go here and enjoy the atmosphere, the personal service and delicious Caribbean fare. The beef pie was yummy as was the chicken and island sampler plates. Their beef pie and chicken, alongside the island sampler plates, are absolutely delightful. And let's not forget about the heavenly bread pudding! We departed feeling fully satisfied and content. Whether you're a local or a tourist in Tampa, this is a must-visit spot. The staff is friendly and welcoming. By the way, this is my third Yelp post, and I simply had to share this gem of a place because it's that good!

input:
Favorite place to go in New Orleans. Chill backyard bar with great local music options.

Smaller groups are better- seating can get tight. The wine and cheese bar up front services the live music venue in back. You can pick 3 or more cheeses and they put together a lovely cheese and accoutrements tray for you. You can also choose a wine to open up in the back. Wines have a great selection, mid-range price (almost all winces over $10-20 a bottle).

Great place to spend the night and have a wonderful time away from the packed tourists hot spots. (Mind you, this place is well known and a hot spot itself).
Rewrite this for me: My preferred destination in New Orleans is a laid-back backyard bar that offers fantastic local music options. It's ideal for smaller groups as seating can be limited. The front part of the bar serves as a wine and cheese bar, which complements the live music venue at the back. You have the option to select three or more cheeses, and they will curate a delightful tray with accompanying accoutrements. Additionally, you can choose a wine to enjoy in the back area. The wine selection is extensive, with prices ranging from moderate to mid-range (most bottles priced between $10-20). This spot is perfect for a memorable evening away from the bustling tourist areas, though it's worth noting that it's quite popular and considered a hotspot in its own right.

input: Had a great lunch here. I ordered a chicken Caesar and my dining companion ordered a custom salad. Waitress had a great personality and did not rush us at all. Allowed us to linger. Great space which is hidden from the outside.
Rewrite this for me: I had a wonderful lunch at this place. I opted for a chicken Caesar while my dining partner ordered a personalized salad. input: Made reservation a over a week ago with request to be near band. On arrival they had no record of it. There open tables near front and were told they were for people with reservations
Rewrite this for me: I made a reservation more than a week ago, specifically requesting to be seated near the band. However, upon arrival, the staff had no record of my reservation. Despite this disappointment, I must give five stars for the excellent cocktails, food, band, and overall atmosphere. However, I must give one star for the complete lack of organization displayed by the establishment. The staff member who took our reservation claimed to be new, but it's always advisable to call and confirm, lesson learned. This experience has been particularly disappointing, especially considering the amazing experiences we have had here in the past. It was disheartening to see that there were available tables near the front, and yet we were told they were reserved for other guests.

input: Great professional tat shop!! My husband and I are very happy with our new ink. Bryan did an outstanding job and I highly recommend him. input: Love this place.  Best view in Santa Barbara.   Awesome wines.  My wife and I are industry, and always treated great.  Tom and Gillian are ALWAYS generous hosts.  My wife works @carrwinery and always refers customers to them.  The Conway cabs are the best SB has to offer.  One of their tasting room employees just gifted us a Conway 13 reserve Syrah.  Beautiful. ...  Thank you Tommy.   Rolos red is a bottle that any wine snob would love,  but a great bottle for those finding their pallet as well.  My son is 5 and always wants mom and dad to go wine tasting when we hit the pier. Never disappointed.
Rewrite this for me:
I absolutely adore this place. It has the most incredible view in Santa Barbara and the wines are truly amazing. As members of the industry, my wife and I are always treated exceptionally well. Tom and Gillian, the hosts, are consistently generous and accommodating. In fact, my wife, who works at Carr Winery, often recommends their wines to customers. The Conway cabs they serve are without a doubt the finest that Santa Barbara has to offer. During our recent visit, one of their tasting room employees surprised us with a bottle of Conway 13 reserve Syrah, and it was absolutely stunning. Thank you so much, Tommy, for your generosity.

Speaking of great bottles, Rolos red is a wine that any wine snob would appreciate, but it is also perfect for those who are still discovering their palate. To give you an idea of how much we enjoy visiting this place, our 5-year-old son always insists that Mom and Dad go wine tasting whenever we visit the pier. And let me tell you, we have never been disappointed.

input:

input: This place is amazing!!! There aren't enough words for how amazing the food is here. Rewrite this for me: I am absolutely in awe of this place! Words alone cannot adequately describe just how incredible the food here is. input: Such a cool atmosphere and unlike anything I've ever been to. You walk into the wine and cheese shop, select a bottle (or 2!) and then select whatever cheeses and meats you so choose from a refrigerator. Once you have your items, you bring it to the counter to pay, they take your cheeses and meats, and deliver it to your outside (or upstairs inside in our case due to the rain!) and it's like magic. It comes back a beautiful cheese board with nuts and spreads and a delicious loaf of sliced artisan bread! Highly recommended! They also have a menu t order from the kitchen if you really need more, but two of us were full after our platter and wine!
Rewrite this for me: The atmosphere is absolutely amazing and unlike any other place I've visited. As you enter the wine and cheese shop, you have the freedom to choose a bottle (or maybe even two!) and pick out your desired cheeses and meats from the refrigerator. Once you've made your selections, you proceed to the counter to make your payment. At this point, the staff takes your chosen cheeses and meats and magically transforms them into a beautiful cheese board accompanied by nuts, spreads, and a delightful loaf of sliced artisan bread. We had the option to enjoy our delightful spread outside, but due to the rain, we were offered a lovely indoor seating area upstairs. Highly recommended! In addition to their cheese offerings, you can also order from their kitchen menu if you're craving more. However, the two of us were pleasantly satisfied after indulging in our generous platter and enjoying the accompanying wine.

input: Seriously one of the most pleasant dining experiences I have had in a while. Smiley himself is a true gem and the food was DELICIOUS. Had so much that I am eating it for lunch again today - and I can't wait! Please recommend to everyone you know in Manayunk, don't want to lose this place!

input: My friend and I had dinner here on Sunday. I was surprised to be seated next to another party on the same table with just a small partition separating us. input: Was rather disappointed in the service.  We found our own table as requested to do but wait staff continually walked by without even acknowledging us. I have previously enjoyed trying flights at different breweries as a means to discover a favorite, but unfortunately, this was not the case here.

input:
I have been here twice for breakfast.  The set-up is really awkward and it's clear the people running it on Saturday mornings don't really know what they're doing.  It's stressful to hear them cursing under their breath and yelling at their line cook, Carlos.  

You are instructed to order at the counter....except ocassionally, for certain clients, they'll actually come to your table and take your order ...but it seems pretty random.  It's all self serve (shitty) coffee and bottled beverages.  After a long time with the sun beating down on you (there are no shades for front window), the food arrives and it's Ok.  there was a lot of grizzle in my pulled pork texas wrap,  but the cornbread pancakes were tasty.  

You then pay afterwards---why not just pay when you get it?  I would like to minimize my face time with the awkward people who staff it on Saturday A.M.s, but no such luck. 

I brought my out-of-town brother here for brunch and regret it.  it's somewhat tasty, but kind of a dive.  Don't go here if you expect a nice/traditional b-fast service (i.e. a waiter and people who fill up your coffee.)  That said, it's pretty cheap so, guess you get what you paid for.
Rewrite this for me:
I have visited this place twice for breakfast and each time, I found the setup to be quite awkward. The individuals in charge on Saturday mornings seem inexperienced and unsure of what they are doing. It is stressful to hear them muttering curse words and yelling at their line cook, Carlos.

The instructions are to order at the counter, although occasionally, they will come to your table and take your order, but this seems to happen randomly. The coffee and bottled beverages are self-serve and not of great quality. Additionally, there are no shades for the front window, so you end up sitting in the sun for a while. Eventually, the food arrives, and while it is decent, my pulled pork Texas wrap contained a lot of gristle. On the bright side, the cornbread pancakes were tasty.

What baffles me is the fact that you have to pay after you receive your food. It would make more sense to pay upfront. I had hoped to minimize interaction with the awkward staff on Saturday mornings, but unfortunately, that wasn't possible.

I made the mistake of bringing my out-of-town brother here for brunch and now regret it. The food is somewhat flavorful, but the overall atmosphere of the place is rather run-down. If you are looking for a pleasant and traditional breakfast experience with waitstaff filling up your coffee, I would advise against coming here. However, considering its affordability, I suppose you get what you pay for.

input: Great classic Greek diner. The Greek omelette with feta, gyro meat, tomato and spinach was super. Classic griddle home fries and outstanding service. We will seek it out when we return to the area.
Rewrite this for me: This diner offers a fantastic experience with classic Greek food. The Greek omelette, filled with feta, gyro meat, tomato, and spinach, was absolutely delicious. The griddle home fries were cooked perfectly, and the service was exceptional. When we come back to this area, we will definitely make a point to find this place again.

input: Sat down over a half hour, only miso and drinks served. Waiting for actual food ordered or someone to cook it ....waiting ...
Rewrite this for me: I patiently sat for more than thirty minutes, yet only miso soup and beverages were brought to my table. I anxiously waited for the actual food I had ordered, or for someone to start preparing it. The anticipation continued, as the wait persisted.

input: Great Doctor. Friendly . Attentive. Professional. Funny.

input: I was craving for Ramen when I found this gem, but it wasn't the Ramen that I'm rating here (it falls a bit short comparing to the Ramens I've had in NY). That Steven roll!!! That was one of the best rolls that I've had! Good thing I was pretty hungry and asked for roll recommendations. I was definitely not disappointed. I would love to come back once I visit Philly again.
Rewrite this for me: When I stumbled upon this hidden spot, I had a hankering for Ramen. However, the Ramen I tried fell slightly short in comparison to the incredible Ramens I've tasted in New York. But oh boy, that Steven roll! It was absolutely outstanding and easily one of the best rolls I've ever had. Luckily, my hunger pushed me to seek out roll recommendations and I definitely wasn't let down. I can't wait to return the next time I visit Philly.

input: Unless you have gray hair , are over 45 and appear wealthy , don't expect to get good service . My girlfriend and I sat there and witnessed our waitress cut up with many older couples in suits , then would check on us every half hour to 40 minutes , and didn't even check on our steaks and how they were prepared. The management never asked how our meal was ,(we witnessed them going table to table). VERY disappointed for spending $80, to get this poor of service .
Rewrite this for me: If you don't meet the criteria of having gray hair, being over 45, and appearing wealthy, don't anticipate receiving satisfactory service. During our dining experience, my girlfriend and I observed the waitress engaging in lively conversations with several older couples dressed in suits. Meanwhile, she would only check on us every thirty to forty minutes and failed to inquire about the preparation of our steaks. Surprisingly, the management never inquired about our meal despite visiting other tables. We are extremely disappointed with the quality of service received after spending $80.

input: The Paris Hair Salon is a warm, friendly inviting personal experience with people who really know hair. I have thick unruly hair and many don't take the time to carefully go through it. Paris Hair takes the time and makes it right, I am so pleased, and the price is right too. Cut, color and hilites all perfect, every time! -Maureen Kerfoot
Rewrite this for me: Maureen Kerfoot highly recommends the Paris Hair Salon as it offers a warm and inviting atmosphere with knowledgeable hair experts. Unlike many other salons, they pay special attention to thick and unruly hair, taking the time to thoroughly work through it. Maureen is delighted with the exceptional results and reasonable prices offered by Paris Hair. Whether it's a haircut, color, or highlights, they consistently deliver perfection.

input:
I love Chick-Fil-A so much and was so excited to get one down the street from me! No more sudden realizations that I'm in Rivergate or Cool Springs and should take advantage of a Chick-Fil-A. I could go any time!

But. What. The. Hell.

Apparently Nashvillians don't know how to use a double lane drive through.

And may I ask why the drive thru goes around the front of the restaurant instead of the back of the restaurant like every other damn fast food restaurant?

Though, kudos for the free WiFi that I can use on my phone while I'm waiting twenty minutes in line at the drive thru.

So I avoid this place like the plague. I'll wait til next time I'm in Rivergate or Cool Springs for some amazing waffle fries.
Rewrite this for me:
I have a deep love for Chick-Fil-A and was overjoyed when one opened near my location. Finally, I thought, no more unexpected realizations that I happen to be in Rivergate or Cool Springs and should seize the opportunity to visit Chick-Fil-A. The convenience of being able to go anytime was incredible.

However, there was a shocking revelation. It seems that the people of Nashville have trouble understanding how to utilize a double lane drive-thru. Additionally, I can't help but question why the drive-thru at this particular Chick-Fil-A goes around the front of the restaurant, unlike every other fast food establishment in existence.

On a positive note, I must commend them for providing complimentary WiFi that allows me to pass the time on my phone during the excruciating twenty-minute wait in the drive-thru line.

Due to these frustrations, I now avoid this location like the plague. Instead, I patiently wait until I'm in Rivergate or Cool Springs again to indulge in the glorious waffle fries.

input:

Will definitely be back to try more things.
Rewrite this for me:
I had a fantastic time at this place! The service was excellent and fast, and what I loved the most was that you could stay and relax after your meal since you've already paid in advance. 

The food was absolutely delicious and made from fresh ingredients. I particularly enjoyed my chicken taco salad and the plantains we ordered. The drinks, especially the mojito, were also impressive.

I will definitely return to explore more dishes on their menu.

input:

input: Just got a pedi so I can't speak to the massage but my pedi was amazing. Place is clean and very nice, I did not have to wait at all and most importantly they know their stuff.

input: Yats is the best Cajun Food that we have ever eaten and is quite economical to enjoy.  The menu is quite eclectic in that they cook each day what they want to cook and put it on a chalkboard.  You just never know what kind of tasty delight you will find on any one day.  This is a regular place to visit for my wife and I.
Rewrite this for me: Yats has surpassed all other Cajun Food experiences we've had, and it offers great value for money. The constantly changing menu adds to its charm as they cook their desired creations daily, showcasing them on a chalkboard. Each visit offers a delightful surprise of unique flavors. Needless to say, it has become a favorite spot for my wife and me.

input: I was impressed with this pizza place's selection.  I stopped in for a quick bite and ordered a roast beef sandwich (that was very delicious.)  The sandwich did take about 15 to 20 minutes to get out of the kitchen.  Seating is non-existent in the restaurant, but there is a community patio next to Castrillo's.  I am excited to try their pizza.  I've only heard good things.
Rewrite this for me: I was truly amazed by the wide range of options available at this pizza establishment. Deciding to grab a quick bite, I opted for their mouthwatering roast beef sandwich, which turned out to be absolutely delicious. However, I must admit that it took approximately 15 to 20 minutes before the sandwich was ready to be served. Unfortunately, the restaurant lacks seating options, but fortunately, there is a community patio adjacent to Castrillo's where guests can sit and enjoy their meals. The anticipation for trying their renowned pizza is truly exhilarating, as I have only heard positive reviews about it.

input: We came here on the holiday, July 4.  This place was great.  All the staff were so friendly and helpful.  My daughter had ear pain and the nurse we saw was very compassionate and patient with my daughter.  He tried to do his best to get the wax loose and out of her ear, but was unsuccessful after multiple attempts.  The doctor then came in to assist and immediately was able to remove a huge chunk of wax.  We were given prescriptions for antibiotics and went over to Target (in same shopping center) to get those filled.  The medication was cheaper at Target than what Med Express quoted us.   It was a great place for going to get immediate care while on vacation at the beach!  Thanks so much!
Rewrite this for me: We arrived here on July 4th for our holiday and found this place to be fantastic. The entire staff was extremely friendly and helpful. When my daughter experienced ear pain, the nurse we consulted showed great compassion and patience towards her. Despite making several attempts, he was unable to remove the wax buildup in her ear. However, the doctor promptly stepped in and successfully extracted a large chunk of wax. Afterward, we received prescriptions for antibiotics and opted to have them filled at the nearby Target, located in the same shopping center. To our pleasant surprise, the medication was less expensive there compared to what Med Express had quoted us. This immediate care facility proved to be an excellent choice for our beach vacation. We are immensely grateful for the exceptional service. Thank you!

input: Hands down the best veggie wings I've had anywhere. Seriously. I can never stop thinking about them. Their fried pickles are also great, though I've found their drinks to be a bit weak. I'll stick to a Mexican coke whenever I'm here.
Rewrite this for me: Without a doubt, these veggie wings are the absolute best I've ever had, no matter where I go. Honestly, they never fail to leave a lasting impression on me. Additionally, their fried pickles are fantastic, although I must admit their drinks could use a bit more kick. Whenever I visit, I'll opt for a Mexican coke instead.

input: Neat diner, unlike other diners as it's quaint and has a good feel to it. I had the Yankee pot roast....which was ok....mashed potatoes were just ok and the meat was kind of bland. The veggies were excellent, fresh, not out of a can.  My wife had an omelette which she said was good. Service was excellent.
Rewrite this for me: This diner is quite tidy and distinctive compared to others, creating a pleasant ambiance. I ordered the Yankee pot roast, which was decent, although the mashed potatoes and meat lacked flavor. On the other hand, the vegetables were outstanding, being fresh and not canned. My wife enjoyed her omelette, describing it as good. The service provided was excellent.

input:
Zero stars for the Chicken Teriyaki Lunch Bento Box.  I have literally never seen a bento box come without rice before.  

Disappoint.

input: Brooke's music needs to go. No more pop edm.

input: Good price, great location and good accommodations with decently sized rooms. The bed is pretty firm though and the sheets are super rough but overall, I would stay here again!
Rewrite this for me: The hotel offers a favorable price, excellent location, and satisfactory accommodations with adequately sized rooms. However, the bed is quite firm and the sheets are noticeably rough. Nevertheless, considering everything, I would definitely choose to stay here again.

input: The pasta was cooked perfectly, chicken parm was delicious and pizza was good. What amazes me most is in a packed place this one cashier/waitress was able to do it all seamless and well. Impressed
Rewrite this for me: I was thoroughly impressed with the meal - the pasta was cooked to perfection, the chicken parm was absolutely delicious, and the pizza was quite good. input: First time eating here today, was fantastic! The food was great but the REAL REASON to go is view and ambience. Sitting outside right on the beach, enjoying your meal while listening to the soothing sound of waves crashing is simply sublime. Another plus, they sell beer! Lol. A must if you're in the area, even if you're not it's worth the drive. I'll definitely be back!
Rewrite this for me: Today was my first experience dining at this establishment, and I must say, it was absolutely fantastic! The food surpassed my expectations, but the true selling point lies in the breathtaking view and delightful atmosphere. Imagine sitting outside, directly on the beach, savoring a meal while the rhythmic crashing of waves serenades you. It truly is an extraordinary experience. On top of that, they even offer a selection of beers for sale! Haha. If you happen to be in the area, I strongly recommend paying them a visit. However, even if you're not nearby, the drive is absolutely worth it. I'm already looking forward to my next visit!

input: Attended a party there. They now have a private room with your own bar and bathroom. I really enjoyed it. The buffet was good, didn't have to wait for a drink and you were able to hear each other talk. I would have a party there!
Rewrite this for me: I went to a party at that place, and I must say, they recently added a private room complete with its own bar and bathroom. I had a great time! The buffet served delicious food, and one of the best parts was that you didn't have to wait long for a drink. Additionally, the atmosphere was perfect for conversations since you could hear each other talk. I would definitely consider hosting a party there!

input: I was a little nervous since this is my first time with LF and I didn't know what to expect. Tori was such a sweetheart. I showed her picture of the hairstyle I wanted, and she turned it into reality! At the end of my visit, she wrote down the products that she used. She also gave me some great suggestions about treating my hair type (fine & thin). The place was clean and modern. Parking was not an issue and I came on Saturday. It was a great experience!
Rewrite this for me: I was feeling a bit anxious as it was my first time visiting LF and I wasn't sure what to anticipate. However, Tori was extremely kind and understanding. I presented her with a photo of the hairstyle I desired, and she skillfully brought it to life! Towards the end of my appointment, she kindly jotted down the products she had utilized. Finding parking was hassle-free, even on a Saturday. All in all, it was a fantastic experience!

input:
WOW!! What A burger, terrific flavor. Well cooked very well seasoned and a healthy portion of sides with it as well. We had homemade potato chips and waffle fries sweet potatoes.  
The outside patio was great, just wish there was a law against smoking ANYWHERE people could eat! 
Out waiter Jesse was jam up and took good care of us! 
This place came on a recommendation from a friend and is off the beaten path just a bit but worth every single moment and delicious place and will return
Rewrite this for me: I am extremely impressed by this burger! The flavor is terrific and it was cooked perfectly, with just the right amount of seasoning. The sides that came with it, homemade potato chips and sweet potato waffle fries, were also delicious and a healthy portion. The outside patio was fantastic, although I do wish there was a smoking ban in place for any areas where people are dining. Our waiter, Jesse, was excellent and took great care of us. This restaurant was recommended by a friend and although it's slightly hidden, it is absolutely worth every moment and the food is incredibly tasty. I will definitely be returning.

input: I've been going to Mark for at least 2 years now. I've gone to salons like Dominic Michael etc and am used to paying $35 plus tip for a cut. I learned about Blades and since I knew the owner had salon experience felt comfortable trying him. Mark is a great guy and I always love my cut.
Rewrite this for me: For the past two years, I have been a loyal client of Mark. Prior to discovering him, I frequented salons such as Dominic Michael, where I typically spent $35 plus tip for a haircut. However, upon learning about Blades and considering the owner's background in salon work, I felt at ease giving Mark a try. I must say, Mark is not only a great guy but also consistently impresses me with his exceptional haircut skills.

input: The decor of this restaurant is pretty modern.  It seems great for people in their 20s.  I had the mahi mahi with pita chips and hummus.  It was really good.  The fish was tender and flavorful.  The service was good, too.
Rewrite this for me: The restaurant has a sleek and contemporary decor that appeals particularly to individuals in their twenties. I was pleased with the attentive service provided as well.

input:
I wish they served a bigger menu of dim sum because it's amazing here! In my opinion, this is the best place for dim sum in reno (CaiE's oriental cafe seems like they serve pre-frozen dim sum). We order in advance and dine in. Whenever I'm craving chicken feet and siu mai, this is the go to. Unless we can go over the hill to Sac. 

They have a good combo meal. I enjoy their sesame chicken with fried rice. Hubby gets beef and broccoli or shrimp and vegetables. Comes with a nice combo appetizer and/or hot cup of soup.
Rewrite this for me:
I really wish the restaurant had a larger variety of dim sum options because the quality here is incredible! In my opinion, this is by far the best place in Reno for dim sum (unlike CaiE's Oriental Cafe, which seems to serve pre-frozen dim sum). We usually make advanced orders and dine in. Whenever I have a craving for chicken feet and siu mai, this is my go-to spot, unless we can make the trip over to Sacramento.

Additionally, they offer a great combo meal. I personally love their sesame chicken with fried rice, while my husband enjoys either the beef and broccoli or the shrimp and vegetables. The combo also includes a delightful appetizer and/or a comforting cup of soup.

input:
I came in for lunch, my group totaled eight hungry people.  There was no wait and after reading other reviews about the crowds, the stars must have aligned for us.  The parking lot was also relatively empty although I did happen to walk by the one car whose door opened just as I happened by, ouch my pancreas!
     The server was excellent although I cannot remember her name, which is a shame 'cause she definitively deserves the cudos for dealing with my rowdy group.
     Yes, I went and ordered the cheeseburger and fries (my kryptonite) and I must say it was perfectly cooked, the fries at the peak of crispiness and my glass never went empty.  Eight people, no complaints, all in all a great time was had by all!
Rewrite this for me:
For lunch, I entered the restaurant with a group of eight individuals who were all eager to eat. Surprisingly, there was no wait, and considering the previous reviews mentioning crowdedness, it seemed like a stroke of luck. The parking lot was considerably empty, although I did happen to pass by the only car whose door unexpectedly opened and accidentally hit me, causing a momentary pain in my pancreas.

The server provided an excellent service, although regrettably, I cannot recall her name. It's a shame because she truly deserves recognition for managing my boisterous group.

As for my order, I couldn't resist indulging in my weakness, a cheeseburger accompanied by fries. It was prepared flawlessly, with the fries reaching the optimum level of crispiness. Additionally, my glass was never left empty. With eight people present, there were no complaints, making it an enjoyable experience for everyone involved.

input: The bayou burger is literally the best burger I've ever had. Great staff also -definitely a big thumbs up.
Rewrite this for me: I have to say, the bayou burger is undeniably the greatest burger I have ever had. Moreover, the staff is fantastic, earning a resounding thumbs up from me.

input:
This review is for a corporate event in a private dining room with a limited food menu & bar. 

I was blown away! One of the best meals I've ever had and service was flawless, expert, courteous, and never intrusive. Passed hors d'ouevres were creative and tasty. Lobster consommé was delicious and filet was PERFECTLY cooked & seasoned, melted in my mouth, and a generous portion. And that view is just stunning! Actually a better view from our private room than the main dining room, where I've been for a happy hour event (which was less perfect since the space was very overbooked resulting in slow service). Highly recommend for an event and may be back here for a special occasion dinner.
Rewrite this for me: This review is for a corporate event held in a private dining room with a limited food menu and bar. Wow, I was incredibly impressed! The meal I had was truly one of the best I've ever experienced, and the service was absolutely flawless. The staff were experts, polite, and always attentive without being intrusive. The hors d'oeuvres that were passed around were both creative and delicious. The lobster consommé was simply divine, and the filet was cooked and seasoned to absolute perfection. It practically melted in my mouth, and the portion size was very generous. On top of that, the view from our private room was absolutely breathtaking! In fact, I felt that it offered an even better view than the main dining room, where I had previously attended a happy hour event that wasn't as lovely due to overcrowding and slow service. I highly recommend this venue for hosting an event, and I may even consider returning for a special occasion dinner.

input: The pizza was the best we've had in the Fairmount/Art Museum/Brewerytown area and we've probably tried 5 or so.  The pepperoni was a little crispy (good thing) and the wings were, too.  That last one is really surprising since there are so many soggy wings out there.  Lazos does it right.  They gave me Sprite instead of Coke but otherwise this was a very good pizza+wing combo.  Will order again!
Rewrite this for me: We had probably tried about 5 pizzas in the Fairmount/Art Museum/Brewerytown area, but the one from Lazos stood out as the best. The pepperoni had a crispy texture, which was a positive thing, and surprisingly, the wings were crispy as well. It's uncommon to find crispy wings, as most tend to be soggy. Lazos definitely knows how to do it right. The only minor issue was that they gave us Sprite instead of Coke, but overall, the pizza+wing combo was very satisfying. We will definitely be ordering from them again!

input: Old school decor - dark woods and copper tile ceiling (real?)  I was there for the express lunch, a good deal.  You get a choice of soup with the entree of the day.  The gumbo and crab bisque were spot on. Gumbo - rich with the andouille sausage adding just a bit of heat. Crab bisque - flavored with old bay style seasoning but not overly salty and just a bit of shredded crab. The entree was a garganelli with roast pork ragu, mushrooms and creole tomatoes.  The sauce was light and blended the flavors well.  The roast pork highlighted the dish - fork tender, caramelized and left me wanting more.
Rewrite this for me:
The restaurant had an old-school ambiance with its dark wooden furniture and a ceiling adorned with copper tiles (are they real?). I decided to visit for their express lunch, which was a great deal. With the lunch special, you could choose a soup to accompany the daily entree. Both the gumbo and crab bisque were exceptional. The gumbo had a rich flavor, enhanced by the addition of andouille sausage, which provided a slight hint of spiciness. The crab bisque was seasoned with an Old Bay-style seasoning that was well-balanced, not overly salty, and had just the right amount of shredded crab. 

For the main course, I opted for the garganelli with roast pork ragu, mushrooms, and creole tomatoes. The sauce was light yet managed to blend all the flavors harmoniously. The roast pork was the star of the dish, as it was incredibly tender, caramelized, and left me yearning for more.

input: great hotel in a very good location. The staff was really friendly, and helped us out a lot. it's a 1-2 minute walk to the bars on Bourbon, 7-8 min walk to Harra's, 10 min walk to Jackson Square. The only downside is parking is $38 a night.
Rewrite this for me: This hotel is fantastic and situated in an excellent location. The staff were extremely friendly and provided us with great assistance. It is conveniently located just a short 1-2 minute walk to the lively bars on Bourbon Street, a 7-8 minute walk to Harra's, and a 10 minute walk to the beautiful Jackson Square. The only drawback is that parking is priced at $38 per night.

input:
Really liked this store yesterday. Great selection, I was impressed by Chloe and Marc Jacobs items and Chanel pumps for $87 (too small for me=(
I found their price range great (now they have summer sales on) but in general you get great value for money. I am not looking for $20-30 T Shirts, I am ready to pay $100 for a silky blouse (which can retail for $300+) so I guess this will be my go-to store. 
And! the lady at the store was super friendly and nice.
Rewrite this for me: I absolutely loved this store yesterday. The selection was fantastic, and I was particularly impressed by the Chloe and Marc Jacobs items, as well as the Chanel pumps priced at an amazing $87 (unfortunately, they were too small for me). The store's price range is excellent, especially with their current summer sales. Overall, you truly get great value for your money. Personally, I'm not interested in cheap $20-30 T-shirts; I'm willing to spend $100 for a luxurious silky blouse that usually retails for $300 or more. Hence, this store will definitely become my new favorite go-to place. Additionally, the lady working there was incredibly friendly and nice.

input:
I was here a few times because my friends won free happy hours. When I won one, I sent in my guest list and tried to call them a few times to confirm. Neither of the people who answered the phone were friendly or helpful, and I never did get in touch with the woman in charge of happy hours. She never returned my emails or phone calls. When I showed up with my friends, they didn't have my name on the list and forgot that they even offered me a happy hour. It was irritating, and after some fighting, they eventually let me through.

There is a dress code (no sneakers, flip flops, hats, etc.), but I don't really mind. The bouncers and bartenders aren't very friendly and can be slow, and I never tried the food. The crowd isn't great either - attractive and douchey (maybe because, like us, they're just trying to get drunk and go somewhere else). 

Free booze is always good, but I wouldn't come here for any other reason.
Rewrite this for me:
I visited this place multiple times as my friends had won free happy hour passes. On the occasion when I won one, I submitted my guest list and made several attempts to reach out for confirmation. Unfortunately, the individuals who answered the phone were neither friendly nor helpful, and my attempts to contact the person in charge of happy hours went unanswered. To my disappointment, upon arriving with my friends, my name was not on the list and they seemed to have forgotten about offering me a happy hour. After some argument, they eventually allowed us in.

While there is a dress code which I don't particularly mind, the bouncers and bartenders lack friendliness and can be quite slow. I cannot provide an opinion on the food as I never had the chance to try it. The crowd also leaves something to be desired - they appear attractive but somewhat pretentious (perhaps because, like us, they are solely interested in getting drunk and moving on).

Free drinks are always a welcome perk, but I wouldn't choose to come here for any other reason.

input:
I don't know this for sure, but my first impression of this place is that it is run by unscrupulous people. Come along with me, as I journey back in time -- all the way back to Wednesday...

I step foot in this 7 Eleven, and the first thing I think is: this is one of the nicest looking 7 Elevens I've ever seen. It is very clean, bright, and spacious. Very nice looking selection of prepared meals. There were many that actually looked like they'd be quite good. But I wasn't hungry this day. No. All I needed were a few items. 

First, some good old TP. And let me be perfectly clear (as clear as Barack Obama): I DON'T buy the cheapest toilet paper because I'm cheap. I buy it because I like the way the cheap stuff feels. The more like sandpaper, the better. I like to feel like its working. I don't need to or even want to feel like an angel is up there. Or some perverted freak named Scott. 

In any case, I got myself 4 rolls. And then I just needed one more thing - some plastic cups for a little party I'm having this weekend. 

I go ahead and drop my stash on the counter, begin to extract several singles from my wallet, when the cashier looks at me and says, "24.99."

I respond, "That's not right."

He points at a price tag on the plastic cups which reads 19.99. I begin laughing. I tell him the price is clearly wrong. He tells me he's got to talk to his manager. Meanwhile, I tell the folks behind me waiting in line that I'm just going to go run and get different plastic cups to hurry the process along. Before he got back from doing his price check, I already had another cashier ringing up my two sleeves of cups for 1.99 each. That's more like it.

At around that same moment, the first cashier comes back from his consultation with his manager. He tells me that the price was, in fact, incorrect. And that the price is actually 14.99.

THAT'S the unscrupulous part.

CLEARLY, THAT price is also far too high. His manager did no actual price check at all. He simply told the cashier to pretend that the real price was actually 5 dollars less, thinking that I'd be stupid enough to accept this. Why, because I'm white, and you're a racially superior Indian? You think white people are stupid don't you? We'll just believe what you tell us, and fork over our money.

Although I can't be certain, my initial impression of this establishment is that it is managed by unethical individuals. Join me as I journey back in time, all the way to Wednesday.

The rougher it feels, the better; it gives me the satisfaction of knowing it's getting the job done. I have no desire to feel as though an angel or someone named Scott is involved in the process.

I grabbed four rolls of TP and proceeded to the counter, where I pulled out some cash from my wallet. At that moment, the cashier informed me that the total amount due was $24.99.

Surprised by the amount, I laughed and explained that it couldn't be right. The cashier pointed to the price tag on the plastic cups, which read $19.99. He mentioned needing to consult his manager, so I informed the people in line behind me that I would quickly grab different plastic cups to expedite the process. Before the cashier returned from his price check, I had already found another cashier who charged me $1.99 each for two packs of cups. Much more reasonable.

Around the same time, the original cashier returned from speaking with his manager. He admitted that the initial price was indeed incorrect and that the actual price was $14.99. This behavior struck me as unscrupulous.

It was evident that no real price check had taken place. Instead, the manager simply instructed the cashier to pretend that the correct price was $5 less, likely expecting me to accept it unquestioningly. Was this assumption based on my being white while considering themselves racially superior due to their Indian heritage? Did they believe that white people are gullible and would readily believe whatever they were told, willingly handing over their money?

input:
For a long, long time, Dallesandro's was my philly cheesesteak haven.  However, since their change in ownership, they've gone steadily downhill.  Chubby's and Mama's tided me over until I could find suitable replacement.  Thanks to Larry's Steaks, I've rekindled my passion for cheesesteaks.

Larry's Steaks, situated by St. Joe's University, offers the closest thing to the original Dallesandro's cheesesteak I've found.  The meat is sliced and minced into tiny little pieces, maximizing surface area.  Then the cheese is melted throughout so it covers most of the steak and ensures a heavenly consistency and flavor.  The onions and mushrooms are up to snuff as well.  It's greasy enough to slide down your throat but not so much that it's a mess to eat.  I can't attest to the other menu items, but that hardly matters.  If you are up for a real philly cheesesteak, skip pat's and geno's (and the whiz, i can't believe people actually eat that stuff) and pick up a Larry's steak.

The cheese is melted throughout, ensuring each bite is filled with heavenly consistency and taste. The onions and mushrooms are also top-notch. It strikes the perfect balance of being greasy enough to slide down your throat with ease, yet not a complete mess to eat. While I can't vouch for their other menu items, that hardly matters. If you're craving an authentic philly cheesesteak experience, forget about Pat's and Geno's (and their questionable whiz cheese), and head straight to Larry's for an unforgettable steak.

input:
I've often passed this swanky little place in Downtown filled with good-looking professionals laughing over drinks, appetizers and spilling over the sidewalk

NOM NOMS
Although you probably won't get full on the sizes, the food is like little art works of flavor. My bowl of mussels and clams was HUGE and I sopped up the buttery, faintly spiced broth with the accompanying breadstick. Well done. The other appetizers like Tuna Tartare and Coconut Shrimp each had awesome flavor surprises - fresh, melty tuna and a wasabi and jam sauce respectively - both excellent and plated beautifully.

My cocktail "The Tryst" didn't impress. Watery and a strange alcohol after taste. I'll forget it tomorrow. 

SERVICE
Thanks Yelp for introducing me here. It's easy to get overlooked at the bar, but once seated, our server was quick and helpful and was great at lowering my inhibitions by telling me what to expect in a "vegetable" beer they offered--spot on. 

SUMMARY
I'll probably stick to the drinks only here because the food prices are above my range... or go during happy hours. Cool, hip place to bring the girlfriends or if you're looking for impressive, gutsy art dishes with good taste.... and if you have cash to blow (but I won't let that subtract a review star)

NOM NOMS
While the portion sizes may not be filling, the food itself is like a masterpiece of flavors. My bowl of mussels and clams was enormous, and I relished every last drop of the buttery, subtly spiced broth with the accompanying breadstick. It was expertly executed. The other appetizers, such as the Tuna Tartare and Coconut Shrimp, pleasantly surprised me with their amazing flavors - the fresh, velvety tuna and the tangy wasabi and jam sauce were both outstanding and presented beautifully.

However, my cocktail "The Tryst" was a letdown. It was weak in taste and left a strange alcoholic aftertaste. I won't remember it tomorrow.

SERVICE
Thank you, Yelp, for introducing me to this place. At the busy bar, it's easy to feel overlooked, but once we were seated, our server was prompt, attentive, and provided excellent guidance, especially when explaining their "vegetable" beer - spot on.

SUMMARY
I'll most likely stick to just drinks when I visit this place, as the prices for food exceed my budget... unless it's during happy hour. It's a cool and trendy spot to go with girlfriends or when you're in the mood for impressive, daring culinary creations with great flavor.... as long as you're willing to spend some cash (though that won't affect my rating).

But I'd gladly go again and would tell friends to try it.

I ordered the beef and lobster, both of which were cooked perfectly and left me satisfied. The mashed potatoes and asparagus that accompanied the dish were also delicious.

However, I wasn't particularly impressed with the appetizer we had, which was the crab and cheese balls. They lacked flavor, had minimal crab taste, and seemed to lack seasoning. Maybe it just wasn't to my taste, but I wouldn't recommend them.

On the other hand, the Creme Brule was solid and definitely something I would order again without hesitation.

Overall, I'd rate my experience a four out of five, mainly because of the disappointing appetizer and the unstable table. It's pretty ridiculous to have such an issue in a nice place like this.

Despite that, I would gladly return and recommend it to my friends.

input: We visited this place because of its location on the wharf, and because my husband loves seafood. It's tiny, but we were there on a Tuesday evening, and only had to wait a few minutes. I had the fried shrimp, and enjoyed it very much; it was not greasy or heavy, and the shrimp was moist and tasty. There is literally nothing but shellfish on the menu. So, the non-seafood enthusiast (me) was happily surprised to enjoy the shrimp so much (plus good onion rings), but the seafood enthusiast (my husband) didn't love the crab sandwich. If we tried this place again, he would order something else. The location is awesome, so if you like shellfish, definitely give this place a try.

On the other hand, I thoroughly enjoyed my order of fried shrimp, which was impressively light, non-greasy, and boasted moist and flavorful shrimp. It's worth noting that their menu is exclusively focused on shellfish, which pleasantly surprised me as someone who isn't a big fan of seafood. I particularly appreciated the delicious onion rings as well. Despite my positive experience with the shrimp, my husband, being a true seafood enthusiast, wasn't captivated by the crab sandwich. If we were to revisit, he would likely opt for a different dish. Nevertheless, given the fantastic location and if you're a fan of shellfish, this place is definitely worth a try.

The waitress proceeded to run outside and tell the rest of the group that we were moving at which point they decided to stay outside, which was fine by my friend and I, but that meant having to be separated from our friends. This, to me, is deplorable behavior on the side of the the waitress and management. The waitress who was supposed to be our waitress inside as well, never arrived to the table and never checked up on us. Needless to say, I had to get another waiter and he was so appalled with the way that everything was handled he told my friend to not give him a tip. I was so appalled myself, that I did not eat because I just did not want to spend my hard earn money at this establishment any longer. I would never recommend this place to anyone even if they were starving!

input:
I really wanted to like this place and heard about it during lent when I had given up meat. I found myself in the area again and decided to give it a try. I usually don't write reviews until I've been to a place a few times but I think my experience was a complete one. I ordered the special and sampled each type of chicken, the modern BBQ sauce, mac&cheese (which the woman behind the counter was very proud of), 
a bananas foster pie, and the new hope birch beer. After finishing everything, I just wanted my $16.20 back. Individual reviews: 

The chicken: It was very average and that is being generous. It wasn't incredibly flavorful but it wasn't dry so it could have been worse. 

The sauce: It had the tang of a traditional North Carolina BBQ sauce, mustard and vinegar based. I can't eat mayo so I was limited with sauce choices but the mayo sauces were recommended. 

The mac&cheese: Salty and mediocre. It combines all of the things I like but makes a mess doing it. The pasta was well cooked but the cheese and bacon combo made it taste like I just licked salt off of my hand without the nice shot of tequila after. 

The bananas foster pie: The crust of the pie needs no improvement but the filling could use an overhaul. I use the term filling loosely because after biting into the flakey crust, I struggled to find the bananas. There was a thin layer of smashed bananas and cinnamon sugar at the bottom and 75% of the interior was empty space. 

The new hope soda: The birch beer (the actual name of the soda escapes me at the moment but it is birch beer) was the highlight of my meal. Everything you would expect from a Pennsylvania birch beer and very refreshing, which surprised me because I normally don't like fountain sodas and prefer root beer.

I gave this place 2 stars instead of 1 because nothing was horrible.  I think the concept works, the decor is nice, and the menu is good but they need to work on the quality of their food because it currently doesn't match the cost.
Rewrite this for me:
I had high hopes for this place, especially after hearing about it during lent when I was abstaining from meat. Visiting the area again, I decided to give it a try, although typically I only write reviews after multiple visits. However, I believe that my first experience was enough to form a complete opinion.

I opted for the special, which included various types of chicken, the highly esteemed modern BBQ sauce, mac&cheese, a bananas foster pie, and a new hope birch beer. Yet, after trying everything, I felt a strong desire to get my $16.20 back. Here are my individual reviews:

The chicken: Frankly, it was nothing special, even being generous. It lacked a vibrant flavor, but at least it wasn't dry.

The sauce: Reminiscent of traditional North Carolina BBQ sauce with its tangy mustard and vinegar base. Unfortunately, my mayo restriction limited my choices, and the mayo-based options were recommended.

The mac&cheese: Salty and mediocre. It attempted to combine all my favorite elements, but the execution was messy. The pasta was well-cooked, yet the cheese and bacon combo left a taste akin to licking salt off my hand without the satisfying tequila shot.

The bananas foster pie: The crust was impeccable; no room for improvement there. However, the filling could use a revamp. Calling it a "filling" is generous since I struggled to find the bananas after biting into the flaky crust. A thin layer of smashed bananas and cinnamon sugar coat the bottom, while 75% of the interior is empty space.

The new hope soda: The highlight of my meal was the birch beer, although I regrettably can't recall its exact name at the moment. It perfectly embodied the essence of Pennsylvania birch beer, providing a surprising burst of refreshment. This surprised me, as I typically dislike fountain sodas and prefer root beer.

I awarded this place 2 stars instead of 1 because nothing was outright terrible. The concept is promising, the decor is pleasant, and the menu is enticing. However, they need to focus on improving the quality of their food, as it currently falls short of its price point.

input:
Spot on!

I got "the veg" and the spicy fries.  "The veg" is a portabella burger, with grilled mozzarella, picked veg, arugula, and gauc.  Wholly non-cow is this thing spectacular for a bella burger!  The bella is on bottom, then the mozzarella is directly fused on top of that.  I actually thought the cheese was halloumi at first because it wasn't super melted (a good thing). The gauc and pickled veg are slightly citrusy and vinegary, but are contrasted by the bitterness of the arugula.  There's a nice bun to contents ratio, and for bonus points it's a potato bun.

Wasn't sure what to expect with the spicy fries going in - are they hot sauce fries, etc?  Turns out they are of the crab-fries variety with some subtle other spices added in.  Nice portion - not too big.

The atmosphere kind of reminds me of a dive bar - I think that's the best way to describe it.  It's pretty small, so I wouldn't choose to ever eat in most likely.
Rewrite this for me:
Absolutely spot on!

I ordered "the veg," which is a delightful portabella burger topped with grilled mozzarella, pickled vegetables, arugula, and guacamole. This burger is a true masterpiece and a fantastic alternative to a traditional beef burger! The portabella sits at the base, followed by a perfectly melted mozzarella. Initially, I mistook the cheese for halloumi because it wasn't overly gooey (which turned out to be a pleasant surprise). The guacamole and pickled vegetables add a slightly citrusy and vinegary kick, beautifully balanced by the bitterness of the arugula. The bun-to-filling ratio is just right, and the fact that it's served on a potato bun is an added bonus.

As for the spicy fries, I wasn't quite sure what to expect. Would they be doused in hot sauce or have other fiery flavors? It turns out they are more like crab fries, with subtle additional spices. The portion size was just perfect, not overwhelming.

When it comes to the ambiance, it has a dive bar feel to it, which I find quite charming. However, the small size of the place would make me more inclined to take my food to-go rather than eating in.

input:
Being a vegetarian while visiting New Orleans is no easy feat.  However, when I have found eats, they are usually very good.  Tomasito's was below the standard I have gotten used to.  Not to say it was bad, not at all.  I had the chips and a bean and cheese burrito. I would have gotten rice in my burrito but it was not vegetarian (really?).  Service was ok, and the flan was excellent (although "with berries" seems to mean one raspberry).
That being said, at least there was food to eat on the menu, and that is not assumes in New Orleans.
Rewrite this for me:
It's quite challenging to be a vegetarian while visiting New Orleans. However, the few times I have found vegetarian options, they have been quite enjoyable. Unfortunately, Tomasito's did not meet the high standard that I have become accustomed to. That's not to say it was terrible, but it fell short. I opted for the chips and a bean and cheese burrito, as I would have liked rice in it but it wasn't vegetarian-friendly (surprising, right?). The service was average, but the highlight was the excellent flan, although the description of "with berries" was misleading as it only included one raspberry.
With that being said, it was still a relief to find vegetarian options on the menu, as it's not always assumed in New Orleans.

input:
All I needed was a written estimate.  A rather simple task one would think.  I needed my factory navigation unit in my Denali replaced, and needed to know costs and in writing.  Now this is a normal standard procedure for an auto repair shop.  Let's just assume its bad (it is), so tell me how much it is to remove bad part, and put the new one in.

Jay Fatimo or something like that, said he was very busy, as were the other service writers, so he handed me his card, and said to just email him with what I needed.  Sounded like a good plan, I wasn't in a big rush.  So I did just that, sent a picture of my vin, and the appropriate RPO codes to know what part I needed, and emailed it all to him.  I never got a response.  I tried again about a week or so later, still nothing.  Made sure it is his email at the dealership, etc.  

I guess I have a hard time with taking my car in or trusting a place to do such repairs (3000 dollar job according to Winkel GMC) if they can't even respond to an email.  He knew I would email that day, and I did.  

I guess the GMC dealer right next door gets my money instead.
Rewrite this for me:

This is a standard procedure for any auto repair shop. Given the situation, I asked Jay Fatimo (or something similar) for assistance. He mentioned that he and the other service writers were extremely busy, so he gave me his card and advised me to email him with my requirements. I thought it was a good plan and wasn't in a hurry, so I followed his suggestion. I sent him a picture of my VIN and the relevant RPO codes to identify the required part. However, I never received a response from him. I tried again after about a week, but still no reply. I made sure I was using the correct email address for him at the dealership. 

It's disheartening that a car repair shop that can't even respond to an email would expect me to trust them with an expensive repair job ($3000 according to Winkel GMC). Jay knew I would email him that day, yet there was no acknowledgment or response from him. In the end, I've decided to take my business to the GMC dealer located right next door.

input:
This tour is one to take when you want to have a lazy day, but you want to do a passive activity.  Me & my friends didn't wan the lunch, we just wanted to take a tour of the Mississippi.  The cost was average - around $28.00.  Con:  Remember it is a tour, so they have the typical tourist traps - photographer - me and friends declined that option.  

I would suggest if you aren't going to eat - to pull out your smartphone and research the Natchez Native American Tribe who inhibited the area prior to the colonization of the New Orleans area - interesting "tid bits of rituals", so that made the boat ride more fun because I became the secondary tour leader to my group.  If you are in the mood-go get a drink and this will comfort you as you learn more about the area on a steamboat.  Not a bad way to spend a few hours.

If you're looking for a relaxing day filled with passive activities, I highly recommend taking this tour. My friends and I decided to skip lunch and instead take a tour around the beautiful Mississippi. The cost was fairly average, coming in at around $28. Unfortunately, there were some typical tourist traps on the tour, like the photographers, but we declined that option.

I would suggest using your smartphone to look up information about the Natchez Native American Tribe, who used to inhabit the area before the colonization of New Orleans. We discovered some interesting "tidbits of rituals," which made the boat ride even more enjoyable as I became the secondary tour guide for my group. If you're in the mood, grab a drink and let it enhance your knowledge about the area while cruising on a steamboat. Overall, spending a few hours on this tour is definitely not a bad way to go.

input: Just visited The Fat Ham with my girlfriend about an hour ago. The place is small, but the vibe is nice. Music isn't too loud, the staff welcomed us and the whiskey display is impressive. We couldn't get a table, so we took the two empty seats at the bar. The bartender, Dan, greeted us immediately. Dan was effecient, quick and friendly. Great service. My girlfriend ordered a margarita, which was reasonably priced and tasty. To eat, we ordered the pimento cheese, skillet cornbread, shrimp & grits and the hot chicken. Everything was delicious. The pimento cheese had some heat, and the country bread it is served with gives it a nice touch of salt. The mollases butter on the cornbread was "to die for". The shrimp & grits was my favorite dish. Creamy grits, perfectly cooked and seasoned shrimp. As for the chicken, they do not lie to you. It is hot. The brioche and ranch dressing compliment it well. For desert, we ordered the raspberry cobbler and a coffee. The cobbler was underwhelming. It wasn't bad - just not as great as the previous plates. Elixr coffee was spot on. Overall, I'll be back. Decent price point, high end comfort food and great service.
Rewrite this for me:
I recently visited The Fat Ham with my girlfriend, and it was about an hour ago. The restaurant is small, but it has a pleasant atmosphere. The music wasn't too loud, and the staff greeted us warmly. The whiskey display was quite impressive. Unfortunately, we couldn't get a table, so we opted for the two available seats at the bar. The bartender, Dan, immediately welcomed us with efficiency, speed, and friendliness. The service was excellent. 

My girlfriend ordered a reasonably priced and delicious margarita. As for the food, we decided on the pimento cheese, skillet cornbread, shrimp & grits, and the hot chicken. Everything was incredibly tasty. The pimento cheese had a nice spicy kick, and the country bread it was served with added a delightful touch of saltiness. The molasses butter on the cornbread was absolutely divine. The shrimp & grits dish was my personal favorite - the grits were creamy and the shrimp perfectly cooked and seasoned. As for the hot chicken, it truly lived up to its name. The brioche bun and ranch dressing served as fantastic accompaniments.

For dessert, we ordered the raspberry cobbler and had a coffee. Sadly, the cobbler was underwhelming. It wasn't terrible, but it didn't match up to the excellence of the previous dishes. On the bright side, the Elixr coffee was spot on. 

Overall, I will definitely be returning to The Fat Ham. The prices were reasonable, the comfort food was of high quality, and the service was excellent.

input: When this place first opened we went. We loved the Greek salad and gyros. It was very fresh tasting and the place was cute. We went back last night- the tables were all dirty, lamps full of dirt and dead bugs- so that was a turn off. We got our food and the quality has gone way down. My salad had one bite of potato salad and two items in the salad - tomato and pepper tasted off. I had to spit them out. My daughter got a fajita bowl with chicken. Her tomato was also gross and the chicken was cooked into charred rubber. We ordered baklava and it was stale. I hope they clean and go back to the quality it was when they first opened. The tables were all dirty, and the lamps were disturbingly filled with dirt and dead bugs, which immediately put us off. To add to the disappointment, the quality of the food has significantly declined. In my salad, I only found a single bite of potato salad along with two questionable ingredients - the tomato and pepper tasted peculiar and unpleasant. I had to spit them out to avoid any further distress. As for my daughter, she ordered a fajita bowl with chicken, but to her dismay, the tomato was equally repulsive and the chicken was overcooked to the point of resembling charred rubber. To top it off, our baklava dessert turned out to be stale. We sincerely hope that the establishment takes immediate action to rectify its cleanliness issues and returns to the exceptional quality it once had when it initially opened. The food used to be scrumptious and the hygiene impeccable.

input:
This was our first time here. I had a coupon so I thought I would try it out. Pulling into the parking lot I noticed it was very busy. I was worried that I would have to wait a long time. I pulled up to the attendant and asked how long it would be for a reg wash. She said each wash takes about 15 minutes. I was surprised since they were busy. I left the car there and proceeded inside. 

The building is huge inside. One side is all windows so you can watch your vehicle move through. They even have a "soap gun" the kids can use to shoot their car. That was a huge hit. 

The cashier greeted me as I walked up to the counter. She took my coupon and handed me a receipt. I walked around while I was waiting. They have drinks she snacks for purchase. They sell lots of greeting cards for every occasion. They have gifts and accessories for your car. The building was cool inside which was great because it was hot the day we came in. I waited about 10 minutes and walked outside. They have a large covered area to wait under. It has some seating so you can sit and wait. After just a few minutes they yelled out my car make to say it was done. I handed the attendant my receipt and tip and I was on my way. Total time was 18 minutes which I think is fair considering they were packed when I arrived. 

The car was clean and vacuumed. Overall they did a great job. The only thing they missed was the front window. It had that haze on it that you notice when the sun hits its. I wiped it off myself. I'm sure they would have fixed it if I noticed before I left. Also, they don't offer free air freshener with the wash like most other places. 

This place was fast and they did a great job. The price was fair and the staff was friendly. I will be coming back soon.

Concerns about a lengthy wait quickly crossed my mind. Approaching the attendant, I inquired about the wait time for a regular wash. Surprisingly, she informed me that each wash takes approximately 15 minutes, despite the busy atmosphere. Trusting her words, I left my car in their care and proceeded into the building.

The interior of the building was impressively spacious. One side boasted all-encompassing windows, allowing customers to observe their vehicles being cleaned. They even had a novelty "soap gun" that children could use to spray their car, which proved to be quite popular.

The cashier warmly greeted me upon my approach to the counter. After accepting my coupon, she handed me a receipt. While waiting, I took a stroll around the premises. They offered a selection of beverages and snacks for purchase, along with an extensive assortment of greeting cards for various occasions. Furthermore, they had an array of car-related accessories and gifts. The building maintained a pleasant coolness, which was a reprieve from the scorching weather that day. After waiting for approximately 10 minutes, I ventured outside. They had a sizable covered area with seating where patrons could wait comfortably. To my surprise, just a few minutes later, my car make was announced to inform me that it was ready. Presenting the attendant with my receipt and tip, I swiftly continued on my way. Considering the fact that they were incredibly busy when I arrived, the total time spent was 18 minutes, which I deemed fair.

Upon inspection, my car was both clean and vacuumed. Overall, they performed admirably. The only oversight was a noticeable haze on the front window, which was resolved by my own initiative to wipe it clean. I'm confident they would have rectified the issue had I noticed it prior to departure. Also noteworthy is the fact that they do not provide complimentary air fresheners with their wash, unlike many other establishments.

This establishment displayed efficiency, delivering superb results. Their pricing was reasonable, and the staff exhibited friendly demeanor. I anticipate returning in the near future.
