input:
Trying to find a restaurant in The Big Easy that serves vegetarian is not an "Easy" feat

We've encountered many the restaurant who would tell us time & time again that they did not have or *would* not make something to accommodate veggie needs & it was such a letdown.....to this day I still remember 1 guy saying "Vegetarian?  Aww, you gotta get out earrrrrly for *that*".  We still laugh about it....

Well, over the last few years, we're noticing more & more places recognizing veggies like to eat Southern / Cajun comfort food & they are starting to open up their menus to us! ( YAY)

Seeing that Muriel's Jackson Square had such an offering, we made rezzies to ensure we veggies got fed - you'll want to do this too - veggie or not!  They were packed & quoting 2 hr waits & this was at 9pm!

Started w/ drinkys at the bar - Sazerac for the Mr & I had the uber-delish Honey Child cocktail: honey-infused vodka & muddled blackberries.  The Mr liked mine so well that he ordered 1 too, to go w/ dinner & just to be nice, I had another as well so he wouldn't have to drink alone

Their veggie appie had eggplant, of which I'm not a fan so we asked the waitress if they could make their Goat Cheese Crepe, veggie & she said sure.  Since the description said it was topped w/ crawfish, we thought, this would be easy..... but unfortunately, the roulade sauce was made seafood stock. ACK!  Wished you had told us this!  The Mr however, said the crepe was nice & plump, the goat cheese was creamy & smooth & he liked it, barring the sauce

Mains consisted of their Veggie Soiree - this was a sampling of little dollops of veggie tastes - some you'll find on their side dish offerings & some not

Divine beets & roasted acorn squash

Polenta topped w/ chickpeas & a basil sauce - flavorful though those beans were crunchy & could have used a bit more time in the cooker.... same w/ the crunchy wild rice

Yams were very flavorful & had lots of ginger - the Mr got to indulge in both our dollops of chard - I tried a bite & it triggered my dislike for cooked greens

Too full for dessert, we left w/ happy tummies & thankfulness for a nice veggie night out.  A-OK night!
Rewrite this for me:
Finding a vegetarian restaurant in New Orleans, known as The Big Easy, is not an easy task. We have come across numerous restaurants that either did not have vegetarian options or were unwilling to accommodate our needs. It was always disappointing, and we still remember one guy who sarcastically remarked, "Vegetarian? Aww, you gotta get out early for that." We still joke about it.

However, in recent years, we have noticed more and more places in New Orleans recognizing that vegetarians also enjoy Southern and Cajun comfort food. These restaurants are starting to include vegetarian options on their menus, which is a great improvement.

When we discovered that Muriel's Jackson Square offered such options, we made reservations to ensure that we, as vegetarians, would be able to enjoy a meal there. And let me tell you, even if you're not vegetarian, you should make reservations too. The place was packed, and they were quoting two-hour waits, even at 9 pm!

We started by having drinks at the bar. My husband had a Sazerac, and I tried their delicious Honey Child cocktail, which was made with honey-infused vodka and muddled blackberries. My husband liked it so much that he ordered one for himself to have with dinner. And to keep him company, I had another one as well.

For the appetizer, they had an eggplant dish, but since I'm not a fan of eggplant, we asked our waitress if they could make their Goat Cheese Crepe vegetarian. She was accommodating and said yes. However, we were disappointed to find out that the sauce used on the crepe was made with seafood stock, something they didn't inform us about. Despite this hiccup, my husband enjoyed the crepe, praising the plumpness, creaminess, and smoothness of the goat cheese.

For the main course, we opted for their Veggie Soiree, which was a selection of small portions of various vegetable dishes, some of which are available as side dishes, and some that are not.

We tried the divine beets and roasted acorn squash, as well as polenta topped with chickpeas and a basil sauce. The flavors were delightful, but the beans in the chickpea dish were a bit too crunchy, as were the wild rice. The yams, on the other hand, were full of flavor and had a strong ginger taste. My husband got to enjoy both of our servings of chard, while I tried a bite and realized that I still don't have a taste for cooked greens.

We were too full for dessert, but we left the restaurant with content stomachs and a sense of gratitude for a satisfying vegetarian night out. It was definitely an exceptional evening.

input:
I ate at Puckett's yesterday for lunch, and I have to say it was some mighty tasty food for an old-fashioned meat-and-three.  But I actually had a meat-and-two!  Definitely check out the squash casserole.  it was quite the tasty dish.  I'd also recommend their meatloaf, which is what I had.

My only complaint--and it's a minor one--is that they advertise cornbread.  Yes, it's cornbread, but not a slice of cornbread like you typically think of it.  People in the North would call it a corn fritter.  Being from KY, I'd call it a hoe cake.  It's cornbread but more like a cornbread pancake.
Rewrite this for me:
I dined at Puckett's yesterday during lunchtime, and let me tell you, their old-fashioned meat-and-three had some remarkably delicious food. Although I opted for a meat-and-two instead of the traditional meat-and-three, I highly recommend trying their delectable squash casserole. It truly was a delightful dish. Additionally, I thoroughly enjoyed their meatloaf, which happened to be my choice.

However, if I were to express a tiny complaint, it would be related to their advertised cornbread. While it is indeed cornbread, it differs from what one might envision as a slice of cornbread. Northerners might compare it to a corn fritter, whereas someone from Kentucky, like me, would refer to it as a hoe cake. It shares similarities with cornbread but takes on more of a cornbread pancake form.

Hilton properties are some of the oldest,  most dilapidated properties in the hotel business.  Additionally,  the customer service is the very worst overall with a few exceptions. 
Made a reservation here for 1 bedroom suite.  Suite wasn't ready.  Had a 12:30 lunch mtg  Needed to shower and change but suite booked wasn't ready.  What I thought was a courtesy extend turned out to be bait a D switch.  They gave e me a 'courtesy room' with the understanding that upon my return,  I would get the suite I booked. 
I  returned just to be to told that 'the room I booked had been sold.' Really,???? 
The suite was $250. The downside graded room was $235. I couldn't cancel the room and all of the rooms at a lower rate were 'sold out'  How is that possible so quickly? 
Fake apologies we're given,  but no satisfaction when more could have been done.   Never again.
Rewrite this for me:
The Hilton properties are known for their age and poor maintenance, making them some of the oldest and most run-down in the hotel industry. Furthermore, their customer service is consistently terrible, with only a few exceptions. 

I had made a reservation for a 1-bedroom suite, but upon arrival, the suite was not ready. This put me in a difficult situation as I had a lunch meeting scheduled for 12:30 and needed to shower and change beforehand. Despite their initial promise to extend a courtesy, it turned out to be a deceitful tactic. They offered me a "courtesy room" with the understanding that I would be able to switch to the suite I had originally booked upon returning from my meeting. 

However, when I returned as agreed, I was informed that the room I had booked had been sold. It was truly frustrating and disappointing. The suite I wanted was priced at $250, while the downgraded room they gave me was $235. I was unable to cancel the room, and to make matters worse, all the rooms at a lower rate were mysteriously "sold out" in such a short time. How is that even possible? 

They offered fake apologies, but it was clear that little effort was made to resolve the situation and provide proper satisfaction. I will never choose to stay at a Hilton property again.

input:
I came here because of the higher rating and they accepted my insurance. My initial visit went well, no complaints on the staff or the doctor at that time. 

They switched my brand from Acuvue to Air Optix and about 2 weeks after using the contact I started to experience pain, redness and irritation. I took my contacts out that evening and had red rings around both of my eyes. I tried contacting them via telephone and left a message as well as email, I failed to hear back from them in a timely manner so I reached out to them again and got ahold of them. I simply wanted my contacts switched back to Acuvue and they tried to tell me that it was allergies causing my problems and were insisiting on me keeping Air Optix. Eventually I did get them to agree to switch my contacts back to acuvue. 

In march I had another eye irritation and I went to Vanderbilt Eye Institue, they told me it was a continued reaction to the Air Optix lenses because I did not give my eyes enough time to heal before applying my new contacts - which was I was not educated on by Music City Optical when I got my new set of contacts. I then reviewed them on facebook at that time. 

Today (8/30/16) I recieved a response to my review on facebook and a corresponding email stating that I was being slanderous and lying, which was not the case at all. I was simply explaining my experience with Music City Optical.
Rewrite this for me:
I visited this place based on its high rating and the fact that they accepted my insurance. My initial visit was satisfactory, with no issues regarding the staff or the doctor.

However, they switched my contact lens brand from Acuvue to Air Optix. About two weeks after using the new contacts, I began experiencing pain, redness, and irritation. Upon removing the contacts, I noticed red rings around both of my eyes. I tried to contact them through phone and email, but received no response. After reaching out to them again, I managed to get in touch with them. My only request was to switch back to Acuvue, but they insisted that my problems were due to allergies and urged me to keep using Air Optix. Eventually, they agreed to switch my contacts back to Acuvue.

In March, I had another eye irritation and sought help from Vanderbilt Eye Institute. They informed me that it was a continued reaction to the Air Optix lenses, as I hadn't allowed enough time for my eyes to heal before using the new contacts. This information was not provided to me by Music City Optical when I received the new contacts. As a result, I left a review about my experience on their Facebook page.

Today (8/30/16), I received a response to my Facebook review, as well as an email accusing me of slander and lying. However, I was simply sharing my honest experience with Music City Optical and not engaging in any form of slander or dishonesty.

It saddens me to say this but I think I need a new nail salon. I have consistently come here for a few years now and the service has never been as bad as it has been the last few times I've been here. Here are my issues:

1) the girl at the front desk never once looked up from her papers while "greeting" me and asking me what I want. She mumbled under her breath to go pick out a color then yelled across the salon that I was getting a mani and pedi. 
2) once I picked out my color I went back to the front and someone who came in after me was seated in a pedi chair, water turned on etc. to get service. Once she saw that I was standing in the front she got a chair going for me. The problem with that is there were no more nail technicians available to work on me.
3) so now I'm sitting in cold water waiting for someone to come and do my feet. 
4) the pedicure started, she painstakingly dug into my toes (which I absolutely hate) and rushed through the Massage part of the pedi
5) after it was all said and done, I find out that their prices have gone up! 

I used to come here because they have later hours and are open on Sunday's but after a 3rd terrible experience here I am not coming back. In the last 3 months, almost the whole staff has changed and these folks are not meeting my needs.
Rewrite this for me:
I'm saddened to admit that I believe I need to find a new nail salon. Despite being a loyal customer for the past few years, the recent service I've received has been consistently disappointing. Here are the issues I've encountered:

1) The girl at the front desk never bothered to look up from her papers while half-heartedly greeting me and asking about my preferences. She muttered instructions for me to pick a color and proceeded to loudly announce across the salon that I was getting a manicure and pedicure.
2) After selecting my color, I returned to the front desk only to find that another customer, who arrived after me, had already been seated in a pedicure chair with the water running. It was only when she noticed me waiting that a chair was made available for me. Unfortunately, there were no nail technicians free to attend to me.
3) Consequently, I ended up sitting with my feet in cold water, waiting for someone to assist me.
4) The pedicure itself was not pleasant. The technician aggressively dug into my toes, something I strongly dislike, and rushed through the massage portion of the pedicure.
5) To make matters worse, I discovered that their prices had increased after the service was completed.

I initially chose this salon because of its convenient late hours and Sunday availability. However, after experiencing three consecutive terrible visits within the past three months and witnessing a significant staff turnover, I have concluded that this establishment can no longer meet my needs. Therefore, I have made the decision not to return.

input:
This place has a great location for the hungry tourist. It manages to be edgy yet chill at the same time. My reason for stopping in was to try the ahi fish tacos with avocado relish, which sounded awesome. At around 3 there was still a healthy amount of people attesting to its popularity and eatability. They had a selection of local microbrews (bottle, not draft) for those interested in getting a taste of Philly in beer form. Alas, I ordered my tacos, but had a little Scooby Doo moment when the arrived. Somehow the chef decided that it was okay to put such a delicate fish in premade taco shells...enough to makes this SoCal girl wince a little and question whether I should consume. Luckily the flavor of the fish was great. I only saw one half inch cube of avocado, but at least the sauce was yummy! 
I got a glimpse of the brunch menu...looks pretty tasty I must say...
Rewrite this for me: This place is conveniently located for hungry tourists. It strikes the perfect balance between being trendy and relaxed. I decided to stop by because I heard their ahi fish tacos with avocado relish were amazing. Even at around 3 o'clock, there were still plenty of people enjoying their food, which speaks to its popularity and quality. They also have a nice selection of local microbrews in bottles for those who want to try Philly's beer scene. However, I was slightly disappointed when my tacos arrived. The chef had made the questionable decision to use pre-made taco shells for the delicate fish, which made me hesitate about eating them as a Southern California native. Thankfully, the flavor of the fish was excellent. Although I only found one small piece of avocado, the sauce made up for it with its delicious taste. I had a quick glance at the brunch menu and it looked quite appetizing, I must admit.

input:
Not really the town you would expect to find a great Indian restaurant, but figured I'd give it a shot.
I'm picky about Indian food, and all I can say is WOW it's good!
The Naan with peach chutney was amazing.
The Lamb Korma was perfect. Perfect amount of spice (too many Indian restaurant set your mouth on fire and you can't enjoy the taste). Not too much, not too little.
The rice and lamb was perfectly cooked. Very authentic.

The decor is very nice (those chairs in the front are impressive) and staff very friendly. Service was also very quick.

I'm relocating to Tampa, and might actually have to make the drive from there a few times to come back. Very impressive!

I would definitely recommend this place, even if it's a bit of a drive.  It's worth it.
Rewrite this for me:
This town isn't what you'd expect to have an amazing Indian restaurant, but I decided to give it a try. As someone who is particular about Indian food, I must say, I was blown away! The Naan with peach chutney was absolutely incredible. The Lamb Korma was just perfect, with just the right amount of spice. It didn't overpower the flavors, like many other Indian restaurants tend to do. The rice and lamb were cooked to perfection, and it felt authentically Indian.

The ambiance of the restaurant is really pleasant, especially those impressive chairs at the front. The staff were friendly and the service was quick as well.

I'm actually moving to Tampa soon, and I might just have to make the drive back here a few times. That's how impressed I am!

I highly recommend this place, even if you have to travel a bit to get here. It's absolutely worth it.

input:
Have you ever tried a new lunch place and liked it so much that you went back for dinner that night and lunch the next day. I have done the back to back to back only once, at Greko. 

I've love the rotisserie chicken pita with fries. If you are in the mood for something healthier, they have great salads. Definitely try the Horta Greens (you can substitute fries for Horta Greens or have them on the side). The perfectly cooked and seasoned greens are delicious. 
I also love the Athenian Chicken (half a rotisserie chicken). 

As a quick, casual, food-first restaurant, Greko has hit the sweet spot.
Rewrite this for me:
Have you ever discovered a new lunch spot that impressed you so much that you ended up returning for dinner that same night and lunch the following day? Well, I had that experience just once, and it was at a place called Greko.

Let me tell you, their rotisserie chicken pita with fries is something to rave about. It's my absolute favorite. But if you're looking for a healthier option, they also offer amazing salads. I highly recommend giving their Horta Greens a try. You can even substitute the fries with these delectably cooked and seasoned greens, or have them as a side. input:
Brother Rabbit you are young, hip, and tasty!

Met friends for drinks and an early dinner. I was the first to arrive so I sat at the bar and ordered the house cider which is great and I followed that with the Oban 18 which is phenomenal so try it while you're there. 

Our dinner kicked off with the most amazing house biscuits and butter that will have you begging for the recipe.

The rest of our dinner was comprised of several selections from the First course menu. We had the daily oysters which were great. Followed by the Brussels sprouts, delicious but the crispy chicken skins were a bit of a let down, they needed more flavor. 

The smoked tuna tartar is great but the sweet chips can overwhelm the dish. Definitely get the marinated shrimp and jalapeño jus it is a wonderfully fresh and bright dish. 

To close thing up we had the dobeger cake with lemon curd and chocolate ice cream, as if that wasn't enough they pour this amazing chocolate sauce on it when it arrives that will have you just dying as you wait to dig in.

Overall Compere Lapin is a great addition to the New Orleans food scene, great for groups or date night with your significant other.
Rewrite this for me:
Hey Brother Rabbit, you're young, cool, and absolutely delicious!

Hung out with friends tonight for some drinks and an early dinner. I got there first, so I grabbed a seat at the bar and ordered their fantastic house cider. Then, I couldn't resist trying the exceptional Oban 18. Seriously, you've gotta give it a shot if you're ever there.

Our dinner started off with these mind-blowing house biscuits and butter that you'll be begging for the recipe once you taste them.

For the rest of our meal, we tried a bunch of dishes from the First course menu. The daily oysters were fantastic. The Brussels sprouts were delicious, but the crispy chicken skins were a bit underwhelming. They needed more flavor, you know?

The smoked tuna tartar was great, but the sweet chips were a bit overpowering. However, make sure to get the marinated shrimp with jalapeño jus. It's a refreshing and vibrant dish that you'll love.

To finish things off, we had the dobeger cake with lemon curd and chocolate ice cream. As if that wasn't enough, they pour this incredible chocolate sauce on top that will have you dying with anticipation before you can dig in.

All in all, Compere Lapin is a fantastic addition to the New Orleans food scene. It's perfect for groups or a romantic date night with your special someone.

input:
Here for convention and Imo's was suggested as "The Best" St. Louis Style pizza by hotel staff. 

I opted for delivery which was good and efficient. The food arrived still hot. I ordered a medium pepperoni and an order of toasted ravioli. 

Now, I knew the cheese on the pizza was provel so it would taste different. I was really not impressed. It may just be a matter of taste preference. It was hard to separate each piece of pizza too.  Like, it wasn't cut all the way through. Not really a fan. So thumbs down on the pizza. 

What bumps the stars up are the T-Ravs!  I was hoping for cheese ravioli but the staple is a meat mixture. Boy...do they do it justice. They were the bomb!  The sauce with it was too watery but still tasty. I would order just the ravioli next time!
Rewrite this for me:
I came to the convention and the hotel staff recommended Imo's as the top choice for St. Louis Style pizza. Instead of dining in, I decided to have it delivered, which turned out to be a good and efficient choice. The food arrived while still hot, and I ordered a medium pepperoni pizza along with an order of toasted ravioli.

Being aware that Imo's pizza uses provel cheese, I was prepared for a different taste. However, I wasn't particularly impressed. It could simply be a matter of personal preference, but I found it difficult to separate each piece of pizza because it wasn't cut all the way through. Unfortunately, I wasn't a fan of their pizza. Thumbs down on that.

On the other hand, the real stars of the meal were the toasted ravioli! Although I was initially hoping for cheese-filled ravioli, the meat mixture that Imo's uses really does it justice. They were absolutely delicious! The accompanying sauce was a bit too watery for my liking, but it still had a tasty flavor. Next time, I would definitely just order the ravioli.

input: I have groen up eating Italian food and i have not come across a more legit place than Mazzaros! Love their sauce and meatballs.

input: Okay, so it's a dance club. It's trendy and offers higher-end cocktails and beers while still offering your run-of-the-mill wells and domestic bottles. On certain nights, guys have to pay a door charge (but that's not really uncommon in the industry). There is a huge patio and, even in the winter, almost the entire patio is still available because they enclose it. The music is pretty hit-or-miss...sometimes you're dancing away to classic hip-hop, pop, and even rock, and other times you're standing there while the DJ spins out an un-danceable tune. If you're on the patio, you can chat...but if you're inside it's (not shockingly) too loud to really talk. If you're in the CWE and you're looking to dance, at least give the Mandarin a shot; it's not going to be for everyone, but it's pretty great if you're in the mood for it.
Rewrite this for me:
Sure, here's a rewrite:

The venue is a stylish dance club that offers a wide range of high-quality cocktails and beers, including both upscale options and more common choices. On certain nights, there is a door charge for guys, which is fairly standard in the industry. Despite the winter season, the club's large patio is mostly enclosed, allowing guests to enjoy it throughout the year. The music selection varies, sometimes featuring popular genres like classic hip-hop, pop, and rock, while other times the DJ plays less danceable tunes. If you prefer to have conversations, the patio is the ideal spot as the indoor area tends to be quite loud. Located in CWE, the Mandarin is worth a try, particularly if you're in the mood for dancing, although it may not appeal to everyone's taste. It offers a pretty great experience overall.

input:
Another gem on Frenchmen.  We made it in just in time to grab the corner tall table and enjoyed the piano player playing some nice tunes.

Order at the bar and they'll bring you the food.  What we had:
pork pot stickers - pretty good - $4 HH price
smoked hanger steak w/ chimichurri sauce on toastones - tasted much better than it looked - $4 HH price
lobster eggrolls w/ sweet chile lime sauce - $8 - didn't look promising but it was tasty
Hopitoulas - $4.5
UFO - $4.5

One of the owners/chefs is Korean, thus the Asian food.

HH everyday from 4-6:30pm, $4 tapas, $5 wines, $3 beers.

We will definitely return.
Rewrite this for me:
We stumbled upon another hidden gem on Frenchmen Street just in time to secure a tall table by the corner. As we settled in, the soothing melodies from the piano player filled the air.

To our surprise, the bar also served food, and all we had to do was place our order there. Here's what we enjoyed:

- The pork pot stickers were pretty good and had a happy hour price of $4.
- The smoked hanger steak on toastones, accompanied by chimichurri sauce, tasted much better than it looked and was also priced at $4 during happy hour.
- Initially, the lobster eggrolls with sweet chile lime sauce didn't seem promising, but they turned out to be quite tasty at $8.
- For drinks, we tried the Hopitoulas and the UFO, both priced at $4.5 each.

Interestingly, one of the owners and chefs is Korean, which explains the presence of Asian cuisine on the menu.

Furthermore, we discovered that happy hour is available every day from 4 pm to 6:30 pm, offering $4 tapas, $5 wines, and $3 beers.

Overall, our experience was delightful, and we have already decided to return in the future.

input:
Four of us had dinner at the Sockeye Grill this weekend.  Service was terrible.  Super slow.  Salads were warm and tasteless.  Dressing was watered down. 

Salmon was excellent.  Nachos were okay. Finger steaks were mushy and drab. 

Waitress  knew her beer. The dark lager was excellent.  The lighter beers we had were too warm. 

Looks like this restaurant need some fine tuning.  The atmosphere was like a warehouse, more like being in a barn than a restaurant. 

Tvs everywhere but the news was on. Huh? How depressing is that? 

We won't be back.
Rewrite this for me:
This past weekend, a group of four of us decided to dine at the Sockeye Grill. Unfortunately, the service we received was quite terrible. It was incredibly slow and disappointing. The salads we ordered were not only warm but also lacked any taste. The dressing was incredibly diluted and unappetizing.

Amidst this disappointing experience, we did find solace in the excellent salmon dish that was served to us. The nachos, however, were just mediocre. On the other hand, the finger steaks were unexpectedly mushy and uninspiring.

One positive aspect of our visit was that our waitress had a good knowledge of their beer selection. The dark lager we ordered was truly excellent. Unfortunately, the lighter beers we tried were served at a warm temperature, which was quite disappointing.

Overall, it seems like this restaurant could benefit from some improvements. The atmosphere was more reminiscent of a warehouse or barn rather than a proper dining establishment. It was also odd that even though there were TVs everywhere, they were all tuned into the news. This choice of programming was quite depressing, to say the least.

Based on our experience, we have decided that we will not be returning to the Sockeye Grill.

input:
We had a very nice dinner here on St. Patrick's day, which happens to be my sister's birthday.  The server was super sweet and served the cake we brought to celebrate.  The bartender was so kind and gave my sister a complimentary St. Patty's cocktail, which was incredibly yummy.  

We ordered various dishes:  tri-tip, rotisserie chicken, pulled pork and a veggie burrito.  All was wonderful, except for the veggie burrito, which was lackluster (but who orders a veggie burrito at a rotisserie grill???).  My father-in-law has visited many more times, raving about the moist, flavorful rotisserie chicken.  

The prices were reasonable, portions adequate and service super!  We will definitely visit again, minus the resident vegetarian.  :)
Rewrite this for me:
On St. Patrick's day, which also coincided with my sister's birthday, we had a delightful dining experience. The server was exceptionally kind and even helped us with our cake, which we brought along to celebrate. Additionally, the bartender generously treated my sister to a delicious St. Patty's cocktail.

Our order consisted of a variety of dishes, including tri-tip, rotisserie chicken, pulled pork, and an unexpected choice of a veggie burrito at a rotisserie grill (not the best decision). While everything was delightful, save for the lackluster veggie burrito, my father-in-law, who has visited multiple times, cannot stop raving about the moist and flavorful rotisserie chicken.

Reasonable prices, decent portions, and fantastic service made our experience even more enjoyable. We will definitely return, perhaps leaving out the resident vegetarian next time. :)

input: I have been told by numerous native philadelphians that Ralph's is one of the best Italian restaurants in the city and is a must to experience. We did not think so. We started off with a grilled calamari appetizer that was soaked in salty red sauce. The amount of sauce overwhelmed the palate to the point where we couldn't even taste the calamari. I got the pasta bolognese with filet mignon tips. Again, the red sauce was very salty. The filet mignon tips was really just average quality beef. My wife ordered the black lobster ravioli which were decent but overly salty. We expected much more from the oldest Italian restaurant in the country.
Rewrite this for me: According to numerous native Philadelphians, Ralph's is highly recommended as one of the top Italian restaurants in the city. However, our personal experience differed from their claims. Our meal began with a grilled calamari appetizer that was heavily drenched in a salt-laden red sauce. The excessive amount of sauce overwhelmed our taste buds to the extent that we could hardly distinguish the flavor of the calamari itself. For my main dish, I opted for the pasta bolognese with filet mignon tips. Once again, the red sauce displayed an excessive saltiness, and the filet mignon tips turned out to be rather average in terms of beef quality. My wife decided to try the black lobster ravioli, which were fairly decent but still overly seasoned with salt. Considering that Ralph's prides itself as the oldest Italian restaurant in the country, we had higher expectations and were left somewhat disappointed.

input:
Beer service was lackluster. The first beer I ordered had an off flavor (sour). I ordered a taste of another similar dark beer to see if the problem was endemic but it wasn't. I would have appreciated it more if the bar tender looked into the off flavor when I sent my beer back. This tells me the bar tender doesn't know beer. I assume that particular draft line needs to be cleaned but maybe the problem was with the keg. 

Another thing that killed me was their use of glassware. They serve beers in the classic American "Shaker" pint glass and serve water in the far superior English Nonic Pint glass. I also saw the bar tender pour a white ale with normal ABV in a stemmed tulip glass.

The shaker pint glasses are kept refrigerated and are too cold in my opinion. I would much rather see them kept at room temp and rinsed in cold water (which they do here). 

All in all, the beer knowledge is not up to par for a place that advertises as a burger joint with a large craft beer selection (30 taps).
Rewrite this for me:
The service at the bar for beer was quite disappointing. Initially, the beer I ordered had a sour off flavor, which suggested a problem with its quality. In an attempt to determine if this issue was consistent, I decided to sample another dark beer, similar to the first one. Surprisingly, the second beer tasted fine, ruling out any widespread problem. However, I would have appreciated it if the bartender had taken the time to investigate the off flavor when I returned the beer. This lack of attention suggests a lack of knowledge about beer on the bartender's part. It is possible that the draft line needs cleaning, but the issue could also be with the keg.

Another concern for me was their choice of glassware. They served beers in the traditional American "Shaker" pint glass, which I found less appealing compared to the far superior English Nonic Pint glass used for water. Moreover, I witnessed the bartender pouring a white ale with a normal alcohol by volume (ABV) into a stemmed tulip glass, which was quite odd.

Additionally, I felt that the shaker pint glasses were excessively chilled. In my opinion, it would be preferable for them to be kept at room temperature and simply rinsed with cold water, as they currently do here.

Overall, the level of beer knowledge at this establishment falls short of expectations for a place that promotes itself as a burger joint with an extensive craft beer selection boasting 30 taps.

input: Finally got to check out Cafe Soleil. One word: Delicieux!! Being from France, I had high expectations, I don't play with my pastries! Boy do they deliver, the croissants were buttery, nice and flaky, and melt in your mouth...even better then some of the ones I had in France. Not surprisingly, the baker "Nico" is french, and you could taste the difference in the food.  The fact that the products are imported does make a big difference in the taste, it's definitely authentic.  Nico was very personable and friendly, it was fun chatting with an ex-parisian :). The one negative thing is they are too far from me, 45 mins drive, but to satiate my sweet tooth, I will definitely be back! I highly recommend this bakery.
Rewrite this for me:
I finally had the chance to visit Cafe Soleil and let me just say: it was absolutely delicious! As someone from France, I hold pastries to a high standard, and Cafe Soleil did not disappoint. The croissants were perfectly buttery, flaky, and practically melted in my mouth. In fact, they were even better than some of the ones I've had back in France. It's no surprise that the baker, Nico, is French himself. You can truly taste the difference in the food. The fact that they use imported ingredients definitely adds to the authenticity of the flavors.

Nico himself was a delight to talk to. He was personable and friendly, and it was enjoyable chatting with a former Parisian. The only downside is that Cafe Soleil is quite far from me, about a 45-minute drive. However, to satisfy my sweet cravings, I will certainly make the trip back. I highly recommend this bakery to anyone looking for an authentic and delicious experience.

input:
Not mediocre at all IMHO.  Makes me wonder if Daniel O. went to the same place we did.

This is a great neighborhood byob place that provides welcoming service and excellent food at a reasonable price.  We started going here because numerous South Philly friends recommended it.  This is not foo-foo Italian.  This is not pretentious Italian.  This is "let's go back and work our way through the menu" Italian.  We found the specials to be good choices.  My husband's broccoli rabe and sausage was excellent, as was a grilled romaine salad with bleu cheese and pine nuts.  Both were generous enough to share.  Last time, sausage & figs was a hit.  If you are in the mood for a basic plate of macaronis with red gravy, you won't be disappointed either.  We had a great time with the waitress because my BIL brought a bottle of Great Wall wine from China (that was the 2nd bottle we opened) and that started a whole crazy discussion.  She didn't know us from Adam, but we left there feeling like regulars.

It's a very doable destination if you are on your way to a sporting event at the Linc or the Cit, or to the Spectrum or Wachovia Center.  For those who rely on public transportation, you can get off the subway at Broad & Oregon, then walk back a block to Broad & Porter.  Make a reservation, though because it can be a popular place.  You also want to make sure you have time to have a relaxing meal and make your event in time.

The last time we went, the sausage and figs dish was a big hit. And even if you're just in the mood for a classic plate of pasta with marinara sauce, you won't be disappointed. 

Our waitress was awesome. We had a great time because my brother-in-law brought a bottle of Great Wall wine from China (which was the second bottle we opened). This sparked a whole crazy discussion with the waitress. Despite not knowing us, she made us feel like regulars by the time we left.

input:
I must say I'm very disappointed, my two stars are for presentation and prompt delivery. I ordered the rainbow roll, white tuna roll, calamari and chicken lettuce wraps. Where do I begin? ok with the bad. 

I strongly feel that when you are delivering food that should be served cold, you don't put it in a bag with hot food because that equals mushy, warm sushi, which is what I got. The rainbow roll, which normally is topped with raw fish was topped with mushy avocado????? which I ended up peeling off to salvage the sushi. The spicy white tuna roll was very good.

The calamari looked like chicken fingers all the breading was falling off and it was under cooked, I took one bite and tossed it. Now I've had lettuce wraps before but mines came with an actual head of lettuce in a bag and chicken filling in a plate. It was not described this way in the menu at all. All in all I don't think I'll be ordering from here again. I'll stick to Niji's on 5th.
Rewrite this for me:
I must express my disappointment with my recent order. I would like to give credit for the presentation and timely delivery, hence the two stars. However, there are several aspects that left me dissatisfied. 

Firstly, I was disappointed with the mishandling of the food. It is imperative that when delivering food that should be served cold, it is not placed in the same bag as hot food. Unfortunately, this led to my sushi becoming mushy and warm, greatly impacting the overall experience. To my surprise, the rainbow roll, which typically includes raw fish as a topping, had mushy avocado instead. I had to peel the avocado off to salvage the sushi. On the brighter side, I must commend the delicious taste of the spicy white tuna roll.

Moving on, the calamari was far from satisfactory. It appeared as if the breading was falling off, resembling chicken fingers. Moreover, it was undercooked. After just one bite, I had no option but to discard it.

Lastly, I have previously enjoyed lettuce wraps, but the ones I received were quite different from what I expected. Instead of the usual arrangement of a plate filled with chicken filling and a separate bag containing lettuce leaves, mine arrived with a whole head of lettuce in a bag. This discrepancy was not mentioned in the menu description.

Due to these disappointing experiences, I have decided that I will not be ordering from here again. I will return to my usual choice, Niji's on 5th.

input:
I came in here the other night for a  post-show snack after seeing a ESO performance at the Winspear. The main reason we chose this location was because it was close to the Winspear, and open late (until 11:30pm on Friday and Saturday). I don't have any strong criticisms of the restaurant. I suppose, if anything, the menu may have seemed a little bit over-priced - at least for what I ordered. I had a Caesar salad with three 'jumbo' shrimp on it, which cost $15. The portion size did not seem to justify the cost and the jumbo shrimp were fairly average in their size, but the flavours were good and the ingredients were fresh. My friend had a soup, which looked and smelled absolutely amazing, and at $6 it didn't seem too unreasonable. She also had the smoked salmon Carpaccio, which looked very appetizing with its thick slices of dark rye bread and generous slices of smoked salmon and capers. The also had a couple of interesting beers on their menu that we were keen to try.

I think if you're going to a show in the area and looking for a spot to get a drink or a snack afterward, this is not a bad option. Their menu at that time of night had an interesting mix of appetizers and desserts that seemed to provide something to suit most tastes.

I'm assuming Normand's Bistro must be connected to the Normand's restaurant which is on Jasper Avenue. Of interest, I have heard that Normand's took over the brunch menu that had formerly been offered at the Glenora Bistro.
Rewrite this for me:
After attending an ESO performance at the Winspear, my friend and I decided to grab a post-show snack at this restaurant. She also ordered the smoked salmon Carpaccio, which was visually appealing with thick slices of dark rye bread, generous portions of smoked salmon, and capers. I assume that Normand's Bistro is associated with the Normand's restaurant located on Jasper Avenue. I've heard that Normand's now serves the brunch menu previously offered at Glenora Bistro, which might be of interest to some.

I said I was new to the area and he said, "That's too bad." What kind of customer service is that?!? I usually don't write reviews, but this place was that bad.

input: i had the seafood combo-catfish (and im talkin like 5 pounds of it), red beans and rice and coleslaw.  the food was pretty damn good.  well, the real reason we walked in to this place was due to the big sign out front: "happy hour, mon-sat, 4pm-7pm, 2 for 1"  Now THAT is what im talkin about.  i ordered a margarita...and being that i'm from California, i have extremely high standards for marg's.  wasn't bad, but really wasn't great... but food made up for it!
Rewrite this for me:
I had the seafood combo, which consisted of a generous portion of catfish, along with a serving size that must have been around 5 pounds. It was accompanied by delicious sides of red beans and rice, as well as coleslaw. The quality of the food was impressive and had me thoroughly satisfied. 

We actually decided to dine at this place mainly because of the enticing sign displayed outside: "Happy Hour, Monday to Saturday, from 4pm to 7pm, 2 for 1." Now, that's exactly what I had in mind. I ordered a margarita, keeping in mind that as a resident of California, my expectations for margaritas are pretty high. It wasn't terrible, but I can't say it was outstanding either. Fortunately, the exceptional food more than made up for it.

input:

input:
The Sunrise Family Restaurant is an old style diner that has a very small-town, homey feel.   Service is prompt and super friendly.

I had a Monte Cristo sandwich per the waitresses recommendation and I won't lie, it was pretty disappointing.  Take a stack of turkey and a couple thick slices of ham out of their respective industrial packs, microwave them with some swiss cheese on top and serve on limp french toast.  Somebody out there might like it.  I didn't. 

It came with a salad and fries, both of which were good.  The fries were thick steak fries cooked to a perfect golden brown.   

I have a feeling there are some good items on the menu.  I would especially be interested in trying breakfast.  I'll be back.
Rewrite this for me:
The Sunrise Family Restaurant is a charming, small-town diner that exudes a warm and welcoming atmosphere. The service is quick and incredibly friendly.

Based on the waitress's recommendation, I opted for the Monte Cristo sandwich. Unfortunately, I must admit that it was rather underwhelming. The sandwich consisted of turkey and ham taken directly from their industrial packaging, microwaved with a slice of Swiss cheese on top, and served on limp French toast. While this might appeal to some tastes, it didn't meet my expectations.

However, I was pleasantly surprised by the accompanying salad and fries. The fries, in particular, were thick steak fries cooked to a delectable golden brown perfection.

Despite my disappointment with the Monte Cristo sandwich, I believe that there are other delightful options on the menu. I am particularly intrigued by the breakfast offerings and look forward to returning to give them a try.

input: First time at Butcher & Bee with my husband who joined me and my co-workers for lunch one day. I love the place, it so cute with the farmhouse feel. It's really open and cute booths that offers some privacy. We had a group of 7 and it was a bit tight, but we were able to be sat right away. I ordered the pork belly gnocchi, and it was good, but not great. I felt it lacked texture. If the pork belly was crispy, it would have sealed the deal. My husband ordered the trout sandwich, unfortunately, he was disappointed that it was basically a 'tuna salad' sandwich. He did not enjoy it. For dessert, we ordered coconut macaroons, which were good. Co-workers had mixed reviews, but one ordered the KFC (Korean Fried Chicken) sandwich, and he liked it. Will definitely have to give this place another try. Also, the use books for bill holders, so cute!
Rewrite this for me: My husband joined me and my co-workers for lunch at Butcher & Bee for the first time. I absolutely adore the place as it has a charming farmhouse ambiance. The spacious layout and adorable booths provide a sense of privacy. Despite our group of seven feeling a bit cramped, we were promptly seated. I decided to try the pork belly gnocchi, which was good but fell short of greatness due to a lack of texture. Crispy pork belly would have elevated the dish. On the other hand, my husband ordered the trout sandwich and was disappointed to find it essentially a "tuna salad" sandwich. He did not enjoy it. For dessert, we indulged in some delightful coconut macaroons. While my co-workers had mixed opinions, one of them opted for the KFC (Korean Fried Chicken) sandwich and enjoyed it. We plan to give this place another chance. Also, I must mention the adorable use of books as bill holders!

input:
This is a really fun event for those who enjoy beer in all its forms. The drinks themselves were relatively cheap ($2-4 for a 4 oz. sample. Most were $2, some were $3, and very few were in the $4 range), however the food was really over priced ($6 for a small cup of fancy macaroni and cheese? really?). For the beer lover, however, there is a wide variety of tried and true along with the new kids on the block from local, national and international lines. Also, if you like what you tasted, you can buy it on site, with a Sobeys/Safeway liquor store right on site doing specials on the sampled brews. 

We went VIP for this event, however I don't think it's worth it. What you get: a glass mug instead of a plastic one, a beer and food class ($2 value) and a beer seminar ($2 value). If you do it all, or really value the glass mug, go for it! But for me, who just did the beer and food class, it wasn't worth it. 

My only complaint is for the venue, but for an event that size, you need the space. $16 for parking on top of your entry fee (though I guess most people would cab or Uber it there so you don't have to have a designated driver), and then you have to buy sample tickets on site. It gets quite expensive.
Rewrite this for me:
This event is a lot of fun for beer enthusiasts. The drinks are reasonably priced, ranging from $2 to $4 for a 4 oz. sample, with most being $2. However, the food is quite pricey, like $6 for a small cup of fancy macaroni and cheese. But for those who love beer, there's a wide selection to choose from, including local, national, and international options. Plus, you can purchase the beers you liked on site, as there's a Sobeys/Safeway liquor store offering specials on the sampled brews.

We decided to opt for the VIP experience, but I don't think it's worth it. The perks include a glass mug instead of a plastic one, a beer and food class, and a beer seminar. If you're interested in all of these things or really value the glass mug, then go for it. But for me, who only attended the beer and food class, it wasn't worth the extra cost.

My only complaint is about the venue, but considering the size of the event, more space is necessary. They charge $16 for parking, in addition to the entry fee. It can get quite expensive, although I suppose most people would use a cab or Uber to get there so they wouldn't need a designated driver. Plus, you have to buy sample tickets on site.

input: I've been here a handful of times and it's always because I don't have time to go to VN Nails near Costco where I prefer to go (they get 5 stars from me). After getting the typical shabby job on a fill with French tips,  I accidentally smudged two nails really badly.  They needed to be repainted and I asked her to do so... I even offered to pay extra.  The nail tech came over to look and she pressed the clumps back down and painted right back over the mess (didn't even keep the paint in the lines) then slathered so much varnish over the train wreck that it was literally dripping down my finger. input:
I tried to like this place... I really did. So much so that I went back to try it after a less that satisfactory first wax.

Wax 1- I had Despina, I think her name was. I waited a good 15 minutes after my appointment time for her to come and get me from the front. Ironic they have a 9 minute policy that if you don't show they'll cancel/charge you or whatever. Anyway, as for the experience with Despina, she did not speak to me. Like at all. Made me feel super awkward the whole time, and missed a fair few chunks of hair. She didn't ask me anything about myself, didn't tell me where to sit or how she wanted me positioned etc. Luckily I got this one half price as it was my first time at EWC.

Wax 2- I booked 3-4 weeks later with Amy Jo (based on previous Yelp reviews). She was a lot friendlier (literally the only reason why I'm giving this 1 star) BUT way too sloppy. I think it's safe to say this is the worst wax I've ever had. She left half of my hair on right before Valentine's Day! I understand they can't get all the hairs all the time but a lottttt of hair right on top was left clearly visible to my waxer. My apt was at 3.45, I walked out of the building at 3.53. Really. This includes the time spent undressing, redressing, and paying. 8 minutes is not long enough for all of this. It went so quick that when she said she was done I was actually shocked.  
I'm about to go to CVS and get some at home wax strips to finish the job... For $47+ I expect way way more. 

The staff- Another reason why I won't be returning. The ladies at the front desk are generally rude and disinterested in showing any glimpse of good customer service. ALSO, I don't like being asked if I'm going to tip - can't you give me the card machine so I can do it myself rather than make me announce if I would like to tip and how much? 

The hunt for a decent Brazilian wax in Philly continues- someone help me PLEASE!
Rewrite this for me:
I made an effort to like this place, truly. I was even willing to give it another chance after my unsatisfactory first wax experience.

During my first wax (with a technician named Despina, I believe), I waited for a good 15 minutes past my appointment time before she finally came to get me. Ironically, the salon has a policy that if you don't show up within 9 minutes, they cancel or charge you or something like that. Anyway, Despina hardly spoke to me throughout the entire process, which made me feel really uncomfortable. She also missed quite a few patches of hair and didn't give me any instructions on where to sit or how to position myself. Luckily, I got a discount on that session since it was my first time at EWC.

For my second wax, I booked an appointment with Amy Jo based on some positive Yelp reviews. She was much friendlier (which is the only reason why I'm giving this place one star), but her technique was extremely sloppy. I can confidently say that this was the worst wax I've ever had. She left a noticeable amount of hair right before Valentine's Day! I understand that they can't remove every single hair, but there was a significant amount left untouched, especially on the top. My appointment was at 3:45, and I walked out of the building at 3:53. I mean, seriously? That includes the time it took to undress, redress, and pay. Eight minutes is definitely not enough time for all of that. It happened so quickly that I was actually taken aback when she said she was done. I'm about to go to CVS and get some at-home wax strips to finish the job myself. For $47 or more, I definitely expect much better results.

In addition to the disappointing waxing experiences, I found the staff to be another reason why I won't be returning. The ladies at the front desk are generally rude and show no interest in providing good customer service. Furthermore, I don't appreciate being asked if I'm going to tip. Can't they just give me the card machine so I can tip on my own, instead of making me announce my decision and amount?

I'm still on the search for a decent Brazilian wax in Philadelphia. If anyone can help me, please do!

input: Amazing and comfortable atmosphere with extremely unique flavor combinations in the dishes. The Cuban Lamb Frita is a must (add the egg! It's worth it). input: I love this food truck. They have the tastiest street foods like their captain crunch tilapia burrito. Who would've thought of that? input: I was having an bad migraine and felt terrible. When woke up I had a sinus infection and my day was just going awful. Jen was understanding and nice, she asked me questions and checked up on me constantly. She even showed me some at home techniques I could use. She took her time, obviously did not rush. Carrie, I believe, was the name of the woman who did a foot massage on my father. He was very pleased and recommended I try it sometime. They also informed me about the membership program which not only is very cost-efficient, but also adheres to my busy schedule. I signed up on the spot with no hesitation. Friendly staff, great atmosphere, comfortable building and very calming environment! Would recommended! I feel so much better already and am going back in a month to get a 90 minute massage.
Rewrite this for me:

Desperate to find some relief, I called around to several places hoping to get a massage appointment for the day. Unfortunately, no one had any availability. Without hesitation, I immediately signed up for the membership.

The staff at Massage Envy were friendly, the atmosphere was great, the building was comfortable, and the environment was incredibly calming. I highly recommend their services. I'm already feeling much better, and I'm looking forward to returning in a month for a 90-minute massage.

input: This place is good~  The chicken is moist, the skin is crispy, the flavor is nice and smokey, this is the best kind of roast chicken I have tried. The smells (smokey, bbq) is so good and hypnotizing, just make my mouth water.  I got the double chicken family which is 2 whole chickens, literally a bed of fries underneath them, and cole slaw.  It was more than enough to feed a family of four.  The dipping sauces that come with it are also real good, i really like the mustard base one, its kinda mustardy with a chipotle flair, and there is also a green sauce that is like a salsa.  The fries are wedge fries and they make you real full because there are plenty to go around. We had leftovers because the meal was that big.  I would rather eat here than popeyes or kfc, because you get more, its healthier, and you get better service. The owners are real nice and friendly. I will be back because I know I will be craving this chicken.
Rewrite this for me: This place is fantastic! The chicken is incredibly juicy with a perfectly crispy skin, and the flavor is a delightful blend of smokiness. It's hands down the best roast chicken I've ever tasted. The scent of the smoky BBQ is simply mesmerizing and makes my mouth water. I ordered the double chicken family meal, which came with two whole chickens sitting on a bed of fries, as well as cole slaw. It was more than enough food to satisfy a family of four. The dipping sauces that accompanied the meal were also exceptional, particularly the mustard-based one with a hint of chipotle. The green sauce resembled a salsa and added a unique touch. The wedged fries were plentiful, leaving me feeling happily full. In fact, we even had leftovers because the portion size was so generous. I would definitely choose this place over Popeyes or KFC any day. Not only do you get more for your money, but the meal is also healthier, and the service is top-notch. The owners are incredibly kind and friendly. I'm already planning on coming back here because I know I'll be craving their amazing chicken.

input:

input:

input:
5 STAR FOOD! 
For sure one of if not the best place to get a sandwich on the beach anywhere between St Pete Beach & Clearwater Beach. All orders cooked to order. The only reason I did not give 5 stars overall as the seating may be an issue for some.
Rewrite this for me: This place is a absolute gem when it comes to finding the best sandwich on the beach between St Pete Beach and Clearwater Beach. input:
We had dinner here after a long day at the convention center.  We asked to sit in a quieter area, and they found us a nice table in a side room.  Service was attentive and professional.  Our waiter recommended the aged ribeye steak--"best steak ever."  I didn't think I wanted an entire 18-ounce boneless, so he suggested we split it.  We did--certainly one of the "best steaks ever"--cooked perfectly medium rare and it was plenty for both of us.  Of course, we also had the signature shrimp cocktail (horseradish) and the iceberg lettuce wedge with crumbled bacon (very pancetta-like).   OK, iceberg wedge isn't the most exciting salad, but it's great when done well, which this was.  
   My only disappointment was a wine list that had a very limited choice of medium-priced wines by the bottle, so wine selection took a while.  A small complaint, so I would rate H & I  4.5 stars if possible.
Rewrite this for me:
After a tiring day at the convention center, we decided to have dinner at this place. Seeking a quieter spot, we requested to be seated in a more serene area, and the staff kindly accommodated us by finding a pleasant table in a side room. The service we received was attentive and professional. Our waiter highly recommended the aged ribeye steak, claiming it to be the "best steak ever." Initially hesitant about ordering a massive 18-ounce boneless steak, he suggested that we split it, and we obliged. It turned out to be truly one of the finest steaks we've ever had, cooked to a perfect medium rare and ample in portion for both of us. We couldn't resist trying their signature shrimp cocktail with a kick of horseradish and the iceberg lettuce wedge topped with delectable crumbled bacon reminiscent of pancetta. While the iceberg wedge salad may not be the most exciting choice, it was executed flawlessly, which made it enjoyable for us. 

However, the only letdown was the limited selection of medium-priced wines on their wine list, which made the decision-making process a bit prolonged. Despite this minor inconvenience, we would still rate H & I a fantastic 4.5 stars if possible.

input: The worst Italian food I have ever tasted!!! I'm far from Italian, but I can make a MEAN lasagna & spaghetti myself compared to this place. 1st of all, we waited 45mins patiently w/ a hungry Hubby, 2yr old, 7yr old, & myself. When we finally got seated, the waitress was very polite, but forgetful at times. Didnt drink any alcohol or sodas but the lemonade was very tart & the garlic bread was not-so-fresh...had to request for some fresh bread after my family devoured the 1st basket from starving & waiting for so long. I ordered the stuffed shells & chicken parmagiana. The salad was very tasty; however, they only have Italian dressing...no ranch or anything else. I am not a picky eater & rarely complain, but the stuffed shells & parmagiana chicken tasted HORRIBLE!! The chicken was very bland & the stuffed shells were hard & overbaked. The meranera sauce tasted like it was old or aged too long (if there's ever such a thing, lol). I could not bring myself to eat my entree. I had to send it back. I heard the lady at the table next to ours say the salmon was good, so I figured the salmon might be safe. It was actually very good! I was still very disappointed after this restaurant was referred to me by many. I felt like they got an easy $50 bucks out of me. I would have rathered gone to the olive garden or macaroni grill. If u r looking for an awesome authentic Italian cusine restaurant in Tucson, I highly recommend Contessa off of Ina Rd. The only reason we didn't go there is b/c it was out of the way from where we were going.  It's pretty far from where we live but always worth the drive. Everything is freshly made & u can definite tell the difference! I'm sorry Caruso, but I don't think my family will be coming here ever again!

input:
If you are looking to be impressed by French-German dishes in New Orleans, please go to Luke Restaurant, I know I was. 

The restaurant is located in the Central Business District, next to the Hilton and in the former Masonic Temple Building, so there is that historic vibe to the restaurant. The front room is a lot more grand than the back room (where we were seated), but that is offset by views of the open kitchen. 

Apparently they only want to seat people with reservations, so since we did not have one, we were refused seating until 9:15pm (it was 6:45pm) but with a little back and forth, we ended up waiting only 15 minutes before we were seated. However, as we walked through the restaurant to the back room, way too many tables were empty that it made no sense that they acted that way. A lot of tables still remained empty throughout the meal.

I decided to start out my meal with a cocktail. I originally wanted the Mint Julep but they were out so I had the Riverbend (vodka, lemon juice, basil syrup, blueberries & ginger ale) at the recommendation of the server. It was a relatively sweet cocktail, with the ginger ale being the most powering flavor, but you could still taste the alcohol.

My friend choose a regular starter and ordered a cup of the Crawfish Bisque. She ate all of it so I am assuming she liked it, but she did complain of a sour aftertaste.

My boyfriend skipped the appetizers and went straight for the entree. He always seems to find the most basic item on the menu and order it. He had the Luke Burger (bacon, caramelized onions, tomatoes, Swiss cheese) and was raving about it. One thing I can tell you, it was a very good size. 

My friend had the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte" with lump crab meat, roasted jalapeño cheese grits, andouille & green onion sausages. She loved it.

I have an obsession with mussels so I had the classic Moules et Frites. Although only having two simply ingredients (garlic & thyme) in the broth, the flavors stood out and the taste was a lot bolder than others I have had with a lot more ingredients. The house-made fries were scrumptious. These are the best kind.

Even with all that food, we still made room for dessert. We first had the Bread Pudding which was delicious but quite sweet. I am also not a fan of over sauced foods.

One wasn't enough so we also ordered the Bourbon Vanilla Bean Creme Brulee. It was superb and not too sweet which is a plus for me. The little cookies on top added nothing to the dessert and if anything could have been left off.

All that good food, I still have to give props to our server. He was amazing and engaging. The front desk soured the mood a little bit a first but he more than made up for it. I couldn't have asked for anyone better.
Rewrite this for me:
If you want to be impressed by French-German cuisine in New Orleans, I highly recommend checking out Luke Restaurant. Located in the Central Business District, right next to the Hilton, the restaurant is housed in the beautiful former Masonic Temple Building, giving it a historic and charming atmosphere. While the front room is more grand, the back room where we were seated still offered views of the open kitchen.

It's worth noting that Luke Restaurant seems to prioritize reservations, as we were initially refused seating since we didn't have one. However, after a little negotiation, we only had to wait for 15 minutes before being seated at 9:15pm, despite it being 6:45pm. It was slightly puzzling to see that many tables were empty as we walked to our seats and remained empty throughout our meal.

To start my dining experience, I opted for a cocktail. Unfortunately, they were out of the Mint Julep, so I took the server's recommendation and tried the Riverbend, a sweet cocktail made with vodka, lemon juice, basil syrup, blueberries, and ginger ale. The ginger ale stood out the most, but the alcohol was still discernible.

My friend decided to go for a regular starter and ordered a cup of Crawfish Bisque. She enjoyed it and finished the whole cup, but mentioned a slight sour aftertaste.

Meanwhile, my boyfriend skipped the appetizers and went straight for the entree, choosing the Luke Burger with bacon, caramelized onions, tomatoes, and Swiss cheese. He couldn't stop raving about it, and I can confirm it was a substantial portion.

As for my friend, she ordered the Jumbo Louisiana Shrimp "En Cocotte", which was served with lump crab meat, roasted jalapeño cheese grits, andouille, and green onion sausages. She absolutely loved it.

Having a weakness for mussels, I couldn't resist ordering the classic Moules et Frites. Despite the simplicity of the broth, which only consisted of garlic and thyme, the flavors were bold and distinct compared to other versions I've tried with more ingredients. The accompanying house-made fries were absolutely delicious – the kind you can't get enough of.

Even after indulging in all that food, we still managed to find space for dessert. We started with the Bread Pudding, which was tasty but quite sweet for my liking, as I'm not a fan of overly sauced dishes.

And because one dessert wasn't enough, we also couldn't resist trying the Bourbon Vanilla Bean Creme Brulee. It was superb and not overpoweringly sweet, which was a definite positive for me. The little cookies on top didn't add much to the overall experience and could have been left off.

Despite the occasional sour note from the front desk, our server truly elevated our dining experience. He was attentive, friendly, and engaging, making up for any initial frustrations. I couldn't have asked for a better server.

input:
I love it!  The reviews were great and I was desperate for good carry out, so we decided to try Pizzaville (is anyone else picturing JT singing - Bring it on down to Pizzaville?).  The prices are a bit high, but the quality of the food is great!  The pizza crust is between a hand tossed and thin crust.  Perfectly crunchy ends and just chewy enough in the middle.  Good quality cheese and tangy tomato sauce. I ordered it with just mushrooms and they put on a lot!   I also asked for heavy sauce.  They put extra sauce on the pizza and even gave me an extra container of sauce in case I needed more. 

I can't decide which was better, the pizza or "breadsticks."  I say "breadsticks" because they were really more like garlic bread strips.  So buttery and garlicy, they were great even without sauce.  I'm ashamed to say I ate nearly the entire order myself.  

The employees are very nice and helpful.  The store is clean. I need to go back and try their lunch buffet.
Rewrite this for me:
I'm absolutely thrilled! After reading rave reviews, my craving for good takeout got the better of me, and so my friends and I decided to give Pizzaville a shot (anyone else picturing JT singing - "Bring it on down to Pizzaville?"). The prices were a tad on the higher side, but the food quality more than made up for it! The pizza crust had the perfect balance between hand-tossed and thin crust - delightfully crispy at the edges and satisfyingly chewy in the center. The cheese was of good quality and the tomato sauce had a tangy kick to it. I opted for mushrooms as my toppings, and boy, they generously loaded up the pizza with them! On top of that, I requested extra sauce, and they went the extra mile by providing an additional container of sauce, just in case I needed more.

Now, I'm torn between deciding which was more delicious, the pizza or the delectable "breadsticks." Well, I say "breadsticks" because they resembled more of garlicky bread strips. So flaky, buttery, and packed with garlic flavor, they turned out to be a great treat even without any sauce. I must admit with a tinge of embarrassment that I devoured almost the entire order by myself.

The employees at Pizzaville were incredibly friendly and helpful, and the store itself was well-maintained. I definitely need to make a return visit and give their lunch buffet a try.

I really enjoyed the atmosphere at the restaurant. The modern and cozy decor created a pleasant vibe. However, the lighting was suitable for dinner but not great for taking selfies, haha. Our waiter was alright, but he seemed overly energetic and impatient. It felt like he was rushing to take care of us rather than sincerely trying to provide a memorable experience.

As for the food, I ordered the Shrimp Breaux Bridge, which was quite tasty. It wasn't exceptional, but it was good. My friend had the Balsamic Salmon, which was also enjoyable. Despite my mixed experience with the service, I would give the restaurant another chance because I'm confident that the service is usually better. Plus, I've heard wonderful things about the menu.

input:
Despite being a spin-off at the burgers from Rouge, I actually think that the burgers here are, dare I say it, better then flagship restaurants.
Over the last year they keep expanding their burger and toppings options by editing the little placard next to the registers, instead of changing their giant menuboard every time  they decide to add a new cheese or vegetable you can put on the burger.

I've been here a few times, trying the 500 (lettuce, bacon, cheddar, special sauce) delicious, and also making my own combos with their Kobe Beef burger (I think its worth the extra few bucks). I like it with truffle cheese and grilled onions. The brioche bun also really makes these burgers something special.

Their fries are also extremely delicious. As a huge fan of truffle oil, I can never resist getting their truffle oil fries. When they come warm out of the fryer, coated in truffle oil, there is just no better taste known to man.

Most important of all, they are open late on weekends.

I have also created my own combinations using their Kobe Beef burger (which I believe is worth the extra cost). Most importantly, they have late-night hours on weekends, which is a key factor for me.

input:
We've been going to the Rib Cook-Off for a few years now, but apparently I've never taken the time to review it. We have our day pretty much planned out before heading down there. 

We walk to the bus stop by our house, the bus takes us directly to the Sparks bus station for a whopping $2 each. No parking, no driving through crowds, and no paying for parking. Winning.

From the bus station, we head immediately to Great Basin to get a large Icky and Bitchin' Berry. Beer is a must for battling these crowds and the large beers are worth the price!

If you have the JA Nugget mobile app, it will tell you where every vendor is and show it on a map. No more mindless wandering looking for your favorite vendor. I don't have a favorite, but go off of recommendations from friends, co-workers, etc.

Some vendors take cards, but we always make sure to bring plenty of cash. 

Be sure to walk through the non-rib vendors too. We got a couple of hats this year, which are nice to have at the event, but are also great beach hats for next year.

Saturday was a whole day affair and required us taking a cab back home. But because there was practically no crowd on Monday, we were able to get a beer, some food, and still use our bus transfer to get back home. Food stops being served at 5:00 pm on Monday and the vendors also start selling off extra food at crazy cheap prices.

To avoid any hassle, we walk to the bus stop near our house. For a reasonable fee of $2 each, the bus takes us directly to the Sparks bus station. This eliminates the need for parking, navigating through crowds, and paying for parking. It's definitely a win.

Once we arrive at the bus station, our first stop is always Great Basin. We can't resist grabbing a large Icky and Bitchin' Berry. It's crucial to have a beer to combat the large crowds, and the large beers are worth every penny!

If you have the JA Nugget mobile app, it's incredibly helpful. It provides information on the location of every vendor and displays it on a map. No more aimless wandering while searching for your favorite vendor. Personally, I don't have a favorite, so I rely on recommendations from friends, co-workers, and others.

Although some vendors accept cards, we always make sure to bring plenty of cash.

Don't forget to explore the non-rib vendors too. We ended up buying a couple of hats this year, which not only added to the enjoyment of the event but will also make great beach hats for next year.

On Saturday, we dedicated the whole day to the Rib Cook-Off and had to take a cab back home. However, Monday was much less crowded. We were able to enjoy a beer, indulge in some food, and still use our bus transfer to return home. It's worth noting that food stops being served at 5:00 pm on Monday, and vendors sell off any leftover food at incredibly low prices.

input:
Excellent food and bar. Slow service.

A friend and I stopped here during an evening of bar hopping in the CBD. We were seated promptly and given our menus, which are half-French, half-English. Not a big deal for anyone who can read French and/or has been living in Louisiana for a reasonable amount of time, but definitely something tourists should be wary of. I didn't have any alcohol because I was the designated driver, but I can say that their drink menu is extensive, and the bar was packed from the moment we arrived until the moment we left. 

This restaurant's biggest strength is it's food. I tasted their crab bisque, and had Poulet Grand-Mère as my entrée. Both were excellent. The latter arrived in a wide cast-iron bowl, which I'm sure has a more proper name, but was an interesting touch nonetheless.

The service was why I gave this restaurant 4/5 instead of 5/5. Most of the wait staff seemed to be interns from culinary school. The handful we dealt with were very friendly, but would do well to be a little more attentive. For example, the server who brought us our desserts ran off before we could ask for spoons to eat the dessert with. 

In summary, a good dining experience, but I think I would rather continue exploring new restaurants in the area before returning.
Rewrite this for me:
The food and bar at this establishment are excellent. However, the service was slow. 

During a night of bar hopping in the CBD, a friend and I decided to stop here. We were seated promptly and handed menus that were in both French and English. While this wasn't an issue for those familiar with either language or the Louisiana culture, it could potentially confuse tourists. As the designated driver, I didn't have any alcohol, but I noticed that their drink selection was extensive and the bar was always packed.

The highlight of this restaurant is undoubtedly the food. I had the pleasure of trying their crab bisque and the Poulet Grand-Mère as my main course, and both dishes were excellent. The latter was served in a wide cast-iron bowl, which I'm sure has a more proper name. Nevertheless, it added a unique touch to the dining experience.

However, the service was the aspect that prevented me from giving this restaurant a perfect score. It seemed that most of the wait staff were interns from culinary school. Although they were friendly, they could have been more attentive. For instance, when our desserts arrived, the server quickly ran off before we could request spoons to enjoy our sweet treats.

In conclusion, it was a good dining experience, but I feel inclined to explore other restaurants in the area before considering a return visit.

input:
Came here for Sunday brunch and walked away with a very full belly and a good buzz! 

Their brunch buffet includes tons of seafood, an omelet station, pasta bar, carving station, custom sushi rolls, fresh fruit, salads, and the usually breakfast foods you'd expect at a buffet. I almost forgot dessert...an entire side of the room is dedicated to a table full of desserts AND a chocolate fountain. The brunch price also include bottomless mimosas which were literally bottomless. Our server never let us empty our glasses and  the mimosas were very heavy on the champagne, so we all got a bit tipsy. At least the alcohol let us forget how much weight we gained during this meal.

As if the buffet spread wasn't enough, they also have an a la carte menu with small dishes. The choices included Belgian waffles, french toast, blintzes, Mahi, and a few other savory dishes.  You can order as many of these items as you want, as many times as you want. Our server was sure to remind us of this, she seemed to enjoy watching how gluttonous our table was! 

Unfortunately we were here during Tropical Storm Debby, so we didn't get to enjoy a beautiful view of the bay, Although, being here while the weather was so awful was very cozy with the fireplace and wood interior. Thanks to the weather it wasn't crowded either, so don't write this place off on account of bad weather. 

At $35 a person, the Sunday brunch seems pricey, but if you have no qualms about overeating and overdrinking, you'll definitely get your money's worth.
