input:
I've been to Mount Laurel's On the Border over 50 times. I used to go to Don Pablo's but I fell in love with On the Border's chips and salsa (their chips are nice and salty, and their salsa is a little spicier).

When I go, 90% of the time I just sit at the bar and drink beer and snack on their chips and salsa. The beer specials are pretty good but could be a little better- weekdays has a happy hour as well as a late night happy hour too.

When I do dine, I often just enjoy a variety of vegetarian sides. Lately, I've grown to enjoy their cheese enchiladas, which I find delicious. Service when dining is usually great.

As for the bartenders, it's really hit-or-miss. Joann is probably my favorite- she's friendly, attentive, funny, and I've really gotten to know her, and I'd give them 5 stars if my experience was with her alone. There is a bartender named Nikki though, and if she's there, I always get the worst service. She barely checks on me/us to see how we're doing, she seems unfriendly, if she actually comes to refill your chips then she will not refill your salsa, she has taken my beer and refilled it without asking (when I was done and trying to leave), and I've had to wait forever to ask her for my check. At least twice, I've had to ask other bartenders to bring my check so that I could finally close out and leave. I'd give them 1 star if my experience was based on her alone.

Overall, good appetizers, cold beer, moderate prices, and usually good service.

When I do decide to dine, I usually opt for a variety of vegetarian sides. Lately, I have discovered a newfound love for their cheese enchiladas, which I find incredibly delicious. The service during my dining experiences is generally excellent.

However, the quality of service from the bartenders can be inconsistent. Among them, Joann stands out as my favorite. She is friendly, attentive, funny, and I have developed a good rapport with her. If my experiences were solely based on her service, I would give them a five-star rating. On the other hand, Nikki, another bartender, consistently provides the worst service. She rarely checks on us, appears unfriendly, neglects to refill salsa when refilling chips, has taken away my empty beer without asking, and I often have to wait excessively to request my check. I have even had to ask other bartenders to bring my check on a couple of occasions just to settle my bill and leave. If my experiences were solely based on Nikki's service, I would rate them one star.

Overall, On the Border offers good appetizers, cold beer, reasonable prices, and usually satisfactory service.

input: Delicious food, sub-par service. I stopped into this dessert bar today to grab some dessert and a coffee to-go. While everyone seemed to be very helpful, or at least wanting to be, I'm not sure I received the best possible service. I ordered two slices of cake, one marshmallow chocolate and one cheesecake. Both were DELICIOUS, but it seemed like I waited forever to receive these, and when i did, it was in a cute but inefficient manner. The to-go boxes were stacked one on top of the other, with a loosely tied string around them. While I admire the aesthetics here, I would have much preferred a bag. Though, the worst part of my experience was the barista. I ordered an iced coffee with milk and sugar. First, he put ice in the cup and filled it halfway with coffee. He then asked me to pick and put in my own sugars from a cup of packets as he stated "I wouldn't know what and how much you want, I only drink my coffee black." As I considered this incompetent statement, i expected him to then put more hot coffee in to help the sugar dissolve. But no, he proceeded to fill the rest of the HALF OF THE CUP with milk. And then handing me the drink he told me I'd better stir it to mix the cream and sugar in. Not sure why I'd paid such a high price to practically make my own half-coffee half-mild beverage, I simply smiled and walked away. I ended up throwing out the drink as I could hardly even taste the coffee and I'm not too fond of a lot of milk in my coffee. Nonetheless, the cakes were delicious, and I will be coming back with the hopes that this new business is still in the process of improving itself.

input:
I visited Joe's on consecutive nights, one with a Living Social coupon.  The beef tacos on the appetizer menu were outstanding, and a great price which will ensure I order them every time I come.  Meatloaf and mashed potatoes were just as I expected; thankfully, no attempt to "fancy them up"; just tasty comfort food.  I asked for French dressing and bleu cheese crumbles on my salad, and they were generous with the cheese.  The salad was cold and fresh and crisp.

The reason I did not give five stars was the service. The first night, we weren't told of specials (ugh, saw them on the way out and would have ordered them!), and my friend's appetizer order was wrong. Drinks were not refilled often enough, and the waitress seemed uninformed about some of the items.  The next night, different waitress. We were one of only two tables, and still waited too long for her to return. She was unable to answer a question about a menu item, as well.

The place is beautiful, and the bathroom was clean and bright.  The menu offers many thoughtfully composed choices. Some of your servers are not up to par.
Rewrite this for me:
I went to Joe's two nights in a row, using a Living Social coupon for one of the visits. The beef tacos on the appetizer menu were absolutely delicious and reasonably priced, which guarantees that I will order them every time I go. The meatloaf and mashed potatoes were exactly what I expected, no attempt to make them fancy, just comforting and flavorful. I requested French dressing and bleu cheese crumbles on my salad and they were very generous with the cheese. The salad was fresh, crisp, and served at the perfect cold temperature.

However, I cannot give this place a five-star rating due to the service. On the first night, we were not informed about any specials (we saw them on our way out and regretted not being able to order them) and my friend's appetizer order was incorrect. Our drinks were not refilled frequently enough and our waitress seemed to lack knowledge about some of the menu items. The next night, we had a different waitress. Despite being one of only two tables, we still had to wait an unreasonable amount of time for her to return. She also couldn't answer a question about one of the menu items.

The restaurant itself is beautiful and the bathroom was clean and well-lit. The menu offers a wide range of carefully crafted options. However, some of the servers are not up to the expected standard.

input:
Food is excellent!
People are welcoming, choices are long list. Sandwiches have great meat in them. Hand made toasted ravioli is some of the best in town.
Rewrite this for me: The food is absolutely amazing! The people here are incredibly welcoming, and the menu offers an extensive selection of choices. The sandwiches are packed with exceptionally delicious meats. And let's not forget about the handcrafted toasted ravioli, which is widely regarded as some of the finest in town.

input: With all the talk of bbq tips, sweetie pie, etc of St. Louis...I decided to try this place after flying in. The customer service was great, they make their own BBQ sauce which is between a sweet, tangy with pinch of spice. It could be considered overpowering if not used to it. The pull pork sandwich was recommended along with beans and Cole slaw. Again, this could be too much for one who has never tried it and/or intake this type of food on a daily basis.
Rewrite this for me: After hearing so much about the barbecue, sweet treats, and other specialties of St. Louis, I made up my mind to give this place a shot right after my flight. I must say, the customer service was exceptional. They take pride in their homemade BBQ sauce, which strikes a perfect balance between sweetness, tanginess, and a hint of spice. However, it might come across as overpowering for those not accustomed to such flavors. The pulled pork sandwich, along with a side of beans and coleslaw, was highly recommended. It's important to note that for someone who has never tried this cuisine before or isn't accustomed to regularly consuming such rich food, this could be quite an overwhelming experience.

input: They call a chicken salad sandwich two cubes of chicken with mayo in it and a salad with a salad that is a bowl Of lettuce a salad? Hmm left here hungry....
Rewrite this for me: The dish they refer to as a chicken salad sandwich consists of merely two chicken cubes mixed with mayo, alongside a bowl of lettuce. And they have the audacity to call that a salad! Curiously, I'm still feeling famished after encountering such a meal.

input:
We had a very nice brunch here. The food was consistently quite good and the service was pretty efficient and courteous. The omelets were sumptuous, the beverages fun (including a bloody mary bar.. we did have to ask for fresh bacon as it had run out). 

I did the budget breakfast which hit the spot with scrambled eggs, roaster taters, and a sweet muffin. The fish tacos were also good. Nice al fresco dining on the patio.
Rewrite this for me: Our brunch experience at this establishment was incredibly enjoyable. The quality of the food remained consistently high, and the service we received was efficient and polite. The omelets were incredibly delicious, and we had a great time trying out different beverages, including the option of creating our own bloody mary at the bar. However, we did have to request fresh bacon as it had unfortunately run out. I opted for the budget breakfast, which consisted of satisfying scrambled eggs, flavorful roasted potatoes, and a delightful sweet muffin. Additionally, the fish tacos were tasty. The patio offered a pleasant outdoor dining experience.

input: I would eat anything they served me. I haven't even had the pancakes yet and I'm sold. The line out the front door and down the sidewalk should be an indication that this place is awesome. I just had basic hashbrowns eggs and bacon, but it was so fab and the service was great! I will definitely go back and sit down to eat. Rewrite this for me: I am willing to try any dish that they offer. I haven't had the opportunity to taste the pancakes yet, but I am already convinced. The long line extending from the front door and down the sidewalk is a clear indication of how amazing this place is. Although I only had basic breakfast items like hashbrowns, eggs, and bacon, they were absolutely fantastic and the service was excellent! I am definitely planning to revisit and dine in. Finding parking might be a bit challenging in that area, but it is to be expected.

input: I just got C & B's via Order Up Delivery Svc and what a perfect wintry in home dinner. I ordered the Swanky Frank w/ fries and completely enjoyed my loaded up frank. Rewrite this for me: I recently received a delightful winter dinner at home from C & B's through Order Up Delivery Svc. It was an absolute win! I had the pleasure of enjoying their delicious Swanky Frank with a side of fries. The frank was loaded with toppings and incredibly satisfying. The fries had a nice seasoning that added an extra touch of flavor. As a lover of chili, I couldn't resist ordering a large bowl of their beef chili from a renowned chili house. input: Great rich food,  but a lil bit pricey.  Everything tastes wonderful but nothing stays the same the menu is always changing.  The most unique donuts you will find.

input:
After visiting with friends and indulging in lots of tastes, consider this my next order at Livery:

(03) The Red Drum - it's a lovely fish dish, and it's a way to get a taste of the yuca fries.

Rewrite this for me:
After a delightful time catching up with friends and enjoying a variety of delectable flavors, here's what I highly recommend ordering at Livery:

1. To begin, try the Carriage House Margarita with its unique brandy twist.
2. Indulge in all the empanadas without any guilt or reservations because they are absolutely irresistible.

Feel free to replicate my order during your visit.

input:
My son and I went in for burgers after a long day's drive returning him to Nashville for the upcoming semester. We were in need of immediate sustenance after a long fast. What we found was a busy place that actually knew how to operate with a full house. Our need were quickly satisfied with courteous and reasonably priced service. 

Since we were just two, we were quickly seated. We started off with a couple Highland stouts. It was a nice drink and at a reasonable price. Before our entree, we shared a large garden salad. It was fresh and flavorful. The dressing was a bit on the heavy side for a vinaigrette. 

For entrees, I had the Black and Blue burger with fries. The burger was just incredible. It was perfectly cooked. The blue cheese was not overpowering. The bun was soft and fresh. The side of regular fries were crisp and lightly salted. Even better, they went perfectly with the homemade ketchup. I'm not a fan of ketchup, but theirs is very nice since they seem to avoid adding too much sweetness. My son had a basic burger with sweet potato fries. I tried the sweet potato fries and think they might be some of the best I've ever eaten. The burger looked as good as mine and my son concurred. 

The burger was well made and consumed within minutes. No words were spoken as we ate. Always a good sign. We shall return.
Rewrite this for me:
After a tiring day of driving my son back to Nashville for his upcoming semester, we decided to stop by a burger joint to satisfy our immediate hunger. To our surprise, the place was bustling with activity yet efficiently managed to handle the crowd. We were swiftly seated since we were only a party of two. 

To kick off our meal, we opted for a couple of Highland stouts, which not only tasted great but also came at a reasonable price. Prior to our main course, we shared a generous portion of garden salad that was refreshingly delicious. However, the vinaigrette dressing seemed a bit heavy-handed.

For our entrees, I selected the Black and Blue burger with fries, and let me tell you, it was absolutely outstanding. Cooked to perfection, the burger struck a perfect balance with its blue cheese topping. The bun was soft and fresh, and the regular fries served on the side were crispy and lightly salted. What impressed me even more was their homemade ketchup, which wasn't overly sweet like most others. I'm not usually a fan of ketchup, but theirs had a nice balance. On the other hand, my son ordered a basic burger accompanied by sweet potato fries. I couldn't resist trying the sweet potato fries, and I must say, they were possibly the best I've ever had. The burger looked just as mouthwatering as mine, and my son wholeheartedly agreed.

Silently, we devoured our delicious burgers within minutes, a clear sign of satisfaction. We left the place already planning our return visit.

input: Nothing more to say than this is the BEST donut place ever. I literally wished they shipped their products. When I moved to Florida, I missed it so much. It's only in New Orleans... sad face!
Rewrite this for me: There is really nothing else to say except that this donut place is absolutely the greatest. I genuinely wished that they offered shipping services for their delectable treats. When I relocated to Florida, how I longed for it! Regrettably, it is exclusively located in New Orleans... what a bummer!

input: Katie's is a neighborhood restaurant that has existed in one form or another for a few generation.  It's classic New Orleans fare with an Italian-American slant.  Great meatballs.  You'll see all types of classic New Orleans old people dinging before 8pm.   You won't be disappointed if your expectations aren't too high.

It's common to spot traditional New Orleans locals, especially older individuals, dining at Katie's before 8pm. While it's important not to set excessively high expectations, you can trust that your dining experience at Katie's will be satisfying.

input: Excellent service! They were super fast, friendly and professional.  This is now my go to place for oil changes

input:

input: This place should be on Restaurant Impossible. It's run down, the decor is tacky, beaten up, miss-matched and cheap. It's really dark...probably to hide how dingy it is. Everything was sticky. I ordered a burger medium and got a charred, tasteless hockey puck. My mom and aunt got the baked crab soup, which before we ordered, we misheard each other and called it baked crap soup. It turned out to be a better description. The crab stuffed mushrooms were heavy on the stuff and light on the crab.  The servers were super nice though.
Rewrite this for me: This establishment is in dire need of a Restaurant Impossible intervention. The overall appearance is dilapidated, with tacky, worn-out, and low-quality decor. The dim lighting probably serves to conceal its dinginess. To make matters worse, everything feels sticky to the touch. My order for a medium burger resulted in receiving a charred, flavorless hockey puck. Meanwhile, my mom and aunt decided to try the baked crab soup, which we mistakenly referred to as baked crap soup prior to ordering. Unfortunately, our initial misinterpretation was surprisingly accurate. The crab stuffed mushrooms were disappointingly heavy on fillings and lacking in abundant crab meat. Despite these flaws, it's worth noting that the servers were exceptionally friendly.

input:
What can I say?  I'm a sucker for new american.  The owner is a very nice gentleman who really enjoys food.  

The service was impeccable and the food was Ridiculously good.  We ordered a mixed berry waffle, huevo rancho, traditional breakfast bagel with grits, and best sandwich with fresh fruits.  

I highly recommend the huevo rancho and best sandwich.  The grits was very good as well. 

If you decide to visit this restaurant, say hi to the owner.  He's a great guy.

I have to admit, I have a weakness for new American cuisine. The owner of this restaurant is an absolute delight who truly has a passion for food.

The service at this place was flawless, and the food, oh my! It was simply outstanding. We tried a variety of dishes, including a delectable mixed berry waffle, the mouthwatering huevo rancho, a classic breakfast bagel with grits, and the best sandwich, accompanied by fresh fruits.

I strongly recommend the huevo rancho and the best sandwich, they were both exceptional. The grits were also superb.

Should you choose to dine at this restaurant, don't forget to say hello to the owner. He is truly a remarkable individual.

input: Great place for happy hour. Oysters were deLISH! My friend and I had 2 dozen and we had some cocktails! The riverbend and champagne au poir we quite tasty. I had a side of fries and she had a side a grits. Best grits I've eaten. Definitely coming back. The server was great too. Just the right amount of attention!
Rewrite this for me: This place is amazing for happy hour! The oysters were absolutely delicious. My friend and I devoured 24 of them along with some delightful cocktails. The Riverbend and Champagne au Poir were particularly tasty. I opted for a side of fries while my friend enjoyed a side of grits, which were the best I've ever tasted. Without a doubt, we will be returning. On top of the amazing food and drinks, the server provided just the perfect amount of attention.

input:
The crew at Bella Vista Designs are FABULOUS.  From start to finish, they are professional, conscientious, and innovative (and affordable!).  They never cease to amaze me with their can-do attitude and absolutely gorgeous and creative design.

input: Moved to Tucson and needed a new dentist, everything went great here!

input:
Couldn't say it better than the below poster. Excellent food, service and prices.

Located where Mugshots used to be (RIP), one of my coworkers had been raving about this place, in particular the falafel and of course the very kind owner.

Went with my pre-wife and we shared beef gyro (carved) pita, falafel pita and hummus plate. Everything was extremely fresh (I concur on the crisp lettuce) well seasoned and just plain delicious.  A lot of food as well and complimentary baklava. We took our leftovers home (I wrapped the two remaining bites of my gyro - it's that good)

I highly recommend this place and you'll definitely walk out with a smile. I think this spot is still relatively unknown and I very rarely post reviews. This is a unique spot to Manayunk and I will be referring all of my friends as I really want the restaurant to succeed - because the owner deserves it and of course for my selfish appetite!
Rewrite this for me:
I couldn't agree more with the previous reviewer. The food, service, and prices at this place are excellent. It's located where Mugshots used to be, and one of my coworkers had been talking non-stop about it, especially praising the falafel and the friendly owner.

I went there with my partner and we decided to share the beef gyro pita, falafel pita, and hummus plate. Everything was incredibly fresh, well-seasoned, and simply delicious. The portions were generous, and they even gave us complimentary baklava. We had leftovers, and I loved the gyro so much that I made sure to save the last two bites.

I highly recommend this place. It's still relatively unknown, and I rarely write reviews, but it's such a gem in Manayunk that I want it to succeed. The owner deserves it, and of course, I want to keep satisfying my own appetite.

input: Great food and excellent service. Only knock I would give them was they brought out our entrees about 10 minutes after our apps came so we were still eating that, otherwise great experience
Rewrite this for me: The food was fantastic and the service was outstanding. The only minor issue we had was that our entrees arrived about 10 minutes after our appetizers, while we were still finishing them. Apart from that, our overall experience was excellent.

input:
This is a very mediocre place.  The location itself is in the same dirty strip mall as Mozzarella Pizza. The inside has that "we don't really care about the looks" feel to it.  It's not dirty, per se.  It just doesn't look very clean.  Everything looks like its falling apart.  It probably gets its business from suburbanites like me craving what we think of as Chinese food.

All that said, the food I had was palatable.  Nothing outstanding or amazing: it was just all right.  I won't recommend against it, but it's nothing that you would think of as that great either.
Rewrite this for me:
This place can be considered average at best. Its location is in a shabby strip mall alongside Mozzarella Pizza. The interior has an indifference towards aesthetics, not necessarily dirty, but lacking cleanliness. The place gives off a dilapidated vibe, seemingly attracting suburbanites like myself who have a craving for what we perceive as Chinese cuisine.

With that being said, the food I tried was acceptable. It neither stood out nor amazed me; it was simply decent. I wouldn't discourage you from trying it, but it's not something you would consider exceptionally great either.

input: Phenomenal place to eat. I has the Hickory burger, that was so damn delicious!! Will be coming back for sure!!!
Rewrite this for me: This place is absolutely amazing for dining. I tried their Hickory burger, and it was incredibly delicious! I am definitely planning on returning in the future!

input: After having been here, I would say that the food had great flavors for the taste buds and it was a unique experience.  Our server, Brian was no doubt a foodie... I've never seen anyone get so excited about food and discuss the ingredients in such detail with so much passion.  The food really was different and had unbelievable flavor.  Anyone who calls themselves a foodie should try this place.  I'm thinking they would be pleased with this place.  But, the portions were small.  And I really didn't like the interior of the restaurant.  I'm more of a booths girl.  Booths can be classy, you know?  All in all, I would say this was an interesting place and I would come back, but the dishes were too complicated for me to want to come back beyond once a year.  Speaking of timing, the chefs change the menu every year.  And these guys really are good at what they do.  The owners actually own the Red Pony and two other restaurants all on the same street!  And they're all doing well.
Rewrite this for me:
Having experienced this place, I must say the food was bursting with incredible flavors that tantalized the taste buds. It was truly a unique dining experience. Our server, Brian, was undoubtedly a passionate food enthusiast. I have never witnessed someone so genuinely excited and knowledgeable about every ingredient, discussing them in great detail. The cuisine was truly distinct and packed with unbelievable flavors. Any self-proclaimed foodie should definitely give this place a try as I believe they would be thoroughly impressed.

However, I must mention that the portions were on the smaller side. Additionally, I personally did not fancy the interior of the restaurant. I have a preference for booths, as they can exude a certain level of class. All things considered, I found this place quite interesting and would be willing to return. Though I must admit, the complexity of the dishes may prevent me from coming back more than once a year. Speaking of timing, the chefs change the menu yearly, displaying their exceptional skills. Interestingly, the owners not only own this establishment but also the Red Pony and two other restaurants on the same street, all of which are thriving.

input:

Food- tasty and lots of options.  Not fancy.  Very affordable.  

Family of four for about 30$.  That's a great deal w today's prices. 

If you are looking for a fast, casual Asian option, give this place a try.
Rewrite this for me:
There has been a significant improvement since my last visit, particularly with the service. A kid named Dillon provided excellent service during my visit.

The ambiance is quite laid-back and casual. You simply place your order and then sit back as they bring the food to you.

The food is both flavorful and provides a wide range of options. It's not fancy but very reasonably priced. A family of four can enjoy a meal here for around $30, which is a fantastic deal considering today's prices.

If you're seeking a quick and casual Asian dining experience, I highly recommend giving this place a try.

input: Use the yelp app to get on the waiting list, we went on a Saturday morning and it was very busy, but the waiting list was cut down significantly by using the app. The menu is expansive, a lot of options. The cinnamon French toast was very good. The traditional breakfast foods were on par with most breakfast joints, but the extras on the menu can keep you busy for many visits trying new things. The strawberry orange juice was excellent so I recommend trying it. It was a little hot in the restaurant, could have been cooled down a lot for a more comfortable experience. The service was very good. There were two places to pay at the counter which I thought was a nice way to speed up the leaving process.
Rewrite this for me: To optimize your wait time, I highly recommend utilizing the Yelp app to secure a spot on the waiting list. When we visited on a bustling Saturday morning, the app significantly reduced our waiting time. The variety of options on the menu is extensive, catering to various preferences. The cinnamon French toast particularly stood out as a delicious choice. While the traditional breakfast fare met the standards expected at most breakfast joints, the additional items on the menu offer endless opportunities to try new things, making repeat visits worthwhile. I must also mention the exceptional strawberry orange juice, which I highly recommend sampling. On the downside, the restaurant was a bit too warm, and adjusting the temperature to provide a more comfortable dining experience would have been appreciated. Nevertheless, the service received was top-notch. Additionally, the availability of two payment counters was a clever way to streamline the process of leaving the establishment.

input:

Same vibe as my old Barber Shop in Philly. 
Big TV in the waiting area. Plush couch to relax in. Young lady checking me in asked if I wanted water, soda or a beer.
Beer? Need I say more. 

Great cut. Great bunch of guys discussing current events, sports, and what's happening around town.
Found my new spot. 

Will be back.

Not only did I get a great haircut, but there was also a friendly group of guys engaging in interesting conversations about current events, sports, and local happenings. I've definitely found my new go-to spot. 

I'll definitely be coming back.

input: Not only was the food excellent, but the people here are beyond nice-and genuine. I had eggs Benedict. The poached eggs were good but the toast they were sitting on was excellent. We were given a cream pancakes to taste test by our awesome server, Tina. I can honestly say it was the best pancake I've ever tasted. So full of flavour-vanilla, and soft aa pillow. I ordered eggs Benedict, and while the poached eggs were good, the toast they were served on was truly outstanding. Our amazing server, Tina, offered us a sample of their delicious cream pancakes. I can honestly say it was the most delicious pancake I have ever had. Bursting with vanilla flavor and incredibly soft, they practically melted in my mouth. I didn't even need to use syrup. Absolutely stellar!

input: Great service. My husband ordered a cheese and bacon burger and I got the crawfish sausage por bo both well made and great tasting.
Rewrite this for me: The service was exceptional. My husband opted for a mouth-watering cheese and bacon burger, while I indulged in a perfectly crafted and delicious crawfish sausage poor boy.

input: Had a wonderful experience with JT and Ashley Furniture store!! He was helpful even when I had to change my order.
Rewrite this for me: My experience with JT and Ashley Furniture store was absolutely fantastic! JT provided excellent assistance throughout the entire process, even when I needed to make changes to my order.

input:
While at Drexel University, I decided to try a new food truck and go for something that wasn't the typical food truck.  My girlfriend and I always noticed this place was crowded around lunch but never knew why.  After being recommended to try it by a friend, we decided to go ahead and order lunch here.  Cucina Zapata is at the end of the food truck row at the center of Drexel University's campus.  The truck has a graffiti style design which can be easily distinguished from the other food trucks here.

I decided to order (2) thai short rib tacos while my girlfriend got the cap'n crunch tilapia burrito.  The food has a good visual appearance which made us more eager to eat it once we got inside the building.  I really enjoyed the thai short rib tacos even though they put hot sauce on it.  They were definitely better than the typical taco bell food and left me with a 5 star review feeling inside.  My girlfriend also really enjoyed her burrito.

Overall, this food truck provides very good food at a good price.  I recommend this place to anyone looking for a good lunch.
Rewrite this for me:
During my time at Drexel University, I decided to step out of my comfort zone and try a unique food truck. One truck in particular caught my attention, as it always seemed to have a bustling crowd during lunchtime. Intrigued by its popularity, my girlfriend and I took the advice of a friend and decided to give it a shot. Located at the end of the food truck row in the heart of Drexel University's campus, Cucina Zapata stood out with its distinctive graffiti-style design that set it apart from the other trucks.

For our lunch, I opted for two Thai short rib tacos, while my girlfriend went for the unconventional Cap'n Crunch tilapia burrito. The food was visually appealing, and we couldn't wait to dig in once we found a spot inside. Despite the addition of hot sauce, the Thai short rib tacos pleasantly surprised me, surpassing the taste of the typical Taco Bell fare and leaving me with a satisfied five-star review. My girlfriend thoroughly enjoyed her burrito as well.

All in all, Cucina Zapata offers high-quality food at a reasonable price. I highly recommend it to anyone seeking a delicious lunch option.

input: got my haircut here for the first time Jessie Becker took the damaged ends off. She's so sweet and does only what you ask of her. She's also great with kids. come see this place and come see her.

Drop by and see for yourself!

input: Great ramen! I'm really happy to have found this place! The service and food are both wonderful!
Rewrite this for me: This place serves amazing ramen! I am absolutely thrilled to have discovered it. The outstanding service and delightful food are truly impressive!

input: Cute place, nice servers and good food but dish sizes are waaaaay too small. I left unsatisfied. I don't like it when restaurants are cheap with portions, especially neighborly ones!

input: Just recently ate here for the first time. The hype was real. My girlfriend had the Greek Salad while I ordered the Chickpea Vegetarian Pita and they were kind enough to allow for some substitutions. The food was on point and portions were very filling and satisfying. Great staff and environment. Will definitely be back again!

I will definitely make a return visit!

input: First time here. Great bar and restaurant area. Open floor plan with plenty of TV's to watch the game. Attached to their O'Fallon brewery (in Maryland Heights, Missouri, a suburb of St. Louis). They ranked 2nd in the St Louis area last year for volume of beer sold by a micro brewery. Today, I tried the House Special IPA...a wonderful IPA, not too bitter, just right. Look for Troy behind the bar! (The only reason for 4 stars is no desserts....)
Rewrite this for me:
This is my first visit to this place, and I must say it has a fantastic bar and restaurant area. The layout is open and there are plenty of TVs for anyone looking to catch a game. What's even better is that it's attached to their O'Fallon brewery, located in Maryland Heights, Missouri - a suburb of St. Louis. Last year, they secured the 2nd rank in the St Louis area for the highest volume of beer sold by a microbrewery.

Today, I had the pleasure of trying their House Special IPA, and it was truly delightful. It had just the right amount of bitterness, not too overwhelming. If you happen to drop by, make sure to look out for Troy, the bartender. The only reason I'm giving it four stars instead of five is that they don't offer any desserts.

input: This is a neighbourhood dive bar on the eastern part of Whyte Avenue.  It's in a strip mall on a one way eastbound side street.  I was there on a Saturday night to check it out. Very average decor with a couple pool tables and a foosball table. It's definitely a younger crowd here.  They had a band and a doorman.  Drinks were reasonable.  A few tv screens.  The wings are always really cheap and come with a carrot and celery stick.  They make pizzas which looked good and cheesy but I did not try. Servers were quite young and pleasant.  The owner gal behind the bar was fine.  I gave it an extra star because I found the previous review a little harsh.
Rewrite this for me: Located on the eastern side of Whyte Avenue, this establishment qualifies as a local dive bar. Situated within a strip mall on a one-way eastbound side street, I decided to pay it a visit on a Saturday night. The interior boasts a rather average decor, featuring a couple of pool tables and a foosball table. The clientele here tends to lean towards a younger demographic. As I observed, they had a live band performing and a doorman stationed at the entrance. The prices of the drinks were reasonably affordable, with a few television screens scattered throughout the space. One noteworthy aspect was their consistently cheap wings, which were served alongside a carrot and celery stick. I noticed that they also offered pizzas, which appeared appetizingly cheesy, though I refrained from sampling them. The servers were notably young and exhibited a pleasant demeanor, while the owner, a female, managed the bar without any issues. Ultimately, I decided to award an extra star to this establishment, as I found the previous review to be somewhat overly critical.

input:

input: I had a small snafu with the Yelp coupon but after that? Food....and it was excellent.  The chicken caeser salad was great and heavy on the chicken.  The subs were fresh and tasty.   And, yes, they have beer!   But I had an old-fashioned Dr. Brown's cream soda because they have all their flavors.   Nicely located.   Just a mile from the Wagon Wheel flea market.

input: I had an amazingly positive experience here. Dr. Neel and Robin were friendly, knowledgable and exceptionally helpful. input: By far the best breakfast I have had in a while. Huge pancakes. Simple home fries with not all the extras. The owner is super sweet and really generous. Deffinetly a new favorite.

input:
Stayed here with the family for six nights on a trip to the Big Easy. A beautiful and charming place to stay. The staff from the doorman to the wait staff for brunch were  friendly and helpful.  The Carousel Bar is a must. 

Great location, will be going back there for sure next time we are in New Orleans.

With its excellent location, we are definitely planning on staying here again the next time we visit New Orleans.

input: I ordered the chicken stew, it was Tasteless chicken, it was a fried chicken possibly a leftover, that was thrown into a pot and made it into a stew.  If I wanted leftovers, I would have eaten at home.  Gross, still feel like I have to throw up.
Rewrite this for me: I placed an order for chicken stew, but unfortunately, the chicken turned out to be flavorless and seemed like it was fried and leftover before being thrown into the pot. If I wanted to indulge in leftovers, I could have simply eaten at home. It's quite repulsive, and I still feel nauseated.

input:
I've been having a terrible time in St Louis finding a decent Chinese place that is within delivery or easy take out range of our house. This time I tried Wei Hong. I told my partner it can't be any worse than the other mediocre places we have been going. I was wrong.
The take out service was fast for a Sat night. We were there within 20 minutes of ordering and it was ready. But the dining room was empty. For a Sat night that should have been a big clue. The rest of the places in the neighborhood were busy.
The steamed dumplings could have been great. The tasted homemade and the filling was good. However, they were so doughy with a really thick wrapper too thick that it detracted from the good filling. Everything else went downhill from there. 
The beef and broccoli was inedible. The beef had an awful weird texture. Like it was boiled and was gelatinous.  The sauce on it had off flavors. We literally scraped it off our plates and threw the whole thing out.  The meat in both the general Tao's chicken and the orange beef also had weird textures. It was mushy and the coating was thick on those as well. The flavors in the sauces would have been fine, but they were gloopy.  The fried rice was fair but nothing memorable.
We won't be going back.
Rewrite this for me:
I've had a terrible time finding a decent Chinese place in St Louis that's within delivery or easy take out range of our house. So, I decided to give Wei Hong a try this time. I even told my partner that it couldn't be any worse than the other mediocre places we've been going to. Well, turns out I was wrong.

On a positive note, the take out service was fast for a Saturday night. We received our order within 20 minutes and it was ready to go. However, it was concerning to see that the dining room was completely empty. Considering it was a Saturday night, that should have been an indication of the restaurant's quality compared to the other busy places in the neighborhood.

The steamed dumplings had the potential to be great. They tasted homemade and the filling was good. Unfortunately, the dumplings were incredibly doughy with an excessively thick wrapper that took away from the otherwise tasty filling. From that point on, everything went downhill.

The beef and broccoli dish was simply inedible. The beef had a strange, unpleasant texture, almost like it was boiled and had a gelatinous consistency. Additionally, the sauce on it had odd flavors that did not appeal to our taste buds. We ended up scraping it off our plates and throwing the entire dish away. The same strange texture was present in both the general Tao's chicken and the orange beef. The meat was mushy and the coating was too thick. Although the sauces had decent flavors, they were excessively thick and gloopy. The fried rice, on the other hand, was average but not memorable.

All in all, we have no intention of returning to Wei Hong.

input: Big shout out to Cecile for helping us load our plywood as we got ready for IRMA. Thanks so much!
Rewrite this for me: I want to give a huge shoutout to Cecile for assisting us in loading our plywood as we prepared for the incoming hurricane, IRMA. We are extremely grateful for your help!

input: The food was outstanding.  I got chicken tagine, with the delicious tender meat falling off the bone, and carrot salad, flavored with mint and cumin.  Service was good, and the inside of the restaurant is cheerful and well-lit.  Total cost was around $13.
Rewrite this for me: The food was absolutely fantastic. I decided to have the chicken tagine, which consisted of incredibly tender meat that effortlessly fell off the bone, accompanied by a delightful carrot salad flaunting flavors of mint and cumin. The service provided was commendable, and the restaurant's interior exuded a cheerful, well-lit ambiance. The overall cost amounted to approximately $13.

input:
After reading a lot of positive reviews, we were really excited to try this place. We were extremely disappointed in the food. I'm going to give the place the benefit of the doubt that it is not always like this as we came in at 10 PM, but if you cannot offer quality food at that hour then don't have your kitchen open. 
All of our food came out within 5 to 10 minutes of ordering which leads me to believe it was not made fresh. The Caesar salad was room temperature and overdressed. The hush puppies were flavorless, and the chicken wings (3 full wings is a serving) were undercooked and barely warm. The only redeeming food item was the chicken and biscuits, which had a nice flavor profile- the biscuit was again, cold in spots. 

On the positive side the place has a nice hip atmosphere and the service is friendly. 

Unfortunately, the food was so sub par we would not consider dining here again.
Rewrite this for me:
After reading numerous positive reviews, we had high expectations when trying out this place. However, we were greatly disappointed with the food. While I want to give them the benefit of the doubt, considering we arrived at 10 PM, the lack of quality in their dishes at that hour makes me question why their kitchen was open.

To begin with, all of our food arrived within 5 to 10 minutes of ordering, which suggests it wasn't made fresh. The Caesar salad was served at room temperature and had an excessive amount of dressing. The hush puppies lacked flavor, and the chicken wings (which were portioned as three full wings) were undercooked and barely warm. The only saving grace was the chicken and biscuits, which had a pleasant flavor profile, though the biscuit had some cold spots.

On a positive note, the establishment had a cool and trendy atmosphere, and the service was friendly.

Regrettably, the subpar quality of the food alone is enough for us to rule out dining here again.

input: For the time and effort I put into ordering online 30 minutes before my pickup, I was pretty disappointed to skip the long line only to be told they 'didn't have anything' in their system. Thanks for nothing.
Rewrite this for me: I was quite disappointed after spending time and effort to order online 30 minutes prior to my pickup. Instead of having to wait in the long line, I was informed that they had absolutely nothing in their system. This experience was truly underwhelming.

input: If you have not had their cream filled donuts then you simply have not lived, my friend! Incredible! I came to Philly to visit my sister and she brought us here on our second to last day. The cream filled doughnut was so incredible that I drove all the way back here on our way home to get a half dozen of them for the drive back to Michigan! Rewrite this for me: If you haven't tried their cream-filled donuts, your life is incomplete, my friend! These donuts are beyond amazing. input:
STAY AWAY from this place unless you want to possibly be hit by a "drunk gambler "coming from there.  It's no wander this Joe Bob's is never busy.  The only thing that the owners and bartenders care about are the gamblers that get over-served and gamble there daily.   I'm definitely gonna stay away from that part of town after 4ish as that's when the "heavy hitters" come in to support the greasy, dirty, place that really only cares about their gamblers.  The kitchen has some kinda mold issues that literally smells like a sewer plant.  The 2 gals that have made a career outta this dump rely on the drunkards to tip them "big" if they win on the slots.  This is a very sad version of any kinda chicken joint or sports bar.  The greed that the owners share is obvious as flat screens are cheap these days and these guys can't even loosen their hands on the "gambling profit" to invest in to this dump.   Is sad as the original owners did a great job and these new guys don't care about anything except the profit from the slot machines, including the nasty food they serve.  The bartenders are high-strung and anything but friendly, unless of course, you are gambling big and they have a chance at a big tip.  
Your better off going to the fast food chicken joint across the stree t"El Pollo Loco" and guessing the kitchen is cleaner and the staff is friendlier and you won't be subjected to the daily drunks that drive to and from this place daily.  VERY SCARY!!!
Rewrite this for me: I would strongly advise against visiting this establishment unless you are willing to run the risk of encountering an intoxicated gambler leaving the premises. It's not surprising that Joe Bob's is always empty; the owners and bartenders only prioritize the gamblers who frequently overindulge and gamble there. Personally, I will avoid that area after 4pm, as that's when the serious gamblers arrive to support this greasy and unsanitary establishment that shows no concern for its patrons. The kitchen suffers from significant mold issues, emitting a putrid odor reminiscent of a sewage plant. The two women who have made a career out of this dump rely on intoxicated individuals to generously tip them if they win on the slot machines. It's a pitiful excuse for a chicken joint or sports bar. The owners' greed is evident, as they refuse to invest any of their gambling profits into improving the place, even though flat-screen TVs are affordable nowadays. It's truly disheartening to witness the decline of what was once a well-run establishment under the original owners, while these new individuals only care about profiting from the slot machines, disregarding the poor quality of food they serve. The bartenders are constantly on edge and far from friendly, unless, of course, you are a big spender who might provide them with a substantial tip. It would be wiser to visit the fast food chicken joint, "El Pollo Loco," across the street instead, where the kitchen is likely cleaner, the staff friendlier, and you won't have to endure the daily presence of inebriated individuals driving to and from this place. It's a truly unsettling experience.

input:
1st time here. We were headed to Terakawa with the family on a cold Friday night, but they had a line out the door so we went here. Glad we did...

Excellent service & friendly staff. Waitress helped my wife take off her jacket as her hands were full with our baby, as I was tied up with the 3yr old.

I had Chicken Katsu Curry Ramen, Sister had Shrimp Katsu Ramen & Wife had Shoyu Ramen. Everything was excellent, I loved mine. Curry soup was tasty &I the fried chicken was done just right. Same for my sisters shrimp, fried just right with good quality shrimp. My wife lived her Shoyu Ramen.

We also got the pork buns which were excellent, but not your traditional porkbun. 

Great, great experience.
Rewrite this for me:
This was my first time here at this restaurant. Originally, we were planning to go to Terakawa with the family on a cold Friday night, but it was too crowded, so we decided to try this place instead. And I'm really glad we did!

The service here was excellent, and the staff was friendly. The waitress even helped my wife take off her jacket since her hands were full with our baby, while I was busy with our 3-year-old.

As for the food, I had the Chicken Katsu Curry Ramen, my sister had the Shrimp Katsu Ramen, and my wife had the Shoyu Ramen. Everything was fantastic, especially mine. The curry soup had a great taste, and the fried chicken was perfectly cooked. The shrimp in my sister's dish was also fried just right, with high-quality shrimp. My wife absolutely loved her Shoyu Ramen.

We also ordered the pork buns, which were excellent. However, they were not your traditional pork buns.

Overall, it was a truly great experience.

input: Where do I start? Brew D Licious has the very best coffee in town. Hands down. I have tried them all and can say that there isn't another coffee house that even comes close. The minute I met the owner, I knew she was not only very well informed about how to brew a great cup of coffee, but also knows how to make the toughest of customer a repeat patron. This coffee is so good that I buy 5#s at a time from Brigitte. It is always fresh and she has even delivered coffee to me while she is under construction of her new place. Personally, I cannot wait until she opens her new location. I never did care much for the Hollander Hotel and I often felt that she was being stifled by the cramped space she worked in. Also, the hotel has a funky smell (sort of like old socks) so I will be glad when she is at her new location and I can sit and enjoy a good cup of coffee without trying to filter out the bad smell from the hotel. I know it will be a long line at the new location but it will be worth the wait.... Thanks Brigitte for showing St. Petersburg what real coffee tastes and smells like!
Rewrite this for me:
I'm wondering where to start when it comes to finding the best coffee in town. Well, look no further than Brew D Licious! In my quest to try every coffee house in town, none of them even come close to comparing to Brew D Licious. The coffee here is so outstanding that I regularly purchase 5-pound bags from Brigitte. I can always count on it being fresh and delicious. So, having the opportunity to sit and savor a good cup of coffee at Brigitte's new location without battling unpleasant odors feels like a dream.

I anticipate there will be long lines at the new spot, but I'm willing to wait patiently. The experience of tasting and smelling true, high-quality coffee is definitely worth the wait. Thank you, Brigitte, for enlightening St. Petersburg on what real coffee should taste and smell like!

input:

input:
I think I would've given this place a 4/5 star rating if not for the lackluster service and attitude. The entrees were good, the prices were spot on, and the breadsticks were delicious.

Ahh, the breadsticks. This is where the attitude part kicks in. These things are advertised as "as much as you want for free." However, my buddy heads up to the front counter to request enough for our table of three only to be given a hard time from the manager that we're eating more breadsticks than what we ordered. Give me a break. Don't advertise what you don't want to deliver.

Even ordering was a chore. It seemed as if they had a new hire manning the register during the lunch hour rush. She was placing orders as to-go for people looking to dine-in and had to have the manager place orders for her. Not a good idea for a Friday lunch rush.

If this Fazoli's location can improve upon these things minor inconveniences, it'd be a great place to grab a quick bite.
Rewrite this for me:
I would have given this place a 4/5 star rating if it weren't for the disappointing service and attitude. The entrees were tasty, the prices were reasonable, and the breadsticks were absolutely delicious.

Speaking of breadsticks, this is where things went downhill. They boldly advertise them as "unlimited and free," but when my friend asked for more for our table of three, the manager gave him a hard time, claiming we were exceeding our breadstick limit. It's frustrating when they can't fulfill what they promote.

Even the ordering process was a struggle. It seemed like they had a new cashier who was handling takeout orders during the busy lunch rush. She had to rely on the manager to place orders for dine-in customers, which was not a wise choice for a busy Friday afternoon.

If this specific Fazoli's location can address these minor inconveniences, it would definitely be a great spot for a quick and satisfying meal.

input:
was on an errand-running run and remembered how ashamed i was at the state of my car the last time i looked at it - five minutes earlier, as i entered said vehicle.

saw the sign as i was about to turn into riverside plaza to make my groceries and decided it was time.  got the basic $12 tchoup and even though there were about 5 cars in the vacuum line ahead of me, my car was ready before i was done checking out the waiting area.  iguanas, parrots, ms. pac man ($1 a game?  the price of nostalgia, i guess).  not to mention the windows that look out into the auto wash system - which is really entertainment enough for me.  i'm not picky.

but then my number was up and i went out and inspected the results.  still some bird poop remnants on the hood and a few bugs didn't give up the ghost on the grill...maybe i am picky after all.  

don't get me wrong - it was better than nothing (which was what my car got in terms of washings since mid-january), but i'm missing my favorite car wash right about now.  their regular automatic wash with vacuum and window cleaning (i.e. the tchoup treatment) is $14, true, but those dudes are much more thorough with the elbow grease post-assembly line washing.

but that place is in los angeles, alas.  which is perhaps the best gauge of how pricey this place is: 85% as expensive as l.a., but 66.67% the quality.  worth it?  you do the math.  i'ma try a completely touchless system next time.  i reckon i'll get about the same results, but with no parrots or ms. pac-man.
Rewrite this for me:
I was on a quick errand run when I suddenly remembered how embarrassed I felt about the condition of my car when I last saw it, just five minutes ago as I got into the vehicle. As I was about to turn into Riverside Plaza to do some grocery shopping, I noticed a sign and decided it was time to address the issue. I opted for the basic $12 car wash package, called Tchoup. Although there were a few cars ahead of me in the vacuum line, my car was ready before I even finished exploring the waiting area, which had iguanas, parrots, and even a Ms. Pac-Man arcade game (which was priced at $1 per game - a nostalgic treat, I suppose). I was also entertained by the windows that provided a view of the auto wash system. I realized that I'm not too particular about these things.

However, when my turn arrived, I inspected the results and noticed that there were still some traces of bird poop on the hood and a few bugs that stubbornly clung to the grill. Perhaps I am more particular than I thought. Don't get me wrong, it was definitely better than nothing, considering my car hadn't been washed since January. But right now, I find myself longing for my favorite car wash. They offer a regular automatic wash with vacuuming and window cleaning, also known as the Tchoup treatment, for $14. However, those guys pay much more attention to detail and put in extra effort after the automated assembly line process.

Unfortunately, that car wash is located in Los Angeles. It's a great indicator of how expensive this current place is: it costs 85% as much as the one in L.A. but only delivers 66.67% of the quality. Is it worth it? Well, you can do the math. I think I'll try a completely touchless car wash next time. I believe I'll get similar results, but without parrots or Ms. Pac-Man to keep me entertained.

input: Update. The large, live turtle tank has been replaced with a colorful fish aquarium. I don't know what happened to the turtle. Still recommended. Highly.

Rewrite this for me: I have naturally straight hair that looks best when cut with scissors. I specifically asked the hair stylist to cut my hair with scissors, blending it down the side. However, she refused to use scissors and I suggested that I could go somewhere else for a scissor cut. Her response was that she could do it with scissors. Confused, I asked her what she was doing, and she unexpectedly used clippers to cut 90% of my hair. I clearly specified that I did not want my hair cut with clippers, and I would advise you to go to a different salon for your haircut unless you want a high and tight fade using clippers.

input: Excellent food, ambiance and location! I ate there for lunch during this trip to NOLA with my friend. I had the artichoke and crab salad - it was SO good! My mouth waters thinking of it now. My friend ate the grilled and roasted vegetable platter and everyhing was excellent! I highly recommend!
Rewrite this for me: This place has it all - amazing food, great ambiance, and a perfect location! During my visit to New Orleans with a friend, we had the pleasure of dining there for lunch. I decided to try the artichoke and crab salad and it exceeded my expectations - I still salivate just thinking about it. Meanwhile, my friend opted for the grilled and roasted vegetable platter and was equally impressed with every bite. Trust me, this place comes highly recommended!

input: Great lunch recommended by someone at Nashville airport.  Funky eclectic atmosphere. Great and healthy food choices. Sweet potato casserole with coconut and dried cranberry was fantastic.
Rewrite this for me: Someone at Nashville airport highly recommends a fantastic lunch spot with a funky eclectic atmosphere. Not only do they offer great food choices, but they also have healthy options available. One dish that stands out is their sweet potato casserole with a delightful combination of coconut and dried cranberry.

input: Whenever we make the trip over from Orlando.. We usually end up here.  I am a big fan of smaller intimate venues and this one does the trick.  Staff is great and the service is on point.  If you get a table.. request #4.
Rewrite this for me: Every time we visit from Orlando, we consistently find ourselves at this place. I have a strong preference for smaller, cozy venues, and this one certainly fits the bill. The staff is exceptional and the service is exceptional as well. If you're fortunate enough to secure a table, make sure to request #4.

input: Great food, great atmosphere, great service. I've been here twice, and neither was a disappointment. The food is always fantastic (if a bit on the pricey side) - maybe it's because I'm a sucker for Nutella, but the Belgian Waffle topped with Nutella is Heaven for your mouth.
Rewrite this for me: The dining experience at this place is truly exceptional - from the delectable food and inviting atmosphere to the impeccable service. I have had the pleasure of dining here on two occasions, and both visits have exceeded my expectations. The food consistently impresses with its incredible flavors, although it may lean towards the more expensive side. Personally, I cannot resist indulging in their Belgian Waffle smothered in Nutella, as it offers a heavenly sensation for the taste buds.

input:
This is a great late brunch option during the weekends when the big morning rush dies down after 1 pm. Usually there is no wait or 5 minute wait at this time. One big complaint is that they don't have an organized system for seating guests. The servers don't always greet incoming patrons (which should be required Waffle House-style) and they sometimes tell you to seat yourself (which can lead to one or two people taking up tables for 4) or they'll seat you (whenever they get around to talking to you). 

I've ordered a several different dishes at this point and they have varies from ok to awesome. The chicken wings and onion rings are just ok. The wings are either lightly dredged in flour or not at and then fried whole. They aren't really seasoned so the wings are pretty bland. The "onion rings" made of formed, chopped onions that are breaded. The chicken fingers were a bit over battered and dry. The smashwich (or whatever it's called) was pretty good: your choice of breakfast meat with hash browns and eggs in a hoagie roll, but unspectacular. The club sandwich is classic diner fare that is very well executed. The egg and omelette platters are a very good deal and dang tasty. The best thing on the menu is definitely the waffle. It's gently sweet, very crispy and covered in butter. So good!

The service is generally pretty attentive (once you're seated), the restaurant and bathrooms are very clean, the food is a good, tasty value
Rewrite this for me:
This is a fantastic option for a late brunch on the weekends when the morning rush subsides after 1 pm. During this time, there is usually no wait or a short wait of about five minutes. However, a major complaint is the lack of an organized seating system for guests. The servers are not consistent in greeting incoming patrons, which should be a requirement similar to Waffle House. They may either tell you to seat yourself, which sometimes leads to individuals occupying larger tables, or they will seat you whenever they get around to speaking with you.

In terms of the food, I have tried several different dishes and have had varying experiences ranging from decent to excellent. The chicken wings and onion rings fall into the category of just being alright. The wings are either lightly dredged in flour or not at all and then fried whole. However, they lack seasoning, resulting in a rather bland taste. The "onion rings" are made of formed and breaded chopped onions. The chicken fingers were overly battered and dry. On the other hand, the smashwich (or whatever it's called) was quite enjoyable. It consists of your choice of breakfast meat, hash browns, and eggs in a hoagie roll, though it doesn't particularly stand out. The club sandwich, a classic diner dish, is executed exceptionally well. The egg and omelette platters offer great value for the price and are delicious. However, the standout item on the menu is undoubtedly the waffle. It possesses a gentle sweetness, utmost crispiness, and is smothered in butter. It is simply phenomenal.

Regarding the service, once you are seated, it is generally quite attentive. The restaurant and bathrooms are kept very clean, contributing to a pleasant dining experience. Overall, the food provides great value in terms of taste and price.

input:
I would give them 5 but I was disappointed by their reuben.  
For some reason, I have to order reuben if it is a new place and the place has a reuben on their menu. 
but the reuben's rye bread was disappointing considering that companion is all about the bread.  

However, my fiancee's sandwich(forgot the name) with chicken, bacon, avocado on french bread was amazing!

had their spice chicken soup with their corn bread.  It was great! the soup had tons of vegetables and chicken, just the right amount of heat and the corn bread is pretty big and delicious.  

their chi latte was not impressive.. do not get it. lol 

little pricey but, it's a great place to have a wonderful breakfast/lunch and the workers are nice and friendly. 

check this place out, let me know what you guys think.
Rewrite this for me:
I would have given them a rating of 5, but I was disappointed with their reuben sandwich. Usually, whenever I visit a new place that offers a reuben, I feel compelled to order it. However, the rye bread used in their reuben was not up to par, which is surprising considering that the establishment prides itself on its bread.

On the other hand, my fiancee had a sandwich with chicken, bacon, and avocado on French bread, and it was absolutely amazing! I cannot recall the exact name of the sandwich, but it was truly delicious.

I had their spice chicken soup paired with corn bread, and I thoroughly enjoyed it. The soup was packed with flavorful vegetables and chicken, and it had just the right amount of spice. The corn bread itself was sizable and incredibly tasty.

Unfortunately, their chi latte was not impressive at all. I would advise against ordering it. (Laughs)

Although the prices may be a bit high, it is still a fantastic establishment to enjoy a delightful breakfast or lunch. The staff members are also very friendly and accommodating.

I recommend giving this place a try and let me know what you all think!

input:
Probably the best thing about Target is that it isn't Wal Mart.

Target is awesome because it has everything from clothes to toys to electronics to makeup. 

I usually stop in here (if I remember) to pick up my makeup, because it's at least $2-3 cheaper than other stores.  They have a great grocery section and their selection of household items (microwaves, etc.) is fantastic.

They are always good about having enough registers open for the number of shoppers in the place, and I rarely have to wait in a line.
Rewrite this for me:
The main advantage of Target over Wal Mart is probably that it offers a wide variety of products. Target is great because it has an extensive range of items, including clothes, toys, electronics, and makeup.

Whenever I remember, I usually make a quick stop at Target to purchase my makeup, as it is generally priced $2-3 lower compared to other stores. Additionally, they have an excellent grocery section and their selection of household items, such as microwaves, is outstanding.

One thing I really appreciate about Target is that they consistently have enough registers open to accommodate the number of shoppers in the store. Consequently, waiting in line is rarely a concern.

input:
