input:
This is the biggest and best location for HMV in the city. The prices aren't any different from other stores but they do have a larger selection of gifting (figurines,mugs,blankets etc) as well as the largest collection of titles that don't fit into what is new and hot at the moment. Anything that they don't carry can actually be ordered in for you but I have to say staff here are not always the best at phoning customers to let them know when their titles are in so one should definitely keep their number by the phone to check in with them after a week or so.

The biggest selling point for me here besides the selection has to be the staff at the tills. It can get a little busy here but lines are always dealt with quickly and I appreciate that they don't push as hard as other locations to try and sign you up for a pure card. F.Y.I to anybody considering the pure rewards program the redemption items are not that great. It took me about a year of collecting just to accumulate enough points for a true blood key chain and when I got it it was placed in a bubble mailer and not even in it's original packaging. Needless to say when it came time to renew the card I opted out.

Anyways to sum it all up I will say for selection and speedy service these guys get five stars but the prices as well as the sometimes slow ordering process drop it down to a 3. Still worth checking out though if you have been on the hunt at smaller stores for a particular movie or cd.
Rewrite this for me:
This HMV location is the largest and best in the city. While their prices are comparable to other stores, they have a wide selection of gifting options such as figurines, mugs, and blankets. Additionally, they have the largest collection of titles that are not currently popular. If they don't carry something you're looking for, they can order it for you. However, the staff here may not always be reliable in notifying customers when their ordered titles are in, so it's best to keep their contact information handy and follow up after a week or so.

The standout feature for me here is the staff at the checkout counters. Despite the store's busyness, the lines are always handled quickly, and they don't aggressively push customers to sign up for their pure card program like some other locations do. It's worth mentioning that the redemption items in the pure rewards program are not impressive. After a year of collecting points, all I got was a cheap keychain for the TV show "True Blood," which arrived in a bubble mailer and not even in its original packaging. As a result, I chose not to renew my card.

In conclusion, I would give this HMV location a five-star rating for its selection and efficient service. However, the prices and occasionally slow ordering process bring it down to a three-star rating. Still, it's worth visiting if you've been struggling to find a specific movie or CD at smaller stores.

input: Wow is all I have to say. Must try the friend oysters!we ordered that and crawfish bisque and shrimp with grits. All the dishes were delicious. Make sure to make reservation.
Rewrite this for me: I am absolutely amazed, and all I can say is "Wow!" The friend oysters are an absolute must-try! In addition, we also indulged in the delectable crawfish bisque and shrimp with grits. Each dish was beyond delicious. Just a friendly reminder, it's advisable to make a reservation in advance.

input: Was on a mission trying to find the perfect coat for the Holidays. Found my idea of the perfect coat at Burlington but they did not have my size. Went to Target, bought a coat but ended up taking it bath. Was not my dream coat. Next stop Ross. The only coat in my size was a beautiful Bomber style jacket made of pleather. Bought it right before Christmas. Now it's a few days after Christmas and my husband Guy points out to me that the coat is really wrinkled. I go on line and look up every possible hack to get wrinkles out of pleather. They all fail miserably. I just went back to Ross with that coat, no receipt, no tags and asked to speak to the manager. The manager is a young male with dark hair and black framed glasses. I tell him of my plight. He literally says go find what you need, no problem. WOW! You won't believe it, but there was my Camouflage coat, in my size, hanging there waiting for me. Oh the irony! They exchanged my coat and after all that I ended up with my Dream coat after all. Thank you Ross Dress for Less. You will forever be my first choice for now on!
Rewrite this for me:
I set out on a mission to find the perfect holiday coat. After searching, I found my ideal coat at Burlington, but unfortunately, it was not available in my size. Determined, I headed to Target and purchased a coat, but it turned out to be a disappointment. It wasn't the coat I had envisioned. 

Undeterred, my next stop was Ross. Luckily, they had a coat in my size—a stunning Bomber-style jacket made of pleather. I bought it just before Christmas. However, a few days later, my husband Guy pointed out that the coat was incredibly wrinkled. Desperate, I scoured the internet for every hack to remove wrinkles from pleather, but none of them worked. 

Frustrated, I returned to Ross with the coat, having lost the receipt and tags, and asked to speak to the manager. The manager was a young man with dark hair and black-framed glasses. I explained my situation, and to my surprise, he simply told me to find what I needed—no problem. It was unbelievable! And there it was, my camouflage coat, hanging there in my size, waiting for me. The irony was not lost on me.

They exchanged my coat, and after all the trouble, I finally ended up with my dream coat. I am immensely grateful to Ross Dress for Less. They will forever be my first choice from now on. Thank you, Ross!

input: You honestly can't go wrong here. My favorites are the Udon Noodle Salad (a-ma-zing) and the Crispy Hipcity Ranch (so, so good). Friendly staff, fast service. Oh, they deliver too!
Rewrite this for me: I assure you, there are no bad options here. The Udon Noodle Salad is absolutely incredible, and the Crispy Hipcity Ranch is unbelievably delicious. The staff is friendly, and the service is quick. Additionally, they also provide delivery service.

input: Philadelphia, I love you.  Places like this remind me why.  We sat at the counter and watched the guys make the pizzas.  Our son hates cheese on a pizza and they had one already on the menu for him: The Marinara (oregano, crushed san marzano tomatoes, garlic, olive oil).  It was simple... but delicious. If you like real wood-fired pizzas that char the crust (a little blackened... in a good way), this is the place to go to.  Our other favorite pizza joints that rival this place are Lombardi's (NYC) and Grimaldi's (Brooklyn).  We all had a slice and were shocked at the lovely simplicity of it. Razor thin slices of garlic dotted the fresh tomato sauce.  My husband and I shared the Salsiccia (fennel sausage, roasted fennel, tomato sauce, mozzarella).  Roasted fennel on a pizza?  Brilliant. I cried a little.  No wait... I REALLY cried when we shared this cocktail: The Brooklyn (Dad's Hat rye, Luxardo cherry, white vermouth).  It says it serves one, but they brought it out in a cute little bottle and gave us each a glass...each with a hand- crafted giant square ice cube (hipster-cool) and Luxardo cherries.  Perfection.  We also shared a Rotolo (pizza dough, mortadella, ricotta, pistacchio pesto).  Those are crazy amazing.  I kept saying my husband could eat the rest... then freaking out and going back for another bite. He's lucky I didn't stab him in the hand with a fork to fight over the last bite (to be fair, he was the smart one who ordered it).  I could've eaten several of those and forgotten the pizza (although that was wonderful too!).  We finished with a little dessert... perfect little Italian cookies ("Cookie Jar" - pignoli, almond cookies, chocolate biscotti, pistacchio gnocchi) and I got an Affogato (fiordilatte soft serve with a shot of espresso).  The soft serve is Italian sweet cream... decadent and lovely... with rich espresso in a pretty little Italian mug.  I'm in Heaven here.  I know nothing about Vetri's other restaurants, but I'm checking them out next time I'm in Philadelphia!  By the way... service was great and friendly.  5 stars all around!
Rewrite this for me: Philadelphia, I have a deep affection for you. Places like this are a constant reminder as to why. We found ourselves perched at the counter, captivated by the pizza-making prowess of the skilled individuals behind it. Luckily, our son's dislike for cheese on pizza was catered to with "The Marinara" already on their menu. Simple yet flawlessly executed, it consisted of oregano, crushed san marzano tomatoes, garlic, and olive oil. If you appreciate wood-fired pizzas with a slightly charred, yet delightful crust, this is the place to be. Lombardi's in NYC and Grimaldi's in Brooklyn are the only other pizza joints that can compare to the quality of this place. As we all took bites of the pizza, we were left astounded by its lovely simplicity. Thin slices of garlic were dotted across the fresh tomato sauce, creating a mouthwatering sensation. My husband and I also indulged in the "Salsiccia", which featured fennel sausage, roasted fennel, tomato sauce, and mozzarella. Who would have thought of adding roasted fennel to a pizza? It was brilliantly executed and I may have shed a tear or two in response. Our emotional experience continued as we shared "The Brooklyn" cocktail – a mixture of Dad's Hat rye, Luxardo cherry, and white vermouth. Though it claims to serve only one, we were pleasantly surprised when they presented it in an adorable little bottle, complete with an artisanal square ice cube and Luxardo cherries for each of us. It was simply perfect. Another delight we shared was the "Rotolo", which combined pizza dough, mortadella, ricotta, and pistachio pesto. These little rolls were unbelievably divine. I kept telling my husband he could have the rest, only to panic and grab another mouthful for myself. In fact, I was dangerously close to forking him over the last bite (though he was the more sensible one who ordered it in the first place). I could have easily devoured multiple servings of those rolls and forgotten about the pizza entirely (although the pizza itself was fantastic too!). To conclude our culinary adventure, we indulged in some petite Italian cookies known as "Cookie Jar", featuring pignoli, almond cookies, chocolate biscotti, and pistachio gnocchi. Additionally, I treated myself to an Affogato – a heavenly combination of fiordilatte soft serve and a shot of espresso. The sweet creaminess of the soft serve paired perfectly with the robust espresso, creating an experience that transported me straight to Heaven itself. While I may not be familiar with Vetri's other restaurants, I vow to explore them the next time I find myself in Philadelphia. I must mention that the service we received was exceptional and friendly, earning this establishment a well-deserved and resounding five-star rating.

input:
This a really price store with great clothes. Mostly high end stuff, everything here is designer. 

The workers here are really friendly and not pushy. They will leave you alone if you just want to be left alone, they are never breathing down your neck trying to make a sale. They carry casual clothing but I think it's much better place for suits and dress shirts and fancy clothing. I think this place stands out in West Edmonton Mall in terms of service and dressy clothing for men. They really do everything to make your shopping experience better. 

Be prepared to spend some coin here, although you won't be disappointed.
Rewrite this for me:
This store is known for its amazing selection of high-quality clothes at reasonable prices. It primarily offers high-end designer items, making it a go-to destination for those seeking sophisticated and fashionable attire.

You'll appreciate the friendly and unobtrusive nature of the store's staff. They understand the importance of personal space and will give you the freedom to browse without any pressure to make a purchase. While they do stock casual clothing, their specialty lies in suits, dress shirts, and other formal wear. When it comes to service and dressy clothing for men, this place truly stands out in West Edmonton Mall.

Rest assured that shopping here may require some investment, but the quality and satisfaction you'll receive will make it worthwhile.

input:
The food was pretty tasty. Nothing outstanding though. It reminds me of any Mediterranean food truck that I've been to. It's a nice late night spot. Definitely hits the spot at the end of the night. To me, the amount of food you get for the price could be improved but I would not say that I feel ripped off. The amount of food you get is fair but I think it'd be easier to justify if you got a little more. 

There's plenty of seating. Despite being near a whole bunch of bar/club scenes, once you're inside it's easy to take a break and have a nice conversation. It is all very clean and well kept. The servers are quick and friendly. When I went there were only two guys working but they weren't busy so it didn't take too long. The entire restaurant is very dimly lit and the atmosphere is a bit of a hodgepodge of things. On one wall there is a mural of outer space and the music that plays seems to have no rhyme or reason to it. 

It's a bit of a strange place but I would definitely go back.
Rewrite this for me:
The food was fairly delicious but not exceptional. It reminded me of any average Mediterranean food truck I've tried. It makes for a decent late-night option and satisfies cravings at the end of the night. The portion size for the price could use some improvement, although I wouldn't say I feel cheated. The quantity of food you receive is acceptable, but it would be easier to justify if there were a bit more.

There is ample seating available. Despite being close to various bar and club scenes, once you're inside, it's a peaceful place to take a break and have a pleasant conversation. The cleanliness and upkeep are top-notch. The servers are prompt and friendly. During my visit, only two staff members were working, but since they weren't busy, the wait time wasn't too long. The entire establishment has a dimly lit ambiance with a mishmash of elements. One wall features a mural of outer space, and the music playing doesn't seem to follow any particular theme.

It's an eccentric place, but I would definitely return.

input:

input:
When giving friends from out of town a tour of the French Quarter, one can only expect they want some classic New Orleans dishes. I've been here a couple of times, but they were the ones that wanted to go, due to their lunch special. It's a nice, well know restaurant that offers a 17.00 lunch special that includes a soup or salad, entree, and the option for a 4.00 Bloody Mary or martini. I got the Bloody Mary and it was a great size for the price. It was spicy and hit the spot.
They text message you when your table is ready, so were able to walk around the quarter while we waited. Thank god a lot of restaurants are getting rid of the those buzzers that make you feel like you are under house arrest. 
We sat down to a beautiful table right by the open shutters. The servers, were ok. They were busy, but forgot a couple of things we asked for. It was still a great experience though!
I got the pork chop with red beans and the turtle soup. The turtle soup was one of the best I have had. The pork chop was cooked to perfection and the read beans were seasoned very well. It came with cornbread, but it was very dry. After this lunch at noon, I didn't find myself hungry till it was basically time for bed. It was a very generous portion and well worth the money.

Muriel's is a great way to get a classic, good quality New Orleans meal at a decent price. The location is spectacular, and the history behind the restaurant made for great conversation at the table.
Definitely check it out if you are in the Quarter!
Rewrite this for me:
If you're showing friends visiting from out of town around the French Quarter, it's safe to assume they'll be craving some traditional New Orleans dishes. Although I've been here a few times before, this time it was their idea to go to Muriel's because of their lunch special. Muriel's is a well-known restaurant that offers a $17.00 lunch special, including a choice of soup or salad, an entree, and the option to add a Bloody Mary or martini for $4.00. I went for the Bloody Mary and it was a good-sized drink for the price, with a nice spicy kick.

The restaurant texts you when your table is ready, which is convenient because it allows you to take a stroll around the quarter while you wait. Thankfully, many restaurants are starting to do away with those cumbersome buzzers that make you feel like you're on house arrest.

Once we were seated at a beautiful table by the open shutters, the service was decent, although the servers were quite busy and forgot a couple of things we had requested. Nevertheless, it was still a great overall experience.

For my meal, I chose the pork chop with red beans and the turtle soup. The turtle soup was outstanding and one of the best I've had. The pork chop was cooked perfectly, and the red beans were seasoned wonderfully. The only downside was that the cornbread that came with it was quite dry. Despite this, I left feeling completely satisfied and didn't find myself hungry again until it was almost bedtime. The portion size was very generous and definitely worth the money.

Muriel's is the perfect place to have a classic and high-quality New Orleans meal at a reasonable price. Its location is amazing, and the restaurant's history provided interesting conversation at the table. If you happen to be in the French Quarter, I highly recommend checking it out.

input: We stopped here's on the recommendation of our shuttle driver.  The red velvet ice cream is wonderful!! Pieces of cake. Creamy goodness.  Yum!
Rewrite this for me: We decided to make a pit stop here based on our shuttle driver's suggestion. And let me tell you, the red velvet ice cream is absolutely amazing! It's like having small chunks of cake mixed with a delightfully creamy texture. It's just incredibly yummy!

input:
I ate here for the first time today.  The woman that works behind the counter is really friendly and offered to waive the minimum credit order amount ($7), since I work nearby.

The food itself is pretty average for American-Chinese food.  Nothing great, but not bad either.  My sauce was greasy, but the food in general doesn't seem to be (e.g. fried rice).  They do have some vegetarian options which are of the tofu variety as opposed to fake meat. 

I would go back since they have lunch specials that come with rice and either a drink, soup, or egg roll ($5.75).

EDIT: I got super sick after leaving this review, and I'm 99% sure it was food poisoning.  Will not be returning.
Rewrite this for me:
Today was my first time eating at this place. The lady who works behind the counter was incredibly friendly and offered to waive the minimum credit order amount of $7 since I work nearby.

The American-Chinese food here is decent, nothing extraordinary but not terrible either. The sauce on my dish was a bit greasy, but the overall food quality seems fine, especially the fried rice. They do provide vegetarian options, mostly tofu-based rather than fake meat.

I would consider going back because they offer lunch specials that include rice and a choice of drink, soup, or an egg roll, all for $5.75.

UPDATE: Unfortunately, I became very ill after writing this review and strongly suspect it was due to food poisoning. Regrettably, I will not be returning to this place.

input:
Delicious! 

I wish they took reservations, but my friend and her fiance go there nice and early so that we could snag a seat inside (it was cold out!). 

We ordered the bianco salad ( to share between 2) and the western addition (to share between 4).

I thought the salad was tasty but nothing special, despite the white chocolate shavings. Cute idea, but not enough crunch or pizazz to make the salad seem really fabulous.

The pizza, however, was pretty darn good. We ordered it deep dish to try their special cornmeal crust and were pretty impressed. 
The crust tastes a little bit like cornbread, a little bit like pizza dough, a tiny bit like grease (the good kind) and a lot like YUM!

I don't know if it was the best pizza I've ever had, but it was very good. It would be even better if it were a tad cheaper, and didn't get so crowded! But definitely worth a visit if you're in the area!
Rewrite this for me:
Yummy! I do wish they accepted reservations, but fortunately, my friend and her fiance arrived early so that we could secure a seat indoors (it was chilly outside!).

To start, we ordered the bianco salad to share between the two of us, and the western addition pizza to share among the four of us.

The salad was tasty, although it didn't possess any extraordinary qualities, despite the addition of white chocolate shavings. It was a charming idea, but lacked the necessary crunch and excitement to make it truly fabulous.

On the other hand, the pizza was quite delicious. We opted for the deep-dish option to explore their special cornmeal crust, and we were pleasantly surprised. The crust had a delightful blend of cornbread and pizza dough, with a subtle hint of grease (the good kind) and a whole lot of YUM!

While I can't say it was the absolute best pizza I've ever had, it was undeniably very good. It would be even more enjoyable if it were slightly more affordable and didn't get so packed. Nonetheless, it's definitely worth a visit if you find yourself in the area!

input: A downtown without a bookstore is like a downtown without... I don't know I lost the metaphor. It's just sad is what it is. You need books, you need a place to browse, talk with other book lovers, and listen to book readings. Indy Reads is that place. And it's more than that because all proceeds support a great cause, adult literacy. Most of the books are used so donate a book and pick up a new (used) one. You may be surprised at all the books they have that you didn't even know you wanted. They also have a small selection of new books. If they don't have what you're looking for, you can order it. The one thing I don't really like is that the $1 children's books can be jammed so tightly that it's hard to look through them. The kids books are also arranged by color, which makes it harder for me to distinguish between titles as I glance through. Prices are excellent throughout, and the space is really nice. Check it out!
Rewrite this for me: A downtown lacking a bookstore is a somber sight. One cannot truly appreciate a thriving city center without the presence of a bookstore. Such an establishment serves as a sanctuary for book enthusiasts, a place to peruse and converse with fellow literary lovers, and enjoy engaging book readings. Indy Reads fulfills all these requirements and more. What sets it apart is that it supports a noble cause - adult literacy - with all proceeds. Donating a book enables one to pick up a new (yet pre-loved) one. Prepare to be pleasantly surprised by the vast selection of books, many of which you may not have even realized you desired. While predominantly offering used titles, they also offer a modest collection of new ones; and if they lack a specific book you seek, they can easily procure it for you. The only drawback I personally find is the tightly packed, $1 children's books, making it challenging to browse through them. Additionally, the arrangement of kids' books by color might make it harder for quick glances to discern titles. Nevertheless, their prices are excellent, and the space itself is quite inviting. I strongly encourage you to visit and see for yourself!

input:
This used to be Red's but they knocked of the "R" and re-launched as Ed's, although when I see the sign from outside I keep forgeting it's called Ed's - cause it just looks like part of the sign fell off. Ed's is huge. If you've ever been on a cruise ship, Ed's has a variety of activity spaces, restaurant, bars and lounges under one roof. 

It's endless entertainment. You could probably float around here for a whole week and never get bored. There is a pool room, video games, bowling, a dance area, restaurants, lounges, a stage and much more around every corner you turn. It's a good place for young kids and birthday parties once you're too old for Chucky Cheese. 

Although I've personally never seen a band here my partner has, and it's not that expensive to see good bands like Ween, Jurassic Five or Interpol. The venue's neither big or small, so Ed's can host lesser known but interesting musicians as they can sell upwards of 600 tickets. So for bands that aren't popular enough to fill the Coliseum, Ed's still helps them establish a presence in E-town.

input:
They used to make an Amiga bowl that had an abundance of shredded grilled chicken on the bottom of a flour tortilla bowl, a layer of rice topped with grilled onions and peppers with a queso sauce drizzeled over the top.
Tonight there was no rice nor any shredded chicken, it had been replaced with chicken crisps. They are the outer parts of a grilled chicken breast with no moisture and very few of them.
Having met the owner in the past and having his wife wait on me I knew something wasn't right.
I explained to the waitress that this dish had changed and wasn't good! She politely offered something else. What to order...if they had modified a basic dish what was next?
To my surprise a male manager came out and "informed" me that this is exactly what they had been serving for 10 years and I must have either special ordered something or was mistaken.
I said this is not what they had served me for the past 5 years and I never had requested a special order before. 
I also asked what they had done to the phenominal soft tacos? They were usually served in a soft warm flour tortilla and had moisture and flavor. Tonight they were stale and crisp and the filing was bland.  Again he informed me I was mistaken while he held my order that had been sent back to the kitchen in front of me.
I apologized and said I didn't wish for anything else, thank you.
Another manager came out a few moments later apologizing and stated that they are unfamiliar with what I had ordered and would "special order" anything I wanted. I declined.
Apparently their cook walked out tonight and they were winging it.
Too bad it was a good place to get a good mexican meal.
Two thumbs down on Poblano's.
Rewrite this for me:

Knowing the owner and having his wife serve me in the past, I sensed that something was amiss. I voiced my concerns to the waitress, explaining that the dish had changed and was not enjoyable. She kindly offered to bring me something else, but I was unsure of what to order. If they had altered a classic dish, what other surprises awaited me?

I disagreed, explaining that this was not the same meal I had been served for the past 5 years, and I had never requested any modifications before. 

I also questioned the quality of their phenomenal soft tacos. Normally served in a soft and warm flour tortilla with great flavor and moisture, tonight they were stale, crispy, and lacking in taste. Once again, the manager dismissed my complaints and held my returned order in front of me.

Feeling frustrated, I apologized and declined the offer of another dish. However, a different manager approached me a few moments later, offering apologies and admitting that they were unfamiliar with the specific item I had ordered. Apparently, their cook had walked out earlier that night, leaving them unprepared and improvising. It was a shame because Poblano's used to be a reliable place to enjoy a delicious Mexican meal. Unfortunately, based on this disappointing visit, I give Poblano's two thumbs down.

input:
I came in with high hopes and left with slight disappointment. 

Our server was super attentive, and very friendly; however I feel like the food was disappointing. Our egg drop soup came out right away at a nice piping hot temperature and when the rest of our food came out it was practically room temperature. 

Feeling adventurous, I had ordered the Shrimp with Candied Walnuts entree with brown rice while he ordered the Sesame Chicken platter. I like the idea of sharing food, but my food was too busy all on its own without adding something else to the mix. The brown rice was cold and very bland while the shrimp was overly sweet and I didn't feel like the candied walnuts and melon balls were complementary flavors.

The chocolate cake we had for dessert was amazing though; 6 layers of chocolate on chocolate. It was so sweet and rich, we ended up sharing a slice.

So to sum up, service was great, dessert was great, but the food needs some work. Sorry PF Changs, I just am not impressed.

One thing I will note (that our server told us) is that they are very big on catering to food allergies (especially gluten).
Rewrite this for me:
I entered the restaurant with high expectations but left slightly disappointed. The server was extremely attentive and friendly, which was impressive. However, I found the food to be underwhelming. Although the egg drop soup was served promptly and at the perfect temperature, the rest of our dishes were disappointingly lukewarm.

I decided to be adventurous and ordered the Shrimp with Candied Walnuts entree with brown rice, while my companion chose the Sesame Chicken platter. While I appreciate the concept of sharing food, my dish was already overwhelming without any additional elements. The brown rice lacked flavor and was cold, and the shrimp was excessively sweet. The combination of candied walnuts and melon balls did not complement each other well.

On a positive note, the chocolate cake we had for dessert was exceptional. With six layers of chocolate, it was incredibly sweet and decadent. We ended up sharing a slice because it was that good.

To summarize, the service was excellent, and the dessert was outstanding. However, the main course left much to be desired. Unfortunately, PF Changs failed to impress me.

I would like to highlight one positive aspect, as mentioned by our server. They take food allergies, particularly gluten, very seriously and cater to them diligently.

input: Tria's employees are very knowledgeable about the selection of beers and wines they offer. This is probably why I look forward to going to Tria. input: Mae's is the best Chinese restaurant on this east side. We tried Mae's due to some rude pricks across the street. Lol! But, luckily things happen for a reason. The environment, the decor, the air inside is so much better to start. The food taste so much more fresher, like it was not frozen or reheated. No greasy/oily after taste. The service is very good,  always right there when you need something, staff is very friendly. My family and I love Mae's and what makes it better are the prices. We're large family and we can do really well with just $60. Lunch specials are awesome! I encourage you to try Mae's.
Rewrite this for me: I highly recommend Mae's as the top Chinese restaurant on the east side. We stumbled upon Mae's after dealing with unpleasant individuals across the street, but it turned out to be a fortunate incident. The ambiance, decor, and air inside the restaurant are exceptional right from the start. The food tastes noticeably fresher, like it has never been frozen or reheated. There is no greasy or oily aftertaste. The service is excellent, with the staff always prompt and friendly whenever you need assistance. My family and I have developed a deep affection for Mae's, and to top it off, the prices are very reasonable. Even with a large family, we can enjoy a satisfying meal for just $60. The lunch specials are especially fantastic. I highly encourage you to give Mae's a try.

input: This place is my absolute fave! The flavors are spot on, they taste exactly the way you imagine, but better! input: This location used to be good, several years ago. About 3 years ago it started to go downhill and now it is just terrible. There were 2 people working on a Saturday evening. They need to either shape up or ship out.
Rewrite this for me: In the past, this place had a good reputation, but over the course of about three years, its quality has significantly declined, and now it's reached an extremely unsatisfactory state. On a Saturday evening, only two staff members were working despite nearly all the tables being occupied and people waiting to place orders and pay. Regrettably, the sandwich I received was made with hard, burnt bread and was barely edible. It's high time for them to make serious improvements or consider closing down altogether.

input:

On the plus side, it's quiet, no zombies and the witches doing spells took time out to photobomb a bit.

So there's that.

Seriously, a well laid out cemetery and some of the better made stones and angels.

And no zombies. Remember that part.

So, at least that's something to appreciate.

In all seriousness, this cemetery is thoughtfully designed, boasting well-crafted tombstones and exquisite angelic sculptures.

And did I mention? No zombies. Let's not forget about that aspect.

input:
On a recent trip to Port Richey, I selected Holiday Inn Express for a couple of reasons.  The main reason was the option of two beds (as I was sharing the room with my brother).  The other reasons were:  price, vicinity to my aunt's home and complementary breakfast. 

My family and I typically stay at the Hyatt Place/House when we're traveling.  However, since it was just my brother and I, I figured we'd give Holiday Inn a shot. 

+  The staff were very friendly and helpful.
+  Free wifi.
+  Breakfast was very good, offering both hot and cold entrees. 

-  Sadly, the beds were WAY TOO soft.  It felt as if the mattresses were past their life expectancy.  As a result, I didn't really sleep well for most of my three nights there.
-  The a/c was hit and miss with the lack of reliable thermostat controls. 

There was a pool and hot tub, but since I didn't utilize either, it wouldn't be fair to rate them.  There also a small gym that I didn't use either. 

All in all, it was just ok.  Hyatt has spoiled me.
Rewrite this for me:
During my recent trip to Port Richey, I decided to stay at Holiday Inn Express for several reasons. The primary factor was the availability of two beds since I was sharing the room with my brother. Additionally, the hotel's price, proximity to my aunt's house, and complimentary breakfast were also appealing.

Usually, my family and I opt for the Hyatt Place/House when we travel. However, considering it was just my brother and me, I thought we would give Holiday Inn a try.

There were several positive aspects of our stay. The staff at Holiday Inn Express were remarkably friendly and accommodating. We also appreciated the complimentary wifi and the breakfast options, which included both hot and cold dishes.

However, there were a couple of drawbacks during our stay. Firstly, the beds were excessively soft, almost as if they were past their prime. This resulted in me having difficulty sleeping well for the majority of the three nights I was there. Additionally, the air conditioning was inconsistent due to the unreliable thermostat controls.

Although there were amenities such as a pool, hot tub, and a small gym, I did not utilize them, so I cannot provide a fair assessment of their quality.

Overall, my experience at Holiday Inn Express was just okay. The Hyatt has set high standards that have spoiled me in terms of comfort and quality.

input: The staff wasn't too interested in helping customers, instead focused on the TV in the lobby, flirting with each other and just standing around. I found the food to be ok, not great, not terrible. I'll round up from the 1.5 I give them.

input:
The food is excellent. The customer service and quantity over time has continued to go down. I've been going to this place every couple weeks for two years. The portions over time have continued to gradually get smaller and smaller. I proceeded to explain my case. I was told if I didn't want to take the food, I didn't have to pay for it. I said ok, and was the berated for not taking the food I ordered. 

Long story short, these people have lost my business. I am not going back.
Rewrite this for me: The food quality at this place is exceptional, but unfortunately, their customer service and portion sizes have been consistently dropping over time. input: Food was great. Staff was nice, friendly and helpful with menu suggestions. The Happy Hour is a good deal and the house margaritas tasted better than many other restaurants I've visited. input:

input:
do not eat here. my husband, two friends and i went out for restaurant week to marmont steakhouse on saturday, january 26, 2013; our experience was horrific.  the four of us ordered the crab bisque soup for our first course, it was cold and we sent it back to be reheated.  my second course was the calamari it was bland, fried too hard and rubbery.  finally two ppl from our party ordered the lobster ravioli for an entree.  it was not lobster ravioli but beef. i asked our waiter and one other waiter to please double check with the chef because this is not lobster, i expressed that i have not eaten beef or pork since 1994, and that it would make me ill. they both came back separately and argued that it was in fact lobster. another party of maybe 6 ppl ordered the lobster ravioli, they had the same problem and sent their dishes back to the kitchen too.  the server finally came over after i'd eaten two of the ravioli to apologize for the kitchens error and telling us that was in fact beef. 
i have been in the bathroom all day with diarrhea from the beef ravioli! the staff was very nonchalant about it and offered an insincere apology.
Rewrite this for me: Avoid dining at this place. On Saturday, January 26, 2013, my husband, two friends, and I decided to try Marmont Steakhouse for restaurant week, and it turned out to be an absolutely dreadful experience. To start, the crab bisque soup we ordered as our first course arrived cold, so we had to send it back to be reheated. Moving on to the calamari, my second course, it was tasteless, over-fried, and had a rubbery texture. To make matters worse, two people in our group ordered the lobster ravioli for our main course, but instead, they were served beef ravioli. I informed our waiter, as well as another waiter, about this mistake and requested them to confirm with the chef, emphasizing that I have not consumed beef or pork since 1994 and that it would have detrimental effects on my health. However, both waiters returned and argued that it was indeed lobster ravioli. Interestingly, another group of about six people also ordered the same dish and encountered the same problem, leading them to send their plates back to the kitchen as well. Finally, after eating two of the ravioli pieces, the server approached us to apologize for the kitchen's error and admitted that it was, in fact, beef. Consequently, I have suffered from diarrhea throughout the entire day due to consuming the beef ravioli. The staff's attitude towards this whole debacle was incredibly casual, and their apology lacked sincerity.

input: It simply does not get any better than Tako for sushi. Everything is fresh & delicious. The private rooms are so fun for a festive night out, it's BYO & when my girls get together we enjoy the feast & atmosphere! Some personal favorites are the jalapeño yellowtail(a must!!), kani salad, bird's nest roll & the naruto (served in cucumber instead of rice. Honestly, you can't go wrong when ordering. And so reasonable!! I rarely spend over $35 including tip when we go, and we do not hold back at all when ordering. Highly, highly recommend Tako!
Rewrite this for me: Tako for sushi is nothing short of amazing. The freshness and deliciousness of their dishes is unparalleled. Their private rooms guarantee a fun and festive night out, and the best part is, it's BYO! When my friends and I gather, we truly indulge in the feast and soak up the incredible atmosphere. There are a few personal favorites that I absolutely need to mention: the jalapeño yellowtail is an absolute must-try, along with the kani salad, bird's nest roll, and the unique naruto, served in a cucumber instead of rice. Honestly, any choice you make will be a winner. And the best part is, it's unbelievably affordable! Even with all the ordering we do, it's rare for me to spend over $35 including the tip. Rest assured, Tako comes highly, highly recommended!

input:
This is a milestone review for me on Yelp.  I had been struggling with which one to chhose.  I decidede to make it Redemption.  This was seriously one of the best meals of my ENTIRE life.  

This review was from about 2 months ago.  Sorry it is a little dated.  Such as life.  

The setting is an old church.  It is really a beautiful surrounding for a restaurant.  Although I am an old church architecture nerd.  It was really cool to look around.   

The service was incredible.  I was hear as part of a group of 7 other characters, several were part of the NOLA restaurant scene.  We wanted a good time with the meal and they provided it!   

Paneed smoked soft shell crab a la Christian.  I was not fortunate enough to have enjoyed the original.  I can not comment on the faithfulness to the founders recipe.  I can say this there is no highe calling for a soft shell crab than to be cold smoked and fried in preparation for this dish.  On to your 77 virgins and mecca for you!  But I experienced heaven eating this.  

Seafood stuffed filet of fish a la Christian's - This was superlative.  Again did not try the original, but the mirliton and seafood stuffing was heavenly, and more importantly improved the taste of the fresh flounder rather than competing for the spot light!   

The combination was quite possibly one of the 10 best meals of my life.  If you have been here, you should try it!
Rewrite this for me:
Here's a revised version of the text:

I recently wrote this milestone review on Yelp after struggling to decide which restaurant to choose. In the end, I settled on Redemption, and let me tell you, it turned out to be one of the most memorable meals I've ever had.

Although it's been about 2 months since my visit, please excuse the delay in sharing this review. That's just life sometimes.

Redemption is housed in an old church, creating a beautiful and unique atmosphere for a restaurant. As someone who appreciates old church architecture, I found it particularly fascinating to look around.

The service at Redemption was absolutely incredible. I dined with a group of seven individuals, some of whom were familiar with the NOLA restaurant scene, and we were all seeking a great dining experience. Fortunately, the staff delivered in every way possible.

Let's talk about the food. The paneed smoked soft shell crab a la Christian was a dish I hadn't tried before, so I can't comment on its faithfulness to the original recipe. However, I can confidently say that there is no better way to prepare a soft shell crab than by cold smoking and frying it for this particular dish. It was an absolute delight to eat.

Moving on to the seafood stuffed filet of fish a la Christian's. This dish was simply superb. Again, I didn't have the opportunity to try the original version, but the combination of mirliton and seafood stuffing was heavenly. Most importantly, it enhanced the flavor of the fresh flounder rather than overpowering it.

The overall dining experience at Redemption was undoubtedly one of the top 10 meals I've ever had. If you haven't been here yet, I highly recommend giving it a try. You won't be disappointed.

input:

Sadly, we refrained from ordering any drinks as it was only two days after Mardi Gras, and I was still in recovery mode. The service we received was truly exceptional, ranking among the best I have ever experienced in this town renowned for its hospitality industry. All in all, it was a truly great dining experience.

input:
I went here on a Wednesday night and, though it wasn't busy, there were no open tables without a reservation,  except the tall tables in the bar area. It still seemed to be a very quiet place anyway. 

The location is not attractive, the street is dark and mostly empty at night, but the inside is stylish in a masculine, refined sort of way; dark wood, low light, maps on the walls and prints of watercolors depicting old Missouri scenes. It was a great place for a quiet, intimate dinner. They've got a couple of TVs up above the bar. 

They seemed very well staffed, as if each table had its own server. 

The menu is one page but very intriguing, I had so many questions for our server about "what is this?" and "what is that?" and he was totally nice and knowledgeable about the menu items. He seemed nervous and unsure at first, but he was friendly and made sure to check on us frequently. 

We decided to split 3 small plates and a side dish between the two of us and, honestly, it was a little too much food for just two people. Perhaps we don't have hearty enough appetites.

Their menu is so varied and interesting, it's really all over the map in terms of seasonings and ethnic origins but the main focus seems to be rustic and warming - at least at this time of year. I have a feeling they may change it up from time to time. I'm sure you'll get things here you won't find anywhere else. The prices are very reasonable, considering the planning and good execution of the food. You'd certainly find more expensive, and less original places in Clayton and down town. 

We ordered the smoked trout, the venison hot dogs, the mini monte cristo sandwiches, and the french fries. 

The venison hot dogs and the smoked trout were fantastic and interesting. The french fries were very well made, and the dipping sauces delicious. I was so impressed with these that I was then a bit underwhelmed by the mini monte cristos. Since everything else there seemed to have a unique spin on it, I expected them to do something original here as well, but they were just like any monte cristo you might have. They were very tasty of course, but nothing new. 

With the food plus two draft beers, our total was $52.05 before tip and we were stuffed and satisfied. I applaud them!
Rewrite this for me:
On a Wednesday night, I visited this place and despite it not being busy, there were no available tables without a reservation, except for the tall ones in the bar area. Nonetheless, it still maintained a peaceful ambiance throughout.

The location itself isn't appealing, as the street is dimly lit and lacks activity during the evenings. However, the interior has a stylish and refined masculine atmosphere, with dark wood, dim lighting, maps adorning the walls, and watercolor prints depicting scenes from old Missouri. It proved to be an ideal spot for a quiet, intimate dinner. Additionally, they had a couple of TVs situated above the bar.

It appeared that they had ample staff, as each table seemed to have their own server.

The menu, though only one page, was intriguing and left me with numerous questions about certain dishes. Our server was incredibly friendly and knowledgeable about the menu items, gladly answering my inquiries. Initially, he seemed a bit nervous and uncertain, but he made an effort to check on us frequently and provide excellent service.

My companion and I decided to share three small plates and a side dish, but in all honesty, it was a bit much for just two people. It's possible that we simply didn't have hearty enough appetites.

Their menu is incredibly diverse and fascinating, featuring an array of seasonings and ethnic influences. However, the main focus appears to be on rustic and comforting dishes, especially during this time of year. I have a feeling that they might change up their menu from time to time. It's certainly a place where you can savor unique dishes not found elsewhere. Furthermore, the prices are quite reasonable, considering the careful thought and skilled execution put into the food. In comparison to Clayton and downtown, you would undoubtedly find more expensive yet less original establishments.

For our meal, we ordered the smoked trout, venison hot dogs, mini monte cristo sandwiches, and french fries.

The venison hot dogs and smoked trout were both incredible and intriguing. The french fries were exceptionally well-made, and the accompanying dipping sauces were delicious. These dishes left a great impression on me, which unfortunately led to some disappointment with the mini monte cristos. Given the originality displayed in their other offerings, I expected them to put their own unique spin on this classic dish as well. However, they turned out to be quite ordinary, similar to any other monte cristo sandwich you might encounter. They were undoubtedly tasty, but nothing innovative.

Our total bill, including two draft beers, came out to be $52.05 before tipping. We left feeling both full and satisfied. I applaud their efforts!

input: I went last night with a few friends and let me say I was impressed, not necessarily with the quality of the food (nothing wrong with it by any means) or the decor, but the servers: how they don't kill every 4th customer is beyond me. I heard tables on both sides of us giving the most ridiculous of complaints to our/their server. Both tables were demanding as hell and already said loudly to eachother that they weren't tipping because of x, y and z reasons, and then were dumbfounded that there's a gratuity on their bill (it says it in the menu, anything over $50) their server, smaller girl so with purple hair, carried upwards of 4 plates at once, explained the menu perfectly and had an eagle eye for every table in her section and dealt with ridiculous complaints like a true professional. Thumbs up and five stars to the staff, customers, learn how to be basic humans, or stay home.
Rewrite this for me:
I went out last night with a few friends and I have to say, I was really impressed. It wasn't necessarily because of the amazing quality of the food (there was nothing wrong with it, though), or the decor. It was actually the servers that left me in awe. I couldn't understand how they managed to handle every fourth customer without losing their cool.

At the tables on both sides of us, there were people making the most absurd complaints to our server as well as their own. These customers were demanding as hell and had already announced loudly to each other that they wouldn't be leaving a tip due to various reasons. To top it off, they were completely surprised to see the gratuity charge on their bill (which was clearly stated on the menu for any bill over $50). 

Our server, a smaller girl with purple hair, skillfully carried multiple plates at once, flawlessly explained the menu, and diligently kept an eye on every table in her section. She handled these ridiculous complaints with the utmost professionalism. 

I give a big thumbs up and five stars to the staff, and as for the customers, I think they need to learn how to behave like decent human beings, or perhaps just stay at home.

input:

I found that their list prices were fair and competitive, as well as the certification and warranties on used vehicles - I just chose a different car make/model than I shopped for at Hallmark. Had I liked the car better than what I was comparing it to, I would have likely bought from them. Based on some pretty terrible experiences at other places, I would recommend trying this dealership if you are looking to buy locally.
Rewrite this for me: Although I didn't ultimately purchase a vehicle from this dealership, I was pleasantly surprised by the straightforward and superior shopping experience compared to other dealerships. The list prices were reasonable and competitive, and they also offered commendable certifications and warranties for their used vehicles. Although I ended up opting for a different make and model from another dealership, the staff at Hallmark, including the salesman and sales manager, were kind and not pushy. Their prompt attention allowed me to quickly test drive the car I was interested in. If I had preferred their vehicle over the one I was comparing it to, I would have likely made a purchase here. input:
It is typical Broad Ripple charming spot. Small, trendy and bustling with activity. They do not take reservations. Which is somewhat annoying when you are traveling from another part of town. Whatever, we just had to arrange to arrive earlier than we would have liked to hopefully secure a table, which we did. When we arrived it was quiet and only several tables had guests seated. As our dinner progressed it became more crowded until every seat was filled. Nice lively scene except then you can not hear squat! It made dinner conversation difficult. Boo!!!! I think this could be an easy fix for them. 

Meal/Drinks:  The cocktails were creative and tasted wonderful. Our servers suggestions were pretty spot on as we enjoyed most of her suggestions. 

The guacamole was very good with the exception of the fact that my friend has a nut allergy and we asked to have them left off and of coarse they arrived with them on! They really weren't necessary in my opinion either as I don't think they add much to the dish. The reason I wanted to try this restaurant- The Harvest salad! We all split this as well and it was good. The combination of fruit and root vegetables was delish! The figs were so good and the herbed goat cheese mouse was a highlight on this plate!

Two of us ordered the Veracruz Trigger fish and the other ordered the Serrano Scallops and all of it was wonderful. The white sweet mashed potatoes were interesting! I am glad we tried them. The Veracruz sauce was wonderful and full of flavor. It was a lot of food though. Had we known we would have probably skipped one of the first course selections or split an entree. That'a ok though- lunch for today :)

We also tried the Tostones and Stewed Black Beans. Beans were very good, full of flavor! Tostones seemed very dry but maybe that is what they are supposed to be- this is the first time I have had them. BUT, dipped in the Stewed Black Beans they tasted great!

We passed on dessert as they had no gluten free, dairy free options. Delicia offers many options for restricted diets, which we loved. Just no dessert, which is probably better anyway-we were so full! 

Go, you will not be disappointed. Just go before 7pm on a Friday night to ensure a table.
Rewrite this for me:
This place in Broad Ripple is a typical charming spot. It's small, trendy, and always bustling with activity. The only downside is that they don't take reservations, which can be quite annoying if you're coming from another part of town. Despite this inconvenience, we managed to arrange an earlier arrival time to secure a table, which we successfully did. When we first arrived, it was quiet with only a few tables occupied. However, as the evening progressed, it became more crowded until every seat was filled. It created a lively atmosphere, but unfortunately, it made it difficult to hear each other during dinner. It's definitely something they should fix.

As for the food and drinks, the cocktails were creative and tasted amazing. Our server had some great suggestions, and we enjoyed most of them. The guacamole was delicious, except for the fact that my friend has a nut allergy, and we specifically asked for them to be left off. Unfortunately, they arrived with the nuts anyway. In my opinion, they didn't add much to the dish. The reason we wanted to try this restaurant was for the Harvest salad, and it didn't disappoint. The combination of fruits and root vegetables was absolutely delicious. The figs were particularly tasty, and the herbed goat cheese mousse was a highlight.

For our entrees, two of us ordered the Veracruz Trigger fish, and the other ordered the Serrano Scallops. All of it was wonderful. The white sweet mashed potatoes were an interesting twist, and we were glad we tried them. The Veracruz sauce was full of flavor and really elevated the dish. It was definitely a lot of food, though. If we had known, we probably would've skipped one of the first course options or split an entree. But that's okay, leftovers for lunch!

We also tried the Tostones and Stewed Black Beans. The beans were packed with flavor and tasted really good. The Tostones, on the other hand, seemed a bit dry, but maybe that's how they're supposed to be. This was my first time having them. However, when dipped in the Stewed Black Beans, they tasted great.

We decided to skip dessert as they didn't have any gluten-free or dairy-free options. Delicia, on the other hand, offers many options for restricted diets, which we really appreciated. Plus, we were so full that dessert probably would've been too much anyway.

Overall, I highly recommend this place. Just make sure to arrive before 7pm on a Friday night to secure a table and avoid disappointment.

input:
This makes my 6th or 7th time to Jackson's in the last 2 years and I thought that after tonight's visit they deserved a review. 

I had the panini Reuben.  Panini was amazing. Great use of garlic. Loved the cut of the meat. Not stringy but nicely chinked in thin slices. Cheese was well melted throughout the mix of kraut and meat. Rye Bread was wonderful. Would love to have it as a staple in my house. 

Salad came out same time as sandwich which was not good.

Presentation was a little sloppy. 

Like every other place I have had a panini (except Panera where they do it right), the sandwich was served directly on a plate. Why don't they serve on a napkin? Particularly when they bring the salad out at the same time as the sandwich?  If the sandwich sits for more than a few moments, the bread gets soggy from the steam.  Nothing serious, but for the price, which is a little high, it seems lacking.  While the price is a little high, i think it is justified considering the food and drink quality. 

They have a great selection of wines and beers that are likely to fit any palette.  

Wait staff have always been friendly. But you can tell this is a place where people are expected to hustle. Sometimes short or even distracted the service can be lacking. 

The second time I visited was during a medium lunch rush and the wait time was 15 min to get drinks. My trip tonight it was about 8 min. For a sat night this is not bad. But not great either. My bartenders were awesome and never left me wanting (except for getting my salad with the main course).

Overall a good experience and I will be back.
Rewrite this for me:
This is my sixth or seventh visit to Jackson's in the past two years, and I felt that after tonight's visit, they deserved a review.

I ordered the panini Reuben, and it was amazing. The panini itself had a great garlic flavor, and I really enjoyed the thinly sliced, non-stringy meat. The cheese was well melted and blended perfectly with the sauerkraut and meat. The rye bread was absolutely wonderful, and I wish I could have it as a regular staple in my own home.

However, I was not pleased with the timing of the salad being served alongside the sandwich. It came out at the same time, which was not ideal. The presentation was also a bit sloppy.

Unlike Panera, where they serve the sandwich on a napkin, Jackson's served it directly on a plate. I feel that serving it on a napkin would help prevent the bread from getting soggy due to the steam if the sandwich sits for too long. This may not be a major issue, but considering the slightly higher price, I find it lacking. However, I believe the higher price can be justified by the quality of the food and drinks.

Jackson's offers a great selection of wines and beers that are likely to cater to any palate.

The wait staff has always been friendly, but it is evident that this is a place where people are expected to work efficiently. Sometimes, the service can be lacking if the staff is short or distracted.

During my second visit, which was during a moderately busy lunch rush, the wait time for drinks was 15 minutes. Tonight, it was around 8 minutes, which is not bad for a Saturday night, but it's also not great. However, the bartenders were awesome and made sure I never felt neglected (except for the salad being served with the main course).

Overall, it was a good experience, and I will definitely return.

input:

She was very friendly and has a very positive attitude.  She took her time with my pedicure and was very thorough with the massaging (which was the best part). 

Unfortunately Young didn't do my manicure.   I had a gel manicure that needed to be soaked off.  The owner did my nails.  She first scraped my nails with the cuticle pusher, but when it wasn't coming off fast enough, she used the drill.  I was really worried as I didn't want my nails to be thin.  But I just let her do her thing.  I'm usually not picky so when she was working on my nails I didn't watch what she was doing until I realized after close examination she didn't fully take the old gel polish off.  
Not only that, the polish didn't go on smoothly, there's are noticeable bumps on my nail bed and the sides of my nails weren't even fully covered.  

I am so disappointed.  I love Young, but I don't know if I'll be going back due to my experience with my gel manicure.

To remove the old polish, she initially used a cuticle pusher, but when it proved to be too slow, she resorted to using a drill. Given that I'm typically not overly particular, I didn't closely observe her work until later on. However, upon closer examination, I noticed that she had not completely removed the old gel polish.

input:
This is a cool place.  I wonder how many people know that an Ouzaria is?  The ambience here is definitely upbeat - I'd rate it a great place for a group or first date.  They have a couple of semi-secluded tables in the back room that keeps it from getting too loud, but it's not a quiet romantic place.  

We brought my Mother-in-Law, who enjoys good food as long as it's not too weird.  I guess my wife is about the same, now that I think about it.  We tried three tapas plates; a three-cheese sampler, featuring feta, goat cheese and kasseri cheese, greek meatballs and pan-seared scallops.  We liked all three of these dishes.  The scallops were especially good - big and tender.   For tapas, they were pretty big portions, so keep this in mind.  The waitress suggested ordering one thing at a time, but we didn't heed her advice and ordered it all up front.   Two at a time would probably be a good idea.  Along with the tapas, we ordered a traditional Greek salad, which ended up being the lone clunker, surprisingly.  We just didn't like the dressing - too sweet for our tastes.  The gyro meat was fine, though, so maybe we'll just get a gyro next time.   One more thing:  The Spanish granacha (can't remember the label) was excellent for just $6 and a nice pour. 

Okay, now for the belly dancer:  She was cute and a good dancer, but I think this is just something that requires more alcohol on my part.  We did have a few laughs about it, though.  I opted not to get a dollar out to stuff in her skirt or whatever.   Fun but a little awkward. 

I've been to a few other Greek places in town that had better food, but for a night out, Momo's is definitely the choice.  We'll be back.

input: If you are shopping for any kind of Italian food product, you need not bother going anywhere but Claudio's.  First, you must understand the culture--Claudio's is old school.  They are family.  There is a reason everyone lines up and tolerates standing in line.  The product is THAT good.  These folks know their cheeses.  They know their food.  If you have a question, they will bend over to help you.  Other customers will too!  I'm "medigan" as they say, American....ie  I am not Italian.  Hanging in Claudio's makes me want to be!!  Going to Claudio's isn't like running to the Acme for a box of pasta----this is an EXPERIENCE.  Everyone should have an experience!
Rewrite this for me: If you're in search of any Italian food product, there is no need to go elsewhere apart from Claudio's. It is important to understand the nature of this place - Claudio's represents old-school Italian culture. They are like a family, and this is the reason why everyone is willing to wait in line. The quality of the products is truly exceptional. Their knowledge of cheeses and food in general is impressive. If you have any questions, they will go out of their way to assist you. Other customers will also be helpful. Being an American, not of Italian descent, spending time at Claudio's makes me wish I were Italian. Going to Claudio's is not like making a quick trip to the Acme for a box of pasta - it is an immersive experience. Everyone should have the chance to experience it!

input:
This hotel was so terrible and I can narrow it down to 4 things:

1. The price: Expect to pay a lot of money from the second you arrive. They charge $35 per person for a round trip shuttle ride to the airport. Our room was roughly $275 a night. It's an incredibly large hotel that offers a nail salon, a Godiva Chocolate store, about 9 restaurants and a few bars. But you'll pay dearly for any of those things - like $2.50 for a small bottle of soda. The hotel is designed to keep you in there and they charge you $15 for a round trip shuttle ride to the downtown Nashville area. 

2. The service: We called the front desk and were on hold for 20 minutes. We went to the front desk and waited in line for an hour. We waited around to ask the concierge questions. And each time we got, "I don't know" as the usual response. The cleaning staff was extraordinarily loud and they actually shouted as they went down the hall at 6:30 a.m.

3. The name: They call this place a resort but that is, by far, a misnomer. This place is a convention hotel, period. It's horrifically loud at all hours of the day because they host about 3 conventions at one time. Our windows faced one of the courtyards and there is music pumping there 24 hours a day. The walls are thin and you can hear *everything* happening in the neighboring rooms. (eww!) If you want to relax at a resort, don't stay here because with all those convention people, loud cleaning staff, 24 hour music and thin walls you will only end up with more stress.

4. The size: It's no joke that you will get lost in this hotel. It's inexplicably large. And when it hits noon, you should already be in one of the few restaurants because they fill up FAST. With several conventions happening at one time, getting a "quick bite" is not possible here. And there's not really any place close by, either. You can walk over to the mall for some fast food but plan enough time for your walk - getting out of the hotel takes at least 5 minutes.

I'm sure glad I was there for a convention and didn't pay out of my own pocket for this ridiculous hotel.
Rewrite this for me:
This hotel was extremely awful, and I can pinpoint four specific reasons for it:

1. The exorbitant prices: From the moment you arrive, be prepared to shell out a hefty amount of money. They charge $35 per person for a round trip shuttle ride to the airport. Furthermore, our room cost around $275 per night. Despite having numerous amenities like a nail salon, a Godiva Chocolate store, nine restaurants, and a few bars, they hike up the prices for everything. For instance, a small bottle of soda costs a whopping $2.50. Additionally, they charge $15 for a round trip shuttle ride to downtown Nashville, as the hotel aims to keep guests within its premises.

2. The appalling service: When we called the front desk, we were put on hold for 20 minutes. Waiting in line at the front desk took us a whole hour. Even when we sought assistance from the concierge, we received unsatisfactory responses such as "I don't know." The cleaning staff was excessively loud, and they actually shouted as they went down the hall at 6:30 a.m.

3. The misleading name: This place may be called a resort, but that is far from the truth. It is primarily a convention hotel, and as a result, it is disturbingly noisy at all times of the day due to hosting multiple conventions simultaneously. If you overlook the incessant 24/7 music in the courtyards, you will likely hear every single sound from neighboring rooms through the thin walls. If you were hoping to relax at a genuine resort, staying here will only cause you more stress due to the constant presence of convention-goers, loud cleaning staff, nonstop music, and inadequate soundproofing.

4. The overwhelming size: It's no exaggeration when I say that you can easily get lost in this hotel. Its sheer enormity is inexplicable. By noon, you need to secure a spot in one of the few restaurants, as they fill up rapidly. With multiple conventions happening simultaneously, grabbing a quick meal is simply impossible. Unfortunately, there aren't many nearby options either. You can walk over to the mall for some fast food, but be prepared to allocate at least 5 minutes just to exit the hotel.

I'm relieved to have attended a convention here and not bear the expenses of this absurd hotel out of my own pocket.

input:
I waited a long time to finally try this place and I have to say I was let down a bit. I tried the mandatory Dan Dan noodles. They were very flavorful and not too spicy. Nothing mind blowing here just a really good lo mein or spicy pasta dish with virtually no protein more or less. Also had the scallion pancakes. I was just in Chinatown recently at a place I also reviewed (first person from Yelp to do so) and they were way better there. ( I highly recommend you try that place) These were more like quesadillas laying flat where as the other ones jumped off the plate and were so much more crispy and substantial. The last appetizer I had was the Wontons in Chilli oil. These were just not good to me at all and one bite was all I needed. Basically it is steamed Wontons in a bowl with the soup being the chilli oil. Just heavy heavy choking heat with very little substance or taste. Take those same homemade wontons and pan fry them with some chilli peppers and a nice light sauce and you have could a real winner but I digress. Finally we tried the Talapia Medallions . These were fried to perfection but there were some greens mixed in that I could not chew through and had to discard via the old napkin trick which to me is a bit of a deal/star breaker.

The service was very good and the atmosphere very nice but I wouldn't go out of my way to eat here again. All I could think about was how much more I prefer Cantonese style where its all about flavors and you can add heat as you like it. I'm sure I could find better authentic Szechuan cuisine that better suits my taste just not here. It feels very commercialized and Americanized. I prefer the hole in the wall places where I am the only caucasian in the place a heck of a lot more.
Rewrite this for me:
After waiting for a long time, I finally got the chance to try this place. However, I was somewhat disappointed. I had the Dan Dan noodles, which were quite flavorful but not too spicy. They were decent, but nothing extraordinary – just a good lo mein or spicy pasta dish lacking in protein. I also ordered the scallion pancakes, but I recently had better ones in Chinatown (which I highly recommend you try). The ones here were more like flat quesadillas, whereas the others were extremely crispy and substantial.

Next, I tried the Wontons in Chilli oil as an appetizer. Unfortunately, they didn't appeal to me at all. One bite was enough to conclude that they lacked taste and substance. It was essentially steamed wontons floating in a bowl of chili oil soup, overwhelming with choking heat. Pan frying those homemade wontons with chili peppers and a light sauce could have made them a winner, but that wasn't the case here.

Lastly, we ordered the Talapia Medallions. They were fried perfectly, but there were some greens mixed in that were impossible to chew through. I had to discreetly remove them using the old napkin trick, which was a bit of a disappointment and made it less enjoyable.

The service was commendable, and the atmosphere was pleasant. However, I don't think I would make a special trip to eat here again. Throughout my experience, I couldn't help but long for the Cantonese style of cuisine – where flavors are emphasized, and you can customize the heat according to your preference. I'm confident I can find more authentic Szechuan cuisine elsewhere, as this place seemed quite commercialized and Americanized. I prefer the hidden gem establishments where I'm the only caucasian person in the restaurant.

input:

Tried again and success!!  Got there right when they opened and there was already people starting to file in.  Managed to get seated and served very quickly.  We both ordered the pancakes.  I had the butter pecan and O.M.G...  His bananas foster pancakes were good too but those butter pecan ones are the best (in my opinion).   The pancakes also come with 2 eggs and a meat.  Big fan of them offering turkey sausage and turkey bacon.   

Go.  It's awesome.  Just get there early and wear loose pants.

I highly recommend going there, it's awesome! Just remember to arrive early and wear loose pants.

input: The food is probably one of the more mediocre Chinese food I've had, but the main appeal of this place is renting a karaoke room for a large group of people and BYOing. input:
This update (and upgrade) to my review of Khyber is long overdue!

I think the most ringing summary is that I have since moved ~1 mile further away from the Khyber, and I still go there just as often.  I have now sampled most of the menu, but the truly excellent Southern barbecue is what usually calls to me.  You can't go wrong whether you pick the brisket, the ribs, the chicken, the pulled pork or a combo of the above.  Their mac and cheese remains my favorite side, and the addition of the very good coleslaw rounds out the experience.

I love the vibe of Kyber.  It usually pretty full, but they usually seem to have a table available for me (Yay!).  It is often loud, but never quite so loud that I wish it were quieter.  The staff is very knowledgeable, and happy to provide beer recommendations and taste tests of drafts.  They Khyber also manages to hit that sweet spot where I never end up being the most or least intoxicated person there!
Rewrite this for me:
I am long overdue in updating my review of Khyber, but this update is finally here! Despite moving a mile away, I still find myself visiting this place just as often. I have now tried almost everything on the menu, but the Southern barbecue remains the standout for me. Whether it's the brisket, ribs, chicken, pulled pork, or a combination, you can't go wrong. Their mac and cheese continues to be my favorite side dish, and the addition of their delicious coleslaw completes the whole experience.

What I love about Khyber is its vibrant atmosphere. It's usually packed, but there's always a table available for me (hooray!). It can get loud, but it's never so loud that I wish it were quieter. The staff is incredibly knowledgeable and always willing to suggest beer options or offer taste tests of drafts. Khyber manages to strike the perfect balance where I never find myself the most or least intoxicated person in the room!

input: Great  breads especially the German rye. My favorite breakfast is the poached eggs, cooked perfectly. For lunch, I go for the eggplant panini or  Laurie's salad.

input: Tony's really has surprisingly good Mexican food, which you wouldn't expect to find out here in Chalmette.  It's actually the best Mexican food I've had in Louisiana. input:

The hotel also offered many places to eat and relax. The casino was very clean and a joy to be in even if you don't gamble like myself. Easy checkout right from the room was a time saver. Well now off to explore Reno some more.
If your considering a hotel that is nice, clean, up to date this is the one.
Rewrite this for me: My husband and I are staying in Reno for the first time and we are absolutely amazed by this wonderful hotel. Our room is fantastic, complete with a spa and a steam room feature in the shower. The hotel has a variety of dining options and relaxation areas, which is truly convenient. Even though I'm not a gambler, I thoroughly enjoyed the clean and pleasant atmosphere of the casino. Surprisingly, I won $41.00 from a $1.00 slot machine! However, when we ventured out to see the rest of Reno, we were not as impressed as we were with our hotel. Fortunately, the easy checkout process from our room saved us time. Now, we're excited to explore more of what Reno has to offer. If you are looking for a nice, clean, and modern hotel, this is the one you should consider.
