To conclude our amazing evening, we indulged in a delightful dessert of fried bananas and ice cream. The service provided was exceptional and attentive. We have definitely made up our minds to revisit this place for more enjoyable experiences in the future!

input: I Love it here. The pizza is fantastic,  and the staff is very friendly. It's a great place to hang out with friends and family.
Rewrite this for me: I have a strong affection for this place. The quality of the pizza is outstanding, and the staff is incredibly welcoming. It serves as an excellent destination to spend time with loved ones and companions.

input: Went here the other day with some friends for a bite and a drink. Service was great as where the drinks ;) Will definitely be back!
Rewrite this for me: I went to this place recently with a group of friends to grab some food and drinks. The service was excellent, and the drinks were enjoyable 😉. I am definitely planning to return!

input: This place was on my list for all of the great reviews. The lamb was very flavorful, but the garlic Naan is just frozen from Trader Joe's. Also, the lamb was fairly expensive for the amount you get. Lastly, despite saying they take American Express at the door, the owner would not accept Amex. I will likely not return.
Rewrite this for me: I had high expectations for this place due to its stellar reviews. The lamb exceeded my expectations with its scrumptious flavor. However, I was disappointed to discover that the garlic Naan was simply frozen from Trader Joe's. Additionally, considering the portion size, the lamb was rather pricy. To add to my disappointment, despite the establishment's claim of accepting American Express, the owner refused to honor it. Considering these factors, it is highly unlikely that I will revisit this place.

input:
This little unassuming shop is tucked away in a strip mall full of furniture stores. Had it not been for Yelp, I would never have known it was here. Now, I won't be taking a trip to Brentwood without stopping for a scoop!

The flavors are quite varied and innovative. I had pumpkin and some sort of whipped cream cheese flavor--both were divine--which when mixed tasted just like pumpkin pie! The owner, Michael, is absolutely a sweetheart and is generous with the samples and the recommendations, and he's always coming up with new flavors to whip up. I can't wait to see what he concocts next!
Rewrite this for me:
Hidden in a strip mall dominated by furniture stores, this inconspicuous little shop would have gone unnoticed if not for the help of Yelp. Thanks to the discovery, I now refuse to visit Brentwood without indulging in a scoop from this delightful place!

The variety of flavors offered here is both diverse and innovative. I had the pleasure of trying the pumpkin and whipped cream cheese flavors, and they were truly divine. When combined, they tasted just like a slice of delectable pumpkin pie! The owner, Michael, is an absolute sweetheart who graciously provides samples and recommendations. He constantly dreams up new and exciting flavors to craft. I eagerly anticipate the next delightful creation he conjures up!

input: Great food and good coffee. Wish they had more of an espresso bar with coffee options, but food and baked goods are spectacular!
Rewrite this for me: The food and coffee here are amazing! My only wish is for an expansion of their coffee options, particularly in the form of an espresso bar. However, the delicious food and baked goods never fail to impress!

input:
holly grove is the best. I'm consistently impressed with their selection of produce. you can basically get everything (plus more stuff they don't have at the normal grocery store) except it's all local. we are so lucky to live in a place with a year round growing season, and we should really take advantage of that! (I will get off my high horse now lol). 

they also have locally raised meats, bread from local bakeries...it's just a great place to support local growers and makers. also there are always people wandering outside tending to the garden. it's a nice atmosphere. the only thing I dislike is the location - because I'm allll the way across town. that's not their fault, though.
Rewrite this for me:
Holly Grove is truly exceptional. The variety of produce they offer never fails to impress me. Their selection goes beyond what you can find at a typical grocery store, including unique items that are locally sourced. We are incredibly fortunate to reside in an area with a year-round growing season, and it is important that we capitalize on this opportunity! (Okay, I'll step down from my soapbox now, haha).

Furthermore, they also provide locally raised meats and bread from nearby bakeries. It is a remarkable place that supports local farmers and artisans. The presence of individuals caring for the garden outside contributes to a pleasant atmosphere. The only drawback for me is the location - it's quite a hike since I'm on the opposite side of town. However, that can't be blamed on Holly Grove, of course.

input:
We tried this place for the first time last night. Being a Saturday night during March Madness the service was a bit slow. The complimentary chips took longer to get to the table than my husband's salad did. Thankfully they had one of the nearby televisions playing a kid's movie to keep my 3 year old happy. Back to the chips, they are home made and were fantastic. I went the safe route and ordered a burger with seasoned fries. It was wonderful. My husband ordered the blackened chicken and while it was good it was a little over seasoned making it a tad too spicy. My daughter had the kid's macaroni and cheese. It looked wonderful but she couldn't stop eating the chips, LoL. The seating inside was a bit weird. There is a table about 2ft from the door to the women's bathroom. Maybe I'm weird for thinking it's weird but I ended up waiting until I got home to go. They offer a 15% military discount which was great. 

Overall I'd definitely recommend this place. I would have given it 5 stars if the service had been a little better.
Rewrite this for me:
Last night, we decided to try this place for the first time. It was a Saturday night during March Madness, so the service was a bit slow. Surprisingly, the complimentary chips took longer to arrive at our table compared to my husband's salad. Fortunately, they had a television playing a kid's movie nearby, which kept my 3-year-old entertained. Speaking of chips, they were homemade and absolutely fantastic. As for our main courses, I opted for the safe choice and ordered a burger with seasoned fries, which turned out to be wonderful. On the other hand, my husband ordered the blackened chicken, which was good but a bit over-seasoned, resulting in it being a tad too spicy. Our daughter had the kid's macaroni and cheese, which looked great, but she couldn't resist devouring the chips instead. 

The seating arrangement inside was a bit peculiar, with a table situated just 2 feet from the door to the women's bathroom. Maybe it's just me, but I found it odd and ended up waiting until I got home to use the restroom. On a positive note, they offer a 15% military discount, which was greatly appreciated. 

Overall, I would definitely recommend this place. However, I would have given it 5 stars if the service had been a bit better.

input: Decent hotel in downtown Tampa. Stayed in the suite with the fold out couch.  This place has a happy hour with FREE drinks, which we missed, but how cool. The complimentary breakfast was awesome.  Made to order omelets, fresh fruit, cereal, toast, bacon, sausage, home fries, juice and pastries.  Did I mention it was complimentary?   Easiest the best free breakfast I've ever had.  Room was nice and modern with two TV's etc.  Clean and a strong shower.
Rewrite this for me: Located in the heart of downtown Tampa, this hotel provided us with a satisfying stay in their suite equipped with a convenient fold-out couch. One of the standout features of this place was their enticing happy hour, offering free drinks, although unfortunately, we missed out on this opportunity. On a positive note, the complimentary breakfast provided was truly fantastic. From made-to-order omelets and fresh fruit, to cereal, toast, bacon, sausage, home fries, juice, and pastries, it covered all bases. I cannot stress enough that this complimentary breakfast was without a doubt the best I have ever experienced. The room itself boasted a nice and modern design, along with two TV's for our entertainment. The cleanliness of the room was commendable, and the shower provided a strong water pressure, leaving us refreshed and satisfied.

input: Very nice restaurant in the heart of downtown St. Petersburg with a nice homey feel to it. The burgers full of flavor and the arugula is a fine touch to the chicken and potato gratin meal.  I was not a fan of the cheese used in the potatoes gratin but will definitely be. Ack for the burger. Wine was a little high priced so I didn't get any. The atmosphere is very nice and so was our waitress.
Rewrite this for me: Located in the bustling downtown area of St. Petersburg, this restaurant stands out as a wonderful dining destination with a cozy and welcoming ambiance. The burgers here burst with an unparalleled depth of flavors, complemented perfectly by the addition of arugula in the delectable chicken and potato gratin dish. While I personally didn't quite fancy the cheese selection in the gratin, I will certainly be coming back to indulge in their succulent burgers. Although the wine prices were a bit steep for my liking, it did not hinder my overall enjoyment of the exquisite atmosphere and the top-notch service provided by our excellent waitress.

input: I have been coming to Cd Roma's for over 10 years. I love this place! The old locations was a bit more home style feeling and cozy and the new spot has a more modern vibe to it. I applaud the change in style with the change in times. Too many places get stuck doing the same thing over and over again. I am glad to see that the food is still delicious. The Chicken Parm, Eggplant Parm, house salad and Alfredo are some of my favorites and they have great pizza. The alfredo sauce is made to order and taste amazing with their breadsticks. Some appetizer items leave something to be desired like the frozen cheesesticks or calimari. I would love to see these replaced with better quality items. Overall, I still love this place and would choose it over Olive Garden any day. I do miss the homey old school vibe from the old location but I also miss the good old days when people talked to each other, fragglerock ruled and hip hop was Wu Tang Clan. Oh well....
Rewrite this for me: I have been a loyal patron of Cd Roma's for more than a decade, and I absolutely adore this place! The previous establishment had a comforting, homestyle ambiance, while the new location embodies a more modern, contemporary feel. I appreciate the change in style, as it shows their adaptability to the ever-evolving times. Unlike many other dining establishments that become stagnant, Cd Roma's continues to innovate. I am thrilled that their delectable cuisine remains consistent throughout the years. Their Chicken Parm, Eggplant Parm, house salad, and Alfredo dishes are personal favorites of mine, and their pizza is outstanding. The made-to-order Alfredo sauce pairs wonderfully with their breadsticks, resulting in a truly amazing flavor. However, some of their appetizers, such as the frozen cheesesticks or calamari, fall short of expectations. It would be fantastic if they could replace these items with higher quality alternatives. Nevertheless, overall, I still adore this place and would choose it over Olive Garden any day. Although I do miss the cozy, old-school vibe from the previous location, I also yearn for a time when people engaged in meaningful conversations, "Fraggle Rock" was all the rage, and Wu-Tang Clan ruled the hip hop scene. Nostalgia often tugs at my heart, but alas, times change.

input:
The Waffle House has consistent quality wherever you go. I'm not really fond of their business model with their yelling and very small dining area, but I get it. 
I still look forward to going for breakfast.
Rewrite this for me: Despite not being a fan of their business model which includes yelling and a cramped dining area, I appreciate the Waffle House for its consistent quality. I still eagerly anticipate my breakfast visits to the establishment.

input:
Henry was a rock star  getting us into a storage locker. He was knowledge, professional, courteous and extremely personable. They were gracious to our four legged girl "Marley" who had to check them out, too.
Great experience in obtaining a storage locker!
We recommend!!!
Rewrite this for me: Henry, the rock star of storage lockers, effortlessly guided us through the process. He exuded knowledge, professionalism, courtesy, and the charm of a true people person. Moreover, he even extended his graciousness to our beloved four-legged companion, Marley, ensuring her comfort during the visit. Obtaining a storage locker has never been more enjoyable! We wholeheartedly recommend Henry and his fantastic service.

input: Phenomenal restaurant. Great location. Great ambience.  Great food and most of all great drinks. If you go, grab a seat at the  bar. Jared is a true mixologist and has created all of the cocktails on the menu. Don't be afraid to challenge him. As for food, I have never had a bad meal and I have had 100's at this point and pretty much everything on the menu. You won't go wrong with anything on the menu. Listen for the specials...they are always wonderful.
Rewrite this for me: This restaurant is absolutely amazing. It is situated in a fantastic location and has a wonderful atmosphere. The food is outstanding, and the drinks are even better. Make sure to secure a seat at the bar where you will meet Jared, an exceptional mixologist who has crafted every cocktail on the menu. Don't hesitate to test his skills. When it comes to food, I have never had a negative experience, having tried countless dishes from their extensive menu. Everything on the menu is guaranteed to impress. Additionally, be sure to pay attention to the daily specials, as they are consistently delightful.

input:
I know people RAVE about this place, but frankly I find it A-OK. 

It is a great location, the food is fresh, and they have a great variety of vegan options. But I find it pretty blah otherwise. I've had the crispy ranch and the curry tofu and enjoyed both of them, but I feel like I expect more out of a specialty vegan place. I did really like chick'n in the crispy ranch. The fries are pretty good too. My green lemonade was way too sweet and lemonade-y for me. 

If I were you, I would try it because people love it so much and you get some unique items. But for the $10 range for a lunch item, I wouldn't  say it's nothing AMAZING.
Rewrite this for me:
Despite the overwhelming praise for this place, I personally think it's just alright. While the location is excellent and they offer a nice selection of fresh vegan dishes, it doesn't really impress me otherwise. The crispy ranch and curry tofu dishes were enjoyable, but as a specialty vegan restaurant, I expected more. I must admit, the chick'n in the crispy ranch and the fries are quite good. However, I found the green lemonade to be overly sweet and lemony for my taste. 

If I were you, I'd give it a try since it's highly regarded by many and offers unique menu items. However, considering the price range of around $10 for a lunch item, I wouldn't describe it as anything particularly amazing.

input: Guy at the counter was rude, the place was filthy, and all around horrible! Would/will not recommend this place at all!
Rewrite this for me: The individual behind the counter displayed a discourteous attitude, and the establishment itself was in a state of disarray, overall leaving me with an unpleasant experience. I strongly advise against recommending this place.

input: My last full day in New Orleans and I HAD to come here!! Came in the pouring rain too!! I really wanted some authentic New Orleans style food (yes... it's still authentic if it's vegan, I don't care what you say! Lol!) Jamone was nice enough to give me a little taste of everything, so I could pick. That just made it harder, because I wanted it ALL!!. I'm telling you,  there is no bad choice here. Everything was SO good and flavorful!! And the bread pudding was the topper for me! I would be a regular if I lived out here! Do yourself a favor and come try this place. Come hungry too, so you can have it all, like me!  Oh...and the other great thing.  This is one vegan place where they give you a TON of food without emptying your wallet!!! Amazing food and service!!
Rewrite this for me: I couldn't miss visiting this place on my last day in New Orleans, even if it meant braving the pouring rain! I was really craving some authentic New Orleans style food, and yes, even if it's vegan, it's still authentic in my book, regardless of what others may argue! Lately, Jamone kindly let me sample a little bit of everything to help me decide. However, that just made it more difficult because I wanted to try it all! Let me tell you, there's no wrong choice here. Every dish was incredibly delicious and bursting with flavor! The cherry on top was definitely the bread pudding. If I lived here, I would become a regular at this place without hesitation! You should definitely do yourself a favor and come give this place a try. Make sure to come with a hearty appetite so you can enjoy it all, just like I did! And the best part? This vegan spot serves generous portions without breaking the bank. Amazing food and service, hands down!

input:
Magical vegan heaven. My wife and I stopped here on a detour from our route back home to Boston and she (a non-vegan) devoured their Philly steak. I literally had to pry her away from ordering more; I don't blame her at all though because the food was damn good. I had the curry tofu wrap and it was delicious. The place is pretty small with limited seating so a lot of people were taking (and I'm assuming regularly take) their food to go, so I'd be wary of this if you're wanting to sit in. 

But yeah this place rocks. Their kale lemonade alone is worth the 5 stars. Next time we're in Philly this place will be among the first in which we stuff our faces.
Rewrite this for me: This vegan establishment is like a magical paradise. While on our way back to Boston, my wife (who is not a vegan) and I made a detour to try their food. To my surprise, my wife couldn't resist their Philly steak and I had to convince her to stop ordering more. I can't blame her though because the food was absolutely delicious. I opted for the curry tofu wrap and it was fantastic. The place is quite small and seating is limited, so many people were taking their food to go. If you prefer dining in, be cautious. However, this place is truly amazing. Their kale lemonade alone deserves a perfect rating. We will definitely make it a priority to visit this place first on our next trip to Philly, so we can indulge in their offerings.

input: My wife and I LOVE this place. The management is always very attentive and the service is excellent! Things to try: Tiger Roll, Pink Lady Roll, Tornado Roll. Ask for Billy he's our favorite. I highly recommend this place of others in the same area. Enjoy!
Rewrite this for me: My spouse and I absolutely adore this establishment! The staff is consistently attentive, and the service provided is top-notch. We highly recommend trying out their Tiger Roll, Pink Lady Roll, and Tornado Roll. If you visit, make sure to ask for Billy as he is our favorite. Among all the options in the vicinity, we strongly suggest giving this place a go. Have a great time!

input: Great place for lunch in NOLA. Love their fried chicken, and the red beans and rice is yummy too. It's a staple on our trips to town. Staff is friendly and attentitve and prices are great.
Rewrite this for me: Looking for a fantastic lunch spot in NOLA? You can't go wrong with this place! Their fried chicken is absolutely scrumptious, and the red beans and rice are equally delightful. Whenever we make our way to town, it's a must-visit for us, as it never fails to impress. The staff is incredibly friendly and attentive, ensuring you feel well taken care of. Plus, the prices are reasonable and won't break the bank.

input: I live in the neighborhood so I try to frequent Mint as much as I can. No choice is a bad choice! Also the Taro Tapioca Smoothie is the perfect cure for a sweet tooth.
Rewrite this for me: Because I reside in the area, I make it a point to visit Mint as often as possible. Every option on their menu is amazing! Moreover, if you have a craving for something sweet, the Taro Tapioca Smoothie is an absolute delight.

input: The salsa and guacamole is. Made fresh daily. The chips are home made as well. The shrimp burrito was huge but was tasty and fresh. The wait staff was just average.
Rewrite this for me: Fresh daily, our salsa and guacamole are made from scratch. The chips are also homemade to perfection. Despite its enormous size, the shrimp burrito delivered a delightful and refreshing taste. However, the service provided by the wait staff was only average.

input:
To be honest, I was kind of disappointed with this place. I really wanted to like it, and it has gotten so many positive reviews, so I thought it was a sure thing, but it was just a little underwhelming. Not bad, just not amazing. I had the costanza, and the fillings were tasty, but the crust was disappointing. It was way too bread-y, as opposed to doughy, and when I think of a calzone, I think of dough like pizza dough- this was not that. The calzones are a good size, but they were a little skimpy with the meat fillings. Probably the most disappointing part was the dessert- we got the apple pie calzone, and it just had a really weird spice to it- something other than cinnamon that I couldn't put my finger on. It also didn't have that many chunks of apples inside- it was almost pureed apple. Meh. 

I like the vibe of this place and it's close and convenient to where i live, so I really want to like it, but I just wasn't thrilled with it the first time. Perhaps I'll give it one more shot, but it seems a little overhyped!
Rewrite this for me: Honestly, I was a bit let down by this place. I had high hopes since it had received numerous positive reviews, but it didn't quite live up to my expectations. It wasn't terrible, just not outstanding. I ordered the costanza and while the fillings were flavorful, the crust left much to be desired. It had a bread-like texture instead of the doughy goodness I associate with calzones. The portions were decent, but they could have been more generous with the meat fillings. The dessert, an apple pie calzone, was the most disappointing. It had an odd spice that I couldn't quite identify, definitely not cinnamon. Additionally, there weren't many apple chunks inside, almost like it was pureed. Overall, I appreciate the ambiance and convenient location, so I really wanted to enjoy it. However, my first experience fell short. I may give it another chance, but it seems somewhat overhyped.

input:
An amazing view, impeccable professional service great fare,don't  skip a visit to this Philadelphia gem. Nick, who is a stellar, incredible server, recommended a lovely 2010 Bordeaux-Chateau Font Merlet which complemented the Tuna Tartare and Steak Tataki.

This is a must see in Philadelphia. After witnessing a fabulous nighttime view, I can't wait to return to check out the spectacular sunsets.
Rewrite this for me: Make sure to visit this Philadelphia gem for its incredible view, outstanding service, and delicious food. Nick, an exceptional server, suggested pairing the Tuna Tartare and Steak Tataki with the delightful 2010 Bordeaux-Chateau Font Merlet. Trust me, this place is a must-visit in Philadelphia. I was absolutely blown away by the stunning nighttime view and I'm already excited to come back and experience the breathtaking sunsets.

input: The food is very good but the ability to turnover the tables is a huge problem on busy days. Waited over an hour to be seated today and about an hour to get food. I just do not have 2 hours available to get breakfast. They do not have the proper staffing to quickly get the food out and clear tables in a timely fashion. There were many upset people there due to the time to wait. While we were eating there were 2 empty tables for at least 15 minutes that they did not seat anyone at yet when we left there was a longer line than when I arrived which we waited an hour to be seated. The workers were trying but were simply overwhelmed. Management needs to do a better job handling the staffing schedules. I will not be coming back due to this experience.
Rewrite this for me: Although the food is delicious, the issue of table turnover poses a significant problem during busy days. Today, I had to wait for over an hour to be seated and then wait another hour to receive my food. Unfortunately, I cannot afford to allocate two hours for breakfast. The restaurant lacks sufficient staff to efficiently prepare and clear tables in a timely manner, resulting in many frustrated customers enduring long wait times. As we were eating, two empty tables remained unoccupied for at least 15 minutes, while the line of waiting customers had grown longer by the time we left, even though we had already waited an hour for our table. The employees were doing their best but were clearly overwhelmed by the workload. The management must improve their handling of staffing schedules. Regrettably, I will not be returning to this establishment after this experience.

input:
Aside from the occasional Eggs Benny, whenever I go out for breakfast, I always order the same...eggs, bacon, hashbrowns and wheat toast with a side of salsa if they have it. 
And that's exactly what I ordered today.
The hashbrowns were undercooked for my taste, so next time I'll ask for them to be crispy/well done. Everything else was quite good. Better than the Cajun Kitchen on Chapala, but not as good as the CK in Goleta.

Thankfully all of the special requests that I DID make were taken care of.

I'm super picky about my breakfast. 
Who am I kidding...I'm super picky about everything, lol.

Large portions(leftovers for tomorrow), super affordable(more so than CK), and loved sitting on their well shaded patio(no patio at CK).
There was one server taking care of 5 tables, she was great and very cheerful. No complaints about the service.

Terraza means balcony/terrace in Spanish and that's exactly why I would come here instead of other breakfast places that don't have one.

Next on the agenda...
Check out their lunch items.
Rewrite this for me:
Whenever I decide to have breakfast out, I usually stick to my go-to order of eggs, bacon, hashbrowns, and wheat toast with a side of salsa if available. Today, I stuck to my routine and ordered exactly that. Unfortunately, the hashbrowns were not cooked to my liking. They were undercooked, so next time I'll make sure to request them crispy or well done. However, everything else was quite delicious. It didn't surpass the quality of the Cajun Kitchen on Chapala, but it was better than the CK in Goleta.

Luckily, all the special requests I made were taken care of, and I appreciate that.

I have high standards when it comes to breakfast, and to be honest, I'm just picky all around, haha.

The portions were generous, so I'll have leftovers for tomorrow, and the prices were very reasonable, even more so than at CK. I particularly enjoyed sitting on their shaded patio, which CK lacks.

Despite having only one server for five tables, she did a fantastic job and remained cheerful throughout. I have no complaints about the service.

The name "Terraza" means balcony/terrace in Spanish, and that's precisely why I prefer coming here over other breakfast places that don't offer such outdoor seating.

Now, it's time to explore their lunch options.

input:
This is an all you can eat place that at $27/adult isn't bad.  But if you ordered from the regular menu, you come to realize just how mediocre the quality is.  Maki rolls are OK, but mine were so cold they had clearly been premade and sat in the fridge.  Oyster ponzu was missing the ponzu and the coating was really heavy - like an A+W onion ring. 

So if you are really hungry and want to eat several plates of rolls and greasy tempura then this is for you. Granted sometimes that is just what you're craving. But avoid the squid.
Rewrite this for me:
This place offers unlimited food for $27 per adult, which is a decent price. However, if you decide to order from the regular menu, you will realize that the quality is quite average. The maki rolls are acceptable, but the ones I had were unexpectedly cold, indicating that they were premade and refrigerated. The oyster ponzu lacked the ponzu sauce and had a thick, heavy coating similar to an A+W onion ring. 

If you're extremely hungry and in the mood for multiple plates of rolls and greasy tempura, then this place might be suitable for you. Sometimes, that's exactly what you crave. However, I would recommend avoiding the squid.

input: I called them after calling another locksmith who was rude to me on the phone. Anyway I called them in the morning and they sent someone out in 20 min. they were done in less than one hour and I received 4 free keys too. their service can't be beat.
Rewrite this for me: After having a negative experience with one locksmith who was rude to me on the phone, I decided to give this company a call. Bright and early in the morning, I reached out to them and within just 20 minutes, they had someone dispatched to assist me. In less than one hour, they completely resolved my issue and to top it off, I was pleasantly surprised to receive four complimentary keys. Their exceptional service truly cannot be surpassed.

input:
This place is VERY crowded and not in a good way - unless you enjoy smelling other people's BO while you eat and drink. Gag! I guess the smell of the patrons matches the smell of the bathrooms which are also gag worthy and dirty. 

The prices aren't really great for the meh food available. Service was also meh. A few times we wondered if our server was every coming back. There are so many better options in Philly as a foodie city to try, so why waste your time and money here? Pass and head somewhere else.
Rewrite this for me:
This place is excessively overcrowded in a negative sense. Unless you have a liking for enduring the scent of other individuals' body odor while you dine and drink, it is not an enjoyable experience. It is truly off-putting! In addition, the odor from the customers somehow matches the foul smell of the disgustingly dirty bathrooms. 

The prices for the mediocre food on offer are far from appealing. The quality of service is also lackluster. Numerous times, we found ourselves questioning whether our server would ever return. There are numerous superior dining options in the food-centric city of Philly, so why waste your time and money here? It's best to move on and choose somewhere else to go.

input: Good beer selection, knowledgeable staff. Had I not ordered food here it would have an enjoyable experience. Some how received undercooked inedible Fries, one well done burger and one burger medium rare.... both burgers were served on buns that felt straight out of the refrigerator, slightly hard and cold. If you're drunk the foods good, don't eat it sober, plus add in service that was lackluster at best. We couldn't even eat the food and left it untouched. We told the the bartender no we didn't want it and what was wrong with it. Charged us full price.
Rewrite this for me: The beer selection was impressive, and the staff was knowledgeable. However, the experience could have been enjoyable if I hadn't ordered food. Unfortunately, the fries were undercooked and inedible, while one burger was well done and the other was medium rare. To make matters worse, both burgers were served on cold and slightly hard buns straight from the refrigerator. If you're intoxicated, the food might be passable, but I would not recommend eating it while sober. Additionally, the service we received was lackluster at best. We were unable to eat the food and left it untouched. When we informed the bartender that we didn't want it and explained the issues, we were still charged the full price.

input:
My first experience did mot go well due to the heavy accents of the employees. I called ahead so my order would be ready for me to pick up and it was, it just was not what I ordered. They are nice people and corrected my order but instead of simply picking up my food I had to wait 20 minutes To get my original order. When all was said and done, the food was good.

I was nearby and decided to give them a second chance. This time I ordered a pizza steak and I was really impressed! I need to have a couple more before I can declare them my new favorite pizza steak. Plenty of mozzarella cheese and the roll is stuffed with meat and just enough sauce. It's looking like this place is a lot better than my first impression.
Rewrite this for me:
Due to the heavy accents of the employees, my initial experience was not favorable. Despite calling ahead for my order, it was prepared but not as I had requested. Thankfully, the employees were kind enough to rectify the situation, but it resulted in a 20-minute wait to receive my original order. However, in the end, the food turned out to be quite delicious.

Deciding to give them another chance, I found myself nearby and placed an order for a pizza steak. To my surprise, I was thoroughly impressed! I might just need to try a couple more before declaring them my new favorite, as the pizza steak had an abundance of mozzarella cheese, a generous amount of meat, and just the right amount of sauce. It seems that this place has exceeded my initial expectations.

input:
The longest bar in the City!  For as crazy busy as the Happy Hours are, the Friday and Saturday late night crowds are really relaxed and there's always a place to sit.  This is the perfect place on a Saturday night after a show at the Troc if you don't want to go to Chinatown or a Dive bar.   I've been walking over after shows at the Electric Factory lately and it's THE place to unwind after standing up for 3 hours.  

IBP has all kinds of sports packages so it's a great place to go to watch that out of town football or baseball game.  The upstairs bar has pool tables and a separate jukebox.

input:
Four stars for the beer, atmosphere and usually service. There is a reason this place is always packed! Half price beer during a generous happy hour, a huge deck that welcomes dogs, and delicious key lime pie.   Sadly, said deck allows smoking, and there is usually lots of it. I wish they at least had a nonsmoking side. 

If giving a review just based on the food, I would give it a two. The pretzels are ok, but the cheese dip is Velveeta nastiest. As a native Wisconsinite, I take offense at plastic cheese. Then, there's the pretzel bun sandwiches. I've sampled the chicken, brat and Italian sausage. It's pricey, considering it comes with potato chips (seriously guys?! Get a fryer!) and just ok. The buns were kind of soggy and the overall experience underwhelming, especially knowing the epic sandwiches for sale next door. I wish the Village pub would focus on what it's best that, serving beer, and let us bring Mitchell's sandwiches over.
Rewrite this for me:
This place deserves four stars for its great selection of beer, enjoyable atmosphere, and typically good service. The fact that it's always packed is a testament to its popularity. During their generous happy hour, you can even get half-priced beer. Additionally, they have a spacious deck where dogs are welcome, and they serve delicious key lime pie. However, the downside is that the deck allows smoking, which can be bothersome as it's usually quite prevalent. It would be great if they had a separate section for non-smokers.

Now, if I were to judge this place solely based on the food, I would give it a two-star rating. The pretzels are decent, but the cheese dip made with Velveeta is quite unpleasant. As a native Wisconsinite, I find it offensive to serve plastic cheese. Furthermore, their pretzel bun sandwiches, which come with potato chips instead of fries, are overpriced and mediocre. I've tried the chicken, brat, and Italian sausage options, but they all left me underwhelmed. The buns were often soggy, and overall, it didn't live up to the hype, especially when you consider the amazing sandwiches available from the neighboring shop, Mitchell's. I believe the Village pub should focus more on what they're best at – serving beer – and allow us to bring our own Mitchell's sandwiches.

input: Could not be more pleased with this establishment. Always clean and has a good feel, like the employees there actually enjoy their job. Rewrite this for me: I am extremely satisfied with this establishment. It is consistently clean and has a positive ambiance, with employees who genuinely seem to enjoy their work. I am now a loyal customer of Modern Laundry, and doing laundry has become just another quick task on my to-do list. Thank you!

input: Food and atmosphere is nice. As one should expect in the CBD. Sometimes the back room can be stuffy on a busy day. I recommend the raw oysters and burgers. A few dollars on the high side for lunch.

input: Great choice in a small shop. Worth the drive. The wine cakes are excellent! Just went here for first time based on yelp reviews and will definitely be going back

input:
I am not known for favorable restaurant reviews.  Most of them below my radar.
The Love is different.  
  We had a Father's Day lunch that was exceptional.
There is little left off the menu and we were hard pressed to make a choice from the wonderful selections listed.  Our waiter was professional and accommodating.  Lovely atmosphere, light and bright.  I was amazed that the inside of my omelet was HOT. A little surprise thrown in with my Potatos..........roasted peppers, and onions.
Greens on every plate. Mine had warm spinach salad as well. My husband had the Belgium waffles made with corn meal and garnished with Blueberry butter.  They use our favorite La Columbe coffee.
Nothing left to wish for.
Rewrite this for me: I don't have a reputation for giving favorable restaurant reviews, with most of them going unnoticed by me. However, The Love is an exception. Our Father's Day lunch there was absolutely outstanding. The menu had so many amazing options, it was difficult to decide what to order. Our waiter was incredibly professional and accommodating. The atmosphere was delightful - bright and airy. I was surprised to find that the inside of my omelet was still hot. To my pleasure, the potatoes came with a little surprise addition of roasted peppers and onions. Every plate came with a side of greens, and my dish even had a warm spinach salad. My husband enjoyed the Belgian waffles made with cornmeal and topped with blueberry butter. The restaurant also served our favorite La Columbe coffee. There was truly nothing more we could have asked for.

input:
Not bad. Sushi roll was good but options were limited. Hibachi grill: i got steak...chef asked me 2x how i like mine-medium...Still ended up with well done. Rest of my group had chicken which all voiced lacked seasoning. 

Beware they DO NOT have a late happy hour 8-11 as advertised on their website. We asked the staff about it and they claimed 8-11 was for a different location. Their website nowhere indicates the happy hour is for a specific location nor does the website indicate they have multiple locations at all.
Rewrite this for me:
The overall experience wasn't bad. The sushi roll was enjoyable, although the options were somewhat limited. As for the hibachi grill, I ordered steak and the chef confirmed twice that I wanted it cooked medium, but it ended up being well done. The rest of my group had chicken, and everyone agreed that it lacked seasoning.

It's important to note that their advertised late happy hour from 8-11 is misleading. We specifically asked the staff about it and they informed us that the happy hour is only valid at a different location. Their website does not mention anything about the happy hour being exclusive to a particular location, nor does it disclose that they have multiple locations.

input:
I saw a deal on Groupon for Lee How Fook recently and after I read the reviews on Yelp, I was really excited to check this place out.  Unfortunately, I just didn't enjoy this restaurant and was pretty disappointed.

Lee How Fook is pretty small, but that didn't make it lose any points in my book.  I could see it getting really busy (especially since there are only about 10 tables available), so I would definitely suggest making reservations if you're going on a weekend.  The service wasn't bad, but when I asked some questions about some dishes on the menu, I had a hard time understanding what she was trying to say.  

Okay now to the main course - food!  For appetizers, we ordered the pan seared pork dumplings and sui mai.  Both appetizers were delicious and the dipping sauce was really good.  For the entrees, we ordered the sweet & sour chicken, pan fried noodle with shrimp, and pan fried noodle with beef and black bean sauce.  The sweet & sour chicken was awful - more sweet than sour - and the vegetables in it were really undercooked (pretty much raw).  (I do have to admit that I like things spicy, so maybe this dish just wasn't for me.)  For both pan fried noodle dishes, they were blah with a side of blah.  The beef dish was supposed to be spicy, but I just didn't taste any heat.  I left here full, but unsatisfied.
Rewrite this for me:
After spotting a deal on Groupon, I was enticed to try out Lee How Fook especially after reading great reviews on Yelp. However, my experience at the restaurant turned out to be quite disappointing.

Despite its small size, Lee How Fook didn't lose any points in my eyes. With only about 10 tables available, I could foresee it getting crowded, especially on weekends. Hence, it is advisable to make reservations beforehand. While the service was acceptable, I did encounter some difficulty understanding the server when asking about certain menu items.

Now, let's move on to the most important aspect - the food! For starters, we ordered the scrumptious pan-seared pork dumplings and the delightful sui mai, both accompanied by a delicious dipping sauce. As for the main courses, we went with the sweet and sour chicken, pan-fried noodles with shrimp, and pan-fried noodles with beef in black bean sauce. Regrettably, the sweet and sour chicken turned out to be a disappointment, leaning more towards the sweet side and the vegetables in it were severely undercooked, almost raw. (Although I must confess that I have a preference for spiciness, so perhaps this dish wasn't tailored to my taste buds.) As for the pan-fried noodle dishes, they were rather lackluster and left much to be desired. The beef dish was meant to be spicy, but I didn't detect any heat at all. By the end of the meal, I left feeling both full and unsatisfied.

input: The hot chicken is probably one of the best fried chickens I've ever eaten, and I'm from the South/NC and have had quite a bit of it. However, the price for the small portion size is really expensive. The drinks here are fantastic too.
Rewrite this for me: The hot chicken at this place is undeniably one of the most delicious fried chickens I've ever tasted, and coming from a Southerner/North Carolinian who has tried plenty, that's saying something. input: I could write a lengthy review, persuasive and layered to hit all the right points. But why do that when Lee How Fook makes food that does it for you? Long story short they have some of the best general tso chicken I have eaten to date. Try it for yourself and get back at me. - Coolie
Rewrite this for me: I possess the ability to craft a detailed and captivating review, carefully incorporating all essential elements. However, there is no need for such an effort since Lee How Fook's food speaks for itself. In a nutshell, their general tso chicken is simply unparalleled, surpassing any other I have ever tasted. input:
Thank you Chef John Besh!  My husband and I stayed at the Hilton hotel on St. Charles. One of my main goals was to find some delicious New Orleans grinds.  I was starving when we arrived and didn't want to do any research on Yelp for a place to eat.  Thank God Luke was connected to our hotel!!!  We ended up eating here 3 times over 5 days.  It's usually full of business suits, but that doesn't bother me when the food is so good.

All the traditional dishes were good, but the huge surprise was the burger.  I was against ordering a burger while I was in New Orleans, because I wanted to try as many local eats as possible... and you can find burgers anywhere.  I overheard this lady raving about how delicious her burger was, so I had to order it the next time we ate there.  She was absolutely right!  It was one of the best burgers I've ever had!  It was huge, juicy, and packed with flavor.  I also highly recommend getting their bread pudding a la mode.  It was mouth-watering good and straight out the oven!
Rewrite this for me:
Chef John Besh, a huge thank you goes out to you! My husband and I had the pleasure of staying at the Hilton hotel on St. Charles during our recent trip. Among our objectives, finding some delectable New Orleans cuisine was at the top of the list. Upon arrival, I was famished and had no desire to search through Yelp for dining options. Thankfully, Luke, a restaurant connected to our hotel, came to our rescue!!! Surprisingly enough, we found ourselves returning to this establishment three times throughout our five-day stay. While it may attract a predominantly business-suited crowd, that fact didn't bother me one bit when the food was as marvelous as it was.

Although all the customary dishes were quite good, it was the burger that truly astounded us. Admittedly, I initially resisted the idea of ordering a burger while in New Orleans, as I sought to savor as many local delicacies as possible, and burgers can be found anywhere. However, fate introduced me to a lady who couldn't stop praising the heavenly taste of her own burger. Intrigued, I felt compelled to try it on our subsequent visit, and let me tell you, she was absolutely right! Without a doubt, it was one of the most outstanding burgers I have ever had the pleasure of experiencing. It boasted an impressive size, succulent juiciness, and an explosion of flavors. Taking my recommendation to heart, do not miss out on the heavenly bread pudding a la mode. Fresh out of the oven, it was simply irresistible and made my taste buds dance with delight.

input: Came down here for some of their tasty fish tacos to find out that they have closed this location.

input:

He gave me a price quote in about 30sec and gave me an accurate time frame as to when he could get to Squaw. He even called when he was running a few minutes late. We enjoyed a nice happy hour in the meantime and when he got to the parking lot, I think it took him less  than 4min to get our key code and create us some new keys. Thanks for saving the day! Honest, quick service. Hope I never need to call them again under the same circumstances, but they'll be the first I call I make if I lose another set of keys. (Alpine accepts AAA).

Jacob, who had clearly dealt with similar situations before, responded promptly. He provided a price quote within 30 seconds and gave me an accurate timeframe for when he could arrive at Squaw. Impressively, he even called to inform me that he would be running a few minutes behind schedule. During the wait, my companions and I enjoyed a pleasant happy hour. Once Jacob arrived at the parking lot, it took him less than 4 minutes to retrieve our key code and create new keys for us. We were extremely grateful for his honest and swift service. Although I hope to never encounter the same circumstances again, if I ever lose another set of keys, Alpine will definitely be the first company I call (plus they accept AAA).

input:
I finally made it to Farmhaus last Saturday, and it was worth the wait.  

As expected for a weekend, it was crowded.  We arrived about 15 minutes early and had to wait on the bench back by the bathrooms for a few minutes.  However, as I said, we were earlier than they anticipated, and they got us to the bar as soon as seats opened up.  They wisely gave us a copy of the menu to be prepared once we were seated, and we did indeed plan our entire meal in advance.  This was helpful, because we were actually seated about 20 minutes late, and I was about to eat the menu itself as I drooled over the descriptions!  

The smoked fish dip and escolar with prawns were fantastic- the standouts of the meal.  The mushroom salad and tapenade were also very good.  The meatloaf was good, but a little on the dry and bland side.  I wanted to get the nachos, but there were no other takers in my group....next time....

Service was good.  It was a bit shaky at times, but it was slammed the whole time we were there and that small space must be tough to work in.  

I would love to go back and check out their blue place special lunches...I have heard amazing reviews.  I think I will head back for dinner when there is outdoor seating, as I think that would add to the experience.
Rewrite this for me:
Last Saturday, I finally had the opportunity to visit Farmhaus, and it was definitely worth the wait. As expected on a weekend, the restaurant was crowded. We arrived about 15 minutes early and had to wait near the bathrooms on a bench for a few minutes. However, we were earlier than anticipated, so as soon as seats became available, they escorted us to the bar. They wisely provided us with a copy of the menu while we waited, allowing us to plan our entire meal in advance. This was quite helpful since we were seated about 20 minutes late, and I found myself drooling over the menu descriptions to the point where I almost considered eating it!

The smoked fish dip and escolar with prawns were absolutely fantastic and truly stood out in our meal. The mushroom salad and tapenade were also exceptionally good. Although the meatloaf was decent, it leaned towards the dry and bland side. I wanted to order the nachos, but unfortunately, nobody else in my group was interested. Maybe next time!

In terms of service, it was generally good. There were some moments where it seemed a bit shaky, but considering how busy they were the whole time we were there, it's understandable given the limited space they have to work in.

I would love to go back and try their special blue plate lunches, as I've heard rave reviews about them. Additionally, I think it would be great to visit for dinner when outdoor seating is available, as I believe that would enhance the overall experience.

input: This restaurant is seriously lacking in customer service!  We have dined many times at Dish.  We like the food.  We made a reservation two weeks ahead for 3 people.  When we arrived we were seated at the smallest table in the restaurant which barely fits two people.  The table next to us had an extra person added at the end, his back was literally a couple of inches from our table.  We asked for a table that would accomdate three people and not involve eating with someone's large back at our very tiny table.  We were rudely informed that it was a take or leave it situation.  It was very frustrating since we booked this as a special night out weeks earlier.  Unfortunately, we are writing this restraurant off our list.
Rewrite this for me: The customer service at this restaurant is seriously lacking. Despite enjoying the food and making a reservation for three people two weeks in advance, we were seated at the smallest table in the whole place, barely suitable for two people. To make matters worse, an extra person was squeezed into the adjacent table, with their back only inches away from ours. When we politely requested a table that could accommodate all three of us without having someone's large back in such close proximity, we were met with rude and inflexible responses. This situation was particularly frustrating as we had planned and looked forward to this special night out well in advance. Unfortunately, due to this experience, we have made the decision to remove this restaurant from our list.

input: This restaurant was pretty good; i'll admit it! I went here in the late evening with my boyfriend to have a nice date! He insisted on us ordering a milkshake and i'm SO GLAD that he did. I couldn't tell what it was but i just got a really strange vibe from the restaurant. Maybe i'm just being crazy!
Rewrite this for me: I must confess, this restaurant was quite impressive! I ventured here for a delightful evening date with my boyfriend, and it turned out to be a wonderful experience. He insisted that we try their milkshake, and I am incredibly grateful that he did. To say the least, it was among the finest milkshakes I have ever had in my entire life. The food and service were also satisfying, but there was an indescribable uneasiness that lingered in the air. Perhaps I am merely overthinking things!

input:
I was so disappointed when this opened; I was hoping for Nashville's first real authentic Greek restaurant (Athens notwithstanding).  This isn't Greek; it isn't even Mediterranean. It's pseudo-Americanized versions of Mediterranean classic cuisine. The corporate chefs got so many things wrong:  Skordalia is a classic Greek dip made out of potatoes and garlic (not bread).  Avgolemono is chicken soup with egg, lemon and rice -- not this thin, awful broth they are currently serving. If one wants true Greek cooking, one should go to Greektown in either Detroit or Toronto. 
Just say no.
Rewrite this for me: I was extremely let down when this place opened; my expectations were for Nashville to finally have an authentic Greek restaurant (excluding Athens, of course). However, this establishment is far from Greek, and it doesn't even fall under the Mediterranean category. Instead, it serves pseudo-Americanized adaptations of Mediterranean dishes. The corporate chefs made numerous mistakes; for instance, skordalia, a classic Greek dip, should be made with potatoes and garlic, not bread. Similarly, avgolemono is traditionally a hearty chicken soup with egg, lemon, and rice, but what they're currently serving is a thin and unpleasant broth. If you're looking for genuine Greek cuisine, Greektown in either Detroit or Toronto is the way to go. My advice: just decline this option.

input: Best meal in New Orleans!!! I was in a group of 4 and we were served by Travis, Susan & Caroline. I had the set price menu: strawberry salad appetiser, chicken entrée & chocolate cake dessert. The salad was fresh and a great start. The chicken is the best chicken I have ever eaten anywhere. It had crispy skin, but was the meat was extremely moist and the corn bread stuffing was superb. The cake was yummy, but very rich. One of our party is vegetarian and she LOVED her vegetable selection plate. The other 2 members had the pork with sweet potato mash and said it was excellent. The staff were wonderful and very attentive. Excellent location and definitely the best meal we had in New Orleans.
Rewrite this for me: We had the absolute best dining experience in New Orleans! Our group of four was taken care of by the amazing servers Travis, Susan, and Caroline. I opted for the set price menu and started off with a refreshing strawberry salad as my appetizer. The chicken entrée that followed was simply outstanding - it surpassed any chicken dish I've ever had before. The crispy skin was a delightful contrast to the unbelievably moist meat, and the corn bread stuffing was absolutely superb. For dessert, I indulged in a delicious chocolate cake, although it was quite rich. Our vegetarian companion raved about her vegetable selection plate, and the other two members of our group delighted in their pork with sweet potato mash, describing it as excellent. On top of the fantastic food, the staff went above and beyond, providing attentive service throughout the meal. With its excellent location, this was definitely the finest meal we enjoyed during our time in New Orleans.

input:
i've been a member of this gym for a couple of weeks now, and i'm enjoying it.  conveniently located, very reasonably priced, and all the basic amenities -- plenty of cardio machines, plenty of weights, a lap pool, a spin class room, and a big aerobics studio.  the staff are all really nice as well, and you get a free personal trainer session when you sign up.  and your membership fee allows you to use all of their area locations for no extra money.  and if you have kids (i don't), they offer babysitting for limited hours.

the only things i'm a bit bummed about are:  1. they don't open until 8am on the weekends (i'm an early riser and would prefer to go a bit earlier than that), and 2. the only group fitness class they offer before work is a 5:45am spin class (i'm sorry, i just can't do spin that early in the morning).

this isn't the gym for you if you want all sorts of foo-foo stuff like a smoothie bar and massage and lots of high-tech equipment.  but if you just want a place to come and work out with nice people on good equipment, then you'll save some money by joining LA fitness.
Rewrite this for me:
I've been a member of this gym for a few weeks now and I'm really enjoying it. It's conveniently located, reasonably priced, and has all the basic amenities you need. They have plenty of cardio machines, weights, a lap pool, a spin class room, and a spacious aerobics studio. The staff are all friendly and when you sign up, you even get a complimentary personal trainer session. The best part is that your membership fee allows you to use all of their locations without any extra charge. Additionally, for those with kids, they offer limited babysitting hours.

The only downsides for me are that they don't open until 8am on weekends (I prefer going a bit earlier) and the only early morning group fitness class they have is a 5:45am spin class (which is too early for me).

If you're looking for a gym with fancy extras like smoothie bars, massage services, and high-tech equipment, this isn't the place for you. However, if you just want a friendly atmosphere to work out with good equipment, then joining LA Fitness will also save you some money.

input: This theater is dated but you can't beat the cheap prices.  Staff is always very friendly and that alone keeps me dividing my time between here and the Loft. input: Fun place, inviting interior and a pleasure to hang outside with the couches, etc. brunch food was very good, and beer selection exceptional.  Waiter, however, was a disaster. input: For Cool Springs on a Thursday when Bonefish grill was packed this place had a comfortable wait of 15 minutes. Also the food is always amazing, but that's a given

input:
Yum-O! We spend the day in Tarpon Springs, and headed here around 3:45 for lunch / dinner. We waited for about 10 minutes for our table and were seated.

Gyro - yum
Chicken Slouvaki - yum
Spanokopita - YES (this is what I ordered, good, but the top filo dough crust was a bit harder than I like)
Hotdog (this is what the 5 year old got)

input: Simply put, the Grypon Cafe makes me feel infinite.  It's about two minutes away from the Wayne Starbucks, but believe me when I say that all the cool informed coffee connoisseurs flock to Gryphon Cafe.  Its setting is quiet and intimate.It exudes a chill and serene vibe, from its very dim lighting and small (in a good way!) space.  The lattes are very good- made with strong espresso.  In addition, it provides various baked goods, although I've had a really dry, stale brownie from there (A big no-no! As a result, I don't care too much for the baked goods).  In addition, Gryphon supports a lively local music scene; music begins at 9 p.m. on Fridays and Saturdays.
Rewrite this for me: The Grypon Cafe is simply amazing, it fills me with a sense of infinity. The atmosphere is peaceful and intimate, emitting a relaxed and tranquil vibe through its dim lighting and cozy space. The lattes there are excellent, crafted with strong espresso. On top of that, they offer a variety of baked goods, although I did have a rather disappointing experience with a dry and stale brownie (definitely not recommended!). However, Gryphon Cafe shines in its support for the local music scene, with live performances starting at 9 p.m. every Friday and Saturday.

input:
Its a rarity that i give five stars for anything. But in comparing this tattoo shop to the others around Indy and how they've jacked me around i decided its simply worth it to give 5. The other places have cancelled on me at the last moment, even when i was en route to go get the tattoo, one guy didnt even remember me when i called the day before to make sure we were on schedule for the tat and yet another had the inks set out and asked me to sit down when he got a call that he needed to go pick up the kids at school - all of these places i scheduled months out in advance as well. So, here we are back at Metamorphosis where they actually like to run a business the way it should be. Honestly i have only had one tat done here by Trevor and at the time it was the most fun 4 hour rib tattoo experience i could have had. They act professional, not like the rock star wanna be's i tried to check out at other places. Just cool chill people who want your business here. Trevor gave me the tattoo i wanted in the place i wanted it even though i feel he would have given me honest advice if it were needed. When it came time to get the tat, he held his appointment and i was treated with respect and as though a customer should be treated. Honestly i dont think this place cost more than any other place where youll get good work. Prices are about average in my opinion for the quality of work done. Dont waste your time going to the other places and getting jerked around - ive already done the work for you. Its a shame too that they may have good artwork at other places but youll feel like less of a human going anywhere else. The artists are just as good here and youll be respected for your $.  And by the way, yes they do ask for a non refundable deposit so they know your serious which is no different than any tattoo place ive ever been to.
Hopefully they dont change up anything, especially their roster as i believe they have a good thing going here. Yes its in hoity toity popular town but its a diamond in the rough and there are no rock star attitudes here. Cant wait to go back to Trevor again.
Rewrite this for me:
I rarely give five-star ratings, but after comparing this tattoo shop to others in Indianapolis and considering how the others have disappointed me, I decided it's worth giving them five stars. The other places have consistently cancelled on me, even when I was already on my way to get a tattoo. One guy didn't even remember me when I called the day before to confirm our appointment, and another had the inks ready but had to leave abruptly to pick up his kids from school. I had scheduled all of these appointments months in advance. So here I am, back at Metamorphosis, where they actually know how to run a business properly.

I've only had one tattoo done here by Trevor, but it was the most enjoyable four-hour rib tattoo experience I could have asked for. The staff here act professionally, unlike the wannabe rock stars at other places. They're just cool, relaxed people who genuinely care about their customers. Trevor gave me the exact tattoo I wanted, in the spot I wanted, and I'm confident he would have given me honest advice if I needed it. He kept his appointment time and treated me with respect as any customer should be treated.

Honestly, I don't think this place is more expensive than any other reputable tattoo shop. The prices are average, considering the quality of work they provide. Don't waste your time at other places where they'll just jerk you around - I've already done the research for you. It's a shame that other places may have great artwork, but you'll feel devalued as a person in their presence. The artists at Metamorphosis are just as skilled, and here, you'll be respected as a paying customer. Also, yes, they do require a non-refundable deposit, which is standard practice at any tattoo shop I've been to.

I hope they don't change anything, especially their staff, because they have something good going here. Yes, it's located in a popular, high-end town, but it's a hidden gem without any pretentious attitudes. I can't wait to go back to Trevor for another tattoo.

input: Had the lengua burrito. It was non greesy and plated neatly. Simple food that was easy on the wallet. Think I will try the flan next time
Rewrite this for me: I ordered the lengua burrito which was not oily and presented in a tidy manner. It was affordable yet satisfying. Considering the enjoyable experience, I am contemplating trying the flan on my next visit.

input:
I mistakenly left my organizer/wallet on my table when eating at Shepard's yesterday (6/24/12). I realized the mistake early this morning and called Shepard's. I was told that no one turned in anything resembling my organizer. 

I called back a few hours later to try and determine who bussed my table and what management was on duty and was told that my organizer had indeed been found and was in the "safe". I asked about the contents of the wallet and discovered that everything was present except for a $100 bill that I had just gotten the night before. I have witnesses to the $100 bill being in the organizer. 

I went today to retrieve the organizer and met with the assistant manager, who told me it was not their responsibility to keep track of guests belongings and would not investigate the issue whatsoever. She would not approach the server, would not ask who turned the organizer in, would not ask who stored it in the safe and essentially told me it was not her problem. 

This is customer service at it's worst... I have no recourse at this establishment to even try to get my money back. I am incensed that they won't even conduct an investigation for me.

input:
I'm only giving them 4 stars because I haven't tried out enough of their menu. But in regards to previous reviews saying the pizza was soggy, they must have listened! The pizza I ordered today was a personal specialty pie. Vegan general tso's pizza. It was so good! No skimping on the "chicken" either. The crust was crisp and fluffy, not greasy at all but still packed with flavor. The chicken had that delicious general tso's sauce coated on each piece, as well as a slight kick at the end.

Moreover, they even called me back to resolve an issue regarding the pricing. The delivery arrived within the estimated time and was still hot. I highly recommend giving them a chance. The seitan they produce in-house is truly remarkable.

input:

Portions are huge and food was good. I had the Cuban sandwich one night and it was massive but delicious. The shandy is good. The margaritas are not and I don't recommend their patron one. I forget the name but it wasn't that good. Their shrimp tacos have a kick but they're good too.

input:
You know how those 5 stars mean, "Woohoo!  As good as it gets!"?

Each one of those stars is well deserved by Tanti and the rest of the crew at Papertini.  They specialize in wedding flowers but these aren't just your clump of red roses.  These are creatively and artistically designed masterpieces speckled with striking elements like papers, wires, luxe fabrics, and more.  As an added bonus, they're just great, friendly people.  A true asset to your wedding team.

If you want traditional wedding flowers, Papertini can do it but I think it would kill their soul - go elsewhere.  If you want something more unique without being artsy-fartsy, I can't recommend them highly enough!

If you're in search of traditional wedding flowers, Papertini can certainly deliver, but I must say, it would be a disservice to their true talents. I wholeheartedly encourage you to look elsewhere for something ordinary. However, if you desire a one-of-a-kind bouquet that marries uniqueness and sophistication without venturing too far into the realm of artsy-fartsy, then look no further! Papertini comes highly recommended by yours truly.

input:
Looking for a delicious New Year's Day brunch was hard this year in New Orleans. We didn't want to wait in line and wanted instant gratification. Although we may have felt tired, my bf and I were appropriately dressed to go to Mr. B's. As soon as we walked in, I felt transported into a different world. Jazz music was playing and I felt at home. 

First of all, I could not have been more grateful for the fresh loaf of bread we were given. We devoured it in a matter of minutes. Then came the gumbo ya-ya. It was spicy and savory and everything I expected from a gumbo. Finally came the bbq shrimp. We had been warned that these shrimp did come with their heads and tails on. Bibs were placed around our necks and we were off. The shrimp were some of the most rich and delicious ones I have ever tasted. The sauce they were served with was divine. Although it was messy, there is no other dish on the menu I would have traded for this.

Overall, service was friendly and quick at Mr. B's. The food was delicious, although a little pricey. Definitely try the brunch if you are able to.
Rewrite this for me:
Finding a delectable brunch spot on New Year's Day in New Orleans proved to be quite the challenge this year. We weren't keen on waiting in line and desired instant satisfaction. Despite feeling a bit weary, my boyfriend and I made sure we dressed appropriately for a visit to Mr. B's. The moment we stepped inside, it felt as if we were transported to a different realm. The soothing melodies of jazz filled the air, instantly making us feel right at home.

First and foremost, I must express my immense gratitude for the fresh loaf of bread we were presented with. Within minutes, we eagerly devoured it. Soon enough, the gumbo ya-ya arrived. We were forewarned that these shrimp would come complete with their heads and tails intact. Sporting bibs around our necks, we embarked on our shrimp adventure. To say they were sumptuously rich and flavorsome would be an understatement. The accompanying sauce was simply divine. Despite the messiness, there wasn't a single dish on the menu that I would have traded for these shrimp.

All in all, the service at Mr. B's was wonderfully friendly and efficient. The food was undeniably delicious, albeit a tad on the pricey side. If given the opportunity, I highly recommend giving their brunch a try.

input:
Nice Steakhouse in St. Louis. We went here for a client dinner and was pleasantly surprised. You get a nice view of the arch on the way in to the restaurant as well. 

The Apps were OK. We ended up getting the Carmine's trio (crab cakes, scallops and toasted ravioli). Crab cakes were above average. The scallops were a little saccharine for my tastes but the ravioli was good; and let's face it...one doesn't come to St. Louis for the scallops. Thankfully the filet mignon was exceptional. It was the perfect size, not too salty and rare just like I had requested. 

This was partnered with an above average wine list to make a great night out.
Rewrite this for me:
We had a great experience at a lovely steakhouse in St. Louis. We dined here for a client dinner and were pleasantly surprised. The restaurant offers a nice view of the arch on the way in.

The appetizers were decent. We decided to try the Carmine's trio, which included crab cakes, scallops, and toasted ravioli. The crab cakes were above average, while the scallops were a bit too sweet for my taste. However, the ravioli was quite good. But let's be honest, one doesn't typically come to St. Louis for the scallops. 

Fortunately, the star of the show was the exceptional filet mignon. It was perfectly sized, not overly seasoned, and cooked exactly as I had requested (rare). To complement our meal, they offered an above average wine list, which made for a fantastic night out.

input: Three from my office had lunch delivered from San Antonio Taco today.  It was our first time from there.  The food did not live up to the reviews. input:
Cousin's is the place to go if you live in North Philly. I take this joint any day over Fresh Grocer. 

The only complaints I have is with the produce (which is expected considering it is COUSIN'S after all) and the hours (like many others have said, they have awful and inconvenient hours post-5pm).

That being said, I can get most essentials here and for much cheaper than anywhere else. 

This is only a two minute bike ride from my apartment so there's no reason not to shop here. Matter of fact, I'm headed there tomorrow.

When it's too cold or you're feeling to cheap to go to Trader Joe's, Cousin's is the place to head to.

input:
I've been here twice now and sampled a bunch of what they have to offer - I feel like what you order will really dictate how much you like this place.  i.e. they do some things great and other things just so-so.

The two things I will surely go back for more of is the Sausage and Pepper Pizza (capitalized - because I mean business) and some sort of puff pastry that has a white cream in the middle - I'm sure it has a name but it escapes me.  The pizza was perfectly flavored and the sausage/peppers had a nice kick to it.  Im sure it would make for great leftovers but unfortunately (fortunately?) for me it was gone well before it found the refrigerator.  The cream puff cream was just awesome - couldn't pin-point the flavor (vanilla?) but I would prefer it to top every dessert I get from this point forward.

I also got a bunch of the other sweets (salted brownie, blondie, red velvet crumb-cake) and a few bagels.  All were good, but not great.  Was pleasantly surprised by the wheat everything bagels - whole wheat bagels usually suck.

What I didn't really like was the pepperoni pizza.  It was pretty bland for my liking - in complete contrast to the sausage and pepper pizza - and the pepperoni was pretty sparse. I also didn't like being told 25 minutes, showing up in 25 minutes and then standing there for 25 minutes waiting for the pizza.  The small shop + no chairs = awkwardly standing there for almost a half hour.  

Since it's close to me and has so many tasty looking treats yet to try - I'll surely be back.  Hopefully I'll get more 'great' than 'so-so'.
Rewrite this for me:
I have visited this place twice now and have tried a variety of their offerings. I have realized that your satisfaction greatly depends on what you order. They excel at certain things, while others are just average.

There are two dishes that I absolutely recommend trying: the Sausage and Pepper Pizza (which I highly recommend, hence the capitalization) and a puff pastry filled with a white cream. I can't recall the exact name, but it was delicious. The pizza had the perfect blend of flavors, with a nice spicy kick from the sausage and peppers. It would have made great leftovers, but unfortunately (or fortunately for my taste buds), it vanished before I could refrigerate it. The cream in the puff pastry was absolutely amazing. I couldn't pinpoint the exact flavor, maybe vanilla, but I would love to have it as a topping on all my future desserts.

I also tried some of their other sweets, such as the salted brownie, blondie, and red velvet crumb cake, as well as a few bagels. They were all good, but didn't reach the level of greatness. However, I was pleasantly surprised by the wheat everything bagels, as whole wheat bagels usually disappoint me.

On the downside, I wasn't a fan of their pepperoni pizza. It lacked flavor compared to the sausage and pepper pizza, and the amount of pepperoni was disappointingly sparse. Additionally, the service was a bit of a letdown. Despite being told it would take 25 minutes, I arrived on time only to end up waiting for the pizza for an additional 25 minutes. Since the shop is small and lacks seating, I felt quite awkward standing there for almost half an hour.

Despite these shortcomings, I will definitely return to this place, as it is conveniently located near me and there are still many tempting treats left for me to try. Hopefully, my future experiences will lean more towards greatness rather than mediocrity.

input:
