input: My go to place for sushi rolls! Their rolls are huge and the service is excellent. My favorite is heat attack appetizer( korean style jalapeno poppers) sapporo roll and honey roll. They also have a section of deepfried rolls on the menu! Their food always look so  fresh and appetizing. Great presentation. Try the spicy sashimi bowl if you wanna try something new!
Rewrite this for me: Whenever I'm craving sushi rolls, this place is my ultimate choice! Not only are their rolls generously sized, but the service is also top-notch. I absolutely love their heat attack appetizer, which are Korean-style jalapeno poppers, as well as the delectable sapporo roll and honey roll. Additionally, they have an entire section dedicated to deep-fried rolls on their menu! Every dish they serve looks impeccably fresh and enticing, with fantastic presentation. For a unique culinary experience, I highly recommend trying their spicy sashimi bowl!

input:
Ok. I am not the type to complain, but I have been here twice and both times I have had terrible service at the bar. The first bartender served me but acted as if I was bothering him.  This second time, with a completely different bartender mind you, it was worse. I am not dressed like a street person or anything, and I am not pan-handling. But you would think that I was the way he acted. First, I sit at the bar and I am waiting for service. So, the bartender walks by me, pours a glass a water, turns in front of me, puts the water down, gives me some stupid half-grin then walks off. Not one audible word of greeting or a grunt passed between his lips. Then, he gets a menu, drops that down and walks off again! Not a sound. Is it me, but when a customer enters an eating establishment, shouldn't they be greeted in some manner?  Not looked at like "why are you here. I have better things to do"?  I am not looking for a royal salute or anything. Just "Hey man, what can I get ya?"  or something to that affect.   Anyway, I start to look at the drink and food menus. Then, a group of anywhere from 10-15 people come in behind me and say, to what looked like a manager, "We don't want to eat, is it ok if we just have a few drinks at the bar?". The manager says "Sure." The guy then says, "Can we get few beers down here"? (paraphrasing). The bartender says "Sure!" and proceed to service this group, one-by-one, as they order drinks. Ok, fine technically, I was looking at the menu when this started. But still, he walked back and forth, right in front of me, for about 10-12 minutes. Not once did he say, "Hey, just shout and I will get you something", or "Hey man, just give me a few minutes and I will be right with you". Nothing!  It was obvious it was a big group, but I mean, he gave no acknowledgement to the fact that I was sitting there waiting! 

Long story short - after this 10-12 minutes of waiting, I just walked out and went somewhere else. Now this place has about 4\5 stars with around 500 reviews. So, I guess people like it. But their bartenders are as unfriendly as I have ever encountered.  Maybe if you get a table it's different.
Rewrite this for me: Alright, I have had two unfortunate experiences at this bar and I feel the need to share my dissatisfaction. On both occasions, I received terrible service at the bar. The first bartender seemed annoyed by my presence and served me with an unwelcoming attitude. The second time, with a different bartender, things were even worse. Despite my decent appearance and manners, the bartender treated me as if I was unworthy of his attention. As I sat at the bar waiting for service, he simply poured a glass of water, placed it in front of me, and gave me a half-hearted grin before walking away. There was no friendly greeting or even a basic acknowledgment. He then dropped off a menu and left again, completely silent. Is it too much to expect a simple greeting when a customer enters an establishment? It shouldn't feel like an inconvenience or as though I am unwelcome. I don't expect a grand entrance, just a friendly "Hey, how can I help you?" or something similar. As I looked through the drink and food menus, a group of 10-15 people entered and asked the apparent manager if they could have drinks at the bar without eating. The manager agreed, and the bartender readily served them, engaging in friendly conversation as they ordered their drinks. Meanwhile, I sat there, unnoticed and neglected, as he repeatedly passed by me for around 10-12 minutes. Not once did he acknowledge my presence or offer any sort of explanation or reassurance. At that point, I couldn't bear it any longer and decided to leave, finding another place to enjoy my evening. Despite the bar's seemingly positive reputation with a high rating and numerous positive reviews, the unfriendly nature of their bartenders leaves much to be desired. Perhaps the experience would be different if I had been seated at a table, but as a bar patron, I felt thoroughly dismissed.

input: I loved loved loved the pizza here. I returned and got their gnocchi and it was amazing as well. Really fresh ingredients nice variety on the menu. Really felt like a small family restaurant in Europe. Best pizza in middle Tennessee.

input: For a $16 haircut, I was expecting an OK-looking trim (all I really needed was some damage control - just someone to lop off my split ends and maybe add a few layers).  What I got was a very professionally looking haircut that works well with my face shape and made my hair a lot healthier and happier.  My expectations were far exceeded - and it definitely surpassed my last 'professional' hair salon experience.  Plus, the shampoo smelled amazing and the girl was really thorough.  I wish I had brought more cash to tip her!!!  The only thing you should keep in mind before going is time.  I had to wait an extra half an hour and it was the longest haircut I've ever had.  I would much rather have the student take the time to make sure it looks good, however, than have someone do a half-ass job.  I think it's important that the school has a series of steps and checklists their students have to go through to ensure they are giving you the best experience possible.  Just make sure you have a decent block of time in your schedule to relax in the chair!
Rewrite this for me: I had initially expected a decent haircut for the $16 price tag. I was simply looking for some damage control, to get rid of my split ends and maybe add some layers. However, I was pleasantly surprised to receive a professionally executed haircut that complemented the shape of my face and improved the health and appearance of my hair. This experience far exceeded my previous encounters at supposed professional salons. Additionally, the shampoo used had a delightful scent and the stylist demonstrated thoroughness in her work. I genuinely regretted not having enough cash to give her a generous tip. The only drawback to consider before going is the time it takes. I had to wait an extra half hour and it turned out to be the longest haircut I've ever had. Nonetheless, I would much prefer the student to take their time ensuring my hair looks good rather than rushing through the job. It's reassuring to know that the school has a series of steps and checklists for their students to follow, guaranteeing the best possible experience. Just ensure you allocate a decent chunk of time in your schedule to fully relax in the salon chair!

input:

input:

input: This place is so great. I love the laid back atmosphere. Walked right in with our dog and were seating on the cozy wrap around porch outside. I had the bananas foster French toast which was amazing but super rich. I couldn't eat it all because of the portion size and richness. My fiancé opted for the healthier choice of a vegetable omelet which was delicious as well. I can't wait to come back here and try something else on the menu. I will definitely try one of their famous juices next time.

input: This place is wonderful! Obviously the chips, salsa and beans are yummy, but get the guacamole too! The chimichanga bites are fantastic, whatever the sauce is that comes with them is super good! For dinner, the street tacos are amazing, so are the enchiladas. They don't have a full bar, but you can still get a real margarita, and they pack a punch! They make them at their other location and bring them over, which is clever, because this location doesn't yet have its liquor license. Overall 4 out 5 stars because it's a good Mexican restaurant, but 5 stars is reserved for my most favorites only. Close second though, and we love that it's right downtown. Oh, and the service... very good! We usually always have the same server, and she is very nice and attentive.
Rewrite this for me: I absolutely love this place! The chips, salsa, and beans are undeniably delicious, but don't forget to try their guacamole. It's a must! The chimichanga bites are simply fantastic, especially with the accompanying sauce that is incredibly tasty. When it comes to dinner, the street tacos and enchiladas are nothing short of amazing. Although they don't have a full bar, their margaritas are the real deal and pack a punch. They cleverly make them at their other location and bring them over, as this location is still waiting for its liquor license. Overall, I would give this Mexican restaurant 4 out of 5 stars because it's really good, but I reserve 5 stars for my absolute favorites. It's a close second though, and being conveniently located downtown adds to its appeal. Moreover, the service is top-notch! We always have the pleasure of being served by the same friendly and attentive server.

input: Holy _____! Good rolls. Great service. Good prices. Lots of healthy options. Try the sushi. It worth every penny!

input: As a fan of the late night kabab, shwarma or gyro in nyc, I made a stop through Ali ba ba's on one occasion and ended up here again near the end of the trip as it hits the spot!  They are bigger in size of the ones I get in NYC and double the price ($6) but I can imagine the cost is a factor of limited demand (small lines) and pallets in NOLA for a gyro vs a po boy.  They only have rooster sauce for hot sauce which is a knock and they can be slow to serve but the gyros are better than the $5 slice next door or the $5+ lucky dogs on the corner.
Rewrite this for me: Being a fan of late-night kabobs, shawarmas, or gyros in NYC, I made a detour to Ali ba ba's once and ended up coming back again towards the end of my trip because it truly satisfies my cravings! These gyros are much larger than the ones I usually get in NYC, but they also come at double the price ($6). However, I understand that the higher cost is likely due to the limited demand (short lines) and the preference for po' boys over gyros in NOLA. The only downside is that they only offer rooster sauce as a hot sauce option, which is a letdown. Additionally, they can be a bit slow with their service, but their gyros are still way better than the $5 pizza slice next door or the $5+ lucky dogs on the corner.

input:
I LOVE JONES. Honestly.....

I was introduced to Jones at the YEE earlier this year. The food was divine. Comfort food to the max. Mac and Cheese that I could've eaten with a ladle, sliders, pigs in a blanket, delicious cocktails. Yum yum gimme some.

We came back with my mother and fell in love again. The calamari is the best calamari I've had in quite some time. Perfectly crisp, not rubbery, full of flavor. Yum.

For dessert? I had the Duncan Hines slice of yellow cake and glass of milk. Genius.

We came back AGAIN a few weeks ago when a friend was visiting from LA. I had the Seared Ahi Tuna. The husband had the Halibut. Our friend had the Roast Beef Dinner. Our friend won when it came to food selection. My belly was so warm and happy after one bite of his roast beef. The meat was succulent, juicy, the perfect medium rare. The mashed taters were creamy with a slight hint of garlic. Mmmm.

I preferred my husband's halibut over my tuna. The tuna was good, but the halibut had more flavor, IMO.

Can't wait to go back again. Yum yum yum.
Rewrite this for me:
Jones is absolutely amazing. Let me tell you, my love affair with this place started when I first experienced it at the YEE earlier this year. The food they served was simply divine, like a warm hug for my taste buds. The Mac and Cheese was so tasty that I could have easily eaten it with a ladle. Sliders and pigs in a blanket were mouthwatering, and those cocktails? Oh boy, they were absolutely delicious. Yum yum, I wanted more!

Then, I brought my mother along for another visit, and we fell in love with Jones all over again. The calamari they serve is seriously the best I've had in a long time. Crispy perfection, not a hint of rubberiness, and bursting with flavor. Simply yum.

And let's not forget about dessert. I indulged in a slice of yellow cake from Duncan Hines and enjoyed it with a glass of milk. It was a stroke of genius, truly.

Oh, and guess what? We went back yet another time, this time with a friend from LA. Our meal choices were quite diverse - I had the Seared Ahi Tuna, my husband opted for the Halibut, and our friend went for the Roast Beef Dinner. Well, I must confess, our friend won the award for the best food selection. With just one bite of his succulent, juicy roast beef, my belly felt warm and blissful. The mashed potatoes accompanying it were heavenly, with a subtle hint of garlic. Mmm, so good.

While I enjoyed my tuna, I actually preferred my husband's halibut. It had a bit more flavor in my humble opinion.

I cannot wait to go back to Jones again and experience their delightful cuisine once more. Yum yum yum.

input: The Penang chicken with the chicken flavor infused white rice will always be one of my favorite meals. Wether in Boston or in Philly, the quality is the same and I am a huge fan. input:

input:
My girlfriends and I ate at the Creole House for dinner. Our decision to dine here was largely based on the fact that it was pouring raining and this restaurant is next door to our hotel. We started with the bacon garlic oysters and jumbo buffalo wings. The bacon garlic oysters were average, at best. The oysters were overpowered by the cheese and bacon, which was disappointing. The buffalo wings were pretty good and seasoned well. For entrees, we ordered: 1) jumbalaya pasta, 2) blackened red fish and 3) canal street red fish. The jumbalaya pasta lacked flavor and was our least favorite (would not order again). The blackened red fish was just okay and the skimpy side of sautéed veggies (spinach, tomatoes, mushrooms) were VERY salty (would order again as a LAST resort). The canal street red fish wasn't great but my friend would order it again. Her biggest complaint was that it had very little garlic sauce. We also ordered paddle boat drinks, which tasted good but were more juice vs alcohol (had to order an extra shot).

So, overall, we were underwhelmed with the food, making it a solid 3 stars. On a positive note, our server, Alexander, was great...very hospitable and tried his best to make sure we were satisfied.

input:
Okay, don't jump on me for this, but its partially my fault because I held them to such high expectations (due to the hype and anticipation of them opening up here) before actually eating at this location. I read so much about it on Facebook and the likes......so reading and seeing the yummy pics; well I just knew it would be all that.....untill yesterday.....

Me and my bf Vince went to BlackFinn for Sunday lunch yesterday. The atmosphere was cool and it was really nice inside. The staff was pleasant as well, so I'm thinking "hum...I like...". We ordered  a couple of mojitos and we also had another drink, which was okay.  Time to order; I ordered the Cuban sandwich, hold the mustard, and add mayo instead....with Black Finn fries and my bf ordered the Prime Rib sandwich with au jus and the same fries.  We got our order, which took a bit of time but it was okay. Everything looked so yummy and I knew they were going to meet my expectations. Now mind ya, my bf put off going to BlackFinn since they day they opened and I've been on him to go here. So anyway, the fries were a bit salty, but good. I had a choice of two dipping sauces, which I believe were ranch and barbeque. Delicious! I bit into the sandwich and what did I taste? A mouth full of mustard!!! Eeewww!! Okay, did I not say "hold the mustard"? So lo and behold, my food had to be returned while my bf ate his food. His beef about his sandwich (no pun intended) was that there was more bread than meat. I looked at it and I noticed the same thing. Also, the au jus was a bit low as well and wasn't enough for the sandwich.  So I'm like the little old lady from the back-in-the-day commercials saying "Where's the beef?" LOL. Wow! 

Finally, after he finishes his sandwich, my food finally comes out and guess what? They left the swiss cheese off the sandwich. WTF! Okay, so at this point I'm like "forget it, just take it back." How many times must I send my sandwich back to get it right? Now I must say that the manager on duty was accommodating and she took care of the check and apolgized for the errors. So for her professionalism and the fact that the staff was very polite, I give them two stars. Will I go back....yes I will give them another chance to redeem themselves, but all in my ear is my bf saying that there must have been a reason why he hesitated to come here and this is why.  Oh well......

From the outside of the building you wouldn't know it was a hookah bar (except the giant sign of course lol). The moment you open that giant wooden door, the decor and paint color gives it that authentic look. Warm yellow paint with evil eyes and giant metal wall lamps with cutouts shining red surrounding all the walls.
When you go up a few steps there's a gift shop, a table, and the register. They ask you to take a seat upstairs and they follow you shortly after. (There's even another upstairs that I barely peaked at).
This is the amazing part: cushions on the floor with giant metal mandala tables!!!! It was so authentic I could barely handle my excitement. They have a menu with drinks, food and hookah. Water was only a dollar which was amazing because hookah bars are usually pretty pricy.
We smoked "sex on the beach" flavored shisha. It was smooth! Very smooth! We even brought bubbles for the trip to have a little fun :)
What I like about this place compared to other loud hookah bars is that it wasn't even close to being hectic. I felt like I should have whispered at first, but after awhile I was more comfortable. Only one other couple was there and they were very nice to talk to as well. The older man and the young guy was extremely nice. The younger dude checked in on us and was sociable which was really kinda nice but not overbearing. 

If you want a low key, quiet and chill hookah bar, this should be at the top of people's lists.

input:
3.50 stars.  

Gabby's wasn't open.  I knew that.  Neither was Rotier's.  But my handy Yelp app had assured me that Fido's was open.  Imagine the disappointment when I realized there was a very real possibility that no burgers would happen on this trip down to the Deep South.  Would I really have to wait two more weeks when I would find solace in East Texas?   

"We can try Burger up," I mentioned.  

"Why don't you just call them?" hissed the appropriately nicknamed Viper.  

True.  We didn't have to keep driving around aimlessly.  So I call Burger Up, and a very pleasant, sweet voice assures me they are indeed open.  

Viper: "What was her name?  She sounded hot."
  
Me: "Paige."

Viper: "Yeah, she's definitely hot.  Have you ever met an unattractive Paige?"

Me: "Good point.  At least we have that going for us."

Paige was indeed attractive, but this review isn't about a photogenic individual who happens to work at Burger Up.  It's about what ended up being a visit to our fourth choice for burgers in Nashville.  

Burger Up follows a national trend towards upscale burgers.  My particular order consisted of a medium rare patty served with aged cheddar, Benton's bacon (very good), and ketchup served on an artisan bun.  Basically, it was a gussied up bacon cheeseburger, but it was a rather tasty one.  My major complaint is that I wish the actual meat itself exhibited more flavor.  Having said that, the burger was cooked properly and the flavors worked well together.  I ordered some wilted spinach on the side (mediocre) and truffle fries.  Let's talk about those truffle fries for a bit.  I know more people are apparently into the sweet potato fries here, but I think they are missing the boat.  Burger Up's truffle tries have pleasant aroma, taste great, and are the perfect texture for soaking up oil.  If you are on a diet, it is true you should skip these delightful fries.  But if that were the case, why are you at a burger joint in the first place?  Seriously, if you get nothing else out of my review, please do yourself a favor and order the truffle fries.  

Burger Up also boast an interesting beer menu with semi-obscure breweries from the Deep South included in the list.  I tried a pecan-infused amber from Mississippi - not bad.  I could imagine Burger Up could be a decent place to drink for a bit after eating.  

If I attended Vanderbilt, I would probably go here on a moderately frequent basis.  If you want a change from the dive bar hamburger, Burger Up is a decent change of pace.

However, the burger was cooked well and the flavors complemented each other. I also ordered some wilted spinach on the side, which was average, and truffle fries. Let's take a moment to talk about those truffle fries. While more people seem to prefer the sweet potato fries, I believe they're missing out. Burger Up's truffle fries have a pleasant aroma, great taste, and the perfect texture for soaking up oil. If you're watching your diet, it's true that you should skip these delightful fries. But if you're at a burger joint, why would you be on a diet in the first place? Seriously, if there's one thing you take away from this review, do yourself a favor and order the truffle fries.

Burger Up also offers an interesting beer menu featuring semi-obscure breweries from the Deep South. I tried a pecan-infused amber from Mississippi and found it to be not bad. I could see Burger Up being a decent place to enjoy some drinks after a meal.

If I were a student at Vanderbilt, I would probably visit Burger Up somewhat regularly. If you're looking for a change from the usual dive bar hamburger, Burger Up is a decent option.

Mandala is very affordable, on par (if not less costly) than online prices and you get to test the products in person with no shipping charges. Please consider shopping locally for your massage supplies rather than purchasing them online in order to support this fantastic small business! Note that Mandala has moved to a quaint Victorian-style home on South Virginia.
Rewrite this for me: Mandala offers a wide range of massage supplies at fantastic prices. Lisa, the staff member, is exceptionally friendly, knowledgeable, and always ready to assist. She guided me through the vast selection of essential oils at the aroma bar, helping me choose the perfect blend. It was an enjoyable and interactive experience. Not only is Mandala affordable, but their prices are also comparable, if not lower than online retailers. Plus, you have the advantage of trying the products in person without any additional shipping charges. Help support this amazing small business by choosing to shop locally for your massage supplies. Keep in mind that Mandala has relocated to a charming Victorian-style home on South Virginia.

input: Adorable little shop. The food/snacks were great and the portions generous but of course the alcohol is the star. While I wasn't too big on the meads, the ciders were wonderful and I ended up enamored enough to bring one all the way back home to the east coast.
Rewrite this for me: This charming shop is absolutely adorable. The food and snacks they serve are amazing, with generous portions. However, the real highlight is the alcohol selection. Although I wasn't a huge fan of the meads, the ciders were absolutely delightful. I was so impressed that I couldn't resist taking one back home with me to the east coast.

input: If you want beignets in Metarie, for my money Morning call is better than this shop.  If you're dead set on Cafe Du Monde, you're only twenty minutes including parking to Decatur.
Rewrite this for me: In my opinion, when it comes to having beignets in Metairie, Morning Call surpasses this shop. However, if you insist on going to Cafe Du Monde, it will only take you twenty minutes, including the time spent on parking, to get there on Decatur street.

input: Beautiful new nail Salon on West Chester Pike .. staff Is friendly.. the salon is brand new .. prices are good .. very serene colors ..  pedi chairs have phone chargers .. definitely recommend it!
Rewrite this for me: I highly recommend the amazing new nail salon located on West Chester Pike. The staff is incredibly friendly and the salon itself is brand new, providing a wonderful and inviting atmosphere. The prices are quite reasonable and the serene color scheme adds to the overall peaceful ambiance. Additionally, an excellent feature is that the pedi chairs come equipped with phone chargers. Don't miss out on this fantastic nail salon experience!

input: Not just for feet. All I can say is....Wow! Worth the extra $$ for an hour full body massage. Simon has the most talented hands to coax your muscles to relax, taking the kinks out with skill. The atmosphere is very desirable and comfortable. You don't realized the importance of human touch until you have a professional work their magic. They provide walk-in service, but I recommend scheduling an appointment for a massage, especially during the early evening hours. My daughter and I had a foot massage there and this too was fantastic! First place whose prices are affordable and well worth indulging in. I highly recommend this little slice of heaven.
Rewrite this for me: It's not just a foot massage. Let me just say...Wow! Paying a little extra for a full body massage is absolutely worth it. Simon's hands are incredibly talented at soothing your muscles and getting rid of any knots. The atmosphere is inviting and cozy. You don't realize how important human touch is until you experience a professional working their magic. They do accept walk-ins, but I highly recommend making an appointment, especially in the early evening. My daughter and I had a foot massage there and it was also fantastic! This place has affordable prices and is definitely worth treating yourself to. I highly recommend this little piece of paradise.

input: Stopped in to check out this new spot around the corner from us, as my boyfriend has been anticipating its opening for quite some time. Can I say it- FINALLY! Am amazing place for sushi in the city. We were there for what they were calling their soft opening, where apparently they are testing out menu and cocktail items for their "official" opening sometime soon. We were very pleased with the ambiance, service and food/drink. The fish is top quality. We said hello to the owner/executive chef and he seemed to be beaming over his accomplishments, rightfully so! This is a must stop if you're a sushi/Asian fusion fan. We look forward to seeing what's in store for Tuna Bar and are thrilled to have this a two minute walk away!
Rewrite this for me: We decided to check out the new restaurant that recently opened around the corner from us, as my boyfriend had been eagerly awaiting its arrival. And finally, it's here! This place is truly amazing for sushi lovers in the city. We happened to visit during their soft opening, where they are testing out their menu and cocktails before their official grand opening. We were incredibly impressed with the atmosphere, service, and the quality of the food and drinks. The fish they serve is of top-notch quality. We had the opportunity to greet the owner and executive chef, who seemed extremely proud of what he has accomplished, and rightfully so! If you're a fan of sushi or Asian fusion, this is a place you must visit. We can't wait to see what more Tuna Bar has in store for us, and we're thrilled that it's just a two-minute walk away from us!

input: I'm all for a dive bar but this place takes it to another level. The walls are old wood panel, the whole place smells disgusting, the drinks are tiny...I don't feel any need to ever go there again.
Rewrite this for me: I fully support the idea of a dive bar, but this particular establishment is on a whole other level. The walls are covered in ancient wood panels, the entire place reeks of a repulsive odor, and the drinks are disappointingly minuscule. Needless to say, there is absolutely no desire within me to ever visit that place again.

input: Really like this place. The food is amazing, great atmosphere and the hostess has such a positive energy. It was my friend's first time and he definitely enjoyed it and wants to come back. The shrimp salad with the lime chili dressing was refreshing.
Rewrite this for me: I love this place so much! The food is absolutely incredible, the atmosphere is wonderful, and the hostess radiates with such positivity. My friend, who was here for the first time, had a fantastic experience and is eager to visit again. The shrimp salad with the lime chili dressing was incredibly refreshing.

input:
Place has really slipped as far as food quality. Pork steak was dry and tough and I wish they'd have let me pick which sauce from the squeeze bottles on the table. The BBQ nachos we'd shared here before many times was soggy and tasteless. We were there early evening Saturday and they weren't busy at all.  I guess words gotten around. 

Still good service like before.

Probably not returning.
Rewrite this for me:
The food quality at this place has drastically declined. The pork steak was disappointingly dry and tough, and it would have been better if they allowed me to choose my own sauce from the squeeze bottles on the table. The BBQ nachos, which we had enjoyed numerous times here in the past, were now soggy and lacking flavor. Despite it being early evening on a Saturday and the restaurant not being busy, it seems that the word about their decline has spread.

However, the service remains good just like it was before. Nevertheless, I doubt I will be returning to this establishment.

input: Excellenet Professional Service ! Loved my experience here today...unfortunately didn't get name of stylist who did my haircut but she was incredibly good !! U earned my confidence
Rewrite this for me: Outstanding Professional Service! I thoroughly enjoyed my experience here today; however, regrettably, I didn't catch the name of the stylist who expertly cut my hair. Nevertheless, their skills were exceptional! You have certainly earned my trust and confidence.

input: We had such a great meal at Spiro's tonight! Neither my dining companion, nor myself had been there previously. We both had a Greek salad, which was prepared table side. I had the Dolmades, and my coworker, the combo plate which had moussaka and dolmas and lamb (which he could not stop raving about). To our surprise our server brought dessert on the house, since we had never dined there before, it was such a nice touch! Ben our server was fantastic and knowledgable. We are both in the industry so we felt guilty about staying until the restaurant closed, but we were just so comfortable and well fed that we lost track of time. Spiro's is very close to my house, it will definitely be my new regular spot. Thank you Ben, and the whole Spiro's crew, for a great time to compliment a rare night off! You rock!
Rewrite this for me: Tonight, we had an incredible dinner at Spiro's. Neither my dining companion nor I had ever been there before. We both decided to start with the Greek salad, which was prepared right at our table. I opted for the Dolmades, while my coworker went for the combo plate with moussaka, dolmas, and lamb. He couldn't stop praising how delicious it was! To our pleasant surprise, as first-time diners, the server treated us to a complimentary dessert. It was such a thoughtful gesture! Our server, Ben, was exceptional and very knowledgeable. Despite both of us working in the industry, we couldn't help but feel guilty for staying until closing time. However, the cozy atmosphere and incredible food made us lose track of time. Spiro's is conveniently located near my home, and it's definitely going to be my go-to spot from now on. A big thank you to Ben and the entire Spiro's team for making our rare night off so memorable. You guys rock!

input: I was in so much pain from my accident, waited for 2 hours and was seen for 5 minutes and discharged with no medications to help me recover. If you are looking for a compassionate care, this is not the place to get it.
Rewrite this for me: After enduring immense pain from my accident, I patiently waited for two whole hours only to be examined for five brief minutes and sent away without any medications to aid my recovery. If you seek compassionate care, I would advise against choosing this particular location.

input:
Good food  cashier Alessandra very polite and respectful . meal box was reasonable for the price 
And it  tasted good as well I will come back if in the area
Rewrite this for me: Alessandra, the cashier at the Good Food restaurant, was exceptionally polite and respectful. The meal box was reasonably priced and, not only did it taste delicious, but it was also satisfying. If I find myself in the area again, I will definitely be returning.

input: Good on the 'getting away from straws' for environmental reasons! Not so good on ingredients in ur mixers! Not so impressed with bar girlZzzz energy Saturday eve... Her Margarita getZ 2 thUmbs DOWN...  ItZ kind of an easy drink...
Rewrite this for me: I applaud your efforts in avoiding straws for environmental reasons! However, I am not satisfied with the ingredients used in your mixers. Furthermore, I was not impressed with the lack of enthusiasm from the bartender on Saturday evening. The Margarita I received was disappointing and in my opinion, a simple drink like that should have been executed better.

input:
I went to my first BarreAmped class at the Music Row location (I've also been to bounce class - on a trampoline - at the Nations location), and it was a great class: definitely a better workout and a better experience than some of the barre classes I've taken in town since moving to Nashville in July. Had a very family vibe - everyone knew each other in my class except for me (a Class Pass-er trying it out for the first time). Great instructor - very hands on. 

The room is TINY, but luckily there were only six or seven of us in the class (it was a random class in the middle of the day on a weekday). The room is oddly shaped and very small, so if the class was full, I'm sure I would have been hitting everyone else with my arms and legs every 30 seconds. Another frustrating thing? BarreAmped is located within a house on 16th that is also a gym. The building does not say BarreAmped on it! No sign at all! It was my first time coming to this location, and I drove right past it and had to circle around to find it. Then, when I walked inside, no one was at the welcome desk, so I wasn't even sure I was in the right building! Finally someone came in (looked like something using the gym rather than working there), and she told me the BarreAmped room was the up the stairs. A bit confusing. I wish that information had been on Class Pass and that they had a sign on the building.

Still it was a great class, and I think I'd go again!
Rewrite this for me:
I attended my first BarreAmped class at the Music Row location, and it exceeded my expectations. Compared to other barre classes I've taken since moving to Nashville in July, this class was a much better workout and overall experience. It had a warm and welcoming atmosphere, with everyone in the class knowing each other, except for me as a first-time Class Pass-er.

Although the room was small and oddly shaped, I was fortunate that there were only six or seven of us in the class. If it had been full, the cramped space would have made it difficult to avoid accidentally bumping into others. One aspect that frustrated me was the location of BarreAmped within a house on 16th Street, which also serves as a gym. The building lacked any signage indicating that it was BarreAmped, causing me to initially drive past it and have to circle back to find it. Moreover, when I entered the building, there was no one at the welcome desk, leaving me uncertain if I was in the correct place. Eventually, someone who appeared to be using the gym rather than working there informed me that the BarreAmped room was upstairs. This lack of clear guidance made the experience a bit confusing. I wish this information had been provided on Class Pass and that there had been a sign on the building.

Despite these slight inconveniences, I thoroughly enjoyed the class and would consider attending again.

input: When I called she put me on hold 3 times. Was very rude. Then when delivery came received wrong order. She wouldn't fix this, and hung up on me 3 times. Very rude and horrible service. Don't go there
Rewrite this for me: She put me on hold three times and was very rude when I called. Moreover, when the delivery arrived, it was the wrong order. Despite my request for her to rectify the mistake, she refused to help and hung up on me three times. This kind of behavior was extremely rude and the service provided was absolutely horrendous. I strongly advise against going there.

input:
Had the chicken and French toast and it was over the top!
While it would do some good to have more shade on the patio it was still an enjoyable experience. They are pet friendly too!
We will be back!
Rewrite this for me: I had the chicken and French toast and it was absolutely fantastic! Even though it would be nice to have more shade on the patio, overall, it was a delightful experience. Additionally, they welcome pets, which is a bonus. We definitely plan on returning!

input: Kudos to this place for providing a much needed late night snack while I was visiting Nashville! Didn't have to wait on delivery because they allowed pick-up at 2 AM! Pizza honestly looked like it wasn't going to be all that great but LOOKS WERE DECEIVING! The pizza was delicious and my only regret was that I didn't order a bigger one!
Rewrite this for me: I want to give praise to this establishment for offering a greatly appreciated late-night snack during my visit to Nashville! It was fantastic that they offered the option to pick up the food at 2 AM, saving me from any delivery wait time. Admittedly, at first glance, the pizza didn't seem incredibly impressive, but appearances can be deceiving! To my delight, the pizza turned out to be absolutely delicious. My sole disappointment was not ordering a larger size!

input: Terrible delivery service & food order was incorrect once received an hour over what I was told.  All the food was under or over cooked.  Never again!  Sad
Rewrite this for me: The delivery service was absolutely awful, and to make matters worse, my food order was completely incorrect and arrived a whole hour later than promised. On top of that, every single dish was either undercooked or overcooked. I am deeply disappointed and vow to never order from them again. It's truly disheartening.

input: Great spot to come to if your in Nashville. The have one the best drink deals you can find on thursdays and Saturday's and Sunday's. Food is okay.
Rewrite this for me: If you're in Nashville, this is an excellent place to visit. They offer fantastic drink deals on Thursdays, Saturdays, and Sundays. The food quality is decent.

input: I like their salads, tea, and french fries! The servers were great...I've been here a few times and I'd come back!
Rewrite this for me: Their salads, tea, and French fries are absolutely delightful! The servers provided excellent service, and I have enjoyed my experience here multiple times. This place definitely deserves a revisit!

input: This was a great place to have brunch with the family. It is very clean and the staff were great. I love the decor!! Plus, my four year old actually ate here!!! That is a HUGE deal. He doesn't like anything.
Rewrite this for me: I had an amazing experience having brunch with my family at this place. The cleanliness was top-notch and the staff were exceptional. The decor was absolutely delightful too! What's even more impressive is that my picky four-year-old actually ate here! That's an incredibly significant achievement considering how difficult it is to please him.

input: Very cute place with a great selection of loose leaf teas and other tea paraphernalia. The drinks and sweets are delicious and creative. Great relaxing ambience. As a tea lover, I loved reading the books about tea that the owner had. The owner is very nice and is very knowledgeable and passionate about tea. I would love to come back again!
Rewrite this for me: This adorable establishment offers an exceptional assortment of loose leaf teas and an array of tea-related items. Their delectable and imaginative drinks and sweets are simply delightful. The ambiance is perfect for unwinding and enjoying a peaceful atmosphere. As a tea enthusiast, I thoroughly enjoyed perusing the collection of tea books curated by the owner. Speaking of whom, the owner is not only incredibly friendly but also extremely well-informed and enthusiastic about tea. Needless to say, I cannot wait to revisit this place!

input: Great food and service. The antipasto was by far the best that I have ever had.  The pasta is all fresh and full of flavor. The Fisherman's stew was loaded with great tender fish in a saffron sauce.
Rewrite this for me: The food and service were exceptional. The antipasto surpassed all expectations and stood out as the best I've ever tasted. The pasta was incredibly fresh and bursting with flavors. The Fisherman's stew was a delightful combination of tender fish in a saffron sauce.

input: Muriel's is a great stop in NOLA. The goat cheese and shrimp crepes are by far the best food I ate in the city (perhaps anywhere ever) and the rest of the meal lived up to the appetizer. Service is great, venue is quintessential French Quarter. It's a little distracting to see ghost tours outside the window at dinner- but the food is so delicious, you won't mind the audience. Rumor has it that Muriel's is haunted, but the only thing other worldly I encountered was the cuisine.
Rewrite this for me: Muriel's in NOLA is an absolute must-visit. Without a doubt, the goat cheese and shrimp crepes I had there were the most exceptional dishes I've ever tasted, not just in the city but possibly anywhere. The quality of the rest of the meal was equally impressive, and the attentive service only enhanced the experience. Situated in the quintessential French Quarter, the ambience of the venue is delightful. The only slight distraction during dinner was the sight of ghost tours passing by outside the window, but the incredible flavors of the food effortlessly overshadowed any minor inconveniences. While there are rumors of Muriel's being haunted, the only otherworldly aspect I encountered was the extraordinary cuisine.

input: Went to this Taco Bell last night.  It was 1 30 and it said 30 minutes to close.  All the lights were on.  We backed up and forward twice and no one would wait on us.  We gave up and pulled up young man was at window closing  register.  Taco Bell was happy to serve us.
Rewrite this for me: Last night, I visited Taco Bell and arrived at 1:30 AM. The sign indicated that the establishment would be closing in 30 minutes, yet all the lights were still illuminated. We maneuvered the car back and forth twice in the drive-thru lane, but unfortunately, no staff members came to take our order. Frustrated, we eventually decided to quit and started to drive away. Surprisingly, just as we were about to leave, a young man appeared at the window, closing the cash register. Suddenly, Taco Bell seemed more than willing to serve us.

input: Cute place to eat at. Ate breakfast here and was dissappointed after seeing such good reviews. Breakfast menu is very limited. The omlet was just OK.  Biscuit didnt have much flavor to it. We were able to be seated really quick (during the week) but i imagine it getting really crowded during the weekends.
Rewrite this for me: This is an adorable restaurant to dine at. However, I was quite let down after reading all the rave reviews. The breakfast options are surprisingly limited. The omelet was decent but nothing exceptional. Unfortunately, the biscuit lacked flavor. On the bright side, we were seated promptly, especially on weekdays. Although, I can imagine it getting quite crowded on weekends.

input:
Probably the most expensive game in town. But totally worth it for me. I upgraded myself to the executive locker rooms because that gives me zero excuses for why I can't go to the gym before work or after if I am going out later that night. I always have my makeup, hair stuff, etc in my locker. Just getting back to the gym after a long absence due to health issues so I'm taking it slow. I've seen one or two machines that are not quite working right but the facility as a whole is pretty sharp & welcoming. You have tons of options of what to do classes wise, equipment wise...
My only 2 down sides are that I wish they were open a little later on weekends, but that's just me moving slowly on my time off. I wish there was a bit more ritation with the class schedule. There are classes I'd like to take but they always run mid day, never really early, after work or weekends. So no option to try them. I'm sure it's an instructor issue so not likely something that will change. Overall I'm super happy that I joined.
Rewrite this for me:
It's probably the most expensive gym in town, but to me, it's totally worth it. I decided to upgrade myself to the executive locker rooms, which means I have no excuses for not going to the gym before or after work, even if I have plans later in the evening. I always have all my makeup, hair products, and other essentials stored in my locker. After a long absence from the gym due to health issues, I'm taking it slow and easing back into my routine. While I have noticed a couple of machines that aren't functioning properly, the overall facility is well-maintained and inviting. There are endless options for classes and equipment, which is fantastic.

However, there are two downsides for me. I wish the gym had later hours on weekends, but that's just because I prefer to take things slowly during my time off. Additionally, I would appreciate a more varied class schedule. There are classes I'd love to try, but they always seem to be scheduled in the middle of the day, never early in the morning, after work, or on weekends. It's possible that this issue is related to specific instructors, so I don't expect it to change. Nonetheless, I'm overall extremely happy that I made the decision to join this gym.

input:
A++

Everyone can be crammed at the bar, and the employees running around like their hair is on fire, and Ally still treats you like you're her only customer. 
Cool vibe, great indoor and outdoor seating. Great addition to the Funk Zone.
Definitely go!!
PS: Say hi to Ally for me :-)
Rewrite this for me: I must emphasize that this place is absolutely amazing, and one of the primary factors contributing to its greatness is the exceptional bar staff. Particularly, there is a bartender named "Ally" who consistently proves to be remarkably kind and attentive. Even in times when the bar is packed with customers and the other employees are running frantically, Ally manages to make you feel like the most important customer she has. The atmosphere is cool, the seating options both indoors and outdoors are fantastic, and it is undoubtedly a superb addition to the Funk Zone. You should definitely visit this place! Oh, and don't forget to send my regards to Ally too :-)

input: Not to bad. I sat at the bar and the bartender was awesome. The lunch menu here is very decent and the beer is ice cold.  I usually come during lunch when it isn't to congested. So, to get consistent service,  go when it isn't to congested. I will definitely go back?
Rewrite this for me: It's pretty good. I took a seat at the bar and the bartender was amazing. The lunch options here are quite satisfactory, and they serve ice-cold beer. I prefer to come for lunch when it's not too crowded. If you want reliable service, visit during less busy times. I will definitely return.

input: The only knock on this place is that they didn't have all the pools open during Memorial Day weekend. Other than that the hotel provides a very friendly environment that's good for adults and families as well plenty of places to eat inside the resort and the atrium was amazing and really fun to explore. Little far from town but a good middle point between music row and the airport. Hotel staff was top notch and the place was clean while still having that old charm. I'd stay here again in a heart beat next time I visit Nashville.
Rewrite this for me: The only downside of this place is that not all the pools were available during Memorial Day weekend. However, apart from that, the hotel offers a welcoming atmosphere suitable for both adults and families. Additionally, there are plenty of dining options within the resort. The atrium is particularly impressive and provides an enjoyable experience for exploration. Although it is a bit far from the city center, it serves as a convenient midpoint between music row and the airport. The hotel staff is exemplary, maintaining cleanliness while still retaining its unique, old-world charm. I would not hesitate to choose this accommodation again when I return to Nashville.

input:
Great treat to beat the heat! I stopped in during the Manayunk Arts Festival yesterday to get a cold refreshing treat and I was very pleased with the service and the quality of the fresh frozen yogurt and toppings.

It is a self service fro-yo establishment with countless options of flavors and toppings. I enjoyed the toasted coconut yogurt and topped it with rainbow sprinkles, fresh strawberries, blueberries and raspberries. The fruit was very refreshing but it was hard to select what to put on it because everything looked so yummy. If you are a chocolate lover there are plenty of candy toppings to add to your fro-yo too. 

If you are not sure what flavor you will enjoy best you can sample them with small paper cups that so you don't have to find out if you like the flavor or not after you already purchase! 

Another plus is that the establishment is kept very clean and it still looks as new as it did when it first opening on Main Street just a couple of years ago!
Rewrite this for me:
Cool off from the heat at the Manayunk Arts Festival by treating yourself to some delicious frozen yogurt! I had a fantastic experience yesterday at this self-service fro-yo joint. They offer an incredible array of flavors and toppings to choose from. 

I decided to go with the toasted coconut yogurt and added a variety of toppings including rainbow sprinkles, fresh strawberries, blueberries, and raspberries. The fruit was so refreshing, but it was a tough decision because everything looked absolutely scrumptious. For all the chocolate enthusiasts out there, they have a wide selection of candy toppings to satisfy your cravings.

One thing I loved about this place is that you can sample different flavors before making a purchase. They provide small paper cups, so you can try out a variety of flavors without any regrets.

Another great aspect of this establishment is that it is immaculately clean. Despite being in business for just a couple of years, it still looks as pristine as the day it opened on Main Street.

input: I think the trendiness of this chain, in general, has sort of faded and what you have left is the basis of this chain, which is over-priced food of a questionable quality. I wouldn't call it bad, but it's a whole lot of fried food and most of the breadings, whether it's fried pickles or okra or calamari or shrimp, are the same across all of that. The batter is fine, but it gets wearing. The coconut shrimp and hush puppies were definitely overcooked, which was kind of disappointing. Coke Zero on tap, but the mix could be better. For the price, it is also worth nothing there is a ton of food here, definitely quantity over quality. Décor is pretty cool and this is parked right along the Boise river, though it's a bit tucked away and has to be more or less sought out...probably worth hitting at least once, but there are far better local places that are more worthy of attention.
Rewrite this for me: I believe that the popularity of this chain has decreased over time, leaving behind an establishment that serves expensive food of uncertain quality. While not necessarily terrible, their menu mostly consists of fried food with similar breading for items like pickles, okra, calamari, and shrimp. Although the batter is decent, it can become monotonous. Unfortunately, the coconut shrimp and hush puppies were overcooked, which was disappointing. They do offer Coke Zero on tap, but their drink mix could be improved. In terms of value, it's important to note that you get a large quantity of food for the price, but the quality may not match. The décor is attractive, and the restaurant is located by the Boise river, although it may require some effort to find. It might be worth visiting at least once, but there are definitely better local establishments worth exploring.

input:
There are bars you can still smoke in?! Yuck. Sorry smokers (I used to be one so I get it) but yuck. The stink of smoke in my hair woke me up in the middle of the night after stopping in here and was so bad I had to get up to wash it before I could get back to sleep. That's not good.

Definitely a dive, this bar is very dim and smokey. The bartender was friendly and came to take my order as soon as I walked up to the bar. The bloody mary I ordered wasn't that great or strong, though.  That's not good either.
Rewrite this for me:
Are there still bars where smoking is allowed? Disgusting. I apologize to smokers (I used to be one, so I understand), but it's disgusting. The smell of smoke in my hair woke me up in the middle of the night after visiting that place, and it was so terrible that I had to wash it before I could go back to sleep. That's not ideal.

This bar is certainly a dive. It's dimly lit and filled with smoke. The bartender was friendly and promptly took my order when I approached the bar. However, the bloody mary I ordered wasn't impressive or very strong. That's also not a good thing.

input: Got there mid-morning today, the early rush was over. Two tables were full, each with three people. The family in one of the tables had just walked in ahead of me, so they were being attended to first. Still, I was immediately welcomed, and in a couple of minutes a friendly lady brought the breakfast menu and asked if I wanted coffee. A cup appeared a few moments later, and was kept full throughout my visit. Radio playing golden oldies from the 70s, my kind of music. The ham omelet with home fries and toast arrive a few minutes later, worth waiting for. Done just right and kept me filled for hours. A friendly family restaurant where you feel welcome and appreciated, just north of Gulfport.
Rewrite this for me: I arrived at the restaurant around mid-morning today, after the early rush had died down. There were two occupied tables, each with three people. I noticed that the family at one of the tables had just entered before me, so they were being served first. However, I was greeted immediately and within a couple of minutes, a friendly lady brought me the breakfast menu and asked if I would like coffee. My cup was quickly filled and remained that way throughout my visit. The radio was playing golden oldies from the 70s, which perfectly suited my taste in music. Shortly after, my ham omelet with home fries and toast arrived, and it was definitely worth the wait. It was cooked to perfection and kept me satisfied for hours. This family-friendly restaurant, located just north of Gulfport, made me feel welcome and appreciated.

input: This place is so lovely. It has everything!! Amazing wine selection, hookah's, Lebanese food which I think is the best in the city.
Rewrite this for me: This location is absolutely enchanting, offering an abundance of attractive features! The wine selection is truly remarkable, accompanied by a variety of hookah options. Moreover, they serve Lebanese cuisine, which, in my opinion, surpasses all other establishments in the city.

input: This was recommended by a colleague who is local in the area. A group of us from work decided to go and give it a try.  As soon as we sat down, Chris, took care of us.  He was patient, understanding and extremely knowledgeable of the menu.  Well, our entire party enjoyed every part of the evening while at Red Mess!  From the chips & salsa to the drinks to each of our entrees ... just absolutely DELICIOUS!

input: This is my 3rd time and 3rd location at a Brick House across the country. This is by far one of the few chain restaurants I will regularly and happily eat at. Rewrite this for me: I have been to a Brick House across the country three times now, and this is my third location. input: So... This place is the sh*t. By far the classiest spot on the block, Siam is nudging STL standards up and up. The sashimi:  top grade. input:
Worn down signs intrigue me.  I had biked passed 16th Street Seafood a ton of times, always wondering what was going on inside.  Now I know the answer, and the answer is- not much. At least in terms of decor. There is a gumball machine, 2 empty candy machines, plus a counter to order at and that's pretty much it. Also absent was the plethora of seafood over ice you would hope to see at a place specializing in seafood. There were some frozen crab cakes, breaded fish fillets, clams, and crabs- but not else. Still, I threw caution to the winds of Tasker Street and put in an order.

I didn't want to go for fried seafood, so the sandwiches and platters were out.

I got a large order of mussels in butter and garlic sauce ($9.50). Mussels are one of those things I like making at home, but it is way too hot for that right now. . My main complaint is that the order came with an unacceptable amount of closed shells - 9!   It was still a good sized order with a big piece of bread to dip in the unexpectedly spicy, broth. As the place is to-go only- they know how to wrap up messy seafood orders, nothing was spilled.

Remember when I said I didn't want anything fried, well that's not ever actually true. So I ended up sneaking in 2 fried shrimps. Not bad, but not worth $1.25 each.
Rewrite this for me:
The worn-out signs caught my attention, piquing my curiosity every time I biked past 16th Street Seafood. I always wondered about what was happening inside. Finally, I discovered the truth: not much, at least when it came to the decor. The establishment only had a gumball machine, two empty candy machines, and a simple counter for placing orders. It was a far cry from the abundance of seafood over ice that one would expect from a seafood specialty place. The offerings were limited to frozen crab cakes, breaded fish fillets, clams, and crabs. Nevertheless, I decided to disregard any concerns and placed an order.

Given my aversion to fried seafood, I ruled out the sandwiches and platters. Instead, I opted for a large serving of mussels in butter and garlic sauce priced at $9.50. Although I usually enjoy cooking mussels at home, the current weather made it unsuitable. However, my main dissatisfaction was the unexpectedly high number of closed shells in my order - a whopping nine! Nevertheless, the portion size was generous, and it was served with a large chunk of bread for dipping into the surprisingly spicy broth. Since the place only offered takeout, they knew how to package messy seafood orders efficiently, as no spills occurred.

I initially claimed that I didn't want anything fried, but that turned out to be a lie. I couldn't resist sneaking in two fried shrimps. While they weren't terrible, I didn't believe they were worth the price of $1.25 each.

input: Great little upscale but not overpriced cafe. Lots of options, but needs a lox bagel sandwich. :) One of my preferred places to lunch with someone.

input:
Animo juice is the best find in Haddonfield (after the Hadrosaurus, of course!)

I stop at Animo every time I go to Jersey to visit my family; or do I visit my family every time I stop at Animo?  Debatable.

Animo started with juice.  Not frozen juices with sorbet & yogurt added.  Real juice.  

Their menu has expanded & they now call themselves "Animo Juice & Burrito Bar!"  The burrito menu features 10 burritos, all under $10, f my favorite the "Haight & Ashbury" is stuffed with rice, beans, meat/roasted veggies, cheese, lettuce, tomato, guacamole & sour cream.

Not that hungry, have a 'petito', a small version of the burrito, averaging $5.  Porky & Petunia - the name is as cute as the petito is yummy:  shredded lettuce, pulled pork & pineapple salsa.  

A breakfast petito & Animo MD juice destroy any hangover.  The MD is juiced greens, carrot, orange, apple, kiwi, banana & spirolina.   My BF loves the Chilly Palmer:  Acai, apple, banana, yogurt & flax seed.  

For a happy belly add or substitute the perfectly cooked quinoa to any dish.  The Border Salad is a perfect example: lettuce, guac, pico de gallo, cheese, tortilla chips, cilantro lime vin, & sub quinoa for meat.   

Fiber-full signature juices, frozen whipped bananas, sliced fresh wheat grass (cheaper than Jameson!) & yogurt/granola bowls!  

The city's juice bars have something to learn from Animo.
Rewrite this for me:
Animo juice is an amazing discovery in Haddonfield, only second to the fascinating Hadrosaurus!

Whenever I visit my family in Jersey, I make sure to stop by Animo every single time. Well, some may argue that I visit my family because I want to stop at Animo. It's debatable, really.

Animo began with a focus on juices, but not your ordinary frozen ones with added sorbet and yogurt. They only offer real, freshly squeezed juices.

However, their menu has now expanded, and they proudly present themselves as the "Animo Juice & Burrito Bar!" Their burrito menu showcases ten delicious options, all priced under $10. My personal favorite is the "Haight & Ashbury," filled with rice, beans, your choice of meat or roasted veggies, cheese, lettuce, tomato, guacamole, and sour cream.

If you're not feeling too hungry, they also offer a smaller version of the burrito called a 'petito' for an average price of $5. Their "Porky & Petunia" petito is not only cute in name but also incredibly tasty. It includes shredded lettuce, pulled pork, and pineapple salsa.

For those in need of a hangover cure, their breakfast petito accompanied by Animo MD juice is the perfect combination. The MD juice is a blend of juiced greens, carrot, orange, apple, kiwi, banana, and spirolina. Trust me, it works wonders. My boyfriend swears by the "Chilly Palmer," a refreshing mix of Acai, apple, banana, yogurt, and flax seed.

To elevate your culinary experience, you can add or substitute the perfectly cooked quinoa to any dish. Take the "Border Salad," for example, which is a delightful combination of lettuce, guacamole, pico de gallo, cheese, tortilla chips, cilantro lime vinaigrette, and you can opt for quinoa in place of meat.

Animo also impresses with their fiber-full signature juices, frozen whipped bananas, sliced fresh wheatgrass (and it's cheaper than a shot of Jameson!), as well as yogurt and granola bowls!

The juice bars in the city could definitely learn a thing or two from Animo.

input: Had a very memorable birthday in SB and was so happy to have Wine Edventures be my gift! Sean picked us up Saturday morning and was super friendly (funny, too). It was just my husband and I along with a group of 10 - who happened to be all guys, having a bachelor party! Haha, so that was pretty funny. We stopped at 3 wineries and 1 brewery. Sean explained where we were as we were driving around and also gave us lessons at the tastings. He provided us with bottled water and souvenir wine glasses. We had lunch at the 2nd vineyard of the day, which was very good - choice of sandwich and a pasta salad side with chips and a cookie (the cookies are awesome). It was a fun day and I'd highly recommend this adventure to anyone looking for a fun day in the SB area.
Rewrite this for me: I had an incredibly memorable birthday experience in SB, thanks to Wine Edventures! Sean, our friendly and funny driver, picked us up on Saturday morning. It was just my husband and I, along with a group of 10 guys who were celebrating a bachelor party - quite a funny mix! Throughout the day, we visited three wineries and one brewery. input:
This is my favorite in Delaware.  The menu is simple and perfectly executed.  Rolls are reasonably priced, artfully made and are PACKED with fish!  I do believe they use flash-frozen sashimi grade fish, but the color, texture, taste and smell are perfect.  Easily the best spicy tuna I have ever had.  I think the secret is the kewpie mayo along w/ the right amount of sriracha and sichimi powder.  Frankly, I can't get enough of this place and have at times, eaten it every day for lunch for weeks.  I've gone as far as to pick it up for dinner AFTER having had it for lunch. Their introduction of short-grain brown sushi rice has been great!

The Sushiman, YC Park is amazing to watch.  I've seen him skin a cucumber with a sword-like sushi knife in no time flat, in a single ribbon and then continue to shave it into a nori thin sheet for his tuna naruto roll roll.  The temaki are as big as a carnival iced cream cone.  You can barely finish one of them, there is so much fish in there.  The nigiri are beautiful.  Uniform pieces of fresh fish, perfectly perched on the best sushi rice I've ever had (just the right amount of vinegar and sugar).

Skip the newly opened Kooma.  Save Mikimotos for a night out, but go to Tokyo for lunch!  The owners are lovely, so support them in this tough economy.  If you must eat sushi, eat it here!

Why not 5 stars?  I have to save it for places that serve the local fresh fish, plucked out of the water that morning.  Let me know if you find a place that does!
Rewrite this for me:
This place in Delaware is my absolute favorite. The menu is simple yet executed perfectly. The rolls are reasonably priced, skillfully made, and filled to the brim with fish! I believe they use flash-frozen sashimi grade fish, but the color, texture, taste, and aroma are flawless. Without a doubt, the best spicy tuna I've ever tasted. I think the secret lies in the combination of kewpie mayo, sriracha, and sichimi powder. Honestly, I can't get enough of this place and have even had it for lunch every day for weeks. On some occasions, I've gone as far as picking it up for dinner after having it for lunch. Their addition of short-grain brown sushi rice has been a fantastic innovation!

YC Park, the Sushiman, is truly amazing to watch. I've witnessed him effortlessly skin a cucumber with a sushi knife that's as sharp as a sword, creating a beautiful ribbon-like sheet to wrap around his tuna naruto roll. The temaki here are enormous, almost the size of an ice cream cone at a carnival. You'll struggle to finish even one of them because they're jam-packed with fish. The nigiri pieces are works of art. Each piece of fresh fish rests perfectly on the most exquisite sushi rice I've ever tasted, with just the right hint of vinegar and sugar.

I would advise against trying the newly opened Kooma. Mikimotos is better saved for a special night out. However, when it comes to lunch, Tokyo is the place to go! The owners are delightful, so let's support them during these challenging times. If you're in the mood for sushi, this is the place to be!

Why not give it 5 stars? Well, I reserve that rating for places that serve locally caught fresh fish, straight from the water that very morning. Let me know if you come across a place that does!

input: So I'm super confused as to why everyone rags on this place. They're super nice, quick, and cheap.  People have complained about their chicken fingers being dry but I have no clue what they're talking about. They're great and their honey mustard is delicious. I've had salads from there too and they give you lots of veggies which I love. Their fries are delish as well and I love that they give you cole slaw with the chicken finger platter. All and all, I love that this place is literally a few steps away from my apartment and that they have decent food. I also don't understand the greasy spoon comments... you do realize it's a pizza joint right? You aren't going there for the ambiance, more for the cheap food.
Rewrite this for me: I'm really confused why people criticize this place so much. The staff is incredibly friendly, service is fast, and the prices are affordable. Some have complained about their chicken fingers being dry, but I completely disagree. I find them great, especially when paired with their delicious honey mustard. Additionally, their salads are packed with plenty of veggies, which I personally love. The fries are also delicious, and I appreciate that they include cole slaw with the chicken finger platter. Overall, I love the convenience of this place being just a few steps away from my apartment, and their food is pretty decent. I also don't understand why some refer to it as a greasy spoon – it's a pizza joint after all. We don't go there for the ambiance, but rather for the affordable food.

input: Ambience OK, too bad stuck in a mall in New Hope.  They were very understaffed (which thankfully they kept apologizing for) so there service was definitely slow, however very very pleasant.  We definitely felt it was worth the wait!  Vegetable Samosas were delicious, chicken were slightly dry.  I ordered chicken tikka masala which was so flavorful and rich and my husband had the chicken tagine...amazing!  Has the feeling of a place where "you get what you get and you don't get upset" but when you get it, it is really out of this world!  Loved the mix of cuisines, just enough choices on the menu.  Restaurant is BYOB so we were unprepared, but we will be back!
Rewrite this for me: Despite being stuck in a mall in New Hope, the ambience was okay. Unfortunately, the restaurant was severely understaffed, leading to slow service. However, the staff was very pleasant and apologetic about the wait, making it worth it in the end. The Vegetable Samosas were delicious, although the chicken was slightly dry. I opted for the chicken tikka masala, which was bursting with flavor and richness, while my husband thoroughly enjoyed the chicken tagine - it was simply amazing. The place had an attitude of "you get what you get and you don't get upset," but when you finally received your order, it was truly exceptional. The mix of cuisines was delightful, and the menu had just the right amount of choices. It's worth mentioning that the restaurant is BYOB, which caught us off guard, but we plan on returning prepared next time.

input: I definitely won't be coming back here. Long story short, I scheduled an appointment online to have the transmission and differential fluid changed on my pilot. I arrived on time, and I was told it would take approximately 2 hours for completion, I also said I wanted an oil change, but " full synthetic". He said it would be $20 more, I said okay. When it was finally done and I was ready to check out, my advisor (Brandon) give me the total cost, which was double than what I expected and paid for in the past. I asked him what was all done, he said, "they completed a transmission flush instead of the regular drain and refill". I told him that's not what I wanted or asked for. He went on to say "it was good for the car and whatever", like I'm some kind of idiot. First of all Honda doesn't recommend doing a transmission flush and secondly, its almost triple what you would normally pay for a standard transmission fluid change. On top of that they didn't even do a full synthetic oil change it was just a blend. I didn't have time to argue with him because I was already late for an appointment, but I have the email showing what I originally asked for, so I'll be calling my bank soon.
Rewrite this for me: I will never return to this place. To summarize, I made an online appointment to have my pilot's transmission and differential fluid changed. Upon arrival, I was informed that it would take around 2 hours to complete. I also requested an oil change with full synthetic oil, for which I agreed to pay an additional $20. When the work was finally finished and I was ready to pay, my advisor, Brandon, informed me that the total cost was double what I had anticipated and paid in the past. Confused, I asked him what had been done, to which he replied that they had performed a transmission flush instead of the regular drain and refill. I clearly stated that this was not what I wanted or asked for. He then proceeded to dismiss my concerns and insinuated that it was good for my car. Firstly, Honda does not recommend a transmission flush, and secondly, the cost was almost triple the usual price for a standard transmission fluid change. Furthermore, they did not even provide a full synthetic oil change as requested; it was simply a blend. Unfortunately, due to being late for another appointment, I did not have time to argue with him. However, I do have the email that shows my original request, and I will be contacting my bank soon.

input: We love, love M.L. Rose! I am a huge beer fan and the flights are so fun to choose and try. I love the neighborhood hangout feel, not too hipster, not too old....just right! We always have awesome service too. My hang up can be the food. Wings not quite crispy enough, burgers not cooked to taste, spinach artichoke dip just meh. The steak and Gouda was flat out gross - big fatty slab of undercooked steak on bread. We were told it is leaving the menu, but they should have removed it long ago. And no visit from the manager when the sandwich was returned, which was a little underwhelming. We will be back, we are big fans, but please get your kitchen together so I can have my fav burger in town cooked just right :-)
Rewrite this for me:
We absolutely adore M.L. Rose! As a passionate beer enthusiast, I find their flights to be exhilarating and enjoyable to select and sample. The ambiance of the place gives off a wonderful neighborhood hangout vibe, striking the perfect balance between trendy and old-fashioned. Moreover, our experiences have consistently been accompanied by exceptional service.

However, I do have some minor grievances concerning the food. The wings often fall short of achieving that desired crispiness, while the burgers tend to miss the mark when it comes to meeting our personal preferences in terms of doneness. The spinach artichoke dip, unfortunately, fails to impress, leaving us feeling somewhat underwhelmed. The steak and Gouda dish was nothing short of repulsive - a substantial slab of poorly cooked steak atop a slice of bread. Although we were informed that this dish will no longer be on the menu, it should have been removed far earlier. Additionally, it was quite disappointing that no visit from the manager occurred when we returned the unsatisfactory sandwich.

Despite these grievances, we remain dedicated supporters and will undoubtedly return. We kindly request that the kitchen staff address these issues so that I can indulge in my favorite burger in town, expertly cooked to perfection.

input:
We went on a non typical day, school year mid week, so we had the luxury of being only a handful of people there  Therefore, my review may not be representative of a typical visit. 
Arrived at opening and found the off season price within reason. Bathrooms and water park were immaculate. The lifeguards were attentive and friendly. 
A star was lost because I found the water and air temp to be a tad too cold. The park was smaller then other indoor water parks I've been to. Only two big slides, one group slide, a couple of younger kids areas, lazy river and a simulated surf area. They would periodically close the big slides in order to open the surf area, for lack of staffing. A minor annoyance since that is why we were there. 
I can see how people  would be upset paying more and sharing the park with hundreds of others. But I think if your timing is right, you could have an enjoyable afternoon.
We did save money by using our AAA card. Could have saved more as it was my sons birthday month, but I didn't have proof on me.
Rewrite this for me:
On a atypical mid-week day during the school year, we had the privilege of being among only a few individuals present. It's important to note that my review may not accurately reflect a typical visit. We arrived as soon as the park opened and found the off-season price to be reasonable. Additionally, the bathrooms and water park were exceptionally clean. The lifeguards were both attentive and friendly.

However, I deducted one star from my review due to the slightly chilly water and air temperature. Moreover, the park itself appeared smaller compared to other indoor water parks I have visited. It consisted of only two large slides, one group slide, a couple of sections for younger kids, a lazy river, and a simulated surf area. Occasionally, the park would close the big slides to open the surf area due to a lack of staff. Although this was a minor inconvenience since it was one of the main reasons we visited, I understand that it could potentially disappoint other guests.

I can empathize with those who may be unhappy paying more and having to share the park with hundreds of others. However, if you plan your visit correctly, you could have a pleasant afternoon. Additionally, we were able to save some money by using our AAA card. It is worth mentioning that we could have saved even more as it was my son's birthday month, but unfortunately, I did not have the necessary proof with me.

input:

input: Great food but the service is so bad we seen our waitress once  everyone else did here job plus I was not finished eating and she gave me the check    Hate that   But good food
