input:
Came here with a group of girls, so we were able to order a bunch of different things to try.  I gotta say they made the best squid steak I ever had.  Flavor was amazing.  

The only downside, was that the service was really slow, and everything is extremely over priced.  The food took forever to come out, and we had to wave the waitress down for drinks.

If we had gotten better service, and the prices not so high, I would have given them 4 stars.
Rewrite this for me:
Arrived with a bunch of girls, allowing us to sample a variety of dishes. I must say, their squid steak was absolutely incredible - the flavor was outstanding.

However, the service left much to be desired as it was exceptionally slow. Additionally, the prices were excessively high. The wait for the food seemed never-ending, and we had to actively seek out the waitress for our drinks.

Had the service been better and the prices more reasonable, I would have easily given them a 4-star rating.

input: I love the whole concept. We had such a great experience here. The food was delicious. Our waiter was the best. We ordered cheesecake which was even better. I can't wait to come on the day they make cinnamon rolls. We will defiantly be back.

I am eagerly looking forward to the day when they make the cinnamon rolls, as I can't wait to try them. Without a doubt, we will definitely be returning.

Rewrite this for me: Meijer is absolutely fantastic and incredibly convenient! input: I love their eggs! Their eggs taste better than any other restaurant eggs I've ever had. We always get the hash. Dawn Patrol is always super generous with the food portioning...with the hash, that is. My brother got a burger to go, and all it was was a piece of meat between two buns. However, he said the burger was really good, but still, I feel that they could've melted some cheese on top of the patty. All of their pastries, bread and jellies are homemade - and really delicious!
Rewrite this for me: I absolutely adore their eggs! They surpass the taste of any other restaurant eggs I have ever had. Our go-to order is always their hash. Dawn Patrol has consistently impressed us with their generous portion sizes when it comes to their hash. On a separate occasion, my brother decided to get a burger to take away, but unfortunately, it was just a simple meat patty tucked between two buns. Nevertheless, he mentioned that the burger was incredibly tasty. In my opinion, though, I believe they could have enhanced it by adding melted cheese on top of the patty. It's worth noting that their pastries, bread, and jellies are all homemade, and they are truly delectable!

input: Came late Friday night for a bite to eat. Much of the soup, hot takeaway were cleaned up. Settled for an individual pizza to share. input: Had lunch here today. My cheeseburger was a 10/10 with an avocado on top. I also had the "ranchero fries" which are French fries with ranch, cheese, and tomatoes on top! input: Great food!  Service was super nice: George!  Crab cakes were awesome.  Just a great place to eat!

input:

input:
I normally wouldn't think Greek food for brunch or lunch; I'm way more of a traditional American-style brunch kind of guy.  But when my friends suggested to meet them here for brunch this past weekend, I trusted their better judgement.  In the end, I'm glad I did.  This cozy Center City spot not only serves an amazing (and dare I say, a contender for the best) brunch in Philly, the staff really make you feel at home.  They really know how to wow their patrons: fresh food, delightful presentation, and so many delicious sounding choices it's hard to choose which dish you want from their one page menu for mains.

Their specialty, and they're not shy to tell you, is the Cyprus Breakfast.  It's a mediterranean twist on the classic combination of eggs, meat, and starch.  The plate comes out with two sunny-side up eggs, fried in olive oil and garnished with fresh parsely.  It's served alongside a grilled slice of lounza (Greek ham), two pieces of salty, crisp fried halloumi, warm bread, and tomato, cucumber, and onion salad.  The menu also features a spread of other traditional Greek, Mediterranean, and Middle Eastern specialities: Avgolemono, Moussaka, Pastitsio, Shaksouka, and Malohwa to name a few.  They even serve Greek Coffee and Frappes!

The service may be a little over-attentive in an attempt to make you feel more than welcome, but it's much appreciated, especially when other restaurants fail to put as much effort into the service as they do the food.  One other tip: reservations are highly recommended, if not required.  Because of Kanella's small space, getting a table at brunch is nearly impossible if you're not on the list.  But if you can score seats here for brunch, then expect nothing less than a stellar way to start your weekend morning (or recover from last night's activities).  Can't wait to come back and try out the dinner menu.
Rewrite this for me:

But if you manage to snag a seat here for brunch, expect nothing short of an exceptional start to your weekend morning (or a perfect recovery from the festivities of the previous night). I am already eager to return and explore their dinner menu.

input: This place gets two stars from me only because the gravy fries were good. Their sandwiches are awful. Thick slabs of badly sliced, tough, dry meat....gross. I made the mistake of ordering their pork sandwich once and it was inedible. I tried to bite into the sandwich and couldn't even bite through because of how tough and rubbery the pork was. I don't understand why they slice the meat the way they do but it makes for a disgusting sandwich. The people raving on how good this place is are just locals who have never had anything better. You're better off going to Wawa for a sandwich. Seriously. It will at least be edible.
Rewrite this for me: I can only give this place a two-star rating simply because their gravy fries were enjoyable. However, their sandwiches are truly awful. The meat slices are thick, poorly cut, and incredibly tough, resulting in a dry and unpleasant experience. I made the regretful decision of ordering their pork sandwich once, and I simply could not consume it. The meat was so tough and rubbery that I couldn't even take a decent bite. I find it puzzling why they choose to slice the meat in such a manner, as it ultimately ruins the overall quality of the sandwich. Those who highly praise this place are likely locals who haven't had the opportunity to taste anything better. I would strongly recommend going to Wawa for a sandwich instead. Trust me, it will at least be edible.

input:

They sell damaged items.  Check your stuff very well before you leave, because you will not be able to bring it back if you discover that they have slipped you the ole' damaged door!

In summation, I strongly advise against supporting this establishment in any way.

input: We stopped here on our way through town and want sure what to expect but we were pleasantly surprised. The service sucked and the staff was rude but the food made up that in the end. We had some pulled pork which was more chopped then pulled, brisket tacos which were define, and pulled chicken which was moist. The sides were pretty good too but nothing to write home about. There were five of us and our bill was close to $60 and one meal was a kids meal. I  really only have two complaints: One, they didn't have ribs for lunch and two, the bathrooms were filthy.
Rewrite this for me: On our journey through town, we decided to make a stop here with uncertain expectations. However, to our pleasant surprise, the food compensated for the subpar service and rude staff. Although the pulled pork was more chopped than pulled, the brisket tacos were exceptional, and the pulled chicken was wonderfully moist. The sides were decent, albeit unremarkable. With five of us dining, our bill approached $60, even with one meal being a kids' meal. I do have just two grievances: firstly, they unfortunately did not offer ribs during lunch, and secondly, the state of the bathrooms was disgustingly unclean.

input:

While some noodle soup dishes and rice plate dishes are true to authentic Chinese food, others are truly found in only American Chinese restaurants. The duck is very fat and very little meat. The stir fry dishes have weird combo of vegetables that do not go together.

And as a typical Chinese restaurant, service does not come with a smile.
Rewrite this for me:
I recently attempted dining at this establishment and observed that the quality of the food was inconsistent. While certain noodle soup and rice plate dishes managed to maintain the essence of authentic Chinese cuisine, others appeared to be exclusive to American Chinese restaurants. For instance, the duck dish consisted of an excessive amount of fat and a scarcity of meat. Furthermore, the stir fry dishes featured an odd combination of vegetables that did not seem to complement each other.

In line with the typical Chinese restaurant experience, the service lacked warmth and smiles were absent.

input:
I have always dreaded going to the hair salon.  I hated the phony atmosphere of most places and I really dreaded the small talk I would be forced to have with my stylist.  Maybe I am unusually insecure, but I always felt intimidated in most salons.  
Then, one day a couple of years ago, I wandered into Andre's salon and I never looked back.  
Andre is warm and personable and made me feel at ease immediately.  Right off the bat, we connected on a topic I care about--dogs--and I didn't feel uncomfortable at all.  Oh, and the cut and color were fantastic!  My highlights last longer than highlights I have received from any other salon.
For the past year or so, Christopher has been styling my hair and I LOVE him to death.  He is incredibly sweet, down-to-earth and talented!  My hair looks amazing for days after he styles it and, try as I might, I can never get it to look as good as he can.
The last time I was at the salon, Christopher, Leah and I had a blast reminiscing about '80s fashion!  I can't remember a time when I enjoyed going to the hair salon (which is probably because I never have!).
Also, back in the spring, I asked Andre if he would be interested in donating a gift for a charity 5K I was helping to organize.  Being the wonderful person he is, Andre didn't hesitate and put together a beautiful basket that was a hit at the race!  Andre has a good heart and that it what I love about going to his salon!
I also love that clients can schedule appointments online through schedulicity!
Great prices, great cuts, great color, great space, convenient scheduling options and, most importantly, great people--you will not regret choosing Andre for your next cut or color!
Rewrite this for me:
I used to dread going to hair salons because of the fake atmosphere and forced small talk with the stylist. It always made me feel insecure and intimidated. However, a couple of years ago, I stumbled upon Andre's salon and it completely changed my perception.
Andre is warm and personable, instantly making me feel at ease. We bonded over our mutual love for dogs, and I no longer felt uncomfortable. Not to mention, the cut and color he gave me were absolutely fantastic, with highlights that lasted longer than any other salon could achieve.
For the past year, Christopher has been styling my hair and I cannot express my love for him enough. He's incredibly sweet, down-to-earth, and incredibly talented. My hair looks amazing for days after he styles it, and no matter how hard I try, I can never recreate that same look on my own.
During my last visit, Christopher, Leah, and I had a blast reminiscing about '80s fashion. It was such a fun experience, and it's a rare instance where I actually enjoy going to a hair salon.
On top of their exceptional skills, Andre also showed his kindness when I asked him to donate a gift for a charity 5K event I was organizing. Without any hesitation, he put together a beautiful basket that was a hit at the race. Andre truly has a good heart, and that's what I appreciate most about his salon.
I also love the convenience of scheduling appointments online through schedulicity. It makes everything so much easier.
So, if you're looking for great prices, cuts, color, and a wonderful environment with amazing people, don't hesitate to choose Andre for your next hair appointment. You won't regret it!

input: Absolutely amazing and unique food. Love their bobba and pork pancake!
Rewrite this for me: Their food is absolutely astonishing and incomparable. I adore their mouth-watering boba and delectable pork pancake!

input:
Nice, old school space with a long bar. It reminded me of some places I've been out west, which might be a little strange in the heart of Philadelphia. 

Not too loud at all - conversations were easy and a lot of the patrons were doing just that. There's a jukebox, so maybe it cranks up later in the evening. We were there pretty early. 

Great service from several people working behind the bar. 

Several beers on tap including a local CCCCC IPA, which was solid. Not many wines, though.

Small menu but very good food. The elote (corn) is quite good, as was the cucumber(?) salad. But the brat plate was the star. Wonderful brat, German potato salad, sauerkraut, pretzel and a hot salsa/relish. Best brat plate ever. Served on a cool wood board.

Prohibition is located in or near a somewhat dicey neighborhood, at least to this non-resident's eye. I may very well be wrong about that. We had to walk a trashy, pissy street past what seemed like skid row coming from the hotel on Race St. If it was later at night we might have chosen not to walk back.
Rewrite this for me:
The atmosphere of this place is charming and reminiscent of older times, with a spacious layout and a lengthy bar. It's interesting to find such a place in the heart of Philadelphia, as it evokes memories of western establishments. 

The noise level is moderate, making conversations easy to have. Many patrons were engaged in conversations themselves. A jukebox is present, so it's possible that the volume increases later in the evening, although we visited during the early hours.

The bar staff provided excellent service, with multiple individuals tending to customers' needs.

There is a decent selection of beers on tap, including a local CCCCC IPA that is highly recommended. However, the wine options are limited.

While the menu is small, the food quality is exceptional. The elote (corn) and cucumber salad are both delicious, but the standout dish is the brat plate. It includes a fantastic bratwurst, accompanied by German potato salad, sauerkraut, pretzel, and a flavorful hot salsa/relish. The presentation on a wooden board adds to its appeal. Undoubtedly, it is one of the best brat plates ever tasted.

It's worth noting that Prohibition is situated in or near a neighborhood that may appear questionable, at least from the perspective of someone not residing in the area. This perception could be incorrect, but we encountered a dirty and unpleasant street while walking back from our hotel on Race St. If it had been later in the night, we might have chosen an alternative transportation method.

input:
On the Run is a convenience store chain and BP gas station. It is in a very convenient location for those who are returning rental cars at Lambert-St. Louis International Airport! How many times have you been on the way back into an airport, and not found a gas station nearby? Happens to me to any times - often you have to go out of your way to find one. Not so here!

Paid at the pump - I note that the pump had a hand scrawled note taped to the pumps - requesting you press the appropriate button (credit or debit) before swiping your credit card. Never seen this before - this is the exact opposite procedure of other gas station pumps when using a credit card!

Refueled and was on my way to Hertz!
Rewrite this for me:
On the Run, a convenience store chain and BP gas station, is strategically located near Lambert-St. Louis International Airport, making it extremely convenient for those returning rental cars. How many times have you found yourself heading back to the airport only to struggle to find a nearby gas station? I have personally experienced this situation countless times, often having to go off route just to refuel. However, this is not the case at On the Run!

One interesting thing I noticed while refueling was a hand-written note taped to the pumps, instructing customers to press the appropriate button (credit or debit) before swiping their credit card. This was a new experience for me since most gas stations follow the opposite procedure when using a credit card.

After refueling, I quickly continued my journey to Hertz.

input: The service was great and the restaurant was clean, but the food was just okay. We had the linguine with marinara and the rotini primavera. The linguine was fine. The primavera, however, is not something anyone should order!!! The sauce had a great flavor, but the vegetables were actually from frozen. I mean, literally from FROZEN. Go to your local grocery store, look at the bag of Bird's Eye mixed vegetables and you will see what they use... right down to the ruffle cut carrots. There is so much wonderful fresh produce in Tucson, there is absolutely no reason to ever use gross frozen vegetables.
Rewrite this for me: The service provided at the restaurant was excellent and the cleanliness of the establishment was truly commendable. However, the food itself was merely satisfactory. We decided to try the linguine with marinara and the rotini primavera. The linguine turned out to be fine, nothing extraordinary. Unfortunately, the same cannot be said about the primavera dish. It is highly advisable to avoid ordering it altogether! Despite the sauce having a delightful flavor, it was rather disheartening to discover that the vegetables used were actually frozen. I mean, they were literally taken from a freezer. If you were to visit your local grocery store and inspect the bag of Bird's Eye mixed vegetables, you would notice an uncanny resemblance to the ones used in this dish, including the distinctive ruffle cut carrots. Considering the abundance of fresh produce available in Tucson, it is truly disappointing that this establishment chose to utilize unappetizing frozen vegetables.

input:
We  heard that Fresh Market was open and since we just got back from vaca we thought we would try it.  First of all, accolades to the staff they could not have been more helpful.  Especially Thomas in the meat section.  For these two things I would give them a five.  However, it does downhill from this point on:  ordered one pound of swiss cheese, after standing there waiting for about 5 minutes, and no one else was on line, the unfriendly clerk waited on us. The imported swiss cheese that we ordered was so poorly cut that in two days we had one clump of swiss cheese, rather than many slices.  I bought ricotta cheese for Easter and went to open it, and it was bad, although it was dated 3/28.  The tomatoes on the vine that I bought on Friday were bad by Sunday.  I have found their prices very high, selection, poor and at this point it is just not worth it. I also bought two pound cakes and their were not up to par.  Very dry and tasteless.. Overall a very disappointing shopping trip 
There is plenty of convenient parking and the store was immaculate, but it is not for me.  The final straw was that I asked for extra cash for Easter gifts, the clerk at the register said there was a $150 limit, the ATM terminal said $100 and the "manager" said $50...I thought they should get their act together.  Best to stay with Weaver's Way... or Whole Foods or Wegmann's.
Rewrite this for me: After hearing that Fresh Market had opened, we decided to give it a try shortly after returning from vacation. Firstly, we must acknowledge the incredibly helpful staff, particularly Thomas in the meat section, who deserves praise. Based on this aspect alone, we would give them a five-star rating. However, our experience took a downward turn from there. We ordered one pound of Swiss cheese and despite being the only customers in line, the unfriendly clerk made us wait for about five minutes before assisting us. Furthermore, the Swiss cheese we received was poorly cut, resulting in a clump rather than individual slices within just two days. On Easter, I purchased ricotta cheese which was dated 3/28, yet it turned out to be in bad condition. Additionally, the tomatoes on the vine that I purchased on Friday became spoiled by Sunday. Not only have I found their prices to be exorbitant, but their selection has been lacking as well. At this point, the overall experience is simply not worth it. I also bought two pound cakes, but they were disappointingly dry and tasteless. Ultimately, this shopping trip proved to be highly unsatisfactory. While the store boasts ample and convenient parking, as well as an immaculate environment, it does not cater to my needs. The final straw was when I requested extra cash for Easter gifts, as the clerk at the register mentioned a $150 limit, the ATM terminal stated $100, and the supposed "manager" claimed it was only $50. It became clear that the store lacked consistency and organization. It is best to stick with Weaver's Way, Whole Foods, or Wegmann's for a better shopping experience.

input:
I've only been once, but I'm ready to return.

Since moving to Fletcher Place, I've been looking for a bar near by that's similar to my neighborhood favorite, J Clydes. I think I've found it.

The Dugout is a simple hole-in-the-wall place. They have a decent selection, Sun King for $4.50, happy hour appetizers, and my favorite part: HOT PEPPER CHEESE BALLS! No longer must I wait until my coveted Mug N' Bun trips for these fried morsels of tasty peppery goodness. Had a nice little piece form this joint, too. 

Really excited to return.
Rewrite this for me:
After visiting once, I am eager to go back again. Since I moved to Fletcher Place, I have been searching for a bar in the vicinity that resembles my favorite neighborhood spot, J Clydes. And I believe I have found it.

The Dugout is a modest and unassuming establishment. It offers a decent range of drinks, with Sun King available for only $4.50. They also serve happy hour appetizers, and the highlight for me are their HOT PEPPER CHEESE BALLS! Now, I no longer have to patiently wait for my special trips to Mug N' Bun to enjoy these delectable fried treats with a kick. Additionally, I had a pleasant experience at this establishment.

I am genuinely thrilled at the prospect of returning to The Dugout.

input:
I heard this ice cream parlour opened last summer, so upon my first trip home (sometime during the fall) I hustled over to try it. Since Friendly's closed a few years ago, Warminster has sorely needed a new ice cream place (DQ was our last one standing for quite some time). 

Much to my dismay, the Big Scoop had already closed for the season. I marked it in my calendar go return in March, when it reopened. Upon my next trip home in the spring, I was disappointed to see that I was just a few days early for their reopening, and would have to wait until my return in April.

After much anticipation, I made it to Big Scoop last weekend with my sister (who has been before). I was shocked to see what a range of products they serve - hot dogs, funnel cake, onion rings, pizza, you name it! I was tempted at the prospect of waffles and ice cream, but I wasn't that hungry so I settled for a scoop of chocolate chip cookie with hot fudge and whipped cream. The generous scoop of ice cream was tasty and packed with globs of cookie dough! I also tasted the birthday cake, which I enjoyed very much. 

The service was quick, and the shop crowded quickly. The interior was nicely remodeled and looks clean and family friendly. The man who helped me was extremely courteous and seemed to be doing most of the work. 

Especially given the lack of competition around here, the Big Scoop gets an easy four stars!
Rewrite this for me:
Upon my first visit back home in the fall, I was eager to try the new ice cream parlour that had opened last summer. With Friendly's closing down a few years ago, Warminster was in desperate need of a new ice cream spot, as DQ had been our only option for quite some time.

To my disappointment, I discovered that the Big Scoop had already closed for the season. I made a note in my calendar to return in March when it reopened. When I visited home again in the spring, I was disheartened to find that I had arrived a few days early and would have to wait until April for their reopening.

Finally, last weekend, I managed to visit the Big Scoop with my sister, who had been there before. I was pleasantly surprised to see that they offered a wide range of products, including hot dogs, funnel cake, onion rings, pizza, and more. The idea of waffles and ice cream caught my attention, but since I wasn't very hungry, I settled for a scoop of chocolate chip cookie ice cream with hot fudge and whipped cream. The generous scoop of ice cream was delicious and filled with delectable chunks of cookie dough. I also had a taste of their birthday cake flavor, which I thoroughly enjoyed.

The service at the Big Scoop was fast, and the shop quickly filled up with customers. The interior had been nicely remodeled and had a clean and family-friendly atmosphere. The man who assisted me was extremely polite and seemed to be managing most of the work.

Considering the lack of competition in the area, I would easily give the Big Scoop a four-star rating!

input: Aparently this review is for Saguaro East. I didnt realize there were two separate parks. This park is fine. We planned to do some hiking, but it just looked like flat average desert you can easily see and hike in the Phoenix area. The visitor center and staff were nice.
Rewrite this for me: It seems that this review pertains to Saguaro East. Initially, I was unaware of the existence of two distinct parks. As for this particular park, it left a satisfactory impression. Our intention was to engage in some hiking, however, it appeared to be a rather ordinary desert landscape that closely resembled what one can readily find and hike in the Phoenix region. On a positive note, the visitor center and the staff were amicable.

input:
Staff is amazing!  Coupons on their website are for 40 percent off a regular priced item... so that means... you are always getting something on sale!

We went in one evening at around 15 minutes before closing to grab some things very quickly... and all staff members were very helpful even so close to closing!  

Great store!
Rewrite this for me:
The staff here is incredible! Their website offers coupons for a generous 40% discount on regular priced items, which means you can always find something on sale!

One evening, we arrived at the store just 15 minutes before closing to quickly grab some items. Despite the late hour, all the staff members were extremely helpful and accommodating!

This store is truly excellent!

input:
This is another one of those anytime coffee shops. You can come get some work done, people watch, or just grab a drink to go. Either way, its open early and late.

For the quarter, its "off the beaten path" but in the busy area the locals hang out, and on the way to Fenchmen where everyone goes for good local music, Jazz, et al. 

They have food, not the cheapest, or local, but its better for you than the greasy, salty, fatty foods. Just make sure your service number is visible I got distracted hid my number, and had to stop the guy looking.  

Service varies. Since its a busy sidewalk, people stop in for that pick me up before work or party. One minute there is a like 12 long, and the barista is running ragged, the next its dead. 

Sometimes I'll sit for over an hour working or catching up on email. I'll order something every so often, and its no big deal for me to queue myself if they get busy. After all it helps those stopping in for a quick drink.

p.s. I love there tall cookies

oh and how many coffee shops can you get a shot in your coffee! That's right, its not a bar, but its New Orleans.
Rewrite this for me:
This is one of those coffee shops that you can visit at any time. Whether you want to get some work done, people watch, or just grab a drink to go, they've got you covered. They open early and stay open late.

It's located off the beaten path, in a busy area where locals like to hang out. It's also on the way to Fenchmen, a popular spot for good local music, jazz, and more.

They serve food here, although it may not be the cheapest or strictly local. However, it's definitely a better option than greasy, salty, and fatty foods. Just make sure to keep your service number visible, as it's easy to get distracted and misplace it.

The level of service can vary. Since it's situated on a busy sidewalk, people often stop by for a quick pick-me-up before work or a party. Sometimes, there could be a long line of about 12 people, and the barista may be overwhelmed. Other times, it could be quite dead.

Personally, I've spent over an hour sitting here, either working or catching up on emails. Every now and then, I'll order something to support the place, and it's not a big deal for me to wait in line if they get busy. After all, it benefits those who just want a quick drink.

By the way, their tall cookies are amazing!

Oh, and let's not forget that you can get a shot of something in your coffee here! Although it's not a bar, this is New Orleans we're talking about.

input: Salad portions are great. I always go with the Greek. One of the few Nick's spots that serves a rustic roast beef sandwich. Highly recommend that one. Pizza isn't that bad. I'd recommend an XL if having guests over. It's probably there better pizza, surprisingly.
Rewrite this for me: Salad portions are generous, and my personal favorite is the Greek. Nick's is one of the rare spots where you can enjoy a delicious rustic roast beef sandwich. I highly recommend trying it. The pizza is not too shabby either. If you're hosting guests, I suggest going for the XL size. Surprisingly, it might just be their best pizza option.

input:
Definitely dug this place...rather hipster-ish and way, way reminiscent of Este Sugarhouse in Salt Lake, but I liked it a lot despite all that...pizza here is definitely a lot better, as is beer selection. This may wind up being one of my more regular haunts as I slog my way through more of their menu (I think I may need to heavily modify next time I'm there), but so far, I have no cause at all for complaint and much to celebrate. It's interesting to me that the environments of the various locations are different, sometimes vastly, yet all have their own unique and innate charm. Whoever is running these is doing a phenomenal job, so props there.

One thing of note here...the ordering system is extremely clunky and seemingly disorganized and I sort of dislike it. Not enough to stop coming here, since I really dig the vibe of these, but on one of my less patient nights, that sort of thing may be enough to cut this out of the running. Definitely a good spot for pizza and a brew (or several), though. I back it.
Rewrite this for me:
I really enjoyed this place, it had a hipster vibe and reminded me a lot of Este Sugarhouse in Salt Lake. Despite that, I still liked it a lot. The pizza here is definitely better, as well as the beer selection. I may end up coming here regularly as I try more items on their menu, although I might have to make some modifications next time I visit. So far, I have no complaints and plenty to celebrate. It's interesting to see how each location has a different environment with its own unique charm. The person in charge is doing an amazing job, so kudos to them.

One thing worth mentioning is that the ordering system is really clunky and disorganized, which I don't really like. However, it's not enough to make me stop coming here since I really enjoy the atmosphere. On a night when I'm feeling less patient, that kind of thing might be enough to make me reconsider. Overall, it's a great place for pizza and drinks. I fully support it.

input:
New St. Louis Wok is one of the few local Chinese places that deliver to our area.  Every time (but one), we've ordered, and gotten the food within an house.  In addition, they have a website where you can order the food (avoiding possible language barriers), and then they follow up with a call for your credit card number.

Food wise, it's the best Chinese delivery we've had here.  Nothing too greasy, and everything comes hot...with lots of sauces and fortune cookies.  For our rare Chinese cravings, it's the go-to place.
Rewrite this for me:
New St. Louis Wok stands out among the limited number of local Chinese restaurants that offer delivery services to our vicinity. We have consistently received our food within an hour of placing an order on every occasion, with only one exception. What sets them apart is their user-friendly website which allows for convenient online ordering, eliminating any potential language barriers. Moreover, they ensure a secure transaction process by following up with a phone call to obtain your credit card information.

When it comes to the quality of the food, New St. Louis Wok undoubtedly excels as the finest Chinese delivery option in our area. Their dishes are not overly greasy, and each item arrives piping hot, accompanied by a generous selection of sauces and fortune cookies. Whenever we find ourselves yearning for Chinese cuisine, this establishment remains our top choice.

input: This is my go to sushi place. it's cheap and the rolls are AMAZING. if you want a new sushi place to try i highly recommend osaka
Rewrite this for me: Osaka is my absolute favorite sushi spot. The prices are affordable and the rolls there are absolutely incredible. If you're looking to explore a new sushi place, I cannot recommend Osaka enough.

input:
Kelly's has changed hands and the menu has completely changed.  It's clear they've had to defend this and it seems to annoy them.  I mean the menu was epic - why change it?

In response, the new crew touted the place being cleaner and it was.

I got the  classic burger and fries.  I'll be honest, it was the worst $11 burger that I've ever had.  Dry and flavorless and made me envy a $2 McDonalds bacon burger flashing on the TV.  The fries were OK.

I was shocked to just walk in at dinner time.  This wasn't possible before.  Now I know why.

:
Rewrite this for me:
The ownership of Kelly's has changed and as a result, the menu has undergone a complete overhaul. It appears that they have faced criticism for this decision, which seems to frustrate them. The previous menu was highly praised, making the change even more incomprehensible.

In response to the criticism, the new staff emphasized the improved cleanliness of the establishment, which was indeed noticeable.

I decided to try the classic burger and fries. To be completely honest, it was the most disappointing $11 burger I have ever had. It lacked moisture and flavor, leaving me longing for a $2 McDonald's bacon burger that I saw advertised on television. The fries, on the other hand, were decent.

I was surprised to find that I could easily walk into the restaurant during dinner time, something that was never possible before. Now I understand why that is the case.

input: Great place to go everyday. I saw huge changes in my strength and flexibility there. All of the teachers are unique and teach beneficial classes. I highly recommend a monthly membership!
Rewrite this for me: Every day, it is a fantastic destination to visit. My strength and flexibility underwent remarkable transformations there. Each teacher possesses their own distinct style and imparts highly advantageous classes. I wholeheartedly recommend obtaining a monthly membership.

input:

I used to be a regular customer in my neighborhood, ordering takeout at least once a week. However, in recent times, I have experienced delays of 10 to 15 minutes as the staff struggles to find change during my pick-up visits. All I wanted was to simply pay for my food and enjoy it at home.

input: Their pizza is pretty good, service is usually cool inside. But today I ordered a delivery for the first time, the driver was very insulting to me. input:
First time here and I have to say it's pretty good! The bake shop fits well with the fishtown environment and it's very clean and welcoming inside. The display of beautiful cakes let's you know you have top quality bakers there. 

I got a few items to share such as a Burbon Pecan cookie, chocolate chip cookie, vanilla cupcake with buttercream icing, and a vanilla cupcake with raspberry icing. 

I had a taste of the Burbon Pecan Cookie. It was not too sweet and you get nice bites of pecan; a nice hot coffee is a perfect compliment.The cupcakes were good (cake wise) but, not a huge fan of the icings. The cake itself was sweet and moist. 

Didn't get to try the Chocolate chip cookie but the concensus was that it's delicious. 

I would definitely come back and I have taken a big interest in having Cake Life make a custom order!
Rewrite this for me:
This is my first visit here, and I must say it's quite impressive! The bakery seamlessly blends with the charming atmosphere of Fishtown, and the interior is exceptionally clean and inviting. The assortment of exquisite cakes on display assures you of the presence of skilled bakers.

I decided to indulge in a few treats to share: a Bourbon Pecan cookie, a chocolate chip cookie, a vanilla cupcake with buttercream frosting, and another vanilla cupcake with raspberry frosting.

Let me start by mentioning the Bourbon Pecan Cookie. It possessed just the right amount of sweetness, and the delightful pecan bites added a lovely touch. Accompanied by a piping hot cup of coffee, it became the perfect combination. As for the cupcakes, the cake itself was deliciously sweet and moist. Unfortunately, I wasn't particularly fond of the icings. Nonetheless, the overall experience was enjoyable.

Although I didn't personally try the Chocolate Chip Cookie, the consensus among others was that it was absolutely delicious.

Without a doubt, I will be returning, and I'm now even considering placing a custom order with Cake Life.

input:
Went here last Thursday and arrived early enough to take advantage of their $5 domestic pitchers during hh which includes mich golden light, my fave! It did take the server about 10-15 minutes to even notice we were there, but after that service was just fine. 

Started off with the wings which were delicious, although the bf was certain it was not actually a pound of wings which they claim on their menu.

I ordered the gyro and fries which were surprisingly really good! Gyro meat was tasty and the fries were awesome! Bf had the French onion soup and potato skins which he said were good as well.

We stayed for rock n roll bingo (which I guess is every Thursday, and free!) and we had a blast. They also have a pool table and darts in the back which we played while waiting for bingo to start.

We will definitely be back!
Rewrite this for me:

To start, we ordered the wings, which were delicious, although my boyfriend was skeptical that it was actually a pound of wings as stated on the menu.

For my main course, I decided to try the gyro and fries, and to my surprise, they were really tasty! The gyro meat was flavorful, and the fries were amazing! My boyfriend, on the other hand, had the French onion soup and potato skins, which he also enjoyed.

We stayed for their rock n roll bingo, a fun event that apparently takes place every Thursday and is free! We had an amazing time. Additionally, they have a pool table and darts in the back, which we played while waiting for bingo to start.

We will definitely return!

input: Johnny Tucci and his crew are the absolute best videographers, hands down. They are professional, prompt, and extremely talented. They made our wedding footage look like a movie production and brought everyone to tears that watched it. My advice is that if you are going to splurge in one area for your special day, spend it on a videographer. They do not disappoint.
Rewrite this for me: There is no doubt that Johnny Tucci and his crew surpass all others as videographers. Their exceptional professionalism, punctuality, and remarkable talent shine through in every project they undertake. They transformed our wedding footage into a veritable cinematic masterpiece, evoking tears from all who viewed it. If you want to indulge in one aspect for your special day, my recommendation is to invest in a videographer. Trust me, you will not be let down.

input:
One of the absolute best places to see a game in the entire country!

Get there early or if it's a blowout, stroll around the park. There are tons of interesting places to eat & drink (including a rooftop bar). Tickets are still amazingly reasonable even after all the success the Phils have had in recent years particularly when compared to the NY parks.

I used to go more often before the team became so prominent (right after the park opened), and I sat all over the joint. Not really anywhere I wouldn't recommend. The outfied is a great option. 

After starting with a 17 game pack many years ago & then buying season tix a few years back (which my company still has), the staff was great about recommending sections that would avoid direct sunlight , etc. (3rd base field level is awesome).

If you are visiting or considering a trip, don't buy the negative publicity about the Philly fans. The crowds are great. Sure, you have idiots and maniacs like you do at any park and for any professional sporting event, but they are by far the minority and Citizens Bank Park is policed pretty well for nonsense. 

I was once with a group of guys & we stood out in one of the open standing areas between 3rd base & the left field wall the whole night. At one point a very nice officer politely asked us not to curse because there were families around. We we were far from out of control, and we all thought that was pretty cool... so we had fun with some occasional lighthearted banter with the officer for the rest of the night.

Don't expect to be sheltered with your kids like you would be in your own living room, but there's no teens running onto the field getting tazed every night nor are there drunk idiots throwing up on people. 

It's a great atmosphere, a wonderful park & still a very fun team to watch.
Rewrite this for me:
Citizens Bank Park is undeniably one of the top destinations nationwide to catch a game! To make the most of your visit, consider arriving early or take a leisurely stroll around the park if the game becomes a blowout. You'll be delighted by the myriad of fascinating dining and drinking options, including a fantastic rooftop bar. Even with the Phillies' recent success, ticket prices remain surprisingly reasonable, especially when compared to the observation deck of the New York parks.

In my earlier days, before the team gained its current prominence, I frequented the park and explored all corners of it. I can honestly say that there isn't a bad seat in the house. Opting for the outfield provides an outstanding experience.

Years ago, I started with a 17-game pack and eventually purchased season tickets, which my company still holds. The staff went above and beyond to suggest sections that offered shade and other amenities. I highly recommend the field level at third base - it's simply awesome.

If you are considering a visit to the park, don't believe the negative reputation surrounding Philly fans. The crowds are fantastic. Granted, there may be a few troublemakers like at any sporting event, but they are definitely the exception rather than the rule. Citizens Bank Park is well-regulated and ensures a pleasant experience.

Once, while standing in an open area between third base and the left field wall with a group of friends, a kind police officer politely asked us to refrain from using profanity due to families being present. We were far from rowdy, and we found the officer's request quite cool. From that point on, we engaged in lighthearted banter with the officer and had a blast for the remainder of the night.

Although it's important to note that the atmosphere may not be as sheltered as your own living room when attending with children, you won't witness teenagers constantly interrupting the game nor drunk individuals causing disturbances. Citizens Bank Park provides a fantastic atmosphere, an exceptional venue, and a highly enjoyable team to watch.

input: I love Cosi but this Cosi is going down hill fast. I always get a signature salad and lately they are made wrong and no dressing at all. How hard is it to make their own signature salad!? It's practically what they are known for!!! So angry.

input: OMG!! what a disappointment today was, I have been so excited to see Rembrandt's reopen after a few months of remodel, what I was thinking is that the new owners would want to do more restorations of this Beautiful, Cozy, old Church, maybe try to find more space to add Tables, but NO, I walked into a Modern, Cold, Hospital Coffee Shop, the Charm is gone, so so disappointed and sad, we all love the Charm of Eagle, but it seems to be fading fast, Please People talk to all the other Eagle Shop Owners when your visiting them especially the old Original Buildings to keep Eagle's charm and quaintness and restore these Beautiful Buildings.
Rewrite this for me: Oh my goodness! Today was such a letdown. I had been eagerly looking forward to the reopening of Rembrandt's after it underwent remodeling for a couple of months. I was hoping that the new owners would prioritize restoring the charm of this beautiful and cozy old church. Perhaps they would even consider finding more space to add tables. However, to my dismay, what I walked into was a modern and cold coffee shop that felt more like a hospital. The charm has completely disappeared, and I cannot express how disappointed and saddened I am. We all cherish the charm of Eagle, but it seems to be vanishing rapidly. I urge everyone to engage in conversations with other shop owners in Eagle, especially those occupying old original buildings. Let's work together to preserve Eagle's charm and quaintness and restore these stunning structures.

input:
The service was lacking. The waiters and waitresses don't know the menu and when you ask for certain things to be brought to your table, it's constantly forgotten. The food is visually appealing but some of the most awkward and distasteful food I've ever had. The waffles are stale, the biscuits are hard as rock and their chorizo is not real chorizo.

The only thing this place has going for it is the atmosphere and their alcohol selection.
Rewrite this for me: The service provided fell short of expectations as the wait staff seemed unfamiliar with the menu and frequently overlooked requests made to bring specific items to the table. Although the food had an appealing presentation, it was disappointing in taste and truly some of the most awkward and unpleasant cuisine I've ever encountered. The waffles were stale, the biscuits resembled hardened rocks, and the chorizo was far from authentic. However, the atmosphere and the wide range of alcoholic beverages are the sole redeeming factors of this establishment.

input:
This restaurant is a nice place to go and sit down to have something to eat. I've ate just about everything they have on the menu and I'd say their burgers are great. Although their pizza is a bit on the tough side I still manage to eat the crust too. 

Very comfortable dining room area as well!
Rewrite this for me: This dining place is an enjoyable spot where you can relax and enjoy a delicious meal. I have tried almost every item on their menu and must say their burgers are fantastic. Despite the pizza being a bit chewy, I still find myself devouring the crust. Additionally, the dining room area is exceptionally comfortable.

input: We live in the neighborhood and have eaten here many times. I feel as if this restaurant is going downhill. This time we were there for dinner early on a Sunday. The bathrooms were filthy. There are 2 and one was not usable due to all of the paper towels that had been put into the toilet (there was no toilet paper). The other one was usable but also no toilet paper. Our server, Ashley, was not interested in providing any semblance of customer service...RUDE! We had a simple question about the beers on special and she became quite defensive. My daughter spilled her drink, which I realize is a pain in the ass for the restaurant and server (although we were outside so it wasn't that big a deal). We apologized profusely but she didn't even try to hide her annoyance. Finally, the chicken quesadilla should have been labeled the gristle quesadilla....more fat than actual meat...yuck. We love the proximity of this place to where we live and it was great in the past but not anymore...will likely not return...not with so many better quality restaurants in Northern Liberties and Fishtown.
Rewrite this for me: As residents of this neighborhood, we have dined at this establishment numerous times. However, lately, we have noticed a decline in its quality. Our recent visit for dinner on a Sunday was particularly disappointing. The condition of the bathrooms was unacceptable - one of them was inoperable due to an abundance of paper towels stuffed into the toilet, while the other one lacked toilet paper as well. Our server, Ashley, displayed a complete lack of interest in providing good customer service. When we asked a simple question about the beers on special, she became defensive and unhelpful. Furthermore, when my daughter accidentally spilled her drink, we sincerely apologized, understanding the inconvenience it caused. However, Ashley did not even attempt to hide her annoyance. Lastly, the chicken quesadilla we ordered should have been renamed the "gristle quesadilla" as it contained more fat than actual meat, leaving a negative impression. While we used to appreciate the restaurant's proximity to our home and have enjoyed it in the past, we are no longer satisfied with the current state. Therefore, we are unlikely to return, especially since there are plenty of higher quality dining options available in Northern Liberties and Fishtown.

input: Pretty average bar/restaurant with the menu offerings you can expect from a place like this. The food was OK, and the service was excellent.
