input: We came here based on the recommendation we received and from the street it doesn't look like much. But when you sit down and you scan the menu you will come to realize that this place serves nothing but home-cooked comfort food. We had the BLT and it was packed full of flavor, they didn't scrimp on the bacon and the vegetables for very fresh. With the sandwiches came some of the best french fries that we've had, and some of the best coleslaw that I've had in the state of Florida. We took a couple of pies home and they were delicious. We will definitely come back.
Rewrite this for me: We decided to visit this place based on a recommendation, although it didn't seem impressive from the outside. However, as we sat down and perused the menu, we quickly realized that this establishment serves exclusively homemade comfort food. Our choice, the BLT, was bursting with flavor as they generously included bacon and fresh vegetables. Accompanying the sandwiches were some of the most delectable french fries we've ever had, along with an exceptional coleslaw that ranks among the best we've tasted in Florida. We couldn't resist taking home a couple of pies, which turned out to be incredibly delicious. Without a doubt, we will be returning to this fantastic place.

input: I was greated by a nice friendly staff. There wasnt a long wait for my food. I ordered a chicken bacon croissant with chipolte sauce. They cut it in half as requested and was served in maybe only 20 seconds after the time it took to cook. Food taste great
Rewrite this for me: The staff welcomed me warmly and with kindness. I didn't have to wait long for my food, and it arrived quickly. I ordered a chicken bacon croissant with chipotle sauce, and it was cut in half as I had requested. It was served to me within 20 seconds after it finished cooking, and the taste of the food was excellent.

input: Excellent food! I am a Thai food junkie, and have travelled to Thailand and throughout Southeast Asia several times. There is ok Thai food in Nashville and then there is Great Thai food. This place was GREAT! The decor is a little dated but who cares...I was there for the food, which is fabulous!!!
Rewrite this for me: The food here is absolutely fantastic! As someone who adores Thai cuisine and has visited Thailand and other countries in Southeast Asia multiple times, I can confidently say that this place serves some of the best Thai food in Nashville. Despite the slightly outdated decor, the quality of the food surpasses all expectations. It is simply fabulous!

input: This place is absolutely fantastic. I honesty really don't even like sweets and am not all that into donuts but this place will make you a believer. The apple fritter is amazingly delicious and you can't go wrong with a chocolate long john. Don't even bother with any other donut shops in stl.
Rewrite this for me: This location is truly incredible. Even though I typically don't have a preference for sweets, especially donuts, this place will undoubtedly change your perspective. The apple fritter is exceptionally delightful, and you can never make a mistake with a chocolate long john. Save yourself the trouble of exploring other donut shops in St. Louis.

input: Of all the restaurants we tried in New Orleans, this was by far our favorite. I had both lunch and dinner on two separate occasions. The service was wonderful, the ambiance is cozy but alive. Make sure to call ahead and get a reservation over the phone if opentable looks booked. Their lunch special spicy fried chicken is a must have! If you are a party of two or three, ask for the corner booth by the window. Best table in the house.
Rewrite this for me: Out of all the dining establishments we sampled in New Orleans, this particular one stood out as our absolute favorite. On two different occasions, I had the pleasure of enjoying both lunch and dinner there. The service provided was exceptional, and the atmosphere struck a harmonious balance between snug and lively. To secure your spot, it is advisable to call in advance for a reservation if booking through Opentable seems fully occupied. It is imperative to treat yourself to their highly recommended lunch special, the tantalizing spicy fried chicken. If your party consists of two or three individuals, don't hesitate to request the corner booth by the window. Without a doubt, it is the ultimate choice for the prime spot within the establishment.

input:
City Parkの近くにある激安かき氷屋さん。シェーブドアイスっていったほうがいいね！
特に夏のニューオーリンズはジメジメして暑いから、公園に行った後にここでかき氷とか最高だと思う！

味の種類は半端なく多いです！50以上はあったはず！
そしてなんといっても安い！ぼくは一番安いチョイスのレギュラーかき氷のスモールを頼みましたが、スモールでも結構十分だと思います。そして値段はたったの$1.50. 安い！！

トッピングをしても５ドル以上はいかないはず。
夏のうだる暑さには、最高のチョイスだと思います！
Rewrite this for me:
There's a cheap shaved ice shop near City Park. It's better to call it "shaved ice"! 
Especially in the hot and humid summers of New Orleans, I think it's the best to have shaved ice here after going to the park!

There are so many flavors, it's unbelievable! There were at least 50 flavors!
And most importantly, it's cheap! I ordered the smallest size of regular shaved ice, called "Small," and even that was quite enough. And the price? Just $1.50. So cheap!!

Even with toppings, it shouldn't go over $5.
I think it's the best choice for the scorching summer heat!

input: Mr. X has amazing flavor and overall a pretty friendly staff. The wait time for carry out is on average about 20 minutes, which is way better than a 45 minute wait at chain pizzerias. I get the hand-tossed crust comparable to traditional NY style pizza, and has excellent flavor and texture!
Rewrite this for me: Mr. X is renowned for its exceptional taste and friendly team. The wait time for takeout usually lasts around 20 minutes, a significant improvement compared to the 45-minute delays experienced at chain pizzerias. I personally opt for their hand-tossed crust, which closely resembles the delectable NY style pizza. The delightful combination of flavors and remarkable texture never fails to impress!

input:
First time being here.  It was a nice place but empty.  Had one old man sitting in there, then us two 40 somethings, then another old man.  That was it.   We came during happy hour, basically waiting for Snake and Jakes to open up so we came here to kill some time.  

Beer selection was nice, Magic Hat, Fat Tire, Blue Moon, etc.  Prices were ok too.

Lotsa dark woods and a few TVs and a lonely but attractive bartender that was very nice.  

Nothing bad to say about this place other than it was kinda dead.  It was very clean looking and nicely decorated, just kinda boring.
Rewrite this for me:
This is my first time being here, and while it's a nice place, it feels empty. There was only one old man sitting in here, then the two of us in our forties, and another old man. That was the entire crowd. We came here during happy hour, just killing some time until Snake and Jakes opens up. 

The beer selection is good, with options like Magic Hat, Fat Tire, and Blue Moon. The prices are also reasonable.

The atmosphere has lots of dark woods, a few TVs, and a lone, attractive bartender who is very friendly. 

There's nothing negative to say about this place except that it lacks energy. It looks clean and well-decorated, but it can be a bit dull.

input:
i dont know what has happened to the in store service in this place!  We have been down here for a few weeks now and have been here 6 times.Only once was the order completed without a screw up!

Today 2 tall decaf coffees took close to 20 minutes.By then our bagels were cold.First i was told the decaf was "brewing' and then i was told there was something 'wrong" with the brewer? After 15 minutes i was offered a decaf americano.
Before we left i politely told a fellow behind the counter the service was abominable and he said 'well we can only store 2 vente size decafs at a time? HUH? I asked if the management knew about this and he just shrugged.
Clearly this staff has never been trained to make it right for the customer.No apology.No coupon.Just a convoluted story.
 
Amazing how you can have numerous people running around a store but you cant get the simplest order straight My next visit to a Starbucks will certainly not be this one.
Rewrite this for me:
I am completely dissatisfied with the in-store service at this place. Despite being here for a few weeks and visiting six times, there has only been one instance where my order was completed correctly. 

Today, it took nearly 20 minutes for two tall decaf coffees to be prepared. By the time they were ready, our bagels had already turned cold. At first, I was informed that the decaf was "brewing," but later I was told that there was an issue with the brewer. After 15 minutes, a decaf americano was offered to me.

Before leaving, I politely expressed my disappointment to a staff member behind the counter, who nonchalantly mentioned that they can only store two vente size decafs at a time. I was taken aback by this statement. When I asked if the management was aware of this problem, he simply shrugged.

It is clearly evident that the staff has not been trained to prioritize customer satisfaction. There was no apology or coupon offered, just a confusing explanation. 

It's truly mind-boggling to see so many people working in a store, yet they cannot manage to get a simple order correct. My next visit to a Starbucks will definitely not be at this particular location.

input:
As a double date with a good long lost friend for a relaxing evening dinner, we were surprised in early august to not get reservations until 8. 
So we arrived an hour early and had drinks in the lobby while the piano man played beautifully. The bartender was a bit slow at first but kept us well tended. 
Our table in the corner against the glass was ready early and we enjoyed watching the rays chase fish around the bay as the sun set.  
I started with the tasty crab and corn chowder but was a bit disappointed with al dente potatoes in the bowl. 
Wife ordered the scallops which were superb as was my crab stuffed grouper. But my rice was also inadequately cooked. 
Creve brûlée was excellent as was Tim's attentive service. 
Worth going again, but they need to get all the parts of the dishes correct to get 5 stars.
Rewrite this for me:
We had the pleasure of going on a double date with a long lost friend for a relaxing dinner, but were taken aback when we couldn't secure a reservation until 8 in early August. To kill time, we arrived an hour early and enjoyed drinks in the lobby while listening to the beautiful melodies played by the piano man. Initially, the bartender was a bit slow, but eventually took good care of us.

Fortunately, our table in the corner by the glass was ready ahead of schedule, allowing us to delight in the sight of rays chasing fish in the bay as the sun gracefully set. I started off with a delectable crab and corn chowder, although I was slightly disappointed by the al dente potatoes. Meanwhile, my wife ordered the scallops, which were truly superb, and I thoroughly enjoyed my crab stuffed grouper. However, I was let down by the inadequately cooked rice accompanying my dish.

The highlight of the evening was the excellently prepared crème brûlée, perfectly complemented by Tim's attentive service. Overall, the experience was worthwhile, but it would be deserving of a five-star rating if they could ensure that all components of their dishes are flawlessly executed.

input: My wife and I visited this hidden gem today and were not let down. The shop was clean, bright, colorful, and comfortable. We were able to sample all the flavors, listen to the story of how they came about, and walked off with many bags of deliciousness. The owners there were so kind. They took the time to understand exactly what kind of foods we enjoy to match us up with the perfect popcorn. Definitely coming back soon!
Rewrite this for me: Today, my wife and I had the pleasure of exploring this delightful hidden treasure, and it truly surpassed our expectations. The establishment exuded cleanliness, radiance, vibrant colors, and an inviting atmosphere. We found ourselves indulging in a plethora of flavors, whilst being captivated by the fascinating tales behind their creation. Leaving with numerous bags of pure delectability, we couldn't help but appreciate the genuine kindness of the owners. They attentively catered to our preferences, ensuring that we discovered the ideal popcorn for our tastes. Without a doubt, we will be eagerly returning in the near future!

input: A really cute new coffee shop in town. We stopped here in the morning to get a much needed caffeine break. Who's warm day so we opted to get an iced coffee. We had many options on the type of milk and sweetener is available. They had limited food items available being mostly donuts this morning. We opted for a piece of the vegan banana bread to share. Iced coffee came out quickly and are banana bread and we went outside to sit with and realize there is no area connected to this restaurant for outdoor seating. The restaurant next-door however was not yet open so we sat at one of their tables thinking no one would mind. It would be nice if the coffee house itself had its own outdoor seating. Are iced coffee was very good and hit the spot. The vegan banana bread was good but seemed very dense to me. I'll be back another time to try some more of the fancy coffee they have available here. I'm hoping that they will add to the food menu as well as a try to not eat donuts most days. Maybe a breakfast sandwich or some other option than a pastry would be good.
Rewrite this for me: We stumbled upon an adorable new coffee shop in town and decided to take a much-needed caffeine break. Since it was a warm day, we opted for a refreshing iced coffee. They offered a variety of milk and sweetener options, but their food selection was somewhat limited, mostly consisting of donuts. Nevertheless, we chose to share a piece of their vegan banana bread. As we received our iced coffees and banana bread, we realized there was no outdoor seating connected to the coffee shop. Fortunately, the neighboring restaurant was still closed, so we claimed one of their tables, assuming no one would mind. It would have been great if the coffee shop had its own outdoor seating area. Regardless, the iced coffee hit the spot and was absolutely delicious. Although the vegan banana bread was tasty, it seemed a bit dense to me. I plan to return in the future to try more of their fancy coffee offerings. Hopefully, they will expand their food menu to include options beyond pastries, such as breakfast sandwiches.

input: I went here after a recommendation that this is "the best coffee place in philly" and I'm so glad I checked it out! The cafe area itself is super nice & clean. They also offer tap and sparking water to customers which is awesome. Prices are very reasonable and the staff is super friendly. My friend and I chatted with one of the baristas for a few minutes and he gave us some pro-tips on how to make a killer espresso. I will definitely be coming back here again soon!
Rewrite this for me: I decided to visit this place after receiving a glowing recommendation as the "ultimate coffee spot in Philly", and I am extremely pleased that I followed through! The cafe space itself is remarkable, boasting a pristine and welcoming ambiance. In addition, they generously provide customers with the option of tap and sparkling water, which is truly delightful. Notably, the prices are highly reasonable, and the staff members are exceptionally friendly. During my visit, my friend and I had a pleasant conversation with one of the skilled baristas, who graciously shared some expert advice on creating a phenomenal espresso. Without a doubt, I intend to revisit this establishment in the near future!

input: It's a college-town bar, what do you expect? Lol. Alcohol, pub/bar food, good tap selection, good atmosphere and specials. A Villanova tradition. It's not an upscale bar, or a great place to grab lunch. It is what it is, a bar!
Rewrite this for me: What can you anticipate from this place? Well, it's a bar in a college town, so the expectations are pretty clear, haha! You can count on finding alcohol, pub/bar food, an impressive range of tap options, an enjoyable ambiance, and some fantastic deals. It's something that has become a Villanova tradition. Just to manage your expectations, it's not a fancy upscale bar or an ideal spot for a lunch outing. Simply put, it's a bar, and it embraces its identity as such!

input: Great customer service! Mary was a great help- helped me pick out frames and she was extremely personable! From the time I walked in the store, I was greeted with smiles and hellos! I will be back in the future!
Rewrite this for me: The customer service was outstanding! Mary provided exceptional assistance in helping me choose frames, and she had a delightful personality! As soon as I entered the store, I was warmly welcomed with smiles and greetings. I definitely plan on returning in the future!

input:
Simply stated...They are true to their word as it relates to having discounted furniture that is less expensive than your name brand furniture stores. The staff was friendly, they definitely don't follow you around the store, however, they get a ding for customer service because they don't seem to be as knowledgeable about the furniture products.

Furniture quality is a mix ranging from low to moderate quality.  

At the end of the day, if you are looking for less expensive furniture or to get a good deal or to find a unique accent pieces this is the place to be!  I mean...I saw "the same" sectional for $1,000 less than the name brand store.   Now that's a deal!!!
Rewrite this for me: In summary, this store lives up to its promise of offering discounted furniture at lower prices compared to name-brand stores. The staff is friendly and not overbearing, but their knowledge about the furniture products may be lacking, which affects their customer service. The quality of the furniture varies from low to moderate. However, if you're on the lookout for affordable furniture, great deals, or unique accent pieces, this is the perfect place to visit. In fact, I came across a sectional that was priced $1,000 less than the same one at a name-brand store. That's definitely a bargain worth considering!

input: I have been here numerous times for brunch, dinner and take out during lunch time hours. Staff is always friendly and the food is delicious.
Rewrite this for me: I've frequented this place countless times for brunch, dinner, and lunch takeout, and I must say that the staff is consistently friendly and the food is incredibly delicious.

input: Amazing dinner.  What a unique menu.  The service was top notch.  Adrian was our server and she was a delight.  I had the endive and beet salad - lovely.  And then the tongue.  Not what my grandmother made and that's okay.  This was spectacular.  Good wine list and yummy dessert.  The meal was wonderful and I'll be back next time I'm in town.  Bravo!!!
Rewrite this for me: The dinner was absolutely incredible. The menu offered a truly unique selection of dishes. The service provided was absolutely top-notch, with Adrian as our delightful server. The endive and beet salad I had was absolutely lovely. As for the main course, the tongue dish was unlike anything my grandmother used to make, but in the best way possible. It was truly spectacular. Additionally, the wine list was impressive and the dessert was absolutely delicious. Overall, the entire meal was fantastic, and I'm already looking forward to returning the next time I'm in town. Bravo!

input: Do not waste your time and money on this place. The "food" is what you might expect from a small town Chi-Chi's.
Rewrite this for me: Save yourself the trouble and don't invest your precious time and hard-earned money in this establishment. The quality of the "food" is on par with what one would anticipate from a modest Chi-Chi's restaurant in a small town.

input:
Cozy and family friendly restaurant. I came here for a private engagement party, where the bride and groom to be had arranged for special menus and baked all of their desserts. There were a few booth tables reserved for presents, wine, and desserts. No room for side tables like in an actual special events space.

The wait staff was nice. From the limited menu, I picked the Penne Fellini, which has prosciutto di parma, peas, onions, and light cream sauce. The whole dish was literally this pasta swimming in sauce. It may have had a light cream flavor, but it was ladled heavily onto the pasta. I didn't have a desire to consume an entire meal of this, so I ended up not finishing.

It was a fun celebration, and we were really there for the friends and family, not the food. Oh, and we also had the bruschetta and salad, neither of which was very memorable. I wouldn't be thrilled to come back here, but I think it's awesome that they turned the whole restaurant into a venue for such a special occasion!
Rewrite this for me:
This is a cozy and inviting restaurant that is suitable for families. I attended a private engagement party here where the bride and groom had organized special menus and even baked their own desserts. Some booth tables were reserved for gifts, wine, and desserts, as there was no space for separate side tables typically found in dedicated event spaces.

The wait staff were pleasant and accommodating. Of the limited menu options, I chose the Penne Fellini, which consisted of prosciutto di parma, peas, onions, and a light cream sauce. However, the dish was overwhelmingly saucy, with the pasta practically swimming in it. While it had a hint of cream flavor, the sauce was excessively poured onto the pasta. Consequently, I did not have the desire to finish the entire meal.

Nevertheless, the celebration itself was enjoyable, and the main focus was on the presence of friends and family rather than the food. We also had the bruschetta and salad, although neither left a lasting impression. While I may not be particularly thrilled about returning to this restaurant, I appreciate their efforts in transforming the entire space into a venue for such a special occasion!

input: We are having a recall fixed on our 1999 Nissan Pathfinder. The staff is very friendly and they keep you updated. We were treated the same as somebody buying a new car. Highly recommend!
Rewrite this for me: We are getting a recall issue resolved with our 1999 Nissan Pathfinder. The staff is exceptionally pleasant and ensures that you receive regular updates. They treated us with the same level of care as someone purchasing a brand new car. I highly recommend their service!

input:
This place is the epitome of a great hole in the wall find.  From  the  70s vintage floral upholstery  to the back entrance off the alley, it undersells it self and sets you up for a great surprise.  The food is good -- not fancy, not at all pretentious - but good. 

A group from work made the trek on the coldest day of the year and we were rewarded for our efforts -- the chicken hot pot was the best example this dish I have ever had.  The seafood dish with shrimp, scallops and squid was very generous for the price of about $10. The beef in black bean sauce was nice and spicy.  

I will certainly return, but only with adventurous companions.
Rewrite this for me:
This place is the perfect embodiment of a hidden gem. From its vintage 70s floral upholstery to its inconspicuous back entrance in the alley, it effortlessly downplays itself, leaving you pleasantly surprised. The food here is not fancy or pretentious, but it is undeniably delicious.

On the coldest day of the year, my coworkers and I embarked on a journey to this place, and our efforts were handsomely rewarded. The chicken hot pot they served us was the epitome of perfection, surpassing all other versions I've ever tasted. Additionally, the seafood dish, consisting of shrimp, scallops, and squid, was surprisingly generous given its affordable price of around $10. The beef in black bean sauce possessed a satisfying spiciness.

Undoubtedly, I will revisit this place, but only in the company of adventurous companions, as they will appreciate the experience just as much as I do.

input:
I k ow looking at the description, this may seem like a festival you wouldn't want to go to.  But trust me, you really really are missing out on a fun weekend afternoon.  I really enjoyed watching the dances performances - some of the dances were absolutely breathtaking.  This year was the first time I visited, but I'll make a point to go every year I am in town.

The best part of this place was the food - yes the lines are long.  but it is definitely worth the wait.  I remember standing in line waiting in anticipation to be able to order the gyros.  My hungry stomach told me a full eternity had passed before we got to the front, but my watch said it was only a few short minutes.  They serve the food very quickly, so do not be discouraged by a long line.  Also, they have menus that tell you exactly what they serve at each of the stalls.  So make sure you double check because you got end p in a line that only has a couple of options.  My two favorite foods from this place were the gyros and the spankopitas.  Another thing I would suggest is coming with a group that is willing to share - that way you get to try a little of everything.  Definitely a great way to spend Labor Day weekend (and an activity that I think the little ones would enjoy).
Rewrite this for me:
Although the festival may not appear appealing based on the description, let me assure you that you are truly missing out on a fantastic weekend afternoon. Personally, I found immense joy in observing the breathtaking dance performances. Even though this was my first time attending, I am determined to make it an annual tradition whenever I am in town.

One of the highlights of this event was undoubtedly the food, despite the long waiting lines. Trust me, the wait is absolutely worth it. I vividly remember eagerly standing in line, anticipating the moment I could order the mouthwatering gyros. Although my grumbling stomach made it feel like an eternity, my watch proved that it was only a few short minutes. The food is served promptly, so don't be discouraged by the long queues. Additionally, they provide menus at each stall, listing the specific offerings. Therefore, make sure to double-check before joining a line that may have limited options. Personally, I highly recommend trying the gyros and the spankopitas, as they were my two favorite dishes. Furthermore, I suggest coming with a group that is willing to share, allowing you to sample a bit of everything. It is undoubtedly a wonderful way to spend Labor Day weekend, and I believe even the young ones would enjoy this activity.

input: The food here is tasty - love the brisket and the cheese grits. BUT - we have had terrible luck with take out. Tried it three times, and an item was missing every time. A disappointing blemish on an otherwise fine restaurant.
Rewrite this for me: The food at this place is delicious; I particularly enjoy the flavorful brisket and the cheesy grits. However, our experience with takeout has been consistently disappointing. We have attempted it on three different occasions, only to discover that an item was missing each time. This unfortunate flaw tarnishes an otherwise excellent dining establishment.

input: Provi is such a wonderful person I came here because of her. The chipotle chicken avocado sandwich and chicken noodle soup is just to die for.
Rewrite this for me: I decided to come here solely because of Provi's delightful existence. The chipotle chicken avocado sandwich and chicken noodle soup are absolutely amazing and worth every bite.

input:
FOOD REVIEW

If you're looking for quality meal that is quick and affordable, the Fountain has you covered. The menu isn't extensive, but it's got a good amount of inexpensive sandwiches, salads, and soups.  

Their Cuban Sandwich ($10 w/ side) was pretty excellent.  The bread wasn't the traditional panini-style, but a French baguette...it was still great and had a little crispness to it.  All the main ingredients (meat, mustard, pickles, cheese) were in good balance.  As a Florida boy who loves his Cuban sandwiches, I would definitely recommend this.

I also tried a bit of their Royal Grille, a grilled-chese sandwich with several cheeses, as well as apple slices, on whole grain wheat bread ($8.50 w/ side, extra to add ham/turkey).  It was damn good and hit the grilled cheese craving just right.  A side salad was also done well.

For my side, I chose their "spicy carrots" which sounded unique.  It consists of sliced raw carrots that have been marinated in a tangy dressing with crushed red pepper, served in a cup. The carrots were cold and crisp and the flavors were fantastic.  The spice was just enough to be pleasant.  I would definitely get these again.

Our food came out super quick and our service was great.  I'm looking forward to trying a couple more items and bumping this up to 5 stars.
Rewrite this for me:
FOOD REVIEW

If you're in need of a delicious and affordable meal that is served promptly, look no further than the Fountain. While the menu isn't extensive, it offers a satisfying selection of reasonably priced sandwiches, salads, and soups.

One standout item is their Cuban Sandwich ($10 with a side). Though it deviates from the traditional panini-style bread, opting for a French baguette instead, it remains excellent with a satisfying crispness. The combination of meat, mustard, pickles, and cheese was perfectly balanced, pleasing even a self-proclaimed Cuban sandwich connoisseur like myself.

Another dish I sampled was the Royal Grille, a grilled cheese sandwich featuring a variety of cheeses and apple slices, all encased in whole grain wheat bread ($8.50 with a side, with the option to add ham or turkey). It surpassed expectations and satisfied my craving for a well-made grilled cheese sandwich. Additionally, their side salad was skillfully prepared.

To accompany my main course, I decided to try their "spicy carrots" – a unique offering. Sliced raw carrots marinated in a tangy dressing with crushed red pepper, served chilled in a cup. The carrots were refreshingly crisp, and the flavors melded together harmoniously. The level of spiciness was just right, providing a delightful kick. I would undoubtedly order these carrots again.

Our food arrived swiftly, and the service we received was exceptional. I eagerly await the opportunity to sample a few more menu items, as I am confident it will elevate my overall dining experience and warrant a well-deserved 5-star rating.

input:
Burger Up is, by far, one of our favorite restaurants in the Nashville area.  It has a cool hipster vibe, without being annoying :)  The burgers are outstanding, and there are endless options, whether you prefer beef, chicken, seafood, or veggie!  I would recommend the Woodstock - the Jack Daniels Maple Ketchup is out of this world, and Benton's bacon is always delicious.  Upgrade to the truffle fries; they're to die for.  Or, if you're a vegetarian, the troyathalon is a great option.  Filling, with great texture and flavor.  As far as drinks go, 12 South Lemonade.

The customer service is also great.  They've always been attentive, but not "on top of you", and they're very knowledgable about their food.  Parking can be a bit difficult at certain times of the day, but it's worth a short walk if necessary.

I would definitely recommend checking it out!
Rewrite this for me:
Burger Up is easily one of our top choices when it comes to restaurants in the Nashville area. It boasts a cool hipster atmosphere that manages to avoid being obnoxious. The burgers here are truly exceptional and the menu offers an abundance of options, whether you're a fan of beef, chicken, seafood, or veggie patties. Personally, I highly recommend trying the Woodstock - the Jack Daniels Maple Ketchup is absolutely mind-blowing, and the Benton's bacon never disappoints. For an extra special treat, upgrade to the truffle fries - they are absolutely heavenly. And for those who prefer vegetarian options, the troyathalon burger is an excellent choice. It's incredibly satisfying, with an impressive combination of texture and flavor. When it comes to beverages, the 12 South Lemonade is a winner.

One aspect that truly sets Burger Up apart is their fantastic customer service. The staff is always attentive without being overly intrusive, and they possess a wealth of knowledge about the menu. While parking can be a bit challenging at certain times of the day, don't let that deter you. A short walk is definitely worth it for the experience that awaits you at Burger Up.

Without a doubt, I wholeheartedly recommend giving this place a visit.

input:
I have mix feelings about this place. First, I didn't make a reservation and we waited about 50 minutes to be seated when they told us it will be about 15 to 20 min wait. I probably should'v left and tried the next time since I was not happy when I was seated due to the waiting.

I knew I couldn't eat the full-course meal so we decided to get cheese fondue and one of their entrees. Cheese fondue was delicious. If I go next time, I would probably just get the cheese fondue. =]

And the entree we had.. was some chicken, meat, shrimp, mushrooms, etc. We decided to go with oil instead of broth because that's what our waitress suggested and I didn't really like it. I think I will try the broth next time if I do and see if I like it any better. Except the mushroom with stuffing, others were ok.

We had this private booth which was very romantic and nice. I think this place would be good for people who want privacy and have plenty of time for dinner. We stayed there for 2&1/2 hours excluding the waiting time.
Rewrite this for me:
I have mixed feelings about this place. Initially, we didn't have a reservation and ended up waiting for about 50 minutes to be seated, even though they had indicated a wait time of 15 to 20 minutes. In hindsight, I should have probably left and tried again another time, as the waiting experience left me feeling unhappy upon finally being seated.

Knowing that I couldn't handle a full-course meal, we opted for cheese fondue along with one of their entrees. The cheese fondue was absolutely delicious. If I were to visit again, I would likely just order the cheese fondue by itself. =]

As for the entree we ordered, it consisted of chicken, meat, shrimp, mushrooms, and more. Our waitress suggested we go with oil instead of broth, but I personally didn't enjoy it. If I do return, I might give the broth a chance to see if I like it better. With the exception of the mushroom with stuffing, the other items were just okay.

On the positive side, we were seated in a private booth, which created a romantic and pleasant ambiance. This place would be suitable for those seeking privacy and who have ample time for a leisurely dinner. In total, we spent 2 and a half hours at the restaurant, excluding the time spent waiting.

input:
Great Mexican BYOB! I went to Las Cazuelas for the first time for my birthday.  We had a wonderful time.  I was looking for a fun and festive place to go with friends.  This was the perfect choice. We brought our own bottle of tequila, and they made tasty margaritas for the table.  Those were a big hit with my friends, and a cool twist for a Mexican BYOB.  The restaurant is cute.  Plus, the food here is delicious. 

I'm surprised this place doesn't have higher reviews on Yelp, because it far exceeded my expectations... 

The guacamole appetizer was fresh and yummy.  I ordered the shrimp entree with rice and vegetables, and asked for it spicy.  My entrée had an attractive presentation on the plate (i.e. looked classy), and was delicious, well seasoned, and very fresh. On my suggestion, my partner ordered one of their mole sauce dishes (i.e. a sauce usually made from unsweetened chocolate and pureed pumpkin seeds), and it was tasty too. 

I should also note that the waitress was very attentive.  When I placed my order, I explained to her that I have mild lactose intolerance and can't eat much butter or cream (but am okay with cheese), so she had the chef cook the veggies in olive oil, rather than butter.  Thanks for being so cool about accommodating that request!  

The prices are extremely reasonable for fancy and unusual Mexican food, and I love the fact they're a BYOB.  The chef serves creative and inspired cuisine, which has a traditional flair and style to it.  In other words: Don't come here for regular tacos or burritos.  Come here for a fun foodie experience at a reasonable price, and bring tequila for the perk of BYOB Margaritas!
Rewrite this for me:
Las Cazuelas is a fantastic Mexican restaurant that allows you to bring your own bottle of tequila, making it a great choice for a fun and festive birthday celebration with friends. Despite not having high Yelp reviews, this place exceeded my expectations in every way. The ambience of the restaurant is cute and the food is absolutely delicious.

We started off with the guacamole appetizer, which was fresh and yummy. For my main course, I opted for the shrimp dish with rice and vegetables, requesting it to be spicy. Not only was the presentation of the dish classy, but it was also incredibly flavorful and made with fresh ingredients. I also encouraged my partner to try one of their mole sauce dishes, which turned out to be a tasty choice.

What impressed me the most was the attentive service provided by the waitress. I informed her about my mild lactose intolerance and she was kind enough to have the chef cook the vegetables in olive oil instead of butter, accommodating my dietary needs. Their prices are reasonable for the quality of the food, which I would describe as fancy and unique Mexican cuisine with a traditional twist. This place is not for those looking for regular tacos or burritos, but rather for those seeking a fun foodie experience at an affordable price. And the added bonus of bringing your own tequila for BYOB Margaritas makes it even better.

input: This was one of the greatest meals I have ever had.  The food was delicious and the hospitality was second to none.  The lamb was cooked to perfection, the rice had the perfect amount of spice.  The ability to easily describe the amount of spice made this meal perfect for spicy lovers, but also easy for those with a milder pallet.  All of this is from someone who has historically not been a fan of Pakistani/Indian food.  I would recommend this restaurant to anyone and would encourage a trip to St. Louis just for the food here.
Rewrite this for me: I must say, this meal has been truly exceptional. The flavors were absolutely delightful, and the warm welcome received was unmatched. The lamb was flawlessly cooked, and the rice had just the right amount of spice. The option to customize the spice level made it an ideal choice for both aficionados of fiery cuisine and those with a more delicate taste. It's worth mentioning that, as someone who hasn't typically favored Pakistani/Indian cuisine, this dining experience has completely won me over. I wholeheartedly recommend this restaurant to anyone and would even go as far as suggesting a trip to St. Louis solely for the incredible food it offers.

input: Amazingly awesome! Tried a couple of different things, everything was delicious! Their Bloody Mary was one of the worst I've ever had, but I didn't go there to drink, and besides that not what they are known for. Their mojoto are good tho.
Rewrite this for me: Incredibly fantastic! Experimented with a few different options, and every single one was mouthwatering! While their Bloody Mary left much to be desired, it's important to note that I didn't visit for the drinks, and that's not their specialty anyway. However, their mojitos are definitely worth trying.

input:
I'm not really sure why I bother going to other restaurants. 

Every Valentine's Day I try to find some cute, new little BYO for me and my boyfriend to try out and I spend weeks scouring menus and Yelp reviews. 

Every year SOMETHING goes wrong and I get frustrated and pissed off and he always says "Let's go to Jones".

This year was no different. We went out last night (2/12/11...the weekend before Valentines Day) to the BYO I picked out and when I made our reservations, no mention was made that they had a special fixed menu that night consisting SOLELY of seafood, which I am allergic to. As I started to get upset at our table, my boyfriend said "Let's go to Jones".

We got there, were told there was a little bit of a wait, so we sat at the bar for a drink. About 5-10 minutes later they came and got us and sat us at our table. Our waiter (who was WONDERFUL and looked like Jared Leto - extra bonus-) came over and took our order and the food came out perfectly (as usual) and right on time.

We both got the filet, done rare and the spinach it came with was fantastic. The mac and cheese is also an app we get every time and is one of my favorites. I got the deviled eggs for the first time and holy crap they were amazing. I'm gonna say, possibly the best ones I've ever had (sorry, Dad). 

Everything about this restaurant leans towards comfort and it's always done so well. The atmosphere, the staff, the decor, the food, hell even the temperature. I've never had a bad experience at Jones and I don't think I ever will. 

Next year....we'll just go straight to Jones.

input: Quack & Cheese is where it is at! We were there for the lunch menu. The duck fries are so delicious. It was my first time there & I ordered the portabello burger. They didn't have the right mushrooms & asked if a substitute was ok. I said sure. But I couldn't eat it. I asked for some kind of sauce & instead they let me order something else. That was so nice. I don't usually complain about anything. I felt like they really catered to our whole party. I would definitely love to come back for a date night.
Rewrite this for me: Quack & Cheese is the place to be! We visited during lunchtime and were blown away by the incredible duck fries. Although it was my first visit, I opted for the portabello burger. Unfortunately, they didn't have the specific mushrooms needed, but graciously offered a substitute. input:
The family and I ate here on Labor Day, 2015.  We wanted to go to another restaurant, but it was closed, so we stopped at Casa Garcia.  The inside of the restaurant is very pleasant.  The fountain is a nice touch.

The chips, salsa and bean dip were very good.  We greatly enjoyed them.  We also all agreed that the tortilla soup was excellent.  It was when the entrees arrived that things went down hill.

The sour cream and guacamole were fresh, but the entrees were just average at best.  The quesadillas had too much cheese and not much else flavor.  

The meal was not bad, but there are better options close by.
Rewrite this for me:
On Labor Day, 2015, my family and I dined at Casa Garcia, as our original restaurant choice was closed. The interior of the restaurant was inviting, with a pleasant atmosphere enhanced by a charming fountain.

We started our meal with the chips, salsa, and bean dip, which we found to be delicious and greatly enjoyed. The tortilla soup, too, exceeded our expectations and was a definite highlight.

However, our enthusiasm dampened when our entrees arrived. While the sour cream and guacamole were fresh tasting, the main dishes were disappointingly average. The quesadillas were overwhelmed with cheese and lacked other flavorful elements.

Overall, the dining experience was not terrible, but there are certainly better dining options nearby.

input: I started coming to Moreno when I moved back to Brandon and had an itch for Alessi Bakery but didn't  want to drive too far. Someone told us about Moreno so we gave them a shot! A great, small, FAMILY-OWNED (love it!) bakery right in the heart of Brandon. They make a HUGE variety of baked goods from fresh bread to huge cupcakes to flan and cookies! They also have the best freshly made cuban sandwich with their own special sauce spread! My favorite thing to get here are the almond sticks. I am a huge fan of anything almond, but these are so fresh with loads of almonds and almond flavoring! If you have a sweet tooth, this is DEFINITELY the place to go!
Rewrite this for me: When I returned to Brandon and had a craving for Alessi Bakery, but didn't want to travel too far, I discovered Moreno. Recommended by someone, we decided to give them a try. They offer an extensive range of baked goods, including fresh bread, sizable cupcakes, flan, and cookies. Additionally, they serve the most incredible Cuban sandwich, featuring their own special sauce spread. Personally, my go-to treat at Moreno is their almond sticks. Being a huge almond fan, I adore the fresh taste and abundance of almonds in these delicate sticks. If you have a sweet tooth, Moreno is an absolute must-visit establishment.

input: I wish I could give this zero stars, this gave my husband and kid a really really bad stomach ache after eating here. This used to be our favorite Chinese restaurant but not anymore. Never eat here. Also on another note the delivery really slow.

input:

input: Good food excellent service, everything was delicious. input: The atmosphere was nice and small. Very busy for brunch, expect at least a 30-45 minute wait. input:
I was just passing through Tuscon. Native American inspired breakfast food? I just had to have some :-).  Basically I ended up with amazing and unique food that I wish I could have everyday! Five stars!

It took me while to decide what I wanted because there was so many things I wanted. 

Finally, I ended up with the pueblo, which basically is the green corn waffle with eggs the way you want it and a choice of a side (I got chorizo). The waiter told me how to eat it: put the syrup + hot sauce on the waffle and enjoy. But, instead, I ended up making an awesome syrup, hot sauce, egg, chorizo and red sauce tower on my waffle for each bite. It was delicious - try it!!!
Rewrite this for me:
While passing through Tuscon, I was intrigued by the idea of Native American-inspired breakfast cuisine. Naturally, I couldn't resist indulging in it! The experience turned out to be nothing short of incredible, offering me a truly unique and mouthwatering meal that I wish I could enjoy every day. I must admit, selecting from the menu took me quite some time because everything seemed equally tempting.

Eventually, I settled on the pueblo dish, which consisted of a delightful green corn waffle accompanied by eggs prepared just the way I preferred. To complement this delectable combination, I opted for chorizo as my side. The waiter kindly advised me on the best way to savor the flavors – by drizzling syrup and adding hot sauce onto the waffle. However, my creativity took over, and instead, I constructed a magnificent tower composed of syrup, hot sauce, eggs, chorizo, and red sauce on each bite of the waffle. The end result was a truly mouthwatering symphony of flavors. I highly recommend giving it a try!

input:
Another wonderful stip mall ethnic restruarant!!! This was my first time at a Veitnamese restuarant and I will say that pho is a little bowl of heaven. It was warm and fragrant and with all the condements they bring on the side, easy to customize. We also got BBQ pork sandwiches and they were very tasty. The meat was tender and flavorful and they had fresh herbs on them and some kind of yummy sauce. They only take cash, so make sure you hit the ATM before you go. The food is very reasonably priced though.

This restuarant started my love affair with pho, but I haven't had any as good anywhere else in Nashville.
Rewrite this for me:
Another amazing ethnic restaurant located in a strip mall! I recently had the pleasure of dining at a Vietnamese restaurant for the first time and let me tell you, pho is like a small bowl of heaven. It was not only warm and fragrant, but also customizable with the plethora of condiments they provided on the side. In addition to the pho, we also tried their BBQ pork sandwiches which were absolutely delicious. The meat was tender and packed with flavor, topped off with fresh herbs and a delectable sauce. Just a heads up, they only accept cash, so be sure to withdraw some from an ATM before you visit. Despite this, the prices here are very reasonable.

This restaurant ignited my passion for pho, although I have yet to find any other place in Nashville that can compare to its greatness.

input:
This shop is a slice of Disney beauty and magic hiding on the edge of Broad Ripple, and a MUST stop of sweets, treats, and dreaminess. Your Instagram needs this place. Hands down the ~best~ red velvet cake of my life.

Appearance: The Cake Bake Shop is a beautifully decorated, small white house with a captivating design. The flowers around the sign make it an #instaworthy post for sure, and when the weather is nice, the outdoor seating must be gorgeous.

Inside the Cake Shop will take your breath away, light airy colors and flowers and twinkling lights. This isn't the kind of cake shop you do take-out at, you'll want to sit and enjoy. 

Food: I wanted to try the Raspberry Champagne cake, unfortunately one wouldn't be ready for a little while, so I ordered a slice of the Red Velvet  Cake. The floral icing work was so perfect I didn't want to touch it, but I had to because come on it's cake. What I assume must have been cream cheese filling in the middle was decadent and I never wanted the cake to end. ***I felt one slice was plenty for two people, it's HUGE

I was torn between the Rose Cappuccino and the Lavender Latte. I went with the Lavender Latte, hot, and it was stunning, it was a creamy, smooth, not-at-all bitter latte and the hint of lavender was enough to taste but not over powering, it was probably the most perfect coffee I've ever had in my life. 

Price: the coffee is pricy, $6, so not a regular coffee stop for me, but for #treatyoself it's the way to go. The slice of cake was $12 but like I mentioned, it was enough for two people and for how amazing it was, I think it's so worth it.

Customer Service: I mentioned Disney initially because the friendliness, care, and attention of the staff felt just like Disney. They were kind, they helped me decide what to try, and the barista even offered to make me the rose cappuccino if I didn't like the lavender latte after trying it - how sweet! 

I will most definitely think to come here if anyone visits and wants something sweet. This place has my heart and is a hidden gem to anyone who has a sweet tooth!

Check out my #FirstTimeFriday highlight of my visit to The Cake Bake Shop on my Instagram @jordanqjordanq for pictures of everything mentioned above!
Rewrite this for me:
Located on the outskirts of Broad Ripple, this charming shop embodies the enchantment and allure of Disney. A must-visit for those seeking delectable sweets, treats, and a touch of dreaminess. Trust me, your Instagram feed needs this place. And let me tell you, their red velvet cake is hands down the best I've ever had.

The Cake Bake Shop is housed in a beautifully adorned, petite white house with a captivating design. The flowers surrounding the sign are guaranteed to make your post #instaworthy. And if the weather permits, their outdoor seating is simply divine.

As you step inside, be prepared to have your breath taken away. The interior boasts light, airy colors, adorned with flowers and twinkling lights. This is no ordinary cake shop, my friends. You won't want to grab and go - you'll want to sit and savor every moment.

When it came time to indulge in their offerings, I initially wanted to try their Raspberry Champagne cake. Unfortunately, it wasn't quite ready, so I opted for a slice of their renowned Red Velvet Cake. The flawless floral icing on top made me hesitant to disturb its perfection. But let's be real, it's cake, and I couldn't resist. The cream cheese filling inside was pure decadence, leaving me yearning for more. Let me just mention, one slice is more than enough for two people - it's HUGE.

Choosing between the Rose Cappuccino and the Lavender Latte was no easy task. In the end, I went with the Lavender Latte, served piping hot. It was absolutely breathtaking. Creamy and smooth, with no trace of bitterness. The hint of lavender was just enough to tantalize my taste buds without overpowering the delicate balance. This, my friends, may just be the most perfect coffee I've ever had the pleasure of sipping.

Now, let's talk prices. The coffee here is a bit on the pricier side, coming in at $6. It's not your everyday coffee stop, but if you're looking to #treatyoself, this is the place to be. As for the slice of cake, it may seem steep at $12, but considering its size and incredible taste, I wholeheartedly believe it's worth every penny.

The staff at the Cake Bake Shop deserves a special mention. From the moment I walked in, their friendliness, care, and attention made me feel like I had stepped into a Disney movie. They went above and beyond, helping me make my decisions and even offering to make me the Rose Cappuccino if I didn't enjoy the Lavender Latte. Talk about sweet customer service!

If anyone ever visits and has a hankering for something sweet, this hidden gem will definitely be at the top of my recommendation list. The Cake Bake Shop has stolen my heart, and it's a true haven for anyone with a sweet tooth.

For a visual feast of my visit to The Cake Bake Shop, check out my #FirstTimeFriday highlight on my Instagram @jordanqjordanq. I've captured all the magical moments mentioned above.

input:
Western cycle is a huge store and sells everything to do with bikes. They've got your $150 kids' bikes with training wheels and your $5,000 racing bikes for triathletes. The staff are knowledgeable, and they've got a mixture of older, more mature and younger people, all of whom seem into biking. 

The one aspect I've enjoyed most about coming here over the years is how they keep returned, out-of-package stuff in a drawer and will sell it to you on discount. I once got $200 pedals for $60 just 'cause they were sitting in a drawer without their proper package. The guys work really hard here to keep their customers loyal, and it works. They're honest and well-trained. You're never left wandering without help. This and United Cycle are pretty much the only two bike places I'll shop.

Western Cycle is a large store that caters to all things related to bikes. Whether you're looking for affordable kids' bikes with training wheels priced at $150 or high-end racing bikes for triathletes costing $5,000, they have it all. The staff at Western Cycle is impressive, comprising a mix of both seasoned individuals and younger enthusiasts who share a passion for biking.

One remarkable aspect of this store that has kept me coming back throughout the years is their policy of offering discounted prices on returned items that are no longer in their original packaging. They store these items in a drawer and sell them at a reduced rate. I once scored a pair of pedals worth $200 for just $60 simply because they were not in their proper package. The dedication of the staff at Western Cycle is evident as they work diligently to ensure customer satisfaction and loyalty. They are honest and well-trained, making sure that no customer ever feels lost or left without assistance. It is for these reasons that Western Cycle, along with United Cycle, are the only two bike shops I trust and prefer to shop at.

input:
I eat at Sukho Thai quite a bit, and I don't really get the negative ratings. Is it the most authentic thai place in the area? No. Sometimes I would say they sometimes substitute certain ingredients. It is however usually pretty consistent as far as quality of food and service. 

I usually get the red or green curry, and almost always get it "native thai hot". I have tried other things on the menu, but they are not quite as good. So I stick with what tastes good and works for me. 

The lady that owns the place is very kind and always very gracious to my wife and I. She always recognizes us and serves us promptly. She not only owns the place, but she waits all of the tables most of the time(which I think is pretty impressive). 
The place is beside a go-cart track, so that makes it a little quirky, but it's something I have grown accustomed to. 

The only thing negative I would say is that I wish they had Kee Mao on the menu, because that's my favorite. I usually go to Siam Cafe or Thai Star for that.
Rewrite this for me:
I frequently dine at Sukho Thai and I don't quite understand the negative reviews. While it may not be the most authentic Thai restaurant in the area, I have noticed occasional substitutions of ingredients. However, the quality of food and service is generally consistent. 

Personally, I often choose the red or green curry, and I always prefer it to be "native Thai hot". Although I have tried other items on the menu, they do not compare in taste. Therefore, I stick to what I know is delicious and works for me. 

The owner of the restaurant is extremely kind and always treats my wife and me with great respect. She recognizes us and provides prompt service. Notably, she not only owns the establishment but also waits on most of the tables herself, which I find impressive. 

The restaurant's location next to a go-cart track adds a bit of quirkiness, but I have grown accustomed to it. 

The only downside is that I wish they offered Kee Mao on the menu, as it is my favorite dish. For that, I usually visit Siam Cafe or Thai Star.

input:
When you dine at Muriel's, check to see if the 2nd level is open for visitors. If so, you can briefly tour the lounge area upstairs (red couches, decorative pieces). There's a wrap-around balcony where you can get a great view of Jackson Square. 

If you're curious, learn why Muriel's is haunted and find out the story behind why there's a table that is always set for two located near the stairs. 

There are two main dining rooms, a middle section (indoor patio dining area) that I personally prefer because it is quieter, and a bar area located at the back near the restrooms. I love the indoor patio dining area because it brings a bit of the outdoors in a quiet indoor setting. 

On my first visit, I ordered from the dinner pre-fix menu which is a great deal (appetizer or soup + entrée + dessert = $40). The seafood gumbo soup was hearty and delicious. The dijon mustard encrusted salmon was cooked perfectly. The bread pudding was a great way to end a delicious meal.

I returned to Muriel's for lunch on another NOLA trip and tried the wood grilled pork chop. The pork chop was flavorful, tender, and moist. I was not too crazy about the red beans and rice it was served with as I found it a bit bland. The entrée was served in a bowl but should perhaps be served on a plate since it was difficult to slice the pork chop since it kept sinking into the bed of red beans and rice. 

Muriel's is one of the places I would love to return to because of the ambiance and the great food.
Rewrite this for me:
When you visit Muriel's for a meal, be sure to check if the second level is open to visitors. If it is, take a quick tour of the upstairs lounge area, where you'll find comfortable red couches and decorative pieces. Don't miss the wrap-around balcony with its stunning view of Jackson Square.

If you're curious, learn about the haunted history of Muriel's and discover the story behind the table always set for two near the stairs. 

The restaurant has two main dining rooms, but my personal favorite is the middle section—an indoor patio dining area that offers a quieter atmosphere. There's also a bar area located at the back, near the restrooms. I love the indoor patio because it brings a touch of the outdoors into a peaceful indoor setting.

During my first visit, I tried the dinner pre-fix menu, which was an excellent deal at $40 for an appetizer or soup, entree, and dessert. The seafood gumbo soup was rich and flavorful, and the dijon mustard encrusted salmon was perfectly cooked. For dessert, the bread pudding was a delightful way to end the meal.

On a subsequent trip to New Orleans, I returned to Muriel's for lunch and opted for the wood-grilled pork chop. It was incredibly tasty, tender, and juicy. However, I wasn't a fan of the red beans and rice it came with, as it lacked flavor. Additionally, the pork chop was served in a bowl, which made it challenging to slice since it kept sinking into the bed of red beans and rice. Perhaps it would be better presented on a plate.

Considering the fantastic ambiance and delicious food, Muriel's is definitely a place I look forward to visiting again.

input:
I like to make a stop at this Walmart since it's located in Meadowlark where my doctor's office is.  It's smaller than  the supercentre but I find it has a decent selection of items in the food section where the prices are cheaper than the nearby stores.  The produce section can have limited items though with just the basics in stock.  I find the snacks and canned food section are fine with good prices.

As for the rest of the store and items, well it's hit or miss.  I was looking for lightbulbs and they only had one brand of the type I was looking for and it was a energy efficient so pricier than others if they had in stock.  However, the price I paid for the item was probably cheaper than other stores.  

Don't expect much help if you need help finding an item.  Associates seem to be difficult to find unless you count some of the younger staff who like racing shopping carts in the store as they were on my last visit.  

The check outs can have at most 5 cashiers working but I find the time in the line ups is never too long so that's good.
Rewrite this for me:
Since my doctor's office is located in Meadowlark, I often make a stop at this Walmart. Although it is smaller than the supercentre, I find that it offers a decent selection of items in the food section with prices that are cheaper than nearby stores. However, the produce section may be limited, only stocking the basics. On the bright side, the snacks and canned food section has good prices.

When it comes to the rest of the store and its items, it's a bit hit or miss. During my recent visit, I was searching for lightbulbs and found that they only carried one brand of the type I needed, which happened to be pricier than others of its kind. Nevertheless, I still ended up paying a lower price compared to other stores.

If you need assistance finding an item, it's best not to expect much help. The associates can be quite difficult to locate, unless you count some of the younger staff who enjoy racing shopping carts through the store.

There are typically only up to 5 cashiers working at the checkouts, but fortunately, the wait times in line are usually not too lengthy.
